sections.title: 什麼是複寫 (Replication)？為什麼資料庫需要複寫？
sections.summary: Data replication involves storing copies of the same data across multiple nodes, machines, or geographic regions rather than in a single location. A primary example is a Content Delivery Network (CDN), which distributes content globally to ensure high availability and minimize latency. Replication extends the concept of collocation by maintaining multiple local copies, enabling faster response times from nearby nodes while providing redundancy if a node fails.
takeaways: Data replication stores identical data across multiple nodes, machines, or geographic regions simultaneously.
Replicating data enhances system availability by allowing redundant nodes to operate if one fails.
Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) use replication across diverse geographical locations to reduce latency and improve availability.
Replication builds upon the concept of collocation by keeping regional data copies close to users to accelerate response times.

sections.title: 從延遲的角度看常見的資料複寫策略
sections.summary: This section examines three common data replication strategies—single-leader, multi-leader, and leaderless replication—specifically through the lens of network latency. Single-leader replication is architecturally simple, but in globally distributed systems, it suffers from high write latency due to physical distance between remote clients and the primary node. Multi-leader replication reduces geographic latency across multiple datacenters by allowing clients to write to local leader nodes, though it introduces significant complexity in conflict resolution and cross-datacenter synchronization. Leaderless replication allows clients to write directly to any available nearby node to minimize latency, but it requires additional mechanisms to maintain consistency across peers.
takeaways: In single-leader replication, all writes must travel to the sole leader node, causing high latency for geographically distant users.
Multi-leader replication is rarely used in single-datacenter environments due to conflict-resolution complexity and minimal latency gains across short distances.
Across multi-datacenter deployments, multi-leader replication significantly reduces write latency by providing local leader nodes across regions such as Asia, the US, and Europe.
The primary operational trade-offs of multi-leader replication include handling concurrent write conflicts, cross-region replication delays, and failover recovery.
Leaderless replication minimizes write latency by allowing clients to write to the closest available node, at the expense of added implementation complexity to ensure data consistency.

sections.title: 一致性與延遲取捨
sections.summary: Maintaining multiple data replicas across different regions requires navigating a fundamental trade-off between consistency and latency. Strong consistency guarantees that clients always see the latest data as if interacting with a single copy, but it introduces higher latency due to synchronous multi-replica coordination. In contrast, eventual consistency tolerates temporary data staleness across replicas in exchange for significantly reduced read and write latencies. System designers must decide whether to prioritize immediate data freshness or lower response times based on application requirements.
takeaways: Replicating data across regions forces a choice between immediate consistency and system latency.
Strong consistency hides multi-replica complexity and avoids stale reads, but incurs higher latency due to cross-node coordination and retries.
Eventual consistency allows replicas to temporarily diverge while guaranteeing they will synchronize eventually.
Low-latency systems often adopt eventual consistency because it eliminates costly synchronous cross-region coordination during write operations.
Under eventual consistency, a local region write can return success immediately before synchronizing with other regions, drastically reducing latency.

sections.title: 本期推薦
sections.summary: This curated selection features technical articles on infrastructure, software design, web performance, and database scalability. Key topics include understanding Kubernetes probes through interactive simulations and exploring the historical origins of default development ports like 3000, 8080, and Vite's 5173. On the engineering side, articles analyze the performance costs of React hydration mismatches, Gin's architecture in Go, and Claude's optimization that sped up claude.ai threefold. Finally, the selection highlights rendering strategies for large code diffs and Etsy's migration of a 425+ TB sharded MySQL database to Vitess.
takeaways: Misconfigured Kubernetes startup and liveness probes—such as setting startup intervals too short or tying database outages to liveness checks—can trigger continuous container restarts or cascading failures.

React hydration mismatches between server and client rendering can trigger full DOM reconstructions that delay Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) by seconds, even when visual differences are imperceptible.
The Claude team used Claude to help accelerate core claude.ai workflows approximately 3x within two weeks by integrating reproducible metrics into CI.
Rendering large code diffs smoothly requires managing memory, layout computation, and DOM node counts simultaneously rather than merely virtualizing the DOM.
Etsy addressed single-point-of-failure issues in its legacy sharded database index by migrating over 425 TB of sharded MySQL to Vitess.

zh.summary: Data replication 涉及將相同資料的副本儲存在多個 node、machine 或 geographic region，而非單一地點。最典型的例子是 Content Delivery Network (CDN)，它在全球分發內容以確保 high availability 並將 latency 降至最低。Replication 透過維護多個本機副本延伸了 collocation 的概念，在提供 node 故障時的 redundancy 同時，也能由鄰近的 node 提供更快的 response time。本節特別從 network latency 的視角，檢視三種常見的 data replication 策略：single-leader、multi-leader 與 leaderless replication。Single-leader replication 在架構上相對簡單，但在全球分散式系統中，由於遠端 client 與 primary node 之間的物理距離，會面臨極高的 write latency。Multi-leader replication 允許 client 寫入當地的 leader node，從而降低跨多個 datacenter 的地理 latency，但這會在 conflict resolution 與跨 datacenter synchronization 上引入相當高的複雜度。Leaderless replication 允許 client 直接寫入任何鄰近可用的 node 以最小化 latency，但需要額外的機制來維持 peer 之間的一致性。在不同 region 間維護多個 data replica，必須在 consistency 與 latency 之間權衡取捨。Strong consistency 保證 client 始終能看到最新資料，如同與單一副本互動，但會因同步的 multi-replica coordination 而引入更高的 latency。相對地，eventual consistency 容許 replica 之間暫時的 data staleness，以換取大幅降低的 read 與 write latency。系統設計師必須依據應用需求，決定是要優先考量即時的 data freshness，還是更低的 response time。

sections.title: 什麼是複寫 (Replication)？為什麼資料庫需要複寫？
sections.summary: Data replication 涉及將相同資料的副本儲存在多個 node、machine 或 geographic region，而非單一地點。最典型的例子是 Content Delivery Network (CDN)，它在全球分發內容以確保 high availability 並將 latency 降至最低。Replication 透過維護多個本機副本延伸了 collocation 的概念，在提供 node 故障時的 redundancy 同時，也能由鄰近的 node 提供更快的 response time。
takeaways: Data replication 會同時將完全相同的資料儲存在多個 node、machine 或 geographic region。
Replicating data 可以在某個 node 發生故障時由備援 node 繼續運作，進而提升系統的 availability。
Content Delivery Network (CDN) 透過在不同地理位置進行 replication，以降低 latency 並改善 availability。
Replication 建立在 collocation 的概念之上，透過將區域資料副本保持在靠近使用者的位置來加速 response time。

sections.title: 從延遲的角度看常見的資料複寫策略
sections.summary: 本節特別從 network latency 的視角，檢視三種常見的 data replication 策略：single-leader、multi-leader 與 leaderless replication。Single-leader replication 在架構上相對簡單，但在全球分散式系統中，由於遠端 client 與 primary node 之間的物理距離，會面臨極高的 write latency。Multi-leader replication 允許 client 寫入當地的 leader node，從而降低跨多個 datacenter 的地理 latency，但這會在 conflict resolution 與跨 datacenter synchronization 上引入相當高的複雜度。Leaderless replication 允許 client 直接寫入任何鄰近可用的 node 以最小化 latency，但需要額外的機制來維持 peer 之間的一致性。
takeaways: 在 single-leader replication 中，所有 write 都必須傳送至唯一的 leader node，這會為地理位置偏遠的使用者帶來高 latency。
由於 conflict-resolution 的複雜性，且在短距離內帶來的 latency 改善微乎其微，multi-leader replication 鮮少用於單一 datacenter 環境。
在跨 datacenter 的部署中，multi-leader replication 透過在亞洲、美國和歐洲等 region 提供在地的 leader node，顯著降低了 write latency。
Multi-leader replication 主要的維運 trade-off 包括處理 concurrent write conflict、跨 region replication delay 以及 failover recovery。
Leaderless replication 透過允許 client 寫入最近的可用 node 來將 write latency 降至最低，代價是必須增加實作複雜度以確保 data consistency。

sections.title: 一致性與延遲取捨
sections.summary: 在不同 region 間維護多個 data replica，必須在 consistency 與 latency 之間權衡取捨。Strong consistency 保證 client 始終能看到最新資料，如同與單一副本互動，但會因同步的 multi-replica coordination 而引入更高的 latency。相對地，eventual consistency 容許 replica 之間暫時的 data staleness，以換取大幅降低的 read 與 write latency。系統設計師必須依據應用需求，決定是要優先考量即時的 data freshness，還是更低的 response time。
takeaways: 在跨 region 進行 data replication 時，必須在即時 consistency 與系統 latency 之間做出抉擇。
Strong consistency 隱藏了 multi-replica 的複雜度並避免 stale read，但會因為跨 node coordination 與 retry 而產生更高的 latency。
Eventual consistency 允許 replica 之間暫時不一致，同時保證它們最終會完成同步。
低延遲系統通常會採用 eventual consistency，因為它消除了 write operation 期間耗時的跨 region 同步 coordination。
在 eventual consistency 下，local region 的 write 可以在與其他 region 同步之前立即回傳成功，從而大幅降低 latency。

sections.title: 本期推薦
sections.summary: 這份精選推薦包含探討 infrastructure、軟體設計、web performance 以及 database scalability 的技術文章。重點主題包括透過互動式模擬理解 Kubernetes probe，以及探索 3000、8080 和 Vite 的 5173 等預設開發 port 的歷史由來。在工程實踐方面，文章深入分析了 React hydration mismatch 的效能成本、Go 語言中 Gin 的架構，以及讓 claude.ai 提速三倍的 Claude 最佳化技巧。最後，本期精選也介紹了大型 code diff 的渲染策略，以及 Etsy 如何將 425+ TB 的 sharded MySQL 資料庫遷移至 Vitess。

server 端與 client 端 rendering 之間的 React hydration mismatch 可能會觸發完整的 DOM 重建，即使視覺差異難以察覺，也會導致 Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) 延遲數秒。
Claude 團隊透過將可重現的指標整合至 CI，在兩週內使用 Claude 協助將 core claude.ai workflow 加速約 3 倍。
要流暢地 rendering 大型 code diff，需要同時管理 memory、layout 計算與 DOM node 數量，而不僅僅是將 DOM virtualization。
Etsy 透過將超過 425 TB 的 sharded MySQL 遷移至 Vitess，解決了其舊有 sharded database index 中的 single-point-of-failure 問題。

items.title: How Work is Organized Inside a GPU

sections.title: Everyone is sleeping on this new JSON extraction model!
sections.summary: Datalab has introduced Lift, an open-weights 9B parameter model that extracts structured JSON directly from documents and images in a single step. The model eliminates traditional multi-stage pipelines that combine OCR, LLM inference, and JSON repair code. Lift processes multi-page documents in a single pass according to a user-provided JSON schema and returns null for missing values to avoid hallucinations. Benchmarks report 90.2% field accuracy over 11,000 fields, rivaling Gemini Flash 3.5 at triple the speed, and the model can be self-hosted with vLLM or Hugging Face.
takeaways: Lift combines OCR, LLM inference, and JSON repair into a single open-weights model.
The 9B parameter model attains 90.2% field accuracy across 11,000 benchmarked fields.
Lift nearly matches Gemini Flash 3.5 performance while operating at three times the speed.
The model handles documents spanning multiple pages in a single pass.
Lift is engineered to mitigate hallucinations by returning null when data is missing.
The model can be self-hosted using vLLM or Hugging Face.

sections.title: How work is organized inside a GPU
sections.summary: A GPU executes large computational workloads by subdividing them into a hierarchical execution model consisting of grids, thread blocks, warps, and threads. When a kernel function is invoked, it instantiates a grid divided into blocks, which are independently mapped onto Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs). Within each SM, threads are bundled into groups of 32 known as warps, which execute the same instruction simultaneously across different data values. The SM achieves high throughput and hides memory access latency by rapidly switching between ready resident warps whenever executing warps encounter stalls.
takeaways: A GPU kernel launch instantiates a grid of execution, which is broken down into independently scheduled thread blocks.
Thread blocks reside on Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), sharing execution state and fast shared memory.
The hardware groups 32 threads into a warp, which serves as the fundamental unit of execution scheduled on an SM.
Branch divergence within a warp forces serialized execution paths, temporarily disabling inactive threads and degrading performance.
GPUs hide memory latency through warp scheduling rather than latency reduction, swapping stalled warps for ready ones at minimal cost.
Workloads must provide sufficient blocks and resident warps to saturate SM compute resources and enable effective latency hiding.

sections.title: Jev-style scoring, LLM decoding & structured output
sections.summary: Many LLM use cases like routing and classification involve choosing among a known set of valid answers rather than generating open-ended text. Standard LLM decoding relies on autoregressive token generation that produces text requiring downstream parsing, whereas structured output masks illegal tokens to enforce a predictable schema like JSON while still decoding token-by-token. In contrast, Jev-style scoring bypasses sequence decoding altogether by directly scoring predefined candidate labels and outputting their probability distribution. The optimal approach depends on whether a system requires open-ended text, schema-constrained unknown values, or direct scoring over known choices.
takeaways: Standard LLM decoding generates text token-by-token, requiring post-processing and parsing to extract discrete decisions.
Structured output uses schemas or grammars to mask invalid tokens at each generation step, but still incurs full token-by-token decoding.
Structured output is most appropriate when target values are not known in advance but need structured shapes like JSON or tool calls.
Jev-style scoring evaluates predefined candidate answers directly, returning probabilities without decoding sentences or JSON objects.
Jev-style scoring is optimized for fixed-choice classification, routing, policy checks, and ranking.

sections.title: GPU 內部的工作組織與排程機制
sections.summary: GPU 透過將龐大的運算 workloads 細分為由 grids、thread blocks、warps 與 threads 組成的階層式 execution model 來執行。當一個 kernel 函式被呼叫時，它會實例化一個劃分為多個 block 的 grid，這些 block 會被獨立映射至 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs)。在每個 SM 內部，threads 會以 32 個為一組打包為 warp，在不同的資料值上同時執行相同的指令。每當執行中的 warps 遇到 stall 時，SM 會透過在就緒的 resident warps 之間快速切換，以實現高 throughput 並隱藏 memory access latency。
takeaways: 一次 GPU kernel launch 會實例化一個 execution grid，該 grid 會被分解為可獨立排程的 thread blocks。
Thread blocks 駐留在 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) 上，共享 execution state 與高速 shared memory。
硬體將 32 個 threads 組成一個 warp，作為 SM 上排程的基本執行單位。
Warp 內的 branch divergence 會迫使執行路徑序列化（serialized），暫時停用非活躍的 threads 並導致效能下降。
GPU 是透過 warp scheduling 而非降低 latency 來隱藏 memory latency，以極低的成本將 stalled warps 置換為 ready warps。
Workloads 必須提供足夠的 blocks 與 resident warps，以充分填滿 SM 的運算資源並實現有效的 latency hiding。

sections.title: Jev-style scoring、LLM decoding 與 structured output
sections.summary: 許多 LLM 使用場景（如 routing 與 classification）涉及在已知的一組有效答案中進行選擇，而非生成開放式文本。標準的 LLM decoding 仰賴 autoregressive token 生成，產生的文本需要下游解析；而 structured output 則透過遮罩非法 token 來強制遵循如 JSON 等可預測的 schema，但仍需逐 token 進行解碼。相較之下，Jev-style scoring 完全繞過 sequence decoding，直接對預先定義的候選標籤進行評分並輸出其機率分佈。最佳做法取決於系統需要的是開放式文本、受 schema 約束的未知數值，還是對已知選項進行直接評分。
takeaways: 標準 LLM decoding 逐 token 生成文本，需要透過後處理與解析來擷取離散的決策。
Structured output 在每個生成步驟中使用 schema 或 grammar 來遮罩無效的 token，但仍需要完整的逐 token 解碼過程。
當目標值無法事先得知，但需要像 JSON 或 tool calls 這樣的結構化格式時，structured output 最為合適。
Jev-style scoring 直接評估預先定義的候選答案，無需解碼句子或 JSON 物件即可回傳機率。
Jev-style scoring 專為固定選項的 classification、routing、policy checks 與 ranking 進行了最佳化。

items.title: EP228: How SSH Works

sections.title: How SSH Works
sections.summary: Secure Shell (SSH) provides secure access to a remote machine across an unsecured network starting with a TCP connection. The client and server negotiate cryptographic algorithms and independently compute matching session keys that are never transmitted over the wire. Host verification occurs when the client checks the server's public key against the known_hosts file. Authentication finishes when the server verifies a digital signature generated by the client's private key against the authorized_keys file.
takeaways: SSH begins by establishing a TCP connection between the SSH client and the SSH server.
Both machines negotiate cryptographic algorithms and run a key exchange protocol to independently derive session keys.
Session keys are never transmitted over the network wire.
The SSH server's public host key is verified against the client's known_hosts file.
Client authentication utilizes public-key cryptography verified against the server's authorized_keys file while the private key never leaves the client machine.

sections.title: Top 6 Techniques to Make Your AI System Efficient
sections.summary: Serving large language models at scale is computationally expensive, requiring targeted techniques to optimize efficiency and reduce latency. Six prominent methods include streaming, quantization, continuous batching, prefix caching, paged KV cache, and speculative decoding. Adopting these techniques decreases memory footprint, reduces GPU idle time, and improves both actual and user-perceived response times.
takeaways: Streaming sends tokens immediately upon generation, reducing perceived latency to time-to-first-token.
Quantization converts model weights to lower-precision formats like FP8 to reduce memory consumption and hosting costs.
Continuous batching dynamically fills open slots with incoming requests, minimizing GPU idle time.
Prefix caching avoids redundant computation by reusing cached calculations for recognized prompt prefixes.
Paged KV cache allocates memory dynamically in fixed-size blocks rather than reserving contiguous chunks upfront.
Speculative decoding uses a smaller speculator model to propose tokens that the primary model verifies in a single pass.

sections.title: The Anatomy of an AI Agent
sections.summary: An AI agent fundamentally functions as an iterative while-loop governed by an underlying LLM that makes decisions, executes actions, and evaluates results until a task is completed. Key architectural components include the LLM as the decision-making brain, planning strategies to decompose complex goals, and tool integrations to interact with the environment. Additionally, agents rely on partitioned short-term and long-term memory systems to maintain context over time. System guardrails such as sandboxing and token limits are vital to regulate autonomous execution and prevent failure.
takeaways: An AI agent operates as an iterative while-loop driven by an LLM deciding actions rather than merely generating text.
Planning mechanisms such as Chain of Thought, Tree of Thoughts, and Reflexion decompose complex goals into discrete actions.
Tools extend agent capabilities through external functions like APIs, web search, code execution, and browsers, often standardized via MCP.
Agent memory is divided into short-term context windows and long-term storage including vector stores, files, and knowledge bases.
Guardrails such as human checks, sandboxing, and token limits are necessary to contain autonomous behavior.

sections.title: How do you know if your AI app actually works?
sections.summary: Evaluating AI applications effectively follows a defined three-step recipe rather than an ambiguous process. First, teams select a specific task or capability to evaluate, such as safety, math, grounding, or retrieval. Second, they collect evaluation data pairing inputs with expected answers or behaviors. Third, developers build a grading system combining code-based graders for deterministic checks, model-based graders for scale, and human graders for nuanced edge cases.
takeaways: A robust AI evaluation framework consists of three steps: selecting a task, collecting evaluation data, and developing a grader.
Evaluation datasets must pair input prompts with ground truth answers or expected behaviors, such as pairing unsafe prompts with refusals.
Code-based graders, such as unit tests, are best suited for cheap checks on outputs with clear correct answers.
Model-based graders (LLM-as-judge) handle subjective dimensions such as safety at scale.
Human graders are reserved for edge cases and high-nuance scenarios where throughput is secondary.
Production AI evaluation pipelines typically combine code-based, model-based, and human graders.

兩台機器會協商密碼演算法，並執行 key exchange protocol 以各自獨立衍生出 session keys。
Session keys 絕不會在網路線路上傳輸。
SSH server 的 public host key 會對照 client 的 known_hosts 檔案進行驗證。
Client authentication 利用 public-key cryptography，並對照 server 的 authorized_keys 檔案進行驗證，而 private key 則永遠不會離開 client 端機器。

sections.title: 讓你的 AI 系統高效運作的 6 大關鍵技術

Quantization 將 model weights 轉換為 FP8 等較低精度的格式，以降低記憶體消耗與 hosting 成本。
Continuous batching 會動態利用傳入的 requests 填補空缺的 slots，將 GPU idle time 降至最低。
Prefix caching 透過重用已識別 prompt prefixes 的快取計算結果，避免重複運算。
Paged KV cache 以固定大小的 blocks 動態分配記憶體，而不是預先保留連續的記憶體區塊。

Agent memory 分為短期 context windows 以及包含 vector stores、files 與 knowledge bases 的長期儲存空間。

sections.title: 你如何知道自己的 AI app 是否真的能正常運作？
sections.summary: 有效評估 AI applications 遵循一套明確的三步驟方法，而非模糊不清的流程。首先，團隊選擇要評估的特定 task 或能力，例如 safety、math、grounding 或 retrieval。其次，他們收集 evaluation data，將 inputs 與預期的 answers 或 behaviors 進行配對。第三，開發者建立一個 grading 系統，結合用於確定性檢查的 code-based graders、用於大規模評估的 model-based graders，以及用於處理細微 edge cases 的 human graders。
takeaways: 一個穩健的 AI evaluation framework 包含三個步驟：選擇 task、收集 evaluation data 以及開發 grader。

Code-based graders（例如 unit tests）最適合用於對具有明確正確答案的 outputs 進行低成本的檢查。
Model-based graders（LLM-as-judge）能在大規模環境下處理如 safety 等主觀維度的評估。
Human graders 則保留用於 throughput 為次要考量的 edge cases 和高度細微（high-nuance）的情境。
Production AI evaluation pipelines 通常會結合 code-based、model-based 與 human graders。

items.title:
Inside-Out AI: Rebuilding Airbnb Behind the Scenes and Across the Guest
 Experience

sections.title: After leading Meta’s Llama models, Ahmad Al-Dahle is now transforming Airbnb with AI — from how its teams develop products to how it serves guests.
sections.summary: Former Meta head of generative AI Ahmad Al-Dahle joined Airbnb as Chief Technology Officer in January to steer its transformation into an AI-native company. Having previously led the development and release of the open-source Llama models from 2023 to 2025, Al-Dahle is implementing an inside-out AI strategy at Airbnb. This approach focuses on using AI internally to accelerate product development while deploying generative capabilities externally to transform guest experiences. Al-Dahle stated that deploying models at scale in production is the next major frontier in artificial intelligence.
takeaways: Ahmad Al-Dahle joined Airbnb as CTO in January to lead its transition into an AI-native company.
Al-Dahle was previously head of generative AI at Meta, where he led the launch of the open-source Llama models from 2023 to 2025.
Airbnb is pursuing an inside-out AI strategy, accelerating internal product development to subsequently improve guest experiences.
Al-Dahle views deploying generative models at scale in production to create user value as the next significant AI challenge.

sections.title: Jumping to prototypes, code is the artifact
sections.summary: Airbnb has transitioned toward becoming an AI-native organization by overhauling its software engineering workflows. Currently, 60% of Airbnb's code is AI-authored, contributing to an 80% year-over-year increase in shipped features and a 1.6x rise in pull-request throughput per engineer. Rather than relying on phased handoffs across product requirements and design tools, product, design, and engineering teams now collaborate directly via prototypes. As a result, working code and prototypes have replaced traditional documentation as the primary artifacts of development.
takeaways: Sixty percent of Airbnb's code is currently AI-authored.
Airbnb has increased the number of shipped features and improvements by nearly 80% year over year.
Average engineer pull-request throughput at Airbnb has grown by approximately 1.6x.
Airbnb replaced traditional handoffs across PRDs and design with direct prototype-driven workflows.
The company shifted from producing intermediate specification artifacts to treating code itself as the primary artifact.

sections.title: AI resolves roughly half of support tickets
sections.summary: Airbnb introduced AI into customer support as its first user-facing AI deployment, identifying it as a particularly challenging area due to high stakes. Currently, roughly half of the company's support tickets are resolved entirely by AI agents, matching Q2 results showing nearly 45% automation. The deployment strategy heavily relies on generating synthetic data to test the system before production, while deliberately routing sensitive matters like safety to human staff.
takeaways: Customer support was Airbnb's first user-facing application of AI.
Approximately 45% to 50% of Airbnb's customer support tickets are now resolved completely by AI.
Airbnb relies on batteries of synthetic data to rigorously test models and agents before deploying to production.
Airbnb intentionally avoids using AI agents for critical topics such as safety issues, delegating them to human personnel.

sections.title: Everest, Airbnb’s AI context graph
sections.summary: Airbnb built an internal organizational context graph named Everest to accelerate product engineering across its codebase. Leveraging LLMs, embeddings, and AI-based retrieval, the tool captures learnings and context to empower generalist developers to work on specialized code. Demonstrating its impact, development of Airbnb's airport pickup service was completed in six weeks by reusing learnings from an earlier grocery delivery project that had taken eight to nine months.
takeaways: Everest is Airbnb's internal context graph that leverages LLMs, embeddings, and AI-based retrieval to query and build code context.
Using Everest allowed Airbnb to shorten development time for its airport pickup service to six weeks, compared to eight to nine months for grocery delivery.
The context graph allows generalist engineers to work across specialist areas of Airbnb's codebase.
Both grocery delivery and airport pickups are Airbnb Services projects involving API integrations with external partners.
CEO Brian Chesky highlighted both products at Airbnb's 2026 Summer Release event.

sections.title: Choosing which models to use and customizing open models
sections.summary: Airbnb operates as a multi-model company, deploying over 10 customized models in production alongside top frontier models. The company evaluates models on a Pareto frontier of cost, performance, and latency tailored to individual use cases through production-sampled evals. For high-stakes, latency-tolerant tasks like coding, Airbnb relies on the strongest frontier models to prevent costly errors, whereas for latency-sensitive, high-scale tasks like search, it deploys small open models post-trained to outperform frontier alternatives.
takeaways: Airbnb describes itself as a multi-model company and deploys at least 10 customized models in production.
Airbnb conducts most of its own post-training and reinforcement learning on open models.
Model evaluation is conducted per use case along a Pareto frontier balancing cost, performance, and latency.
Production search queries and customer support edge cases are sampled directly from production for targeted evals.
Coding tasks are assigned to the strongest frontier models because defects are expensive despite latency tolerance.
Small, specialized models are post-trained for high-scale, latency-sensitive tasks like search, sometimes outperforming frontier models.

sections.title: Async agents: the next big shift
sections.summary: Airbnb has developed an internal agent named AirChat that integrates organizational context via Model Context Protocol (MCP). The company is expanding into asynchronous agents that run in containers triggered by events, such as Grafana monitoring alerts. These event-driven agents automate initial on-call duties by diagnosing issues, dismissing flaky alerts, or submitting pull requests for human engineers to review. Moving forward, Airbnb plans to deploy fleets of asynchronous agents across its marketplace platform to handle software defects, fraud detection, trust violations, and platform quality.
takeaways: Airbnb developed an internal agent named AirChat containing MCP organizational context.
Airbnb is transitioning toward asynchronous, containerized agents activated by monitoring events to automate on-call triage.
Async agents can independently close flaky alerts or open pull requests for human engineers to review.
Similar software factory approaches with teams of agents are already in use by open-source projects like Vercel's AI SDK, Astro, Flue, and tldraw.
Airbnb aims to scale asynchronous agents across its marketplace to handle fraud, trust violations, platform quality, and code defects.

sections.title: Maintaining the craft of software engineering
sections.summary: Al-Dahle argues that becoming an AI-native organization requires structuring teams around objectives and missions rather than feature development. A primary concern during this shift is ensuring junior engineers continue developing technical judgment and craft despite AI automation. To address this, he insists that every engineer be capable of explaining their work, even when pull requests are AI-generated.
takeaways: Organizing teams around outcomes and missions rather than feature development is crucial for AI-native companies.
AI automation poses a risk to junior engineers' development of architectural judgment and foundational engineering craft.
Senior engineering judgment is typically built through years of shipping production software and learning from past failures.
Requiring engineers to explain all submitted code, even if generated by AI, helps preserve standards in interface design, architecture, and testing.

sections.title: 在領導 Meta 的 Llama 模型之後，Ahmad Al-Dahle 現正透過 AI 改造 Airbnb——從其團隊如何開發產品，到如何服務房客。
sections.summary: 前 Meta generative AI 主管 Ahmad Al-Dahle 於 1 月加入 Airbnb 擔任 Chief Technology Officer，以引領其轉型為 AI-native 企業。Al-Dahle 先前曾於 2023 至 2025 年間主導開源 Llama 模型的開發與釋出，如今他在 Airbnb 推行 inside-out 的 AI 策略。該方法聚焦於內部利用 AI 加速產品開發，同時在外部部署 generative 功能以翻轉房客體驗。Al-Dahle 表示，在 production 環境中大規模部署模型是 artificial intelligence 的下一個重要前沿。
takeaways: Ahmad Al-Dahle 於 1 月加入 Airbnb 擔任 CTO，領導其轉型為 AI-native 企業。
Al-Dahle 先前為 Meta 的 generative AI 主管，曾於 2023 至 2025 年間主導開源 Llama 模型的推出。
Airbnb 正推行 inside-out 的 AI 策略，透過加速內部產品開發來進一步改善房客體驗。
Al-Dahle 認為在 production 環境中大規模部署 generative models 以創造使用者價值，是下一個重大的 AI 挑戰。

sections.title: 直接切入 prototypes，code 即是 artifact
sections.summary: Airbnb 透過全面革新其 software engineering 工作流程，邁向成為 AI-native 組織。目前 Airbnb 有 60% 的 code 為 AI-authored，促使 shipped features 年增 80%，且每位工程師的 pull-request throughput 提升了 1.6 倍。產品、設計與工程團隊不再依賴跨產品需求與設計工具的分階段交接（phased handoffs），而是直接透過 prototypes 進行協作。因此，可運作的 code 與 prototypes 已取代傳統 documentation，成為開發的核心 artifacts。
takeaways: 目前 Airbnb 有 60% 的 code 為 AI-authored。
Airbnb 的 shipped features 與改進項目數量相較去年同期增加了近 80%。
Airbnb 工程師的平均 pull-request 吞吐量成長了約 1.6 倍。
Airbnb 以直接由 prototype 驅動的工作流程，取代了跨 PRD 與 design 的傳統 handoff。
該公司從產出中間規格 artifact，轉變為將 code 本身視為主要的 artifact。

sections.title: AI 解決了約半數的 support ticket
sections.summary: Airbnb 將 AI 導入 customer support 作為其首個面對使用者的 AI deployment，並因其 high stakes 而認定這是一個特別具挑戰性的領域。目前，該公司約有一半的 support ticket 完全由 AI agent 解決，符合第二季顯示近 45% 自動化的結果。其 deployment 策略高度仰賴生成 synthetic data 在上 production 前測試系統，同時刻意將安全等敏感問題 route 給真人處理。
takeaways: Customer support 是 Airbnb 第一個面對使用者的 AI 應用。
Airbnb 目前約有 45% 到 50% 的 customer support ticket 完全由 AI 解決。
Airbnb 仰賴大量 synthetic data，在 deploy 到 production 前對 model 與 agent 進行嚴格測試。
Airbnb 刻意避免在安全問題等關鍵主題上使用 AI agent，而是交由真人處理。

sections.title: Everest，Airbnb 的 AI context graph
sections.summary: Airbnb 構建了一個名為 Everest 的內部組織 context graph，以加速跨 codebase 的 product engineering。該工具結合 LLM、embedding 與基於 AI 的 retrieval，擷取經驗與 context，讓 generalist 開發者能夠處理 specialized code。展現其影響力的是，Airbnb 的機場接送服務開發僅花費六週便完成，原因是復用了先前耗時八到九個月的雜貨配送專案所累積的經驗。
takeaways: Everest 是 Airbnb 的內部 context graph，利用 LLM、embedding 和基於 AI 的 retrieval 來 query 並建立 code context。
使用 Everest 讓 Airbnb 將機場接送服務的開發時間縮短至六週，而相較之下雜貨配送則耗時八至九個月。
此 context graph 讓 generalist 工程師能夠跨足 Airbnb codebase 的 specialist 領域。
雜貨配送與機場接送皆為 Airbnb Services 專案，涉及與外部合作夥伴的 API integration。
CEO Brian Chesky 在 Airbnb 的 2026 Summer Release 活動中重點介紹了這兩項產品。

sections.title: 選擇要使用的 model 並客製化 open model
sections.summary: Airbnb 以 multi-model 公司模式運作，在 production 環境中部署了 10 多個客製化 model 以及頂尖的 frontier model。該公司透過取樣自 production 的 eval，針對個別 use case 在 cost、performance 和 latency 的 Pareto frontier 上評估 model。對於像 coding 這類 high-stakes、對 latency 容忍度高的任務，Airbnb 仰賴最強大的 frontier model 以防止代價高昂的錯誤；而對於像 search 這類對 latency 敏感且大規模的任務，則部署經過 post-training、表現超越 frontier 替代方案的小型 open model。
takeaways: Airbnb 自稱是一家 multi-model 公司，並在 production 中部署了至少 10 個客製化 model。
Airbnb 在 open model 上自行進行大部分的 post-training 與 reinforcement learning。
Model evaluation 是依據每個 use case，沿著平衡 cost、performance 與 latency 的 Pareto frontier 進行。
Production 搜尋 query 與 customer support 的 edge case 會直接從 production 取樣，用於針對性的 eval。
Coding 任務被分配給最強大的 frontier model，因為儘管對 latency 有容忍度，但 defect 的代價十分高昂。
針對像 search 這類大規模、對 latency 敏感的任務，小型 specialized model 經過 post-training 後，有時表現會超越 frontier model。

sections.title: Async agent：下一波重大轉變
sections.summary: Airbnb 開發了一個名為 AirChat 的內部 agent，透過 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 整合組織上下文資訊。該公司正進一步拓展至由事件（例如 Grafana 監控告警）觸發、在 container 中運行的非同步 agents。這些事件驅動的 agents 透過診斷問題、忽略 flaky alerts 或提交 pull requests 供人類工程師審查，來自動化初期的 on-call 職責。展望未來，Airbnb 計劃在其 marketplace 平台上部署大量非同步 agents，以處理軟體缺陷、詐欺偵測、信任違規與平台品質問題。
takeaways: Airbnb 開發了一個名為 AirChat 的內部 agent，其中包含 MCP 組織上下文資訊。
Airbnb 正轉向由監控事件啟動的非同步、container 化 agents，以實現 on-call 分流（triage）的自動化。
非同步 agents 能獨立關閉 flaky alerts，或建立 pull requests 供人類工程師審查。
類似這種採用 agent 團隊的軟體工廠模式，已被 Vercel 的 AI SDK、Astro、Flue 和 tldraw 等開源專案所採用。
Airbnb 旨在將非同步 agents 擴展至其整個 marketplace，以處理詐欺、信任違規、平台品質以及程式碼缺陷。

sections.title: 維護軟體工程的工藝精神
sections.summary: Al-Dahle 主張，要成為一個 AI-native 組織，團隊架構必須圍繞目標與使命建立，而非單純的功能開發。在此轉型過程中的一項主要隱憂，是即便有 AI 自動化，仍須確保 junior 工程師能持續培養技術判斷力與工程工藝。為了因應這一點，他堅持每位工程師都必須能解釋自己的工作內容，即便 pull requests 是由 AI 生成的也是如此。
takeaways: 圍繞成果與使命而非功能開發來組織團隊，對於 AI-native 公司來說至關重要。
AI 自動化對 junior 工程師在架構判斷力與基礎工程工藝的培養上構成了風險。
資深工程師的判斷力通常是透過多年交付 production 軟體並從過往失敗中學習而累積建立的。
要求工程師解釋所有提交的程式碼（即使是由 AI 生成），有助於維持介面設計、架構和測試的標準。

items.title: We Should Be Encouraged By AI’s Cybersecurity Abilities

sections.title: We Should Be Encouraged By AI’s Cybersecurity Abilities
sections.summary: Anthropic's recent evaluation indicates that the open-weight model GLM-5.3 achieves cybersecurity exploitation capabilities approaching those of leading closed models like Claude's Mythos. The cost of identifying vulnerabilities is decreasing sharply, as demonstrated by GLM-5.3 finding a Google Chrome vulnerability for only $20.40 in compute tokens. Analogous to historical advances in aviation safety, managing AI cyber risk is fundamentally an engineering challenge centered on containment, sandboxing, and monitoring. Because defenders naturally possess deeper system context than attackers, rapid engineering iterations are poised to give cyberdefenders a decisive long-term advantage.
takeaways: Anthropic found open-weight model GLM-5.3 succeeded in 12% of vulnerability exploit attempts on a subset of ExploitBench, close to Mythos' 14%.
Using GLM-5.3-Flash tokens totaling $20.40 was sufficient to locate a recently disclosed security vulnerability in Google Chrome.
Weakening guardrails on frontier open-weight models could further increase their offensive and defensive utility.
Incidents like the OpenAI-Hugging Face hack are driving the implementation of improved sandboxing and agent monitoring architectures.
Andrew, Rohit Prsad, and Devika Verma are developing OpenWorker, an agent harness for security workflows that integrates Nvidia's safety framework.

The program consists of four courses covering data generation, ingestion, storage, transformation, and serving.
Coursework includes building batch and streaming pipelines using AWS and open-source tools.
The course instructor is Joe Reis, co-author of Fundamentals of Data Engineering.

sections.title: An Unexpected Open Weights Leader
sections.summary: Xiaomi released open-weights models led by MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL and MiMo-V2.6-Flash, achieving top open-weights scores on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index and the Vals Index at lower per-task costs than proprietary alternatives. The models rely on a mixture-of-experts architecture and a unified reinforcement learning stage powered by Group Relative Policy Optimization. To prevent models from learning sloppy coding habits, Xiaomi implemented secondary AI grader models and checklists to reward code quality and maintainability rather than simple test completion. Alongside the models and weights under an MIT license, Xiaomi open-sourced over 7,000 reinforcement learning task environments and associated training code.
takeaways: MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL (1.02T parameters, 42B active) ranked first among open-weights models on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index v4.3.2 with a score of 46.
MiMo-V2.6-Flash (309B parameters, 15B active) and MiMo-V2.6-Pro topped open-weights models on the Vals Index with 59.58 percent and 59.47 percent accuracy, respectively.
Xiaomi open-sourced over 7,000 reinforcement learning task environments and training code under an MIT license.
The models' reinforcement learning stage relied on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) combined with AI-assisted code-quality grading to discourage reward hacking and poorly maintainable code.
Xiaomi disclosed the reinforcement learning training costs as $2.6 million for MiMo-V2.6-Pro and $0.9 million for MiMo-V2.6-Flash.
Anthropic alleged that Xiaomi improperly generated over 400,000 training exchanges by routing user queries to Claude using OpenClaw and OpenCode.

sections.title: Voice, Video, and Reasoning in One
sections.summary: Google has launched Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, two low-latency speech-to-speech models based on Gemini 3 Pro designed for real-time voice agents. Gemini 3.8 Live is optimized for cost and scale, whereas 3.8 Live Extended Thinking handles high-complexity tasks with simultaneous reasoning. Unlike traditional cascaded speech-text-speech pipelines, these models process native audio and support multimodal image and video inputs alongside background tool execution. Evaluations by Artificial Analysis show top-tier performance for both models, with 3.8 Live offering low operating costs and strong user preference in conversational dynamics.
takeaways: Google released Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, both based on Gemini 3 Pro with a knowledge cutoff of January 2025.
Gemini 3.8 Live supports 97 languages, multimodal image/video input, and background API/tool execution during dialogue.
Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking ranked first in Artificial Analysis's Speech to Speech Index (82.6%) and Tau Voice benchmark (68.6%).
Gemini 3.8 Live is the cheapest model in the Speech to Speech Index at $0.84 per hour of input audio, compared to $3.50 per hour for 3.8 Live Extended Thinking.
All audio generated by Google's AI products using these models is watermarked using SynthID.
The models bypass traditional speech-to-text-to-speech pipelines to reduce latency and allow simultaneous listening and speaking.

sections.title: Learn More About AI With Data Points!
sections.summary: Data Points is an artificial intelligence newsletter published twice weekly, delivering six brief news summaries per edition. The publication monitors and explains rapid developments across the AI industry. A recent edition reported on OpenAI halting model training along with major announcements unveiled at OpenAI's DevDay.
takeaways: Data Points is published twice a week with six concise news stories per issue.
OpenAI halted model training as reported in a recent newsletter edition.
The newsletter highlighted the most significant announcements from OpenAI's DevDay.

sections.title: DeepSeek’s Flash Leapfrogs Pro Again
sections.summary: DeepSeek has released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, an open-weights model featuring a redesigned architecture engineered to drastically reduce key-value cache memory and context serving costs. The 552-billion parameter backbone architecture uses cross-layer cache sharing inspired by YOCO and 4-bit quantization, shrinking cache requirements to 890 bytes per token. In addition to offering up to 1-million-token context windows and multimodal image support, the model achieves high inference speeds of 225.6 tokens per second. Independent evaluations show it outperforming its predecessor and surpassing leading frontier models on agent-based workflows such as AutomationBench-AA.
takeaways: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash contains 552 billion backbone parameters and a 196 billion parameter memory module, activating 8 billion tokens during prefill and 16 billion during decoding.
The model reduces key-value cache size to 890 bytes per token—four times smaller than DeepSeek-V4-Flash and 437 times smaller than DeepSeek-V1—via 4-bit quantization and cross-layer cache reuse.
Only 4 of the model's 40 layers compute a full input cache, using an architecture influenced by Microsoft and Tsinghua University's YOCO design.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash supports up to 1 million input tokens with vision capabilities, generating output at 225.6 tokens per second under an MIT license.
On AutomationBench-AA, the model scored 68.9 percent at max reasoning, outscoring competing models including GPT-6 Astra and Grok 4.6.

sections.title: Agents That Can Check Their Own Work Piece by Piece
sections.summary: Researchers at the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence developed AREX, a research agent framework designed to iteratively hone answers through evidence collection, reflection, and targeted follow-up queries. Rather than evaluating candidate responses with a binary pass/fail decision, AREX inspects tentative answers requirement by requirement to retain validated information and pinpoint missing or conflicting evidence. The developers fine-tuned Qwen3.5 models using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, focusing the training signals on key decision points flagged by heuristic rules. Evaluated across multiple agentic benchmarks including BrowseComp and WideSearch-en, the fine-tuned AREX systems consistently outperformed larger unfine-tuned models.
takeaways: AREX verifies answers requirement by requirement, retaining confirmed facts and generating targeted follow-up searches for unresolved criteria.
The agent periodically compresses research traces into a brief state recording verified facts, discarded hypotheses, unresolved points, and future plans.
Training utilized heuristic rules to concentrate supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning signals specifically on high-value decision points.
AREX with fine-tuned Qwen3.5-122B-A10B achieved 82.5 percent accuracy on BrowseComp and 82.0 percent F1 on WideSearch-en.
Fine-tuning allowed the compact Qwen3.5-4B to outperform the unfine-tuned Qwen3.5-35B across five out of six benchmarks.

MiMo-V2.6-Flash（309B parameters，15B active）與 MiMo-V2.6-Pro 在 Vals Index 上分別以 59.58% 和 59.47% 的 accuracy 稱霸 open-weights models。
Xiaomi 在 MIT license 下開源了 7,000 多個 reinforcement learning task environments 與 training code。
該模型的 reinforcement learning 階段仰賴 Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)，並結合 AI 輔助的 code-quality grading，以抑制 reward hacking 並避免產生難以維護的程式碼。
Xiaomi 公布其 reinforcement learning 的 training costs：MiMo-V2.6-Pro 為 $2.6 million，MiMo-V2.6-Flash 為 $0.9 million。
Anthropic 指控 Xiaomi 透過 OpenClaw 與 OpenCode 將使用者 queries 導向 Claude，不當生成了超過 400,000 次 training exchanges。

sections.title: 語音、視訊與 Reasoning 集於一體
sections.summary: Google 推出了 Gemini 3.8 Live 與 Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking，這是兩款基於 Gemini 3 Pro 的 low-latency speech-to-speech 模型，專為即時 voice agents 設計。Gemini 3.8 Live 針對成本與規模進行了最佳化，而 3.8 Live Extended Thinking 則能透過同步 reasoning 處理高複雜度任務。不同於傳統級聯式（cascaded）的 speech-text-speech pipelines，這些模型原生處理 audio，並在背景 tool execution 的同時支援多模態 image 與 video 輸入。Artificial Analysis 的評測顯示兩款模型均具備頂尖效能，其中 3.8 Live 提供極低的營運成本，且在對話動態（conversational dynamics）上展現出強大的使用者偏好。
takeaways: Google 發布了 Gemini 3.8 Live 與 Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking，兩者皆基於 Gemini 3 Pro，knowledge cutoff 為 2025 年 1 月。
Gemini 3.8 Live 支援 97 種語言、多模態 image/video 輸入，以及在對話過程中的背景 API/tool execution。
Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking 在 Artificial Analysis 的 Speech to Speech Index（82.6%）與 Tau Voice benchmark（68.6%）中均名列第一。
Gemini 3.8 Live 是 Speech to Speech Index 中成本最低的模型，每小時 input audio 僅需 $0.84，相較之下 3.8 Live Extended Thinking 為每小時 $3.50。
Google AI 產品使用這些模型所生成的所有 audio，皆會使用 SynthID 加上浮水印。
這些模型繞過了傳統的 speech-to-text-to-speech pipelines，以降低 latency 並實現同時聆聽與說話。

sections.title: 透過 Data Points 掌握更多 AI 新知！
sections.summary: Data Points 是一份每週發行兩次的 AI 電子報，每期提供六則精簡的新聞摘要。該刊物持續追蹤並解析 AI 產業的快速進展。最近一期報導了 OpenAI 暫停 model training，以及在 OpenAI DevDay 上揭曉的重大消息。
takeaways: Data Points 每週出刊兩次，每期收錄六則簡潔的新聞報導。
正如最新一期電子報所報導，OpenAI 暫停了 model training。
該電子報重點報導了 OpenAI DevDay 上最具代表性的重大發表。

sections.title: DeepSeek 的 Flash 再次超車 Pro
sections.summary: DeepSeek 發布了 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash，這是一款 open-weights 模型，採用重新設計的架構，旨在大幅降低 key-value cache 記憶體與 context serving 成本。其 552B 參數的 backbone 架構採用了受 YOCO 啟發的 cross-layer cache sharing 與 4-bit quantization，將每 token 的 cache 需求縮減至 890 bytes。除了提供高達 100 萬 token 的 context windows 與多模態 image 支援外，該模型的 inference 速度更高達每秒 225.6 tokens。獨立評測顯示，其表現超越了前代版本，並在如 AutomationBench-AA 等基於 agent 的 workflow 上領先眾多 frontier models。
takeaways: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 包含 5,520 億（552B）backbone 參數與 1,960 億（196B）參數的 memory module，在 prefill 階段啟用 80 億個 tokens，在 decoding 階段啟用 160 億個 tokens。
該模型透過 4-bit quantization 與 cross-layer cache reuse，將 key-value cache 大小降至每 token 890 bytes——比 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 小 4 倍，比 DeepSeek-V1 小 437 倍。
該模型的 40 個 layers 中僅有 4 個會計算完整的 input cache，採用了受 Microsoft 與清華大學 YOCO 設計啟發的架構。
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 支援高達 100 萬個 input tokens 並具備 vision 能力，在 MIT license 下能以每秒 225.6 tokens 的速度生成 output。
在 AutomationBench-AA 上，該模型在 max reasoning 設定下取得 68.9% 的分數，超越了包括 GPT-6 Astra 和 Grok 4.6 在內的競爭模型。

sections.title: 能逐項自我檢查成果的 Agents
sections.summary: 北京智源人工智能研究院（Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence）的研究人員開發了 AREX，這是一個 research agent framework，旨在透過證據收集、反思（reflection）與針對性的追問來反覆打磨答案。AREX 並非以二元的 pass/fail 決策來評估候選回答，而是逐項（requirement by requirement）檢驗初步答案，以保留已驗證的資訊並精準標記缺失或衝突的證據。開發團隊使用 supervised fine-tuning 與 reinforcement learning 對 Qwen3.5 模型進行微調，將 training signals 聚焦於由 heuristic rules 標記的關鍵決策點上。在包括 BrowseComp 和 WideSearch-en 等多個 agentic benchmarks 的評測中，微調後的 AREX 系統表現持續優於未經微調的大型模型。
takeaways: AREX 逐項檢驗答案，保留已確認的事實，並針對未解決的準則生成目標明確的追蹤搜尋。
該 agent 會定期將 research traces 壓縮為簡短的狀態，記錄已驗證的事實、被摒棄的假說、未解決的疑點以及後續計畫。
訓練過程利用 heuristic rules，將 supervised fine-tuning 與 reinforcement learning 的訊號專門聚焦在高價值的決策點上。
搭載 fine-tuned Qwen3.5-122B-A10B 的 AREX 在 BrowseComp 上達到 82.5% 的 accuracy，並在 WideSearch-en 上取得 82.0% 的 F1。
Fine-tuning 讓輕量級的 Qwen3.5-4B 在六項 benchmark 中的五項超越了未經 fine-tune 的 Qwen3.5-35B。

sections.title: 與 Andrew Ng 一同工作
sections.summary: Andrew Ng 旗下的 AI 組織目前正積極為多個團隊招募各類職缺。開出職缺的單位包括 DeepLearning.AI、AI Fund、Landing AI 以及 LearnVector。本節亦提供電子報 The Batch 的一般聯絡與訂閱管理詳情，該電子報總部位於加州 Mountain View。
takeaways: DeepLearning.AI、AI Fund、Landing AI 以及 LearnVector 目前皆有職缺開放應徵。
讀者可將關於電子報的意見回饋或洽詢寄至 thebatch@deeplearning.ai。
DeepLearning.AI 位於美國加州 Mountain View。

sections.title: Managing observability across a Kubernetes cluster
sections.summary: Observability configuration in Kubernetes functions as a continuous reconciliation challenge due to dynamic pods and nodes. The open-source Dynatrace Operator manages this by declaring and enforcing desired monitoring states via a DynaKube custom resource. It uses mutating webhooks to inject instrumentation into pods and can leverage a CSI driver to cache code modules locally on nodes. The operator can also orchestrate components such as ActiveGate, log monitoring, and the OpenTelemetry Collector.
takeaways: Kubernetes turns observability into a continuous reconciliation problem as pods and nodes change over time.
Dynatrace Operator uses the DynaKube custom resource to declare and maintain desired monitoring state.
Application-monitoring mode relies on a mutating webhook to inject instrumentation into pods without modifying base images.
An optional CSI driver caches and shares code modules across pods on the same node to prevent duplicate downloads.
The operator can manage additional components such as the OpenTelemetry Collector and ActiveGate.

sections.title: MCP App, clearly explained:
sections.summary: Major AI companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Microsoft back MCP Apps, a standard for embedding interactive applications directly inside AI chat interfaces. Unlike standard MCP servers that only return raw data, MCP Apps deliver interactive UI elements such as booking cards and checkout flows while synchronizing state with the underlying model. This evolution marks a transition from traditional SEO and AEO toward in-chat product delivery. The open-source framework Skybridge, maintained by Julien at alpic-ai, enables developers to convert standard React applications into MCP Apps.
takeaways: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Microsoft back MCP Apps as a common standard for running interactive applications inside AI chats.
Companies including Booking.com, Figma, and Canva have already begun adopting MCP Apps.
Unlike basic MCP servers that return data, MCP Apps deliver both data and interactive UI with bidirectional state awareness.
The evolution of product discovery is framed as SEO (search engine discovery), AEO (AI citation), and MCP Apps (interactive product display inside chat).
Skybridge is an open-source framework that converts React applications into MCP Apps.

sections.title: Google Advent of Agents Season 3 is here!
sections.summary: Google Cloud has launched Advent of Agents Season 3, a 31-day instructional series focused on building secure and governed AI agents for production. Each daily tutorial released throughout October addresses practical security and customer questions with runnable code. Key operational topics covered include agent identity, sandboxing, guardrails, evaluations, MCP security, and fleet management.
takeaways: Advent of Agents Season 3 is a free 31-day series organized by Google Cloud.
A hands-on tutorial with runnable code is released each day across October.
The series focuses on production-level AI agent security, governance, and fleet management.
Specific topics covered include agent identity, guardrails, sandboxing, observability, evaluations, MCP security, and cost controls.

sections.title: Building a production agent harness with LangGraph and Jev
sections.summary: Parts 3 and 4 of the Agent Engineering course demonstrate how to build a production agent harness and verification loop using LangChain Middleware, LangGraph, and Jev. Jev functions as a System One model that provides calibrated probabilities for typed decisions instead of generating free-form text. These probabilities are used across the agent workflow for model routing, request classification, tool-risk assessment, and evidence verification. The system combines deterministic logic, Jev's bounded probabilistic judgments, and independent LLM verification to improve control and efficiency without relying entirely on general-purpose LLMs.
takeaways: Jev is a System One model designed to return calibrated probabilities for typed decisions rather than generating open-ended text.
Part 3 focuses on agent harness controls such as PII redaction, retries, hard call limits, permission enforcement, and human approval for write actions.
Part 4 places the agent in an explicit LangGraph loop with structured planning, stuck detection, replanning, and execution budgets.
A three-layer verification system employs deterministic checks for clear failures, Jev for high-confidence accept/reject decisions, and an independent LLM for the uncertain range.
Jev probabilities act as an additional signal within a larger control system rather than replacing deterministic checks, permissions, or human approvals.

sections.title: The LLM scheduling loop, clearly explained:
sections.summary: When an inference request reaches an LLM serving engine, a scheduler manages its lifecycle across iterations rather than passing it directly to the GPU. The scheduler evaluates token limits and remaining KV-cache space before building each execution batch, prioritizing decode tasks before admitting new work. Incoming requests first undergo a prefill phase to compute key-value tensors, after which they transition to autoregressive token generation in the decode phase. Through continuous batching, modern serving engines combine prefill and decode work dynamically, replacing finished requests with waiting ones after every step.
takeaways: The LLM scheduler manages inference requests one iteration at a time based on processing token limits and remaining KV-cache space.
Prefill processes prompt tokens in parallel to construct KV tensors and may chunk long prompts to avoid blocking active generations.
The decode stage generates tokens autoregressively, typically producing one token per active request per model step.
Continuous batching enables serving engines to mix prefill and decode operations in the same GPU batch and adjust batch composition after every step.
Completed requests immediately release their KV-cache blocks, allowing the scheduler to admit new requests from the queue.

sections.summary: 當推論請求到達 LLM serving engine 時，scheduler 會跨 iteration 管理其生命週期，而不是直接將其傳遞給 GPU。scheduler 在建立每個 execution batch 之前會評估 token 限制與剩餘的 KV-cache 空間，在接收新工作之前優先處理 decode 任務。傳入的請求首先會經歷 prefill 階段以計算 key-value tensors，隨後在 decode 階段轉換為 autoregressive token generation。透過 continuous batching，現代 serving engines 動態結合了 prefill 和 decode 工作，在每一步之後將已完成的請求替換為等待中的請求。
takeaways: LLM scheduler 根據處理 token 的限制與剩餘的 KV-cache 空間，一次一個 iteration 地管理推論請求。
Prefill 會平行處理 prompt tokens 以建構 KV tensors，並可能將長 prompt 進行 chunk 切塊處理，以避免阻塞進行中的生成任務。
decode stage 會以 autoregressive 方式生成 token，通常在每個 model step 中為每個 active request 產出一個 token。
Continuous batching 讓 serving engine 能夠在同一個 GPU batch 中混合 prefill 與 decode 操作，並在每個 step 後調整 batch 的組成。
已完成的 request 會立即釋放其 KV-cache block，讓 scheduler 能從 queue 中准入新的 request。

items.title: Why State is the Hardest Thing in Software Design

sections.title: Why State is the Hardest Thing in Software Design
sections.summary: State is the information retained by a system that influences its ongoing functionality, making it an essential component of useful software. Managing state is challenging because systems must preserve accuracy during overlapping requests, server scaling, machine failures, and software deployments. While common software advice suggests designing stateless applications, this practice merely decouples and delegates state to external layers rather than eliminating it. Effective state management requires analyzing why state exists, which components own it, and how failures impact availability.
takeaways: State is defined as information retained by a system that impacts its functionality.
Core difficulties in state management stem from concurrent requests, infrastructure scaling, hardware failures, and software updates.
Advising an application to be stateless means making application servers replaceable by relocating state elsewhere, rather than completely removing state.
Proper system design requires understanding state existence, ownership, and behavior during unavailability.

items.title: Jev for RAG, clearly explained!

sections.title: Agents without memory aren’t agents at all
sections.summary: Large language models are inherently stateless and rely on external systems to retain context across interactions. Agent memory solves this by dividing state into short-term working memory for active sessions and long-term memory for cross-session persistence. Long-term memory is further categorized into semantic, episodic, and procedural types, each governed by specialized storage and retrieval policies rather than model weight updates. Oracle AI Agent Memory implements this structured approach, significantly reducing per-turn token consumption and outperforming flat conversation history in benchmark evaluations.
takeaways: Large language models do not store state in weights across sessions; persistence must be managed externally by the application.
Agent memory operates across two primary scopes: short-term working state for current sessions and long-term state across sessions.
Long-term memory comprises semantic memory for facts, episodic memory for past experiences, and procedural memory for instructions and workflows.
Different memory categories require distinct write and retrieval policies based on persistence needs.
In an 80-turn evaluation, Oracle AI Agent Memory capped inputs at around 1,300 tokens per request, compared to over 13,900 tokens for flat history.
The managed-memory agent outperformed flat history in 48 out of 80 evaluated turns, with 13 losses and 19 ties.

sections.title: Jev for RAG, clearly explained!
sections.summary: Hybrid search often retrieves passages that share terms or semantic similarity without actually providing valid evidence to answer a query. Jev introduces an explicit evaluation stage between retrieval and generation to score candidates via typed probability estimates in a single batch request. Application logic can then filter passages based on these probabilities and assess overall answerability before passing context to the LLM. This decouples subjective relevance judgments from deterministic business policies and enables improved auditability.
takeaways: Hybrid search can achieve high recall via dense search, BM25, and reciprocal rank fusion, but retrieval quality bounds the system's overall performance.
Jev evaluates whether passages provide true evidence by returning typed probability scores across all candidates in a single packed request.
Decoupling probability estimation in Jev from policy thresholds in application code allows teams to tune precision-recall tradeoffs independently.
Jev can perform secondary checks in the same request, such as evaluating whether the collective retained passages are sufficient to answer the query or flagging potential prompt injections.
An open-source example integrates Jev as an evaluation judge alongside Comet Opik for AI observability and trace auditing.

sections.title: Top 12 agentic use cases for Jev:
sections.summary: Jev is a tool designed to handle semantic decisions that standard code cannot reliably express, outputting typed answers and probabilities while code controls the workflow. It supports twelve practical agentic use cases including bounded DOM action selection, trace pruning, dynamic skill loading, function argument extraction, semantic CI evaluation, and trace lesson extraction. The Beacon open-source project by Asymptote Labs uses Jev to analyze sessions across developer agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex to extract reusable lessons.
takeaways: Jev provides typed answers and probabilities to make semantic decisions within programmatic workflows.
Key agentic use cases for Jev span DOM interaction, verbatim trace pruning, skill selection, argument validation, trajectory labeling, and CI semantic regression testing.
Jev can act as a secondary verification or reranking layer behind cheaper extractors or embedding-based retrieval pipelines.
The Beacon open-source project uses Jev to extract reusable lessons and corrections across more than 20 agent harnesses, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode.

items.title: How DoorDash Built a Toolbox for AI Agents

sections.title: Why an AI Agent Needs Tools
sections.summary: Language models lack native access to external systems such as code repositories, incident reports, and production logs, requiring software integrations referred to as tools. An AI agent is an application that leverages a language model to orchestrate multi-step tasks by selecting and executing these tools. Tool outputs are fed back to the model iteratively to guide subsequent reasoning and actions. Tools encompass both read operations and state-modifying write operations, enabling organizations like DoorDash to connect agents to internal systems, documentation, and third-party services.
takeaways: Language models do not inherently have access to external systems such as code repositories, incident reports, or production logs.
An AI agent is defined as an application that uses a language model to choose which tools and steps to execute for a task.
The host application executes the tool chosen by the model and returns the output for subsequent reasoning.
Tools can perform read-only actions, like searching documentation, or write actions that modify external systems, such as opening a pull request.
DoorDash sources agent capabilities across internal services, engineering systems, documentation platforms, and third-party software.

sections.title: Why MCP Is Not Enough
sections.summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes capability discovery and invocation between AI agents and external tools, but it does not address higher-level enterprise governance. Companies like DoorDash must manage access control, credential handling, and operational monitoring across disparate agent workflows. To prevent redundant and fragmented integrations across engineering teams, DoorDash identifies three core requirements: access, tool-surface curation, and operations. The Agent Gateway consolidates these responsibilities into a unified platform to govern tool interactions reliably.
takeaways: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a common interface for discovering capabilities via tools/list and invoking them via tools/call.
MCP does not enforce enterprise-specific rules such as identity, credential management, access permissions, or operational monitoring.
Decentralized tool integrations lead to duplicated effort across engineering teams for secret handling, OAuth flows, and usage logging.
DoorDash organizes agent tool governance into three distinct concerns: Access, Tool-surface Curation, and Operations.
The Agent Gateway centralizes access control, tool filtering, and production operations into a shared enterprise platform.

sections.title: The Core Components of the Agent Gateway
sections.summary: DoorDash's Agent Gateway architecture controls agent access by routing Model Context Protocol (MCP) requests to downstream MCP servers. The gateway relies on two core architectural components: a proxy within the data plane and a registry within the control plane. The proxy handles live traffic by verifying callers, enforcing permissions and rate limits, injecting credentials, and logging audit information. The registry acts as the source of truth, storing metadata, tool catalogs, policies, and connection settings managed by engineering teams. To maintain distinct trust boundaries, DoorDash segments internal and external-facing proxy planes while sharing unified governance concepts and libraries.
takeaways: The Agent Gateway acts as an intermediary that controls access and routes MCP requests from agents to downstream MCP servers.
The gateway consists of two primary components: a proxy (data plane) and a registry (control plane).
The proxy handles live traffic tasks, including caller verification, permission checking, rate limiting, credential attachment, and audit logging.
The registry functions as the source of truth, holding configurations, agent and MCP server details, tool catalogs, and access policies.
DoorDash divides internal workflows and external use cases into distinct proxy planes to preserve separate trust boundaries while retaining shared governance concepts.

sections.title: Verifying Who is Calling and What They Can Do
sections.summary: DoorDash's engineering team built an Agent Gateway that relies on authentication and authorization to control agent interactions. Authentication establishes caller identity, while authorization evaluates fine-grained context including the user, agent, requested tool, and environment. The system distinguishes between read-only and administrative capabilities rather than granting blanket server access. By propagating identity downstream and centralizing security policies, the gateway eliminates the need to encode authorization rules into prompts or individual tools.
takeaways: Authentication identifies whether a caller is a user, a service, or an agent acting on a user's behalf.
Authorization in the gateway provides granular control rather than coarse access to an entire MCP server.
DoorDash's Agent Gateway considers multiple contexts, including agent, user, tool, environment, and read-versus-write capabilities.
Caller identity is preserved throughout request routing and usage recording to enable downstream attribution.
Centralizing access control prevents developers from encoding security checks in prompts or duplicating authorization logic across tools.

sections.title: Why Identifying the Caller is Different from Supplying Credentials
sections.summary: In DoorDash's agent gateway architecture, caller identification is decoupled from the credentials required by downstream services. Rather than allowing agents to hold raw API keys or tokens, the gateway implements credential injection, attaching appropriate credentials before requests are forwarded. The architecture supports four credential models: Internal Service Identity, Gateway-held Token, Per-user OAuth, and Service Principal. This approach centralizes secret storage, credential rotation, auditing, and revocation outside of the AI agents.
takeaways: Caller identity entering an agent gateway is functionally distinct from the downstream credentials needed by external systems.
Credential injection is the process where the gateway attaches necessary secrets to outgoing requests without exposing them to agents.
Internal Service Identity passes DoorDash-verified caller context directly to internal microservices.
Gateway-held Tokens store vendor and service keys in gateway secret storage and prevent agents from seeing raw secrets.
Per-user OAuth enables the gateway to securely store, inject, and refresh user-delegated tokens for external services.
Service Principals provide software and team automations with short-lived credentials via gateway-managed identities.
Centralizing credentials in the gateway provides a single location to manage, rotate, audit, and revoke access keys.

sections.title: How a User Connects an Account During a Tool Call
sections.summary: Tools acting on behalf of a specific user require authorization, typically handled via OAuth access and refresh tokens. DoorDash's agent gateway centralizes user connection flows and encrypted token storage across product teams. When authorization is missing, the gateway initiates an OAuth flow, optionally utilizing MCP elicitation to pause requests while the user authorizes via a browser prompt. For clients lacking elicitation support, the gateway provides a structured response with a connection URL for recovery.
takeaways: OAuth provides access tokens for authorized API calls and refresh tokens to replace expired ones.
DoorDash's agent gateway centralizes connection flows and encrypted token storage, replacing separate implementations across product teams.
For clients supporting MCP elicitation, the gateway pauses the tool request, prompts user authorization in a browser, securely stores the token, and resumes the call.
Agents do not receive the raw user credentials during or after the OAuth elicitation process.
Clients without MCP elicitation support receive a structured error response with an authorization connection URL.

sections.title: Why Agents Should See a Selected Tool Catalog
sections.summary: Presenting an agent with an entire server catalog introduces unnecessary choices and complex descriptions that degrade performance. To address this, DoorDash engineering exposes smaller, task-specific catalogs using bundles and filters. Bundles combine tools across multiple Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers into a single endpoint, while filters selectively expose approved capabilities based on agent or environment criteria. Gateways can also improve usability by standardizing descriptions and namespacing overlapping tool names.
takeaways: Presenting an overly broad tool surface creates unnecessary choices that force models to interpret more descriptions and distinguish between similar tools.
DoorDash engineering exposes smaller, relevant tool catalogs tailored specifically to the work being performed.
A bundle combines tools across multiple MCP servers into a single logical MCP endpoint address.
Filters control which tools appear in an interface based on the bundle, agent, user group, environment, or audience.
Agent gateways can apply namespacing and aliases to resolve overlapping names across multiple tool servers.

sections.title: What Happens During Discovery and Execution
sections.summary: Tool discovery and tool execution occur at distinct stages and necessitate independent validation and policy checks. During discovery, an agent issues a tools/list request to a gateway, which uses fan-out across downstream servers to assemble, filter, and return an aggregated catalog. At execution time, the agent issues a tools/call request, prompting the gateway to re-evaluate policy, enforce rate limits, inject credentials, and route to the correct server. This architecture relieves agents from having to manage downstream server routing or provider-specific credentials.
takeaways: Discovery controls which tools are presented in the catalog, whereas invocation controls whether an execution is permitted.
A tool appearing in a discovery response still requires independent authorization at execution time.
During discovery, the gateway utilizes fan-out to query multiple downstream servers and unify their tools into one catalog.
During execution (tools/call), the gateway manages authorization, rate limits, server routing, and credential injection.
The agent interacts exclusively with the gateway, removing the need for client-side routing or credential management.

sections.title: Understanding What Happened After a Request
sections.summary: Observability enables teams to monitor and understand systems where multiple agents interact with various tools. Positioned in the path of all tool calls, the gateway captures structured events containing metadata such as identity, timing, errors, and payload sizes. It also aggregates metrics on request counts, latencies, authorization decisions, and downstream failures. This telemetry allows platform, security, and tool teams to audit access, diagnose issues, and analyze adoption.
takeaways: Observability refers to the ability to understand a running system through the information it produces.
Because all tool requests pass through the gateway, it acts as a central recording component for telemetry.
The gateway records structured events that capture consistent metadata, including server, tool, bundle, owner, identities, status, and timing.
Metrics produced by the gateway aggregate behavior across requests, including request counts, tool response times, OAuth refresh outcomes, and rate-limit decisions.
Observability data serves distinct enterprise roles: security teams audit access, platform teams investigate agent behavior, and tool owners track adoption and failures.

sections.title: Making the Platform Easy for Teams to Adopt
sections.summary: DoorDash enables broad internal adoption of its centralized agent gateway by providing a self-service management interface and API. Teams register Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, allowing the platform to discover capabilities via tools/list before teams configure approval, ownership, authentication, and access policies. Bundled tools are continuously monitored for latency, failure rates, authorization decisions, and costs. The gateway now acts as the default access route for DoorDash engineering, managing over 200 MCP servers and millions of weekly tool calls.
takeaways: DoorDash offers a self-service UI and API for registering and configuring MCP servers on its centralized gateway.
The platform discovers raw tool catalogs via tools/list, requiring explicit approval and access policy configuration before tools can be used.
Capabilities are bound to ownership metadata and grouped into bundles to enable operational accountability and policy enforcement.
Teams can monitor tool traffic, response times, execution failures, authorization decisions, and cost metrics once agents start using bundles.
The gateway hosts more than 200 registered MCP servers and handles millions of weekly tool calls across DoorDash.

sections.title: What DoorDash Plans to Improve Next
sections.summary: DoorDash is planning future improvements to its centralized AI agent-tool gateway architecture. Key planned areas include stronger agent identity and user delegation using cryptographic identities and short-lived scoped credentials. The company is also developing dynamic tool discovery based on tasks, access policies, and usage signals to offer context-relevant capabilities. Additional enhancements target tool quality and security evaluation, such as detecting sensitive data, simplifying server registration, and streaming redacted tool-call events.
takeaways: DoorDash plans to implement agent identity and user delegation using cryptographic identities and short-lived credentials scoped to user, agent, task, and target tool.
Dynamic tool discovery will refine tool selection dynamically based on current task, access policy, and usage signals.
DoorDash intends to improve tool evaluation to detect risky descriptions and sensitive information like secrets or PII in errors.
The platform aims to simplify tool server creation and registration while providing redacted tool-call event streams.
