sections.title: 為什麼 AI Agent 需要 Tools
sections.summary: 語言模型缺乏原生存取外部系統（如 code repositories、incident reports 及 production logs）的能力，因此需要稱為 tools 的軟體整合。AI agent 則是一種利用語言模型來選擇並執行這些 tools，進而編排多步驟任務的應用程式。Tool 的輸出會迭代地回饋給模型，以引導後續的 reasoning 和 actions。Tools 同時涵蓋唯讀操作與會變更狀態的寫入操作，讓 DoorDash 這類的企業能將 agents 連接到內部系統、技術文件以及第三方服務。
takeaways: 語言模型本身不具備存取外部系統（如 code repositories、incident reports 或 production logs）的能力。
AI agent 被定義為一種使用語言模型來決定任務中應執行哪些 tools 與步驟的應用程式。
Host application 會執行模型所選取的 tool，並將輸出回傳以進行後續的 reasoning。
Tools 可以執行唯讀操作（例如搜尋文件），或是會修改外部系統的寫入操作（例如建立 pull request）。
DoorDash 的 agent 功能來源涵蓋內部服務、工程系統、文件平台以及第三方軟體。

sections.title: 為什麼 MCP 還不夠
sections.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) 將 AI agent 與外部 tool 之間的能力探索（capability discovery）與調用（invocation）標準化，但它並未解決更高層級的企業治理（enterprise governance）問題。像 DoorDash 這樣的公司必須在各個不同的 agent workflow 中管理 access control、credential handling 和 operational monitoring。為了避免各工程團隊之間出現重複且零碎的整合，DoorDash 定義了三個核心需求：access、tool-surface curation 和 operations。Agent Gateway 將這些職責整合進一個統一的平台，以可靠地治理 tool 的互動。
takeaways: Model Context Protocol (MCP) 提供了共通介面，透過 tools/list 探索功能，並透過 tools/call 進行調用。
MCP 並未強制執行企業特有的規則，例如 identity、credential management、access permissions 或 operational monitoring。
去中心化的 tool 整合會導致工程團隊在 secret handling、OAuth flows 與 usage logging 方面付出重複的努力。
DoorDash 將 agent tool 治理歸納為三個主要面向：Access、Tool-surface Curation 與 Operations。
Agent Gateway 將 access control、tool filtering 和 production operations 集中到一個共享的企業級平台中。

sections.title: Agent Gateway 的核心元件
sections.summary: DoorDash 的 Agent Gateway 架構藉由將 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 請求路由至下游 MCP server 來控制 agent 的存取。此 gateway 仰賴兩個核心架構元件：位於 data plane 的 proxy，以及位於 control plane 的 registry。Proxy 負責處理即時流量，包括驗證 caller、強制執行權限與 rate limit、注入 credential 以及記錄 audit 資訊。Registry 則作為 source of truth，儲存由工程團隊管理的 metadata、tool catalog、policy 與連線設定。為了維持明確的信任邊界（trust boundaries），DoorDash 將內部與對外的 proxy plane 進行區隔，同時共享統一的治理概念與函式庫。
takeaways: Agent Gateway 作為中介層，負責控制存取並將來自 agent 的 MCP 請求路由至下游 MCP server。
該 gateway 由兩個主要元件組成：proxy (data plane) 與 registry (control plane)。
Proxy 負責處理即時流量任務，包括 caller 驗證、權限檢查、rate limiting、credential 附加以及 audit logging。
Registry 作為 source of truth，保存配置、agent 與 MCP server 詳細資訊、tool catalog 以及 access policy。
DoorDash 將內部 workflow 與外部 use case 切分到不同的 proxy plane，以維持獨立的 trust boundary，同時保留共享的治理概念。

sections.title: 驗證是誰在呼叫以及他們能做什麼
sections.summary: DoorDash 的工程團隊打造了仰賴 authentication（身份驗證）與 authorization（授權）來控制 agent 互動的 Agent Gateway。Authentication 確立 caller 的身份，而 authorization 則評估細粒度的 context，包括 user、agent、請求的 tool 以及 environment。該系統會區分唯讀（read-only）與管理權限（administrative capabilities），而非授予寬鬆的完整 server 存取權。透過將身份傳遞至下游並集中化 security policy，gateway 讓開發者不再需要將 authorization 規則寫入 prompt 或各別 tool 中。
takeaways: Authentication 負責識別 caller 是 user、service，或是代表 user 行事的 agent。
Gateway 中的 authorization 提供細粒度的控制，而非對整個 MCP server 提供粗粒度的存取權限。
DoorDash 的 Agent Gateway 會考量多種 context，包括 agent、user、tool、environment 以及 read 與 write 權限的差異。
Caller identity 在整個 request routing 與使用記錄過程中都會被保留，以實現下游歸因（attribution）。
將 access control 集中化可避免開發者在 prompt 中編寫安全檢查，或在各 tool 之間重複實作 authorization 邏輯。

sections.title: 為什麼識別 Caller 與提供 Credential 是兩回事
sections.summary: 在 DoorDash 的 agent gateway 架構中，caller identification 與下游服務所需的 credential 是解耦的。Gateway 實作了 credential injection，在轉發請求前附加適當的 credential，而不是讓 agent 直接持有原始 API key 或 token。該架構支援四種 credential model：Internal Service Identity、Gateway-held Token、Per-user OAuth 以及 Service Principal。這種做法將 secret 儲存、credential rotation、auditing 與 revocation 集中在 AI agent 之外管理。
takeaways: 進入 agent gateway 的 caller identity 在功能上與外部系統所需的下游 credential 是截然不同的。
Credential injection 是指 gateway 在不將 secret 暴露給 agent 的情況下，將必要的 secret 附加至外發請求（outgoing request）的過程。
Internal Service Identity 將 DoorDash 驗證過的 caller context 直接傳遞給內部的 microservices。
Gateway-held Tokens 將 vendor 和 service keys 儲存在 gateway 的 secret storage 中，防止 agent 接觸到原始 secret。
Per-user OAuth 讓 gateway 能夠為外部服務安全地儲存、inject 並 refresh 使用者委派的 token。
Service Principals 透過 gateway 管理的 identity，為軟體和團隊自動化提供短效 credentials。
將 credentials 集中在 gateway 中，提供了一個單一位置來管理、rotate、audit 和 revoke access keys。

sections.title: 使用者如何在 Tool Call 期間連結帳號
sections.summary: 代表特定使用者執行的 tool 需要授權，通常透過 OAuth access token 與 refresh token 處理。DoorDash 的 agent gateway 集中管理各產品團隊的使用者連線流程與加密 token 儲存。當缺少授權時，gateway 會發起 OAuth 流程，並可選用 MCP elicitation 暫停請求，同時讓使用者透過瀏覽器提示進行授權。對於不支援 elicitation 的 client，gateway 則提供帶有連線 URL 的結構化回應以進行復原。
takeaways: OAuth 提供用於授權 API 呼叫的 access token，以及用來替換過期 token 的 refresh token。
DoorDash 的 agent gateway 集中管理連線流程與加密 token 儲存，取代了各產品團隊個別的實作。
對於支援 MCP elicitation 的 client，gateway 會暫停 tool 請求、提示使用者在瀏覽器中授權、安全儲存 token，並恢復呼叫。
在 OAuth elicitation 過程期間或之後，agent 都不會接收到原始的使用者 credentials。
不支援 MCP elicitation 的 client 會收到包含授權連線 URL 的結構化錯誤回應。

sections.title: 為什麼 Agent 應該只看到精選的 Tool Catalog
sections.summary: 讓 agent 面對整個 server catalog 會引入不必要的選擇與複雜描述，進而降低效能。為了改善此問題，DoorDash engineering 使用 bundle 與 filter 來公開較小且針對特定任務的 catalog。Bundle 將跨多個 Model Context Protocol (MCP) server 的 tool 整合至單一 endpoint，而 filter 則根據 agent 或環境條件選擇性地公開經過核可的能力。Gateway 還能透過標準化描述以及為重複的 tool 名稱加入 namespacing 來提升可用性。
takeaways: 提供過於龐大的 tool surface 會產生不必要的選擇，迫使模型解析更多描述並在相似的 tool 之間做區分。
DoorDash engineering 僅公開針對當前執行任務量身打造、較小且高度相關的 tool catalog。
Bundle 將跨多個 MCP server 的 tool 整合至單一邏輯 MCP endpoint 位址。
Filter 會根據 bundle、agent、user group、環境或受眾，控制哪些 tool 會出現在介面中。
Agent gateway 可以套用 namespacing 和 alias 來解決跨多個 tool server 的名稱重複問題。

sections.title: Discovery 與 Execution 階段會發生什麼事
sections.summary: Tool discovery 與 tool execution 發生在不同階段，且需要各自獨立的驗證與 policy 檢查。在 discovery 期間，agent 向 gateway 發出 tools/list 請求，gateway 會對下游 server 使用 fan-out 來組合、過濾並回傳聚合後的 catalog。在 execution 階段，agent 發出 tools/call 請求，促使 gateway 重新評估 policy、實施 rate limit、注入 credentials，並路由至正確的 server。此架構讓 agent 無需自行管理下游 server 的路由或特定 provider 的 credentials。
takeaways: Discovery 控制哪些 tool 會顯示在 catalog 中，而 invocation 則控制執行是否被允許。
出現在 discovery 回應中的 tool，在 execution 階段仍需要獨立的授權。
在 discovery 期間，gateway 利用 fan-out 查詢多個下游 server，並將它們的 tool 統一彙整為單一 catalog。
在 execution（tools/call）期間，gateway 負責管理授權、rate limit、server 路由以及 credential 注入。
agent 僅與 gateway 進行互動，完全無需在 client-side 進行 routing 或 credential 管理。

sections.title: 理解請求（Request）發出後發生的事情
sections.summary: Observability 讓團隊能夠監控並理解多個 agent 與各類 tool 互動的系統。Gateway 位於所有 tool call 的路徑中，能擷取包含 identity、timing、error 和 payload size 等 metadata 的 structured event。它還匯總了關於 request count、latency、authorization decision 以及 downstream failure 的 metrics。這些 telemetry 資料讓 platform、security 和 tool 團隊能夠 audit 存取、診斷問題並分析 adoption 狀況。
takeaways: Observability 是指透過執行中系統所產生的資訊來理解該系統的能力。
由於所有 tool request 都會經過 gateway，它便成為記錄 telemetry 的中心元件。
Gateway 會記錄包含一致 metadata 的 structured event，涵蓋 server、tool、bundle、owner、identities、status 與 timing。
Gateway 產生的 metrics 匯總了跨 request 的行為，包括 request count、tool response time、OAuth refresh 結果以及 rate-limit decision。
Observability 資料為不同的企業角色提供支援：security 團隊 audit 存取權限、platform 團隊調查 agent 行為，而 tool owner 則追蹤 adoption 與 failure 情況。

sections.title: 讓平台更易於被各團隊採用（Adopt）
sections.summary: DoorDash 透過提供 self-service 管理介面與 API，促進其 centralized agent gateway 在內部的廣泛採用。各團隊註冊 Model Context Protocol (MCP) server，讓平台能在團隊設定 approval、ownership、authentication 與 access policy 之前，透過 tools/list 探索各種 capability。打包成 bundle 的 tool 會持續受到監控，包括 latency、failure rate、authorization decision 與 cost。該 gateway 現已成為 DoorDash 工程團隊的預設存取途徑，管理著超過 200 個 MCP server 以及每週數百萬次的 tool call。
takeaways: DoorDash 提供 self-service UI 與 API，用於在其 centralized gateway 上註冊與設定 MCP server。
平台透過 tools/list 探索原始 tool catalog，且必須經過明確的 approval 與 access policy 設定後才能使用這些 tool。
Capability 會與 ownership metadata 綁定並打包成 bundle，以落實維運當責（operational accountability）與 policy enforcement。
一旦 agent 開始使用 bundle，團隊便能監控 tool traffic、response time、execution failure、authorization decision 與 cost metrics。
該 gateway 託管了超過 200 個註冊的 MCP server，並處理 DoorDash 全公司每週數百萬次的 tool call。

sections.title: DoorDash 下一步計畫改進的方向
sections.summary: DoorDash 正在規劃未來對其 centralized AI agent-tool gateway 架構的改進。重點規劃領域包括利用 cryptographic identity 和 short-lived scoped credential 來強化 agent identity 與 user delegation。該公司也正在開發基於 task、access policy 與 usage signal 的 dynamic tool discovery，以提供與 context 相關的 capability。其他增強功能則針對 tool quality 與 security evaluation，例如偵測敏感資料、簡化 server registration 以及串流經過脫敏（redacted）的 tool-call event。
takeaways: DoorDash 計劃使用 cryptographic identity 以及針對 user、agent、task 和 target tool 限定 scope 的 short-lived credential，來實現 agent identity 與 user delegation。
Dynamic tool discovery 將根據當前的 task、access policy 與 usage signal，動態微調 tool 的選擇。
DoorDash 打算改進 tool evaluation，以偵測有風險的 description 以及 error 中像 secret 或 PII 等敏感資訊。
該平台的目標是簡化 tool server 的建立與註冊，同時提供經脫敏處理（redacted）的 tool-call event stream。

items.title: Build a real-time hotel booking voice agent

sections.title: vLLM closed this feature request as “not planned”:
sections.summary: Developers have requested the ability to run multiple small models on a single GPU through one inference server, but vLLM has officially declined to implement this feature. The standard workaround requires running separate vLLM instances for each model, which leads to redundant memory and process overhead. An alternative solution called Superlinked Inference Engine (SIE) manages multiple models behind a single server by loading them on demand and using LRU eviction. Performance benchmarks show that SIE can reduce the execution time of a four-model pipeline from 18.58 seconds to 1.47 seconds.
takeaways: vLLM has closed a long-standing feature request for multi-model serving on a single GPU as 'not planned'.
The recommended vLLM workaround involves separate processes and memory allocations for every model, requiring an additional routing layer.
Superlinked Inference Engine (SIE) allows multiple models to be served through a single inference server on one GPU.
SIE manages GPU memory by keeping active models resident and evicting the least-recently-used (LRU) models when space is needed.
In testing, SIE improved the performance of a four-model agent pipeline by over 90% compared to direct model loading.
SIE is available as an open-source project on GitHub.

sections.title: Build a real-time hotel booking voice agent
sections.summary: This section details the construction of a real-time hotel booking voice agent designed to handle noisy environments and complex data like names and dates. The architecture utilizes a modular pipeline where speech-to-text, reasoning, and speech generation are handled by separate, replaceable components. LiveKit serves as the core infrastructure, integrating Speechmatics Linden for transcription, OpenRouter for LLM access, and Fish Audio for text-to-speech. The implementation emphasizes low latency and the ability to handle mid-sentence corrections through a Streamlit-based monitoring interface.
takeaways: The voice agent pipeline is modular, allowing speech-to-text, reasoning, and speech generation components to be swapped independently.
LiveKit Inference simplifies integration by managing authentication, routing, and billing for providers like Speechmatics and Fish Audio.
Speechmatics Linden is optimized for voice agents, offering a 250ms latency for final transcripts and high accuracy for alphanumeric strings and accents.
The system uses partial transcripts to provide real-time visual feedback in the UI before the final turn is processed.
Latency is specifically measured from the completion of a final transcript to the start of the agent's vocal response.
The agent's prompt is configured to limit responses to three sentences and prioritize missing reservation fields while preserving user corrections.

sections.title: Where does all the VRAM go during LLM inference?
sections.summary: LLM inference memory consumption is divided into model weights, KV cache, activations, and runtime overhead. While weights remain relatively constant, the KV cache scales with context length and concurrent requests, often leading to out-of-memory errors even if the model initially fits. Quantization reduces the weight footprint, which indirectly provides more VRAM for larger batches and longer sequences. Ultimately, inference performance is constrained by memory movement and bandwidth as much as arithmetic throughput.
takeaways: Model weights are fixed in size based on precision, with FP16 and BF16 requiring two bytes per parameter.
The KV cache grows dynamically with context length and the number of concurrent requests.
Activations and workspace memory hold intermediate values and vary based on sequence length and batch size.
Runtime overhead includes CUDA contexts, memory allocators, and metadata, which are small but essential.
Quantization helps by shrinking weights to free up VRAM for larger KV caches or higher concurrency.
GPU performance in LLM inference is often limited by memory movement from high-bandwidth memory rather than raw compute throughput.

Where does all the VRAM go during LLM inference?

zh.summary: 開發者曾提出希望透過單一 inference server 在單張 GPU 上執行多個小模型，但 vLLM 已正式回絕實作這項 feature。標準的 workaround 需要為每個模型執行獨立的 vLLM instance，這會導致重複的記憶體和 process overhead。另一種名為 Superlinked Inference Engine (SIE) 的替代解決方案，則是透過 on-demand 載入與 LRU eviction 機制，在單一 server 背後管理多個模型。Performance benchmark 顯示，SIE 能將四模型 pipeline 的執行時間從 18.58 秒縮短至 1.47 秒。本節將詳細說明如何建構一個即時飯店預訂 voice agent，該 agent 專為處理吵雜環境以及姓名、日期等複雜資料而設計。其架構採用模組化 pipeline，將 speech-to-text、reasoning 與 speech generation 交由獨立且可替換的元件處理。LiveKit 作為核心基礎架構，整合了用於 transcription 的 Speechmatics Linden、用於 LLM access 的 OpenRouter，以及用於 text-to-speech 的 Fish Audio。該實作強調低延遲，並透過基於 Streamlit 的監控介面實現處理句中修正（mid-sentence correction）的能力。LLM inference 的記憶體消耗可分為 model weight、KV cache、activation 與 runtime overhead。雖然 weight 保持相對固定，但 KV cache 會隨 context length 與 concurrent request 增加而擴大，即使模型最初能塞進顯存，也常會導致 out-of-memory (OOM) 錯誤。Quantization 能縮減 weight 的佔用量，進而間接為更大的 batch 和更長的 sequence 釋出更多 VRAM。歸根究柢，inference 效能受限於 memory movement 與 bandwidth 的程度，不亞於 arithmetic throughput。

在 LLM inference 期間，所有的 VRAM 都去哪了？

sections.title: vLLM 將此 feature request 標記為「not planned」並予以關閉：
sections.summary: 開發者一直希望能透過單一 inference server 在單張 GPU 上運行多個小型模型，但 vLLM 已正式拒絕實作此功能。標準的 workaround 需要為每個模型運行獨立的 vLLM instance，這會導致重複的記憶體與 process overhead。另一種名為 Superlinked Inference Engine (SIE) 的替代解決方案，透過 on demand 載入模型並使用 LRU eviction 機制，在單一伺服器背後管理多個模型。效能 benchmark 顯示，SIE 能將四模型 pipeline 的執行時間從 18.58 秒縮短至 1.47 秒。
takeaways: vLLM 已將一項存在已久、關於在單張 GPU 上進行 multi-model serving 的 feature request 標記為「not planned」並予以關閉。
官方建議的 vLLM workaround 涉及為每個模型配置獨立的 process 與記憶體分配，且需要額外的 routing layer。
Superlinked Inference Engine (SIE) 允許在單張 GPU 上透過單一 inference server 提供多個模型的 serving。
SIE 透過將 active models 常駐，並在需要空間時驅逐 least-recently-used (LRU) 模型來管理 GPU 記憶體。
在測試中，與直接載入模型相比，SIE 將四模型 agent pipeline 的效能提升了 90% 以上。
SIE 已作為開源專案在 GitHub 上釋出。

sections.title: 打造即時飯店預訂 voice agent
sections.summary: 本節詳細介紹如何建構一個即時飯店預訂 voice agent，旨在處理吵雜環境以及姓名、日期等複雜資料。該架構採用模組化 pipeline，將 speech-to-text、reasoning 與 speech generation 分別交由獨立且可替換的組件處理。LiveKit 作為核心基礎架構，整合了用於 transcription 的 Speechmatics Linden、用於 LLM access 的 OpenRouter，以及用於 text-to-speech 的 Fish Audio。該實作強調低 latency，並透過基於 Streamlit 的監控介面提供處理話講到一半進行修正（mid-sentence corrections）的能力。
takeaways: 該 voice agent pipeline 採模組化設計，允許獨立替換 speech-to-text、reasoning 與 speech generation 組件。
LiveKit Inference 透過管理 Speechmatics 和 Fish Audio 等 provider 的驗證、routing 與計費，簡化了整合工作。
Speechmatics Linden 專為 voice agent 進行最佳化，為 final transcript 提供 250ms 的 latency，並對英數字串與各類口音具備極高的準確度。
系統在處理 final turn 之前，利用 partial transcript 在 UI 中提供即時的視覺回饋。
Latency 是特別從 final transcript 完成起算，直到 agent 開始發出語音回應為止。
Agent 的 prompt 經過設定，將回應限制在三句話以內，並優先確認遺漏的預訂欄位，同時保留使用者的更正內容。

sections.title: 在 LLM inference 期間，所有的 VRAM 都去哪了？
sections.summary: LLM inference 的記憶體消耗主要分為 model weights、KV cache、activations 與 runtime overhead。雖然 weights 相對固定，但 KV cache 會隨著 context length 和並發請求（concurrent requests）數量增加而擴展，即使模型最初裝得下，也常導致 out-of-memory 錯誤。Quantization 可縮減 weight footprint，進而間接釋出更多 VRAM 供更大的 batch 與更長的 sequence 使用。歸根結底，inference 效能受限於記憶體搬移與頻寬的程度，並不亞於運算吞吐量（arithmetic throughput）。
takeaways: Model weights 的大小取決於 precision 且固定不變，其中 FP16 和 BF16 每個 parameter 需要兩個 byte。
KV cache 會隨著 context length 和 concurrent requests 數量動態增長。
Activations 與 workspace memory 用於暫存中間值，並隨著 sequence length 和 batch size 而變動。
Runtime overhead 包含 CUDA contexts、memory allocators 與 metadata，雖然佔用不大但不可或缺。
Quantization 透過縮減 weights 來釋放 VRAM，以供更大的 KV cache 或更高的 concurrency 使用。
在 LLM inference 中，GPU 效能往往受限於從 high-bandwidth memory 進行的記憶體搬移，而非純粹的 compute throughput。

items.title: Why Do LLMs Lie?

sections.title: What Hallucination Actually Means
sections.summary: In the context of large language models, hallucination refers to generated text that is factually incorrect, invented, or inconsistent with designated source material. A response does not need to be entirely false to be considered a hallucination, as a single fabricated detail can mislead a user who relies on it. Although hallucinations resemble confident falsehoods, they differ from lying because models lack an intent to deceive and produce these errors via normal generation mechanisms. Ultimately, whether an invention constitutes a hallucination depends on context and whether the output claims to represent factual reality.
takeaways: Hallucination in LLMs is defined as generated information that is invented, factually incorrect, or inconsistent with reference material.
An otherwise correct or useful explanation can be compromised by a single fabricated detail, date, or citation.
Hallucinations mimic lies by presenting confident falsehoods, but they do not involve an intention to deceive.
The classification of invented text as a hallucination depends heavily on context and what the generated text claims to represent.

sections.title: Three Ways an Answer Can Go Wrong
sections.summary: AI support assistant errors can be systematically analyzed across three primary categories: factual hallucinations, faithfulness hallucinations, and fabrications. Factual hallucinations contradict real-world reality, whereas faithfulness hallucinations occur when an answer conflicts with its supplied source evidence. Fabrications involve inventing entirely nonexistent items, often overlapping with factuality failures. Notably, an AI can produce a faithful summary of an outdated source document and still be factually wrong, demonstrating the necessity of addressing both model behavior and source data quality.
takeaways: Factual hallucinations represent contradictions of real-world facts or policies.
Faithfulness hallucinations represent contradictions between the model's response and the provided reference evidence.
Fabrication refers to inventing nonexistent information, such as policy sections or confirmation numbers, and often falls under factuality failures.
A fundamental distinction exists between validating agreement with reality versus validating agreement with supplied evidence.
An answer can be faithful to an outdated reference document while remaining factually incorrect in practice.

sections.title: How Predicting Text Produces Hallucinations
sections.summary: Large language models generate responses iteratively by calculating next-token probabilities and selecting continuations rather than verifying facts. During pretraining, model parameters absorb grammatical structures, concepts, and relationships across massive text collections, but this does not verify situation-specific facts. Consequently, models can generate structurally plausible assertions or fabricated citations accompanied by confident language without underlying evidentiary support.
takeaways: LLMs construct text sequentially by calculating probabilities over tokens and iteratively selecting continuations.
A high token probability indicates text generation likelihood rather than verified truth.
Words expressing certainty like 'certainly' and 'definitely' are learned linguistic patterns rather than signs of actual verification.
Pretraining adjusts model parameters to mirror broad patterns and concepts, but fails to guarantee accuracy on instance-specific facts.
LLMs can fabricate citations that accurately mimic the structure of real research references without referencing actual papers.

sections.title: Why Models Struggle to Admit Uncertainty
sections.summary: Large language models are primarily optimized to generate plausible continuations rather than guarantee truthful answers. Common evaluation setups reward guessing by penalizing uncertainty admissions identically to incorrect answers, which actively incentivizes hallucinations. While models exhibit some limited self-evaluation capabilities under specific conditions, they lack dependable mechanisms to generalize uncertainty detection to unfamiliar tasks. Requesting verbalized confidence percentages does not solve this issue without empirical calibration to verify that reported scores reflect actual accuracy.
takeaways: Large language models are optimized for plausible text generation rather than verified factual accuracy.
Scoring rubrics that penalize admitting uncertainty identically to incorrect answers encourage models to guess, resulting in hallucinations.
Hallucinations are not solely an unavoidable architectural flaw; models possess conditional self-evaluation capabilities.
Current models lack an internal guarantee that consistently separates correct statements from guesses across novel tasks.
Prompting a model for a confidence percentage is unreliable without calibration measuring accuracy against reported confidence.

sections.title: Giving the Model Evidence with RAG
sections.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mitigates missing information by retrieving relevant documents, augmenting the model's prompt, and then generating a grounded response. In practical contexts like customer support, having retrieved policies enables an assistant to identify incomplete conditions rather than making unsupported assumptions. However, RAG introduces potential failure modes including retrieving outdated or incorrect policies, missing contextual exceptions, and misinterpreting retrieved passages. To avoid these issues, documents must be properly structured with explicit metadata such as effective dates and product names, and chunked so related conditions remain together.
takeaways: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) operates via three steps: retrieval of relevant information, augmentation into the prompt, and answer generation.
RAG allows models to recognize when user input leaves certain policy conditions unresolved rather than guessing.
Common RAG failure points include retrieving outdated or incorrect policies, omitting exceptions, or generating unsupported promises.
Documents used for RAG require explicit metadata such as clear product names, effective dates, and approval status to resolve policy conflicts.
Document chunking should keep related conditions together to prevent retrieving incomplete rules.
Inspecting the exact context retrieved by the model helps differentiate retrieval failures from interpretation errors.

sections.title: Looking Up the Missing Facts with Tools
sections.summary: LLM-based assistants require tools to retrieve customer-specific facts and execute external operations that go beyond static document policies. By interacting with external systems via APIs, models can ground their responses in factual verification and reduce task errors. Document retrieval via RAG and operational tool use often work complementarily to satisfy policy conditions. To avoid hallucinations, applications must verify that external tool operations actually succeed before presenting actions or facts as completed.
takeaways: Tool use allows LLM applications to retrieve external information or execute operations outside the model's direct scope.
Interacting with external information sources through tools reduces errors on evaluated tasks.
RAG and tool use can overlap when document retrieval is implemented as an external tool.
Tool executions must actually occur; merely generating text claiming an action was performed is not proof and introduces hallucinations.
External operations, such as issuing payments, require confirmed successful execution from the external system before the assistant claims completion.

sections.title: Writing Useful Answers
sections.summary: Making insufficient evidence a valid outcome provides an effective defense against hallucinations in AI assistants. Instructions can direct an assistant to ground claims in supplied text and identify missing information rather than forcing an unsupported conclusion. Preserving partial facts while detailing the specific obstacles to a full answer is significantly more helpful than a bare admission of ignorance. Consequently, software systems should implement intermediary states such as 'needs review' instead of forcing binary outcomes like 'eligible' or 'ineligible'.
takeaways: Treating insufficient evidence as an acceptable, valid outcome serves as a defense against hallucinations.
Explicit instructions can direct models to identify missing information and ground claims in supplied materials, reducing hallucinations.
Providing partial answers that identify missing criteria is more useful than a bare admission of ignorance.
System designs should incorporate non-binary states like 'needs review' rather than strictly binary outcomes to handle missing evidence.

sections.title: Why an Explanation Is Not Proof
sections.summary: Chain-of-thought prompting prompts models to solve problems through intermediate steps, which can improve answers and make errors easier to spot. However, a generated explanation is not equivalent to proof because it can rely on false premises or fail to faithfully reflect the model's underlying process. More explanation cannot compensate for missing or inaccurate grounding facts. Reliable systems should instead output concise justifications linked directly to checkable evidence that human reviewers can verify.
takeaways: Chain-of-thought prompting asks models to work through problems in intermediate steps, aiding task performance.
Generated explanations are not proof and can be unfaithful or based on incorrect premises.
Adding more explanation does not supply missing or incorrect facts.
Effective systems should link justifications to checkable evidence such as specific policy clauses and account data.

sections.title: Checking the Answer Before It Reaches the Customer
sections.summary: Verification should be implemented as an independent stage in the workflow to systematically reduce hallucinations. Responses must be decomposed into individual factual claims so that statements lacking evidence can be removed. Citations facilitate these checks, but the citations themselves require verification against source document existence and quote accuracy. Finally, techniques like lowering sampling temperature do not guarantee truthfulness, making deterministic code the preferable choice for enforcing unambiguous rules.
takeaways: Drafting an answer, generating verification questions, and answering them independently reduces hallucinations.
Complex responses contain multiple distinct claims that each require separate evidence, and unsupported claims should be removed.
Citations only improve reliability if verified for existence, relevance, and verbatim textual support.
Lowering sampling temperature concentrates probability distribution but does not ensure factual correctness.
Deterministic application code can evaluate unambiguous policy rules against verified facts, reserving language models for explanation.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: An improved LLM-based customer support workflow minimizes hallucinations by executing a structured sequence that retrieves policies, verifies account facts, and validates citations. Cases with missing data receive explicit unresolved statuses, while complex scenarios requiring judgment are routed for review. The system's reliability and usefulness must be evaluated using realistic test cases featuring edge cases, outdated policies, and false assumptions. Ultimately, developers are responsible for ensuring that assistant responses are strictly bounded by verifiable evidence rather than over-answering or unnecessarily declining requests.
takeaways: A structured support sequence verifies policies, account facts, conditions, and citations before finalizing an explanation.
When required information is missing or judgment is needed, the system generates an unresolved status or routes the case to human review.
Testing must use realistic scenarios, such as missing account records, outdated policies, and user prompts containing false assumptions.
Evaluation must balance correctness against usefulness to prevent assistants from either making unsupported claims or routinely declining answerable requests.
LLM assistants should clearly disclose which conditions are satisfied, which remain unresolved, and what evidence supports the claims.

sections.title: 幻覺的真正意涵
sections.summary: 在大型語言模型的語境下，幻覺（hallucination）是指生成的文本在事實上不正確、憑空捏造，或與指定的來源資料不一致。一個回答不需要完全錯誤才會被認定為幻覺，因為單一虛構的細節就足以誤導依賴該資訊的使用者。雖然幻覺看起來像是自信滿滿的錯誤言論，但它們與說謊不同，因為模型缺乏欺騙的意圖，且是透過正常的生成機制產生這些錯誤。歸根結底，虛構內容是否構成幻覺，取決於情境以及該輸出是否宣稱代表客觀事實。
takeaways: LLMs 中的幻覺被定義為捏造、事實錯誤或與參考資料不一致的生成資訊。
一個原本正確或有用的解釋，可能會因為單一捏造的細節、日期或 citation 而失去可信度。
幻覺透過展現自信的錯誤言論來模擬謊言，但它們並不包含欺騙的意圖。
將虛構文本歸類為幻覺，很大程度上取決於上下文情境以及該生成文本宣稱所代表的內容。

sections.title: 回答可能出錯的三種方式
sections.summary: AI 客服助理的錯誤可以有系統地歸納為三大類：事實性幻覺（factual hallucinations）、忠實性幻覺（faithfulness hallucinations）以及捏造（fabrications）。事實性幻覺與現實世界的事實相牴觸，而忠實性幻覺則發生在回答與提供的來源證據衝突時。捏造涉及憑空發明完全不存在的項目，通常與事實性錯誤有所重疊。值得注意的是，AI 可能對過時的來源文件產生忠實的摘要，但在實務上依然是事實錯誤，這凸顯了同時解決模型行為與來源資料品質的必要性。
takeaways: 事實性幻覺代表與現實世界的事實或政策相牴觸。
忠實性幻覺代表模型的回答與提供的參考證據之間存在矛盾。
捏造是指憑空創造不存在的資訊，例如政策條款或確認號碼，通常屬於事實性失敗（factuality failures）的一種。
驗證是否符合現實，與驗證是否符合提供的證據，兩者之間存在根本的差異。
一個回答可以忠實於過時的參考文件，但在實務上仍可能在事實層面是錯誤的。

sections.title: 文本預測如何產生幻覺
sections.summary: 大型語言模型藉由計算 next-token 機率並選取接續內容來反覆生成回答，而非透過驗證事實。在 pretraining 期間，模型參數從龐大的文本集中吸收語法結構、概念與關聯性，但這並無法驗證特定情境下的事實。因此，模型可能會以自信的語調生成結構上看似合理的主張或捏造的 citation，卻缺乏背後的證據支撐。
takeaways: LLMs 透過計算 token 的機率並反覆選取接續詞，循序構建出文本。
高 token 機率代表的是文本生成的可能性，而非經過驗證的事實真相。
像「certainly」和「definitely」這種表達確定性的詞彙，只是學到的語言模式，而非實際經過驗證的跡象。
Pretraining 會調整 model parameters 來反映廣泛的 pattern 與概念，但無法保證特定 instance-specific facts 的準確度。
LLMs 可能會捏造出能精準模仿真實研究文獻格式的 citations，但實際上並未引用任何真實 papers。

sections.title: 為什麼 Models 很難坦承 Uncertainty
sections.summary: Large language models 主要是針對生成看似合理的接續文本進行最佳化，而非保證提供真實的回答。常見的 evaluation 機制將坦承 uncertainty 與答錯給予相同的懲罰，變相鼓勵 model 去猜測，進而主動誘發 hallucinations。雖然 models 在特定條件下展現出些許有限的 self-evaluation 能力，但仍缺乏可靠的機制將 uncertainty detection 泛化至不熟悉的任務。若沒有透過實證 calibration 來驗證回報的分數是否反映實際準確度，單純要求 model 講出 confidence percentages 並無法解決這個問題。
takeaways: Large language models 是針對生成看似合理的文本進行最佳化，而非經過驗證的事實準確度。
將坦承 uncertainty 與答錯給予相同懲罰的評分準則（scoring rubrics）會鼓勵 models 進行猜測，從而導致 hallucinations。
Hallucinations 並不完全是不可避免的架構缺陷；models 仍具備有條件的 self-evaluation 能力。
現有的 models 缺乏內在保證機制，無法在面對全新任務時始終如一地將正確陳述與猜測區分開來。
在缺乏比對回報信心度與實際準確度之 calibration 的情況下，透過 prompt 要求 model 提供 confidence percentage 是不可靠的。

sections.title: 透過 RAG 為 Model 提供 Evidence
sections.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) 藉由檢索相關 documents、增強 model 的 prompt，進而生成有根據的 grounded response，以緩解資訊缺失的問題。在客戶支援等實際應用場景中，檢索到的 policies 能讓 assistant 識別出未滿足的條件，而非做出毫無根據的假設。然而，RAG 也帶來了潛在的 failure modes，包含檢索到過期或錯誤的 policies、遺漏上下文中的例外情況，以及誤解檢索到的段落。為了避免這些問題，documents 必須具備良好結構，並帶有明確的 metadata（例如生效日期與產品名稱），且在 chunked 時應將相關條件保留在一起。
takeaways: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) 的運作包含三個步驟：檢索相關資訊、將其 augmentation 至 prompt 中，以及生成答案。
RAG 讓 models 能夠識別出使用者輸入中尚未滿足特定 policy 條件的情況，而非盲目猜測。
常見的 RAG failure points 包括檢索到過期或不正確的 policies、遺漏例外條款，或是生成缺乏依據的承諾。
用於 RAG 的 documents 需要明確的 metadata（例如清楚的產品名稱、生效日期和審核狀態），以解決 policy 之間的衝突。
Document chunking 應將相關條件保留在一起，以防止檢索到不完整的規則。
檢視 model 所檢索到的精確 context，有助於區分 retrieval failures 與 interpretation errors。

sections.title: 透過 Tools 查詢缺失的 Facts
sections.summary: LLM-based assistants 需要 tools 來檢索客戶專屬的 facts，並執行超出靜態 document policies 範圍的外部操作。透過 APIs 與外部系統互動，models 能將其回應建立在事實查核（factual verification）的基礎上，並減少任務錯誤。透過 RAG 進行 document retrieval 與使用 operational tools 往往相輔相成，共同滿足 policy 條件。為了避免 hallucinations，應用程式必須在將動作或事實呈現為已完成之前，先驗證外部 tool operations 確實成功執行。
takeaways: Tool use 讓 LLM applications 能夠檢索外部資訊，或執行超出 model 直接涵蓋範圍的操作。
透過 tools 與外部資訊來源互動，可減少在評估任務上的錯誤。
當 document retrieval 被實作為外部 tool 時，RAG 與 tool use 就可能產生重疊。
Tool executions 必須實際發生；僅生成宣稱已執行該動作的文本並不是證明，反而會引入 hallucinations。
外部操作（例如發送款項）在 assistant 宣稱完成之前，需要來自外部系統確認執行成功的反饋。

sections.title: 撰寫實用的 Answers
sections.summary: 將「證據不足」視為有效輸出結果，能有效防禦 AI assistant 的 hallucination。透過 instructions 可以引導 assistant 將論點 ground 在提供的文本中，並找出缺少的資訊，而非強行導出缺乏依據的結論。保留部分事實並詳細說明無法給出完整回答的具體障礙，遠比單純承認不知道有用得多。因此，軟體系統應實作如「needs review」這類的中間狀態，而非強制輸出如「eligible」或「ineligible」的二元結果。
takeaways: 將證據不足視為可接受且有效的結果，可作為防禦 hallucination 的手段。
明確的 instructions 可以引導模型識別缺失的資訊，並將論點 ground 在提供的資料上，進而減少 hallucination。
提供指出缺少哪些條件的部分回答，比單純承認不知道更有用。
系統設計應納入如「needs review」等非二元狀態來處理證據缺失的情況，而非採用嚴格的二元結果。

sections.title: 為什麼 Explanation 不等於 Proof
sections.summary: Chain-of-thought prompting 會提示模型透過中間步驟解決問題，這能改善回答品質並使錯誤更容易被發現。然而，生成的 explanation 並不等於 proof，因為它可能依賴錯誤的前提，或者無法忠實反映模型底層的推論過程。提供更多解釋無法彌補缺失或不準確的 grounding facts。可靠的系統應輸出直接連結到可查證證據的簡明 justification，以便 human reviewer 進行驗證。
takeaways: Chain-of-thought prompting 要求模型透過中間步驟推導問題，有助於提升任務表現。
生成的 explanation 並非 proof，且可能不忠實反映推論過程或基於錯誤的前提。
增加更多 explanation 並不能補足缺失或錯誤的事實。
有效的系統應將 justification 連結到可查證的證據，例如特定的 policy 條款與帳戶資料。

sections.title: 在回答送達客戶前進行檢查
sections.summary: Verification 應作為 workflow 中的獨立階段來實作，以系統性地減少 hallucination。Response 必須被拆解為個別的事實 claims，以便移除缺乏證據的陳述。Citation 有助於這些檢查，但 citation 本身也需要針對來源文件的存在性與引用精確度進行 verification。最後，調低 sampling temperature 等技術並無法保證真實性，因此對於執行明確無歧義的規則，deterministic code 仍是更好的選擇。
takeaways: 先起草回答、生成 verification questions，並獨立回答這些問題，可以減少 hallucination。
複雜的 response 包含多個不同的 claims，每個 claim 都需要獨立的證據，且應移除缺乏依據的 claim。
只有在針對存在性、相關性以及逐字文本支持（verbatim textual support）進行驗證後，citation 才能提升可靠性。
降低 sampling temperature 會集中機率分佈，但並不能保證事實的正確性。
Deterministic application code 可以根據已驗證的事實來評估明確無歧義的 policy 規則，而將 language models 保留用於 explanation。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: 改善後的 LLM-based 客服 workflow 透過執行結構化流程（檢索 policy、驗證帳戶事實、驗證 citation）來最大程度地減少 hallucination。缺少資料的個案會獲得明確的 unresolved 狀態，而需要判斷的複雜情境則會被 route 進行審查。系統的可靠性與實用性必須使用包含 edge cases、過期 policy 和錯誤假設的擬真 test cases 進行評估。最終，開發者有責任確保 assistant 的回答嚴格受限於可驗證的證據，而不是過度回答或無謂地拒絕請求。
takeaways: 結構化的支援流程會在定稿 explanation 之前，先驗證 policy、帳戶事實、條件與 citation。
當缺少必要資訊或需要判斷時，系統會產生 unresolved 狀態，或將個案 route 至 human review。
Testing 必須使用擬真情境，例如缺失帳戶記錄、過期的 policy，以及包含錯誤假設的 user prompt。
Evaluation 必須在正確性與實用性之間取得平衡，以防止 assistant 做出缺乏依據的主張，或慣性拒絕可回答的請求。
LLM assistant 應清楚揭露哪些條件已滿足、哪些仍 unresolved，以及哪些證據支持這些 claims。

items.title: AI Agents Can Think. Now They Can Pay.

sections.title: The Problem with Today’s Payment Flow
sections.summary: The internet's underlying infrastructure was built under the assumption that it would be used primarily by human users, but automated traffic now constitutes the majority of web requests. According to Cloudflare, automated systems account for 57.5% of HTTP requests as AI tools rapidly evolve into autonomous agents. Despite this transition, standard online payment interfaces remain tailored to human workflows, creating substantial friction for software. The Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) addresses this gap by offering a standardized payment interface designed for AI agents to settle transactions without human involvement.
takeaways: Automated systems currently generate approximately 57.5% of HTTP requests to web content according to Cloudflare.
AI tools are shifting from reactive conversational chatbots to autonomous agents capable of planning, executing, and evaluating tasks.
Existing web payment systems remain constrained by human-centric design assumptions.
Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) provides an interface that allows AI agents to settle payments directly with online services regardless of payment method.

sections.title: What is MPP?
sections.summary: Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) is a standardized system co-authored by Stripe and Tempo to automate machine-to-machine payment negotiations without human intervention. Submitted to the IETF as the Payment HTTP Authentication Schema, MPP structures payment negotiation into three distinct steps: Challenge, Credential, and Receipt. These interactions occur via standardized HTTP headers, enabling software clients and agents to autonomously discover terms, submit proof of payment, and obtain receipts. Payment methods are governed separately by individual rails, ensuring MPP remains an open, fee-free foundation for internet agent transactions.
takeaways: MPP was co-authored by Stripe and Tempo and launched on March 18, 2026.
The protocol core is published as the Payment HTTP Authentication Schema and submitted to the IETF standards track.
MPP structures transactions around three core objects: Challenge (server request), Credential (client proof), and Receipt (confirmation).
Protocol data is passed via HTTP headers including WWW-Authenticate: Payment, Authorization: Payment, and Payment-Receipt.
Payment rails such as card networks, blockchains, and processors maintain their own specifications to interface with the core protocol.
MPP is open and free, requiring no licensing fees to implement.

sections.title: How Does MPP Work?
sections.summary: The Machine Payment Protocol (MPP) workflow enables autonomous AI agents to pay for API and service access on demand using standard HTTP interactions. When an agent requests a service, the server responds with an HTTP 402 Payment Required status and a challenge header detailing payment terms. The agent verifies the terms against preconfigured delegated spending limits, signs the payment authorization, and retries the request with a payment credential. Upon verification, the server fulfills the request and provides a receipt, avoiding user account creation and preventing unpaid side effects.
takeaways: Servers issue an HTTP 402 response containing a WWW-Authenticate: Payment challenge with terms, amounts, and recipient details.
Agents authorize payments using delegated signing keys that have predefined spending caps, expirations, and recipient scopes rather than relying on LLM reasoning.
Requests are retried with an Authorization: Payment header containing a single-use bearer credential that servers verify before executing any stateful actions.
Failed verifications return a new HTTP 402 status with structured problem details (e.g., payment-insufficient, payment-expired) rather than an HTTP 401.
With payment rails like Stripe, payments map directly to primitives like PaymentIntent without requiring customer account creation or API key purchases.

sections.title: Two use cases of agentic payment
sections.summary: This section serves as an introduction to practical applications of MPP in the context of agentic payments. It signals a shift toward examining concrete scenarios where automated agent payment mechanisms can be utilized. The brief introductory remark frames upcoming examples illustrating these implementations.
takeaways: The section focuses on identifying use cases for MPP.
The broader topic addresses applications of agentic payment systems.
Specific implementation scenarios for agentic payments are framed for subsequent examination.

sections.title: Use Case 1: How AI Agents Can Pay Pennies
sections.summary: AI agents frequently require granular, low-cost services such as web searches or lookups, but standard financial systems make sub-cent transactions unviable due to flat fees and confirmation delays. Traditional internet billing bundles services into subscriptions or credit packs to overcome this threshold, which does not suit the ad-hoc patterns of autonomous agents. To solve this, MPP utilizes session-based payments where an agent deposits funds upfront and issues signed IOUs per request. Once the session terminates, the accumulated total is settled in a single on-chain or banking transaction, lowering transaction costs and verification latency.
takeaways: Moving micro-amounts through traditional banking cards or blockchains incurs flat fees that often exceed the transaction value itself.
Traditional billing relies on subscriptions and bundled credits because single micro-transactions fall below an economically viable cost threshold.
Autonomous agents execute granular, continuous tasks (such as thousands of searches or lookups) that cannot be efficiently bundled into conventional plans.
MPP addresses this friction by introducing sessions where money is set aside as an initial deposit.
Within an MPP session, every individual request is accompanied by a signed digital IOU rather than an immediate financial settlement.
Accumulated IOUs are settled in a single aggregate transaction when the session closes, amortizing the processing fee across thousands of requests.

sections.title: Use Case 2: Purchase ByteByteGo Newsletter Single Article
sections.summary: Micropayment protocols (MPP) enable frictionless pay-per-use transactions, allowing readers to purchase single articles from publications such as ByteByteGo without recurring subscriptions. Demonstrated by Michael Blau using Drip and a Tempo wallet, writers can receive payments as low as a single cent in milliseconds. Looking forward, MPP provides a native protocol-level payment layer for the web, presenting an alternative to ad-driven monetization. Consequently, AI agents can become direct economic participants capable of autonomously purchasing services like compute and data.
takeaways: MPP enables pay-per-use micropayments for individual articles, removing the necessity of long-term subscriptions.
Michael Blau demonstrated single-article purchases for ByteByteGo via Drip with agents transacting through an attached Tempo wallet.
Writers can receive micropayments as low as one cent within milliseconds behind the scenes.
Protocol-level micropayments offer a native payment layer for the internet as an alternative to advertising-funded models.
Autonomous AI agents can use these payment rails to buy compute, data, and other services directly.

sections.title: When Every Customer is a Stranger
sections.summary: Adopting the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) eliminates traditional user signup flows, which complicates customer identification, abuse mitigation, dispute resolution, and commercial sales tracking. Because an MPP transaction exposes only a public key rather than user identity, identity verification and dispute handling are being developed as separate protocol layers. To ensure security and control, the MPP specification introduces strict guardrails, including mandatory TLS, expiring proofs, capped delegated signing keys, payload verification, and advisory-only service directories.
takeaways: Under MPP, payments only verify control of a public key, removing traditional account records like names, emails, and purchase history.
Removing user accounts creates challenges for abuse control, sales conversions from free tiers, and customer contact.
Identity and dispute mechanisms are intentionally designed as separate layers outside of the base MPP payment flow.
Identity specifications backed by Visa and Cloudflare allow agents to sign requests so servers can recognize automated clients across workflows.
MPP does not define a standard refund flow, relying instead on returning unclaimed session funds or refunding directly to the originating payment key via card networks or blockchains.
MPP mandates security guardrails such as mandatory TLS, single-use proofs, no credential logging, capped delegated keys, and strict verification of signed payment payloads over descriptive text.

sections.title: Your Next Customer Might Be an Agent
sections.summary: The Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) has been operational in production since March 2026, logging roughly 30,000 transactions by August 2026. While current transaction numbers are comparatively modest, early adoption resembles the formative stage of the Apple App Store, where early volume underrepresented future platform impact. The key significance is the arrival of automated agents acting as an entirely new category of paying customer.
takeaways: The Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) entered production in March 2026.
As of August 2026, approximately 30,000 transactions have been processed via MPP.
Early MPP transaction volumes are analogized to the initial launch phase of the Apple App Store.
The protocol facilitates commerce driven by automated agents as a new class of customer.

sections.title: 當今支付流程的問題
sections.summary: 網際網路的底層 infrastructure 最初是在主要由人類使用者使用的假設下構建的，但現在 automated traffic 已佔了 web requests 的大部分。根據 Cloudflare 的數據，隨著 AI 工具迅速演進為 autonomous agents，自動化系統已佔 HTTP requests 的 57.5%。儘管發生了這樣的轉變，標準的線上支付介面仍專為人類的工作流程而設計，對軟體造成了相當大的阻力。Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) 透過提供標準化的支付介面來填補這一缺口，專為 AI agents 設計，使其無需人類介入即可結算交易。
takeaways: 根據 Cloudflare，自動化系統目前約佔網頁內容 HTTP requests 的 57.5%。
AI 工具正從被動的回應式對話 chatbots 轉變為能夠規劃、執行與評估任務的 autonomous agents。
現有的 web 支付系統仍受限於以人為中心的設計假設。
Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) 提供了一個介面，讓 AI agents 無論採用何種支付方式，都能直接與線上服務完成款項結算。

sections.title: 什麼是 MPP？
sections.summary: Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) 是一套由 Stripe 與 Tempo 共同制定的標準化系統，旨在無須人為介入的情況下自動化 machine-to-machine 支付協商。MPP 作為 Payment HTTP Authentication Schema 提交至 IETF，將支付協商分為三個明確步驟：Challenge、Credential 與 Receipt。這些互動皆透過標準 HTTP headers 進行，使軟體 clients 與 agents 能夠自主發現條款、提交付款證明並獲取收據。支付方式由各別的 rails 獨立管理，確保 MPP 始終作為網路 agent 交易的開放、免手續費基礎設施。
takeaways: MPP 由 Stripe 與 Tempo 共同制定，並於 2026 年 3 月 18 日推出。
該 protocol core 以 Payment HTTP Authentication Schema 發布，並已提交至 IETF standards track。
MPP 圍繞三個 core objects 構建 transaction：Challenge（server request）、Credential（client proof）以及 Receipt（confirmation）。
Protocol 資料是透過 HTTP headers 傳遞，包括 WWW-Authenticate: Payment、Authorization: Payment 和 Payment-Receipt。
如 card networks、blockchains 與 processors 等 payment rails 會維護各自的規格，以與 core protocol 進行介接。
MPP 是開放且免費的，實作不需要支付任何 licensing fees。

sections.title: MPP 如何運作？
sections.summary: Machine Payment Protocol (MPP) workflow 讓自主 AI agent 能利用標準的 HTTP 互動，隨需支付 API 和服務存取費用。當 agent 請求服務時，server 會回傳 HTTP 402 Payment Required 狀態碼以及詳細列出支付條款的 challenge header。Agent 會對照預先設定的 delegated spending limits 驗證條款、簽署支付授權，並附帶 payment credential 重試 request。驗證成功後，server 會完成該 request 並提供 receipt，從而避免建立使用者帳號並防止未付款的 side effects。
takeaways: Server 會發出 HTTP 402 response，其中包含帶有條款、金額和 recipient 詳細資訊的 WWW-Authenticate: Payment challenge。
Agent 會使用具有預先定義 spending caps、過期時間和 recipient scopes 的 delegated signing keys 來授權支付，而不是依賴 LLM reasoning。
Request 會透過帶有 single-use bearer credential 的 Authorization: Payment header 進行重試，server 會在執行任何 stateful actions 之前對其進行驗證。
驗證失敗時會回傳帶有結構化 problem details（例如 payment-insufficient、payment-expired）的全新 HTTP 402 狀態，而非 HTTP 401。
透過像 Stripe 這樣的 payment rails，支付可以直接對應到像 PaymentIntent 這樣的 primitives，而無需建立客戶帳號或購買 API key。

sections.title: Agentic payment 的兩個使用案例
sections.summary: 本節旨在介紹 MPP 在 agentic payments 背景下的實際應用。這標誌著轉向探討可利用自動化 agent 支付機制的具體情境。簡短的引言為接下來展示這些實作的範例做了鋪陳。
takeaways: 本節著重於探討 MPP 的 use cases。
更廣泛的主題則探討了 agentic payment 系統的應用。
為後續探討設定了 agentic payments 的具體實作情境。

sections.title: Use Case 1：AI Agent 如何支付極小額費用 (Pennies)
sections.summary: AI agent 經常需要細粒度（granular）、低成本的服務（例如網路搜尋或 lookups），但傳統金融系統因固定手續費（flat fees）和確認延遲，使得低於一分錢（sub-cent）的 transaction 變得不可行。傳統網路計費將服務打包成 subscription 或 credit packs 來跨越這個門檻，但這並不適合自主 agent 的 ad-hoc 模式。為了解決這個問題，MPP 採用了 session-based payments：agent 預先存入資金，並在每次 request 發出簽署的 IOU。一旦 session 結束，累積的總額便會在一筆 on-chain 或銀行 transaction 中進行結算，從而降低交易成本與 verification latency。
takeaways: 透過傳統銀行卡或 blockchain 轉移微額資金會產生固定費用（flat fees），這通常會超過交易金額本身。
傳統計費方式依賴 subscription 與打包的 credits，因為單筆微額交易（micro-transaction）低於具經濟效益的成本門檻。
自主 agent 執行的細粒度、連續性任務（例如數千次搜尋或 lookups），無法被有效打包進傳統方案中。
MPP 透過引入 session 來解決這種摩擦，在 session 中資金會被預留作為初始 deposit。
在 MPP session 中，每個單獨的 request 都附帶一份簽署的數位 IOU，而不是立即進行金融結算。
當 session 結束時，累積的 IOU 會在單一筆 aggregate transaction 中完成結算，將處理手續費分攤到數千個 request 上。

sections.title: 當每位客戶都是陌生人時
sections.summary: 採用 Machine Payments Protocol（MPP）消除了傳統的使用者註冊流程，這使得客戶識別、防範濫用、爭議處理和商業銷售追蹤變得更加複雜。由於 MPP 交易僅公開公鑰而非使用者身分，身分驗證和爭議處理正被開發為獨立的協議層。為確保安全性與可控性，MPP 規範引入了嚴格的 guardrail，包括強制性 TLS、具時效性的 proof、設有上限的委託簽署金鑰、payload 驗證，以及僅具建議性質的 service directory。
takeaways: 在 MPP 下，付款僅驗證對公鑰的控制權，移除了姓名、電子郵件和購買歷史記錄等傳統帳號記錄。
移除使用者帳號對濫用防範、免費方案的銷售轉換以及客戶聯繫帶來了挑戰。
身分與爭議機制被刻意設計在基礎 MPP 支付流程之外的獨立層級。
由 Visa 和 Cloudflare 支援的身分規格允許 agent 對 request 進行簽署，讓伺服器能在跨 workflow 中辨識自動化 client。
MPP 沒有定義標準的退款流程，而是依賴歸還未請領的 session 資金，或透過信用卡網路或區塊鏈直接退款至發起付款的 key。
MPP 強制要求安全 guardrail，例如強制性 TLS、單次使用 proof、不記錄 credential、設有上限的委託金鑰，以及對已簽署的 payment payload 進行嚴格驗證（優先於描述性文字）。

sections.title: Your agent hit a wall. Beacon handoff lets another one pick up where it left off.
sections.summary: Beacon is an open-source memory layer designed to solve the problem of context fragmentation across different AI coding agents. It captures session activity from tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex, allowing users to resume work in a different agent without starting over. By generating handoff briefs or using native resume commands, Beacon ensures that progress made in one session is portable across various agent harnesses. The tool operates locally, reading session stores directly from the user's machine to maintain privacy and security.
takeaways: Beacon provides a portable memory layer that captures activity across 20+ coding agent harnesses.
The beacon handoff command allows users to resume sessions in the same or a different agent.
When native resume is unavailable, Beacon generates a handoff brief containing goals, progress, and relevant files.
The tool is local-first, reading session stores on the user's machine without uploading data.
Beacon supports major coding agents including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and Cline.
It is an open-source project developed by Asymptote Labs.

sections.title: System 1 vs. System 2 Agent Harnesses
sections.summary: The text distinguishes between System 1 and System 2 AI integration patterns, where System 1 handles bounded judgments and System 2 manages open-ended, multi-step tasks. HarnessRouter is introduced as an open-source infrastructure layer designed to unify these patterns under a single execution framework. By utilizing the Unified Harness Protocol, developers can manage diverse AI workflows without rebuilding task lifecycles for every specific model or runtime.
takeaways: System 1 harnesses are designed for fast, bounded judgments where the application code maintains control over the workflow.
System 2 harnesses are used for complex tasks like coding or research where the LLM plans steps but operates within guarded tool permissions.
HarnessRouter is an open-source infrastructure layer that standardizes the execution of both System 1 and System 2 patterns.
The Unified Harness Protocol provides a single contract for task management, including streaming progress, file exchange, and failure reporting.
Specific models like Jev are optimized for System 1 roles, while Codex, Claude Code, and Hermes are used for System 2 agent-harness bases.

sections.title: How MoE routing works across GPUs?
sections.summary: Mixture of Experts (MoE) layers reduce computational FLOPs by activating only a subset of experts for each token, but they introduce significant communication overhead when experts are distributed across multiple GPUs. A router determines expert assignments, necessitating the transfer of activation vectors via interconnects like NVLink for intra-server or InfiniBand for inter-server communication. This 'all-to-all' communication pattern can increase end-to-end latency despite the reduced per-token computation. Optimization techniques such as balanced routing and communication overlap are essential to mitigate these networking delays.
takeaways: MoE layers replace dense feed-forward networks with multiple experts, executing only a small subset of weights per token.
Inference latency may increase in MoE models because the system must move activation vectors between GPUs where specific experts are stored.
Intra-server GPU communication is typically handled by high-bandwidth fabrics like NVLink and NVSwitch.
Inter-server communication for MoE routing often utilizes InfiniBand or Ethernet cluster networks.
The exchange of activations across a batch of tokens and multiple GPUs is referred to as all-to-all communication.
Optimization strategies for MoE include balanced routing to prevent GPU bottlenecks and overlapping communication with local computation.

sections.summary: 文中區分了 System 1 與 System 2 AI 整合模式，其中 System 1 處理有界限的判定，而 System 2 負責處理開放式、多步驟的任務。HarnessRouter 作為一個開源 infrastructure layer 被引入，旨在將這些模式統整在單一 execution framework 之下。透過採用 Unified Harness Protocol，開發者可以管理多元的 AI workflow，而無需為每個特定 model 或 runtime 重建 task lifecycle。

sections.title: 跨 GPU 的 MoE routing 是如何運作的？
sections.summary: Mixture of Experts (MoE) layer 透過對每個 token 僅啟動部分 expert 來降低計算 FLOPs，但當 expert 分散在多張 GPU 時，會帶來顯著的 communication overhead。Router 決定 expert assignment，因此需要透過 intra-server 的 NVLink 或 inter-server 的 InfiniBand 等 interconnect 傳輸 activation vector。儘管減少了 per-token 計算量，這種「all-to-all」通訊模式仍可能增加 end-to-end 延遲。因此，balanced routing 與 communication overlap 等最佳化技術對於減緩這些網路延遲至關重要。
takeaways: MoE layer 取代了 dense feed-forward network，改用多個 expert，每個 token 僅執行少部分權重計算。
MoE model 的推論延遲可能會增加，因為系統必須在存放特定 expert 的不同 GPU 之間傳遞 activation vector。
Intra-server 的 GPU 通訊通常由 NVLink 和 NVSwitch 等高頻寬 fabric 負責處理。
用於 MoE routing 的 inter-server 通訊通常仰賴 InfiniBand 或 Ethernet 叢集網路。
跨 token batch 與多個 GPU 交換 activation 的過程稱為 all-to-all communication。
MoE 的最佳化策略包括透過 balanced routing 來避免 GPU bottleneck，以及將 communication 與 local computation 進行重疊（overlapping）。

sections.title: LLM, RAG, AI Agent & Agentic AI
sections.summary: This section defines and contrasts four core paradigms in modern AI: LLMs, RAG, AI agents, and Agentic AI. A base LLM generates responses directly from learned parameters by predicting tokens sequentially. RAG incorporates a retriever to ground LLM outputs with external indexed knowledge, though it cannot guarantee complete correctness. AI agents introduce goal orientation, tool calling, and feedback loops to dynamically track state and achieve objectives, while Agentic AI orchestrates multiple agents and workflows using shared states to fulfill broader goals.
takeaways: An LLM generates text by predicting tokens one at a time using its learned parameters.
RAG sends a query to a retriever first to fetch relevant data from an indexed knowledge base before passing it to the LLM.
RAG produces grounded responses, but correctness is not guaranteed.
An AI agent maintains task state, plans actions, utilizes tools, and iteratively updates actions via a feedback loop until a goal is met.
Agentic AI systems employ an orchestration layer to coordinate multiple AI agents and workflows toward a shared objective.
Agents in an agentic system read and write to shared task states while accessing tools, data, and their environment.

sections.title: MCP vs Function calling
sections.summary: Both Model Context Protocol (MCP) and function calling are mechanisms that enable large language models to interact with tools via an agent runtime. In both paradigms, the model identifies which tool to call and emits a request that the runtime executes before returning results back to the model. The key distinction is execution architecture: traditional function calling runs functions locally on the user's machine, whereas MCP communicates over a standardized protocol to execute tools hosted on remote servers. This distinction allows MCP agents to seamlessly interface with vast ecosystems of publicly and remotely hosted tools.
takeaways: Both MCP and function calling allow LLMs to select and trigger external tools via an agent runtime.
The primary difference between MCP and function calling is where functions are implemented and executed.
In local function calling, functions reside and execute directly on the user's local machine.
MCP enables tool execution on remote servers using the MCP protocol.
MCP allows an agent runtime to integrate with hundreds of thousands of remotely hosted, publicly accessible tools.

sections.title: If Claude Code is a burger...
sections.summary: Claude Code constructs its context window by assembling information from nine distinct sources before each model call. The architecture also integrates dynamically fetched auto memory, path-scoped rules, tool specifications, and conversation history. To manage context limits over long interactions, older conversation segments are systematically replaced by compact model-generated summaries.
takeaways: Claude Code constructs its context window from nine distinct layers prior to each model invocation.
CLAUDE.md organizes instructions across a four-level hierarchy spanning managed, user, project, and local scopes.
Environment data including Git status and branch info is gathered dynamically via getSystemContext().
Auto Memory uses an LLM to scan file headers asynchronously and retrieve up to five relevant memory files on demand.
Long-running conversation history is condensed using model-generated compact summaries when length limits are approached.

sections.title: LLM、RAG、AI Agent 與 Agentic AI
sections.summary: 本節定義並比較現代 AI 的四大核心範式（paradigms）：LLMs、RAG、AI agents 與 Agentic AI。Base LLM 透過循序預測 token，直接從學習到的參數中生成回應。RAG 結合了 retriever，利用外部索引知識來為 LLM 輸出提供依據（grounding），但無法保證完全正確。AI agents 引入目標導向、tool calling 與回饋迴圈（feedback loops）來動態追蹤狀態並達成目標，而 Agentic AI 則透過共享狀態編排（orchestrate）多個 agents 與 workflows，以實現更宏大的目標。

Agentic AI 系統採用 orchestration layer 來協調多個 AI agents 與 workflows，以邁向共同目標。
Agentic 系統中的 agents 在存取工具、資料及其環境的同時，也會對共享的任務狀態進行讀寫。

sections.title: MCP vs Function calling

MCP 與 function calling 之間的主要差異在於函式的實作與執行位置。
在 local function calling 中，函式直接常駐並執行於使用者的本機端。
MCP 透過 MCP protocol 實現遠端伺服器上的工具執行。
MCP 讓 agent runtime 能夠整合數十萬個遠端託管、公開可存取的工具。

sections.title: Your best model shouldn’t be answering every request
sections.summary: TrueFoundry's Auto Routing feature optimizes LLM production traffic by classifying requests based on complexity and routing them to appropriate models. The system uses zero-latency heuristics to categorize tasks into simple, medium, or complex tiers. This approach maintains conversation context and provides fallback mechanisms if a lower-tier model fails. Benchmarks show significant cost savings with minimal impact on output quality compared to using high-end models for all tasks.
takeaways: TrueFoundry Auto Routing classifies incoming LLM requests into three tiers: simple, medium, and complex.
The classification process uses in-process heuristics based on signals like code or reasoning phrases to avoid added latency.
Conversation pinning ensures that follow-up requests in a complex thread remain with the higher-tier model.
The system includes an automatic fallback that moves requests to a higher tier if the assigned model fails.
In testing against an all-Opus baseline, the routing system reduced costs by 69% while maintaining 98% quality.

sections.title: Contrastive Language Model, clearly explained
sections.summary: NVIDIA and Stanford researchers have introduced the Contrastive Language Model (CLM), a System 1 architecture designed for rapid decision-making in AI agents. Unlike traditional LLMs that generate text token-by-token, CLM treats decision-making as a retrieval problem by encoding states and actions into a shared vector space. This approach allows for action embeddings to be cached, resulting in up to 9x lower latency compared to the Jev model while maintaining comparable performance in gaming and tool-calling tasks. The model uses a frozen Qwen3-8B backbone and is trained using contrastive learning techniques.
takeaways: CLM treats AI decision-making as a retrieval task rather than a generative one, improving speed for repeated actions.
The architecture achieves up to 9x faster performance than the Jev model by caching action embeddings and using cheap dot products.
The model utilizes a frozen Qwen3-8B backbone with a small trainable state projection head.
Training follows a three-stage process using InfoNCE, starting with QA pairs and moving to real agent trajectories.
CLM is optimized for System 1 tasks such as tool selection, request routing, and game actions.
While highly efficient, CLM cannot generate new actions and is limited to evaluating supplied candidates.
The research and code for CLM are open-source.

sections.summary: NVIDIA 與 Stanford 的研究人員推出了 Contrastive Language Model (CLM)，這是一種專為 AI agent 快速決策設計的 System 1 架構。不同於傳統以 token-by-token 方式生成文字的 LLM，CLM 將決策視為 retrieval 問題，把 state 與 action 編碼至同一個向量空間中。這種方法允許快取 action embedding，與 Jev 模型相比延遲降低高達 9 倍，同時在遊戲和 tool-calling 任務中保持相當的表現。該模型採用 frozen Qwen3-8B backbone，並使用 contrastive learning 技術進行訓練。

items.title: The Life of Data: From Creation to Deletion

sections.title: The Life of Data: From Creation to Deletion
sections.summary: While web applications appear simple to users, underlying data is replicated across multiple components as a system grows. A single record commonly exists in databases, caches, search engine indices, analytics pipelines, and backups, each fulfilling a different purpose with its own lifespan and update schedule. Understanding the end-to-end data lifecycle helps connect distinct architectural and operational decisions, including system performance, storage costs, database design, recovery, and privacy.
takeaways: Data within growing systems rarely resides in a single location and is replicated across various architectural components.
A single record may be copied or transformed across databases, caches, search engine indices, analytics pipelines, and backups.
Each copy of data maintains its own dedicated purpose, update frequency, and overall lifespan.
Tracing the data lifecycle unifies architectural decisions across database design, performance, privacy, reporting, storage costs, and recovery.

items.title: Build a Jev Judge

sections.title: Another brilliant course by Andrew Ng!
sections.summary: DeepLearning.AI and Oracle have launched a free course titled 'Building Adaptive AI Agents' to help developers prevent coding agents from repeating errors. The curriculum focuses on transforming noisy execution traces into structured, reusable procedures and code knowledge graphs. It also covers the specific conditions under which model fine-tuning is necessary to resolve persistent failures. Students learn a multi-layered approach to agent adaptation that combines procedural learning, structural context retrieval, and weight adjustment.
takeaways: Raw execution traces often contain redundant or misleading information like abandoned hypotheses.
The course introduces a three-layer adaptation framework: procedure extraction, context retrieval, and fine-tuning.
Agents can extract reusable procedures from traces, which are then validated by humans.
Code knowledge graphs utilize Git history and structural imports to improve retrieval beyond simple keyword search.
Fine-tuning is specifically reserved for failures that persist even when the agent has access to correct procedures and context.

sections.title: MoE inference engineering, clearly explained
sections.summary: Jev is a specialized model from TypeSafe AI designed for structured decision-making and agent evaluation, offering an alternative to traditional generative LLM judges. Unlike generative models that produce text token-by-token, Jev returns typed values from a predefined answer space, which reduces latency and cost. It works by evaluating multiple independent questions against a shared state in parallel. When paired with observability tools like Opik, it allows teams to scale their evaluation workflows and catch failures more efficiently.
takeaways: Jev uses a typed interface to return structured values instead of generating free-form text, reducing token usage and latency.
The model evaluates multiple independent questions against the same context (state) in a single request to improve efficiency.
Opik serves as the observability and experimentation layer, recording traces and evaluation results produced by Jev.
Jev's Noul primitive returns a probability for a proposition, while the Score primitive provides a probability-weighted average across rubric levels.
Jev is optimized for focused, bounded judgments rather than evaluations requiring detailed written explanations or complex hidden reasoning.
Evaluation systems using Jev should still incorporate deterministic checks for exact rules and human review for uncertain cases.

sections.title: Redis built a cache that cuts LLM costs by 70%!
sections.summary: Redis LangCache is a semantic caching service designed to optimize LLM application performance and cost. By using embeddings to match semantically similar queries, it avoids redundant LLM calls that traditional prefix caching cannot prevent. The service provides a managed environment with features like similarity thresholds, access control, and monitoring. Users can achieve up to 15x faster response times and 70% cost savings on cache hits.
takeaways: Semantic caching allows for reusing LLM responses even when query wording differs but meaning is the same.
Redis LangCache uses embeddings and similarity thresholds to match incoming queries with stored responses.
A cache hit in LangCache eliminates the need for an LLM call, reducing latency by up to 15x.
The service can reduce LLM-related costs by approximately 70% depending on workload repetition.
Redis manages infrastructure details like TTL, eviction, and access scopes via a REST API.

sections.title: MoE inference engineering, clearly explained
sections.summary: Mixture of Experts (MoE) inference engineering focuses on optimizing the execution of sparse models where only a subset of 'experts' is activated per token. While MoE reduces the computation required per token, the serving system must still manage the memory footprint of the entire model's parameters. Efficient deployment requires specialized techniques like dispatching tokens into expert-specific matrices, using grouped GEMM for execution, and managing expert parallelism across multiple GPUs to handle interconnect bottlenecks.
takeaways: MoE layers replace dense feed-forward networks with a router and multiple experts, reducing per-token computation but not the total memory footprint.
The Qwen3-30B-A3B model utilizes 3.3 billion activated parameters out of 30.5 billion total parameters by selecting 8 of 128 experts per token.
The MoE serving path consists of routing, dispatch (grouping tokens), expert execution (GEMM), and combine (merging results).
Grouped GEMM is a critical optimization that allows the GPU to execute multiple expert matrices of varying sizes in a single kernel launch.
Expert parallelism distributes experts across GPUs, necessitating all-to-all communication of token activations rather than moving weights.
Resident parameters, which include all selectable experts and attention weights, determine the actual GPU memory requirements for deployment.
DeepSeekMoE and DeepSeek-V3 introduce architectural variations like shared experts and node-limited routing to optimize performance and communication.

items.title: How to Customize a Model to Learn New Tricks

sections.title: When Instructions and Information Are Not Enough
sections.summary: Model customization begins with prompting and few-shot examples to define constraints and output expectations. When required context or updated documentation is missing, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) supplies external data directly into the request input without modifying model parameters. If recurring weaknesses persist or input token overhead becomes prohibitive, fine-tuning provides an alternative by updating model parameters directly through training on examples. While fine-tuning embeds default behaviors and internalizes facts, retrieval remains necessary when information changes frequently or requires traceable sourcing.
takeaways: Prompting and few-shot prompting guide model behavior using input instructions and examples without altering model parameters.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) incorporates external or updated information into a model's input at query time.
Relying on large numbers of prompt examples increases the amount of input that applications must process and maintain.
Fine-tuning trains a model on many examples to embed desired behaviors directly into learned parameters.
Retrieval remains preferred over fine-tuning when underlying information changes frequently or traceable answers are required.

sections.title: How Fine-Tuning Changes an Existing Model
sections.summary: Fine-tuning adapts an existing pretrained model to specific tasks using a targeted dataset, significantly reducing the training needed compared to pretraining from scratch. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) uses input-target pairs to update model parameters via backpropagation and an optimizer based on measured loss. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) addresses SFT's limitations by training a separate reward model based on human-ranked outputs. While full fine-tuning modifies every parameter and incurs heavy memory costs, efficient methods like LoRA and QLoRA allow adaptation without adjusting every parameter independently.
takeaways: Fine-tuning builds on capabilities acquired during pretraining, lowering the amount of training required for specialization.
Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) measures prediction loss against target responses and updates parameters using backpropagation and an optimizer.
Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) ranks multiple generated responses to train a separate reward model that scores quality, helpfulness, and safety.
Full fine-tuning allows every model parameter to be updated, requiring substantial GPU memory to store weights, update states, and intermediate activations.
LoRA and QLoRA provide efficient alternatives to full fine-tuning by avoiding independent adjustments to every parameter.

sections.title: LoRA: Learning a Smaller Set of Changes
sections.summary: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that minimizes the number of parameters updated during training. It keeps original model weights frozen and attaches small trainable adapter components to internal calculations. These adapters use pairs of compact low-rank matrices to compute additive adjustments to the model's intermediate representations. A configurable rank setting dictates adapter capacity and resource overhead, enabling targeted adaptation of attention and other layer transformations without altering the base model's foundation.
takeaways: LoRA freezes original model weights and updates only small trainable adapter components attached to internal computations.
Each adapter is implemented via two compact matrices that create an intermediate representation and produce additive adjustments.
The rank hyperparameter dictates adapter capacity, balancing adaptation flexibility against parameter size and compute costs.
Standard LoRA adapters begin training with zero contribution, ensuring the model retains its original behavior at initialization.
LoRA can target specific internal operations, such as attention calculations and layer transformations.

sections.title: QLoRA: Reducing the Memory the Frozen Model Still Needs
sections.summary: While LoRA reduces parameter update costs, the frozen base model still consumes significant memory for large models. QLoRA solves this problem by combining LoRA with quantization, typically storing the frozen base weights in a 4-bit format while keeping trainable adapters in 16-bit or 32-bit precision. Compressed weights are dynamically reconstructed to higher precision during calculation so adapters can train on the combined output. This approach allows larger models to be fine-tuned within a fixed memory budget, although total memory is still affected by activations and workspace.
takeaways: QLoRA combines LoRA with weight quantization to reduce the memory footprint of the frozen base model.
QLoRA commonly stores frozen base weights in 4-bit precision while maintaining adapter parameters in 16-bit or 32-bit representations.
Base weights are stored in a compact format and reconstructed into higher-precision approximations during computation.
Adapters learn alongside the quantized base model, which allows them to adapt to and partially recover performance lost to quantization error.
Compressed weights only account for part of the memory profile; optimizer states, intermediate activations, and working space still require capacity.

sections.title: Turning the Techniques Into a Training Process
sections.summary: Setting up an effective fine-tuning process requires selecting a capable base model and establishing a prompt baseline before training begins. Training data must be rigorously prepared and partitioned into distinct training, validation, and test splits to prevent data leakage and contradictory signals. Key configuration parameters such as rank, adapter placement, learning rate, batch size, gradient accumulation, and gradient checkpointing manage capacity, memory constraints, and stability. Finally, evaluation must track task-specific correctness and ensure that adapter training does not degrade other essential capabilities.
takeaways: A baseline should be established with a prompt before training to measure improvement accurately.
Data must be strictly split into training, validation, and test sets without duplicate or related examples leaking across splits.
Contradictory labels or unsupported summary claims in the training data directly degrade learned behavior.
Gradient accumulation and gradient checkpointing reduce memory requirements during training and complement LoRA or QLoRA.
Overfitting occurs when training performance continues to improve while validation performance worsens, often requiring an earlier checkpoint.
Fine-tuning adapters can degrade existing capabilities even while keeping original weights frozen, necessitating end-to-end evaluation.

sections.title: Using the Specialization in an Application
sections.summary: LoRA training produces lightweight adapter weights that can remain separate from the base model or be merged directly into it. Keeping adapters separate enables a single base model to serve multiple tasks, whereas merging eliminates runtime adapter overhead at the expense of higher storage. Implementation details for merging and quantization can alter numerical representations and outputs, requiring evaluation of the exact deployment version. Specialized models can continue to operate alongside standard application patterns like prompts, RAG, and output validation.
takeaways: LoRA adapter files are significantly smaller than full models but require a compatible base checkpoint to function.
A single base model can be combined with different adapters to efficiently serve multiple specialized tasks.
Merging adapter weights into the base model creates a standalone full model, eliminating separate adapter computations at the cost of storage.
Quantization and merging behavior vary across serving implementations and can alter numerical representations and model outputs.
Specialized fine-tuned models can be combined with prompts, RAG pipelines, and output validation code.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: Fine-tuning enables models with broad capabilities to achieve reliable specialization by learning from demonstrations and recurring response patterns. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning approaches like LoRA reduce computational costs by training compact adjustments over frozen original weights. QLoRA builds upon this by storing those frozen base weights at lower precision to significantly decrease memory consumption. However, these techniques must be paired with representative training data, clear task definitions, and thorough evaluation to achieve measurable improvements.
takeaways: Fine-tuning adapts broadly capable models toward reliable specialization via demonstration data.
LoRA reduces fine-tuning costs by training compact weight adjustments while leaving original model weights frozen.
QLoRA further cuts memory overhead by quantizing the frozen weights to lower precision.
Neither LoRA nor QLoRA substitutes for quality examples, well-defined tasks, or thorough evaluation.

items.summary: Model customization begins with prompting and few-shot examples to define constraints and output expectations. When required context or updated documentation is missing, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) supplies external data directly into the request input without modifying model parameters. If recurring weaknesses persist or input token overhead becomes prohibitive, fine-tuning provides an alternative by updating model parameters directly through training on examples. While fine-tuning embeds default behaviors and internalizes facts, retrieval remains necessary when information changes frequently or requires traceable sourcing. Fine-tuning adapts an existing pretrained model to specific tasks using a targeted dataset, significantly reducing the training needed compared to pretraining from scratch. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) uses input-target pairs to update model parameters via backpropagation and an optimizer based on measured loss. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) addresses SFT's limitations by training a separate reward model based on human-ranked outputs. While full fine-tuning modifies every parameter and incurs heavy memory costs, efficient methods like LoRA and QLoRA allow adaptation without adjusting every parameter independently. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that minimizes the number of parameters updated during training. It keeps original model weights frozen and attaches small trainable adapter components to internal calculations. These adapters use pairs of compact low-rank matrices to compute additive adjustments to the model's intermediate representations. A configurable rank setting dictates adapter capacity and resource overhead, enabling targeted adaptation of attention and other layer transformations without altering the base model's foundation.
