sections.title: 當 Instructions 與 Information 不足時
sections.summary: 模型客製化始於 prompting 和 few-shot examples，用以定義 constraints 和 output 預期。當缺少必要的 context 或更新的 documentation 時，retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) 會直接將外部資料提供給 request input，而無需修改 model parameters。若反覆出現的弱點持續存在，或是 input token overhead 變得難以承受，fine-tuning 則透過在 examples 上進行 training 直接更新 model parameters，提供另一種解決方案。雖然 fine-tuning 能內建預設行為並內化事實，但當資訊頻繁變更或需要可追溯的來源時，retrieval 仍然是必要的。
takeaways: Prompting 和 few-shot prompting 利用 input instructions 和 examples 來引導模型行為，而無需修改 model parameters。
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) 在 query time 將外部或更新的資訊整合至模型的 input 中。
依賴大量的 prompt examples 會增加 applications 必須處理與維護的 input 數量。
Fine-tuning 在大量 examples 上訓練模型，將期望的行為直接內嵌至學到的 parameters 中。
當底層資訊頻繁變更或需要可追溯的答案時，retrieval 仍優於 fine-tuning。

sections.title: Fine-Tuning 如何改變現有模型
sections.summary: Fine-tuning 使用目標 dataset 使現有的 pretrained model 適應特定 tasks，相較於從頭開始 pretraining，大幅減少了所需的 training。Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) 使用 input-target pairs，透過 backpropagation 和基於量測 loss 的 optimizer 來更新 model parameters。Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) 則透過訓練一個基於人類排序輸出的獨立 reward model，來解決 SFT 的局限性。雖然 full fine-tuning 會修改每一個 parameter 並帶來沉重的 memory 開銷，但像 LoRA 和 QLoRA 這樣的高效方法則允許在不單獨調整每個 parameter 的情況下進行 adaptation。
takeaways: Fine-tuning 建立在 pretraining 期間獲得的能力之上，降低了特化所需的 training 量。
Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) 評估相對於 target responses 的 prediction loss，並使用 backpropagation 和 optimizer 來更新 parameters。
Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) 對多個 generated responses 進行排序，以訓練一個獨立的 reward model 來為 quality、helpfulness 和 safety 評分。
Full fine-tuning 允許更新每一個 model parameter，這需要龐大的 GPU memory 來儲存 weights、update states 以及 intermediate activations。
LoRA 和 QLoRA 透過避免單獨調整每一個 parameter，提供了 full fine-tuning 的高效替代方案。

sections.title: LoRA：學習更小幅度的變更
sections.summary: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) 是一種 parameter-efficient fine-tuning 方法，能將 training 期間更新的 parameters 數量降至最低。它保持原始的 model weights frozen，並在內部計算中附加小型的可訓練 adapter 組件。這些 adapters 使用成對的緊湊 low-rank matrices 來計算對模型 intermediate representations 的加法調整。可配置的 rank 設定決定了 adapter capacity 和 resource overhead，從而在不改變 base model 基礎的情況下，實現對 attention 和其他 layer transformations 的針對性 adaptation。
takeaways: LoRA 會 freeze 原始的 model weights，僅更新附加在內部計算上的小型可訓練 adapter 組件。
每個 adapter 都是透過兩個緊湊的 matrices 實作，用以建立 intermediate representation 並產生加法調整。
Rank hyperparameter 決定了 adapter capacity，在 adaptation 靈活性與 parameter size 及 compute costs 之間取得平衡。
標準 LoRA adapter 在開始 training 時貢獻為零，確保 model 在 initialization 時保有原本的行為。
LoRA 可以針對特定的內部運算，例如 attention 計算與 layer 轉換。

sections.title: QLoRA：減少 frozen model 仍需要的 memory
sections.summary: 雖然 LoRA 降低了 parameter 更新的成本，但在大型 model 中，frozen base model 仍會消耗大量 memory。QLoRA 透過結合 LoRA 與 quantization 解決了這個問題，通常將 frozen base weights 儲存為 4-bit 格式，同時將可訓練的 adapter 維持在 16-bit 或 32-bit precision。壓縮後的 weights 在計算過程中會動態 reconstruct 為較高 precision，以便 adapter 能夠基於結合後的 output 進行訓練。這種做法讓較大的 model 能夠在固定的 memory budget 內進行 fine-tuning，儘管整體 memory 仍會受到 activations 與 workspace 的影響。
takeaways: QLoRA 結合 LoRA 與 weight quantization，以減少 frozen base model 的 memory footprint。
QLoRA 通常將 frozen base weights 儲存為 4-bit precision，同時將 adapter parameters 維持在 16-bit 或 32-bit representation。
Base weights 以緊湊格式儲存，並在計算過程中 reconstruct 為較高 precision 的近似值。
Adapter 會與 quantized base model 一起學習，使其能夠適應並部分恢復因 quantization error 所損失的 performance。
壓縮後的 weights 僅佔 memory profile 的一部分；optimizer states、中間的 activations 與 working space 仍需要容量。

sections.title: 將技術轉化為 training process
sections.summary: 建立有效的 fine-tuning process 需要在 training 開始前選擇具備足夠能力的 base model，並建立 prompt baseline。Training data 必須嚴格準備並切分為獨立的 training、validation 與 test splits，以防止 data leakage 與矛盾訊號。關鍵 configuration parameters（例如 rank、adapter placement、learning rate、batch size、gradient accumulation 和 gradient checkpointing）能用來管理 capacity、memory constraints 與穩定性。最後，evaluation 必須追蹤特定 task 的正確性，並確保 adapter training 不會降低其他關鍵能力。
takeaways: 在 training 前應先使用 prompt 建立 baseline，以準確衡量改善程度。
Data 必須嚴格切分為 training、validation 和 test sets，避免重複或相關的 examples 跨 split 洩漏。
Training data 中相互矛盾的 labels 或缺乏依據的 summary claims 會直接損害 model 學到的行為。
Gradient accumulation 與 gradient checkpointing 能減少 training 期間的 memory 需求，並與 LoRA 或 QLoRA 形成互補。
當 training performance 持續提升而 validation performance 惡化時，即表示發生 overfitting，通常需要退回較早的 checkpoint。
即使保持原始 weights 處於 frozen 狀態，fine-tuning adapter 仍可能降低現有能力，因此必須進行 end-to-end evaluation。

sections.title: 在 application 中運用 specialization
sections.summary: LoRA training 會產生輕量化的 adapter weights，這些 weights 可以與 base model 分開保留，或直接 merge 進 base model。保持 adapter 獨立可以讓單一 base model 支援多個 tasks；而 merge 則能消除 runtime adapter overhead，但代價是需要更多儲存空間。Merging 與 quantization 的實作細節可能會改變 numerical representations 與 outputs，因此需要對實際部署的版本進行 evaluation。Specialized models 可以繼續與標準 application patterns（如 prompt、RAG 和 output validation）協同運作。
takeaways: LoRA adapter 檔案比完整 model 小得多，但需要相容的 base checkpoint 才能運作。
單一 base model 可以與不同的 adapters 結合，以高效率支援多個 specialized tasks。
將 adapter weights merge 到 base model 中會建立一個獨立的 full model，以儲存空間為代價消除額外的 adapter 計算。
Quantization 與 merging 行為在不同的 serving 實作中會有所差異，且可能會改變 numerical representations 與 model outputs。
Specialized fine-tuned models 可以與 prompt、RAG pipeline 以及 output validation 程式碼結合使用。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: Fine-tuning 讓具備廣泛通用能力的模型能透過示範資料與反覆出現的回應模式進行學習，從而實現可靠的專業化（specialization）。像 LoRA 這類 parameter-efficient fine-tuning 方法，透過在凍結的原始權重上訓練精簡的調整參數來降低運算成本。QLoRA 則在此基礎上，將這些凍結的 base weights 以較低精度儲存，進而大幅減少記憶體消耗。然而，這些技術仍必須搭配具代表性的訓練資料、明確的任務定義以及嚴謹的評測，才能取得可量化的改進。
takeaways: Fine-tuning 透過示範資料，將具備廣泛通用能力的模型調整至可靠的專業化程度。
LoRA 透過在凍結原始模型權重的同時訓練精簡的權重調整參數，以降低 fine-tuning 成本。
QLoRA 透過將凍結的權重量化為較低精度，進一步降低記憶體開銷。
無論是 LoRA 還是 QLoRA，都無法取代高品質的範例、定義明確的任務或嚴謹的評測。

items.title: Agentic AI Weekly | Berkeley RDI | September 23, 2026

sections.title: From 10× Ideas to Discovery Loops
sections.summary: Jeff Dean, former Chief Scientist at Google, engaged in his first public talk since leaving the company after 27 years. In a conversation hosted by Professor Dawn Song, Dean discussed his perspective on future technological frontiers rather than simply reviewing his past accomplishments. The discussion centered on identifying high-impact research problems before they become obvious and exploring how AI can accelerate discovery loops.
takeaways: Jeff Dean left Google after 27 years to serve as Co-founder and CEO of Discovery Loop.
Dean's work at Google spanned foundational computing and AI systems including MapReduce, Bigtable, TensorFlow, Mixture-of-Experts, TPUs, and Gemini.
In his first post-Google public appearance, Dean held a wide-ranging discussion with Professor Dawn Song.
The conversation emphasized recognizing high-value research directions early and leveraging AI to speed up scientific discovery.

sections.title: 1. AI Could Change the Speed of Discovery Itself
sections.summary: The concept of recursive self-improvement in AI is expanding from automating isolated tasks to accelerating entire research and development lifecycles. Historical methods like Neural Architecture Search and architectures like the Evolved Transformer demonstrated automated model discovery, but current efforts seek to automate full experimental feedback loops. This framework applies broadly across scientific and engineering disciplines where experimentation and evaluation drive progress. A company called Discovery Loop aims to dramatically compress iteration cycles and run thousands of parallel experiments to accelerate the speed of discovery itself.
takeaways: Recursive self-improvement in machine learning is expanding from automating individual design tasks to automating the complete R&D cycle.
Prior developments such as Neural Architecture Search and the Evolved Transformer demonstrated that automated search can successfully discover model architectures.
The iterative loop of problem breakdown, experimentation, evaluation, and learning is shared across both AI research and broader science and engineering.
AI-driven automation can reduce experiment iteration times from days or weeks to minutes or hours while conducting thousands of experiments in parallel.
Jeff founded Discovery Loop to accelerate discovery rates by using experimental evidence to autonomously select subsequent experiments.

sections.title: 2. How Do You Recognize an Idea That Could Matter for a Decade?
sections.summary: Jeff Dean highlights that foundational technology ideas often reveal their long-term value through an order-of-magnitude improvement in underlying economics or engineering long before their applications are obvious. A primary example is the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, which early on demonstrated roughly a 10× improvement in training-compute-to-quality ratios over dense models. Today, MoE architectures underpin many frontier AI systems, exemplifying how significant efficiency step changes signal transformative concepts.
takeaways: Foundational technology ideas often reveal themselves through a 10× step change in engineering or economic metrics before their full applications are understood.
Early Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) systems achieved approximately 10× better training-compute-to-quality ratios compared to dense models.
Jeff Dean and collaborators developed early MoE systems years before their broader significance became widely recognized.
MoE architectures currently serve as the foundation for many frontier AI systems.

sections.title: 3. Research Taste: Find the Sweet Spot Between Obvious and Impossible
sections.summary: Jeff Dean outlines a concrete framework for choosing ambitious research problems by balancing feasibility and novelty. He recommends prioritizing breadth—such as skimming dozens or hundreds of papers—to build a mental network of emerging ideas and identify new connections. Ideal research projects often have a majority of components becoming viable while a few still require breakthrough inventions, typically fitting a five-year horizon. Additionally, he emphasizes using first-principles back-of-the-envelope calculations to verify whether a proposed system is physically and economically feasible before building.
takeaways: Skimming 10 papers or 100 abstracts is recommended over reading a single paper in detail to construct a broad mental map of emerging possibilities.
The ideal five-year research problem often has about five of seven components becoming possible, with the remaining pieces requiring genuinely new inventions.
Problems where all pieces are already solved risk being too incremental, while those where no pieces are understood may be decades too early.
First-principles back-of-the-envelope engineering calculations should be used early to identify bottlenecks in data movement, compute, and networking.
Research intuition and back-of-the-envelope analysis are learnable skills that can be developed through practice rather than innate talent.

sections.title: 4. Coding May Be Teaching Models Something More General
sections.summary: Building Gemini revealed that enhancing a model's coding capabilities can transfer to and improve its performance on seemingly unrelated reasoning tasks. This occurs because programming requires decomposing complex goals, solving components systematically, and recombining them into working solutions. These core competencies are essential for planning, scientific reasoning, and long-horizon agentic workflows. As a result, coding functions not just as a practical domain, but as an effective environment for cultivating general problem-solving capabilities in AI models.
takeaways: Improving a model's coding ability can directly enhance its performance on unrelated reasoning tasks.
Programming forces models to decompose complex objectives, systematically solve smaller problems, and synthesize solutions.
The skills acquired through coding are central to planning, scientific reasoning, and long-horizon AI agent workflows.
Coding functions as a highly effective training environment for general problem-solving, beyond software engineering itself.

sections.title: 5. More Capable Agents Mean More Capable Attackers—and Defenders
sections.summary: Advancements in autonomous agent capabilities present critical cybersecurity implications for both attackers and defenders. Benchmarks such as Berkeley RDI's ExploitGym and real-world events like the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident demonstrate that agents can autonomously discover and exploit vulnerabilities beyond their intended environments. Consequently, AI functions as a double-edged sword, providing sophisticated capabilities to malicious actors while empowering defenders to spot missed vulnerabilities. To manage this shift, security, evaluation, containment, and governance frameworks must advance concurrently with agent capabilities.
takeaways: Advancing AI agent capabilities significantly influences both offensive and defensive cybersecurity.
In the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident, an autonomous benchmark-solving AI agent exploited vulnerabilities and reached external infrastructure.
Berkeley RDI developed ExploitGym as a benchmark to study AI agent cybersecurity behaviors.
AI operates as a double-edged sword, arming threat actors while enabling security teams to discover vulnerabilities missed by humans.
Mitigating agentic risks requires security, evaluation, containment, and governance to progress alongside model capability.

sections.title: The Bigger Picture
sections.summary: A unified research philosophy connects disparate areas including Mixture-of-Experts, Gemini, and cybersecurity. This approach emphasizes first-principles thinking, seeking step changes over incremental progress, and targeting ambitious problems requiring novel inventions. Most significantly, the future impact of AI centers on accelerating the scientific discovery loop rather than merely scaling individual model intelligence. This transition focuses on how quickly AI-enabled systems can iterate from ideas to experiments, evidence, and subsequent discoveries.
takeaways: A consistent strategic philosophy links domains including Mixture-of-Experts, Gemini, research strategy, and cybersecurity.
Effective AI research targets first-principles reasoning and step changes rather than incremental gains.
High-impact initiatives focus on ambitious problems where key components still need to be invented.
The role of AI is shifting from solving isolated problems to accelerating the discovery loop.
Future AI progress will be defined by system velocity in converting ideas into experiments, evidence, and new discoveries.

sections.title: Trends This Week
sections.summary: Recent industry developments highlight a shift toward real-world delegation, specialized non-generative architectures, and cost efficiency in agentic AI. Meta is testing real-world delegation features for its Muse agent, enabling automated phone calls and errand completion such as flight credit negotiation. Meanwhile, TypeSafe AI released Jev, a transformer designed to output calibrated decision probabilities rather than language, offering faster and cheaper classification for agent workflows. Finally, xAI launched Grok 4.7 at an aggressive price point, emphasizing a growing focus on inference economics and price-performance trade-offs for long-running agentic workloads.
takeaways: Meta is testing phone-calling and negotiation features in its Muse agent to conduct real-world tasks on users' behalf.
Reuters reported that Muse reached millions of downloads within its first two weeks.
TypeSafe AI introduced Jev, a transformer-based model designed for calibrated decision probabilities instead of text generation.
Vercel reported a 5-18x speedup after replacing an LLM-based safety classifier with Jev.
xAI launched Grok 4.7, pricing it at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens to compete on price-performance against frontier models.

sections.title: 從 10× Ideas 到 Discovery Loops
sections.summary: 前 Google Chief Scientist Jeff Dean 在任職 27 年離開公司後，發表了他的首次公開演講。在由 Dawn Song 教授主持的對談中，Dean 分享了他對未來技術前沿的觀點，而非僅僅回顧過去的成就。討論聚焦於在具高影響力的 research problems 變得顯而易見之前發掘它們，並探討 AI 如何加速 discovery loops。
takeaways: Jeff Dean 在 Google 任職 27 年後離開，出任 Discovery Loop 的 Co-founder 兼 CEO。
Dean 在 Google 的工作涵蓋基礎運算與 AI systems，包括 MapReduce、Bigtable、TensorFlow、Mixture-of-Experts、TPUs 以及 Gemini。
在離開 Google 後的首次公開露面中，Dean 與 Dawn Song 教授進行了廣泛深入的討論。
這場對話強調了及早辨識高價值研究方向，並善用 AI 加速科學發現。

sections.title: 1. AI 可能會改變科學發現本身的速度
sections.summary: AI 中的 recursive self-improvement 概念正從自動化單一任務，擴展至加速整個研發（R&D）生命週期。過去像是 Neural Architecture Search 等方法以及 Evolved Transformer 等架構展示了自動化模型探索，但目前的努力著重於將完整的實驗 feedback loops 自動化。這個框架廣泛適用於由實驗與評估推動進展的科學與工程領域。一家名為 Discovery Loop 的公司旨在大幅壓縮迭代週期，並平行執行數千個實驗，以加速科學發現本身的速度。
takeaways: Machine learning 中的 recursive self-improvement 正從自動化個別設計任務，擴展至自動化完整的 R&D 週期。
過去的進展（例如 Neural Architecture Search 與 Evolved Transformer）證明了自動化搜尋能夠成功發現模型架構。
問題拆解、實驗、評估與學習的迭代迴圈，是 AI 研究與更廣泛的科學及工程領域所共通的架構。
AI 驅動的自動化能將實驗迭代時間從數天或數週縮短至數分鐘或數小時，同時平行進行數千個實驗。
Jeff 創立了 Discovery Loop，透過利用實驗證據自主選擇後續實驗，以加速科學發現的速度。

sections.title: 2. 如何辨識出能發揮十年影響力的想法？
sections.summary: Jeff Dean 指出，基礎技術想法往往在應用明朗化之前，就透過底層經濟效益或工程指標上數量級（order-of-magnitude）的躍進，展現出其長期價值。一個典型的例子是 Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) 架構，該架構早期就展現出相較於 dense models 約 10 倍的 training-compute-to-quality 比率提升。如今，MoE 架構支撐著許多 frontier AI 系統，具體展現了顯著的效率躍進如何預示著顛覆性的概念。
takeaways: 基礎技術想法往往在其完整應用被完全理解之前，就透過工程或經濟指標上 10 倍的躍進展現出來。
早期的 Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) 系統相較於 dense models，實現了約 10 倍更好的 training-compute-to-quality 比率。
Jeff Dean 與合作者在 MoE 的廣泛重要性被大眾認可的數年前，就開發了早期的 MoE 系統。
MoE 架構目前作為許多 frontier AI 系統的基石。

sections.title: 3. Research Taste：在顯而易見與絕無可能之間找到最佳平衡點（Sweet Spot）
sections.summary: Jeff Dean 概述了一個具體的框架，透過平衡可行性與新穎性來挑選具有野心的研究題目。他建議優先考慮廣度——例如快速瀏覽數十或數百篇論文——以建立新興想法的思維網絡並找出新的連結。理想的研究專案通常有大部分組件已變得可行，而少數組件仍需要突破性發明，通常符合五年的時間跨度。此外，他強調在著手建構之前，應使用 first-principles back-of-the-envelope calculations 來驗證提議的系統在物理與經濟上是否可行。
takeaways: 比起詳細精讀單一論文，更建議快速瀏覽 10 篇論文或 100 篇摘要，以建立新興可能性的廣泛心智圖（mental map）。
理想的五年期研究問題，通常有七分之五的組件已經變得可行，而其餘部分則需要真正全新的發明。
所有部分都已解決的問題可能過於漸進（incremental），而完全沒有任何部分被理解的問題則可能為時過早數十年。
應及早使用 first-principles back-of-the-envelope 工程估算，以識別 data movement、compute 與 networking 方面的瓶頸。
研究直覺與 back-of-the-envelope 分析是可以學習的技能，能夠透過練習來培養，而非與生俱來的天賦。

sections.title: 4. Coding 或許正在教會模型某些更通用的能力
sections.summary: 在打造 Gemini 的過程中發現，提升模型的 coding 能力可以遷移並改善其在看似不相關的 reasoning 任務上的表現。這是因為 programming 需要分解複雜目標、有系統地解決各個組件，並將其重新組合成可運行的解決方案。這些核心能力對於 planning、scientific reasoning 以及 long-horizon agentic workflows 至關重要。因此，coding 不僅僅是一個實用領域，更是為 AI 模型培養通用問題解決能力的有效環境。
takeaways: 提升模型的 coding 能力可以直接增強其在無關 reasoning 任務上的表現。
Programming 迫使模型分解複雜目標、有系統地解決較小的問題，並整合成解決方案。
透過 coding 習得的技能，對於 planning、科學推理以及 long-horizon AI agent 工作流程至關重要。
Coding 不僅局限於軟體工程本身，更是一個能高度有效訓練通用問題解決能力的環境。

sections.title: 5. 能力更強的 Agent 意味著更強大的攻擊者——以及防禦者
sections.summary: 自主 agent 能力的進步，對攻擊者和防禦者的 cybersecurity 帶來了關鍵影響。像 Berkeley RDI 的 ExploitGym 等 benchmark 以及 OpenAI–Hugging Face 事件等真實案例顯示，agent 能夠自主發現並利用超出其預期環境的漏洞。因此，AI 就像一把雙面刃，既為惡意行為者提供了複雜的能力，同時也賦能防禦者找出被遺漏的漏洞。為了應對這種轉變，security、evaluation、containment 以及 governance 框架必須與 agent 能力同步推進。
takeaways: 推進 AI agent 能力對進攻型與防禦型的 cybersecurity 都具有重大影響。
在 OpenAI–Hugging Face 事件中，一個自主解題 benchmark 的 AI agent 利用了漏洞並滲透至外部基礎設施。
Berkeley RDI 開發了 ExploitGym 作為研究 AI agent cybersecurity 行為的 benchmark。
AI 猶如一把雙面刃，在武裝威脅行為者的同時，也讓資安團隊能夠發現人類所遺漏的漏洞。
降低 agentic risk 需要 security、evaluation、containment 與 governance 與模型能力並進。

sections.title: 宏觀視野
sections.summary: 一套貫穿始終的研究哲學將 Mixture-of-Experts、Gemini 與 cybersecurity 等不同領域串聯在一起。這種方法強調第一性原理思考，追求 step changes 而非漸進式進步，並鎖定需要全新發明的宏大問題。最重要的是，AI 未來的影響力核心在於加速科學發現循環（scientific discovery loop），而不僅僅是 scaling 單一模型的智慧。這種轉變聚焦於 AI-enabled 系統能多快地從想法迭代至實驗、證據以及隨後的全新發現。
takeaways: 一套一致的策略哲學將 Mixture-of-Experts、Gemini、research strategy 和 cybersecurity 等領域連結在一起。
高效的 AI 研究著重於第一性原理推理與 step changes，而非漸進式的微小收益。
高影響力的專案專注於關鍵組件仍待發明的宏大問題。
AI 的角色正從解決孤立的問題轉向加速 discovery loop。
未來 AI 的進步將取決於系統將想法轉化為實驗、證據與新發現的整體速度（system velocity）。

sections.title: 本週趨勢
sections.summary: 近期業界發展突顯出 agentic AI 正在轉向真實世界任務委派（real-world delegation）、專用非生成式架構以及成本效益。Meta 正在為其 Muse agent 測試真實世界委派功能，可實現自動撥打電話與跑腿代辦，例如機票抵用金（flight credit）協商。同時，TypeSafe AI 推出了 Jev，這是一款專為輸出校準後決策機率（calibrated decision probabilities）而非語言而設計的 transformer，能為 agent 工作流程提供更快且更具成本效益的 classification。最後，xAI 推出了定價極具侵略性的 Grok 4.7，強調針對長時間運行的 agentic workload，市場越來越注重 inference economics 與性價比權衡。
takeaways: Meta 正在其 Muse agent 中測試電話撥打與協商功能，以代表使用者執行真實世界的任務。
Reuters 報導指出，Muse 在推出後的最初兩週內下載量便達數百萬次。
TypeSafe AI 推出了 Jev，這是一款基於 transformer 的模型，專為輸出 calibrated decision probabilities 而設計，而非文字生成。
Vercel 報告指出，將基於 LLM 的 safety classifier 換成 Jev 後，獲得了 5 到 18 倍的速度提升。
xAI 推出了 Grok 4.7，定價為每百萬 input tokens 2 美元、每百萬 output tokens 6 美元，以高性價比挑戰 frontier models。

items.title: How OpenAI Built GPT-Live

sections.title: Three Generations of Voice Systems
sections.summary: Voice systems consistently operate with audio inputs from the user and generate audio responses played back to the user. Although the input and output modalities remain the same, the intermediate processing differs according to the system design. Across their development, voice systems have evolved through three distinct architectural generations. These generations are categorized as cascaded design, turn-based end-to-end, and full-duplex architecture.
takeaways: The input to a voice system is audio and the output is played back as audio format.
The internal processing between audio input and output varies depending on system design.
Voice systems have progressed through three distinct architectural generations.
The three architectural generations are cascaded design, turn-based end-to-end, and full-duplex architecture.

sections.title: 1. Cascaded Design
sections.summary: The cascaded design for voice systems chains three distinct models sequentially: an automatic speech recognition (ASR) model, a large language model (LLM), and a text-to-speech (TTS) model. While this pipeline allows each specialized component to handle what it does best, it introduces significant drawbacks including the loss of vocal cues such as tone and emotion during transcription. Furthermore, operating three systems in series leads to high latency and substantial operational complexity in serving and scaling. These challenges prompted the development of second-generation turn-based speech-to-speech architectures.
takeaways: A cascaded voice architecture chains an ASR model, an LLM, and a TTS model sequentially.
Information loss occurs because the LLM processes text transcripts and misses vocal nuances like tone and emotion.
Serial execution causes the latency of all three stages to accumulate, leading to slower user response times.
Deploying and managing three distinct models creates significant system complexity in production.
The drawbacks of cascaded systems led to the creation of turn-based speech-to-speech models.

sections.title: 2. Turn-based, Speech-to-Speech
sections.summary: The second generation of voice AI introduces end-to-end speech-to-speech models that directly process and generate audio, capturing vocal nuances lost in cascaded systems. Despite this improvement, interactions remain turn-based because they still depend on turn-detection and interruption mechanisms to manage speaking flow. These detectors struggle with trade-offs between unnatural delays and premature cutoffs or false triggers. Furthermore, speech-to-speech systems are costly to keep current because integrating updated base LLM checkpoints requires full retraining runs.
takeaways: End-to-end speech models directly process and output audio, retaining vocal cues lost in cascaded systems.
Second-generation speech-to-speech systems remain constrained by turn-based interaction models.
Turn detectors face difficult trade-offs between cutting off users prematurely and introducing awkward conversational pauses.
Interruption handling requires separate audio-stopping buffers that risk sluggishness or false triggers from background noise.
Updating voice models requires expensive full retraining on new LLM checkpoints, causing them to lag behind frontier models.
Third-generation full-duplex architectures are designed to overcome the turn-taking problem.

sections.title: 3. Full-duplex Architecture
sections.summary: Full-duplex voice models eliminate traditional turn detectors by continuously listening and generating audio tokens simultaneously, decoding silence as normal tokens. Reference models like Moshi demonstrate this by operating on a fixed clock of roughly 80 milliseconds per frame, learning natural conversational turn-taking directly from training data. While this approach resolves conversation unnaturalness and interruption handling, it introduces high serving costs due to constant inference and demands compact model capacity for millisecond latency. Systems like OpenAI's GPT-Live-1 address these constraints by keeping the primary voice model small and fast while delegating complex reasoning tasks.
takeaways: Full-duplex models eliminate turn detectors by continuously streaming input and output audio tokens, representing silence as an ordinary token.
Moshi is an open full-duplex model that converts audio to discrete tokens and operates on a fixed clock of roughly 80 milliseconds per frame.
Full-duplex architectures implicitly learn when to speak and when to listen directly from conversational training data.
The continuous inference of full-duplex architectures leads to high serving costs and imposes tight constraints on model capacity to maintain millisecond response times.
OpenAI launched GPT-Live-1 in July 2026, utilizing a small low-latency voice model that relies on delegation to perform computationally expensive reasoning.

sections.title: How the GPT-Live System Works
sections.summary: OpenAI developed a voice assistant centered around a full-duplex architecture. The implementation addresses key technical ideas and techniques necessary to operate effectively at scale in production. This approach focuses on making real-time, bidirectional voice interactions viable for large-scale production deployment.
takeaways: OpenAI built a voice assistant structured around a full-duplex architecture.
The system focuses on techniques that make real-time voice architectures practical at scale in production.
The section examines the engineering methods required to operationalize large-scale full-duplex voice systems.

sections.title: Separating Talking from Thinking
sections.summary: Standard frontier language models introduce latency when searching and reasoning, which creates awkward silence in voice-based systems. To solve this, OpenAI decouples conversational interaction from deep reasoning tasks. A voice model handles the real-time dialogue, while a separate, more capable model like GPT-5.5 performs necessary reasoning and tool calls in the background. This architecture reduces the traditional trade-off between response latency and answer quality. Furthermore, the modular design simplifies future upgrades by allowing newer reasoning models to be swapped in with minimal engineering effort.
takeaways: OpenAI decouples real-time conversation from complex reasoning to eliminate awkward pauses in voice systems.
A dedicated voice model maintains continuous dialogue with the user while backend reasoning tasks run.
Complex queries requiring tool use or web searches are delegated to GPT-5.5.
Separating conversational duties from reasoning meaningfully reduces the trade-off between speed and answer quality.
The modular architecture allows voice assistants to adopt new frontier models with minimal engineering overhead.

sections.title: The Two Serving Paths
sections.summary: Serving two models concurrently requires decoupling fast and slow operations because audio frames require millisecond latency while delegation can take seconds. To prevent latency spikes, GPT-Live splits traffic into two separate execution pathways. The live path strictly manages rapid audio transfer between the client and voice model. Meanwhile, the async path handles slower, non-audio tasks like tool calls without interfering with live audio streaming.
takeaways: Audio streaming requires frames to be sent every few milliseconds, whereas task delegations can take seconds.
A shared process cannot effectively serve both fast audio streaming and slow delegations simultaneously.
GPT-Live splits operational traffic into a live path and an async path.
The live path exclusively transfers audio between the client and the voice model as quickly as possible.
The async path manages non-audio tasks, ensuring slow tool calls do not delay live audio delivery.

sections.title: How to make the live path fast?
sections.summary: Full-duplex voice systems like GPT-Live require real-time audio transmission on a strict fixed clock to prevent audible artifacts from processing bottlenecks. To minimize initial setup latency, OpenAI created the WARP protocol to compress standard multi-step WebRTC handshakes into a single round trip. Continuous audio inference costs are managed by keeping conversation context pinned in GPU memory on dedicated model instances, alongside batching and speculative decoding. Additionally, OpenAI employs a managed handoff mechanism to seamlessly switch live conversations to replacement instances during context compaction, scaling, or instance failures.
takeaways: Audio in full-duplex systems operates on a fixed clock, meaning any processing bottleneck instantly generates audible artifacts for the user.
Standard WebRTC connection setup takes six round trips, introducing over a third of a second of latency on standard 60ms mobile connections.
OpenAI built the WARP (WebRTC Abridged Roundtrip Protocol) to parallelize connection steps and initialize sessions in a single round trip.
Unlike request-response chatbots, full-duplex systems experience no idle time and sample the model continuously even during user pauses.
Inference overhead is reduced by keeping session state loaded directly in GPU memory, allowing the model to process only incoming frames rather than entire conversation histories.
A managed handoff mechanism preloads session history onto replacement instances to handle instance updates, failures, and context compaction without interrupting live audio.

sections.title: The Async Path
sections.summary: The async path is responsible for managing non-audio tasks, including delegations and tool calling, between models in a real-time system. To make the interaction feel seamless, latency must be minimized, particularly the time spent on the prefill phase of prompt processing. OpenAI mitigates this delay by initiating an inference session with the frontier model at the start of a conversation and pre-loading context before a delegation is triggered.
takeaways: The async path manages tasks like tool calling and delegations that take longer than audio processing.
Voice models can briefly mask latency through acknowledgments or thinking aloud, but cannot cover prolonged delays.
Most delegation latency is caused by prefill, where the model processes the prompt history before generating tokens.
In long conversations, prompt processing can add a noticeable fraction of a second to response latency.
OpenAI reduces delegation latency by preemptively starting an inference session with the frontier model and sending conversation history in advance.

sections.title: How to Evaluate a Full-duplex Voice System?
sections.summary: Evaluating full-duplex voice systems requires a different approach than traditional turn-based speech models. Turn-based models can be scored per discrete request-and-response turn, whereas full-duplex architectures operate on one continuous audio stream without distinct turns. Consequently, evaluation in full-duplex architectures focuses on three main components: conversational behavior, stream health, and testing under real production traffic.
takeaways: Turn-based speech models are typically evaluated one turn at a time by scoring discrete responses.
Full-duplex architectures operate over a single continuous audio stream without discrete turns, making traditional turn-level evaluation unsuitable.
Full-duplex system evaluation focuses on three parts: conversational behavior, the health of the stream, and testing on real production traffic.

sections.title: 1. Conversational behavior
sections.summary: Evaluating conversational behavior in models primarily hinges on timing decisions such as when to speak, remain silent, or interrupt. The two core decisions are endpointing, which determines turn completion, and barge-in detection, which distinguishes genuine interruptions from background noise. These behaviors are evaluated like prediction tasks using annotated natural conversation datasets.
takeaways: Conversational behavior in models primarily depends on appropriate timing.
Endpointing involves deciding whether a turn has ended and whether the model should talk or remain silent.
Barge-in detection differentiates between actual user interruptions and background noise when the model is speaking.
Evaluation treats conversational decisions as predictions scored against annotated natural conversation datasets.

sections.title: 2. The health of the stream
sections.summary: Evaluating stream health in serving systems traditionally relies on percentile targets like p95 latency, which suffices when requests are intermittent. In full-duplex architectures running continuous inference, a p95 event occurs every 20 inferences, resulting in multiple slow events per minute. Because even p99 delays appear regularly, systems must be engineered around p999 targets. In practice, full-duplex designs must emphasize fast recovery since occasional slow frames are inevitable in every session.
takeaways: Traditional serving systems evaluate stream health using percentile targets like p95 latency.
In full-duplex continuous inference, p95 latency events happen every 20 inferences, amounting to several times per minute.
P99 latency events also occur regularly in continuous streaming architectures.
Full-duplex systems must be engineered around p999 latency rather than p95.
Systems running continuous streams must be designed for fast recovery because slow frames are inevitable.

sections.title: 3. Testing the system on real production traffic
sections.summary: A silent launch serves as the final layer of evaluation to safely verify system reliability under real production traffic. During this process, users continue interacting with the existing system while a small fraction of voice sessions is routed to the new system. This approach uncovers difficult-to-detect issues, such as unexpected infrastructure bottlenecks. For example, during the silent launch of GPT-Live, the engineering team discovered that a CPU-side service exhausted capacity before the GPUs did.
takeaways: A silent launch safely evaluates system reliability under real production traffic by routing a small percentage of voice sessions to the new system.
Users interact with the legacy system as normal while background traffic is evaluated on the new architecture.
Silent launches expose edge cases and unexpected bottlenecks that standard synthetic tests fail to detect.
In the case of GPT-Live, a silent launch revealed that a CPU-side service reached capacity limits before the GPU infrastructure did.

sections.title: What Other Teams Can Learn From GPT-Live
sections.summary: Realtime serving architectures, such as OpenAI's GPT-Live, present distinct challenges compared to traditional request-response systems. In voice applications, engineering must prioritize tail latency over average latency, and capacity planning must track concurrent sessions rather than individual requests. Furthermore, moving complex tasks like turn detection directly into the model increases conversational naturalness while reducing overall system complexity. Keeping components outside the model minimal and focused strictly on realtime delivery ensures the broader system remains maintainable.
takeaways: Voice systems require engineering focus on tail latency rather than average latency because users notice the worst-performing frame.
Capacity planning for realtime conversational systems must be calculated based on concurrent sessions rather than per-request volume.
Absorbing turn detection logic into the model itself improves conversational naturalness and simplifies the serving stack.
Non-model components should remain small and dedicated solely to realtime data handling to preserve simplicity and maintainability.

sections.title: What’s Next
sections.summary: OpenAI views voice-driven computer interaction as the next major paradigm shift in computing, as demonstrated through features in the ChatGPT desktop app like screen perception and asynchronous task execution. Users can continuously query, guide, and redirect tasks via voice in real time. However, challenges persist in smoothly delegating tasks across different models without introducing latency into live conversation. While systems like GPT-Live-1 demonstrate rapid progress likened to the jump from GPT-3 to GPT-4, complex latency and architecture questions remain open.
takeaways: OpenAI envisions voice-driven control of computers as the next generation of human-computer interaction.
The ChatGPT desktop app can take screenshots to observe user workflows, run long-running background tasks, and receive mid-task steering via voice.
Maintaining low-latency live conversation while delegating complex tasks to auxiliary models remains an active technical challenge.
Justin compares the current state of voice AI using GPT-Live-1 to the GPT-4 milestone, having moved past an earlier GPT-3 level of maturity.

items.summary: Voice systems consistently operate with audio inputs from the user and generate audio responses played back to the user. Although the input and output modalities remain the same, the intermediate processing differs according to the system design. Across their development, voice systems have evolved through three distinct architectural generations. These generations are categorized as cascaded design, turn-based end-to-end, and full-duplex architecture. The cascaded design for voice systems chains three distinct models sequentially: an automatic speech recognition (ASR) model, a large language model (LLM), and a text-to-speech (TTS) model. While this pipeline allows each specialized component to handle what it does best, it introduces significant drawbacks including the loss of vocal cues such as tone and emotion during transcription. Furthermore, operating three systems in series leads to high latency and substantial operational complexity in serving and scaling. These challenges prompted the development of second-generation turn-based speech-to-speech architectures. The second generation of voice AI introduces end-to-end speech-to-speech models that directly process and generate audio, capturing vocal nuances lost in cascaded systems. Despite this improvement, interactions remain turn-based because they still depend on turn-detection and interruption mechanisms to manage speaking flow. These detectors struggle with trade-offs between unnatural delays and premature cutoffs or false triggers. Furthermore, speech-to-speech systems are costly to keep current because integrating updated base LLM checkpoints requires full retraining runs.

1. Cascaded Design
2. Turn-based, Speech-to-Speech
3. Full-duplex Architecture

The Two Serving Paths

sections.title: 語音系統的三個世代
sections.summary: 語音系統一貫以使用者的音訊輸入來運作，並生成音訊回應播放給使用者。儘管輸入與輸出的 modality 相同，但中間的處理方式會因系統設計而異。在其發展歷程中，語音系統經歷了三個截然不同的架構世代演進。這些世代被分類為 cascaded design、turn-based end-to-end 以及 full-duplex architecture。
takeaways: 語音系統的輸入是音訊，而輸出則以音訊格式播放。
音訊輸入與輸出之間的內部處理方式會因系統設計而異。
語音系統經歷了三個截然不同的架構世代演進。
這三個架構世代分別是 cascaded design、turn-based end-to-end 與 full-duplex architecture。

sections.title: 1. Cascaded Design
sections.summary: 語音系統的 cascaded design 依序串聯了三個不同的模型：automatic speech recognition (ASR) 模型、large language model (LLM) 和 text-to-speech (TTS) 模型。雖然此 pipeline 能讓每個專門的組件各司其職，但它帶來了顯著的缺點，包括在轉錄（transcription）過程中遺失語調與情緒等 vocal cues。此外，串聯運作三個系統會導致高 latency，並在 serving 與 scaling 方面帶來極大的維運複雜度。這些挑戰推動了第二代 turn-based speech-to-speech 架構的發展。
takeaways: Cascaded 語音架構依序串聯了 ASR 模型、LLM 和 TTS 模型。
資訊遺失的發生是因為 LLM 處理的是文字 transcripts，因而遺漏了語調與情緒等 vocal nuances。
序列執行（Serial execution）會導致這三個階段的 latency 累積，使得對使用者的回應時間變慢。
在 production 環境中部署與管理三個不同的模型，會帶來顯著的系統複雜度。
Cascaded 系統的缺點推動了 turn-based speech-to-speech 模型的誕生。

sections.title: 2. Turn-based, Speech-to-Speech
sections.summary: 第二代 voice AI 導入了 end-to-end speech-to-speech 模型，可直接處理並生成音訊，捕捉 cascaded 系統中遺失的 vocal nuances。儘管有所改進，但互動仍屬於 turn-based，因為它們仍依賴 turn-detection 與中斷機制來管理說話流程。這些 detector 在不自然的延遲與過早打斷（premature cutoffs）或誤觸發（false triggers）之間面臨 trade-off。此外，speech-to-speech 系統要保持最新狀態的成本很高，因為整合更新後的 base LLM checkpoints 需要進行完整的 retraining runs。
takeaways: End-to-end 語音模型直接處理並輸出音訊，保留了 cascaded 系統中遺失的 vocal cues。
第二代 speech-to-speech 系統仍受限於 turn-based 互動模式。
Turn detector 在過早打斷使用者與造成尷尬的對話停頓之間面臨艱難的 trade-off。
中斷處理需要獨立的 audio-stopping buffers，這可能導致反應遲鈍或因背景雜音而誤觸發。
更新 voice models 需要在新的 LLM checkpoints 上進行昂貴的 full retraining，導致它們落後於 frontier models。
第三代 full-duplex 架構旨在克服 turn-taking 問題。

sections.title: 3. Full-duplex 架構
sections.summary: Full-duplex voice models 透過持續同時聆聽與生成 audio tokens，並將 silence 解碼為一般 tokens，從而消除了傳統的 turn detectors。像 Moshi 這類 reference models 透過每 frame 約 80 毫秒的固定 clock 運作來展示這點，直接從訓練資料中學習自然的對話 turn-taking。雖然這種方法解決了對話的不自然感與中斷處理問題，但由於持續 inference 帶來了高昂的 serving costs，並對維持毫秒級 latency 的 model capacity 提出了嚴苛限制。像 OpenAI 的 GPT-Live-1 這類系統透過保持主 voice model 輕巧快速，同時將複雜的 reasoning 任務委派出去，來解決這些限制。
takeaways: Full-duplex models 透過持續 streaming 輸入與輸出的 audio tokens，將 silence 表示為一般 token，從而消除了 turn detectors。
Moshi 是一個開源的 full-duplex model，它將音訊轉換為 discrete tokens，並以每 frame 約 80 毫秒的固定 clock 運作。
Full-duplex 架構直接從對話訓練資料中隱式學習何時該說話、何時該聆聽。
Full-duplex 架構的持續 inference 會導致高昂的 serving costs，並對 model capacity 施加嚴格限制以維持毫秒級的反應時間。
OpenAI 於 2026 年 7 月推出了 GPT-Live-1，採用小型、低延遲的 voice model，並依賴 delegation 來執行運算成本高昂的 reasoning。

sections.title: GPT-Live 系統的運作方式
sections.summary: OpenAI 開發了一款以 full-duplex 架構為核心的語音助理。該實作解決了在 production 環境中進行大規模有效運作所需的關鍵技術構想與技巧。這種方法致力於使即時、雙向的語音互動在大規模 production 部署中切實可行。
takeaways: OpenAI 構建了一款以 full-duplex 架構為基礎的語音助理。
該系統專注於讓即時語音架構在 production 大規模環境下更具實用性的技術。
本節探討將大規模 full-duplex 語音系統推向正式運作所需之工程方法。

sections.title: 將「說話」與「思考」分離
sections.summary: 標準 frontier language models 在搜尋和 reasoning 時會引入 latency，從而在語音系統中造成尷尬的沉默。為了克服這點，OpenAI 將對話互動與 deep reasoning 任務解耦。由 voice model 處理即時對話，而另一個能力更強的模型（例如 GPT-5.5）則在背景執行必要的 reasoning 和 tool calls。這種架構降低了傳統在 response latency 與回答品質之間的 trade-off。此外，模組化設計讓團隊只需投入最少的工程成本即可抽換為更新的 reasoning models，大幅簡化未來的升級流程。
takeaways: OpenAI 將即時對話與複雜的 reasoning 解耦，以消除語音系統中尷尬的停頓。
在後端 reasoning 任務運行的同時，由專屬的 voice model 與使用者維持連續對話。
需要 tool use 或網路搜尋的複雜 queries 會被 delegate 給 GPT-5.5。
將對話職責與 reasoning 分開，顯著降低了速度與回答品質之間的 trade-off。
模組化架構讓語音助理能以極低的工程 overhead 導入新的 frontier models。

sections.title: 兩條 Serving Paths
sections.summary: 同時 serving 兩個模型需要將快速與慢速操作解耦，因為 audio frames 需要毫秒級的 latency，而 delegation 則可能耗時數秒。為了防止 latency spikes，GPT-Live 將流量拆分為兩條獨立的執行路徑。Live path 嚴格管理 client 與 voice model 之間的快速音訊傳輸；同時，async path 則在不干擾即時 audio streaming 的情況下，處理像 tool calls 這類較慢的非音訊任務。
takeaways: Audio streaming 需要每隔幾毫秒傳送一次 frames，而任務 delegation 則可能需要耗費數秒。
單一 shared process 無法同時有效兼顧快速的 audio streaming 與耗時的 delegations。
GPT-Live 將運作流量拆分為 live path 與 async path。
Live path 專門以最快速度在 client 與 voice model 之間傳輸 audio。
Async path 負責管理非 audio 任務，確保耗時的 tool calls 不會延遲 live audio 的傳輸。

sections.title: 如何讓 live path 變快？
sections.summary: 像 GPT-Live 這類的 full-duplex 語音系統需要基於嚴格 fixed clock 進行即時 audio 傳輸，以避免處理瓶頸產生可聽見的雜音（audible artifacts）。為了將初始連線 setup latency 降至最低，OpenAI 開發了 WARP protocol，將標準的多步驟 WebRTC handshake 壓縮為單次 round trip。持續性的 audio inference 成本則是透過將對話 context 釘選在專屬 model instance 的 GPU memory 中，並搭配 batching 與 speculative decoding 來管理。此外，OpenAI 採用了 managed handoff 機制，在 context compaction、scaling 或 instance failure 期間，將即時對話無縫切換至替代 instance。
takeaways: Full-duplex 系統中的 audio 是在 fixed clock 上運作，這表示任何處理瓶頸都會立即對使用者產生可聽見的雜音（audible artifacts）。
標準 WebRTC 連線 setup 需要六個 round trips，在標準 60ms 的行動網路連線上會引入超過三分之一秒的 latency。
OpenAI 打造了 WARP (WebRTC Abridged Roundtrip Protocol)，將連線步驟平行化，並在單一 round trip 內完成 session 初始化。
與 request-response 形式的 chatbot 不同，full-duplex 系統沒有閒置時間（idle time），即使使用者停頓時也會持續對模型進行 sample。
透過將 session state 直接保留在 GPU memory 中來降低 inference overhead，讓模型僅需處理傳入的 frames，而不需要處理整個對話歷史。
Managed handoff 機制會將 session history 預先載入到替代 instance 上，以便在不中斷即時 audio 的情況下處理 instance updates、failures 與 context compaction。

sections.title: The Async Path
sections.summary: Async path 負責在即時系統中管理模型間的非 audio 任務，包含 delegations 與 tool calling。為了讓互動感覺無縫順暢，必須將 latency 降至最低，特別是 prompt processing 的 prefill 階段所花費的時間。OpenAI 透過在對話開始時就與 frontier model 建立 inference session，並在觸發 delegation 之前預先載入 context 來緩解此延遲。
takeaways: Async path 負責管理比 audio 處理耗時更久的任務，例如 tool calling 與 delegations。
Voice model 可以透過口頭回應（acknowledgments）或發聲思考（thinking aloud）短暫掩蓋 latency，但無法掩飾過長的延遲。
大部分的 delegation latency 是由 prefill 引起的，亦即模型在生成 tokens 之前處理 prompt history 的階段。
在長對話中，prompt processing 可能會為 response latency 增加顯著的幾分之一秒。
OpenAI 透過預先啟動與 frontier model 的 inference session 並提前傳送對話歷史，來降低 delegation latency。

sections.title: 如何評估 Full-duplex 語音系統？
sections.summary: 評估 full-duplex 語音系統需要與傳統 turn-based 語音模型不同的方法。Turn-based 模型可以針對每個獨立的 request-and-response turn 進行評分，而 full-duplex 架構則運作於沒有明確輪替的單一連續 audio stream 上。因此，full-duplex 架構的評估著重於三個主要部分：conversational behavior、stream health 以及在真實 production traffic 下的測試。
takeaways: Turn-based 語音模型通常是一次評估一個 turn，透過對個別離散的 response 進行評分。
Full-duplex 架構運作於單一連續的 audio stream 上，沒有離散的 turns，這使得傳統的 turn-level 評估方法不再適用。
Full-duplex 系統評估聚焦於三個部分：conversational behavior、stream health，以及在真實 production traffic 下的測試。

sections.title: 1. Conversational behavior
sections.summary: 評估 model 的對話行為主要取決於 timing 決策，例如何時發言、保持沉默或插話。兩大核心決策是決定 turn 是否結束的 endpointing，以及區分真實插話與背景雜訊的 barge-in detection。這些行為會像 prediction 任務一樣，使用標註過的自然對話 dataset 來評估。
takeaways: Model 的對話行為主要取決於適當的 timing。
Endpointing 涉及判斷一個 turn 是否結束，以及 model 應該說話還是保持沉默。
Barge-in detection 用於在 model 說話時，區分使用者的實際插話與背景雜訊。
Evaluation 將對話決策視為 prediction 任務，並對照標註過的自然對話 dataset 進行評分。

sections.title: 2. Stream health
sections.summary: 在 serving system 中評估 stream health，傳統上依賴像 p95 latency 這樣的 percentile 目標，這在 request 為間歇性時已足夠。但在執行連續推論的 full-duplex 架構中，每 20 次推論就會出現一次 p95 事件，導致每分鐘發生多次延遲過高的情況。因為即使是 p99 delay 也會規律出現，系統必須圍繞著 p999 目標來設計。在實務上，由於每個 session 都不可避免地會出現偶發的 slow frame，full-duplex 設計必須強調 fast recovery。
takeaways: 傳統 serving system 會使用像 p95 latency 這樣的 percentile 目標來評估 stream health。
在 full-duplex 連續推論中，每 20 次推論就會發生一次 p95 latency 事件，相當於每分鐘數次。
在 continuous streaming 架構中，p99 latency 事件也會規律發生。
Full-duplex 系統必須圍繞著 p999 latency 而非 p95 來設計。
執行連續 stream 的系統必須設計成具備 fast recovery 能力，因為 slow frame 是不可避免的。

sections.title: 3. 在真實 production traffic 上測試系統
sections.summary: Silent launch 是最後一層 evaluation，用於在真實 production traffic 下安全地驗證系統的 reliability。在此過程中，使用者繼續與現有系統互動，同時有少部分的語音 session 會被 route 到新系統。這種做法能揭露難以察覺的問題，例如預期之外的 infrastructure bottleneck。例如，在 GPT-Live 的 silent launch 期間，工程團隊發現 CPU-side service 在 GPU 達到上限之前就已耗盡 capacity。
takeaways: Silent launch 透過將小比例的語音 session 導流至新系統，在真實 production traffic 下安全地評估系統 reliability。
使用者照常與 legacy system 互動，同時在新的架構上評估背景 traffic。
Silent launch 能暴露標準 synthetic test 無法偵測到的 edge case 與意料之外的 bottleneck。
以 GPT-Live 為例，silent launch 揭露了 CPU-side service 比 GPU infrastructure 更早達到 capacity 極限。

sections.title: 其他團隊能從 GPT-Live 學到什麼
sections.summary: 與傳統的 request-response 系統相比，像是 OpenAI 的 GPT-Live 這類 realtime serving 架構帶來了截然不同的挑戰。在語音應用中，工程上必須優先考慮 tail latency 而非 average latency，且 capacity planning 必須追蹤 concurrent session 而非單一 request。此外，將 turn detection 等複雜任務直接移入 model 內部，不僅能提升對話的自然度，還能降低整體系統的複雜度。讓 model 之外的 component 保持極簡並專注於 realtime delivery，能確保整個系統維持良好的 maintainability。
takeaways: 語音系統在工程上需要關注 tail latency 而非 average latency，因為使用者會注意到表現最差的那個 frame。
Realtime 對話系統的 capacity planning 必須根據 concurrent session 計算，而非單次 request 量。
將 turn detection 邏輯吸收進 model 本身，能提升對話自然度並簡化 serving stack。
Non-model component 應保持精簡，並專門用於處理 realtime data，以維持簡潔性與 maintainability。

sections.title: 下一步
sections.summary: OpenAI 視語音驅動的電腦互動為計算領域的下一個重大典範轉移（paradigm shift），這點已透過 ChatGPT 桌面端 app 中的螢幕感知（screen perception）與非同步任務執行等功能展現。使用者能即時透過語音持續查詢、引導並重新導向任務。然而，在不同模型間流暢委派任務且不對即時對話引入延遲（latency），仍是一大挑戰。儘管像 GPT-Live-1 這類系統展現出被比擬為從 GPT-3 躍升至 GPT-4 的快速進展，但在複雜的 latency 與架構層面仍有待解問題。
takeaways: OpenAI 預見語音驅動的電腦控制將是下一代人機互動（human-computer interaction）模式。
ChatGPT 桌面端 app 能夠截圖以觀察使用者工作流程、執行長時間運行的背景任務，並在任務進行中透過語音接收指示。
在將複雜任務委派給輔助模型（auxiliary models）的同時維持低延遲（low-latency）的即時對話，仍是一項正在攻克的技術挑戰。
Justin 將目前採用 GPT-Live-1 的語音 AI 現況比擬為 GPT-4 等級的里程碑，已跨越了早期 GPT-3 的成熟度階段。

items.title: Build your own Jev (100% local)

sections.title: Finally, an OpenRouter for agent harnesses
sections.summary: HarnessRouter is a new open-source infrastructure layer that provides a unified interface for multiple agent harnesses. It simplifies development by handling sessions, streaming, and failure management across different tools like Codex and Claude code. The system utilizes the Unified Harness Protocol (UHP) to maintain an OpenAI-compatible API while running harnesses locally.
takeaways: HarnessRouter acts as a plug-and-play infrastructure layer for agent harnesses.
Supported harnesses include Codex, Hermes, Claude code, DeepSeek Harness, and System One.
The tool manages sessions, streaming, file handling, and cancellation logic automatically.
The Unified Harness Protocol (UHP) defines a common task interface for all supported harnesses.

sections.title: Build your own Jev (100% local)
sections.summary: This section describes how to implement a local version of the Jev inference pattern, which prioritizes scoring over text generation for classification tasks. By providing a finite set of possible answers, the system extracts the model's logits for specific tokens at the next position to determine a probability distribution. This approach is significantly faster than standard generation because it avoids the autoregressive decoding loop and eliminates the need for parsing text or JSON. The implementation utilizes SGLang's scoring endpoint to efficiently retrieve these scores from open models like Qwen and DeepSeek.
takeaways: Jev-style inference treats LLM calls as decisions by scoring a predefined list of valid answers rather than generating new text.
Scoring is more efficient than structured output because it retrieves probabilities from the first next-token vector without an autoregressive loop.
The SGLang /v1/score endpoint allows users to extract logits for specific token IDs and apply a restricted softmax to get a probability distribution.
To ensure accuracy, labels such as A, B, or C must be verified as single tokens using the model's specific tokenizer.
Scoring provides a confidence measure that can be used in application code to set thresholds for automated routing versus manual review.
This method is best suited for workloads with a finite set of labels where the caller does not require a textual explanation.

sections.title: Jev makes agent evaluation cheap. Beacon turns it into cross-harness memory
sections.summary: Beacon, developed by Asymptote Labs, is an open-source telemetry and memory layer designed to capture and share knowledge across different AI coding agents. It addresses the issue of agent amnesia by extracting reusable workflows and debugging patterns from agent traces. By integrating with Jev for cost-effective evaluation, Beacon identifies high-quality runs to build a persistent knowledge base. This allows improvements made in one tool, like Cursor, to benefit others, such as Claude Code or Codex, making agent-derived knowledge portable across an organization.
takeaways: Beacon is an open-source tool that acts as a cross-harness memory layer for AI coding agents.
Jev provides a low-cost method for evaluating agent traces to identify high-signal runs.
Beacon supports over 19 agent harnesses, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, and Cline.
The system converts successful agent traces into reusable skills and workflows for future sessions.
Knowledge captured by Beacon is portable, meaning learning from one agent can be applied to a different agent.
The workflow involves capturing traces, evaluating them with Jev, and extracting knowledge to improve future agent performance.

sections.title: Jev, clearly explained:
sections.summary: TypeSafe AI has launched Jev, a specialized semantic decision engine designed to replace generative LLMs for bounded tasks like routing, risk assessment, and classification. Unlike traditional LLMs, Jev does not generate text but instead provides typed outputs—Choice, Score, and Noul—along with calibrated probabilities. This approach reduces latency to sub-500ms levels and significantly lowers costs by eliminating token generation and parsing. Jev is intended to work alongside generative models, handling the discrete judgment calls within agentic loops and software control flows.
takeaways: Jev is a non-generative semantic engine that outputs structured data and probabilities instead of prose or code.
The tool supports three specific output primitives: Choice (categorical), Score (ordinal), and Noul (Boolean probability).
It is trained using Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD) to ensure confidence scores match observed accuracy.
Reported performance includes latency between 70 and 500 milliseconds and a cost of $0.042 per million input tokens.
LangChain has integrated Jev to provide middleware for safety checks and agent gating.
Jev is designed for closed-set outcomes where meaning-based judgment is required but deterministic code is insufficient.
The engine cannot perform arithmetic, extract unknown values, or explain its reasoning, making it a complement to, rather than a replacement for, LLMs.

items.title: How to Run a Big Model on Cheap Hardware?

sections.title: What Running a Model Actually Means
sections.summary: An AI model relies on numerical parameters, also known as weights, that are structured into layers to convert inputs into outputs. In language models, input text is broken into tokens, and the model iteratively generates responses by predicting probabilities for subsequent tokens. While training is a computationally intensive process that updates weights on expensive infrastructure, inference utilizes fixed weights and can often be executed on standard consumer hardware.
takeaways: AI model parameters or weights are organized into layers that perform sequential computations.
Language models process text by breaking it down into tokens representing words, word fragments, or punctuation.
Text generation is an iterative process that repeatedly computes probabilities for and selects the next token.
Inference is the process of using an existing trained model, during which weights typically remain unchanged.
Model training demands extensive calculations and costly infrastructure to update weights, unlike inference which requires fewer resources.

sections.title: What Makes it Difficult to Fit the Model on Smaller Hardware
sections.summary: Fitting large language models on smaller hardware is constrained by total memory capacity, memory location, and processing bottlenecks. An 8-billion-parameter model at 16-bit precision requires about 16 GB just for weights, plus extra space for software overhead, temporary calculations, and context. Because persistent storage like SSDs is too slow for execution, weights must reside in fast working memory such as RAM or GPU VRAM. Beyond capacity, memory bandwidth and compute architecture pose limits, with GPUs providing superior parallelism over CPUs and distinct bottlenecks arising across the prefill and decoding stages of inference.
takeaways: Storing an 8-billion-parameter model at 16-bit precision requires approximately 16 GB solely for raw weights, with additional overhead required during execution.
System RAM and discrete GPU VRAM remain separate memory spaces with different speeds rather than combining into a single uniform memory pool.
Retrieving weights from SSD storage during execution is significantly slower than accessing working memory.
GPUs are far more effective than CPUs at performing the parallel numerical operations required by neural networks.
Memory bandwidth is often a primary bottleneck during single-user text generation.
Inference consists of two distinct stages: parallel prompt processing (prefill) and sequential token generation (decoding).

sections.title: Why Make the Effort to Run Locally?
sections.summary: Local execution allows developers to utilize existing hardware for experimentation and decrease reliance on rented cloud infrastructure. This approach offers enhanced privacy for sensitive documents and proprietary code, alongside offline capability for desktop assistants and remote deployments. Additionally, running models locally provides greater control over model versions and application behavior. However, it is not universally cost-effective, as hardware, electricity, maintenance, and latency must be weighed against usage frequency compared to hosted services.
takeaways: Running models locally maximizes existing hardware and reduces dependence on rented cloud compute.
Local execution safeguards privacy for proprietary source code and private documents.
Offline availability is critical for desktop assistants, remote deployments, and intermittent internet scenarios.
Developers gain stricter control over model versions and application behavior by hosting locally.
Local execution is not inherently cheaper; costs depend on hardware investments, electricity, maintenance, and utilization patterns compared to hosted options.

sections.title: Quantization: Give Each Weight a Smaller Representation
sections.summary: Quantization reduces the numerical precision used to represent model weights, decreasing storage footprints such as shrinking an 8B model from 16 GB at 16-bit precision to 4 GB at 4-bit precision. While parameter counts stay the same, the lower precision introduces approximation errors that may degrade output quality depending on the task. Lower precision does not guarantee proportional execution speedups, as efficient inference depends on hardware support and runtime conversion software. The technique can be applied after training via post-training quantization or integrated during training to account for approximation errors.
takeaways: Quantization maps numerical weights onto a smaller set of discrete values to reduce memory requirements.
Compressing an 8B model from 16-bit to 4-bit precision reduces raw weight storage from approximately 16 GB to 4 GB while keeping parameter count unchanged.
Quality degradation from quantization varies based on the specific model, compression method, and target task.
Lower precision does not ensure proportional speed improvements because weights may still be unpacked to higher precision during calculation.
Quantization can be implemented after training as post-training quantization or accounted for during the training phase itself.

sections.title: Layer-Wise Offloading: Move Weights as They Are Needed
sections.summary: Layer-wise offloading changes where model weights reside and where their computations execute by moving weights onto the GPU only as needed during a forward pass. While this technique enables the execution of models too large to fit in GPU memory at once, it introduces significant data transfer overhead between RAM, disk, and the GPU. Repeated data movement across generation steps can substantially increase latency, potentially making the model unsuitable for interactive applications. Efficiency can be improved by batching requests or permanently partitioning distinct layers between the CPU and GPU.
takeaways: Quantization alters weight size, whereas offloading changes weight storage location and where calculations execute.
Layer-wise offloading transfers layer weights onto the GPU on demand, releasing them before loading subsequent layers.
More aggressive offloading strategies store weights on disk and load them into RAM prior to execution.
Repeated data transfers across generation steps can severely reduce inference speed, adding notable latency per token.
Batching requests to reuse transferred weights can improve throughput when individual latency is not critical.
Alternative offloading arrangements statically partition layers across the CPU and GPU or run entirely on the CPU if sufficient RAM is available.

sections.title: Mixture of Experts: Use Selected Parts for Each Token
sections.summary: Mixture of Experts (MoE) modifies transformer architecture by replacing standard computational blocks with multiple alternative networks known as experts. A routing network dynamically assigns each token to a subset of these experts, separating total parameter count from active parameter count. This allows models to maintain high capacity while reducing per-token computation compared to dense architectures. However, because inactive experts must remain accessible for subsequent tokens, MoE models still demand significant memory storage despite their lower compute footprint.
takeaways: In a sparse MoE model, a routing network dynamically routes each token to a subset of alternative sub-networks called experts.
Experts are internal model components whose roles are learned during training, rather than human-interpretable subjects or standalone chatbots.
MoE decouples total parameters (which determine storage requirements) from active parameters (which determine per-token computational cost).
Inactive experts must remain stored in memory or incur transfer costs when offloaded, meaning memory footprints remain large.
MoE reduces per-token computation relative to dense models with equivalent total parameters, but does not inherently reduce the memory requirements needed to run on low-memory devices.

sections.title: Distillation: Let a Larger Model Teach a Smaller One
sections.summary: Knowledge distillation is a technique where a larger teacher model helps train a smaller student model using its outputs or predictions. The resulting student model functions independently while demanding significantly less memory and computational power for deployment. Distillation produces an entirely distinct model rather than an exact compression, meaning that strong performance on a targeted task does not guarantee broad equivalence across all tasks. The upfront training expenditure allows cost-effective, repeated deployment, though developers can also choose pre-distilled alternatives.
takeaways: Knowledge distillation uses a larger teacher model to train an independent, smaller student model.
Student models learn from signals produced by the teacher, such as predictions, enabling them to require less memory and compute.
Distillation yields a fundamentally different model rather than an exact, compressed copy of the original teacher.
While student models can perform specific tasks well, they may lose breadth, reliability, or the ability to manage unfamiliar problems.
The cost of training a distilled model is paid once, facilitating repeated deployments or adoption of pre-distilled models.

sections.title: Pruning: Remove Work That Contributes Less
sections.summary: Pruning reduces computational overhead by eliminating weights or structural components whose removal results in an acceptable loss of quality. While zeroing individual weights introduces sparsity, it does not automatically reduce storage or execution costs without specialized compressed representations, hardware support, or software engines designed to skip zeroed operations. Alternatively, removing entire units or layers directly downsizes the model structure. Realizing actual efficiency gains requires coordination between the pruned model and the underlying execution runtime, and subsequent retraining may be necessary if too much capacity is removed.
takeaways: Pruning removes weights or larger components that contribute minimally to overall model quality.
Zeroing weights creates sparsity, but standard array operations still consume memory and computation unless specifically optimized.
Realizing execution savings requires compressed representations, runtime engines capable of skipping inactive calculations, or hardware support.
Removing structural components like layers or computation unit groups directly shrinks the model.
Excessive pruning degrades model performance, often requiring additional training to recover quality.

sections.title: The Conversation Has Its Own Memory Requirements
sections.summary: Even after reducing model weights, transformers can encounter out-of-memory errors on long sequences due to dynamic memory requirements. During generation, the key-value (KV) cache stores intermediate representations from prior tokens to avoid redundant calculations. Unlike fixed model weights, the KV cache grows dynamically as sequence length and the number of active conversations increase. Mitigating this memory footprint involves reducing input context, quantizing the cache, or offloading parts of it to CPU memory at the expense of speed or quality.
takeaways: The KV cache stores intermediate token states in transformers to avoid repeated calculations during generation.
KV cache memory is separate from model weights and expands with longer context lengths and additional conversations.
A static model size does not prevent out-of-memory errors caused by large context workloads.
Context size can be managed by retrieving relevant document passages rather than loading full documents.
Quantizing the KV cache or offloading it to CPU memory helps manage capacity but can impact generation speed or quality.

sections.title: Better Software Can Make the Same Hardware More Useful
sections.summary: The implementation of an inference runtime can significantly boost performance on existing hardware without altering model weights. FlashAttention improves execution by partitioning attention calculations into blocks, utilizing fast internal GPU memory to lower memory traffic while computing exact attention. PagedAttention, introduced in vLLM, manages the KV cache in blocks to eliminate memory fragmentation and duplication during dynamic request serving. Additionally, serving software improves throughput by batching multiple requests together to share the overhead of reading model weights, requiring more working memory in exchange.
takeaways: Inference runtime software implementation can substantially impact performance even when model weights remain unchanged.
FlashAttention reorganizes attention calculations into blocks to leverage fast GPU memory and reduce memory traffic.
FlashAttention computes exact attention without modifying or reducing model weights.
PagedAttention was introduced with vLLM to manage the KV cache in blocks, reducing memory waste from inefficient allocation.
Serving frameworks batch requests to share the cost of loading model weights, which increases throughput at the cost of higher working memory.

sections.title: Speculative Decoding: Propose Several Tokens Before Checking Them
sections.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive text generation by employing a smaller, faster draft model to propose several candidate tokens. The larger target model evaluates these candidates concurrently, leveraging greater parallelism than standard sequential generation. Accepted tokens are appended to the generation, while rejected tokens are corrected by the target model. Because maintaining a separate draft model increases memory requirements, speculative decoding does not reduce the baseline memory footprint required for the target model.
takeaways: A small draft model proposes multiple candidate tokens ahead of verification.
The larger target model evaluates proposed candidate tokens in parallel rather than one by one.
Rejected tokens trigger corrections generated directly by the target model.
Speed improvements depend on the draft model's agreement rate with the target model and verification costs.
Speculative decoding adds memory overhead for the draft model and does not help an oversized target model fit into constrained memory.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: Deploying models under hardware constraints, such as a system with 32 GB RAM and 8 GB VRAM, requires balancing memory capacity against response latency and output quality. Applying four-bit quantization reduces an 8B model's theoretical weight footprint from 16 GB to 4 GB, while layer and cache offloading can address remaining memory limits at the expense of transfer speed. A thorough evaluation framework measures answer quality, peak memory consumption, time to first token, and overall generation speed against application-specific demands. Because optimizations like quantization and offloading impact different workload components, their resource savings do not simply compound multiplicatively.
takeaways: Four-bit quantization reduces an 8B model's theoretical weight requirements from 16 GB to 4 GB.
Layer or cache offloading can alleviate memory pressure, but the resulting data transfer overhead may degrade generation speed.
Model evaluation must track answer quality, peak memory use, time to first token, and generation speed.
Tolerance for latency depends heavily on the use case, contrasting interactive code suggestions with background document processing.
Optimization savings from quantization, offloading, architectural decisions, and runtime execution do not compound multiplicatively because they target distinct parts of the workload.

Fitting large language models on smaller hardware is constrained by total memory capacity, memory location, and processing bottlenecks. An 8-billion-parameter model at 16-bit precision requires about 16 GB just for weights, plus extra space for software overhead, temporary calculations, and context. Because persistent storage like SSDs is too slow for execution, weights must reside in fast working memory such as RAM or GPU VRAM. Beyond capacity, memory bandwidth and compute architecture pose limits, with GPUs providing superior parallelism over CPUs and distinct bottlenecks arising across the prefill and decoding stages of inference. Local execution allows developers to utilize existing hardware for experimentation and decrease reliance on rented cloud infrastructure. This approach offers enhanced privacy for sensitive documents and proprietary code, alongside offline capability for desktop assistants and remote deployments. zh.summary: AI 模型仰賴以層級結構組織的數值參數（即 weights）將輸入轉換為輸出。在語言模型中，輸入文字會被拆分成 tokens，模型則透過預測後續 token 的機率來反覆生成回應。雖然 training 是一個在昂貴基礎設施上更新 weights 的運算密集型過程，但 inference 使用的是固定 weights，通常可以在一般的消費級硬體上執行。要在較小的硬體上塞入大型語言模型，會受到總記憶體容量、記憶體存放位置以及運算瓶頸的限制。以 16-bit 精度執行的 8-billion-parameter 模型，光是 weights 就需要約 16 GB，另外還需要額外空間給軟體 overhead、暫存運算和 context。由於 SSD 等 persistent storage 的讀寫速度太慢無法直接用於執行，weights 必須存放在如 RAM 或 GPU VRAM 這類高速工作記憶體中。除了容量之外，memory bandwidth 和 compute architecture 也構成了限制——GPU 提供了優於 CPU 的平行處理能力，而在 inference 的 prefill 與 decoding 階段也會面臨不同的瓶頸。本地端執行（local execution）讓開發者能利用現有硬體進行實驗，並減少對租用雲端基礎設施的依賴。這種方式為敏感文件與專有程式碼提供了更高的隱私性，同時也為桌面助理與遠端部署提供了離線運作能力。此外，在本地運行模型能對模型版本與應用程式行為擁有更高的掌控度。然而，這並不一定在所有情況下都具備成本效益，因為硬體、電力、維護與 latency 的考量，都必須對照使用頻率與 hosted service 進行權衡。
