最接近的匹配結果可能是錯誤的 Policy

sections.title: LLM 需要證據來回答問題
sections.summary: Large language models 缺乏直接存取企業內部私有文件的能力，需要 context 中提供外部依據才能準確回答問題。Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) 透過 embedding models 和 vector databases 在將相關文件段落傳送給 LLM 之前先進行檢索，藉此解決這個問題。最終生成答案的品質高度取決於 retrieval 階段，因為即便模型能力再強，不完整或過時的檢索 context 都會導致答案不正確。因此，文件集合必須以適當的 granularity 建立索引且可被搜尋，才能支援可靠的輸出。
takeaways: Language models 本身並不知道私有文件的內容，必須在查詢時提供相關佐證。
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) 是一種架構模式，應用程式會檢索相關的文字段落並餵給 LLM，以回答問題並引用來源。
Embedding models 會將問題轉換為數值表示，由 vector databases 進行儲存與搜尋以找出相關段落。
生成回答的準確度直接取決於生成前的檢索階段；檢索出的 context 若不完整或過時，將導致錯誤的回答。
高效的 RAG 系統需要文件集在適當的詳細程度下具備可搜尋性。

sections.title: 文件如何轉換為可搜尋的段落
sections.summary: 將整份文件視為單一可搜尋單元會產生過於寬泛的表示，進而掩蓋具體的規則。為了解決這個問題，檢索應用程式會將文件劃分為稱為 chunk 的較小單元，以精確定位個別段落。Chunking 需要在精確度與 context 之間取得平衡，因為過小的 chunk 可能會遺漏關鍵限制條件，而過大的 chunk 則會引入無關的雜訊。像是加入章節標題以及在相鄰 chunk 之間保留有限的 overlap 等技巧，有助於保留必要的 context，讓段落即使單獨存在也能被理解。
takeaways: 將整份文件作為單一單元建立索引會產生寬泛的表示，進而掩蓋具體的 policy 規則。
Chunking 將文件分割為較小的單元，使搜尋系統能夠回傳精確的段落，而非整份原始文件。
Chunk size 涉及搜尋精確度與 context 完整性之間的權衡（trade-off）。
將規則與其條件或例外情況拆分到不同的 chunk，可能導致 assistant 生成錯誤的回答。
保留章節標題並在相鄰 chunk 之間使用有限的 overlap，有助於維持獨立理解的能力。

sections.title: LLM 如何理解不同詞彙背後的意涵
sections.summary: Embeddings 透過將段落表示為共享空間中的高維數值向量（vectors），實現了跨不同用詞的語意搜尋（semantic search）。語意並非編碼在孤立的維度中，而是透過整個向量的整體 pattern 來表現，其中語意相關的段落會緊密聚類在一起。有效的檢索需要使用相容的 encoders 將 queries 與 document chunks 映射到同一個空間中，而非僅僅共享向量長度的模型。此外，向量記錄必須保留與底層段落文字、chunk ID 及 metadata 的關聯，讓 language models 能夠解讀並維護檢索到的資訊。
takeaways: Embedding models 會將文字段落轉換為包含數百或數千個小數維度的向量（vectors）。
語意是分布在完整的向量 pattern 中，而非分配給個別具標籤的維度。
Queries 與 document chunks 必須使用相容的 encoders 嵌入（embed）到同一個 vector space 中。
兩個模型具有相同的向量維度，並不代表 encoder 具備相容性。
可搜尋的記錄必須將 vector embeddings 與 raw text、chunk ID 以及版本和章節等 metadata 連結起來，以供 LLM 解讀。

sections.title: 多近才算足夠接近？
sections.summary: 搜尋系統需要 similarity 或 distance metrics 來定義向量表示之間的相近程度。核心指標如 cosine similarity、Euclidean distance 與 dot product 在處理向量長度（magnitude）時表現各異，但正規化（normalization）至 unit length 後，它們的排序結果會是等價的。選擇適當的 metric 直接取決於 embedding model 原本的設計，而非流行程度。此外，similarity scores 代表的是向量之間的幾何關係，而非檢索出的段落在事實上為真的機率。
takeaways: Cosine similarity 會比較向量方向，同時忽略向量長度。
Euclidean distance 測量端點之間的直線距離，因此對向量長度十分敏感。
Dot product 同時反映方向對齊程度與向量長度。
當向量被正規化（normalized）為 unit length 時，dot product 就等於 cosine similarity，且 Euclidean distance 會產生完全相同的排序。
選擇 distance metric 時，應嚴格對齊 embedding model 的設計。
Similarity scores 量化的是向量之間的關聯性，並不代表答案正確的機率。

sections.title: 為什麼搜尋每一段 passage 的成本過於高昂
sections.summary: Flat vector search 會將 query 與每個符合條件的向量進行比對，以得出精確的 nearest neighbors，但其運算成本會隨 collection size 與 vector dimensionality 呈線性增長。為了降低搜尋成本，Inverted-File (IVF) indexing 將向量圍繞代表性中心組織成 cluster，僅查詢選定的分組子集。nprobe 參數決定了要搜尋多少個分組，以計算速度換取 recall。因此，IVF 接受了跳過某些分組中相關 passage 的風險，進而引入了近似（approximation）。
takeaways: Flat index 搜尋比對的規模會隨 collection size 呈線性增長（O(n)），並隨 vector dimensionality 增加。
Flat search 在數值上保證能找到精確的 nearest neighbors，但無法確保語意上的正確性。
Inverted-File (IVF) indexing 透過將向量圍繞 cluster centers 分組，並僅搜尋選定的組別來減少比對工作量。
nprobe 參數控制在 IVF 搜尋期間要檢查多少個向量分組。
搜尋更多組別會提高 recall，但也會增加運算量。
IVF 是一種 approximate search 方法，因為被跳過的組別中可能包含相關的 passage 而遭到遺漏。

sections.title: 順著連結找到正確的 neighborhood
sections.summary: Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) 是一種基於圖（graph-based）的 indexing 方法，專為 approximate nearest-neighbor search 設計，可避免窮舉式的向量比對。它將跨階層的向量連結組織起來，從稀疏的上層導航到底層完整的節點層，以高效率收斂搜尋範圍。雖然 HNSW 大幅減少了比對操作，但 routing 捷徑偶爾可能會錯過真正的 nearest neighbors。在 HNSW、flat search 與 Inverted-File indexing 之間做選擇時，取決於可用記憶體、query volume 與 latency 要求等因素，而非僅僅取決於向量數量。
takeaways: HNSW 將向量連線組織成一個多層圖（multi-layered graph），上層較為稀疏，最底層則包含完整節點。
搜尋導航採由上而下（top-down）的方式進行，先迅速朝向目標 neighborhood 移動，最後在底層進行更細粒度的 candidate exploration。
如同 Inverted-File indexing，HNSW 執行的也是 approximate nearest-neighbor search，以可能遺漏真正的 nearest neighbors 為代價來降低比對成本。
沒有固定的 collection size 規定何時該用 Inverted-File 或 HNSW indexing 取代 flat search。
系統架構的選擇高度取決於記憶體容量、vector dimensions、query volume、filtering 需求以及 latency 限制。

sections.title: 搜尋到什麼程度才算足夠？
sections.summary: Approximate search 在檢索速度與 nearest-neighbor recall 之間帶來了固有的權衡（tradeoff）。評估系統時，需要區分 index recall 與檢索出的佐證對使用者 query 的實際相關性。在 HNSW 演算法中，M、ef_construction 和 ef_search 等參數控制了 graph connectivity、建置成本以及 candidate exploration 的廣度。調整這些設定必須透過具代表性問題的實證測試來推動，而不是在沒有提升回答準確度的情況下單純增加 latency。
takeaways: 相較於 exact nearest-neighbor search，approximate search 在搜尋速度與 recall 之間產生了可衡量的權衡（tradeoff）。
Index recall 衡量的是對 exact search 結果的逼真度（fidelity），而不是檢索到的 passage 是否真正回答了使用者的問題。
在 HNSW 中，M 決定了 graph connectivity，以較高的記憶體使用量與 build time 換取更好的 recall。
ef_construction 決定了 insertion 期間的搜尋廣度，而 ef_search 則控制 query 時 candidate exploration 的廣度。
Candidate exploration 的廣度（ef_search）與最終返回結果的數量無關。
Parameter tuning 應針對具代表性的問題進行驗證，以確保增加的 latency 能帶來實質的檢索效益。

sections.title: 最接近的匹配結果可能是錯誤的 Policy
sections.summary: 若未強制套用地區或生效日期等資格條件（eligibility criteria），單靠 similarity search 可能會檢索到不相關的文件。Metadata filtering 透過限制結果來解決這個問題，常見做法包括在 ranking 前評估條件的 pre-filtering，或在候選結果檢索後進行過濾的 post-filtering。在 vector 和 graph search 中，單純的 pre-filtering 或 post-filtering 都非萬能的最佳解，因為不合條件的節點可能仍是關鍵的 traversal 路徑。因此，搜尋引擎通常會透過 filtering-aware graph 結構、特化的 traversal 策略，或針對小規模子集進行 exact scan，將 filtering 直接整合至搜尋流程中。
takeaways: 當單靠 similarity ranking 會找出語義相近但不合資格的記錄時，metadata filtering 便不可或缺。
Pre-filtering 在 similarity ranking 之前識別出符合資格的記錄，而 post-filtering 則是在候選結果檢索完成後才剪除記錄。
如果 similarity 最高的前幾名候選結果大多不符合資格條件，post-filtering 可能會無法回傳足夠的有效結果。
在 graph search 中，若在 traversal 期間完全封鎖不合資格的節點，可能會導致符合資格的鄰近節點無法抵達。
Filtering 可以透過 filtering-aware graph、調整 traversal 方式或 exact scan，直接整合進搜尋演算法中。

sections.title: 當答案變更時會發生什麼事？
sections.summary: 當來源資訊變更時，必須謹慎維護 document collection，以防止檢索系統給出矛盾或過時的答案。修改已向量化的文字需要重新生成 embedding，但如果 metadata 本身未被向量化，metadata 的更新通常無需 re-embedding 即可執行。使用 version identifier 和 active-version 規則來協調更新，有助於避免 ingestion 期間出現短暫的資料缺口或重複。此外，切換到新的 embedding model 需要全面規劃，將整個 corpus 重新 embed 到新模型的 vector space 中。
takeaways: 修改來源文字需要產生新的 embedding，但未變更的 chunk 可以透過穩定的 identifier 重複使用。
如果 metadata 未包含在 embedding 文字中，純 metadata 的更新通常可以略過 re-embedding。
在插入新 chunk 之前刪除舊 chunk 會造成暫時性的檢索缺口，而先插入再刪除則有暫時重複的風險。
Version identifier 與 active-version 規則有助於實現可預測的轉移，並保留對歷史 policy 的存取能力。
更換 embedding model 需要將既有的 document collection 重新 embed 到新的 representation space 中。

sections.title: 從潛在的匹配結果到有依據的答案
sections.summary: 最後的檢索階段會將候選文件轉化為 large language model 的可靠佐證。Reranker 會評估並從 vector search 的初步結果集中選出最相關的段落。Hybrid search 結合了基於 embedding 的 semantic search 與針對精確詞彙的 keyword search，進一步提升候選結果的品質。系統設計者也必須考慮無法回答的查詢（unanswerable queries），意識到找到最近的 vector match 並不保證存在事實答案。
takeaways: Reranker 會直接將候選段落與使用者問題進行比對，以選出最相關的佐證依據。
Hybrid search 將基於 embedding 的 semantic 檢索與基於 keyword 的檢索相結合。
Keyword search 有助於確保特定 identifier、名稱及罕見技術名詞的 exact match。
即使資料庫中沒有與 query 相關的資訊，vector search 仍然會回傳 nearest-neighbor 的匹配結果。
應用程式應在檢索到的 policy context 缺乏答案時明確說明，而不是產生 hallucination。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: 為 LLM 應用程式建構高效的 retrieval pipeline 時，需要對文件進行 chunking，並將其表示為 vector embedding 以捕捉 semantic similarity。隨著文件量擴展，flat search、IVF 和 HNSW 等 indexing 策略在 query 速度、memory footprint 與 recall 之間進行明確的 trade-off。除了 similarity matching 之外，系統還仰賴 metadata filtering、持續的 index hygiene、hybrid search 和 reranking 來挑選精確且最新的 context。最終，LLM 最終回覆的品質與事實可靠性，直接取決於這套整合的 retrieval workflow。
takeaways: Embedding 將文字 chunk 轉換為 vector，從而實現跨不同措辭的 semantic 檢索。
Flat search 執行窮舉式的 vector 比對，而 IVF 和 HNSW 則透過分組與 graph traversal 來降低 latency，代價是在 memory 和 recall 之間做出 trade-off。
若未依據文件類型、地區或政策版本進行 metadata filtering，單靠 Vector similarity 不足以保證提供有效的佐證資料。
定期更新 index 是必要的，以避免過期與重複的文件污染 retrieval 結果。
結合 hybrid search 與 reranking 能提升提供給 LLM 的最終 context 品質。

items.title: Do LLMs Have the Memory of a Goldfish?

sections.title: What Does “memory” Mean for an LLM?
sections.summary: The term 'memory' in the context of large language models refers to multiple distinct concepts rather than a single unified mechanism. It is critical to differentiate between these meanings to avoid confusion. This section serves as an introduction to examining and clarifying the various types of memory associated with LLMs.
takeaways: The word 'memory' has multiple distinct meanings when applied to large language models.
Different forms of LLM memory should not be conflated with one another.
A detailed breakdown is required to understand each specific type of LLM memory.

sections.title: Trained Memory
sections.summary: During training, large language models encode patterns from vast amounts of data into billions of parameters or weights, enabling general knowledge recall without explicit prompt context. However, standard API interactions do not update these weights, meaning models lack persistent personal memory of individual conversations. Instead, models rely on a temporary context window as working memory to process instructions, conversation history, and retrieved context. Once this context window is cleared, the model loses access to that information unless it is reintroduced by the application.
takeaways: Patterns learned during LLM training are encoded into billions of numerical parameters or weights.
Standard API responses do not modify or rewrite model weights, preventing the base model from permanently retaining user-specific facts.
A model's context window serves as its temporary working memory for generating responses.
The context window contains system instructions, conversation history, retrieved documents, tool outputs, and user preferences.
Information in the context window is ephemeral and cannot be recovered by the model once cleared unless re-provided by the application.

sections.title: Persistent Application Memory
sections.summary: Persistent memory operates external to the model, typically residing in systems such as databases, files, vector stores, or profile services. When required, the application retrieves this stored information and injects it directly into the active context. Consequently, models do not inherently possess persistent memory on their own. Instead, they depend on external auxiliary systems to supply persistent information during execution.
takeaways: Persistent memory is maintained outside the model in external systems like databases, vector stores, files, or profile services.
The application retrieves relevant persistent information and inserts it into the model context when needed.
Models do not natively possess persistent memory.
All persistent information utilized by the model is delivered to it by external systems.

sections.title: What Happens During a Basic API Call?
sections.summary: AI model API calls are inherently stateless, meaning the model does not store an internal record or memory of prior interactions once a request finishes. If an application requires context from earlier turns, it must re-send the preceding conversation history within the current request payload. As a result, most providers implement a stateless Messages API that depends on the client supplying the full dialogue history for multi-turn conversations.
takeaways: AI models do not retain memory or state across independent API calls.
A request lacking previous context cannot reliably access details supplied in earlier requests.
Applications must retransmit previous exchanges in multi-turn dialogues to preserve context.
Most model providers utilize a stateless Messages API design that expects the conversation history in each request.

sections.title: Does Every API Call Really Start From Zero?
sections.summary: A new model API call does not start completely from zero because it retains its trained weights, general language capabilities, platform safety instructions, and provided context. However, models inherently lack an automatically updated personal memory of specific users or past conversations. Outputs are strictly generated from the model's static weights combined with whatever context is supplied for that specific invocation. Even when APIs offer server-managed conversation state via session identifiers, the server is simply reconstructing the context for the model rather than imparting personal memory to it.
takeaways: A model invocation retains trained weights, language abilities, training knowledge, and platform safety instructions.
Models do not possess an automatically updated memory of specific users or ongoing conversations.
Every output is generated purely from the model's weights and the context supplied for that specific invocation.
Prior conversation history is completely unavailable unless the surrounding system explicitly forwards it.
Server-managed conversation state uses conversation identifiers to reconstruct context behind the scenes without changing the model's stateless nature.

sections.title: How AI Chatbots Create the Illusion of Memory
sections.summary: AI chatbots create the appearance of conversational recall by appending the full dialogue history, including system instructions and past user-assistant turns, into each subsequent prompt. To the underlying model, this interaction is simply an evaluation of a single large input rather than true temporal retention. Because application-level continuity exists, this technique is more appropriately classified as reconstructed or context-based memory rather than fake memory.
takeaways: Chatbot applications construct a single large input containing all previous conversation turns and system instructions for each new turn.
Underlying language models do not store persistent memories across interactions, but process prior conversational context present in the active prompt.
Continuity in chat systems exists at the application level rather than within the model itself.
The phenomenon of passing conversation history as prompt context is best described as reconstructed memory or context-based memory.

sections.title: The Context Window is a Working-Memory Budget
sections.summary: The context window of a large language model acts as a finite working-memory budget measured in tokens. Beyond the visible conversation, this budget must accommodate system instructions, tool definitions, retrieved documents, and the output response. When capacity is reached, applications must remove, compress, or replace content to stay within limits. Crucially, larger context windows do not ensure perfect recall, as models face a degradation phenomenon known as context rot when processing excessive information.
takeaways: Context windows are measured in tokens, which represent words or parts of words.
A context window must allocate space for hidden system instructions, tool definitions, retrieved documents, and generated output in addition to visible conversation history.
Once context limits are met, an application must compress, remove, or replace existing information.
Larger context windows do not guarantee accurate recall due to a degradation problem known as context rot.
Managing the context window requires active attention management and information filtering, not just raw token capacity.

sections.title: Why Long Conversations Become Expensive
sections.summary: LLM APIs charge for processed tokens, causing the cumulative token cost of long conversations to grow rapidly as earlier history is reprocessed with every new turn. In addition to escalating financial costs, longer contexts increase generation latency. Prompt caching can mitigate latency and repetitive processing expenses by reusing prefixes such as system prompts and history. However, because cached tokens still consume context window space, prompt caching serves as an efficiency optimization rather than a true memory architecture.
takeaways: Conversational rounds reprocess prior history on every request, leading to cumulative input token growth that exceeds the visible conversation size.
Longer contexts increase latency because the model must process more information before beginning output generation.
Additional elements like system prompts, tool definitions, and retrieved documents compound per-request token consumption.
Prompt caching reduces cost and latency by reusing precomputed prefixes like system prompts and conversation history.
Prompt caching is an optimization technique and does not grant unlimited memory or expand the context window.

sections.title: What Happens When the Context Window Fills Up?
sections.summary: Large language models and their hosting applications have no single universal behavior when reaching context window limits. Instead, systems use various strategies such as request rejection, message truncation, rolling windows, and compaction. Compaction preserves the core state of a conversation in a reduced representation to enable long-running sessions. However, this summarization technique is inherently lossy, meaning seemingly unimportant details might be prematurely discarded.
takeaways: Context window exhaustion has no universal standard behavior across LLM providers and applications.
Common strategies for handling full context windows include rejecting requests, evicting oldest messages, using rolling windows, and substituting past context with compact summaries.
Compaction preserves essential conversation state in a smaller format to permit extended interactions under reduced context usage.
Summarization in context management is lossy, creating a tradeoff where information deemed low-value initially may be needed later.

sections.title: The Main Techniques to Extend Memory
sections.summary: Real-world applications typically require combining multiple approaches to extend memory rather than relying on an isolated solution. Integrating different techniques allows systems to handle memory constraints more effectively in practice. This section introduces an exploration into several of these specific memory-extension methods.
takeaways: Practical applications generally combine multiple techniques to extend memory.
Relying on a single memory extension technique is usually insufficient for real-world systems.
A variety of distinct techniques exist to address memory extension in detail.

sections.title: Sliding-window Memory
sections.summary: Sliding-window memory retains only the most recent portion of a conversation by discarding the oldest messages when new ones arrive. A typical setup preserves system instructions, a fixed number of recent turns, and the current user input. While simple, fast, and predictable, this technique is best suited for dialogues where recent context matters far more than historical context. Its main disadvantage is permanent information loss once earlier requirements or facts exit the active context window.
takeaways: A sliding window retains the newest messages and removes the oldest as conversations progress.
Common setups preserve system instructions, the current user message, and a fixed number of recent turns (e.g., 20 turns).
The technique provides simplicity, fast execution, and predictable memory usage.
Effectiveness relies on recent conversational context being more critical than past messages.
Facts that leave the context window are forgotten, preventing the model from recalling earlier constraints.

sections.title: Conversation Summarization
sections.summary: Conversation summarization periodically compresses older conversation turns into concise descriptions to maintain the context efficiently. A standard context structure consists of system instructions, the conversation summary, recent unsummarized messages, and the current user query. However, summarization acts as an interpretation that strips nuance, simplifies uncertainty, and risks converting assumptions into false facts. To avoid progressive information distortion from repeated summarization, essential facts should be stored separately rather than entrusted to a narrative summary alone.
takeaways: Summarization periodically condenses older messages into a compact description while discarding original turns.
A typical conversation context layout combines system instructions, the summary, recent unsummarized turns, and the current user prompt.
Repeatedly summarizing prior summaries causes cumulative distortion, similar to photocopying a photocopy.
Summaries tend to lose nuance, flatten uncertainty, and can misrepresent assumptions as confirmed facts.
Critical facts are more reliably preserved by storing them separately rather than relying on iterative narrative summaries.

sections.title: Structured Entity Extraction
sections.summary: Structured entity extraction records specific conversational facts into predefined fields rather than storing interactions as raw prose. This approach provides higher reliability when an application needs to access exact project state and confirmed parameters. While effective for discrete items like user preferences, technical decisions, and workflow statuses, it struggles to capture nuanced narrative details that resist structured schemas.
takeaways: Structured entity extraction parses specific facts into structured fields instead of relying on prose conversation logs.
Querying structured fields is more reliable for exact project state retrieval than searching long text summaries.
Structured memory is well-suited for discrete data including user preferences, technical decisions, workflow statuses, and deadlines.
Subtle, narrative information that cannot be mapped to predefined schemas is poorly served by structured entity extraction.

sections.title: Vector-store-backed Memory
sections.summary: Vector-store-backed memory enables conversational systems to perform semantic retrieval rather than appending entire conversation histories into context. The system segments past dialogue into chunks, transforms them into embeddings, and compares them against incoming queries to identify relevant passages. Only the highest-ranking passages are inserted into the prompt, effectively managing the model's context window. However, semantic search can retrieve irrelevant, outdated, or poorly matched memories, making metadata filtering crucial for accuracy.
takeaways: Vector stores enable semantic retrieval by segmenting past conversations and converting them into embeddings.
Embeddings numerically capture meaning, allowing matches between texts that express similar concepts without identical wording.
The workflow embeds new queries, retrieves semantically similar memory candidates, filters and ranks them, and inserts the top results into the prompt.
Semantic retrieval selects relevant memories for the context window rather than increasing the window size.
Failure modes include retrieving irrelevant matches, missing memories phrased unusually, and returning outdated decisions.
Using metadata like user ID, project ID, date, and memory type is essential to prevent retrieval errors.

sections.title: Long-term User Profiles
sections.summary: A long-term user profile stores durable preferences and facts that remain useful across multiple conversations. Systems must distinguish between stable, repeatedly confirmed preferences and transient session-level details. Profiles require ongoing updates because user preferences evolve over time. Effective implementations enrich memory entries with metadata such as timestamps, sources, and confidence scores.
takeaways: Long-term user profiles preserve durable facts across conversations rather than transient statements.
Session information reflects temporary activities, whereas durable preferences require repeated confirmation.
User profiles must be updated over time to accommodate evolving preferences.
Robust memory systems tag memory entries with metadata including timestamps, sources, and confidence scores.

sections.title: How Cross-session Memory Works
sections.summary: Cross-session memory enables information to persist across separate chat sessions and influence subsequent interactions. A background process identifies durable details from a conversation and saves them into a user-, project-, or organization-level store. When a new session begins, relevant memories are retrieved and explicitly inserted into the model's active context window. This context insertion step is critical, as the model requires the remembered information to be present in its prompt to inform responses.
takeaways: Cross-session memory allows information to survive past the end of an individual chat session.
Durable information is identified and saved to a user-level, project-level, or organization-level memory store.
For cross-session memory to function, retrieved memories must be explicitly injected into the new conversation's context.
The underlying model generates responses relying on the supplied memories placed within its current context.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: Large language models do not intrinsically carry personal experiences or episodic memory from one interaction to the next. Instead, apparent LLM memory is produced by an architectural system combining model weights, context windows, conversation storage, long-term memory, and a memory manager. This setup relies on processes including context reconstruction, summarization, retrieval, and persistent storage. Ultimately, the quality and effectiveness of an LLM application's memory depend heavily on its surrounding software architecture rather than just the underlying model.
takeaways: Model weights contain general knowledge acquired during training but do not retain interaction history across calls.
The context window holds only the information active for generating the current response.
Conversation storage preserves previous messages, whereas long-term memory stores selected facts, preferences, and past events.
The memory manager governs what information is retrieved and placed into active context.
LLMs do not automatically carry personal experiences from one API call to the next.
LLM memory is an engineered system of context reconstruction, summarization, retrieval, and persistent storage.

items.summary: The term 'memory' in the context of large language models refers to multiple distinct concepts rather than a single unified mechanism. It is critical to differentiate between these meanings to avoid confusion. This section serves as an introduction to examining and clarifying the various types of memory associated with LLMs. During training, large language models encode patterns from vast amounts of data into billions of parameters or weights, enabling general knowledge recall without explicit prompt context. However, standard API interactions do not update these weights, meaning models lack persistent personal memory of individual conversations. Instead, models rely on a temporary context window as working memory to process instructions, conversation history, and retrieved context. Once this context window is cleared, the model loses access to that information unless it is reintroduced by the application. Persistent memory operates external to the model, typically residing in systems such as databases, files, vector stores, or profile services. When required, the application retrieves this stored information and injects it directly into the active context. Consequently, models do not inherently possess persistent memory on their own. Instead, they depend on external auxiliary systems to supply persistent information during execution.

sections.title: 對 LLM 而言，“memory” 意味著什麼？
sections.summary: 'memory' 一詞在 large language models 的語境下指的是多個截然不同的概念，而非單一的統一機制。區分這些含義至關重要，以避免混淆。本節旨在探討並釐清與 LLM 相關的各種類型 memory。
takeaways: 當應用於 large language models 時，'memory' 一詞具有多種截然不同的含義。
不同形式的 LLM memory 不應混為一談。
需要詳細拆解才能理解每一種特定類型的 LLM memory。

sections.title: Trained Memory
sections.summary: 在 training 期間，large language models 會將來自海量數據的 pattern 編碼進數十億個 parameters 或 weights 中，從而在沒有顯式 prompt context 的情況下實現通用知識召回。然而，標準的 API 互動並不會更新這些 weights，這意味著模型缺乏對個別對話的 persistent personal memory。相反地，模型依賴暫時的 context window 作為 working memory，來處理指令、對話歷史和 retrieved context。一旦這個 context window 被清空，模型就會失去對該資訊的存取權限，除非 application 重新引入它。
takeaways: 在 LLM training 期間學到的 pattern 會被編碼進數十億個數值 parameters 或 weights 中。
標準的 API response 不會修改或重寫 model weights，從而使 base model 無法永久保留特定於使用者的事實。
模型的 context window 是其生成回應時的暫存 working memory。
context window 包含 system instructions、conversation history、retrieved documents、tool outputs 與 user preferences。
context window 中的資訊是暫態的（ephemeral），一旦被清除，除非 application 重新提供，否則模型無法復原。

sections.title: Persistent Application Memory
sections.summary: Persistent memory 運作於模型外部，通常存放於 databases、files、vector stores 或 profile services 等系統中。當需要時，application 會檢索這些儲存的資訊，並直接注入到當前的 context 中。因此，模型本身並不原生具備 persistent memory；相反地，它們仰賴外部輔助系統在執行期間提供 persistent 資訊。
takeaways: Persistent memory 維護在模型外部的系統中，例如 databases、vector stores、files 或 profile services。
Application 會在需要時檢索相關的 persistent 資訊，並將其插入至 model context 中。
模型原生並不具備 persistent memory。
模型所使用的所有 persistent 資訊，都是由外部系統提供給它的。

sections.title: 基本的 API Call 過程中會發生什麼事？
sections.summary: AI 模型的 API calls 本質上是 stateless 的，這意味著一旦 request 結束，模型就不會儲存先前互動的內部紀錄或記憶。若 application 需要前幾輪對話的 context，就必須在當前的 request payload 中重新發送先前的 conversation history。因此，大多數 provider 都實作了 stateless 的 Messages API，仰賴 client 端為多輪對話提供完整的對話歷史。
takeaways: AI 模型不會在獨立的 API calls 之間保留記憶或 state。
缺少先前 context 的 request 無法可靠地存取早期 requests 中提供的詳細資訊。
Application 必須在多輪對話中重新傳送先前的交談內容，以保留 context。
大多數模型 provider 都採用 stateless 的 Messages API 設計，預期在每個 request 中接收 conversation history。

sections.title: 每一次 API Call 真的都從零開始嗎？
sections.summary: 一個新的模型 API call 並非完全從零開始，因為它保留了訓練好的 weights、通用語言能力、platform safety instructions 以及所提供的 context。然而，模型本質上缺乏針對特定使用者或過去對話的自動更新個人記憶。Output 完全是根據模型的 static weights 結合該次特定 invocation 所提供的 context 所生成的。即使 API 透過 session identifiers 提供 server-managed conversation state，server 也只是在替模型重建 context，而不是賦予它個人記憶。
takeaways: 一次 model invocation 會保留訓練好的 weights、語言能力、訓練知識以及 platform safety instructions。
模型並不具備針對特定使用者或進行中對話的自動更新記憶。
每個 output 純粹是從模型的 weights 以及為該次特定 invocation 提供的 context 所生成。
除非周圍的系統明確轉發，否則先前的 conversation history 完全無法取得。
Server-managed conversation state 在幕後使用 conversation identifiers 來重建 context，而不會改變模型的 stateless 本質。

sections.title: AI Chatbot 如何營造出擁有記憶的假象
sections.summary: AI chatbot 透過將完整的對話歷史（包含 system instructions 與過去的 user-assistant turns）附加到後續的每個 prompt 中，營造出具備對話記憶的假象。對底層模型而言，這種互動僅僅是對單一大型 input 的評估，而非真正的時間性保留。由於 application 層級的連續性確實存在，這種技術被歸類為重建型（reconstructed）或 context-based memory，會比稱為假記憶（fake memory）更為貼切。
takeaways: Chatbot 應用程式會在每個新輪次中建構一個包含所有先前 conversation turns 和 system instructions 的單一大型 input。
底層的 language models 並不會跨互動儲存持久的記憶，而是處理當前 active prompt 中所包含的先前對話 context。
chat systems 的連貫性存在於 application level，而非 model 本身內部。
將對話歷史作為 prompt context 傳遞的現象，最貼切的描述是 reconstructed memory 或 context-based memory。

sections.title: Context Window 是一筆 Working-Memory Budget
sections.summary: large language model 的 context window 就像是以 token 為計量單位的有限 working-memory budget。除了可見的對話之外，這筆 budget 還必須容納 system instructions、tool definitions、retrieved documents 以及輸出的 response。當容量達到上限時，application 必須移除、壓縮或替換內容以保持在限制之內。關鍵在於，更大的 context windows 並不能保證完美的 recall，因為 models 在處理過多資訊時會面臨稱為 context rot 的退化現象。
takeaways: Context windows 是以 token 為計量單位，代表單詞或單詞的一部分。
除了可見的對話歷史之外，context window 還必須為隱藏的 system instructions、tool definitions、retrieved documents 和生成的 output 分配空間。
一旦達到 context 限制，application 就必須壓縮、移除或替換現有資訊。
由於稱為 context rot 的退化問題，更大的 context windows 並不能保證準確的 recall。
管理 context window 需要主動的 attention 管理和資訊過濾，而不僅僅是 raw token capacity。

sections.title: 為什麼長對話會變得昂貴
sections.summary: LLM API 會針對處理過的 token 收費，導致長對話的累積 token 成本迅速增加，因為每一次新的 turn 都會重新處理早期的歷史紀錄。除了不斷攀升的財務成本外，更長的 context 還會增加 generation latency。Prompt caching 可以透過重複使用 system prompts 和歷史紀錄等 prefix 來降低 latency 和重複處理的開銷。然而，由於 cached tokens 仍然會占用 context window 空間，因此 prompt caching 只是一種效率最佳化手段，而非真正的 memory 架構。
takeaways: 對話輪次在每次 request 時都會重新處理先前的歷史紀錄，導致累積的 input token 增長幅度遠超過可見的對話規模。
更長的 context 會增加 latency，因為 model 在開始輸出 generation 之前必須先處理更多資訊。
額外的元素如 system prompts、tool definitions 和 retrieved documents 會使每次 request 的 token 消耗量成倍增加。
Prompt caching 透過重複使用預先計算的 prefix（例如 system prompts 和對話歷史）來降低成本和 latency。
Prompt caching 是一種最佳化技術，並不會提供無限的 memory 或擴大 context window。

sections.title: 當 Context Window 裝滿時會發生什麼事？
sections.summary: 當達到 context window 限制時，large language models 及其託管的 applications 並沒有單一通用的行為。相反地，系統會採用各種策略，例如 request rejection、message truncation、rolling windows 和 compaction。Compaction 透過縮減後的表示形式來保留對話的核心 state，以支援長時間運行的 session。然而，這種 summarization 技術本質上是有損（lossy）的，這意味著看似不重要的細節可能會被過早捨棄。
takeaways: Context window 耗盡在各個 LLM providers 和 applications 之間並沒有統一的標準行為。
處理 context window 已滿的常見策略包括拒絕 request、驅逐最舊的 message、使用 rolling windows，以及將過去的 context 替換為精簡的摘要。
Compaction 以較小的格式保留關鍵對話 state，以便在減少 context 使用量的情況下支援更長期的互動。
Context 管理中的 summarization 是有損的（lossy），這會產生一種權衡：最初被認為價值較低的資訊，後續可能會被需要。

sections.title: 擴展 Memory 的主要技術
sections.summary: 在實際應用中，通常需要結合多種方法來擴展 memory，而不是依賴單一的解決方案。整合不同技術能讓系統在實務上更有效地應對 memory 限制。本節將探討其中幾種具體的 memory 擴展方法。
takeaways: 實際應用通常會結合多種技術來擴展 memory。
在真實世界系統中，單純依賴單一 memory 擴展技術通常是不夠的。
目前存在多種不同的技術，可具體解決 memory 擴展的問題。

sections.title: Sliding-window Memory
sections.summary: Sliding-window memory 僅保留對話中最新的部分，並在新訊息到達時捨棄最舊的訊息。典型的配置會保留 system instructions、固定數量的近期對話輪次（turns）以及當前的 user input。雖然這種技術簡單、快速且具備可預測性，但最適合用於近期 context 遠比歷史 context 重要的對話場景。其主要缺點在於，一旦早期的需求或事實脫離了作用中的 context window，就會造成永久性的資訊遺失。
takeaways: 隨著對話推進，sliding window 會保留最新的訊息並移除最舊的訊息。
常見配置會保留 system instructions、當前 user message 以及固定數量的近期對話輪次（例如 20 turns）。
該技術具備簡單、執行快速以及 memory 使用量可預測的優勢。
其有效性取決於近期對話 context 是否比過往訊息更為關鍵。
脫離 context window 的事實將被遺忘，導致 model 無法回想先前的 constraints。

sections.title: Conversation Summarization
sections.summary: Conversation summarization 會定期將較早的對話輪次壓縮為精簡描述，以有效維持 context。標準的 context 結構包含 system instructions、對話 summary、近期未摘要的訊息以及當前的 user query。然而，summarization 本質上是一種解讀，會削弱細微差異（nuance）、淡化不確定性，並有將假設誤轉為錯誤事實的風險。為避免因反覆 summarization 造成漸進式的資訊失真，核心事實應分開儲存，而非完全依賴敘事性的 summary。
takeaways: Summarization 會定期將較舊的訊息濃縮為精練描述，同時捨棄原始對話輪次。
典型的對話 context 佈局結合了 system instructions、summary、近期未摘要的對話輪次，以及當前的 user prompt。
對先前的 summary 反覆進行摘要會導致累積失真，類似於拿影印本再次影印。
Summary 往往會遺失細節差異、抹平不確定性，並可能將假設誤傳為已確認的事實。
相較於依賴反覆迭代的敘事性 summary，將關鍵事實分開儲存能更可靠地保留資訊。

sections.title: Structured Entity Extraction
sections.summary: Structured entity extraction 將具體的對話事實記錄至預定義欄位中，而非將互動儲存為原始文字（raw prose）。當應用程式需要存取確切的專案狀態與確認過的參數時，這種方法具備更高的可靠性。雖然它在處理 user preferences、技術決策和 workflow statuses 等離散項目時相當有效，但難以捕捉無法納入結構化 schemas 的細緻敘事細節。
takeaways: Structured entity extraction 將特定事實解析至結構化欄位中，而不是依賴文字形式的對話日誌。
相較於搜尋長篇文字 summary，查詢結構化欄位對於檢索確切的專案狀態更為可靠。
Structured memory 非常適合處理離散資料，包括 user preferences、技術決策、workflow statuses 和截止期限。
無法對應到預定義 schema 的隱性敘事資訊，難以透過 structured entity extraction 妥善處理。

sections.title: Vector-store-backed Memory
sections.summary: Vector-store-backed memory 讓對話系統能夠執行語意檢索（semantic retrieval），而不是將整個對話歷史直接附加至 context 中。系統會將過往對話切分成 chunks，轉換成 embeddings，並將其與傳入的 queries 進行比對以找出相關段落。僅有排序最高（highest-ranking）的段落會被插入到 prompt 中，進而有效管理 model 的 context window。然而，語意搜尋可能會檢索出無關、過期或匹配度低的 memory，因此 metadata filtering 對於維持準確度至關重要。
takeaways: Vector stores 透過將過去的對話切分並轉換為 embeddings 來實現 semantic retrieval。
Embeddings 以數值化方式捕捉語意，讓表達相似概念但用詞不同的文字之間能夠進行比對。
此工作流程會將新的 queries 轉為 embeddings、檢索語意相似的 memory 候選項目、進行過濾與排序，並將 top results 插入 prompt 中。
Semantic retrieval 是為 context window 挑選相關的 memory，而非單純擴大 window size。
常見的 failure modes 包括檢索出不相關的結果、遺漏措辭特殊的 memory，以及返回過時的決策。
使用像 user ID、project ID、date 與 memory type 等 metadata，對於避免檢索錯誤至關重要。

sections.title: Long-term User Profiles
sections.summary: Long-term user profile 儲存了跨多次對話依然有用的持久偏好與事實。系統必須區分穩定且經過反覆確認的偏好，與暫態的 session-level 細節。由於使用者偏好會隨時間演進，profiles 需要持續更新。高效的實作會為 memory entries 加上 timestamp、source 與 confidence score 等 metadata。
takeaways: Long-term user profiles 保留的是跨對話的持久事實，而非短暫的陳述。
Session 資訊反映的是暫時性的活動，而持久偏好則需要經過反覆確認。
User profiles 必須持續更新，以因應隨時間演變的偏好。
穩健的 memory 系統會為 memory entries 標記 metadata，包括 timestamps、sources 與 confidence scores。

sections.title: Cross-session Memory 的運作原理
sections.summary: Cross-session memory 讓資訊能夠跨越不同的 chat sessions 持續存在，並影響後續的互動。背景行程會從對話中識別出持久的細節，並將其儲存至 user-level、project-level 或 organization-level 的 store 中。當新 session 開始時，相關的 memories 會被檢索出來，並明確地插入模型的 active context window 中。這個 context insertion 步驟至關重要，因為模型需要 prompt 中具備被記憶的資訊，才能做出準確的回應。
takeaways: Cross-session memory 讓資訊能在單一 chat session 結束後繼續保留。
持久資訊會被識別出來，並儲存至 user-level、project-level 或 organization-level 的 memory store 中。
要讓 cross-session memory 正常運作，檢索出的 memories 必須明確地注入到新對話的 context 中。
底層模型依靠放置在當前 context 中的 memories 來產生回應。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: Large language models 本質上並不會在互動之間傳遞個人經驗或 episodic memory。相反地，看似具備的 LLM memory 是由一個結合了 model weights、context windows、conversation storage、long-term memory 和 memory manager 的架構系統所建構出來的。此架構依賴 context reconstruction、summarization、retrieval 與 persistent storage 等處理程序。最終，LLM 應用的 memory 品質與成效，很大程度上取決於其周圍的軟體架構，而非僅僅是底層模型本身。
takeaways: Model weights 包含在訓練期間獲得的通用知識，但不會保留跨 calls 的互動紀錄。
Context window 僅保存用於生成當前回應的有效資訊。
Conversation storage 保存先前的訊息，而 long-term memory 則儲存精選的事實、偏好與過往事件。
Memory manager 負責控制哪些資訊會被檢索並放入 active context 中。
LLMs 不會自動將個人經驗從一次 API call 延續到下一次。
LLM memory 是一個由 context reconstruction、summarization、retrieval 與 persistent storage 所構成的工程化系統。

sections.title: Tracing what happens inside an LLM pipeline
sections.summary: Dynatrace has released a reference application to help developers inspect and debug the internal operations of LLM pipelines. The application demonstrates how to use distributed tracing to measure latency across embeddings, retrieval, and generation steps rather than treating the pipeline as a single opaque call. Built with Python, it utilizes Amazon Bedrock for core AI tasks and OpenTelemetry for observability, providing a template for instrumenting production LLM apps.
takeaways: Measuring only the outer HTTP request latency is insufficient for debugging complex LLM pipelines involving retrieval and agents.
Dynatrace's reference application includes a Python travel advisor with basic, RAG, and agentic execution paths.
The system uses Amazon Bedrock for both text generation and embedding tasks.
Observability is achieved using OpenTelemetry and Traceloop to record workflows and export traces via OTLP.
The reference repository provides sample dashboards and deployment files for local or Kubernetes-based execution.

sections.title: Easiest way to run agent harnesses using local models
sections.summary: Magnitude is an open-source tool designed to simplify the process of running local LLMs for agent harnesses. It addresses the complexity of model selection by profiling hardware and benchmarking performance rather than just checking memory capacity. The tool recommends practical models based on context length and quantization, then facilitates connection to agents like Claude Code or OpenCode. This approach ensures that the selected model is fast enough for the repetitive workloads typical of agent loops.
takeaways: Local model selection depends on weights, context length (KV-cache), and quantization levels.
Available RAM or VRAM is an insufficient metric for determining if inference speed is adequate for agent loops.
Agent harnesses generate long, repeated workloads that differ from isolated prompt-response cycles.
Magnitude profiles hardware and benchmarks performance to recommend practical local models.
Magnitude supports integration with harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi.

sections.title: Practical defenses for prompt injection
sections.summary: Prompt injection is identified by OWASP as the primary threat to LLM applications, necessitating a shift from behavioral constraints to architectural enforcement. Five key defenses are proposed: using delimiters for untrusted text, establishing an instruction hierarchy, applying the principle of least privilege to tools, requiring human-in-the-loop approval, and implementing the Dual LLM pattern. These strategies, such as those formalized in Google's Spotlight and DeepMind's CaMeL framework, aim to create robust security boundaries by layering multiple protective measures.
takeaways: OWASP ranks prompt injection as the number one threat to LLM-based applications.
Delimiters like XML tags or Base64 encoding provide structural signals to models to treat input as data rather than instructions.
Instruction hierarchy assigns trust levels to different prompt sources, ensuring developer instructions override third-party content.
The principle of least privilege reduces risk by restricting an agent's tool access to the absolute minimum required for a task.
The Dual LLM pattern separates reasoning (Planner) from action (Executor) to prevent untrusted data from influencing control flow.
Google DeepMind's CaMeL framework successfully addressed the AgentDojo security benchmark using architectural isolation.

items.title: LLMs as a Judge: How to Know if Your LLM is Healthy

sections.title: What Does it Mean for an LLM Application to be Healthy?
sections.summary: An LLM application is considered healthy when it consistently delivers useful outputs while satisfying constraints across accuracy, safety, speed, reliability, and cost. Evaluating health requires examining multiple interconnected dimensions of quality rather than relying on a single metric like output correctness. Furthermore, evaluators must distinguish between the health of the underlying LLM and the broader application system. Failures can stem from surrounding factors like faulty prompts, retrieval issues, stale data, or tooling errors rather than the model itself.
takeaways: An LLM is considered healthy if it consistently produces useful results within acceptable limits of accuracy, safety, speed, reliability, and cost.
Assessing application health requires evaluating multiple quality dimensions rather than a single metric such as correctness.
A model might perform well in one dimension, like tone or relevance, while failing critically in others, like factual accuracy or latency.
System evaluators must decouple the health of the underlying LLM from the health of the overall application.
Application issues frequently originate outside the model, including poor retrieval logic, incorrect prompts, missing documents, or flawed tool calls.

sections.title: Why Ordinary Tests Are Not Sufficient for LLMs?
sections.summary: Traditional software testing is insufficient for large language models because LLMs produce non-deterministic, probabilistic outputs where multiple distinct phrasings can be correct. Additionally, evaluating LLM output quality is multidimensional and subjective, requiring clear and concrete definitions of target attributes such as tone and detail. Correctness often hinges directly on contextual inputs, meaning evaluations must account for the specific data provided to the model. Nonetheless, deterministic software components within LLM applications, such as JSON parsing and tool execution, still require standard unit and integration testing.
takeaways: Traditional tests rely on deterministic single-correct-answer outputs, whereas LLMs generate variable responses probabilistically.
Exact string matching fails for LLM evaluation because different sentences can convey identical meaning.
Setting a low temperature does not guarantee perfect reproducibility across different models and infrastructure setups.
LLM quality evaluation is subjective and multidimensional, requiring precise criteria rather than vague quality targets.
LLM output correctness is context-dependent and must be evaluated relative to supplied data such as policies and user status.
Traditional unit and integration tests remain necessary for deterministic parts of LLM systems, including JSON parsing, API contracts, and tool execution.

sections.title: The Basic Evaluation Loop
sections.summary: A practical LLM evaluation system operates as a continuous iterative loop to maintain application quality and prevent regressions. The process begins by running representative test cases through the application and inspecting the outputs using multiple evaluation methods. New iterations are compared against the production baseline to block or investigate any observed regressions. Finally, real production traffic is monitored to detect edge cases and failures, which are continuously fed back into the test set to expand the evaluation dataset.
takeaways: A practical LLM evaluation loop requires testing against representative cases and inspecting outputs using multiple evaluation methods.
Application updates are compared against the current production version to block or investigate regressions.
Real production traffic must be monitored for novel failure modes and ambiguous inputs missed by existing tests.
Evaluation datasets must continuously evolve by incorporating newly discovered production failures.

sections.title: Golden Datasets for Repeatable Tests for LLM Behavior
sections.summary: A golden dataset acts as a unit-testing suite for LLMs by defining curated inputs along with criteria for what constitutes a valid response rather than enforcing exact string equality. Robust datasets should reflect diverse scenarios including common queries, boundary cases, ambiguous prompts, adversarial instructions, and historical production failures. Splitting the dataset into development and holdout sets prevents prompts from overfitting to specific test examples. Test cases can encompass complex evaluation criteria such as expected facts, forbidden claims, allowed tool calls, and scoring rubrics.
takeaways: Golden datasets serve as repeatable evaluation suites for LLMs without requiring exact string equality matching.
Effective test cases define correct decisions, constraints, expected facts, and forbidden claims rather than a single reference answer.
Golden datasets should incorporate edge cases, boundary conditions, unanswerable queries, multilingual inputs, prompt injections, and past production failures.
Splitting datasets into development and holdout sets prevents overfitting prompts to known examples during refinement.
Test cases can be multifaceted, containing inputs, source context, tool call specifications, rubrics, and optional references.

sections.title: Automated Metrics: Fast but Limited Checks
sections.summary: Automated metrics evaluate LLM outputs using code rather than human or model inspection, making them inexpensive, fast, and repeatable for large test suites. They include exact match checks for constrained extraction, schema validators and regular expressions for structural conformance, and programmatic checks for specific constraints like URLs or ranges. Overlap-based metrics like BLEU and ROUGE evaluate surface wording, whereas embedding-based semantic similarity metrics compare underlying meaning. However, automated metrics are fundamentally constrained to narrow, observable properties, and semantic similarity does not inherently guarantee factual correctness.
takeaways: Automated metrics rely on code to inspect outputs, providing fast and repeatable evaluations for large test batches.
Exact match checks are effective for constrained tasks like country codes or IDs, but fail on open-ended natural language.
Regular expressions and schema validators verify structural requirements such as valid JSON syntax and field data types.
BLEU and ROUGE quantify word overlap for machine translation and summarization, but penalize semantically equivalent paraphrasing.
Semantic similarity metrics assess response meaning via embeddings or specialized models, but similarity does not equate to correctness.
Automated metrics should be limited to narrow, observable properties that code can reliably verify.

sections.title: What Does LLM-as-a-Judge Mean?
sections.summary: LLM-as-a-Judge is an evaluation technique where one language model assesses another model's generated output against defined criteria. In scenarios such as evaluating a RAG assistant, the judge model examines the query, retrieved context, generated answer, and evaluation rubric to score qualities like accuracy, completeness, and relevance. This technique offers greater flexibility than exact matching by identifying semantic equivalence and subtle generation errors.
takeaways: LLM-as-a-Judge utilizes a secondary language model to evaluate a primary model's responses based on specific criteria.
Common inputs to the judge model include the original question, retrieved source documents, the assistant's answer, an evaluation rubric, and an optional reference answer.
Qualities assessed by the judge model can include relevance, factual support, completeness, clarity, and instruction compliance.
Unlike rigid exact matching, an LLM judge can recognize semantically equivalent phrasing across different wordings.
Judge models can detect nuanced failure modes, such as partially answered queries or unsupported factual claims.

sections.title: Different Ways a Judge Model Can Evaluate an Answer
sections.summary: This section serves as an introduction to how judge models evaluate answers. It highlights that multiple standard methodologies exist for conducting such evaluations. The passage prepares the reader for a detailed breakdown of each specific evaluation approach.
takeaways: Judge models rely on multiple common methods to evaluate generated answers.
Different evaluation techniques exist for assessing answer quality.
The section introduces an in-depth examination of each evaluation method.

sections.title: Point-based Scoring
sections.summary: Point-based scoring involves using a judge model to assign numerical ratings, such as a scale of 1 to 5, across distinct quality dimensions. This method produces quantitative metrics that simplify tracking performance changes over time as models are iteratively refined. However, a major challenge is score inconsistency across evaluations. To maintain reliability, practitioners must define rigorous evaluation rubrics that specify concrete criteria for each numerical score level.
takeaways: In point-based scoring, a judge model evaluates quality dimensions using numerical ranges such as 1 to 5.
Quantitative scores provide metrics that are easy to track over time during model refinement.
The primary drawback of point-based scoring is inconsistency in how score values are interpreted.
Rigorous, detailed rubrics defining the exact meaning of each score are required to ensure consistent evaluations.
Score definitions can be structured around factual support against reference documents, ranging from complete contradiction (score 1) to full support (score 5).

sections.title: Pass or Fail Classification
sections.summary: A judge model can evaluate whether an output meets a defined minimum standard, making it useful for deployment gates with clear-cut requirements. Examples of these strict requirements include avoiding policy contradictions, preventing privacy leaks, and ensuring instructions are valid. While pass-or-fail evaluations offer operational simplicity, they mask gradual performance declines. As a result, system quality can drop from excellent to marginally acceptable without triggering a failure threshold.
takeaways: Judge models can evaluate whether model outputs satisfy a minimum acceptable threshold.
Pass-or-fail evaluation is especially suitable for deployment gates when requirements are explicitly defined.
Binary classification effectively enforces non-negotiable criteria like privacy protection, policy compliance, and instruction validity.
A major drawback of pass-or-fail results is that they conceal subtle quality drops.
Performance can decline substantially from excellent to barely acceptable without crossing the failure boundary.

sections.title: Pairwise Comparison
sections.summary: Pairwise comparison is an evaluation method where a judge model evaluates two candidate answers and decides which one is superior. This technique often produces more consistent results than assigning absolute numerical scores, as relative assessments are easier to determine. A known limitation of this approach is position bias, where the judge model favors whichever answer appears first or second. Reversing the presentation order of candidate responses is recommended to counteract this bias.
takeaways: In pairwise comparison, a judge model evaluates two responses to decide which is better.
The method can compare outputs between an existing production prompt and a newly proposed prompt.
Relative pairwise ranking is generally more consistent and easier than assigning absolute numerical scores.
Judge models are prone to position bias, systematically favoring either the first or second response presented.
Reversing the presentation order of responses mitigates position bias.

sections.title: Error Identification
sections.summary: Judge models can identify specific problems rather than merely producing a numerical evaluation score. They are able to flag issues such as unsupported claims, unanswered parts of a prompt, irrelevant sections, and violated instructions. This diagnostic capability provides clear explanations for score fluctuations, making it especially valuable during the development phase.
takeaways: Judge models can pinpoint granular errors rather than just assigning overall scores.
Common errors identified include unsupported claims, unanswered parts of a question, irrelevant sections, and violated instructions.
Detailed error identification is useful during development to explain why evaluation scores change.

sections.title: Human Evaluation and Calibration
sections.summary: Human evaluation remains the ultimate benchmark for measuring model quality, especially in domain-specific tasks requiring legal, medical, or scientific expertise. Because human review is costly and slow, reviewers are best utilized to calibrate automated judge LLMs using representative sample sets. Comparing expert evaluations with automated scores reveals judge model accuracy, blind spots, and necessary threshold adjustments. Additionally, measuring reviewer agreement is necessary to identify ambiguous rubrics and account for subjectivity before treating human judgments as ground truth.
takeaways: Domain experts are crucial in human evaluation when correctness depends on specialized legal, medical, financial, or scientific knowledge.
A primary role of human evaluation is calibrating automated judge LLMs using representative sample ratings.
Comparing expert decisions against a judge model uncovers agreement rates, missed failure modes, and required passing threshold adjustments.
Measuring reviewer agreement is necessary before treating human scores as a perfect reference, as disagreement indicates rubric ambiguity or genuine subjectivity.
Human evaluation is vital for validating initial rubrics, handling high-risk failures, assessing novel requests, and periodically auditing automated judges for drift.

sections.title: The Evaluation Stack
sections.summary: The LLM evaluation stack operates as a series of complementary layers rather than a hierarchy of mutually exclusive replacements. Foundational deterministic methods, including conventional software testing and automated checks, verify schemas, permissions, and latency. LLM judges and golden datasets handle semantic interpretation and repeatable end-to-end evaluation. Finally, human review provides calibration for judges on subjective or critical tasks, while production monitoring detects real-world failures that pre-deployment test sets miss.
takeaways: The evaluation stack is composed of complementary layers rather than a strict replacement ladder.
Conventional software tests verify deterministic components like tool schemas, calculations, permissions, and database writes.
Automated checks reliably measure properties such as JSON validity, latency, citation structure, and required fields.
LLM judges evaluate semantic properties, assessing whether responses are relevant, complete, and supported by evidence against a rubric.
Human reviewers are used to calibrate LLM judges and assess subjective or high-consequence cases.
Production monitoring is necessary because static test sets cannot anticipate all real-world user requests.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: LLM evaluation should not be approached as a pursuit of a single accuracy score, but as a holistic system for establishing confidence in an application. A robust evaluation framework combines golden datasets for repeatability, automated metrics for objective checks, LLM judges for rubric-based assessment, and human reviewers for calibration. Ultimately, evaluation aims to ensure that the entire application remains safe, accurate, useful, fast, and cost-effective across critical scenarios, while providing telemetry to detect regressions.
takeaways: LLM evaluation is intended to build confidence in a model rather than compute a single accuracy metric.
Golden datasets enable the repeatable testing of critical situations.
Automated metrics provide fast verification of narrow, objective properties.
LLM judges evaluate semantic meaning based on predefined rubrics.
Human reviewers calibrate LLM judges and resolve difficult edge-case decisions.
Evaluation must assess the whole application across accuracy, safety, reliability, speed, and cost, ensuring performance drift is detectable.

Traditional software testing is insufficient for large language models because LLMs produce non-deterministic, probabilistic outputs where multiple distinct phrasings can be correct. Additionally, evaluating LLM output quality is multidimensional and subjective, requiring clear and concrete definitions of target attributes such as tone and detail. Correctness often hinges directly on contextual inputs, meaning evaluations must account for the specific data provided to the model. Nonetheless, deterministic software components within LLM applications, such as JSON parsing and tool execution, still require standard unit and integration testing. A practical LLM evaluation system operates as a continuous iterative loop to maintain application quality and prevent regressions. The process begins by running representative test cases through the application and inspecting the outputs using multiple evaluation methods. New iterations are compared against the production baseline to block or investigate any observed regressions. Finally, real production traffic is monitored to detect edge cases and failures, which are continuously fed back into the test set to expand the evaluation dataset.

sections.title: 什麼樣的 LLM 應用程式才稱得上健康（Healthy）？
sections.summary: 一個 LLM 應用程式只有在滿足準確度、安全性、速度、可靠性與成本等限制條件，並持續交付有用輸出的情況下，才會被視為健康。評估健康狀態需要審視多個相互關聯的品質維度，而非僅依賴輸出正確性這類的單一指標。此外，評估者必須區分底層 LLM 的健康狀態與更廣泛的應用系統。故障可能源於周遭因素，例如有缺陷的 prompt、retrieval 問題、陳舊資料或 tooling 錯誤，而非模型本身。
takeaways: 若 LLM 能在準確度、安全性、速度、可靠性與成本的可接受範圍內持續產生有用結果，則被視為健康。
評估應用程式的健康狀態需要評估多個品質維度，而非僅依賴如正確性這類的單一指標。
模型可能在某個維度表現良好（例如 tone 或 relevance），但在其他維度卻嚴重失常（例如 factual accuracy 或 latency）。
系統評估者必須將底層 LLM 的健康狀態與整體應用程式的健康狀態解耦（decouple）。
Application 的問題通常源自 model 外部，包括不良的 retrieval logic、不正確的 prompts、遺失的文件，或是出問題的 tool calls。

sections.title: 為什麼一般的測試對 LLMs 來說不夠？
sections.summary: 傳統軟體測試對 large language models 來說並不充分，因為 LLMs 會產生 non-deterministic（非確定性）且具機率性質的輸出，其中多種完全不同的措辭可能都是正確的。此外，評估 LLM 的輸出品質是多維度且主觀的，需要對目標屬性（如 tone 和 detail）有清晰且具體的定義。正確性通常直接取決於 contextual inputs，這表示 evaluation 必須考慮提供給 model 的特定資料。儘管如此，LLM application 內部的 deterministic 軟體組件（例如 JSON parsing 和 tool execution）仍然需要標準的 unit testing 與 integration testing。
takeaways: 傳統測試依賴 deterministic 的單一正確答案輸出，而 LLMs 則是以機率方式生成多樣化的回應。
Exact string matching 在 LLM evaluation 中會失效，因為不同的句子可能表達完全相同的語意。
設定較低的 temperature 並不能保證在不同 models 和 infrastructure 設定下具有完美的 reproducibility。
LLM 品質評估是主觀且多維度的，需要精確的 criteria，而非模糊的品質目標。
LLM 輸出的正確性取決於 context，必須相對於所提供的資料（例如 policies 和 user status）進行評估。
傳統的 unit tests 與 integration tests 對於 LLM 系統中的 deterministic 部分仍然至關重要，包括 JSON parsing、API contracts 以及 tool execution。

sections.title: 基礎 Evaluation Loop
sections.summary: 一個實用的 LLM evaluation 系統以持續的迭代循環（continuous iterative loop）運作，以維持 application 品質並防止 regressions。該流程首先是透過 application 執行具代表性的 test cases，並使用多種 evaluation 方法檢查輸出。新的迭代會與 production baseline 進行比較，以阻擋或調查任何觀察到的 regressions。最後，監控真實的 production traffic 以偵測 edge cases 和 failures，並持續回饋到 test set 中以擴充 evaluation dataset。
takeaways: 一個實用的 LLM evaluation loop 需要針對具代表性的案例進行測試，並使用多種 evaluation 方法來檢查輸出。
Application 更新會與目前的 production 版本進行比較，以阻擋或調查 regressions。
必須監控真實的 production traffic，以找出既有測試所遺漏的新型 failure modes 和模稜兩可的 inputs。
Evaluation datasets 必須透過納入新發現的 production failures 來持續演進。

sections.title: 用於 LLM 行為可重現測試的 Golden Datasets
sections.summary: Golden dataset 扮演 LLMs 的 unit-testing suite 角色，它定義了精心挑選的 inputs 以及何謂有效回應的 criteria，而非強制要求 exact string equality。健全的 datasets 應反映多元的情境，包括常見 queries、boundary cases、模稜兩可的 prompts、adversarial instructions 以及過去的 production failures。將 dataset 切分為 development 和 holdout sets 可以防止 prompts overfitting 到特定的測試範例。Test cases 可以包含複雜的 evaluation criteria，例如 expected facts、forbidden claims、allowed tool calls 以及 scoring rubrics。
takeaways: Golden datasets 可作為 LLMs 的可重現 evaluation suites，而無需 exact string equality 比對。
有效的 test cases 會定義正確的決策、constraints、expected facts 和 forbidden claims，而非單一的 reference answer。
Golden datasets 應納入 edge cases、boundary conditions、無法回答的 queries、多語言 inputs、prompt injections 以及過去的 production failures。
將 datasets 切分為 development 和 holdout sets，可在調校過程中避免 prompts overfitting 到已知範例。
Test cases 可以是多面向的，包含 inputs、source context、tool call specifications、rubrics 和可選的 references。

sections.title: Automated Metrics：快速但受限的檢查
sections.summary: Automated metrics 使用程式碼而非人工或 model 審查來評估 LLM 輸出，使其在大型 test suites 中具有成本低、快速且 repeatable 的優勢。它們包括針對受限抽取的 exact match 檢查、用於結構一致性的 schema validators 和 regular expressions，以及針對特定條件（如 URLs 或範圍）的程式化檢查。基於重疊度的指標（如 BLEU 和 ROUGE）評估表層措辭，而基於 embedding 的語意相似度指標則比較底層語意。然而，automated metrics 本質上受限於狹隘且可觀察的屬性，且語意相似度本質上並不保證 factual correctness。
takeaways: Automated metrics 依賴程式碼來檢查輸出，為大批次的測試提供快速且 repeatable 的 evaluations。
Exact match 檢查對於國家代碼或 ID 等受限任務非常有效，但無法應對開放式的 natural language。
Regular expressions 與 schema validators 用於驗證結構性需求，例如有效的 JSON 語法及欄位 data types。
BLEU 和 ROUGE 量化 machine translation 與 summarization 的詞彙重疊度，但會對語意等價的改寫（paraphrasing）進行懲罰。
Semantic similarity 指標透過 embeddings 或專用模型評估回覆的含義，但相似度並不等於正確性。
Automated metrics 應局限於程式碼能可靠驗證的狹義、可觀察屬性。

sections.title: 什麼是 LLM-as-a-Judge？
sections.summary: LLM-as-a-Judge 是一種評估技術，由一個語言模型依據定義好的標準來評估另一個模型生成的輸出。在評估 RAG 助理等情境中，judge model 會檢查 query、retrieved context、generated answer 以及 evaluation rubric，為準確性、完整性與相關性等特質評分。這項技術能識別語意等價性以及細微的生成錯誤，因此比 exact matching 提供更高的彈性。
takeaways: LLM-as-a-Judge 利用次要語言模型，根據特定標準評估主要模型的回覆。
judge model 常見的輸入包括原始問題、檢索到的來源文件、助理的回答、evaluation rubric 以及選填的 reference answer。
judge model 評估的特質可包括相關性、事實依據、完整性、清晰度以及 instruction compliance。
與死板的 exact matching 不同，LLM judge 能夠辨識不同措辭之間在語意上等價的表達。
Judge models 可以偵測出細微的 failure modes，例如僅部分回答的 queries 或缺乏依據的事實主張。

sections.title: Judge Model 評估回答的不同方式
sections.summary: 本節介紹 judge models 如何評估回答。文中強調進行此類評估存在多種標準方法，並引導讀者深入了解每種具體評估方法的詳細剖析。
takeaways: Judge models 仰賴多種常見方法來評估生成的回答。
評估回答品質存在多種不同的評估技術。
本節將深入介紹每種評估方法。

sections.title: Point-based Scoring
sections.summary: Point-based scoring 涉及使用 judge model 在不同的品質維度上賦予數值評分（例如 1 到 5 分）。這種方法產生的量化指標簡化了在模型反覆調校過程中隨時間追蹤效能變化的工作。然而，主要挑戰在於評估之間的分數不一致性。為了保持可靠性，工程師必須定義嚴格的 evaluation rubrics，為每個分數等級具體說明明確的標準。
takeaways: 在 point-based scoring 中，judge model 會使用例如 1 到 5 的數值範圍來評估品質維度。
量化分數提供的指標便於在模型調校過程中隨時間持續追蹤。
Point-based scoring 的主要缺點在於對分數數值的詮釋存在不一致性。
必須具備嚴謹且詳細的 rubrics 來定義每個分數的確切意涵，以確保評估的一致性。
分數定義可以圍繞對照 reference documents 的事實支持度來構建，範圍從完全矛盾（1 分）到完全支持（5 分）。

sections.title: Pass or Fail Classification
sections.summary: judge model 可以評估輸出是否符合定義好的最低標準，這使其非常適合用於具有明確要求的 deployment gates。這些嚴格要求的範例包括避免違反 policy、防止隱私洩漏以及確保 instructions 有效。雖然 pass-or-fail 評估在維運上很單純，但它們會掩蓋漸進式的效能衰退。其結果就是，系統品質可能從極佳下滑到勉強可接受，卻不會觸發 failure threshold。
takeaways: Judge models 可以評估 model outputs 是否達到最低可接受的 threshold。
當需求被明確定義時，pass-or-fail 評估特別適用於 deployment gates。
Binary classification 能有效執行不可妥協的標準，例如隱私保護、policy compliance 以及 instruction validity。
Pass-or-fail 結果的一大缺點是它會隱藏細微的品質下降。
效能可能從優秀大幅下滑到勉強可接受，卻未跨過 failure boundary。

sections.title: Pairwise Comparison
sections.summary: Pairwise comparison 是一種評估方法，由 judge model 評估兩個候選回答並判斷哪一個更優。相較於給予絕對數值分數，這種技術通常能產生更一致的結果，因為相對評估更容易判定。此方法的一個已知局限是 position bias，即 judge model 會偏好出現在第一個或第二個的回答。建議調換候選 responses 的呈現順序，以消除這種 bias。
takeaways: 在 pairwise comparison 中，judge model 會評估兩個 responses 以決定哪一個更好。
此方法可以比較現有 production prompt 與新提議 prompt 之間的 outputs。
相較於給予絕對數值分數，相對的 pairwise ranking 通常更具一致性且更容易。
Judge models 容易出現 position bias，系統性地偏好呈現的第一個或第二個 response。
調換 responses 的呈現順序可以減輕 position bias。

sections.title: Error Identification
sections.summary: Judge models 可以識別特定問題，而不僅僅是產生數值評估分數。它們能夠標記出未獲佐證的論點、prompt 中未回答的部分、無關段落以及違反 instructions 的情況。這種診斷能力能為分數波動提供清晰的解釋，在開發階段尤其有價值。
takeaways: Judge models 可以精確指出 granular errors，而非僅僅給出總體分數。
常見被識別出的錯誤包括未獲佐證的論點、問題中未回答的部分、無關的段落，以及違反 instructions。
詳細的 error identification 在開發過程中非常實用，有助於解釋評估分數變動的原因。

sections.title: Human Evaluation and Calibration
sections.summary: Human evaluation 仍然是衡量 model quality 的最終基準，尤其是在需要法律、醫療或科學專業知識的 domain-specific 任務中。由於人工審核成本高昂且緩慢，審核人員最好用於透過具代表性的樣本集來 calibrate 自動化的 judge LLMs。將專家評估與自動化分數進行比對，可以揭露 judge model 的準確度、盲點以及所需的 threshold 調整。此外，在將人類評判視為 ground truth 之前，有必要衡量 reviewer agreement，以識別模糊不清的 rubrics 並考量主觀性因素。
takeaways: 當正確性取決於法律、醫療、金融或科學等專業知識時，domain experts 在 human evaluation 中至關重要。
Human evaluation 的主要作用之一，是使用具代表性的樣本評分來 calibrate 自動化的 judge LLMs。
將專家決策與 judge model 進行比較，可以揭露 agreement rates、未捕捉到的 failure modes，以及所需的 passing threshold 調整。
在將人工評分視為完美參考之前，必須先衡量 reviewer agreement，因為意見分歧代表 rubric 存在模糊性或是本質上的主觀性。
Human evaluation 對於驗證初始 rubrics、處理高風險 failure、評估全新 requests 以及定期審查 automated judges 是否發生 drift 至關重要。

sections.title: Evaluation Stack
sections.summary: LLM evaluation stack 的運作方式是一系列互補的層級（layers），而非彼此互斥的替代階梯。基礎的 deterministic 方法（包含傳統軟體測試與自動化檢查）負責驗證 schema、權限與 latency。LLM judges 與 golden datasets 則處理語意解讀以及可重複的 end-to-end 評估。最後，human review 針對主觀或關鍵任務為 judges 提供校準（calibration），而 production monitoring 則能偵測部署前測試集所遺漏的真實環境故障。
takeaways: Evaluation stack 是由互補的層級組成，而非嚴格相互取代的階梯。
傳統軟體測試可驗證 deterministic 元件，例如 tool schema、計算邏輯、權限以及 database 寫入。
自動化檢查能可靠地衡量 JSON 有效性、latency、citation 結構與必填欄位等屬性。
LLM judges 依據 rubric 評估語意屬性，檢驗回覆是否切題、完整且有證據支持。
Human reviewers 用於校準 LLM judges，並評估主觀或高風險（high-consequence）的案例。
Production monitoring 是必要的，因為靜態測試集無法預測所有真實世界的使用者請求。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: LLM evaluation 不應只是追求單一 accuracy 分數，而是要作為一套為應用程式建立信賴度的全方位系統。一個健全的 evaluation framework 結合了確保可重複性的 golden datasets、用於客觀檢查的 automated metrics、基於 rubric 評估的 LLM judges，以及用於校準的 human reviewers。歸根究底，evaluation 的目標是確保整個應用程式在關鍵情境下保持安全、準確、實用、快速且具成本效益，同時提供 telemetry 來偵測 regression。
takeaways: LLM evaluation 的目的在於建立對模型的信心，而非僅計算單一 accuracy 指標。
Golden datasets 能夠針對關鍵情境進行可重複的測試。
Automated metrics 能夠快速驗證特定且客觀的屬性。
LLM judges 依據預先定義的 rubric 評估語意內容。
Human reviewers 負責校準 LLM judges，並處理棘手的 edge-case 決策。
Evaluation 必須在 accuracy、安全性、可靠性、速度與成本等多個面向全面評估整體應用程式，確保能夠偵測到 performance drift。

items.title: What It Takes to Build a Production Agent Harness

sections.title: Building a production agent harness in LangChain
sections.summary: An agent harness serves as the execution layer that manages interactions between models, tools, and application state. This series demonstrates building such a harness using LangChain and LangGraph to transition from simple requests to stateful production applications. The implementation addresses critical system design challenges including error propagation, state persistence, and deterministic execution control.
takeaways: An agent harness is the execution layer responsible for managing the interaction between models, tools, and state.
Production agent platforms require capabilities like sessions, checkpoints, tracing, and human-in-the-loop approval.
LangChain provides interfaces for models, messages, and tools, while LangGraph offers explicit state transitions and execution control.
System design for agents involves deciding which state is run-specific versus persistent across conversations.
The harness must handle tool failures by deciding whether to retry, request human input, or stop execution.

sections.title: Your agent harness should repair itself
sections.summary: The section describes a self-repairing agent harness system using Hermes and Opik to learn from production failures without retraining model weights. It distinguishes between runtime learning, where successful procedures are saved as skills, and offline optimization using the GEPA algorithm for prompt and skill evolution. The workflow involves capturing execution traces, diagnosing root causes with the Ollie tool, and establishing regression tests to prevent recurring errors. By modifying external artifacts like instructions and configurations, the system converts production incidents into structured, reviewable inputs for continuous improvement.
takeaways: Agent systems can improve by modifying external artifacts like instructions, skills, and configurations instead of updating model weights.
Hermes preserves successful task procedures as editable SKILL.md files, which serve as procedural memory for future reuse.
The GEPA (Genetic-Pareto Prompt Evolution) method enables offline optimization of agent artifacts without requiring GPU fine-tuning.
Opik provides a tracing infrastructure that captures model spans and tool spans to pinpoint the exact step where a multi-step decision process failed.
Ollie acts as a diagnostic bridge that inspects project files and proposes code or configuration diffs based on trace data.
A robust repair loop requires human approval of proposed changes followed by verification through reruns and the creation of regression test cases.
Opik Test Suites use natural-language assertions and LLM judges to validate agent behavior against expected outcomes.

zh.summary: Agent harness 作為 execution layer，負責管理 models、tools 與 application state 之間的互動。本系列展示如何使用 LangChain 與 LangGraph 打造這樣的 harness，從簡單的 request 轉換為具備 state 的 production 應用程式。該實作解決了關鍵的 system design 挑戰，包括 error propagation、state persistence 與 deterministic execution control。此章節描述了一個使用 Hermes 與 Opik 的 self-repairing agent harness 系統，能在不重新訓練模型權重的情況下從 production failures 中學習。它區分了 runtime learning（將成功程序儲存為 skills）以及離線最佳化（利用 GEPA 演算法進行 prompt 與 skill 的演化）。其工作流程涵蓋擷取 execution traces、利用 Ollie 工具診斷 root causes，並建立 regression tests 以防止錯誤再次發生。透過修改 instructions 與 configurations 等外部 artifacts，系統將 production incidents 轉化為結構化且可審查的輸入，以實現持續改進。

sections.summary: Agent harness 作為 execution layer，負責管理 models、tools 與 application state 之間的互動。本系列展示如何使用 LangChain 與 LangGraph 打造這樣的 harness，從簡單的 request 轉換為具備 state 的 production 應用程式。該實作解決了關鍵的 system design 挑戰，包括 error propagation、state persistence 與 deterministic execution control。
takeaways: Agent harness 是負責管理 models、tools 與 state 之間互動的 execution layer。
Production agent 平台需要具備 sessions、checkpoints、tracing 以及 human-in-the-loop 審核等能力。
LangChain 提供 models、messages 與 tools 的介面，而 LangGraph 則提供明確的 state 轉移與 execution control。
Agent 的 system design 涉及決定哪些 state 僅屬於單次 run，哪些 state 則需要在跨對話中保持 persistent。
Harness 必須透過決定是否 retry、請求 human input 或是停止執行，來處理 tool failures。

sections.title: 你的 agent harness 應該具備自我修復能力
sections.summary: 本節介紹了一個 self-repairing agent harness 系統，使用 Hermes 與 Opik 從 production failures 中學習，而無需重新訓練 model weights。它區分了 runtime learning（將成功的程序儲存為 skills）以及使用 GEPA algorithm 進行 prompt 和 skill 進化的 offline optimization。其工作流程包括擷取 execution traces、使用 Ollie 工具診斷 root causes，並建立 regression tests 以防止錯誤再次發生。透過修改 instructions 和 configurations 等 external artifacts，該系統將 production incidents 轉化為結構化且可審查的輸入，以實現持續改進。
takeaways: Agent 系統可以透過修改 instructions、skills 和 configurations 等 external artifacts 來改進，而不需要更新 model weights。
Hermes 將成功的任務程序保存為可編輯的 SKILL.md 檔案，作為日後重複使用的 procedural memory。
GEPA (Genetic-Pareto Prompt Evolution) 方法能對 agent artifacts 進行 offline optimization，而不需要 GPU fine-tuning。
Opik 提供 tracing infrastructure，可擷取 model spans 與 tool spans，精準找出多步驟決策過程失敗的具體步驟。
Ollie 扮演診斷橋樑的角色，負責檢查專案檔案，並根據 trace data 提出程式碼或 configuration diffs。
一個穩健的 repair loop 需要對提議的變更進行 human approval，接著透過重新執行進行驗證，並建立 regression test cases。
Opik Test Suites 使用 natural-language assertions 和 LLM judges，根據預期結果驗證 agent 行為。

items.title: EP225: Why Does Git Revert Cause Conflicts?

sections.title: Why Does Git Revert Cause Conflicts?
sections.summary: The git revert command undoes changes from an earlier commit by generating a new commit rather than rewriting project history, making it safe for shared branches. However, revert conflicts arise when a subsequent commit modifies the exact same lines of code that the targeted commit introduced or changed. Because Git cannot automatically determine which version takes precedence, it pauses the operation for manual intervention. Once the conflict is resolved and staged, Git finalizes the new commit to undo the target changes while keeping subsequent updates intact.
takeaways: git revert creates a new commit that inverts earlier changes rather than rewriting history like git reset.
Reverting is safe for shared branches because it preserves an intact and traceable commit log.
A revert conflict occurs when a later commit modifies the same lines as the commit being reverted.
When a revert conflict occurs, Git pauses execution until conflicts are manually resolved and staged.
Resolving the conflict allows Git to complete the revert commit without discarding subsequent unaffected edits.

sections.title: 12 Claude Code Features Every Engineer Should Know

Core workflow features include project memory via CLAUDE.md files, pre-execution planning modes, and automatic checkpoint rollbacks. The system also supports modular extensibility and external connectivity using Skills, lifecycle Hooks, Plugins, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). To handle complex workflows and context limits, it provides conversation compaction and parallel execution via subagents.
takeaways: CLAUDE.md serves as a project memory file loaded at session start to enforce custom rules and conventions.
Plan Mode enforces a planning phase prior to code execution, allowing developer review before changes are applied.
Checkpoints take automatic project snapshots to facilitate reverting errors during execution.
Lifecycle hooks enable the execution of custom shell scripts around events such as PreToolUse and PostToolUse.
Plugins bundle third-party integrations comprising skills, MCP tools, and lifecycle hooks.

sections.title: Symmetric vs. Asymmetric Encryption
sections.summary: Symmetric and asymmetric encryption solve different cryptographic problems with distinct performance trade-offs. Symmetric encryption uses a single shared key for both encryption and decryption, making it fast, efficient, and well-suited for bulk data despite the challenge of secure key distribution. In contrast, asymmetric encryption relies on a public-private key pair to eliminate the upfront key-sharing requirement. However, because asymmetric encryption is computationally expensive and slow, it is primarily applied to identity, authentication, and key exchange rather than large payloads.
takeaways: Symmetric encryption uses a single shared key to both encrypt and decrypt data.
Symmetric encryption is fast and efficient, making it ideal for encrypting files, database records, and message payloads.
The main drawback of symmetric encryption is the difficulty of securely distributing the secret key between parties.
Asymmetric encryption uses a public key for encryption and a private key for decryption.
Asymmetric encryption avoids the upfront secret-sharing problem but is slower and computationally expensive.
Asymmetric encryption is primarily used for identity, authentication, and key exchange rather than large datasets.

sections.title: 7 Key Load Balancer Use Cases
sections.summary: Load balancers serve multiple essential functions in modern server infrastructure by distributing incoming traffic evenly across backend instances. They enhance performance and security by handling tasks like SSL termination and mitigating DDoS attacks through rate limiting. Furthermore, load balancers support system reliability and horizontal scalability by maintaining session persistence and actively monitoring server health to reroute traffic away from failing nodes.
takeaways: Load balancers evenly distribute traffic across server instances to optimize resource utilization.
SSL termination can be offloaded to load balancers to reduce workload on backend servers.
Session persistence is achieved by directing all requests from a single user to the same server instance.
System availability is maintained by monitoring instance health and rerouting traffic away from unhealthy servers.
Horizontal scaling is facilitated by load balancers accommodating new instances into the server pool.
DDoS attack impacts are mitigated via request rate limiting and wider surface traffic distribution.

sections.title: How can Cache Systems go wrong?
sections.summary: Caching systems can fail in four typical scenarios: thunder herd problem, cache penetration, cache breakdown, and cache crash. The thunder herd problem occurs when multiple keys expire simultaneously, overwhelming the database; it can be mitigated by jittering expiration times or prioritizing core traffic. Cache penetration involves requests for nonexistent keys in both cache and database, solvable via caching null values or applying Bloom filters. Cache breakdown happens when high-traffic hot keys expire, which can be avoided by making hot keys permanent, while cache crashes can be handled via circuit breakers or clustering.
takeaways: The thunder herd problem occurs when many cache keys expire concurrently, overloading the database with queries.
Thunder herd issues can be mitigated by adding random jitter to key expiry times or by rate-limiting non-core database queries.
Cache penetration occurs when requested keys exist neither in the cache nor the database, putting pressure on both systems.
Cache penetration can be resolved by caching null values for missing keys or using a Bloom filter to check existence before querying the database.
Cache breakdown happens when a hot key expires, and it can be prevented by omitting expiration times for keys serving large query volumes.
Cache crashes can be handled by implementing a circuit breaker to block access during outages or deploying a cache cluster to ensure high availability.

sections.title: 為什麼 Git Revert 會造成衝突？
sections.summary: git revert 指令透過產生一個新的 commit 來復原較早 commit 的變更，而不是重寫專案 history，這讓它在 shared branches 上使用時非常安全。然而，當後續的 commit 修改了目標 commit 所引入或變更的完全相同程式碼行時，就會產生 revert conflicts。因為 Git 無法自動判斷哪個版本具有優先權，因此會暫停操作以等待手動介入。一旦衝突解決並 staged 後，Git 會完成新的 commit 以復原目標變更，同時保持後續的更新完好無損。
takeaways: git revert 會建立一個反轉早期變更的新 commit，而不是像 git reset 那樣重寫 history。
Reverting 對 shared branches 是安全的，因為它保留了完整且可追溯的 commit log。
當較晚的 commit 修改了與正在被 revert 的 commit 相同的行時，就會發生 revert conflict。
當發生 revert conflict 時，Git 會暫停執行，直到衝突被手動解決並 staged。
解決衝突可讓 Git 完成 revert commit，而不會捨棄後續未受影響的修改。
