Momentum 透過利用過去 gradient 的 moving average 來 update parameters，從而解決震盪問題。
該技術加速了水平方向朝向 minima 的移動，同時減少了不必要的垂直步幅。
momentum rate 是一個必須經過調校的 hyperparameter，以避免 overshooting 或收斂過慢。
透過 PySpark MLlib 進行分散式訓練與 Bayesian Optimization 是文中提及用於訓練最佳化的替代方法。
過高的 momentum rate 可能會導致最佳化過程衝過（overshoot）loss function 的極小值點。

sections.title: 使用 GRPO 打造 Reasoning LLM
sections.summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) 是一種 reinforcement learning 方法，旨在無需標註資料的情況下增強 LLM 的 reasoning 與數學能力。此流程包含生成多個候選回應、透過 deterministic reward functions 進行評估，並使用特定的 GRPO loss function 更新模型。可利用 UnslothAI 與 HuggingFace TRL 等工具，在 Qwen3-4B 等 base models 上高效實現此 fine-tuning 流程。
takeaways: GRPO 透過使用 deterministic reward functions 為模型輸出評分，免除了對人工標註資料的需求。
該方法依賴 sampling engine 為每個 reasoning task 生成多個候選回應。
UnslothAI 用於高效的 fine-tuning，而 HuggingFace TRL 則提供 GRPOTrainer 與 GRPOConfig 組件。
此框架中的 reward functions 會依據精確格式、近似格式、答案正確性及數值來驗證回應。
採用 LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) 來 fine-tune 特定模組，而非整個模型的權重。
Open R1 Math 資料集是 reasoning fine-tuning 流程中所使用數學題目的主要來源。

items.title: Built for Reliability: How American Express Processes Payments at Scale

sections.title: Core Payments Ecosystem
sections.summary: American Express operates as the core payment network connecting acquiring banks to card issuers during transactions. In 2018, the company began modernizing its platform onto cloud-native infrastructure, shifting away from hardware engineered for continuous uptime to an environment where unexpected server failures are common. Traditional patterns like event-driven processing and monolithic designs were rejected due to strict low-latency requirements and scaling constraints. Instead, the engineering team adopted a design rooted in cell-based architecture to isolate failures and maintain real-time performance.
takeaways: American Express functions as the core payment network between an acquiring bank and a card issuer.
American Express began migrating its core payment platform to cloud-native infrastructure in 2018.
Cloud infrastructure required designing for frequent, uncontrollable server failures rather than relying on high-reliability hardware.
Event-driven architecture was rejected because core payment processing demands real-time responses with low latency.
Monolithic architecture was deemed a poor fit for the platform's scaling requirements.
The engineering team chose an approach based on cell-based architecture, building on patterns developed internally during the Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) era.

sections.title: Cell Boundaries
sections.summary: In a cell-based architecture, a cell is a complete and self-contained copy of an application stack designed to function as an independent failure domain. Each cell owns its required components—such as microservices, databases, and infrastructure—and avoids synchronous cross-cell dependencies along the critical execution path. Unlike microservices, which partition systems by functional domain, cells partition architectures by failure boundaries. Engineers at American Express structure these boundaries around specific real-time transaction journeys to isolate failures and maintain platform availability.
takeaways: A cell is a self-sufficient copy of a processing stack containing all microservices, databases, and infrastructure required to process a transaction locally within a region.
Cells form isolated failure domains that can be taken out of rotation for maintenance or incidents without disrupting the broader platform.
Synchronous cross-cell dependencies are strictly excluded from the critical transaction path, although reference data replication and observability aggregation can span cells.
Microservices divide systems functionally, whereas cells divide systems by failure boundaries; a single cell typically encapsulates multiple microservices.
American Express engineers recommend sizing cells around user journeys, isolating real-time processing requirements from after-the-fact processing workflows.

sections.title: Data Locality
sections.summary: American Express manages data locality within its cellular architecture by categorizing data as immutable, semi-static, or dynamic based on change frequency. Immutable and semi-static data are proactively pushed to all cells prior to transactions to prevent cold cache penalties and eliminate external synchronous calls. For dynamic data that updates per transaction, the architecture inverts the paradigm by moving transactions to the data using deterministic routing. Handled by the Global Transaction Router, routing decisions are derived from transaction attributes for consistency, while asynchronous replication runs in the background for failover.
takeaways: American Express divides data into three categories: immutable, semi-static (changing hours to yearly), and dynamic (changing per transaction).
For immutable and semi-static data, reference data is pushed and distributed to every cell beforehand rather than pulled via on-demand caching.
Pushing data ahead avoids cold-cache fall-through reads and keeps replication entirely outside the critical transaction path.
For dynamic data, the architecture avoids stale-state issues by routing the transaction to the data rather than replicating data to the transaction.
The Global Transaction Router handles deterministic routing based on payload attributes like partner, market, and payment type, alongside priority-based routing for other use cases.
Message-based replication between cells runs asynchronously in the background to ensure failover data availability without delaying in-flight transactions.

sections.title: Global Transaction Router
sections.summary: The Global Transaction Router routes traffic and enforces boundaries across cells in a distributed payment system, acting as the sole communication path between cells and external institutions. To prevent this critical component from becoming a failure point, American Express engineers excluded payment business logic, limiting the router to minimal message parsing for routing decisions. Resilience is further maintained by running instances nearly stateless with non-persistent storage, using asynchronous logging and configuration updates, and deploying parallel active instances across regions. This design demonstrates how essential structural chokepoints remain reliable through deliberate simplicity and minimal dependencies.
takeaways: Cells in the payments mesh lack direct communication capabilities and rely entirely on the Global Transaction Router for both inter-cell and external routing.
American Express engineers kept the router simple by excluding payment business logic, avoiding centralized data lookups.
Router instances maintain high availability by staying nearly stateless with state kept in non-persistent storage.
Asynchronous mechanisms for logging with buffer truncation and memory-based configuration loading prevent transactional bottlenecks.
An active-active deployment across multiple regions is favored over active-standby to enhance availability for stateless components.

sections.title: Credit Card Authorization Flow
sections.summary: The credit card authorization flow at American Express demonstrates a decoupled architecture managed by the Global Transaction Router. Upon receiving a transaction initiated from a merchant point-of-sale terminal, the router forwards the request to an internal processing cell using deterministic or priority-based routing. Within the cell, microservices handle data enrichment, transformation, validation, and issuer identification, but they never communicate directly outside their boundary. Instead, the transaction is returned to the router, which interfaces with card issuers and routes responses back to the context-holding cell before returning confirmation to the acquiring bank.
takeaways: A point-of-sale transaction first enters American Express systems through the Global Transaction Router.
The router directs transactions to internal processing cells using either deterministic or priority-based routing depending on the use case.
Microservices inside a cell handle validation, enrichment, transformation, and issuer determination.
Cells are strictly isolated and never communicate directly with external card issuers.
The Global Transaction Router contacts card issuers and uses deterministic routing to route the response back to the specific cell holding the transaction context.

sections.title: Mid-Transaction Failure
sections.summary: Payments processing at American Express utilizes an orchestrated microservices architecture to manage workflows and monitor service health. When a mid-transaction failure occurs, the orchestrator halts execution and returns the request to the Global Transaction Router to find a healthy cell. Crucially, the system discards any completed partial work and restarts the transaction from scratch in the new cell. This design choice prevents cross-cell shared state and synchronization issues, accepting the minor cost of redoing a sub-second transaction in exchange for loose coupling.
takeaways: American Express uses an orchestrator microservice to supervise payment workflows and detect failures in individual microservices.
When a failure occurs, the transaction is sent back to the Global Transaction Router to select a healthy cell.
Instead of resuming from partial progress, American Express discards incomplete work and restarts the transaction from the beginning.
Discarding partial progress avoids shared state between cells, eliminating cross-cell synchronization problems and consistency risks during failover.
Each cell maintains its own database clusters and runs independently without reliance on state from other cells.
Redoing work is viable because payment transactions complete in hundreds of milliseconds, making the structural isolation worth the minimal latency cost.

sections.title: Recovery Semantics
sections.summary: Transaction recovery semantics define a point of no return up to which transactions can be safely restarted or rerouted before reaching external systems like card issuers. American Express optimizes this by placing irreversible steps late in the payment flow to maximize the recoverable window, while relying on idempotency keys to suppress duplicate processing when late rerouting is impossible. When failed cells recover, platforms mitigate stale state writes through fast transaction completion, downstream idempotency duplicate suppression, and paced, percentage-based traffic shifting.
takeaways: Rerouting transactions is safe within the core ecosystem but unsafe once sent to external systems like card issuers.
American Express maximizes the recoverable window by placing the point of no return as late as possible in payment processing.
Transactions carry consistent unique identifiers that downstream systems use for idempotency and duplicate suppression.
Percentage-based canary shifting enables gradual cell draining, partial-load validation, and controlled failback during recovery.
Preventing recovered cells from writing stale state relies on transaction speed, idempotency identifiers, and paced recovery.

sections.title: Design Tradeoffs
sections.summary: American Express accepts key trade-offs in its cell-based architecture to preserve cell independence and protect data integrity. These trade-offs include duplicating services across cells to eliminate cross-cell network hops, along with dropping non-critical application logs via buffer truncation during high platform pressure. Observability experiences latency because telemetry is written locally first and aggregated asynchronously, and transactions with strong consistency requirements may be rejected if cross-cell data is not validated. Ultimately, partitioning the platform into independent units trades higher management complexity for a significantly reduced blast radius during failures.
takeaways: American Express duplicates service implementations across cells to eliminate cross-cell network hops and preserve cell independence.
A buffer truncation policy drops application observability logs during sustained pressure to ensure transaction processing continues.
Global dashboards experience visibility lag because metrics, logs, and traces are written locally within each cell before asynchronous aggregation.
Transactions requiring strong consistency may be rejected to protect data integrity if asynchronous cross-cell data synchronization cannot be validated.
Cell-based systems reduce the blast radius of failures rather than reducing overall failure frequency, trading complexity for limited failure impact.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: The American Express engineering team designed a resilient payment platform capable of surviving cell failures by ensuring transactions never depend on multiple cells simultaneously. This architecture separates data strategies by pushing static reference data to all cells while routing transactions directly to rapidly changing data. System dependability is anchored by a thin Global Transaction Router that avoids complex logic at critical chokepoints. Instead of resuming partial work across shared state, the platform discards partial transactions and restarts them, pushing the point of no return as late as possible to maximize failure survivability.
takeaways: Transactions are isolated to prevent a single transaction from depending on two cells simultaneously.
Infrequently changing reference data is distributed to all cells ahead of time, whereas volatile data remains local and transactions are routed to it.
The Global Transaction Router maintains dependability at the system chokepoint by minimizing its internal logic.
The platform chooses restarting over resuming failed transactions, eliminating shared state across cells at a latency cost of a few hundred milliseconds.
Positioning the point of no return late in the execution flow widens the window for survivable failures.

sections.title: Core Payments 生態系
sections.summary: American Express 在交易過程中扮演連接收單行與發卡機構的核心支付網路。2018 年，該公司開始將其平台現代化遷移至 cloud-native 基礎設施，從專為 continuous uptime 設計的硬體，轉向非預期伺服器故障很常見的環境。由於嚴苛的 low-latency 需求與擴展限制，傳統的 event-driven processing 與 monolithic 設計均被捨棄。相反地，工程團隊採用了植基於 cell-based architecture 的設計，以隔離故障並維持即時效能。
takeaways: American Express 扮演收單行與發卡機構之間的核心支付網路。
American Express 於 2018 年開始將其核心支付平台遷移至 cloud-native 基礎設施。
Cloud 基礎設施需要針對頻繁且不可控的伺服器故障進行設計，而非依賴高可靠性硬體。
Event-driven architecture 被捨棄，是因為核心支付處理需要 low latency 的即時回應。
Monolithic architecture 被認為無法滿足該平台的 scaling 需求。
工程團隊選擇了基於 cell-based architecture 的做法，建立在 Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) 時代內部開發的 pattern 之上。

sections.title: Cell 邊界 (Cell Boundaries)
sections.summary: 在 cell-based architecture 中，cell 是一個完整且獨立的 application stack 副本，設計用來作為獨立的 failure domain。每個 cell 都擁有其所需的組件——例如 microservices、databases 與 infrastructure——並避免在 critical execution path 上產生同步的 cross-cell dependencies。不同於依 functional domain 切分系統的 microservices，cell 是依 failure boundaries 來劃分架構。American Express 的工程師圍繞特定的即時 transaction journeys 來建構這些邊界，以隔離故障並維持平台的 availability。
takeaways: Cell 是一個能夠自給自足的 processing stack 副本，包含在單一 region 內本地處理 transaction 所需的所有 microservices、databases 和 infrastructure。
Cell 構成了隔離的 failure domains，可以在進行維護或發生 incident 時脫離輪替（taken out of rotation），而不會中斷更廣泛的平台運作。
同步的 cross-cell dependencies 被嚴格排除在 critical transaction path 之外，儘管 reference data replication 與 observability aggregation 可以跨越 cell。
Microservices 是按功能劃分系統，而 cell 則是按 failure boundaries 劃分系統；單一 cell 通常封裝了多個 microservices。
American Express 工程師建議圍繞 user journeys 來規劃 cell 的規模（sizing），將即時處理需求與事後處理的 workflows 隔離開來。

sections.title: Data Locality
sections.summary: American Express 在其 cellular architecture 中，依據變更頻率將資料分類為 immutable、semi-static 或 dynamic 來管理 data locality。Immutable 與 semi-static 資料會在 transaction 發生前主動 push 到所有 cell，以防止 cold cache penalty 並消除外部的同步呼叫。對於每筆 transaction 都會更新的 dynamic 資料，該架構反轉了此典範，使用 deterministic routing 將 transaction 導向資料所在之處。由 Global Transaction Router 處理，routing 決策是衍生自 transaction attributes 以確保一致性，同時 asynchronous replication 在背景運行以支援 failover。
takeaways: American Express 將資料分為三類：immutable、semi-static（變更頻率從數小時到數年不等）以及 dynamic（隨每筆 transaction 變更）。
對於 immutable 與 semi-static 資料，reference data 會事先被 push 並分發到每個 cell，而不是透過 on-demand caching 來 pull。
事先 push 資料可避免 cold-cache fall-through reads，並使 replication 完全位於 critical transaction path 之外。
對於 dynamic 資料，該架構透過將 transaction 路由至資料所在處，而非將資料複製到 transaction 處，從而避免 stale-state 問題。
Global Transaction Router 根據 partner、market 和 payment type 等 payload attributes 處理 deterministic routing，並針對其他 use cases 提供基於優先級的 routing（priority-based routing）。
Cell 之間的 message-based replication 在背景非同步運行，以確保 failover 的資料 availability，而不會延遲正在進行中的 transactions。

sections.title: Global Transaction Router
sections.summary: Global Transaction Router 在分散式支付系統中負責路由流量並強制執行跨 cell 的邊界，作為 cell 與外部機構之間唯一的通訊路徑。為了防止這個關鍵組件成為 failure point，American Express 的工程師排除了支付相關的 business logic，將 router 限制在僅進行最基本的 message parsing 以做出 routing 決策。透過使用 non-persistent storage 讓 instances 維持接近 stateless 的狀態、採用非同步 logging 與 configuration 更新，並在各 region 部署並行的 active instances，進一步確保了 resilience。這項設計展示了關鍵的架構瓶頸（structural chokepoints）如何透過刻意的簡潔性與最小化 dependencies 來維持可靠性。
takeaways: Payments mesh 中的 cell 缺乏直接通訊能力，完全依賴 Global Transaction Router 進行 inter-cell 及外部 routing。
American Express 的工程師透過排除支付 business logic、避免集中式 data lookups，使 router 保持精簡。
Router instances 透過保持近乎 stateless，並將 state 保留在 non-persistent storage 中，以維持 high availability。
具備 buffer truncation 的非同步 logging 機制與基於記憶體的 configuration loading，可防止 transaction 出現瓶頸。
跨多個 regions 的 active-active 部署比 active-standby 更受青睞，以提高 stateless 組件的 availability。

sections.title: Credit Card Authorization Flow
sections.summary: American Express 的信用卡 authorization 流程展示了由 Global Transaction Router 管理的解耦架構。在收到由商家 point-of-sale 終端發起的交易後，router 會使用 deterministic 或 priority-based routing 將 request 轉發至內部的 processing cell。在 cell 內部，microservices 負責處理 data enrichment、transformation、validation 與 issuer identification，但它們絕不會直接與其邊界外部通訊。相反地，交易會被送回 router，由其與 card issuers 對接，並在將 confirmation 回傳給 acquiring bank 之前，將 response 路由回持有 context 的 cell。
takeaways: point-of-sale 交易首先會透過 Global Transaction Router 進入 American Express 系統。
router 會依據 use case，使用 deterministic 或 priority-based routing 將交易導向內部的 processing cells。
cell 內部的 microservices 負責處理 validation、enrichment、transformation 以及 issuer determination。
Cells 之間保持嚴格隔離，且絕不直接與外部 card issuers 通訊。
Global Transaction Router 會與 card issuers 聯繫，並使用 deterministic routing 將 response 路由回持有該交易 context 的特定 cell。

sections.title: Mid-Transaction Failure
sections.summary: American Express 的支付處理採用 orchestrated microservices 架構來管理 workflows 並監控 service health。當發生 mid-transaction failure 時，orchestrator 會暫停執行並將 request 退回給 Global Transaction Router 以尋找健康的 cell。至關重要的是，系統會捨棄任何已完成的部分工作，並在新的 cell 中從頭重新開始交易。這種設計選擇避免了 cross-cell shared state 與 synchronization 問題，以重新執行 sub-second 交易的微小成本換取 loose coupling。
takeaways: American Express 使用 orchestrator microservice 來監控支付 workflows 並偵測個別 microservices 中的 failure。
當 failure 發生時，交易會被送回 Global Transaction Router 以選擇健康的 cell。
American Express 並非從部分進度中恢復，而是捨棄未完成的工作，並從頭重新開始交易。
捨棄部分進度可避免 cells 之間的 shared state，消除 failover 期間的 cross-cell synchronization 問題與 consistency 風險。
每個 cell 都維護自己的 database clusters，並獨立運作，不依賴來自其他 cells 的 state。
重新執行是可行的，因為支付交易在數百毫秒內即可完成，這使得結構性隔離所帶來的微小 latency 成本非常值得。

sections.title: Recovery Semantics
sections.summary: 交易的 recovery semantics 定義了一個 point of no return，在此之前，交易在送達 card issuers 等外部系統前都可以安全地重新啟動或重新路由。American Express 透過將不可逆的步驟延後至支付流程後期來最佳化這一點，以最大化 recoverable window，同時在無法進行 late rerouting 時依賴 idempotency keys 來抑制重複處理。當故障的 cells 恢復時，平台透過快速的 transaction completion、downstream idempotency 重複抑制，以及受控的 percentage-based traffic shifting 來緩解 stale state writes。
takeaways: 在核心生態系統內重新路由交易是安全的，但一旦發送到 card issuers 等外部系統後就不再安全。
American Express 透過將 point of no return 盡可能延後至支付處理的後期，來最大化 recoverable window。
交易帶有具一致性的 unique identifiers，downstream 系統會用其來實現 idempotency 與 duplicate suppression。
Percentage-based canary shifting 可以在復原期間實現漸進式 cell draining、partial-load validation 以及受控的 failback。
防止已復原的 cells 寫入 stale state，仰賴於交易速度、idempotency identifiers 以及受控步調的 recovery。

sections.title: Design Tradeoffs
sections.summary: American Express 在其 cell-based 架構中接受了關鍵的 trade-offs，以維持 cell 的獨立性並保護 data integrity。這些 trade-offs 包括跨 cells 複製 service 以消除 cross-cell network hops，以及在平台高負載期間透過 buffer truncation 捨棄非關鍵的 application logs。由於 telemetry 優先寫入本地端並以非同步方式聚合，observability 會出現 latency；此外，若 cross-cell 資料未經驗證，具有 strong consistency 需求的交易可能會被拒絕。歸根結底，將平台分割成獨立單元是以較高的管理複雜度換取 failure 時大幅縮小的 blast radius。
takeaways: American Express 跨 cells 複製 service implementations，以消除 cross-cell network hops 並維持 cell 的獨立性。
buffer truncation policy 會在持續高壓期間捨棄 application observability logs，以確保交易處理能持續進行。
全域 dashboard 會出現可見性延遲（visibility lag），因為 metrics、logs 和 traces 在非同步聚合之前，都是先寫入各個 cell 的本地端。
若無法驗證跨 cell 的非同步資料同步，需要強一致性（strong consistency）的 transaction 可能會被拒絕，以保護資料完整性。
Cell-based 系統是為了降低故障的 blast radius（爆炸半徑），而不是降低整體的故障頻率，這是以複雜度換取有限的故障影響範圍。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: American Express 工程團隊設計了一個具備韌性（resilient）的支付平台，透過確保交易絕不同時依賴多個 cell，使其能在 cell 故障時存活。此架構將資料策略拆分：將靜態 reference data 推送到所有 cell，同時將 transaction 直接導向快速變化的資料。系統的可靠性（dependability）由一個輕量級的 Global Transaction Router 作為支撐，避免在關鍵瓶頸點引入複雜邏輯。平台選擇捨棄局部 transaction 並重新開始，而非跨共享狀態恢復部分作業，並盡可能將 point of no return 推遲，以最大化故障容忍度（failure survivability）。
takeaways: Transactions 彼此隔離，以防止單一 transaction 同時依賴兩個 cell。
變更不頻繁的 reference data 會預先分發到所有 cell，而易變動的資料（volatile data）則保留在本地，並將 transaction 導向該處。
Global Transaction Router 透過將其內部邏輯最小化，來維持系統瓶頸點的可靠性（dependability）。
平台選擇重新啟動而非恢復失敗的 transaction，以數百毫秒的 latency 為代價，消除了跨 cell 的共享狀態。
將 point of no return 安排在執行流程的後期，能擴大系統承受故障的容許窗口。

sections.title: Free Observability Engineering Masterclass with Liz Fong-Jones & Honeycomb

takeaways: Traditional dashboards are often ineffective for debugging non-deterministic LLM agent failures because they are built around known failure modes.
Effective observability involves recording enough context per request to allow for post-hoc analysis on unplanned variables.
Liz Fong-Jones, co-author of the O'Reilly book Observability Engineering, is the instructor for the masterclass.
The masterclass includes practical training on using OpenTelemetry for system instrumentation.
Upcoming sessions focus on performance thresholds, cost management, and monitoring mobile apps and ML systems.
Honeycomb provides recordings and hands-on labs for all sessions in the series.

sections.title: LLM routing can cost more than not routing
sections.summary: LLM routing optimizes costs by directing tasks to the most efficient model, but traditional implementations often suffer from high overhead and cache invalidation. DigitalOcean's Inference Router addresses these challenges by moving routing logic into the infrastructure layer using specialized, small-parameter models for intent resolution. Key features include session pinning to preserve prefix caching and real-time model ranking based on latency and price. This approach allows agentic workflows, which consume significantly more tokens, to remain cost-effective without sacrificing performance.
takeaways: Naive routing can be more expensive than single-model usage due to classification costs and prefix cache invalidation.
Specialized small models like the 1.5B parameter Arch-Router can outperform frontier models in routing accuracy and speed.
Session pinning via the X-Model-Affinity header allows agent loops to reuse attention state caches across multiple turns.
The Inference Router uses real-time metrics from Prometheus and pricing APIs to dynamically rank model pools.
Agentic workflows are estimated by Gartner to use 5 to 30 times more tokens than standard chat interactions.
DigitalOcean provides pre-configured routers for specific workloads like software engineering and document intelligence.

sections.title: Hands-on guide to Red Teaming LLM apps
sections.summary: Red teaming has become a critical component of LLM development, with major labs like OpenAI, Meta, and Google investing heavily to identify vulnerabilities that standard accuracy metrics miss. While manual red teaming is resource-intensive, the open-source framework DeepTeam automates this process by simulating over 10 attack methods and detecting more than 40 types of vulnerabilities. The tool supports both single-turn and multi-turn conversational testing and generates detailed risk assessments without requiring pre-existing datasets. DeepTeam also integrates with platforms like Confident AI for comprehensive risk logging and dashboarding.
takeaways: OpenAI launched a $500,000 red-teaming challenge in August 2025 specifically for the gpt-oss-20b model.
Standard evaluation metrics like correctness and faithfulness fail to capture how easily a model can be exploited through prompt injections or jailbreaking.
DeepTeam is an open-source framework that enables end-to-end LLM red teaming with just a few lines of code.
The framework can detect vulnerabilities including PII leakage, bias, toxicity, and unauthorized access across 40+ categories.
DeepTeam differentiates between single-turn tests for immediate jailbreaks and multi-turn tests for conversational grooming.
Adversarial attacks in DeepTeam are dynamically simulated at runtime, removing the need for manual dataset creation.
Risk reports generated by DeepTeam can be logged and assessed via the Confident AI dashboard.

items.title: How to Deal With Errors and Failures in LLM-Powered Applications

sections.title: Meaning of Error Handling and Resiliency
sections.summary: Error handling is the mechanism within a program that decides how to respond to individual failures, such as by retrying requests, logging issues, or switching to backup options. In contrast, resiliency focuses on the entire system's capacity to maintain operation even when components fail. Resilient systems manage failures through controlled processes, also known as graceful degradation, rather than crashing entirely. Together, precise error handling and graceful degradation ensure applications remain functional and provide fallback value to users.
takeaways: Error handling determines the appropriate action to take when a specific operation fails, such as retrying, logging, or utilizing a backup.
Effective production error handling requires understanding and distinguishing between different causes and types of failures.
Resiliency is the ability of an overall system to continue functioning despite partial failures.
Graceful degradation allows an application to fail in a controlled manner and provide reduced functionality instead of completely crashing.
While error handling focuses on individual failures, resiliency addresses system-wide behavior during failures.

sections.title: Why do LLM Applications Need Special Treatment for Error Handling?
sections.summary: Unlike traditional deterministic software where successful execution indicates valid results, large language models produce probabilistic outputs that can logically fail despite a successful API status code. These failures include hallucinations, instruction omission, format mismatches, and incorrect tool selection. Failures are categorized into technical failures, which prevent completion of operations, and semantic failures, where operations technically succeed but produce incorrect or unusable results. As a result, robust LLM applications must incorporate error handling for both technical and semantic failure types.
takeaways: A technically successful LLM API call does not guarantee a valid, usable, or correct response due to the probabilistic nature of LLMs.
LLM response issues include hallucinations, schema mismatches like returning text instead of JSON, token limit truncation, false refusals, and invalid tool calls.
Errors in LLM applications are split into technical failures (e.g., timeouts, network errors) and semantic failures (logically flawed or unsafe outputs).
Traditional error handling addresses only technical failures, whereas LLM systems must handle both technical and semantic failures.

sections.title: How Does a Request Flow in an LLM-powered App?
sections.summary: LLM-powered applications are complex systems consisting of multiple interacting components beyond the core language model, including external databases and APIs. Across this pipeline, failures can arise at any integration boundary, from invalid user inputs and database search misses to model timeouts and streaming interruptions. To achieve genuine system resilience, engineering teams must evaluate and safeguard the complete end-to-end request flow rather than treating the LLM as an isolated component.
takeaways: LLM applications rely on multiple surrounding components, such as product databases and inventory APIs, to complete user requests.
Potential points of failure exist at every boundary in the system, not just within the language model.
Common failure modes include invalid user input, empty search results, LLM timeouts, hallucinated identifiers, and external service outages.
System failures can still occur late in the request lifecycle, such as interruptions during response streaming to the user.
Resilience requires treating the request path end-to-end rather than isolating the LLM.

sections.title: Main Types of Errors and Failures
sections.summary: This section introduces an examination of the primary errors and failures that can occur within the application. It serves as a transition into detailing specific failure modes and system risks. The focus is set on identifying and categorizing potential operational issues.
takeaways: The text introduces an inquiry into the primary types of errors and failures relevant to the application.
Categorizing failure modes is framed as the key next step in analyzing application behavior.
The focus is on identifying potential breakdown points inherent to such systems.

sections.title: Invalid User Input
sections.summary: Failures in LLM applications often occur prior to invoking the model itself due to invalid user inputs such as empty messages, unacceptable file formats, or oversized documents. Applications should perform deterministic input validation to catch missing mandatory fields or threshold violations before issuing model requests. Rejecting invalid requests early saves both processing time and operational costs. Furthermore, enforcing fixed validation rules allows the system to return clearer and more actionable error messages to users.
takeaways: Input failures such as empty prompts, invalid dates, and oversized files can be detected before calling an LLM.
Validating obvious requirements upfront eliminates unnecessary LLM calls.
Early rejection of invalid requests reduces processing latency and infrastructure costs.
Deterministic rule-based validation enables clearer, more consistent error messages for users.

sections.title: Network and Connection Failures
sections.summary: Applications communicating with LLM providers over the internet are subject to network connection interruptions, lost responses, and DNS lookup failures. Because these network issues are typically transient, applications can retry failed requests. However, retries should not be attempted indefinitely, and developers must assess whether repeating an operation is safe and free of unintended side effects.
takeaways: Network connections between applications and LLM providers are susceptible to interruptions and lost responses.
DNS lookup failures are an example of temporary failures that can occur during communication.
Retrying requests is a viable strategy for handling temporary network failures.
Applications must avoid indefinite retries to prevent unbounded execution loops.
Retrying operations requires careful consideration of safety and potential side effects.

sections.title: Timeouts
sections.summary: When a large language model takes longer to respond than an application can tolerate, requests can remain indefinitely stuck and consume resources unless a timeout is set. A timeout explicitly bounds the maximum duration an application will wait for a response. The optimal duration should be dictated by user experience needs and the nature of the task. Interactive interfaces demand short thresholds, whereas background processes can accommodate much longer limits.
takeaways: Lacking a timeout can cause application requests to hang indefinitely and consume system resources.
A timeout value specifies the upper bound of time an application will wait for an LLM response.
Appropriate timeout lengths depend on user experience requirements and execution context.
Interactive applications like chat typically require short timeouts such as 20 seconds.
Offline or background workloads, like document analysis, can tolerate timeouts of several minutes or longer.

sections.title: Rate Limits
sections.summary: LLM providers enforce limits on the volume of requests or tokens an account can consume within a given timeframe. When an application exceeds these thresholds, the provider responds with an HTTP status code 429 rate-limit error. Rather than indicating a broken service, this error reflects that request volume exceeds current provider capacity. Applications can mitigate rate limits by adding delays, reducing concurrency, utilizing queues, or switching to alternative models.
takeaways: LLM providers restrict the number of requests or tokens an account can use within a time period.
Exceeding rate limits triggers an HTTP status code 429 rate-limit error.
A rate limit indicates the application is sending more requests than provider capacity allows, not that the service is broken.
Recommended mitigations include delaying requests, reducing concurrency, queueing tasks, or switching to alternative models with available capacity.

sections.title: Provider and Server Failures
sections.summary: Temporary internal issues can cause LLM providers to become unavailable, typically signaled by HTTP 5xx status codes. While attempting a limited number of retries is reasonable because transient issues may resolve quickly, continuous retrying increases load on a struggling service. Therefore, applications should halt retries when failures persist and redirect requests to an alternative execution path.
takeaways: LLM provider outages caused by temporary internal issues commonly return HTTP 5xx status codes.
A limited number of retry attempts is appropriate for brief, transient provider failures.
Repeated retries exacerbate the issue by placing additional load on an already struggling service.
Applications should stop retrying and fail over to an alternative execution path if failures continue.

sections.title: Authentication and Permission Failures
sections.summary: Providing an expired or invalid API key to an LLM provider leads to HTTP 401 or 403 status codes. Retrying these requests automatically is not recommended because the failure cannot be resolved without updating credentials. Applications encountering these errors should log the incident, notify responsible parties, and provide a generic message to the end user. Throughout this handling process, systems must ensure that secret API keys and internal security metadata are not leaked.
takeaways: Expired or invalid API keys result in HTTP 401 or 403 responses from LLM providers.
Retrying requests after authentication or permission failures is futile and should be avoided.
Systems should log the error and notify appropriate teams when authentication failures occur.
User-facing error responses must never expose API keys or internal security details.

sections.title: Context-length Failures
sections.summary: Every language model operates under a context window limit that constrains the total amount of text processed in a single request, including prompts, history, retrieved documents, tool definitions, and expected responses. Exceeding this boundary can trigger request rejections or truncated completions. Resilient software designs counter this failure mode by monitoring token counts prior to sending requests. Practical remediation strategies include pruning conversation history, summarizing previous interactions, limiting retrieved retrieval-augmented generation documents, and decomposing tasks into smaller chunks.
takeaways: Every language model has an upper limit on the text it can process per request.
The context window encompasses the prompt, conversation history, retrieved documents, tool definitions, and the generated response.
Overloading the context window leads to request rejection or insufficient space for the model's answer.
Resilient applications track token consumption prior to dispatching requests.
Managing context pressure can be achieved by pruning history, summarizing earlier content, reducing retrieved documents, or chunking jobs.

sections.title: Malformed or Unexpected Output
sections.summary: Applications expecting machine-readable output often fail when language models return unstructured natural language explanations. Although human-readable, these responses break downstream processing designed for formats such as JSON. To mitigate this issue, systems should leverage structured output capabilities provided by model platforms. Furthermore, applications should systematically validate model outputs against an expected schema before downstream execution.
takeaways: Models may return conversational text when an application strictly expects structured data like JSON.
Unstructured responses cannot be processed by downstream application logic that relies on structured formats.
Developers should use built-in structured output features from model providers to constrain replies.
Applications should enforce schema validation on model responses prior to consumption.

sections.title: Incorrect or Invented Information
sections.summary: The most dangerous large language model failures occur when systems produce plausible yet completely incorrect answers due to model hallucination. Because these failures do not trigger technical exceptions, traditional error-handling mechanisms fail to detect them. Addressing these errors requires implementing additional verification checks, anchoring models to trusted data sources, or introducing human intervention.
takeaways: Plausible but completely false outputs constitute the most dangerous LLM failures.
Incorrect or invented outputs are driven by model hallucination.
Standard software exception handling cannot catch hallucinated outputs because no technical exception is thrown.
Mitigating hallucination requires extra verification checks, trusted data sources, or human intervention.

sections.title: Tool Failures and Partial Completion
sections.summary: LLMs are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents that perform external operations such as API calls, database queries, and financial transactions. A major operational challenge occurs when an action succeeds at the service level, but the enclosing workflow fails due to issues like lost network connections. Blindly retrying such unconfirmed operations risks adverse side effects, such as charging a customer twice. Consequently, robust tool-based systems require built-in idempotency, state tracking, and recovery mechanisms.
takeaways: LLM agents execute real-world actions including API calls, database searches, messaging, and financial transactions.
A tool execution can succeed remotely even if the client workflow fails before confirmation is received.
Blindly retrying actions without confirmation can result in duplicate executions, such as double charging a customer.
Tool-based agent architectures require idempotency, state tracking, and recovery mechanisms to prevent inconsistent state.

sections.title: How to Classify Failures to Take Appropriate Action
sections.summary: Handling errors in LLM-powered applications requires classifying failures into categories to determine the appropriate response. The three primary error types are transient, permanent, and semantic errors. Transient errors resolve with retries or fallbacks, permanent errors require system or request corrections, and semantic errors demand validation, automated repairs, or human review. Some errors, such as context-length limits, exhibit characteristics of multiple categories depending on how requests are modified.
takeaways: Transient errors are temporary (e.g., rate limits, network failures) and should be handled with retries after a short delay or fallbacks.
Permanent errors persist until request or system modifications are made (e.g., invalid credentials, malformed requests) and must be reported for correction.
Semantic errors occur when a response is technically valid but fails application constraints (e.g., hallucinations, invalid JSON), requiring validation, repair, or human intervention.
Errors do not always fit strictly into one category; for instance, context-length errors are prompt-dependent and can be resolved by prompt reduction.

sections.title: How To Retry a Request Correctly?
sections.summary: Retrying requests is a foundational method for improving application resiliency against transient failures like brief network issues or timeouts. To prevent worsening an outage or increasing infrastructure costs, systems should limit the total number of attempts and employ exponential backoff. Adding jitter introduces randomized delay intervals to prevent synchronized retry spikes from overwhelming services. Retries are recommended for transient errors like 429 and certain 5xx responses, but should be avoided for deterministic client errors like invalid credentials or bad input.
takeaways: Retrying failed requests improves application resiliency against transient issues like network disruptions.
Infinite retry loops must be avoided as they escalate costs and exacerbate outages.
Exponential backoff increases the delay exponentially between consecutive retry attempts.
Jitter adds random time variations to delays to avoid synchronized request bursts and traffic spikes.
Retries should target transient failures like timeouts, network issues, 429 status codes, and select 5xx status codes.
Retries should not be used for deterministic failures such as invalid credentials, bad input, or prohibited requests.

sections.title: How to Manage Fallbacks and Graceful Degradation?
sections.summary: Fallback mechanisms provide alternative execution paths when a primary model or system fails in an application. A typical graceful degradation hierarchy progresses from a primary high-quality model to a smaller backup model, pre-defined or cached responses, and human escalation. The fallback choice must be tailored to task requirements to ensure essential operational constraints are not violated. In addition, systems must avoid a single point of failure by ensuring primary and backup pathways do not rely on the same provider.
takeaways: A common degradation hierarchy transitions from a primary model to a smaller backup model, cached/pre-defined responses, and finally human intervention.

Fallback approaches must strictly align with the operational requirements of the specific task (e.g., acceptable for meeting summaries or FAQs, but not for complex legal documents or real-time account balances).
To ensure genuine redundancy, primary and backup models must not rely on the same provider to avoid a single point of failure.

sections.title: How Do Circuit Breakers Work in this Setup?
sections.summary: A circuit breaker prevents redundant requests and wasted resources when a service such as an LLM provider is unavailable. It operates across three states: closed, open, and half-open. In the closed state, traffic proceeds normally, whereas in the open state, requests are immediately blocked or redirected. The half-open state sends trial requests to test for system recovery, returning to closed on success or open on failure to isolate errors and support fallbacks.
takeaways: Continuing to query an unavailable LLM provider leads to wasted resources and poor user experience.
A circuit breaker temporarily halts calls to a failing service using closed, open, and half-open states.
The closed state permits requests to proceed at normal cadence.
The open state immediately rejects or redirects requests because the target service is considered unhealthy.
The half-open state permits a limited number of test requests to evaluate service recovery.
Successful trial requests in the half-open state reset the circuit to closed, while failures return it to open.
Circuit breakers prevent repeated failures from cascading across the application and allow fallback configurations.

sections.title: Rate Limiting, Queues, and Concurrency Control
sections.summary: LLM-powered applications must actively manage incoming traffic rather than passing all user submissions directly to model providers. Unchecked request volume risks overwhelming downstream provider rate limits, database connections, memory, and infrastructure budgets. Implementing rate limiting, concurrency control, and queues allows systems to throttle submission rates, cap simultaneously processed jobs, and buffer overflow tasks. Furthermore, applications should prioritize interactive user tasks over background workloads while enforcing strict boundaries on tokens, tool calls, and execution runtimes.
takeaways: Forwarding large request spikes directly to LLM providers can exhaust provider limits, memory, database connections, and application budgets.
Rate limiting controls how frequently a user or client can submit incoming requests.
Concurrency control caps the total number of requests an application can process simultaneously.
Queues buffer excess work until sufficient processing capacity becomes available.
Interactive requests requiring immediate user feedback should be prioritized over background batch tasks.
Applications should establish strict constraints on token usage, document size, retrieved passages, tool calls, and workflow durations.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: LLM-powered applications experience failure modes distinct from traditional software due to the probabilistic nature of large language models. Addressing these issues effectively requires classifying failure types so that applications can execute appropriate remediation. Despite novel challenges, conventional software resilience techniques remain directly applicable to LLM systems. Strategies such as retries, fallbacks, circuit breakers, rate limiting, and queuing provide essential error handling.
takeaways: LLM-powered applications exhibit failure modes different from traditional software due to their probabilistic nature.
Proper failure classification is critical for applications to take targeted corrective actions.
Resiliency in LLM applications relies heavily on traditional error-handling and stability patterns.
Effective mitigation techniques include retries, fallbacks, circuit breakers, rate limiting, and queuing.

items.summary: Error handling is the mechanism within a program that decides how to respond to individual failures, such as by retrying requests, logging issues, or switching to backup options. In contrast, resiliency focuses on the entire system's capacity to maintain operation even when components fail. Resilient systems manage failures through controlled processes, also known as graceful degradation, rather than crashing entirely. Together, precise error handling and graceful degradation ensure applications remain functional and provide fallback value to users. Unlike traditional deterministic software where successful execution indicates valid results, large language models produce probabilistic outputs that can logically fail despite a successful API status code. These failures include hallucinations, instruction omission, format mismatches, and incorrect tool selection. Failures are categorized into technical failures, which prevent completion of operations, and semantic failures, where operations technically succeed but produce incorrect or unusable results. As a result, robust LLM applications must incorporate error handling for both technical and semantic failure types. LLM-powered applications are complex systems consisting of multiple interacting components beyond the core language model, including external databases and APIs. Across this pipeline, failures can arise at any integration boundary, from invalid user inputs and database search misses to model timeouts and streaming interruptions. To achieve genuine system resilience, engineering teams must evaluate and safeguard the complete end-to-end request flow rather than treating the LLM as an isolated component.

zh.summary: Error handling 是程式內部決定如何回應個別 failure 的機制，例如重試 request、記錄問題（logging）或切換到備援選項。相反地，resiliency 著重於整個系統即使在組件故障時仍能維持運作的能力。具備韌性的系統會透過受控的流程來處理 failure，也就是所謂的 graceful degradation（優雅降級），而非直接全面崩潰。精準的 error handling 與 graceful degradation 相輔相成，確保 application 能維持運作並向使用者提供 fallback 價值。與傳統「成功執行即代表結果有效」的確定性（deterministic）軟體不同，LLM 產生的是機率性輸出，即便 API status code 顯示成功，邏輯上也可能出錯。這些 failure 包括 hallucination（幻覺）、遺漏指令、格式不合以及工具選擇錯誤（incorrect tool selection）。Failure 主要分為阻止操作完成的 technical failure，以及操作技術上成功但產生錯誤或無法使用之結果的 semantic failure。因此，穩健的 LLM application 必須同時納入針對 technical 和 semantic failure 類型的 error handling。以 LLM 驅動的 application 是複雜的系統，除了核心 language model 外，還包含多個互相協同運作的組件，如外部資料庫和 API。在整個 pipeline 中，任何整合邊界都可能發生 failure，從無效的 user input、資料庫搜尋未命中（search misses），到模型 timeout 與 streaming 中斷。為了實現真正的系統韌性，工程團隊必須評估並防護完整的 end-to-end request flow，而不是僅將 LLM 視為一個孤立的組件。

sections.title: Error Handling 與 Resiliency 的意涵
sections.summary: Error handling 是程式內部決定如何回應個別 failure 的機制，例如重試 request、記錄問題（logging）或切換到備援選項。相反地，resiliency 著重於整個系統即使在組件故障時仍能維持運作的能力。具備韌性的系統會透過受控的流程來處理 failure，也就是所謂的 graceful degradation（優雅降級），而非直接全面崩潰。精準的 error handling 與 graceful degradation 相輔相成，確保 application 能維持運作並向使用者提供 fallback 價值。
takeaways: Error handling 決定了當特定操作失敗時應採取的適當行動，例如重試、記錄 log 或使用備援方案。
在 production 環境中實現有效的 error handling，需要理解並區分不同 failure 的成因與類型。
Resiliency 是整體系統在發生局部 failure 時仍能繼續運作的能力。
Graceful degradation 允許 application 以受控的方式發生故障，並提供降級功能，而不是直接全面崩潰。
雖然 error handling 聚焦於個別 failure，但 resiliency 著重的是系統在 failure 期間的整體行為。

sections.title: 為什麼 LLM 應用程式的 Error Handling 需要特殊處理？
sections.summary: 不同於傳統確定性（deterministic）軟體中只要執行成功就代表結果有效，LLM 產生的機率性輸出即使 API status code 回傳成功，在邏輯上也可能出錯。這些 failure 包括 hallucination、遺漏 instruction、格式不符以及錯誤的 tool selection。Failure 主要分為兩類：阻礙操作完成的 technical failure，以及操作在技術層面成功但產出錯誤或不可用結果的 semantic failure。因此，穩健的 LLM 應用程式必須針對 technical 與 semantic 兩種 failure 類型都導入 error handling。
takeaways: 由於 LLM 的機率性本質，技術上成功的 LLM API call 並不能保證回傳有效、可用或正確的 response。
LLM 的 response 問題包括 hallucination、schema 不符（例如回傳純文字而非 JSON）、token limit 截斷、錯誤拒絕（false refusal）以及無效的 tool call。
LLM 應用程式中的 error 可分為 technical failure（例如 timeout、網路錯誤）與 semantic failure（邏輯缺陷或不安全的輸出）。
傳統的 error handling 僅處理 technical failure，而 LLM 系統則必須同時處理 technical 與 semantic failure。

sections.title: Request 在 LLM-powered 應用程式中是如何流轉的？
sections.summary: LLM-powered 應用程式是複雜的系統，除了核心語言模型外，還包含多個互相協作的元件，例如外部資料庫與 API。在整個 pipeline 中，任何整合邊界都可能發生 failure，從無效的 user input、資料庫搜尋未命中，到模型 timeout 與 streaming 中斷。為了實現真正的系統 resilience，工程團隊必須評估並防護完整的端到端（end-to-end）request flow，而不是將 LLM 視為孤立的元件。
takeaways: LLM 應用程式仰賴多個周邊元件（例如產品資料庫與庫存 API）來完成 user request。
系統中的每個邊界都存在潛在的 failure point，而非僅限於語言模型內部。
常見的 failure mode 包括無效的 user input、搜尋結果為空、LLM timeout、產生幻覺的識別碼（hallucinated identifier）以及外部服務中斷。
在 request lifecycle 的後期仍可能發生系統 failure，例如向使用者進行 response streaming 時發生中斷。
Resilience 需要以 end-to-end 的視角來處理整個 request path，而非將 LLM 孤立看待。

sections.title: Error 與 Failure 的主要類型
sections.summary: 本節將探討應用程式中可能出現的主要 error 與 failure，作為深入說明特定 failure mode 與系統風險的過渡段落，重點在於識別並分類潛在的維運問題。
takeaways: 本文探討了與該應用程式相關的主要 error 與 failure 類型。
將 failure mode 進行分類，被視為分析應用程式行為的關鍵下一步。
重點在於識別此類系統固有的潛在故障點（breakdown point）。

sections.title: 無效的 User Input
sections.summary: LLM 應用程式中的 failure 往往在呼叫模型之前就已發生，原因出在無效的 user input，例如空白訊息、不支援的檔案格式或過大的文件。應用程式應執行 deterministic input validation，在發送模型 request 之前攔截缺少的必填欄位或超出閾值的情況。提早拒絕無效 request 不僅能節省處理時間，還能降低營運成本。此外，實施固定的驗證規則有助於系統向使用者回傳更清楚、更具可行性的 error message。
takeaways: 諸如空白 prompt、無效日期以及過大檔案等 input failure，都可以在呼叫 LLM 之前被偵測出來。
預先驗證明確的基本要求，可避免不必要的 LLM call。
及早拒絕無效的 request 可降低處理 latency 與基礎架構成本。
基於確定性規則的驗證（deterministic rule-based validation）能為使用者提供更清楚、更一致的 error message。

sections.title: 網路與連線失敗
sections.summary: 透過網際網路與 LLM provider 通訊的應用程式，可能會遇到網路連線中斷、response 遺失以及 DNS lookup 失敗等問題。由於這些網路問題通常是暫態的（transient），應用程式可以 retry 失敗的 request。然而，不應無限制地嘗試 retry，且開發者必須評估重複執行某項操作是否安全且不會產生非預期的 side effects。
takeaways: 應用程式與 LLM provider 之間的網路連線容易受到中斷和 response 遺失的影響。
DNS lookup 失敗是通訊期間可能發生的暫時性故障範例之一。
Retry request 是處理暫時性網路故障的可行策略。
應用程式必須避免無限制地 retry，以防止無窮的執行迴圈。
Retry 操作時需要仔細考量安全性與潛在的 side effects。

sections.title: Timeout
sections.summary: 當大型語言模型回應的時間超過應用程式所能容忍的範圍時，除非設定了 timeout，否則 request 可能會無限期卡住並消耗資源。Timeout 明確限制了應用程式等待 response 的最長時間。最佳時間長度應由使用者體驗需求及任務本質決定。互動式介面需要較短的 threshold，而背景處理程序則可以接受長得多的限制。
takeaways: 缺乏 timeout 可能會導致應用程式的 request 無限期停滯並消耗系統資源。
Timeout 數值明確規範了應用程式等待 LLM response 的時間上限。
合適的 timeout 長短取決於使用者體驗需求與執行 context。
像 chat 這類互動式應用程式通常需要較短的 timeout，例如 20 秒。
像文件分析這類離線或背景的 workload，則可以容忍數分鐘甚至更長的 timeout。

sections.title: Rate Limit
sections.summary: LLM provider 會針對帳號在特定時間範圍內可消耗的 request 數量或 token 數設定上限。當應用程式超過這些 threshold 時，provider 會回傳 HTTP status code 429 的 rate-limit 錯誤。這項錯誤並非代表服務故障，而是反映出 request 量超過了 provider 當前的負載容量。應用程式可以透過增加 delay、降低 concurrency、使用 queue，或切換至替代模型來緩解 rate limit。
takeaways: LLM provider 會限制帳號在特定時段內可使用的 request 數或 token 數。
超出 rate limit 會觸發 HTTP status code 429 rate-limit 錯誤。
Rate limit 表示應用程式發送的 request 量超出了 provider 的處理容量，而非服務故障。
建議的緩解措施包括 delay request、降低 concurrency、將任務放入 queue，或是切換至尚有可用容量的替代模型。

sections.title: Provider 與伺服器故障
sections.summary: 暫時性的內部問題可能導致 LLM provider 無法提供服務，這通常會以 HTTP 5xx status code 來表示。雖然因為暫時性問題可能很快解決而嘗試有限次數的 retry 是合理的，但持續不斷 retry 會增加該負載過重服務的負擔。因此，當失敗持續發生時，應用程式應停止 retry，並將 request 重導向至替代的 execution path。
takeaways: 由暫時性內部問題引起的 LLM provider 服務中斷通常會回傳 HTTP 5xx status code。
針對短暫且瞬態的 provider 故障，嘗試有限次數的 retry 是適當的做法。
重複 retry 會對已在苦撐的服務造成額外負載，進而使問題惡化。
若持續發生失敗，應用程式應停止重試並 fail over 至備用執行路徑。

sections.title: 身分驗證與權限失敗
sections.summary: 提供過期或無效的 API key 給 LLM provider 會導致 HTTP 401 或 403 狀態碼。由於不更新憑證就無法解決此失敗，因此不建議自動重試這些 request。遇到這些錯誤的應用程式應記錄此 incident、通知相關負責人員，並向終端使用者提供一般通用訊息。在整個處理過程中，系統必須確保機密的 API key 與內部安全 metadata 不會外洩。
takeaways: 過期或無效的 API key 會導致 LLM provider 回傳 HTTP 401 或 403 response。
在身分驗證或權限失敗後重試 request 是徒勞無功的，應該予以避免。
發生身分驗證失敗時，系統應記錄錯誤並通知相關團隊。
面向使用者的錯誤 response 絕不能洩漏 API key 或內部安全細節。

sections.title: Context-length 失敗
sections.summary: 每個 language model 都在 context window 的限制下運作，該限制約束了單一 request 中處理的文字總量，包括 prompt、對話歷史紀錄、檢索到的文件、tool definitions 以及預期的 response。超出此邊界可能會觸發 request rejection 或被截斷的 completion。具韌性的軟體設計會在發送 request 之前監控 token 數量，以應對這種 failure mode。實用的緩解策略包括修剪對話歷史紀錄、總結先前的互動、限制檢索到的 retrieval-augmented generation 文件數量，以及將任務拆解為更小的 chunk。
takeaways: 每個 language model 每次 request 能處理的文字量都有其上限。
Context window 涵蓋了 prompt、對話歷史紀錄、檢索到的文件、tool definitions 以及生成的 response。
Context window 超載會導致 request 被拒絕，或是沒有足夠空間容納模型的回答。
具韌性的應用程式會在 dispatch request 之前追蹤 token 消耗量。
管理 context pressure 可以透過修剪歷史紀錄、總結先前內容、減少檢索文件或將工作 chunking 來達成。

sections.title: 格式錯誤或非預期的輸出
sections.summary: 當 language model 回傳非結構化的自然語言解釋時，預期機器可讀輸出的應用程式往往會失敗。儘管人類可讀，這些 response 卻會破壞專為 JSON 等格式設計的下游處理流程。為緩解此問題，系統應利用模型平台提供的 structured output 功能。此外，應用程式在進行下游執行前，應系統化地依據預期的 schema 驗證模型輸出。
takeaways: 當應用程式嚴格預期像 JSON 這樣的結構化資料時，模型可能會回傳對話式文字。
非結構化的 response 無法被依賴結構化格式的下游應用程式邏輯處理。
開發人員應使用 model provider 內建的 structured output 功能來約束回覆。
應用程式在採用模型 response 之前，應強制執行 schema validation。

sections.title: 不正確或捏造的資訊
sections.summary: 最危險的 large language model 失敗，發生在系統因模型 hallucination 而產生看似合理卻完全不正確的答案。由於這些失敗不會觸發技術上的 exception，傳統的錯誤處理機制無法偵測到它們。解決這些錯誤需要實作額外的驗證檢查、將模型錨定至可信的資料來源，或引入人工介入。
takeaways: 看似合理卻完全虛假的輸出構成了最危險的 LLM failure。
不正確或捏造的輸出是由模型 hallucination 所致。
標準的軟體 exception handling 無法捕捉 hallucination 產生的輸出，因為系統並未拋出任何技術上的 exception。
緩解 hallucination 需要額外的 verification check、可信賴的資料來源或人工介入。

sections.title: Tool 失敗與 Partial Completion
sections.summary: LLM 越來越常被部署為 autonomous agent，以執行 API call、database query 和金融交易等外部操作。當某個 action 在 service 層級成功執行，但包覆它的 workflow 卻因網路連線中斷等問題而失敗時，就會產生重大的維運挑戰。盲目 retry 這類未確認的操作會有產生負面 side effect 的風險，例如對客戶重複扣款。因此，穩健的 tool-based 系統需要內建 idempotency、state tracking 和 recovery 機制。
takeaways: LLM agent 執行現實世界中的 action，包括 API call、database 搜尋、發送訊息以及金融交易。
即使 client 端的 workflow 在收到確認前就失敗，遠端的 tool 執行仍可能已經成功。
在未經確認的情況下盲目 retry action，可能導致重複執行，例如對客戶重複扣款。
Tool-based 的 agent 架構需要具備 idempotency、state tracking 與 recovery 機制，以防止 state 不一致。

sections.title: 如何對 Failure 進行分類以採取適當行動
sections.summary: 在 LLM-powered 應用程式中處理 error 時，需要先將 failure 分門別類，以決定最適當的應對方式。三種主要的 error 類型為 transient error、permanent error 與 semantic error。Transient error 可透過 retry 或 fallback 解決；permanent error 需要修改系統或修正 request；semantic error 則需要 validation、自動修復或人工審查。某些 error（例如 context-length 限制）會根據 request 的修改方式而展現出多種類別的特性。
takeaways: Transient error 屬於暫時性問題（例如 rate limit、網路連線失敗），應在短暫延遲後透過 retry 或 fallback 來處理。
Permanent error 會持續存在，直到修改 request 或系統設定為止（例如 invalid credentials、格式錯誤的 request），且必須回報以進行修正。
Semantic error 發生在 response 在技術層面上有效、卻未符合應用程式限制條件的情況（例如 hallucination、無效的 JSON），需要進行 validation、修復或人工介入。
Error 並不總是嚴格歸屬於單一類別；例如，context-length error 取決於 prompt，可透過縮減 prompt 來解決。

sections.title: 如何正確地 Retry 一個 Request？
sections.summary: Retry request 是提高應用程式 resiliency 的基礎方法，可應對短暫的網路問題或 timeout 等 transient failure。為了避免加劇 outage 或增加 infrastructure 成本，系統應限制總嘗試次數並採用 exponential backoff。加入 jitter 可以引入隨機的延遲間隔，防止同步的 retry spike 壓垮服務。建議針對 429 和特定的 5xx response 等 transient error 進行 retry，但應避免針對 invalid credentials 或 bad input 等 deterministic 的 client error 進行 retry。
takeaways: Retry 失敗的 request 能提高應用程式面對網路中斷等 transient issue 的 resiliency。
必須避免無窮 retry loop，因為這會導致成本飆升並加劇 outage。
Exponential backoff 會在連續的 retry 嘗試之間以指數方式增加延遲時間。
Jitter 會在延遲中加入隨機的時間變化，以避免同步的 request burst 與 traffic spike。
Retry 應針對 timeout、網路問題、429 status code 以及特定的 5xx status code 等 transient failure。
Retry 不應用於 invalid credentials、bad input 或被禁止的 request 等 deterministic failure。

sections.title: 如何管理 Fallback 與 Graceful Degradation？
sections.summary: 當應用程式中的主要 model 或系統發生 failure 時，fallback 機制能提供替代的執行路徑。典型的 graceful degradation 層級通常是從主要的 high-quality model，逐步降級至較小的 backup model、預先定義或 cached response，最後則是 human escalation。Fallback 的選擇必須依據任務需求量身打造，以確保不違反關鍵的維運限制。此外，系統必須確保主要路徑與備用路徑不依賴同一個 provider，以避免 single point of failure。
takeaways: 常見的 degradation 層級是從主要 model 轉移到較小的 backup model、cached／預先定義的 response，最後則是人工介入。
Fallback 方案必須嚴格符合特定任務的維運需求（例如：適用於會議摘要或 FAQ，但不適用於複雜的法律文件或即時帳戶餘額）。
為了確保真正的 redundancy（備援性），主要與備用模型絕不能依賴相同的 provider，以避免 single point of failure（單點故障）。

sections.title: 在這種架構下，Circuit Breaker 是如何運作的？
sections.summary: 當 LLM provider 等服務不可用時，circuit breaker 可以防止多餘的請求並避免資源浪費。它在三種狀態之間運作：closed、open 和 half-open。在 closed 狀態下，流量正常通行；而在 open 狀態下，請求會立即被阻擋或重新導向。half-open 狀態則會發送測試請求以檢驗系統是否復原，成功時切回 closed，失敗時則重回 open，以隔離錯誤並支援 fallback 機制。
takeaways: 持續向不可用的 LLM provider 發送查詢會導致資源浪費並帶來不佳的使用者體驗。
Circuit breaker 透過 closed、open 與 half-open 三種狀態，暫時中止對故障服務的呼叫。
Closed 狀態允許請求以正常的步調繼續執行。
Open 狀態會立即拒絕或重新導向請求，因為目標服務被視為 unhealthy。
Half-open 狀態允許發送有限數量的測試請求，以評估服務是否已復原。
在 half-open 狀態下，若測試請求成功，會將 circuit 重設為 closed；若失敗，則會將其切回 open。
Circuit breaker 能防止重複的失敗在整個應用程式中產生連鎖效應（cascading failures），並支援 fallback 設定。

sections.title: Rate Limiting、Queue 與 Concurrency Control
sections.summary: LLM-powered 應用程式必須主動管理連入流量（incoming traffic），而不是將所有使用者提交的內容直接轉發給模型 provider。未受控的請求量可能會超出下游 provider 的 rate limit、耗盡 database connection、記憶體以及基礎設施預算。實作 rate limiting、concurrency control 與 queue，可讓系統調節請求提交速率、限制同時處理的工作數量，並緩衝溢出的任務。此外，應用程式應優先處理互動式的使用者任務，而非背景工作負載，同時對 token、tool call 以及執行時間（runtime）施加嚴格的限制。
takeaways: 將大量突增的請求（request spikes）直接轉發給 LLM provider，可能會耗盡 provider 配額上限、記憶體、database connection 與應用程式預算。
Rate limiting 控制使用者或 client 端提交連入請求的頻率。
Concurrency control 限制了應用程式能同時處理的請求總數上限。
Queue 會緩衝過量的任務，直到有足夠的處理能力可用為止。
需要即時使用者反饋的互動式請求，優先權應高於背景 batch 任務。
應用程式應對 token 使用量、文件大小、retrieved passages、tool call 以及 workflow 執行時長設定嚴格的限制。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: 由於大型語言模型（LLM）具備機率本質（probabilistic nature），LLM-powered 應用程式面臨的 failure mode 與傳統軟體截然不同。要有效解決這些問題，必須對 failure 類型進行分類，以便應用程式能執行適當的補救措施。儘管面臨全新挑戰，傳統軟體的 resilience（韌性）技術依然能直接套用於 LLM 系統。諸如 retry、fallback、circuit breaker、rate limiting 與 queuing 等策略，皆提供了不可或缺的錯誤處理機制。
takeaways: 由於其機率本質，LLM-powered 應用程式展現出與傳統軟體不同的 failure mode。
正確的 failure 分類對於應用程式採取針對性的修正措施至關重要。
LLM 應用程式的 resilience 高度仰賴傳統的錯誤處理與穩定性 pattern。
有效的緩解技術包括 retry、fallback、circuit breaker、rate limiting 以及 queuing。

items.title: KV Cache Engineering for LLM Serving

sections.title: KV cache engineering for LLM serving
sections.summary: KV cache engineering is critical for managing GPU memory during LLM inference because the cache grows dynamically with sequence length. The article outlines twelve techniques categorized by whether they reduce heads, layers, tokens, dimensions, or bits. Architectural methods like GQA and MLA modify the model structure, while serving-level optimizations like paging and Quest improve memory handling and read efficiency. These techniques involve trade-offs between memory savings, computational speed, and model accuracy.
takeaways: Llama 3.1 70B requires approximately 40 GB of BF16 KV cache for a single 128K-token sequence.
GQA and MQA reduce memory usage by sharing key-value heads across multiple query heads within a layer.
Cross-layer attention (CLA) can achieve a 2x reduction in KV cache by sharing cached data between adjacent transformer layers.
Sliding-window attention fixes the cache size for local layers by only retaining the most recent tokens.
Multi-head latent attention (MLA), introduced by DeepSeek-V2, compresses the KV cache into a latent representation to increase throughput.
Hybrid models like Jamba and Qwen3-Next interleave attention layers with recurrent layers to maintain fixed-size states.
Quest optimizes inference speed by reading only the most relevant pages of the cache based on query scores without deleting entries.

items.title: EP224: MCP vs RAG vs AI Agents

sections.title: MCP vs RAG vs AI Agents
sections.summary: The text contrasts Model Context Protocol (MCP), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and AI agents. MCP provides an open standard protocol that connects AI models to external tools, databases, and third-party applications without requiring custom point-to-point integrations. RAG enables models to pull fresh, relevant data from documents and databases at query time to mitigate hallucinations and deliver up-to-date responses. In contrast to standard request-response chatbots, AI agents operate autonomously to execute tasks and make operational decisions.
takeaways: MCP is an open standard protocol designed to connect AI models with external tools, APIs, and data sources.
MCP eliminates the need to build individual custom integrations for each external application, such as Gmail, Slack, or GitHub.
RAG retrieves fresh information from external sources like documents, PDFs, and databases during query execution to reduce hallucinations.
AI agents function autonomously and make decisions to complete tasks, distinguishing them from traditional request-response chatbots.

sections.title: 9 Distributed Systems Patterns You Should Know
sections.summary: Distributed systems utilize specialized architectural patterns to ensure scalability, fault tolerance, and data consistency. Data distribution and consistency are achieved through techniques such as replication, horizontal sharding, consistent hashing, and quorum read/write agreements. System resilience is maintained using mechanisms like circuit breakers to halt failing operations and retry with backoff to recover from temporary glitches. Coordination and transaction workflows across microservices rely on asynchronous PubSub messaging, leader election, and compensating sagas.
takeaways: Replication copies data across distinct servers, whereas sharding partitions databases horizontally across different machines.
Consistent hashing assigns data across machines using a virtual circular ring structure.
PubSub decouples service creators from consumers via asynchronous messaging.
Circuit breaker and retry with backoff serve as resiliency mechanisms to prevent cascading failures and manage transient errors.
Leader election assigns a single master node to manage cluster operations and avoid split-brain scenarios.
Quorum read/write guarantees data consistency in distributed databases by ensuring replica overlap.
The Saga pattern orchestrates distributed transactions across microservices via local steps and compensating actions.

sections.title: Virtualization vs. Containerization
sections.summary: Virtualization and containerization are two distinct approaches to isolating computing workloads. Virtualization operates at the hardware level, using hypervisors to emulate physical hardware so complete guest operating systems can run independently with their own kernels. In contrast, containerization provides OS-level isolation where isolated processes share the host operating system's kernel. While virtual machines offer broad flexibility across different operating systems at the cost of heavier resource use and minute-scale startup times, containers provide lightweight execution and millisecond startups bounded by host kernel compatibility.
takeaways: Virtualization provides hardware-level isolation by running full operating systems with separate kernels on emulated hardware.
Virtual machines take minutes to boot because an entire operating system must initialize from scratch.
Containerization delivers OS-level isolation by sharing the host operating system kernel among isolated process environments.
Containers start in milliseconds because they launch processes rather than booting full operating systems.
All containers running on a host must be compatible with that host's underlying kernel.

sections.title: HTTP vs. HTTPS
sections.summary: HTTP transmits data in plain text across a standard TCP handshake, leaving sensitive data vulnerable to interception. In contrast, HTTPS incorporates SSL/TLS to authenticate the server and encrypt data in transit. It begins with a TCP handshake, follows with certificate verification by a trusted Certificate Authority, establishes a shared session key via asymmetric encryption, and subsequently secures communication using symmetric encryption.
takeaways: HTTP sends data in plain text, making passwords, tokens, and forms readable in transit.
HTTP relies solely on a standard three-way TCP handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) without encryption.
HTTPS uses an SSL/TLS certificate containing the server's public key, signed by a trusted Certificate Authority, to authenticate domain ownership.
HTTPS performs key exchange via asymmetric encryption to establish a shared symmetric session key.
Subsequent data transmission in HTTPS is protected using symmetric encryption via the shared session key.

takeaways: MCP 是一種開放標準協定，旨在將 AI models 與外部 tools、APIs 和 data sources 連結。
MCP 消除了為每個外部應用程式（例如 Gmail、Slack 或 GitHub）個別建置自訂 integration 的需求。

sections.title: 9 個你應該知道的 Distributed Systems Patterns
sections.summary: Distributed systems 利用專門的 architectural patterns 來確保 scalability、fault tolerance 與 data consistency。Data distribution 和 consistency 是透過 replication、horizontal sharding、consistent hashing 以及 quorum read/write 機制來達成的。系統的 resilience 是透過像 circuit breakers（用來中斷失敗的操作）和 retry with backoff（用於從暫時性錯誤中恢復）等機制來維持。跨 microservices 的協調與 transaction workflows 則仰賴非同步的 PubSub messaging、leader election 與 compensating sagas。
takeaways: Replication 將資料複製到不同的伺服器上，而 sharding 則是將資料庫水平切分（partition）到不同的機器上。
Consistent hashing 利用虛擬環狀結構（circular ring）將資料分配到不同的機器上。
PubSub 透過非同步 messaging 將服務的 producer 與 consumer 解耦。
Circuit breaker 與 retry with backoff 作為 resilience 機制，能防止 cascading failures 並處理 transient errors。
Leader election 會指定單一 master node 來管理 cluster 操作，並避免 split-brain 情況發生。
Quorum read/write 透過確保 replica 的重疊，來保證 distributed databases 中的 data consistency。
Saga pattern 透過 local steps 與 compensating actions，來協調整合跨 microservices 的 distributed transactions。

sections.title: Virtualization vs. Containerization
sections.summary: Virtualization 與 containerization 是隔離運算工作負載（workloads）的兩種不同方法。Virtualization 運作於硬體層級，利用 hypervisors 模擬實體硬體，讓完整的 guest operating systems 可以帶著各自的 kernel 獨立運作。相比之下，containerization 提供了 OS-level 的隔離，隔離的 processes 共享 host operating system 的 kernel。雖然 virtual machines 能支援不同作業系統的廣泛彈性，但代價是較高的資源消耗與數分鐘級的開機時間；而 containers 則提供輕量級的執行環境與毫秒級的啟動速度，但受限於 host kernel 的相容性。
takeaways: Virtualization 透過在模擬的硬體上運行帶有獨立 kernel 的完整作業系統，提供 hardware-level 的隔離。
Virtual machines 需要數分鐘才能開機，因為整個作業系統必須從頭開始初始化。
Containerization 透過在各個隔離的 process 環境間共享 host operating system kernel，提供 OS-level 的隔離。
Containers 可以在數毫秒內啟動，因為它們是啟動 process，而不是開機整個作業系統。
在 host 上運行的所有 containers 都必須與該 host 的底層 kernel 相容。

sections.title: HTTP vs. HTTPS
sections.summary: HTTP 透過標準的 TCP handshake 以明文（plain text）傳輸資料，導致敏感資料容易被攔截。相較之下，HTTPS 結合了 SSL/TLS 來驗證伺服器身分並加密傳輸中的資料。它從 TCP handshake 開始，接著由受信任的 Certificate Authority 進行憑證驗證，透過非對稱加密（asymmetric encryption）建立共享的 session key，隨後使用對稱加密（symmetric encryption）來保護通訊安全。
takeaways: HTTP 以明文（plain text）傳送資料，使得密碼、tokens 和表單在傳輸過程中都能被讀取。
HTTP 僅依賴標準的三向 TCP handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK)，完全沒有加密。
HTTPS 使用包含伺服器 public key 且由受信任的 Certificate Authority 簽署的 SSL/TLS 憑證，來驗證網域所有權。
HTTPS 透過非對稱加密進行 key exchange，以建立共享的對稱 session key。
在 HTTPS 中，後續的資料傳輸是透過共享的 session key 使用對稱加密進行保護。

items.title: 5 Embedding Compression Techniques

sections.title: The easiest way to find out which models you can run on your computer
sections.summary: The Magnitude CLI is a tool designed to help users identify which AI models are suitable for their local hardware. It profiles the user's machine and provides rankings based on speed, accuracy, intelligence, and memory requirements. Once a model is selected, it can be used with various development harnesses such as Claude Code or Codex.
takeaways: Magnitude is a CLI tool installed via npm for local model profiling.
The tool evaluates models across four dimensions: speed, accuracy, intelligence, and memory.
It assists users in selecting models that fit their specific hardware constraints.
Magnitude supports integration with external harnesses like Pi, OpenCode, and Claude Code.
The project is hosted on GitHub and developed by Magnitude Dev.

sections.title: 5 embedding compression techniques
sections.summary: Embedding compression techniques optimize vector storage and retrieval by reducing dimensionality or bit precision. Methods like PCA and Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) allow for smaller vector sizes, while scalar and binary quantization reduce the memory footprint per dimension. Product Quantization further compresses data by encoding subvectors as centroid IDs. These techniques are often combined and used in multi-stage retrieval systems to balance memory efficiency with search accuracy.
takeaways: Embedding compression targets either the number of dimensions or the bits per dimension.
MRL allows embeddings to be truncated at inference while maintaining utility.
Scalar quantization reduces float32 to int8, achieving a 4x reduction in payload.
Binary quantization provides a 32x reduction and enables faster search via XOR operations.
Product Quantization approximates distances using subvector centroid lookups.
OpenAI's text-embedding-3-large at 256 dimensions outperforms text-embedding-ada-002 on MTEB.
Compressed retrieval often requires a rescoring step with high-precision embeddings for optimal ranking.

sections.title: 72 techniques to optimize LLMs in production
sections.summary: LLM inference in production is characterized by an asymmetry between the compute-bound prefill phase and the memory-bandwidth-bound decode phase. To address these bottlenecks, developers employ a stack of over 70 optimization techniques ranging from model compression and advanced attention mechanisms to speculative decoding and model routing. These strategies collectively bridge the cost-efficiency gap between naive deployments and optimized serving stacks, significantly reducing the price per million tokens.
takeaways: Prefill saturates GPU tensor cores by processing prompts in parallel, while decode is limited by memory bandwidth as it generates tokens sequentially.
Model compression techniques like INT8, INT4, and FP8 reduce memory footprints, with FP8 providing native speedups on Hopper and Blackwell architectures.
Advanced attention variants such as FlashAttention, PagedAttention, and Multi-Latent Attention (MLA) optimize IO and KV cache memory usage.
Speculative decoding methods like Medusa and EAGLE accelerate generation by predicting multiple tokens per forward pass.
Batching strategies, including continuous and disaggregated prefill-decode, improve hardware utilization and reduce per-token costs.
Caching mechanisms (prefix, semantic, and response caching) and prompt compression tools like LLMLingua further minimize operational overhead.
Model routing and cascading allow for cost optimization by directing simpler queries to smaller, more efficient models.

items.summary: The Magnitude CLI is a tool designed to help users identify which AI models are suitable for their local hardware. It profiles the user's machine and provides rankings based on speed, accuracy, intelligence, and memory requirements. Once a model is selected, it can be used with various development harnesses such as Claude Code or Codex. Embedding compression techniques optimize vector storage and retrieval by reducing dimensionality or bit precision. Methods like PCA and Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) allow for smaller vector sizes, while scalar and binary quantization reduce the memory footprint per dimension. Product Quantization further compresses data by encoding subvectors as centroid IDs. These techniques are often combined and used in multi-stage retrieval systems to balance memory efficiency with search accuracy. LLM inference in production is characterized by an asymmetry between the compute-bound prefill phase and the memory-bandwidth-bound decode phase. To address these bottlenecks, developers employ a stack of over 70 optimization techniques ranging from model compression and advanced attention mechanisms to speculative decoding and model routing. These strategies collectively bridge the cost-efficiency gap between naive deployments and optimized serving stacks, significantly reducing the price per million tokens.

sections.title: 5 種 embedding compression 技術
sections.summary: Embedding compression 技術透過降低維度或位元精度來優化向量儲存與檢索。像 PCA 和 Matryoshka Representation Learning（MRL）等方法可縮減向量大小，而 scalar 和 binary quantization 則能降低每個維度的 memory footprint。Product Quantization 透過將 subvector 編碼為 centroid ID 來進一步壓縮資料。這些技術通常會相互結合並應用於多階段檢索（multi-stage retrieval）系統中，以在記憶體效率與搜尋精確度之間取得平衡。
takeaways: Embedding compression 的目標主要是維度數量或每個維度的位元數。
MRL 允許 embedding 在 inference 階段被截斷（truncate），同時仍保有其效用。
Scalar quantization 將 float32 降低至 int8，實現 4 倍的 payload 縮減。
Binary quantization 提供 32 倍的縮減，並能透過 XOR 運算實現更快的搜尋。
Product Quantization 透過 subvector centroid 查找來近似距離。
OpenAI 的 text-embedding-3-large 在 256 維度下的表現優於 MTEB 上的 text-embedding-ada-002。
壓縮檢索（compressed retrieval）通常需要搭配高精度 embedding 進行 rescoring 步驟，以達到最佳排序。

sections.title: 72 種在 production 優化 LLM 的技術
sections.summary: 在 production 環境中的 LLM inference 具有 compute-bound 的 prefill 階段與 memory-bandwidth-bound 的 decode 階段之間的非對稱特性。為了解決這些瓶頸，開發者採用了超過 70 種優化技術組成的技術棧，涵蓋從模型壓縮、進階 attention 機制到 speculative decoding 與 model routing。這些策略共同縮小了 naive 部署與優化 serving stack 之間的成本效益差距，大幅降低每百萬 token 的成本。
takeaways: Prefill 透過平行處理 prompt 來使 GPU tensor cores 達到飽和，而 decode 則因循序生成 token 而受限於記憶體頻寬。
INT8、INT4 和 FP8 等模型壓縮技術可降低 memory footprint，其中 FP8 在 Hopper 與 Blackwell 架構上提供了原生加速。
FlashAttention、PagedAttention 和 Multi-Latent Attention（MLA）等進階 attention 變體可優化 IO 與 KV cache 的記憶體使用量。
Medusa 和 EAGLE 等 speculative decoding 方法透過在每次 forward pass 預測多個 token 來加速生成。
包括 continuous 以及 disaggregated prefill-decode 在內的 batching 策略，可提升硬體利用率並降低每 token 成本。
Caching 機制（prefix、semantic 與 response caching）以及像 LLMLingua 這類的 prompt compression 工具能進一步減少 operational overhead。
Model routing 與 cascading 透過將較簡單的查詢導向較小且更高效的模型，來實現成本最佳化。

sections.title: InsForge: The first backend built for AI coding agents
sections.summary: InsForge is a backend infrastructure platform specifically engineered for AI coding agents, aiming to solve the context fragmentation issues found in human-centric platforms like Firebase and AWS. By implementing a semantic layer, it provides agents with structured, machine-readable primitives that include metadata and cross-primitive awareness. This design results in significant performance gains, including doubled accuracy compared to Supabase MCP and improved token efficiency. The project is open-source under the Apache 2.0 license and supports major agents like Claude Code and Cursor.
takeaways: Traditional backend platforms like AWS and Supabase cause AI agents to hallucinate because they provide fragmented context through MCP servers.
InsForge introduces a semantic layer where backend primitives like auth and databases are natively machine-readable.
Primitives in InsForge are aware of each other, allowing auth systems to understand database permissions and storage policies automatically.
Benchmarking shows InsForge is approximately 2x more accurate than Supabase MCP and 30% more token-efficient.
The platform is compatible with popular AI coding tools including Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, and Codex.
InsForge is released as open-source software under the Apache 2.0 license.

sections.title: Attention Mechanisms in LLMs, clearly explained
sections.summary: The text provides a comprehensive overview of attention mechanisms in Large Language Models, focusing on how different architectures address the memory bottleneck created by the KV cache. It traces the evolution from memory-intensive Multi-Head Attention to more efficient variants like Multi-Query, Grouped-Query, and Multi-Head Latent Attention. Additionally, it explores computational optimizations like FlashAttention, architectural sparsity for long contexts, and serving-layer innovations like PagedAttention and RadixAttention.
takeaways: The primary constraint for long sequences and large batches in LLMs is GPU memory used by the KV cache, not computational math.
Multi-Head Attention (MHA) is memory-expensive because every head maintains its own independent KV cache.
Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) has become the industry standard by balancing memory efficiency and model expressiveness.
Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) uses low-rank compression to reduce the cache footprint to 5-13% of MHA requirements.
FlashAttention improves performance by optimizing memory traffic between HBM and SRAM without changing the underlying attention math.
Sparse attention mechanisms like Sliding Window Attention (SWA) and Native Sparse Attention (NSA) are essential for scaling to million-token contexts.
Serving engines use PagedAttention and RadixAttention to manage memory allocation and reuse common prefixes across requests.
