sections.title: 一個很棒的 LLM 技術面試題目：
sections.summary: 將 RAG 應用程式從 local 環境遷移到具有多個 replica 的 production 環境時，會帶來 state management 方面的挑戰。Local 配置通常將 vector indices、對話歷史與 documents 存放在記憶體或 local disk 中，當在 load balancer 後方進行 scale 時，會導致資料遺失或不一致。為了確保 production 的可靠性，開發者必須透過像 pgvector 這樣的 persistent vector stores、藉由 LangGraph 等工具進行 shared state checkpointing，以及使用 centralized object storage 來將這些元件外部化（externalize）。Akamai 提供了 reference implementations 與工作坊，以協助開發者架構這些 production-ready 的系統。
takeaways: Local RAG 配置在 production 中會失敗，因為 in-memory 變數與 local disk 無法跨經過 load balancing 的多個 replica 共享。
Vector indices 必須持久化（persistent）且可被所有 replica 存取，以避免開機時出現空結果或重複的 embedding 處理流程。
對話歷史需要外部的 checkpointing（例如 LangGraph 的 Postgres 整合），以在不同的 replica 之間維持 context。
Documents 需要 shared object storage，以確保所有 replica 都能存取一致的語料庫（corpus），並避免每個 replica 各自重複執行 ingestion。
'rag-langgraph-k8s-quickstart' repository 展示了在 LKE 上使用 FastAPI、LangChain 和 Terraform 的 production 架構。
Akamai 的 'akamai-workshop-ai-inference' 涵蓋了自建（self-hosted）模型的進階主題，例如 KV cache 的權衡（tradeoffs）與 continuous batching。

sections.title: Static vs. Dynamic vs. Continuous Batching
sections.summary: 本文比較了在 GPU 上 serving 大型語言模型（LLM）時的 static、dynamic 與 continuous batching 策略，並強調 decoding 階段主要受到權重讀取所導致的 memory-bound 限制。Continuous batching（或稱 iteration-level scheduling）被視為處理可變輸出長度最高效的方法，因為它允許 request 在每次 forward pass 時進出 batch。為了解決 continuous batching 中因大型 prompt 造成的 latency spikes，文中介紹了 chunked prefill 技術，將輸入處理切分到多個 iteration 中執行。
takeaways: LLM decoding 效能主要受限於 memory bandwidth，而非運算能力（compute capacity）。
Static batching 對於 autoregressive 模型來說效率低落，因為它會迫使整個 batch 等待最慢的 sequence 處理完畢。
Dynamic batching 雖然使用計時器來組成 batch，但仍將整個 batch 視為單一執行單位，從而導致閒置時間（idle time）。
Continuous batching 允許 requests 在每個 iteration 進出 batch，針對不同長度的輸出最大化 GPU 使用率。
KV cache 是限制 continuous batching 系統中最大 batch size 的主要記憶體瓶頸。
Chunked prefill 將大型 prompt 切分成較小的片段，以維持現有 request 穩定的 token 生成延遲（latency）。
Static batching 仍適用於固定輸出長度的任務，例如 classification 與 embedding generation。

sections.title: 在大型資料集上訓練經典 ML 模型
sections.summary: 本文探討在超出記憶體容量的大型 tabular 資料集上，訓練經典機器學習模型（特別是 tree-based ensembles）的挑戰。雖然像 Spark MLlib 這類的 framework 提供了其中一種解法，但 Random Patches 方法則提供了另一種選擇：在 row 與 column 的隨機子集上訓練個別的 tree。相較於傳統的 random forests，這種方法不僅能支援大規模資料的訓練，通常還能提升模型效能並降低 variance。透過確保各個 tree 之間的差異盡可能最大化，此方法有效地達成了 bagging 降低 variance 的目標。
takeaways: Scikit-learn 在其經典機器學習實作中對 batch processing 的支援有限。
標準的 tree-based ensemble 方法通常需要將完整資料集載入至記憶體中。
Random Patches 方法涉及為 ensemble 中的每棵 tree 同時對隨機 rows 與隨機 columns 進行採樣（sampling）。
實證結果顯示，Random Patches 在多種資料集上的表現通常優於傳統的 random forests。
在不同的 data patches 上進行訓練可減少 tree 之間的重疊，從而有效降低模型的 variance。
此技術允許在超出單機記憶體負荷的資料集上建立強健的（robust）模型。

sections.title: Researchers built a new AI inference engine
sections.summary: Superlinked has released the Superlinked Inference Engine (SIE), an open-source tool designed to reduce AI self-hosting costs by approximately 4x. Unlike traditional setups that require separate servers for each model in an agentic pipeline, SIE serves multiple models from a single process on one GPU. It optimizes resource usage by dynamically loading and evicting models based on traffic using a least-recently-used policy. The engine supports over 85 models and is compatible with major vector databases and AI frameworks.
takeaways: SIE reduces self-hosting costs by consolidating multiple models onto a single GPU process.
The engine supports over 20 model architectures and 85+ specific models, including embedders, rerankers, and LLMs.
It uses a least-recently-used (LRU) eviction strategy to manage GPU memory dynamically based on traffic.
SIE is a drop-in replacement for the OpenAI API and is licensed under Apache 2.0.
The tool integrates with vector databases like Qdrant, Weaviate, Chroma, and LanceDB, as well as LangChain and LlamaIndex.

sections.title: WebMCP by Google, clearly explained!
sections.summary: WebMCP is a browser API developed by the Chrome and Edge teams that allows websites to explicitly define actions for AI agents. By providing named tools with descriptions and JSON Schema inputs, it eliminates the need for agents to guess functionality from pixels or generic DOM structures. The API operates within the user's existing browser session, ensuring that agents have immediate access to authenticated features without requiring separate API keys. Developers can integrate WebMCP by registering JavaScript objects or by adding specific attributes to existing HTML forms.
takeaways: WebMCP enables websites to expose specific functionalities as machine-readable tools with plain-English descriptions and typed inputs.
The API uses JSON Schema for input validation, ensuring compatibility with major models like Claude, GPT, and Gemini.
Actions run within the user's active browser tab, leveraging existing login sessions and removing the need for separate authentication tokens.
Available tools can dynamically update based on the user's state, such as showing more actions after a user signs in.
Implementation can be done via a JavaScript registerTool method or by adding toolname and tooldescription attributes to HTML forms.
WebMCP is positioned as a more reliable and token-efficient alternative to pixel-based 'computer use' or generic browser automation.

sections.title: Sparse random projections
sections.summary: Sparse random projection serves as an efficient alternative to PCA for high-dimensional datasets, addressing PCA's cubic time complexity which becomes impractical at 1000+ dimensions. The technique projects data into a lower-dimensional space while approximately preserving the pairwise distances between points, a property validated by similar silhouette scores in K-Means clustering experiments. While effective for datasets with over 700-800 features, the method can be unstable for low-dimensional data and requires tuning the target dimension as a hyperparameter. This principle is also applied in LLM fine-tuning through the VeRA technique, which uses frozen, shared random matrices to reduce trainable parameters.
takeaways: PCA's cubic relationship with dimensions makes it unsuitable for very high-dimensional datasets.
Sparse random projection preserves the distance between data points while reducing dimensionality.
K-Means clustering performance, measured by silhouette score, remains stable when using random projections until the target dimension becomes too low.
The target dimension for projection is a hyperparameter that must be tuned to balance efficiency and clustering quality.
Random projections are recommended for datasets with 700-800+ features but are unstable for data with fewer than 100 dimensions.
VeRA is an LLM fine-tuning method that utilizes frozen, shared random matrices to minimize trainable parameters compared to LoRA.

items.title: What Happens Inside an AI Chatbot Between Enter and the First Word?

sections.title: How the Input to the Model is Assembled?
sections.summary: User queries are not sent directly to large language models in isolation; instead, an assembled document containing system prompts, tool definitions, memory, retrieved documents, and conversation history is provided. Managing what goes into this input and how it is structured is an essential discipline known as context engineering. Because models possess finite attention budgets, longer inputs can gradually degrade reasoning precision even on basic tasks. Consequently, products using the identical underlying model can generate differing responses depending on how they curate and time the assembly of context.
takeaways: The actual input sent to a model is a curated document consisting of system prompts, tool definitions, memory, retrieved data, conversation history, and the user prompt.
Context engineering is the discipline of selecting, structuring, and pruning material within the model's input document.
LLMs have a finite attention budget, meaning that precision and accuracy degrade gradually as input length grows.
Two products powered by the identical model can produce different responses to identical queries due to differences in context engineering.
Context material can be retrieved completely up front for faster speed or retrieved dynamically via lightweight references to conserve tokens.

sections.title: Why is Every Input Message to the Model Independent?
sections.summary: Large language models are stateless by design, requiring the entire conversation history to be resent with every new turn. Because conversation history accumulates with each interaction, input token volume compounds and typically dominates total API costs despite lower per-token pricing than outputs. When exchanges exceed the context window, naive retransmission breaks down, necessitating strategies such as dropping older turns, summarizing chat history, or using external storage and retrieval. Consequently, long conversations suffer from escalating latency, higher expenses, and potential loss of fine-grained conversational details.
takeaways: Models retain no memory between requests, requiring the full conversation history to be reconstructed and resent on every turn.
Input token counts compound with each exchange, causing input costs to dominate overall spend despite lower unit pricing than output tokens.
The naive strategy of resending the entire conversation fails once the interaction exceeds the model's context window.
Context mitigation strategies include trimming older turns, summarizing prior dialogue, or storing data externally for on-demand retrieval.
Extended interactions result in increased processing latency, higher costs, and potential information loss due to trimming or condensation.

sections.title: Performing Safety Checks on the Input
sections.summary: AI systems can perform input safety checks using a distinct, decoupled safety model before answer generation begins. This architectural separation allows the safety mechanism to be independently retrained, monitored, and used for routing or escalations without modifying the primary assistant. While early single-classifier designs incurred an expensive 24 percent compute overhead and raised false refusals by 0.38 percentage points, modern deployments resolve this via a cascade architecture. In this cascaded setup, a low-cost validation inspects all traffic, routing only flagged inputs to the more resource-intensive classifier to bring compute overhead down to approximately one percent.
takeaways: Input safety checks utilize a decoupled, smaller model to evaluate requests before the primary assistant generates a response.
Decoupling the safety layer permits independent retraining, fine-tuning, monitoring, and actions such as logging, routing, or human escalation.
Early production safety classifiers increased compute requirements by approximately 24 percent and increased harmless query refusals by 0.38 percentage points.
A cascaded safety architecture deploys a lightweight validator across all traffic and invokes the resource-intensive classifier only on flagged inputs.
Cascaded validation cuts compute overhead down to roughly one percent and harmless query refusal rates to 0.05 percent.

sections.title: How the Model Understands the Words?
sections.summary: Documents are converted into tokens, sub-word chunks of text that models process as their primary units. Modern systems typically construct tokens from raw bytes to ensure representation across all writing systems, averaging roughly three-quarters of an English word per token. Because token counts for the same content can vary across translations by up to fifteen times, speakers of certain languages face higher costs, slower processing, and reduced effective context window capacity. Furthermore, chunking text into tokens makes fine-grained, character-level tasks like counting specific letters awkward for models.
takeaways: Tokens are sub-word text chunks positioned between individual characters and whole words, averaging approximately 0.75 English words each.
Modern systems build tokens from raw bytes rather than characters to reliably represent any writing system.
Equivalent text translated into different languages can exhibit token count variations of up to 15 times.
Higher token density per text reduces usable context window space, increases latency, and inflates financial cost.
Operating on multi-character token chunks complicates character-level reasoning tasks, such as letter counting.

sections.title: How the Model is Shared Across Multiple Conversations
sections.summary: Serving large models economically requires batching multiple requests together to minimize memory bandwidth bottlenecks caused by repeatedly loading model parameters. While naive batching underutilizes hardware due to differing output lengths among conversational requests, scheduling at individual generation steps allows new requests to fill finished slots immediately. This step-level scheduling approach can achieve up to 23 times higher throughput and lower median response times over naive batching. However, concurrent execution causes numerical variations, meaning identical prompts can produce different outputs even when randomness is disabled.
takeaways: Batching multiple requests amortizes the memory bandwidth cost of loading model parameters on modern accelerators.
Naive batching leaves hardware partially idle because requests have variable lengths, forcing compute to wait for the longest completion.
Scheduling requests at the level of individual generation steps can improve throughput by up to 23 times over naive batching while also lowering median response times.
Sharing compute hardware across varying batch sizes causes numerical variations, leading identical prompts to produce dozens of distinct outputs even with randomness turned off.

sections.title: Prefill And Decode
sections.summary: Generating a response occurs in two distinct phases: an initial prefill phase that processes all input tokens in parallel and a subsequent decode phase that generates output tokens sequentially. The prefill phase is computationally bound and scales with input length, leading to longer wait times before output begins in extended conversations. In contrast, the decode phase is memory-speed bound and outputs tokens at a relatively steady rate regardless of input size. System performance is measured through time to first token and time per output token, with techniques like input chunking used to prevent long requests from stalling concurrent batch generation.
takeaways: Inference is split into two phases: a parallel, compute-bound prefill phase and a sequential, memory-bound decode phase.
The prefill phase duration scales with the length of the input context, causing the pause before generation starts to increase in longer conversations.
The decode phase produces tokens at a roughly constant rate regardless of the prior conversation length.
Total response time approximately equals the time to first token plus the time per output token multiplied by reply length.
Splitting long inputs into chunks and interleaving them with ongoing token generation prevents batched requests from stalling.

sections.title: Caching the Existing Calculations
sections.summary: During the generation phase of language model inference, intermediate calculations from previous tokens are stored in memory and reused to avoid repeating redundant computation. This conversation state consumes significant memory, often making it the primary bottleneck for serving capacity rather than the model weights themselves. Borrowing virtual memory techniques from operating systems, modern serving architectures allocate storage in small on-demand blocks, cutting memory waste from up to 80% to under 4% and increasing throughput by 2-4 times. Additionally, caching reusable prompt prefixes across turns provides substantial cost discounts and motivates structuring prompts with static content placed before dynamic content.
takeaways: Intermediate token calculations are cached and reused across inference steps, but can consume gigabytes of memory per request for a 70-billion-parameter model with an 8000-token context.
Concurrent user serving capacity is typically limited by the memory required for conversation state rather than model weights.
Early serving systems reserved contiguous memory blocks for the maximum possible response length, leaving 60% to 80% of memory unused.
Allocating memory in small fixed-size blocks on demand reduces memory waste to under 4% and improves serving throughput by 2 to 4 times.
Cached portions of prompts are often priced around one-tenth of normal input rates by API providers.
Prompt caching relies on prefix reuse, necessitating that stable content be placed at the top and changing content at the bottom of prompts.

sections.title: Streaming And Guardrails
sections.summary: During the AI response phase, streaming delivers text word-by-word to match or exceed human reading speeds of roughly six tokens per second, substantially improving perceived latency. However, conventional output safety checks require evaluating the completed response before judging it, making it impossible to retract already displayed words. Delaying output until safety verification finishes eliminates the benefits of streaming. Emerging alternatives to address this include token-by-token stream evaluation and inspecting internal model states during generation.
takeaways: Streaming output word-by-word improves perceived generation speed by avoiding a blank waiting period.
Human reading speed averages around six tokens per second, which production systems comfortably exceed.
Traditional output safety checks inspect entire finished responses, conflicting with the real-time nature of streaming.
Buffering responses until safety checks complete entirely negates the perceived speed advantage of streaming.
Modern workarounds include guards that inspect text token-by-token or inspect internal model states during generation.

sections.title: How Tools Are Run?
sections.summary: Integrating tools changes the standard linear generation process into an iterative execution loop. Language models do not execute external actions like web searches directly; rather, they emit text requesting an action, which the host application fulfills and appends back into context. Each completed tool action restarts the full pipeline—including reassembly, tokenization, queuing, and generation. Consequently, multi-step queries incur noticeable latency and sharply compounding token costs as accumulating context is repeatedly processed across successive calls.
takeaways: Models do not directly execute tools like web searches or database queries; they output formatted text requests for the surrounding application to run.
Tool execution converts the one-way generation path into a multi-step loop where results are fed back into context as new input.
Each tool call forces the entire pipeline to rerun from scratch, including assembly, checks, tokenization, queuing, and two generation phases.
Multiple round trips across tools create noticeable latency compared to simple generation.
Context costs compound severely because early messages and instructions are resent and billed on every subsequent call within a session.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: In an LLM interaction, the end-to-end response delay is driven by multiple components including network latency, document assembly, safety checks, queueing, and input reading. Because language models retain no inherent memory, conversational history must be reconstructed and re-read from scratch with every turn. In extended conversations, processing this accumulated input context consumes the largest fraction of initial latency. Consequently, longer chats suffer from increased delay, higher operational costs, and potential detail loss.
takeaways: Input reading accounts for the largest fraction of initial delay in extended conversations, causing the initial pause to lengthen over time.
Models have no stateful memory, requiring the full conversation context to be rebuilt from scratch on every turn.
Input safety checks utilize cascaded designs that account for approximately one percent of total compute.
The overhead incurred from tokenization is negligible in overall response latency.
Document assembly and context gathering constitute a larger fraction of delay than raw network overhead and authentication.

zh.summary: 使用者 query 並非單獨直接傳送給大型語言模型；相反地，系統會提供一份組裝好的 document，內容包含 system prompts、tool definitions、memory、檢索出的 documents 以及對話歷史。管理輸入內容及其組織架構是一門至關重要的專業領域，稱為 context engineering。由於模型的 attention budget 有限，過長的輸入即使在基礎任務上也可能逐漸降低推理精確度。因此，使用相同底層模型的產品，可能會因為其 context 的組織與組裝時機不同而產生相異的回應。大型語言模型在設計上是 stateless 的，每一輪新對話都需要重新傳送整個對話歷史。隨著互動次數增加，對話歷史持續累積，使得輸入 token 量呈複合增長；儘管輸入 token 單價通常低於輸出，它往往仍主導了整體的 API 成本。當對話超過 context window 時，單純的重複傳送策略便會失效，必須採用捨棄較舊對話輪次（turns）、摘要聊天紀錄，或是使用外部儲存與檢索等策略。因此，長對話會面臨持續攀升的 latency、更高的花費，以及可能遺失對話細微細節的風險。AI 系統可以在生成回答之前，使用獨立、解耦（decoupled）的 safety 模型執行輸入的安全檢查。這種架構分離使 safety 機制能夠獨立進行 retrain、監控，並用於 routing 或 escalation，而無需修改主要的 assistant。雖然早期的單一分類器（single-classifier）設計帶來了高達 24% 的運算開銷（compute overhead），並使錯誤拒絕率（false refusal rate）增加了 0.38 個百分點，但現代部署透過 cascade architecture 解決了此問題。在這種 cascaded 架構下，低成本的驗證機制會檢查所有 traffic，僅將被標記的輸入 route 到消耗較多資源的分類器，進而將運算開銷降至約 1%。

sections.title: Model 的 Input 是如何組裝的？
sections.summary: 使用者的 query 並不是單獨直接傳送給 large language models；相反地，系統會提供一份組裝好的 document，其中包含 system prompts、tool definitions、memory、retrieved documents 以及 conversation history。管理哪些內容會進入這個 input 以及其如何被結構化，是一門被稱為 context engineering 的核心專業。由於 model 具有有限的 attention budgets，較長的 input 即使在基本任務上也可能逐漸降低 reasoning 的精準度。因此，即使使用完全相同的底層 model，不同產品也會因為如何 curate 和掌握 context 組裝的時機，而產生截然不同的 response。
takeaways: 實際發送給 model 的 input 是一份經過 curated 的 document，由 system prompts、tool definitions、memory、retrieved data、conversation history 與 user prompt 所組成。
Context engineering 是一門在 model 的 input document 內挑選、結構化與 pruning 材料的專業。
LLM 擁有有限的 attention budget，這意味著隨著 input 長度增加，precision 與 accuracy 會逐漸下降。
兩款由相同 model 驅動的產品，可能會因為 context engineering 的差異，而對相同的 query 產生不同的 response。
Context 資料可以在一開始完整 retrieve 以換取更快的速度，或是透過輕量的 reference 動態 retrieve 以節省 token。

sections.title: 為什麼傳送至 Model 的每個 Input Message 都是獨立的？
sections.summary: Large language models 在設計上是 stateless 的，每一次新的 turn 都必須重新發送完整的 conversation history。因為 conversation history 會隨著每次互動而累積，即使 input token 的單價低於 output，其用量也會呈複合式增長，並通常主導了整體的 API 成本。當對話超過 context window 時，單純的重新傳送機制便會失效，必須採用捨棄較舊的 turns、總結 chat history，或使用外部儲存與 retrieval 等策略。因此，長對話會面臨持續升高的 latency、更高的花費，以及可能遺失細粒度對話細節的問題。
takeaways: Model 在各個 request 之間不會保留任何 memory，因此每一輪 turn 都必須重新建構並重新發送完整的 conversation history。
Input token 數量會隨著每次對話累積複合增長，導致儘管單價低於 output token，input 成本仍會占據整體支出的主要部分。
一旦互動超出 model 的 context window，單純重新發送整段對話的 naive 策略就會失效。
Context mitigation 策略包括 trimming 較舊的 turns、摘要先前的對話，或是將資料儲存在外部以進行 on-demand retrieval。
長時間的互動會導致處理 latency 增加、成本上升，並可能因 trimming 或 condensation 而造成潛在的資訊遺失。

sections.title: 對 Input 執行 Safety Checks
sections.summary: AI 系統可以在開始產生回答之前，使用獨立且 decoupled 的 safety model 來執行 input safety checks。這種架構上的解耦讓 safety 機制可以獨立進行 retraining、監控，並用於 routing 或 escalation，而無須修改主要的 assistant。雖然早期的 single-classifier 設計會帶來高達 24% 的 compute overhead，並使 false refusal 增加 0.38 個百分點，但現代部署透過 cascade architecture 解決了這個問題。在這種串聯架構中，低成本的 validation 會檢查所有流量，僅將被標記的 input 導向至更耗費資源的 classifier，使 compute overhead 降至約 1%。
takeaways: Input safety checks 利用 decoupled 的較小 model，在主要 assistant 產生 response 之前評估 request。
將 safety layer 解耦可實現獨立的 retraining、fine-tuning、monitoring，以及 logging、routing 或 human escalation 等操作。
早期的 production safety classifiers 增加了約 24% 的 compute 需求，並使無害 query 的拒絕率增加了 0.38 個百分點。
cascaded safety architecture 在所有流量上部署 lightweight validator，並僅在被標記的輸入上調用資源密集型的 classifier。
Cascaded validation 將 compute overhead 降至約 1%，並將無害 query 的拒絕率降至 0.05%。

sections.title: 模型如何理解單詞？
sections.summary: 文件會被轉換成 tokens，也就是模型作為主要處理單元的次詞（sub-word）文本塊。現代系統通常直接從 raw bytes 構建 tokens，以確保支援所有書寫系統，平均每個 token 約代表四分之三個英文單詞。由於相同內容在不同語言翻譯中的 token 數量最多可相差達 15 倍，特定語言的使用者面臨著更高的成本、更慢的處理速度，以及有效 context window 容量的縮減。此外，將文本切分成 tokens 會使模型在處理細粒度（fine-grained）的字元層級（character-level）任務（如計算特定字母數量）時變得非常棘手。
takeaways: Tokens 是介於個別字元與完整單詞之間的 sub-word 文本塊，平均每個約等於 0.75 個英文單詞。
現代系統從 raw bytes 而非字元構建 tokens，以可靠地表示任何書寫系統。
相同語意的文本翻譯成不同語言後，token 數量可能會有高達 15 倍的差異。
每段文本更高的 token 密度會減少可用的 context window 空間、增加 latency，並推高財務成本。
以多字元的 token 區塊進行運算，會使字元層級（character-level）的推理任務（如字母計數）變得複雜。

sections.title: 模型如何在多個對話之間共享
sections.summary: 經濟高效地 serving 大型模型需要將多個 requests 進行 batching，以最大程度減少因重複載入模型參數而造成的 memory bandwidth 瓶頸。雖然 naive batching 因對話 requests 的輸出長度不同而導致硬體利用率不足，但在各個 generation step 進行排程可以讓新 requests 立即填補已完成的 slots。這種 step-level scheduling 方法相比 naive batching 可實現高達 23 倍的 throughput，並降低中位數回應時間。然而，並行執行會導致 numerical variations，這意味著即使關閉隨機性，相同的 prompt 也可能產生不同的輸出。
takeaways: 將多個 requests 進行 batching 可以分攤現代加速器載入模型參數的 memory bandwidth 成本。
Naive batching 會使硬體部分處於閒置狀態，因為 requests 長度不一，迫使運算資源等待耗時最長者完成。
在個別 generation step 的層級對 requests 進行排程，相比 naive batching 可提高高達 23 倍的 throughput，同時還能降低中位數回應時間。
在不同的 batch size 間共享運算硬體會導致 numerical variations，即使關閉隨機性，也會使相同的 prompt 產生數十種不同的輸出。

sections.title: Prefill 與 Decode
sections.summary: 生成回應分為兩個不同階段：初始的 prefill phase 會平行處理所有輸入 tokens，隨後的 decode phase 則會循序生成輸出 tokens。prefill phase 屬於 compute-bound，其耗時隨輸入長度增加而放大，導致在長對話中開始輸出前的等待時間變長。相較之下，decode phase 屬於 memory-bound，無論輸入大小為何，輸出 token 的速率都相對穩定。系統效能通常透過 time to first token 和 time per output token 來衡量，並使用如 input chunking 等技術來防止長 requests 阻礙同時進行的 batch generation。
takeaways: Inference 分為兩個階段：平行的 compute-bound prefill phase，以及循序的 memory-bound decode phase。
Prefill phase 的耗時會隨著輸入 context 的長度而增加，導致在較長的對話中，生成開始前的停頓時間拉長。
無論先前的對話長度為何，decode phase 都能以大致恆定的速率產出 tokens。
總回應時間大約等於 time to first token 加上 time per output token 乘以回覆長度。
將長輸入切分成 chunks 並與進行中的 token generation 交錯處理，可防止 batched requests 出現停頓。

sections.title: 快取既有的運算結果
sections.summary: 在語言模型 inference 的 generation 階段，來自先前 token 的中間運算結果會存放在記憶體中並重複使用，以避免重複進行多餘的計算。這種對話狀態會消耗大量記憶體，往往成為 serving capacity 的主要瓶頸，而非模型權重本身。借鑒作業系統的 virtual memory 技術，現代 serving 架構採用依需求分配的小區塊儲存，將記憶體浪費從高達 80% 降至 4% 以下，並將 throughput 提升 2 到 4 倍。此外，跨 turn 快取可重複使用的 prompt prefix 能大幅降低成本，這也推動了將靜態內容置於動態內容之前的 prompt 結構設計。
takeaways: 中間的 token 運算結果會被快取並在各個 inference step 中重複使用，但在 70B（70-billion-parameter）模型搭配 8000-token context 的情況下，每個 request 可能會消耗數 GB 的記憶體。
Concurrent 使用者的 serving capacity 通常是受限於對話狀態所需的記憶體，而非模型權重本身。
早期的 serving 系統會為最大可能的 response 長度預留連續記憶體區塊，導致 60% 到 80% 的記憶體未被使用。
依需求以小型的固定大小區塊分配記憶體，可將記憶體浪費降低至 4% 以下，並將 serving throughput 提高 2 至 4 倍。
API 提供商對 prompt 中被快取的部分，定價通常約為正常 input 費率的十分之一。
Prompt caching 依賴 prefix reuse，因此必須將穩定不變的內容置於 prompt 頂部，變動內容置於底部。

sections.title: Streaming 與 Guardrails
sections.summary: 在 AI response 階段，streaming 會逐字輸出文字，以達到或超越人類每秒約 6 個 token 的閱讀速度，大幅改善體感 latency。然而，傳統的 output safety checks 需要在評估完整 response 後才能做出判斷，這使得已經顯示的字詞無法撤回。若延遲輸出直到安全驗證完成，將徹底失去 streaming 的優勢。為了解決這個問題，新興的替代方案包括逐 token 的 stream 評估，以及在 generation 過程中檢查模型內部狀態。
takeaways: 逐字 streaming 輸出能避免空白等待時間，進而提升體感 generation 速度。
人類的平均閱讀速度約為每秒 6 個 token，production 系統能輕鬆超越此速度。
傳統的 output safety checks 會檢查完整的 finished response，這與 streaming 的即時性產生衝突。
將 response 暫存（buffering）直到 safety checks 完成，會完全抵消 streaming 的體感速度優勢。
現代的因應方案包括逐 token 檢查文字的 guard，或是在 generation 過程中檢查模型內部狀態。

sections.title: Tool 是如何運行的？
sections.summary: 整合 tool 會將標準的線性 generation 流程轉變為迭代執行的迴圈（loop）。語言模型不會直接執行像網路搜尋這類外部操作，而是輸出請求該操作的文字，再由 host application 執行並附加回 context 中。每次完成 tool 操作都會重啟整個 pipeline——包括 reassembly、tokenization、queuing 與 generation。因此，隨著累積的 context 在連續呼叫中被重複處理，多步驟查詢會產生顯著的 latency，並導致 token 成本大幅複利增加。
takeaways: 模型不會直接執行 web search 或 database query 等 tool；它們輸出格式化文字請求，交由周圍的應用程式執行。
Tool 執行會將單向的 generation 路徑轉換為多步驟 loop，在此過程中，執行結果會作為新的 input 回傳至 context 中。
每次 tool call 都會迫使整個 pipeline 從頭重新執行，包括 assembly、checks、tokenization、queuing 以及兩個 generation 階段。
與單純的 generation 相比，跨 tool 的多次 round trip 會造成明顯的 latency。
Context 成本會嚴重複利增加，因為先前的訊息和指令在 session 內的每一次後續呼叫中都會被重新發送並計費。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: 在 LLM 互動中，end-to-end 的 response 延遲是由多個環節造成的，包括 network latency、document assembly、safety checks、queuing 以及 input reading。由於語言模型本身不具備記憶能力，因此每一輪對話（turn）都必須從頭重建並重新讀取對話歷史。在長對話中，處理這些累積的 input context 佔據了 initial latency 的最大比例。因此，越長的對話會面臨延遲增加、維運成本升高以及潛在細節遺失的問題。
takeaways: 在長對話中，input reading 佔據了 initial delay 的最大比例，導致最初的等待停頓時間隨著時間推移而拉長。
模型沒有 stateful memory，因此每一輪對話都必須從頭重新構建完整的對話 context。
Input safety checks 採用 cascaded designs，約佔總 compute 的 1%。
Tokenization 所產生的 overhead 在整體 response latency 中幾乎可以忽略。
Document assembly 與 context gathering 所造成的延遲比例，高於純粹的 network overhead 與 authentication。

items.title: ExplainThis 全端開發雙週報 #87 軟體工廠 (Software Factory) 是什麼? 有什麼限制?

sections.title: ExplainThis 全端開發雙週報 #87 軟體工廠 (Software Factory) 是什麼? 有什麼限制?
sections.summary: This newsletter issue introduces the evolution of AI-driven software development from autocompletion in 2021 to advanced AI agents by 2026. As AI agent technologies have matured, emerging concepts such as Harness Engineering, Loop Engineering, and Software Factory have become central to community discussions. The issue explores why the concept of the Software Factory has re-emerged in the AI era, contrasts it with traditional software factories, and addresses current limitations and potential solutions.
takeaways: AI coding tooling evolved from simple autocompletion in 2021 to sophisticated AI agents by 2025 and 2026.
By the second half of 2026, the discussion around AI agents spurred new concepts including Harness Engineering, Loop Engineering, and Software Factory.
Although 'Software Factory' is not a brand-new term, it has been revitalized with new characteristics in the AI era.
Implementing modern AI-driven software factories faces specific limitations that require new engineering practices to overcome.

sections.title: 什麼是軟體工廠?
sections.summary: The concept of software factories dates back to 1968, originally focusing on standardized environments, reusable components, and industrialized production, but it was limited by the need for human handling of edge cases and design changes. In the AI era, AI agents can understand requirements, explore codebases, and autonomously write, test, and debug code based on human-defined specs. In 2026, StrongDM unveiled an autonomous software factory operating without human code writing or review. StrongDM calls this approach 'non-interactive development,' and community members have likened it to an industrial 'dark factory' where operations run fully automatically without human presence.
takeaways: The software factory concept originated in 1968, but legacy implementations could only achieve industrialized software production rather than autonomous code generation.
Modern AI agents can read specifications, inspect existing codebases, generate tailored code, and self-debug errors until tests pass with minimal human intervention.
In 2026, StrongDM introduced an automated software factory where humans neither write nor review code during the implementation process.
StrongDM terms this paradigm 'non-interactive development' because the AI executes tasks end-to-end without back-and-forth prompt interactions with human engineers.
The community compares this fully autonomous development model to an industrial 'dark factory' (lights-out factory) operating completely without humans.

sections.title: 規模化的迴圈
sections.summary: Loop engineering has emerged as a key approach to automating software factories with AI agents. Instead of direct manual prompting, developers construct loops—effectively while-loops with explicit termination and validation criteria such as test passage and style consistency. Industry implementations include Claude Code and StrongDM's open-source attractor project, which iteratively retries and corrects errors. Modern frontier models increasingly support tool use and extended execution, enabling agents to run uninterrupted for over 30 hours.
takeaways: Loop engineering focuses on designing continuous execution loops for AI agents instead of writing manual prompts.
Claude Code lead Boris Cherny stated that his primary role has shifted from prompting Claude to writing loops.
Effective agent loops require precisely defined termination conditions, such as passing new and regression tests and adhering to code style.
StrongDM's open-source 'attractor' project demonstrates a core execution loop that records errors and attempts self-correction in subsequent iterations.
Cursor's research highlights that modern frontier models can sustain autonomous agent execution for more than 30 hours.

sections.title: 軟體工廠真的如想像中美好嗎?
sections.summary: This section examines the practical challenges and criticisms of fully automated 'software factories' or 'lights-out factories' powered by AI agents. Critics point out that fully hands-off code generation often results in chaotic, hard-to-maintain codebases where tests may satisfy superficial criteria without meeting actual requirements. Notable engineer Dex from HumanLayer argued in an article that software factories fail in practice due to the massive human effort needed to untangle AI-generated code. Additionally, the token costs suggested by proponents like StrongDM can reach over $250,000 per engineer annually, challenging the cost-benefit balance despite the potential long-term value of working toward automation.
takeaways: Fully hands-off software development by AI agents introduces risks of producing messy, unmaintainable code that increases long-term maintenance costs.
If AI writes both the implementation and tests, automated testing may merely pass flawed logic without reflecting intended functionality.
Dex, the founder of HumanLayer, documented that his team spent weeks manually refactoring and untangling agent-generated code when issues arose.

StrongDM's target of consuming at least $1,000 in tokens per engineer equates to roughly $250,000 annually per engineer, equivalent to the salaries of multiple senior engineers in regions like Taiwan.
While 100% lights-out automated software factories may not be feasible today, reducing required human intervention remains a valuable objective.

sections.title: 閱讀更多
sections.summary: A major concern in the community regarding software factories is long-term maintainability and cost. Concrete approaches to lowering expenses and increasing maintainability when using AI agents were covered in the online course 'AI Coding 201 — From Practice to Best Practices'. The E+ membership deep-dive articles further explore recent community perspectives to help engineers move closer to full automation with AI agents. Additionally, many members participate by expensing the E+ membership via corporate educational training subsidies.
takeaways: Community concerns about software factories primarily focus on long-term maintainability and operational costs.
The online course 'AI Coding 201' shares practical methods to reduce costs and enhance maintainability when deploying AI agents.
E+ membership articles curate recent community insights aimed at achieving fully automated AI agent workflows.
E+ membership can be reimbursed via corporate education and training subsidies with standard tax invoices.

sections.title: 本期推薦
sections.summary: This curated selection features technical articles covering systems engineering, software design, and architecture challenges. Topics include Cursor's Git hosting architecture Origin and Cloudflare's optimization of 1.1.1.1's DNS cache to save 100 terabytes of memory. Other analyses explore organizational factors leading to poor code quality at large tech firms, the limitations of using PostgreSQL as a job queue, critiques of standard MVC patterns, ordering issues when choosing WebSockets versus SSE, and underlying behavioral differences between ECMAScript Modules and CommonJS in JavaScript.
takeaways: Cursor detailed 'Origin', an infrastructure designed to address the challenges of hosting Git repositories at scale and maintaining consistency.
Cloudflare saved approximately 100 terabytes of memory by redesigning the data structures in the 1.1.1.1 DNS cache.
Subpar code written at large tech companies often stems from systemic and organizational mechanisms rather than individual engineering ability.
Using PostgreSQL as a job queue can create severe performance bottlenecks under high concurrency due to lock contention and data cleanup overhead.
Evaluating WebSockets versus Server-Sent Events (SSE) should focus on event ordering and correctness rather than purely on ease of implementation or performance.
Differences between ECMAScript Modules (ESM) and CommonJS—especially around imported values, shared state, execution order, and circular dependencies—explain subtle JavaScript behavior issues.

The concept of software factories dates back to 1968, originally focusing on standardized environments, reusable components, and industrialized production, but it was limited by the need for human handling of edge cases and design changes. In the AI era, AI agents can understand requirements, explore codebases, and autonomously write, test, and debug code based on human-defined specs. In 2026, StrongDM unveiled an autonomous software factory operating without human code writing or review. StrongDM calls this approach 'non-interactive development,' and community members have likened it to an industrial 'dark factory' where operations run fully automatically without human presence. Loop engineering has emerged as a key approach to automating software factories with AI agents. Instead of direct manual prompting, developers construct loops—effectively while-loops with explicit termination and validation criteria such as test passage and style consistency. Industry implementations include Claude Code and StrongDM's open-source attractor project, which iteratively retries and corrects errors. Modern frontier models increasingly support tool use and extended execution, enabling agents to run uninterrupted for over 30 hours.

sections.title: ExplainThis 全端開發雙週報 #87 軟體工廠 (Software Factory) 是什麼? 有什麼限制?
sections.summary: 本期電子報介紹了 AI 驅動軟體開發的演進，從 2021 年的自動補全到 2026 年的高階 AI agents。隨著 AI agent 技術日益成熟，Harness Engineering、Loop Engineering 以及 Software Factory 等新興概念已成為社群討論的核心。本期探討了為何 Software Factory 的概念會在 AI 時代重新崛起、將其與傳統軟體工廠進行對比，並探討了當前的限制與潛在解決方案。
takeaways: AI coding 工具從 2021 年單純的自動補全，演進至 2025 與 2026 年複雜的 AI agents。
到了 2026 下半年，圍繞 AI agents 的討論催生了包括 Harness Engineering、Loop Engineering 與 Software Factory 在內的新概念。
儘管「Software Factory」並不是一個全新的名詞，但它在 AI 時代已被賦予了新的特性並重獲新生。
實作現代 AI 驅動的軟體工廠面臨著特定的限制，需要新的工程實踐來克服。

sections.title: 什麼是軟體工廠?
sections.summary: 軟體工廠的概念可追溯至 1968 年，最初著重於標準化環境、可重複使用的元件以及工業化生產，但其受限於仍需人類處理 edge cases 與設計變更。在 AI 時代，AI agents 可以理解需求、探索 codebase，並根據人類定義的 specs 自主編寫、測試與 debug 程式碼。2026 年，StrongDM 展示了一個無需人類編寫或審查程式碼即可運作的自主軟體工廠。StrongDM 將這種方法稱為「non-interactive development」，社群成員更將其比作工業上的「關燈工廠」（dark factory），即完全無人介入、全自動化運作。
takeaways: 軟體工廠概念起源於 1968 年，但舊有的實作只能實現工業化的軟體生產，而非自主的程式碼生成。
現代 AI agents 可以閱讀規格、檢視既有的 codebase、生成量身定製的程式碼，並在極少的人類介入下自行 debug 錯誤直到測試通過。
在 2026 年，StrongDM 推出了一個自動化軟體工廠，在實作過程中人類既不寫 code 也不 review code。
StrongDM 將這種範式稱為「non-interactive development」，因為 AI 端到端執行任務，而不需要與人類工程師進行來回的 prompt 互動。
社群將這種完全自主的開發模式比作完全不需要人類在場運作的工業「關燈工廠」（dark factory / lights-out factory）。

sections.title: 規模化的迴圈
sections.summary: Loop engineering 已成為使用 AI agents 自動化軟體工廠的關鍵方法。開發者不再直接進行手動 prompting，而是構建 loops——本質上是帶有明確終止條件與驗證標準（如測試通過與風格一致性）的 while-loops。業界實作包括 Claude Code 與 StrongDM 的開源 attractor 專案，它們會反覆重試並修正錯誤。現代 frontier models 越來越支援 tool use 與長時間執行，使 agents 能夠不間斷運行超過 30 小時。
takeaways: Loop engineering 專注於為 AI agents 設計持續執行的 loops，而非撰寫手動 prompts。
Claude Code 負責人 Boris Cherny 表示，他的主要角色已經從 prompt Claude 轉變為撰寫 loops。
高效率的 agent loops 需要明確定義的終止條件，例如通過全新與 regression tests，以及符合 code style。
StrongDM 的開源「attractor」專案展示了一個核心 execution loop，能記錄錯誤並在後續 iteration 中嘗試自我修正。
Cursor 的研究指出，現代 frontier models 能夠維持自主 agent 執行超過 30 小時。

sections.title: 軟體工廠真的如想像中美好嗎?
sections.summary: 本節探討由 AI agents 驅動的完全自動化「軟體工廠」或「關燈工廠」在實踐中的挑戰與批評。批評者指出，完全不插手的程式碼生成往往會導致混亂、難以維護的 codebase，其中的測試可能只滿足了表面條件，卻未達到實際需求。來自 HumanLayer 的知名工程師 Dex 在一篇文章中主張，軟體工廠在實踐中會失敗，原因是理清 AI 生成的程式碼需要耗費龐大的人力。此外，像 StrongDM 這樣的支持者所預估的 token 成本，每年每位工程師可能超過 250,000 美元，儘管邁向自動化具有潛在的長期價值，但這仍對成本效益的平衡帶來了挑戰。
takeaways: 由 AI agents 進行完全不插手的軟體開發，存在產出雜亂、難以維護的程式碼之風險，進而增加長期的維護成本。
若 AI 同時撰寫實作與測試，自動化測試可能只是驗證了有缺陷的邏輯，而無法反映出預期的功能。
HumanLayer 創辦人 Dex 記錄到，當問題出現時，他的團隊花了數週時間手動重構並釐清 agent 生成的程式碼。
StrongDM 設定每位工程師消耗至少 $1,000 token 的目標，相當於每位工程師每年約 $250,000，等同於台灣等地區多位 senior engineers 的薪資。
雖然 100% 全自動（lights-out）的軟體工廠目前可能還不可行，但減少所需的人工介入仍然是一個非常有價值的目標。

sections.title: 閱讀更多
sections.summary: 社群對軟體工廠的主要擔憂在於長期可維護性與成本。線上課程「AI Coding 201 — From Practice to Best Practices」涵蓋了使用 AI agents 時降低支出並提高可維護性的具體做法。E+ 會員深度探討文章進一步探討了近期社群的觀點，以協助工程師更邁向使用 AI agents 的全自動化。此外，許多會員透過企業教育訓練補助來報銷 E+ 會員費用。
takeaways: 社群對軟體工廠的擔憂主要集中在長期可維護性與營運成本。
線上課程「AI Coding 201」分享了部署 AI agents 時降低成本與提高可維護性的實用方法。
E+ 會員文章彙整了近期的社群見解，旨在實現全自動化的 AI agent 工作流程。
E+ 會員資格可透過公司教育訓練補助報銷，並提供標準統一發票。

sections.title: 本期推薦
sections.summary: 本期精選技術文章涵蓋系統工程、軟體設計與架構挑戰。主題包括 Cursor 的 Git 代管架構 Origin，以及 Cloudflare 對 1.1.1.1 DNS cache 的最佳化以節省 100 terabytes 的記憶體。其他分析則探討了導致大型科技公司程式碼品質不佳的組織因素、將 PostgreSQL 作為 job queue 的限制、對標準 MVC 模式的批判、在 WebSockets 與 SSE 之間選擇時的事件順序問題，以及 JavaScript 中 ECMAScript Modules 與 CommonJS 之間的底層行為差異。
takeaways: Cursor 詳細介紹了「Origin」，這是一套旨在解決大規模代管 Git repositories 並維持一致性挑戰的基礎架構。
Cloudflare 透過重新設計 1.1.1.1 DNS cache 中的資料結構，節省了約 100 terabytes 的記憶體。
大型科技公司產出的劣質程式碼，往往源自系統性與組織機制，而非個別工程師的能力問題。
在高併發情況下，將 PostgreSQL 作為 job queue 使用可能會因為 lock contention 與資料清理開銷而造成嚴重的效能瓶頸。
評估 WebSockets 與 Server-Sent Events (SSE) 時，應著重於事件順序（event ordering）與正確性，而非單純考量實作簡易度或效能。
ECMAScript Modules (ESM) 與 CommonJS 之間的差異——特別是圍繞在 imported values、shared state、執行順序以及 circular dependencies——解釋了 JavaScript 微妙的行為問題。

sections.title: Turn any PDF, image, DOCX, and PPTX into clean MD
sections.summary: Datalab Marker v2 is an open-source document parsing pipeline designed to convert PDFs, images, and office documents into clean Markdown, JSON, or HTML. It utilizes a shared inference server architecture to maximize GPU throughput by batching requests from multiple CPU workers, achieving up to 23.7 pages per second on a B200 GPU. The system is powered by Surya 2, a 650M parameter model that handles OCR, layout analysis, and table recognition across 90+ languages.
takeaways: Marker v2 achieves high throughput by using a shared Surya inference server that batches requests from multiple lightweight CPU workers.
The underlying Surya 2 model is a single 650M parameter model performing OCR, layout, reading order, and table recognition.
Three operational modes are available: balanced (high quality), fast (text-layer focused), and disable_ocr (CPU-only).
On the olmOCR-bench, Marker v2 scored 76.0%, outperforming MinerU (72.7%) and Docling (50.3%) while maintaining higher throughput.
Fast mode is significantly faster but less accurate for math-heavy documents as it relies on the PDF's native text layer.
The pipeline supports over 90 languages and handles complex elements like equations and low-confidence tables.

sections.title: Why KV cache stores K and V vectors but never Q?
sections.summary: LLMs operate autoregressively, where each new token is generated using only the last hidden state of the previous pass. In the attention mechanism, a query vector (Q) is used only once to compute the attention row for its specific position, whereas key (K) and value (V) vectors are reused in every subsequent decoding step. Because K and V vectors remain constant for a given token due to causal masking, they are stored in a KV cache to avoid redundant computations, while Q vectors are discarded after their single use.
takeaways: The prefill stage processes the entire prompt in parallel and is the primary contributor to Time to First Token (TTFT).
During decoding, only the query vector of the current token is required to compute the attention output for that step.
Key and value vectors are reused across all future decoding steps because causal masking prevents future tokens from affecting past K and V values.
Query vectors are position-specific and are never reused once the hidden state for that position is generated.
The KV cache is one of four common caching layers, alongside prefix caching, prompt caching, and semantic caching.

sections.title: Build the ultimate MCP Server for multimodal AI
sections.summary: This section provides a guide on building a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for multimodal AI applications. The architecture utilizes Pixeltable for infrastructure and data management across various modalities like video and audio, while CrewAI handles the orchestration of the agentic workflow. The system design features a router agent that directs queries to specialized agents to generate coherent responses based on the input modality.
takeaways: Pixeltable is an open-source Python library designed to streamline multimodal AI pipelines from storage to execution.
CrewAI is used to orchestrate the agentic workflow within the multimodal system.
The system architecture includes a router agent that identifies the modality of a user query and triggers a specialist agent.
Pixeltable supports multiple data types including images, videos, text, and audio.
The MCP server is built directly on top of the Pixeltable infrastructure.

sections.title: 為什麼 KV cache 只儲存 K 與 V 向量，卻從不儲存 Q？
sections.summary: LLM 以自迴歸（autoregressively）方式運作，每個新的 token 僅使用前一次 pass 的最後一個 hidden state 來生成。在 attention 機制中，query 向量 (Q) 僅會被使用一次來計算其特定位置的 attention row，而 key (K) 與 value (V) 向量則會在後續的每一個 decoding step 中被重複使用。由於 causal masking，特定 token 的 K 與 V 向量會保持不變，因此它們會被儲存在 KV cache 中以避免重複運算，而 Q 向量在單次使用後即被丟棄。
takeaways: prefill 階段會平行處理整個 prompt，且是影響 Time to First Token (TTFT) 的主要因素。
在 decoding 期間，只需要當前 token 的 query 向量即可計算該 step 的 attention 輸出。
Key 與 value 向量會在未來所有的 decoding step 中重複使用，因為 causal masking 會阻止未來的 token 影響過去的 K 和 V 值。
Query 向量具有位置特定性（position-specific），一旦該位置的 hidden state 生成後就絕不會再被重複使用。
KV cache 是四種常見 caching 層之一，另外三種為 prefix caching、prompt caching 與 semantic caching。

sections.summary: 本節提供為 multimodal AI 應用建置 Model Context Protocol (MCP) server 的指南。該架構利用 Pixeltable 處理跨影片與音訊等不同模態（modalities）的基礎架構與資料管理，並由 CrewAI 負責編排 agentic workflow。系統設計採用 router agent，將查詢導向專門的 agent，以根據輸入的模態生成連貫的回應。

系統架構包含一個 router agent，用於識別使用者查詢的模態並觸發專門的 agent。

sections.title: How to change an agent’s task while it’s still running:
sections.summary: Managing long-running AI agent tasks effectively requires moving the task state out of the prompt and into an explicit external structure. This approach allows for incremental updates where only specific subgraphs of a plan are invalidated when requirements change, rather than restarting the entire run. Apodex has implemented this architecture in their Apodex 1.1 models and FrontierAgent runtime, which supports parallel subagent coordination. Their PIVOT-RL method further optimizes this by allowing agents to resume from the last valid state in a trajectory during both training and execution.
takeaways: Externalizing task state from prompts enables agents to handle mid-run changes without discarding previous work.
Dependency tracking allows systems to mark only downstream artifacts as stale when a new requirement is introduced.
Apodex 1.1 is designed for complex analysis tasks involving file inspection, code execution, and automated error repair.
FrontierAgent provides an open-source runtime for sequential or parallel subagent coordination on macOS and Linux.
PIVOT-RL optimizes both training and runtime by restoring environment states and building shorter continuations from failure points.
Apodex 1.1 mini is a 35B open-weight model that can be deployed locally.

sections.title: Implementing Siamese Network with Contrastive Learning
sections.summary: This guide details the implementation of a Siamese Network using contrastive learning, a self-supervised technique for learning representations by comparing samples. The process involves creating a dataset of image pairs, passing them through a shared neural network, and using contrastive loss to optimize embedding distances. The text also highlights OpenAI's CLIP model as a prominent application of these principles in multimodal systems like Retrieval-Augmented Generation.
takeaways: Contrastive learning teaches models to distinguish between similar and dissimilar samples by comparing their embeddings.
A Siamese Network processes two inputs through the same network to generate embeddings in a shared representation space.
Contrastive loss minimizes the distance between embeddings of the same class and maximizes it for different classes.
CLIP (Contrastive Language–Image Pretraining) by OpenAI is a key multimodal model that uses contrastive learning for text and images.
The implementation uses PyTorch to create a custom SiameseDataset class for generating image pairs from the MNIST dataset.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems often utilize CLIP as a component for reasoning across different data modalities.

sections.title: Guardrails for AI Agents
sections.summary: Guardrails are essential components for AI agents that prevent issues like hallucinations, infinite loops, and unreliable outputs by validating task results. A guardrail is implemented as a function that checks output against specific criteria, returning a success status and either the validated result or an error message. When a guardrail fails, the agent can attempt to retry the task to correct the output before terminating. This concept is part of a broader framework for building robust agentic systems, which includes roles, tools, memory, and cooperation.
takeaways: Guardrails function as validation checkpoints that can limit tool usage and specify fallback mechanisms.
A guardrail function must return a boolean success value and either the validated output or an error message.
Agents can be configured to retry tasks multiple times when a guardrail validation fails.
Guardrails are identified as one of the six core pillars of great AI agents, alongside Role, Tools, Focus, Memory, and Cooperation.
The AI Agents crash course provides a 17-part curriculum covering everything from basic agentic systems to advanced patterns like ReAct and Planning.

items.summary: Managing long-running AI agent tasks effectively requires moving the task state out of the prompt and into an explicit external structure. This approach allows for incremental updates where only specific subgraphs of a plan are invalidated when requirements change, rather than restarting the entire run. Apodex has implemented this architecture in their Apodex 1.1 models and FrontierAgent runtime, which supports parallel subagent coordination. Their PIVOT-RL method further optimizes this by allowing agents to resume from the last valid state in a trajectory during both training and execution. This guide details the implementation of a Siamese Network using contrastive learning, a self-supervised technique for learning representations by comparing samples. The process involves creating a dataset of image pairs, passing them through a shared neural network, and using contrastive loss to optimize embedding distances. The text also highlights OpenAI's CLIP model as a prominent application of these principles in multimodal systems like Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Apodex 1.1 專為涉及檔案檢查、程式碼執行與自動化錯誤修復的複雜分析任務所設計。

sections.title: 使用 Contrastive Learning 實作 Siamese Network
sections.summary: 本指南詳細介紹了如何使用 contrastive learning 實作 Siamese Network。contrastive learning 是一種透過比較樣本來學習 representation 的 self-supervised 技術。該流程包含建立影像對（image pairs）資料集、將它們輸入共用的神經網路，並使用 contrastive loss 最佳化 embedding 之間的距離。本文還重點介紹了 OpenAI 的 CLIP 模型，作為這些原理在 Retrieval-Augmented Generation 等多模態系統中的代表性應用。
takeaways: Contrastive learning 透過比較樣本的 embedding，教導模型區分相似與不相似的樣本。
Siamese Network 透過相同的網路處理兩個輸入，以在共用的 representation space 中生成 embedding。
Contrastive loss 會最小化同類別 embedding 之間的距離，並最大化不同類別之間的距離。
OpenAI 的 CLIP (Contrastive Language–Image Pretraining) 是一個關鍵的多模態模型，它對文字與影像採用了 contrastive learning。
該實作使用 PyTorch 建立自訂的 SiameseDataset 類別，用以從 MNIST 資料集生成影像對。
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) 系統常利用 CLIP 作為跨不同資料模態進行推論的元件。

可將 Agents 設定為在 guardrail 驗證失敗時重試任務多次。

sections.title: Why per-user memory graphs break normal graph DBs
sections.summary: Traditional graph databases like Neo4j are designed for single large graphs, making them inefficient for agent memory workloads that require millions of small, per-user graphs. Zep developed Konig to solve this by implementing a tiered storage architecture that moves idle graphs to object storage while keeping active ones in RAM. This design allows for per-graph encryption, sub-200ms end-to-end latency, and inline execution of algorithms like PageRank. Konig also leverages AVX-512 search kernels and bi-temporal facts to optimize performance and data management.
takeaways: Traditional graph databases like Neo4j are optimized for single large graphs, whereas agent memory requires millions of small, isolated graphs.
Konig manages millions of graphs by using a tiered storage system involving RAM, local NVMe, and object storage.
Per-graph isolation in Konig allows for individual encryption keys and retention rules for each user or project.
Konig enables inline PageRank execution in milliseconds by limiting query scope to a single graph.
The system maintains sub-200ms end-to-end latency even when scaling from thousands to tens of millions of graphs.
Konig utilizes AVX-512 search kernels and supports bi-temporal facts for advanced data processing.

sections.title: KV vs Prefix vs Prompt vs Semantic Caching
sections.summary: The article distinguishes between four types of caching in LLM stacks: KV, Prefix, Prompt, and Semantic caching. While the first three are exact-match techniques that store attention tensors to optimize prefill and decoding performance, Semantic caching uses fuzzy-match embeddings to return stored responses. The text details how these caches impact memory bandwidth and cost, while also identifying common failure modes like dynamic prompt headers that invalidate cache blocks. Technical optimizations such as Grouped-query attention and FP8 quantization are highlighted as methods to manage the high memory requirements of these systems.
takeaways: KV caching stores key and value vectors to avoid recomputing the full sequence during decoding, shifting the bottleneck from compute to memory bandwidth.
Prefix caching, used by engines like vLLM, stores KV tensors in fixed-size blocks identified by hash chains to allow sharing across requests.
Prompt caching is a commercial version of prefix caching offered by providers like Anthropic and OpenAI with specific read/write pricing.
Semantic caching returns stored response strings based on embedding similarity, which can lead to incorrect answers if the similarity threshold is too low.
Dynamic content like timestamps or user IDs at the start of a prompt will invalidate all subsequent cache blocks.
Advanced architectures like Multi-head latent attention (MLA) in DeepSeek models compress KV caches into latent vectors to save space.

sections.title: What is Temperature in LLMs?
sections.summary: Temperature is a hyperparameter in Large Language Models (LLMs) that adjusts the probability distribution of the next-token prediction by modifying the softmax function. Low temperature values concentrate probability on the most likely tokens, making the model's output more deterministic and predictable. High temperature values spread the probability more evenly across the vocabulary, resulting in more diverse, creative, or potentially nonsensical responses.
takeaways: Temperature modifies the softmax function applied to logits to influence token sampling.
Low temperature values create a peaked distribution, leading to greedy and predictable token selection.
High temperature values create a more uniform distribution, resulting in stochastic and creative outputs.
Traditional classification models are typically deterministic, whereas LLMs rely on sampling from probabilities.
Excessive temperature values can degrade output quality into gibberish.

sections.summary: 像 Neo4j 這類傳統圖形資料庫是專為單一大型圖所設計，因此在處理需要數百萬個小型、per-user 圖的 agent memory 工作負載時效率不彰。Zep 開發了 Konig 來解決此問題，它實作了一種分層儲存架構，將閒置的圖移至 object storage，同時將活躍的圖保留在 RAM 中。此設計支援 per-graph 加密、低於 200ms 的 end-to-end 延遲，以及像 PageRank 這類演算法的 inline 執行。Konig 還利用 AVX-512 search kernels 和 bi-temporal facts 來最佳化效能與資料管理。
takeaways: 像 Neo4j 這類傳統圖形資料庫是針對單一大型圖進行最佳化，然而 agent memory 卻需要數百萬個小型且互相獨立的圖。
Konig 透過結合 RAM、本機 NVMe 與 object storage 的 tiered storage 系統來管理數百萬個 graph。
Konig 的 per-graph isolation 能為每個使用者或專案提供獨立的 encryption key 與 retention rule。
Konig 透過將 query scope 限制在單一 graph 內，實現毫秒級的 inline PageRank 執行。
即使從數千個 graph 擴展到數千萬個，該系統仍能維持 200ms 以下的 end-to-end latency。
Konig 利用 AVX-512 search kernel 並支援 bi-temporal fact，以進行進階資料處理。

sections.title: KV vs Prefix vs Prompt vs Semantic Caching
sections.summary: 本文區分了 LLM stack 中的四種 caching 類型：KV、Prefix、Prompt 與 Semantic caching。前三者是 exact-match 技術，透過儲存 attention tensor 來最佳化 prefill 與 decoding 效能；而 Semantic caching 則是利用 fuzzy-match embedding 來回傳已儲存的 response。文中詳細說明了這些 cache 如何影響 memory bandwidth 與成本，同時也指出常見的 failure mode，例如會使 cache block 失效的 dynamic prompt header。文中亦強調 Grouped-query attention 與 FP8 quantization 等技術最佳化手段，可作為管理這些系統龐大記憶體需求的方法。
takeaways: KV caching 儲存 key 與 value vector，以避免在 decoding 期間重新計算完整 sequence，從而將 bottleneck 從 compute 轉移到 memory bandwidth。
像 vLLM 這類 engine 所使用的 Prefix caching，會將 KV tensor 存放在由 hash chain 識別的固定大小 block 中，以實現在多個 request 之間共用。
Prompt caching 是由 Anthropic 與 OpenAI 等 provider 提供的 prefix caching 商業版本，具有特定的 read/write 定價。
Semantic caching 根據 embedding similarity 回傳已儲存的 response 字串，如果 similarity threshold 設得太低，可能會導致錯誤的答案。
在 prompt 開頭放置 timestamp 或 user ID 等 dynamic content，會使後續所有的 cache block 失效。
DeepSeek 模型中的 Multi-head latent attention (MLA) 等進階架構會將 KV cache 壓縮成 latent vector 以節省空間。

sections.title: 什麼是 LLM 中的 Temperature？
sections.summary: Temperature 是 Large Language Models (LLM) 中的一個 hyperparameter，透過修改 softmax 函數來調整 next-token prediction 的機率分佈。較低的 temperature 數值會將機率集中在最可能的 token 上，使模型的輸出更具確定性（deterministic）且更可預測。較高的 temperature 數值則會將機率更均勻地分散在 vocabulary 中，產生更多樣、更有創意或可能毫無意義的 response。
takeaways: Temperature 透過修改套用在 logit 上的 softmax 函數來影響 token sampling。
較低的 temperature 數值會產生尖銳的分佈，導致 greedy 且可預測的 token selection。
較高的 temperature 數值會產生更均勻的分佈，帶來更具 stochastic 與創意的輸出。
傳統的 classification model 通常是 deterministic 的，而 LLM 則依賴從機率中進行 sampling。
過高的 temperature 數值會使輸出品質退化為胡言亂語（gibberish）。

items.title: Background Work: From Cron Jobs to Distributed Systems

sections.title: Background Work: From Cron Jobs to Distributed Systems
sections.summary: Handling all processing tasks synchronously during a user request path can degrade user experience by causing noticeable delays. Background work addresses this problem by moving resource-intensive and secondary tasks, such as image manipulation and distribution, outside the active request flow. Tasks executed in the background can be triggered by user interactions, fixed clock intervals, system events, or batch processing demands. Although simple systems typically begin with a single scheduled script on one host, expanding workloads require more advanced distributed strategies.
takeaways: Executing tasks like image resizing and scanning in the synchronous request path causes poor user experience.
Moving non-critical operations to the background allows web applications to respond immediately after initially persisting data.
Background work can be initiated by user actions, scheduled times, third-party system events, or bulk processing efficiency requirements.
Teams commonly start managing background work with a single scheduled script on one machine before scaling to distributed systems.

items.title: Agentic AI Weekly | Berkeley RDI | August 26, 2026

sections.title: From Longer-Horizon Agents to Physical Intelligence
sections.summary: The focus of artificial intelligence is shifting from merely scaling model size toward creating systems capable of acting, learning, and adapting over long horizons in complex environments. Discussions spanning agentic foundational capabilities, robotics, and world models examine how autonomous systems can reliably operate on real-world data and act within the physical world. This evolution highlights a broader paradigm shift where scaling encompasses complete system capabilities rather than solely the underlying model.
takeaways: AI development is moving beyond scaling model parameters toward systems that learn and adapt across long time horizons.
Autonomous agents require capabilities to improve through experience and handle real-world data reliably.
A key objective is enabling agents to reason and perform physical actions through robotics and world models.
The next scaling paradigm focuses on moving beyond the individual model to entire systemic workflows.

sections.title: 1. Scaling Is Moving Beyond the Model
sections.summary: Recent AI progress has relied primarily on scaling compute, data, and model parameters, but researchers are increasingly shifting attention to optimizing the broader system surrounding the model. Industry experts argue that the next major advancements will stem from architectural components such as memory, context compression, evaluation, and tool integration. Additionally, enterprise deployment highlights the importance of proprietary, dynamic data that cannot be stored directly within model weights. Consequently, the focus is transitioning from standalone model scaling toward full-system optimization and agent-level engineering.
takeaways: Jerry Tworek predicts that architectural breakthroughs will drive AI gains over the next two years rather than raw model scaling alone.
Oriol Vinyals advocates for expanding model architecture to include memory, context compression, evaluation frameworks, tools, and agent scaffolding.
Weizhu Chen emphasizes optimizing surrounding infrastructure and systems before focusing directly on model optimization.
Dan Roth notes that real-world deployment in healthcare, finance, and government depends on dynamic, proprietary data that cannot reside solely in model weights.
Data governance, quality, and structure are identified as primary determinants of agentic AI capabilities.

sections.title: 2. Longer Autonomy Requires Stronger Evaluation and Resilience
sections.summary: As AI agents handle longer-horizon tasks, expanding their flexibility and tool access significantly increases their attack surface and operational risk. Addressing this requires an ecosystem-level approach to AI resilience, integrating automated red teaming, least-privilege architecture, and defense-in-depth from the start. Furthermore, rigorous evaluation is a prerequisite for recursive self-improvement, as autonomous systems cannot effectively improve without accurately measuring progress. Consequently, evaluation and resilience must be treated as foundational architecture rather than afterthoughts as autonomy scales.
takeaways: Granting AI agents greater flexibility and tool access expands their attack surface, requiring defenses like least-privilege design from the start.
According to Wojciech Zaremba, AI resilience has no single silver bullet and instead requires an ecosystem of standards, detection, and infrastructure analogous to fire safety.
Evaluation and ideation are core bottlenecks for recursive self-improvement because agents cannot improve without reliable performance metrics.
Scaling autonomy across longer horizons necessitates scaling evaluation frameworks and resilience mechanisms in tandem.

sections.title: 3. Physical AI Needs Its Own Scaling Laws
sections.summary: Physical AI requires scaling dynamics distinct from language models, as current robotics remains in an early, unpredictable phase. Leading researchers suggest that physical intelligence must scale through world-action models, multimodal reasoning, and egocentric video rather than narrow task specialization. Additionally, the field is transitioning from open-loop imitation learning toward closed-loop reinforcement learning and interactive world simulators.
takeaways: Jim Fan argues robotics lacks predictable scaling dynamics and remains stuck in the age of alchemy.
Proposed scaling axes for physical AI include world-action models, long-context memory, and large-scale egocentric video.
Sergey Levine advocates for robotic reasoning using high-level goal decomposition and images as intermediate thoughts.
Anastasis Germanidis highlighted interactive world models acting as learned simulators for counterfactual exploration.
Autonomous driving and robotics policies are shifting from open-loop imitation to closed-loop reinforcement learning and self-play.

sections.title: 4. The Real Frontier May Be the Learning Loop
sections.summary: The AI field is not converging on a single technical recipe, with unresolved debates spanning robotics, world models, and digital agents. Across both physical and digital domains, progress relies increasingly on iterative loops that connect action, observation, evaluation, and feedback. Ultimately, the next frontier of AI scaling may depend less on single model breakthroughs and more on building end-to-end systems capable of continuous learning from experience and environments.
takeaways: The AI field is not converging on a single unified methodology across robotics and digital agents.
Robotics research remains divided between video-based versus structured world representations, imitation learning versus reinforcement learning, and simulation versus real-world experience.
Effective digital agents require integrations of external memory, tool harnesses, evaluation frameworks, security guardrails, and automated experimentation loops.
Robotics extends the agent loop into the physical domain via: perceive, reason, act, observe outcome, learn, and try again.
Future AI scaling is shifting focus toward closed-loop continuous learning systems rather than individual model breakthroughs.

sections.title: The Bigger Picture
sections.summary: The AI frontier is moving beyond standalone models toward comprehensive systems, feedback loops, and environments that support autonomous agents and real-world interaction. In a featured discussion, Jeff Dean and Prof. Dawn Song reviewed milestones in AI development, such as mixture-of-experts and the natively multimodal design of Gemini. Looking ahead, Dean addressed the dual-use cybersecurity challenges posed by agentic systems and introduced Discovery Loop, a venture focused on accelerating scientific discovery through coordinated AI agents.
takeaways: System design—including learning environments, feedback loops, and safeguards—is becoming as crucial as underlying model capabilities for autonomous agents.
Jeff Dean reflected on foundational advancements in modern AI, notably mixture-of-experts architectures and designing Gemini as natively multimodal.
Increasing model autonomy and agency introduces dual-use risks, particularly within cybersecurity.
Jeff Dean's venture, Discovery Loop, aims to accelerate scientific discovery by decomposing problems, coordinating agents, and rapidly running experiments.

sections.title: Trends This Week
sections.summary: Enterprises are shifting focus from selecting single frontier models toward dynamic model routing to lower costs and maintain performance across tasks. Companies such as AT&T, Ramp, and Callosum are investing heavily in routing infrastructure, while Stripe has moved into the layer by agreeing to acquire model gateway OpenRouter. Meanwhile, AI capabilities and developer tooling continue expanding into adjacent workflows, exemplified by DeepSeek's new experimental visual-agent model and Cursor's release of its Origin code-hosting platform.
takeaways: AT&T routes approximately 40% of its internal AI queries to open models, achieving up to 56% cost reductions with only a ~2% performance drop.
Ramp routes over 2.75 trillion tokens per month via its internal model router, reducing LLM costs by roughly 30%.
Callosum raised $100 million to build infrastructure that dynamically matches workloads across different models and hardware chips.
Stripe agreed to acquire OpenRouter, an AI gateway routing over 10 trillion tokens daily across 400+ models from 80+ providers.
DeepSeek introduced V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, an experimental multimodal model tailored for visual-agent tasks at low inference costs.
Cursor launched Origin, an agent-native code-hosting platform featuring repositories, pull requests, and GitHub synchronization.

items.summary: The focus of artificial intelligence is shifting from merely scaling model size toward creating systems capable of acting, learning, and adapting over long horizons in complex environments. Discussions spanning agentic foundational capabilities, robotics, and world models examine how autonomous systems can reliably operate on real-world data and act within the physical world. This evolution highlights a broader paradigm shift where scaling encompasses complete system capabilities rather than solely the underlying model. Recent AI progress has relied primarily on scaling compute, data, and model parameters, but researchers are increasingly shifting attention to optimizing the broader system surrounding the model. Industry experts argue that the next major advancements will stem from architectural components such as memory, context compression, evaluation, and tool integration. Additionally, enterprise deployment highlights the importance of proprietary, dynamic data that cannot be stored directly within model weights. Consequently, the focus is transitioning from standalone model scaling toward full-system optimization and agent-level engineering. As AI agents handle longer-horizon tasks, expanding their flexibility and tool access significantly increases their attack surface and operational risk. Addressing this requires an ecosystem-level approach to AI resilience, integrating automated red teaming, least-privilege architecture, and defense-in-depth from the start. Furthermore, rigorous evaluation is a prerequisite for recursive self-improvement, as autonomous systems cannot effectively improve without accurately measuring progress. Consequently, evaluation and resilience must be treated as foundational architecture rather than afterthoughts as autonomy scales.

takeaways: Jerry Tworek 預測，未來兩年推動 AI 進展的將是架構上的突破，而非單純的 raw model scaling。

Weizhu Chen 強調在直接關注 model 優化之前，應先優化周圍的 infrastructure 與系統。

Data governance、quality 與 structure 被視為決定 agentic AI 能力的關鍵因素。

根據 Wojciech Zaremba 的說法，AI resilience 沒有單一的特效藥（silver bullet），而是需要一套類似消防安全的標準、偵測機制與 infrastructure 生態系。
Evaluation 與 ideation 是 recursive self-improvement 的核心瓶頸，因為缺乏可靠的 performance metrics，agents 便無法自我改進。
要在更長遠的 horizons 下 scaling autonomy，必須同步 scaling evaluation frameworks 與 resilience mechanisms。

針對 physical AI 所提出的 scaling axes 包括 world-action models、long-context memory 以及大規模的 egocentric video。
Sergey Levine 主張利用 high-level goal decomposition 以及將影像作為 intermediate thoughts 來進行 robotic reasoning。
Anastasis Germanidis 強調 interactive world models 可作為 learned simulators，用於 counterfactual exploration。
Autonomous driving 與 robotics policies 正在從 open-loop imitation 轉向 closed-loop reinforcement learning 與 self-play。

sections.title: 4. 真正的 Frontier 或許是 Learning Loop

takeaways: AI 領域在 robotics 與 digital agents 之間，並未收斂至單一且統一的 methodology。
Robotics 研究在以下面向依然存在分歧：video-based 對比 structured world representations、imitation learning 對比 reinforcement learning，以及 simulation 對比 real-world experience。
高效的 digital agents 需要整合 external memory、tool harnesses、evaluation frameworks、security guardrails 以及 automated experimentation loops。
Robotics 透過以下循環將 agent loop 延伸至實體領域：perceive、reason、act、observe outcome、learn，然後 try again。
未來的 AI scaling 重點正轉向 closed-loop continuous learning systems，而非個別 model 的突破。
