items.title: How to Make LLMs 3X Faster

sections.title: Autoregressive Decoding
sections.summary: Text generation in language models operates autoregressively, producing content one token at a time through sequential forward passes across all model layers. Because each new token strictly depends on the presence of all previous tokens, forward passes cannot be executed simultaneously without breaking coherence. Consequently, total generation duration equals the token count multiplied by the per-pass latency, which scales with model size. Modern inference systems mitigate the computational burden of subsequent passes by using a KV cache to store prior attention states, though the requirement for one pass per token remains.
takeaways: Text generation runs sequentially, computing a probability distribution and appending one token at a time.
A 500-token output necessitates 500 sequential forward passes because each token depends on the previous ones.
Total generation latency is determined by multiplying the number of generated tokens by the duration of a single forward pass.
Per-token cost is uniform regardless of whether the output is text or code, but increases on larger models running on identical hardware.
A KV cache stores attention states for previously processed tokens, reducing per-pass workload without eliminating the pass-per-token requirement.

sections.title: Memory Bandwidth
sections.summary: During model inference, a forward pass spends the majority of its execution time moving data rather than computing arithmetic. In token generation, model weights must be transferred from VRAM to compute units for each single token, resulting in low compute utilization between 20 and 40 percent while the memory bus runs near capacity. In contrast, prompt processing achieves 90 to 95 percent utilization because weights are reused across thousands of input tokens. Consequently, increasing memory bandwidth accelerates token generation significantly more than adding raw compute capacity.
takeaways: A single forward pass spends most of its duration moving data from memory rather than executing arithmetic.
For a 70-billion-parameter model at 16-bit precision, approximately 140 GB of weights must be transferred per generated token.
Compute utilization falls from 90-95% during prompt processing to 20-40% during token generation.
Prompt processing applies loaded weights across thousands of tokens at once, while token generation reloads weights for a single token.
GPU memory bandwidth is a more significant driver of token generation speed than raw compute capability.

sections.title: Parallel Verification
sections.summary: Transformers can evaluate an entire sequence simultaneously in a single forward pass, generating a next-token prediction for every position at once. Causal masking within the attention mechanism ensures each position only attends to preceding tokens, maintaining the validity of autoregressive conditioning. Consequently, candidate tokens can be verified in parallel during a single pass rather than sequentially, mirroring the computational efficiency of prompt processing.
takeaways: A Transformer evaluates all sequence positions simultaneously within a single forward pass, generating a next-token prediction at each position.
Causal masking inside the attention mechanism prevents positions from attending to subsequent tokens, preserving identical conditioning to sequential generation.
Prompt processing exploits this parallel forward pass to process thousands of tokens in one pass instead of one token at a time.
Candidate tokens can be verified simultaneously by appending them to the context and running a single forward pass.
Verification and generation perform identical computational work per position, but parallel verification saves cost by grouping evaluations into one pass.

sections.title: Draft and Verify
sections.summary: The draft and verify framework accelerates language model inference by combining a small draft model with a large target model. In each round, the draft model serially generates a sequence of candidate tokens, which the target model verifies simultaneously in a single forward pass. Tokens are accepted sequentially until the first mismatch, at which point the target model's already-computed prediction is retained as an additional correct token. This setup bounds the worst-case throughput to that of standard single-token decoding while offering significant speedups with draft lengths typically set between 3 and 5.
takeaways: The inference loop relies on two models: a primary target model and a draft model that has 10 to 20 times fewer parameters and typically shares the same tokenizer.
Each round executes in three steps: serial drafting of K tokens, single-pass batched evaluation by the target model, and left-to-right verification.
Matching tokens are retained, and the target model's prediction at the first mismatch position is accepted at no extra computation cost.
In the worst case where all candidate tokens are rejected, the system still outputs one correct token, matching the baseline output of standard decoding.
Draft length K is commonly tuned between 3 and 5 to balance potential speedups against the diminishing probability of later tokens being accepted.

sections.title: Lossless Guarantee
sections.summary: Speculative decoding generates text with the exact same statistical properties as the target model operating independently, enforced via an acceptance rule. In greedy decoding, candidate tokens are accepted only if they match the target model's top prediction. When sampling with randomness, candidate acceptance depends on the probability distribution comparison between the target and draft models, with rejected tokens resampled from an adjusted distribution. The resulting token probabilities depend strictly on the target model, with deviations occurring only due to inherent sampling variance or numerical precision limits.
takeaways: Speculative decoding preserves the target model's exact output distribution through an acceptance rule.
Under greedy decoding, a candidate token is retained only if it equals the target model's highest-probability choice.
Under sampling, a candidate is always accepted if the target model assigns it equal or higher probability than the draft model, and probabilistically accepted if lower.
Rejected candidates are replaced by sampling from an adjusted distribution that subtracts the draft model's probabilities, ensuring mathematical equivalence to the target model.
Outputs can still differ between runs due to inherent sampling randomness and hardware-level floating-point rounding limits.

sections.title: Acceptance Rate
sections.summary: In candidate-token acceleration approaches, the speedup is primarily dictated by the acceptance rate, which represents the fraction of proposed tokens preserved by the target model. Repetitive or structured tasks like code generation and summarization yield high acceptance rates, whereas open-ended tasks like creative writing result in frequent model divergence and lower acceptance. Higher sampling temperatures lower acceptance further by flattening output probability distributions, with the process becoming inefficient when acceptance drops below roughly 50 percent. Demonstrating this in practice, DeepSeek documented an 80 to 90 percent acceptance rate for the second predicted token during production serving of DeepSeek-V3, which yielded roughly 1.8x generation throughput.
takeaways: Acceptance rate is the fraction of candidate tokens kept by the target model, while acceptance length includes confirmed tokens plus one trailing free token.
Structured and repetitive workloads (such as code generation, summarization, and retrieval-augmented answers) yield high acceptance rates.
Open-ended outputs (such as creative writing and conversation) yield low acceptance rates due to small model divergence.
Higher sampling temperature flattens token probability distributions and decreases acceptance.
Acceptance rates below approximately 50% result in the computational overhead exceeding the efficiency gains.
DeepSeek achieved 80% to 90% acceptance on the second predicted token in production serving of DeepSeek-V3, reaching roughly 1.8x generation throughput.

sections.title: Candidate or Draft Sources
sections.summary: Speculative drafting relies on four primary mechanisms to obtain fast, low-cost token predictions: deploying a separate smaller sibling model, adding multi-token prediction heads to the target architecture, executing a lower-precision or pruned variant of the same weights, or retrieving matching sequences from prior context. Each option introduces distinct trade-offs between hardware overhead, training requirements, implementation complexity, and contextual applicability. Tokenizer alignment strictly dictates draft compatibility, often presenting a higher barrier than model quality differences. Ultimately, all four drafting strategies necessitate sufficient spare compute capacity during serving to provide a net speedup.
takeaways: Using a separate smaller model requires an identical tokenizer and family, consuming server VRAM from the KV cache budget.
Lightweight extra prediction heads can be trained alongside the base model during pretraining and repurposed for inference drafting, as seen in DeepSeek-V3.
QuantSpec executes draft generation using 4-bit weights and a 4-bit KV cache, yielding speedups above 1.78x with acceptance rates exceeding 90 percent.
Context-based text searching requires zero memory overhead and provides 2x to 4x acceleration on repetitive tasks such as document editing and summarization.
A draft model cannot be paired with a target model having a different vocabulary unless additional translation machinery is implemented.

sections.title: Concurrency Limits
sections.summary: The speedup provided by speculative decoding depends significantly on server load and operating concurrency. As concurrent requests increase, compute units approach saturation and verification must compete with incoming requests, causing latency gains to diminish and potentially fall below baseline throughput. Serving systems such as vLLM manage this tradeoff by dynamically reducing draft length or disabling speculation beyond certain batch sizes. Additionally, because the technique targets token generation rather than prompt evaluation, it offers minimal latency benefits for workloads characterized by long prompts and short outputs.
takeaways: Speculative decoding gains diminish as server load increases and compute capacity becomes saturated.
Empirical evaluations on a 70B model showed acceleration dropping from 1.96x at batch size 1 down to 1.21x at batch size 128, with potential net throughput losses under heavy concurrency.
vLLM allows users to configure batch size thresholds to dynamically reduce draft length or disable speculation entirely.
Time to first token remains unchanged by speculative decoding, limiting its utility for long-prompt, short-completion workloads.
DeepSeek observed that multi-token prediction slightly reduces throughput while noticeably improving end-to-end generation latency.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: Speculative decoding reorganizes the timing of token generation rather than reducing the total work executed by the target model. It leverages the transformer architecture's ability to evaluate multiple candidate tokens in parallel for roughly the cost of a single token. When drafted tokens are rejected, the verification pass still produces a correct token at the point of mismatch, preventing wasted computation. Consequently, baseline output quality is maintained by design through the acceptance rule without additional tuning.
takeaways: Token generation is memory-bandwidth bound because reading model weights dominates over arithmetic execution.
Transformers can evaluate multiple candidate tokens in a single parallel pass for approximately the same cost as evaluating one.
Draft rejections truncate rather than waste compute because the verification step yields a valid token at the mismatch position.
Output quality is preserved directly by the acceptance rule without requiring tuning.
Performance speedups depend on output predictability, server spare compute capacity, and draft generation costs.

sections.title: Autoregressive Decoding
sections.summary: 語言模型中的文字生成是以 autoregressive 方式運作，透過跨所有模型層的循序 forward pass，一次生成一個 token。由於每個新 token 都嚴格依賴所有先前 token 的存在，因此 forward pass 無法在不破壞連貫性的情況下同時執行。因此，總生成時間等於 token 數量乘以每次 pass 的 latency，而這會隨著模型大小而增加。現代 inference 系統透過使用 KV cache 儲存先前的 attention states 來減輕後續 pass 的運算負擔，但每個 token 需要一次 pass 的要求仍然存在。
takeaways: 文字生成是循序執行的，計算機率分佈並一次附加一個 token。
一個 500 個 token 的輸出需要 500 次循序的 forward pass，因為每個 token 都依賴先前的 token。
總生成 latency 是由生成的 token 數量乘以單次 forward pass 的時間所決定。
無論輸出是文字還是程式碼，每個 token 的成本都是一致的，但在相同硬體上運行較大的模型時成本會增加。
KV cache 儲存先前已處理 token 的 attention states，能減少每次 pass 的工作負載，但無法免除每個 token 需執行一次 pass 的要求。

sections.title: Memory Bandwidth
sections.summary: 在模型 inference 期間，forward pass 將大部分執行時間花在搬移資料而非算術運算上。在 token generation 過程中，每個單一 token 都必須將模型權重從 VRAM 傳輸到 compute units，導致 compute utilization 偏低（介於 20% 到 40% 之間），而 memory bus 則幾乎滿載運作。相較之下，prompt processing 可達到 90% 到 95% 的 utilization，因為權重會在數千個輸入 token 之間被重複使用。因此，提高 memory bandwidth 對加速 token generation 的效果，顯著大於單純增加 raw compute capacity。
takeaways: 單次 forward pass 的大部分時間都花在從記憶體搬移資料，而非執行算術運算。
對於 16-bit 精度的 700 億參數模型，每生成一個 token 大約必須傳輸 140 GB 的權重。
Compute utilization 從 prompt processing 期間的 90-95% 下降到 token generation 期間的 20-40%。
Prompt processing 會一次將載入的權重套用在數千個 token 上，而 token generation 則是為了單一 token 重新載入權重。
相較於 raw compute capability，GPU memory bandwidth 是影響 token generation 速度更為關鍵的因素。

sections.title: Parallel Verification
sections.summary: Transformers 可以在單次 forward pass 中同時評估整個 sequence，一次為每個 position 生成 next-token prediction。attention mechanism 中的 causal masking 能確保每個 position 僅 attend 至先前的 token，維持 autoregressive conditioning 的有效性。因此，candidate token 可以在單次 pass 中平行驗證，而非循序處理，這與 prompt processing 的運算效率如出一轍。
takeaways: Transformer 在單次 forward pass 中同時評估所有 sequence position，並在每個 position 生成 next-token prediction。
attention mechanism 內部的 causal masking 可防止各 position attend 到後續的 token，保有與 sequential generation 完全相同的 conditioning。
Prompt processing 利用這種平行 forward pass 在單次 pass 中處理數千個 token，而非一次僅處理一個 token。
將 candidate token 接在 context 之後並執行單次 forward pass，即可同時對其進行驗證。
Verification 與 generation 在每個 position 上執行的運算量相同，但 parallel verification 透過將多次評估整合至單次 pass 中來節省成本。

sections.title: Draft and Verify
sections.summary: Draft and verify 架構透過結合小型 draft model 與大型 target model 來加速語言模型 inference。在每個 round 中，draft model 會循序生成一系列 candidate token，接著 target model 會在單次 forward pass 中同時驗證這些 token。Token 會依序被接受，直到出現第一個 mismatch 為止，此時 target model 已經計算出的 prediction 會被保留作為額外的正確 token。此設定將最差情況下的 throughput 限制在標準 single-token decoding 的水準，同時在 draft length 通常設為 3 到 5 時帶來顯著的 speedup。
takeaways: 此 inference loop 依賴兩個模型：主要 target model，以及參數量少 10 到 20 倍且通常共享同一個 tokenizer 的 draft model。
每個 round 包含三個執行步驟：循序 draft 出 K 個 token、由 target model 進行單次 pass 的 batched evaluation，以及由左至右（left-to-right）的 verification。
吻合的 token 會被保留，且在無需額外運算成本的情況下，第一個 mismatch 位置處的 target model prediction 也會被接受。
在所有 candidate token 皆被拒絕的最差情況下，系統仍會輸出一個正確的 token，與標準 decoding 的 baseline 產出相同。
Draft length K 通常調整在 3 到 5 之間，以在潛在 speedup 與後續 token 被接受機率遞減之間取得平衡。

sections.title: Lossless Guarantee
sections.summary: Speculative decoding 透過 acceptance rule 來確保生成的文本具有與 target model 獨立運作時完全相同的統計特性。在 greedy decoding 中，只有當 candidate token 與 target model 的 top prediction 吻合時才會被接受。當採用帶有隨機性的 sampling 時，candidate 的接受與否取決於 target model 與 draft model 之間的機率分佈比較，被拒絕的 token 則會從調整後的分佈（adjusted distribution）中重新 sampling。最終產生的 token 機率嚴格依賴於 target model，僅會因為固有的 sampling variance 或數值精度限制（numerical precision limits）而產生偏差。
takeaways: Speculative decoding 透過 acceptance rule 來保留 target model 精確的 output distribution。
在 greedy decoding 下，只有當 candidate token 等同於 target model 機率最高的選擇時，才會被保留。
在 sampling 下，若 target model 分配給 candidate 的機率大於或等於 draft model，則該 candidate 一律被接受；若機率較低，則依機率接受。
被拒絕的 candidate 會透過從扣除 draft model 機率後的 adjusted distribution 中 sampling 來取代，從而確保與 target model 在數學上的等價性。
由於固有的 sampling 隨機性以及硬體層級的浮點數捨入限制（floating-point rounding limits），不同 run 之間的輸出仍可能存在差異。

sections.title: Acceptance Rate
sections.summary: 在 candidate-token 加速方法中，speedup 主要取決於 acceptance rate，它代表 target model 保留 proposed token 的比例。具重複性或結構化的任務（如 code generation 與 summarization）具有較高的 acceptance rate，而開放式任務（如 creative writing）則常導致模型 divergence 以及較低的 acceptance。較高的 sampling temperature 會透過拉平 output probability distribution 進一步降低 acceptance，當 acceptance 降至約 50% 以下時，該流程的效率便會顯著下降。在實際應用中，DeepSeek 記錄了在 DeepSeek-V3 的 production serving 期間，第二個預測 token 的 acceptance rate 達到 80% 至 90%，帶來約 1.8x 的 generation throughput。
takeaways: Acceptance rate 是 target model 所保留 candidate token 的比例，而 acceptance length 則包含確認的 token 加上一個隨附的 trailing free token。
結構化與重複性的 workload（例如 code generation、summarization 與 retrieval-augmented answers）能帶來高 acceptance rate。
開放式輸出（例如創意寫作與對話）會因小型模型的 divergence 而導致較低的 acceptance rate。
較高的 sampling temperature 會使 token 機率分佈平坦化，並降低 acceptance。
當 acceptance rate 低於約 50% 時，計算 overhead 將會超過效率收益。
DeepSeek 在 DeepSeek-V3 的 production serving 中，第二個預測 token 達到了 80% 至 90% 的 acceptance，實現約 1.8 倍的 generation throughput。

sections.title: Candidate 或 Draft 來源
sections.summary: Speculative drafting 依賴四種主要機制來獲取快速、低成本的 token 預測：部署獨立的小型 sibling model、在 target architecture 中加入 multi-token prediction heads、執行相同權重的低精度（lower-precision）或 pruned 變體，或從先前 context 中檢索匹配的 sequence。每種選項在硬體 overhead、訓練需求、實作複雜度以及 context 適用性之間都有不同的 trade-off。Tokenizer 的 alignment 嚴格決定了 draft 的相容性，其門檻往往高於模型品質的差異。歸根結底，這四種 drafting 策略在 serving 期間都需要足夠的 spare compute capacity 才能帶來淨加速（net speedup）。
takeaways: 使用獨立的 smaller model 需要相同的 tokenizer 與 family，並會佔用伺服器原本可用於 KV cache budget 的 VRAM。
輕量級的額外 prediction heads 可以在 pretraining 期間與 base model 一同訓練，並轉用於 inference drafting，如 DeepSeek-V3 所示。
QuantSpec 使用 4-bit 權重與 4-bit KV cache 執行 draft generation，在 acceptance rate 超過 90% 的情況下實現了 1.78 倍以上的加速。
基於 context 的文字搜尋不需要任何 memory overhead，並在文件編輯與摘要等重複性任務中提供 2 倍至 4 倍的加速。
除非實作額外的 translation 機制，否則 draft model 無法與 vocabulary 不同的 target model 配對。

sections.title: Concurrency 限制
sections.summary: Speculative decoding 帶來的加速幅度高度取決於伺服器負載與運行的 concurrency。隨著並行請求增加，運算單元趨於飽和，verification 必須與傳入的請求競爭資源，導致 latency 的改善減少，甚至可能低於 baseline throughput。如 vLLM 等 serving 系統透過在超過特定 batch size 時動態縮短 draft length 或直接停用 speculation 來平衡這項 trade-off。此外，由於該技術針對的是 token generation 而非 prompt evaluation，因此對於長 prompt、短 output 特徵的 workload 而言，能帶來的 latency 效益非常有限。
takeaways: 隨著伺服器負載增加且運算容量趨於飽和，speculative decoding 的效益會逐漸遞減。
在 70B 模型上的實證評估顯示，加速效果從 batch size 為 1 時的 1.96 倍下降至 batch size 為 128 時的 1.21 倍，且在高 concurrency 下可能導致淨 throughput 損失。
vLLM 允許使用者設定 batch size 門檻值，以動態縮短 draft length 或完全停用 speculation。
Time to first token (TTFT) 不會因 speculative decoding 而改變，因而限制了它在長 prompt、短 completion workload 中的實用性。
DeepSeek 觀察到 multi-token prediction 會略微降低 throughput，但能顯著改善 end-to-end 的 generation latency。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: Speculative decoding 重新調整了 token generation 的時序，而非減少 target model 執行的總運算量。它利用了 Transformer 架構能以大約評估單一 token 的成本來平行評估多個 candidate tokens 的能力。當 drafted tokens 被拒絕時，verification 階段仍會在 mismatch 的位置產出一個正確的 token，避免運算浪費。因此，透過 acceptance rule 在設計上就能維持 baseline 的輸出品質，無需額外的 tuning。
takeaways: Token generation 屬於 memory-bandwidth bound，因為讀取模型權重佔據的主導地位遠高於算術運算的執行。
Transformers 可以在單次平行 pass 中評估多個 candidate tokens，其成本與評估單個 token 大致相同。
Draft 被拒絕時會被截斷（truncate）而非浪費運算資源，因為 verification 步驟會在 mismatch 位置產出一個有效的 token。
透過 acceptance rule 直接保留輸出品質，無需進行 tuning。
效能加速取決於輸出的可預測性、伺服器的 spare compute capacity 以及 draft generation 的成本。

items.title: [Hands-on] Turn Scientific Figures Into Structured Data with Mistral OCR

sections.title: Anthropic did something you’ll regret ignoring
sections.summary: Anthropic's research into multi-agent systems revealed that splitting tasks among specialized roles often leads to excessive coordination costs and information degradation, a phenomenon termed the 'telephone game.' While OpenAI and Google have introduced SDKs to manage agent handoffs through pre-defined wiring, these methods struggle with dynamic, unforeseen workflows. Flint AI's Switch platform addresses this by placing agents and humans in shared communication channels, ensuring persistent context and ad-hoc collaboration. This approach reduces redundant work and provides the entire team with visibility into agent activities and results.
takeaways: Anthropic found that agents can spend more tokens on coordination than on the actual task when roles are split.
The 'telephone game' effect causes information to degrade as it is handed off between specialized agents.
OpenAI's Agents SDK and Google's ADK use design-time wiring for agent handoffs, which requires pre-defined routing.
Switch by Flint AI allows for dynamic routing by placing agents and humans in the same chat channel.
Shared channels prevent agents from recomputing work by providing access to the full history of previous sessions.
Switch supports integration with major platforms like Slack, Teams, and Discord, and is compatible with frameworks like Claude Code and OpenAI Codex.
Using a shared channel ensures that negative results or 'no regression' findings are visible to the entire team immediately.

sections.title: Turn scientific figures into structured data w/ Mistral OCR
sections.summary: This workflow automates the extraction of structured data from scientific figures, which are often ignored by traditional PDF parsers. By using Mistral OCRv4, the system captures layout, text, and embedded images in a single pass, preserving the context of charts and legends. A secondary multimodal agent powered by Mistral Small 4 then analyzes the visual content to interpret trends and quantitative data. This approach reduces the time required to review papers from weeks to hours while ensuring all findings are searchable and consistent.
takeaways: Traditional PDF parsers often fail to extract data from figures because they prioritize the text layer over visual elements.
Mistral OCRv4 performs a layout-aware pass that returns text, images, and structured metadata in a single API call.
The workflow separates extraction from analysis to prevent OCR errors from compounding during the reasoning phase.
Mistral Small 4 acts as a multimodal agent to interpret axis labels, legends, and plotted data within extracted images.
CrewAI is used to orchestrate the pipeline, including validation, deduplication, and batching of figures.
The system can process a paper in approximately 26.6 seconds, compared to 36 minutes for manual review.
Mistral OCRv4 supports self-hosted deployments for organizations requiring high data privacy for proprietary research.

sections.title: 使用 Mistral OCR 將科學圖表轉換為 structured data

items.title: How to Steal an AI Model’s Private Thoughts

sections.title: Reasoning Traces
sections.summary: Modern frontier models produce an extended internal sequence of text prior to outputting a visible response, allowing them to explore hypotheses and correct errors. This internal sequence is referred to as a reasoning trace or chain of thought. Unlike the final polished output, the reasoning trace holds raw tool outputs, intermediate exploration, and any sensitive contextual data processed during the session. For instance, when a coding agent is instructed to purge hardcoded credentials, those credentials inevitably pass through the reasoning trace.
takeaways: Frontier models generate extended internal text sequences before producing a final answer.
A reasoning trace is also known as a chain of thought.
Reasoning traces capture intermediate hypotheses, abandoned paths, and raw tool outputs.
Reasoning traces are denser and more revealing than final outputs, often holding contextual secrets or user data.
Tasks such as removing credentials cause sensitive data to be exposed within the reasoning trace.

sections.title: Concealment Rationale
sections.summary: Model providers conceal reasoning traces primarily for commercial and safety-related reasons. Commercially, competitors can harvest traces from a capable model to extract its methodology and train cheaper imitation models. From a safety standpoint, models often generate intermediate reasoning about harmful subjects prior to issuing a refusal. Because safety filtering is applied after trace generation to produce the final response, releasing raw traces bypasses these guardrails and exposes harmful material to users.
takeaways: Model providers hide reasoning traces due to commercial competition and safety concerns.
Exposing reasoning traces reveals the methodology behind computations, allowing competitors to train cheaper imitation models.
Models frequently generate reasoning about harmful topics during the process of formulating a refusal.
Safety filtering operates downstream on completed traces to generate safe visible answers.
Publishing reasoning traces circumvents post-generation safety filters, potentially exposing users to harmful content.

sections.title: State Management
sections.summary: In multi-turn conversations, earlier reasoning traces must remain accessible across requests despite model APIs being fundamentally stateless. Providers face two architectures: storing traces on the server referenced by session identifiers, or encrypting traces and delegating storage back to the client. Leading providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google chose the client-side encrypted approach. This architecture satisfies confidentiality and integrity while eliminating the infrastructure cost of server-side trace storage.
takeaways: Model APIs are inherently stateless, meaning conversation continuity must be explicitly reconstructed with each request.
Server-side state storage tracks conversation traces in a database using identifiers, which is straightforward but expensive at global scale.
Client-side state storage encrypts the trace and returns it to the client, requiring the provider to store nothing between turns.
OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google all use the client-side encrypted trace approach.
The client-side encrypted approach achieves confidentiality against competitors, integrity against trace tampering, and cost savings via statelessness.

sections.title: Envelope Structure
sections.summary: The payload block returned to clients is formatted as a base64-encoded AEAD (Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data) envelope that provides both encryption and tamper protection. The envelope consists of a header with metadata like model name and version, along with a nonce, authentication tag, and ciphertext. Different providers name this container differently, such as Anthropic using signature, OpenAI using encrypted_content, and Google using thinkingSignature. Notably, authentication covers the model name and version but omits account and conversation identifiers, with observed behavior suggesting providers use a single global key across an ecosystem.
takeaways: Blocks returned to clients are base64-encoded AEAD envelopes that conceal content while ensuring tamper-protection.
The envelope contains a header (e.g., model name, block type, version, key ID), a nonce, an authentication tag, and ciphertext.
The payload field is named 'signature' by Anthropic, 'encrypted_content' by OpenAI, and 'thinkingSignature' by Google.
Authentication covers the model name and version, but excludes user account and conversation identifiers.
Observable behavior suggests providers use a single global key across their entire ecosystem.

sections.title: Trace Compatibility
sections.summary: Researchers analyzed block compatibility when authenticated fields lack origin information, identifying three progressively permissive forms: cross-session, cross-user, and cross-model compatibility. Cross-model compatibility allows for dynamic tasks like mid-conversation model switching and automatic rerouting. An evaluation conducted in July 2026 across various model combinations revealed differing levels of support across major AI models. While Gemini accepted all combinations across generations and Claude accepted nearly all combinations except Fable 5, GPT's compatibility was generation-dependent, with GPT-5.6 accepting blocks from older generations.
takeaways: Block compatibility is categorized into three levels: cross-session, cross-user, and cross-model compatibility.
Cross-session compatibility allows replaying blocks out of order, modifying conversation history, and trimming sessions to context limits.
Cross-model compatibility permits blocks from one model to be accepted by another, enabling mid-conversation model switching and rerouting.
Gemini accepted every tested block combination across every generation in tests from July 2026.
Claude accepted almost all combinations, but Fable 5 blocks were only accepted by Fable 5 itself.
The GPT-5.6 series accepted blocks from all earlier GPT generations, while older GPT models only accepted their own blocks.

sections.title: Extraction Method
sections.summary: Flagship AI models undergo anti-distillation training to conceal their reasoning, but smaller models within the same family receive significantly less protection due to cost and speed optimizations. Researchers leveraged this cross-model compatibility gap by extracting encrypted reasoning blocks from flagship models and prompting smaller models to transcribe them into plaintext. The fidelity of the recovered reasoning was verified by matching re-encoded token counts against exact reasoning token counts in API billing records. Extraction difficulty differed between providers, requiring a single prompt for Claude while GPT required chunking and dozens of candidate extractions.
takeaways: Flagship models receive anti-distillation training that smaller, cost-optimized models in the same family largely lack.
Reasoning traces from strong models can be recovered by feeding their reasoning blocks into weaker sibling models acting as fuzzy decoders.
The flagship model's refusal training is bypassed because it is only queried with an ordinary question that generates a benign output.
Billing records reporting exact reasoning token counts were used across 120 programming tasks to verify reconstruction faithfulness.
Claude models required only a single prompt for extraction, whereas GPT models required chunked outputs and up to 50 attempts per block to evade verbatim reproduction filters.

sections.title: Attack Vectors
sections.summary: The research outlines four distinct attack vectors arising from hidden or encrypted model reasoning traces, categorized by whether the blocks are created by attackers or third parties. Attackers can use reasoning traces to enhance model distillation and bypass visible safety guards through jailbreaking hidden reasoning. Furthermore, third-party agent logs shared on platforms like GitHub and Hugging Face routinely leak un-sanitized secrets including API keys and passwords. Finally, attackers can plant malicious instructions inside encrypted blocks of shared agent trajectories to execute prompt injection attacks upon session resumption.
takeaways: Distillation leveraging reasoning traces raised MATH500 accuracy from 68.4 percent to 76.0 percent compared to answer-only training.
Decoding 10,000 reasoning traces costs roughly $720 at Claude Haiku 4.5 pricing.
Jailbreaking models via traces is viable because models are rarely trained to constrain harmful reasoning, allowing sensitive details to stay hidden inside traces while visible outputs appear benign.
An analysis of 6,708 public trajectories across GitHub and Hugging Face revealed 1,028 leaking blocks containing 62 API keys, 33 passwords, and 24 access tokens.
Encrypted blocks in resumed agent runs facilitate prompt injection, demonstrated by tricking GPT-5.6 Sol into exfiltrating PowerPoint files.

sections.title: Field Observations
sections.summary: Recovering reasoning traces at scale reveals that returned summaries can diverge substantially from actual internal model reasoning. In an example from an AIME 2025 problem, an API summary claimed methodical geometric derivation, whereas the underlying trace showed memory recall and trial-and-error backward justification. Additionally, recovered GPT traces typically consist of compressed, ungrammatical telegraphic notes rather than fluent English. This lack of legibility creates significant hurdles for trace monitoring and AI oversight.
takeaways: API-generated summaries sometimes diverge from the actual reasoning path observed in recovered traces.
On an AIME 2025 problem, the summary reported methodical geometry steps using the law of cosines, while the trace showed post-hoc rationalization from memory.
Smaller models tasked with summarizing larger models inherently compress and filter the original thought process.
Recovered GPT reasoning traces often consist of telegraphic, ungrammatical notes with dropped articles.
Trace monitoring and oversight mechanisms are challenged when internal traces lack legibility.

sections.title: Proposed Mitigations
sections.summary: The research paper establishes that security issues arise because reasoning block envelopes authenticate content but neglect context. Cross-user replay can be cheaply mitigated without server-side storage by embedding an account identifier directly into the authenticated data at issuance. To secure cross-session contexts without breaking portability features like conversation forking or turn compaction, the authors propose a hash chain paired with a Merkle tree. For existing blocks signed without context, rotating cryptographic keys is the primary retroactive fix, alongside API gateway model version verification and refusal training.
takeaways: Reasoning block envelopes authenticate content but do not authenticate the context in which a block was produced or replayed.
Cross-user replay attacks can be prevented without server-side storage by embedding account identifiers into authenticated issuance data.
Binding blocks to complete transcripts would break legitimate features like forking conversations, compacting history, and model downgrades.
A combination of hash chains and Merkle trees enables session binding and ordering integrity while allowing pruned histories.
Addressing previously published blocks requires key rotation, which unavoidably invalidates legitimate continuations of older sessions.
Supplemental mitigations include server-side storage, model version verification at API gateways, and training models to refuse transcription requests.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: The security issues discussed do not stem from a failure of cryptographic techniques, but rather from a lack of binding between an encrypted block and the context that generated it. A displayed answer summary is distinct from the underlying trace and can diverge from it, while sanitization cannot safely clean uninspectable encrypted blocks without removing them completely. Furthermore, the overall security of a model family is dictated by its least protected model, meaning anti-distillation safeguards on flagship models are undermined if cheaper sibling models accept the same blocks.
takeaways: Cryptographic envelopes functioned properly, but lacked authenticated binding between blocks and their generating context.
A summary displayed next to an answer is an independent artifact from the trace it describes, allowing the two to diverge.
Session log sanitization only affects plaintext, requiring encrypted blocks to be eliminated entirely since they cannot be inspected.
A model family's security depends on its least protected member, reducing the efficacy of flagship anti-distillation training if cheaper sibling models accept identical blocks.

items.summary: Modern frontier models produce an extended internal sequence of text prior to outputting a visible response, allowing them to explore hypotheses and correct errors. This internal sequence is referred to as a reasoning trace or chain of thought. Unlike the final polished output, the reasoning trace holds raw tool outputs, intermediate exploration, and any sensitive contextual data processed during the session. For instance, when a coding agent is instructed to purge hardcoded credentials, those credentials inevitably pass through the reasoning trace. Model providers conceal reasoning traces primarily for commercial and safety-related reasons. Commercially, competitors can harvest traces from a capable model to extract its methodology and train cheaper imitation models. From a safety standpoint, models often generate intermediate reasoning about harmful subjects prior to issuing a refusal. Because safety filtering is applied after trace generation to produce the final response, releasing raw traces bypasses these guardrails and exposes harmful material to users. In multi-turn conversations, earlier reasoning traces must remain accessible across requests despite model APIs being fundamentally stateless. Providers face two architectures: storing traces on the server referenced by session identifiers, or encrypting traces and delegating storage back to the client. Leading providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google chose the client-side encrypted approach. This architecture satisfies confidentiality and integrity while eliminating the infrastructure cost of server-side trace storage.

sections.title: Reasoning Traces
sections.summary: 現代 frontier models 在輸出可見的回應之前，會先生成一段長篇的內部文字 sequence，讓它們能探索假設並修正錯誤。這個內部 sequence 被稱為 reasoning trace 或 chain of thought。與最終修飾過的回應不同，reasoning trace 包含未經處理的 tool outputs、中間探索過程，以及在 session 期間處理的任何敏感 context 資料。例如，當 coding agent 被指示清除 hardcoded credentials 時，這些 credentials 必然會經過 reasoning trace。
takeaways: Frontier models 在產出最終答案之前，會先生成長篇的內部文字 sequences。
Reasoning trace 也被稱為 chain of thought。
Reasoning traces 會擷取中間假設、放棄的路徑以及未經處理的 tool outputs。
Reasoning traces 比最終輸出更密集且透露更多資訊，通常包含 context 中的機密或使用者資料。
移除 credentials 等任務會導致敏感資料暴露在 reasoning trace 之中。

sections.title: 隱藏理由
sections.summary: Model providers 隱藏 reasoning traces 主要是出於商業和安全性考量。在商業層面上，競爭對手可以從高能力模型中蒐集 traces 來提取其 methodology，並訓練出成本更低的 imitation models。從安全角度來看，模型在提出拒絕回應（refusal）之前，通常會先生成有關有害主題的中間推理。因為 safety filtering 是在 trace 生成之後才應用以產生最終回應，釋出未加工的 traces 會繞過這些 guardrails 並向使用者暴露有害內容。
takeaways: Model providers 基於商業競爭與安全考量而隱藏 reasoning traces。
公開 reasoning traces 會揭露運算背後的 methodology，讓競爭對手得以訓練出成本更低的 imitation models。
模型在組織拒絕回應（refusal）的過程中，經常會生成關於有害主題的推理。
Safety filtering 是在完成的 traces 下游運作，以產出安全的可見回應。
發布 reasoning traces 會繞過 generation 後的 safety filters，可能使使用者接觸到有害內容。

sections.title: 狀態管理
sections.summary: 在 multi-turn conversations 中，儘管 model APIs 本質上是 stateless 的，但先前的 reasoning traces 仍必須能在多次 requests 間被存取。Providers 面臨兩種架構選擇：將 traces 存儲在 server 端並以 session identifiers 引用，或是加密 traces 並將存儲委派回 client 端。包含 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 在內的頂尖 providers 都選擇了 client-side encrypted 方案。該架構在滿足 confidentiality 與 integrity 的同時，消除了 server 端存儲 trace 的 infrastructure cost。
takeaways: Model APIs 本質上是 stateless 的，這意味著 conversation 的連續性必須在每次 request 中被明確地重構。
Server-side state storage 使用 identifiers 在 database 中追蹤 conversation traces，這種做法直截了當，但在 global scale 下成本高昂。
Client-side state storage 會加密 trace 並將其返回給 client 端，使 provider 在各 turn 之間無需存儲任何內容。
OpenAI、Anthropic 與 Google 都採用 client-side encrypted trace 的做法。
Client-side encrypted 方案對競品實現了 confidentiality、防止 trace 被篡改的 integrity，並透過 statelessness 節省成本。

sections.title: Envelope Structure
sections.summary: 返回給 client 端的 payload block 被格式化為 base64-encoded AEAD (Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data) envelope，同時提供 encryption 與 tamper protection。該 envelope 包含帶有 model name 和 version 等 metadata 的 header，以及 nonce、authentication tag 與 ciphertext。不同 providers 對此 container 的命名各不相同，例如 Anthropic 使用 signature，OpenAI 使用 encrypted_content，而 Google 則使用 thinkingSignature。值得注意的是，authentication 涵蓋了 model name 與 version，但省略了 account 和 conversation identifiers，觀察到的行為顯示 providers 在整個 ecosystem 中使用單一 global key。
takeaways: 返回給 client 端的 blocks 是 base64-encoded AEAD envelopes，在隱匿內容的同時確保 tamper-protection。
Envelope 包含 header（例如 model name、block type、version、key ID）、nonce、authentication tag 以及 ciphertext。
該 payload 欄位在 Anthropic 被命名為 'signature'，在 OpenAI 被命名為 'encrypted_content'，在 Google 則被命名為 'thinkingSignature'。
Authentication 涵蓋了 model name 與 version，但排除了 user account 和 conversation identifiers。
可觀察到的行為顯示 providers 在其整個 ecosystem 中使用單一 global key。

sections.title: Trace Compatibility
sections.summary: 研究人員分析了當 authenticated fields 缺乏來源資訊時的 block compatibility，並歸納出三種寬鬆程度遞增的形式：cross-session、cross-user 與 cross-model compatibility。Cross-model compatibility 支援動態任務，例如 mid-conversation model switching 與 automatic rerouting。2026 年 7 月針對多種 model 組合進行的一項評估顯示，各大主流 AI models 的支援程度各不相同。Gemini 接受跨世代的所有組合，Claude 接受了除 Fable 5 之外的幾乎所有組合，而 GPT 的相容性則取決於世代，其中 GPT-5.6 可以接受來自舊世代的 blocks。
takeaways: Block compatibility 被分為三個層級：cross-session、cross-user 以及 cross-model compatibility。
Cross-session compatibility 允許亂序 replay blocks、修改 conversation history，以及將 sessions 裁切至 context limits。
Cross-model compatibility 允許一個 model 的 blocks 被另一個 model 接受，從而實現 mid-conversation model switching 與 rerouting。
在 2026 年 7 月的測試中，Gemini 接受了跨各世代所有被測試的 block 組合。
Claude 接受了幾乎所有組合，但 Fable 5 的 blocks 僅能被 Fable 5 本身接受。
GPT-5.6 系列接受所有早期 GPT 世代的 blocks，而較舊的 GPT models 僅接受自身的 blocks。

sections.title: Extraction Method
sections.summary: 旗艦級 AI models 會經過 anti-distillation training 以隱藏其 reasoning，但同家族中較小的 models 由於 cost 和 speed 的最佳化，獲得的保護顯著較少。研究人員利用了這種 cross-model compatibility 的落差，從旗艦 models 中擷取加密的 reasoning blocks，並 prompt 較小的 models 將其轉譯為 plaintext。透過將 re-encoded token 數量與 API billing records 中的精確 reasoning token 數量進行比對，驗證了復原 reasoning 的 fidelity。不同 providers 的 extraction 難度有所不同：Claude 只需要單一 prompt，而 GPT 則需要 chunking 以及數十次 candidate extractions。
takeaways: 旗艦 models 接受了 anti-distillation training，而同家族中較小、經過 cost-optimized 的 models 則大多缺乏這種訓練。
強大 models 的 reasoning traces 可以透過將其 reasoning blocks 餵給扮演 fuzzy decoders 的較弱 sibling models 來復原。
旗艦模型的 refusal training 被繞過，因為它只被詢問了一個會產生良性輸出的普通問題。
利用 120 個程式設計任務中回報確切 reasoning token 數量的計費記錄，來驗證 reconstruction faithfulness。
Claude 模型僅需單一 prompt 即可完成擷取，而 GPT 模型則需要 chunked outputs 以及每個 block 最多 50 次嘗試，以規避 verbatim reproduction filters。

sections.title: 攻擊向量
sections.summary: 該研究概述了源於隱藏或加密的 model reasoning traces 的四種不同攻擊向量，依據 blocks 是由攻擊者還是第三方建立來分類。攻擊者可以利用 reasoning traces 來增強 model distillation，並透過對隱藏 reasoning 進行 jailbreaking 來繞過可見的 safety guards。此外，在 GitHub 和 Hugging Face 等平台上共享的第三方 agent logs 經常外洩未經清理的機密資訊，包括 API keys 和密碼。最後，攻擊者可以在共享 agent trajectories 的加密 blocks 中植入惡意指令，以便在 session resumption 時執行 prompt injection 攻擊。
takeaways: 相較於僅使用答案的 training，利用 reasoning traces 進行 distillation 將 MATH500 的準確率從 68.4% 提升至 76.0%。
以 Claude Haiku 4.5 的定價計算，解碼 10,000 個 reasoning traces 的成本約為 $720 美元。
透過 traces 對模型進行 jailbreaking 是可行的，因為模型鮮少接受限制有害推理的訓練，這使得敏感細節可以隱藏在 traces 內部，而可見的輸出則顯得毫無危害。
對 GitHub 和 Hugging Face 上 6,708 個公開 trajectories 的分析顯示，有 1,028 個洩漏的 blocks，其中包含 62 個 API keys、33 個密碼和 24 個 access tokens。
在恢復執行的 agent runs 中，加密的 blocks 會助長 prompt injection，這已透過誘騙 GPT-5.6 Sol 外洩 PowerPoint 檔案得到證實。

sections.title: 實地觀察
sections.summary: 大規模復原 reasoning traces 顯示，回傳的摘要可能與模型實際內部的 reasoning 有實質上的分歧。在一個 AIME 2025 題目的範例中，API 摘要聲稱進行了有條理的幾何推導，而底層的 trace 卻顯示出記憶回想以及試錯反推的辯護過程（trial-and-error backward justification）。此外，復原的 GPT traces 通常由壓縮、不合語法的電報式筆記組成，而非流暢的英文。這種缺乏可讀性的狀況，對 trace monitoring 和 AI oversight 造成了重大障礙。
takeaways: API 生成的摘要有時會與復原的 traces 中觀察到的實際 reasoning path 產生分歧。
在一個 AIME 2025 的題目中，摘要回報了使用餘弦定理的有條理幾何步驟，而 trace 卻顯示是來自記憶的事後合理化（post-hoc rationalization）。
負責總結較大模型的較小模型，本質上會壓縮並過濾原始的思考過程。
復原的 GPT reasoning traces 通常由省略冠詞、不合語法的電報式筆記所組成。
當內部 traces 缺乏可讀性時，trace monitoring 和 oversight 機制將面臨挑戰。

sections.title: 建議的緩解措施
sections.summary: 該研究論文指出，安全問題的產生是因為 reasoning block envelopes 驗證了內容，卻忽略了 context。透過在發行時直接將帳戶識別碼嵌入已驗證的資料中，即可在不需要 server-side storage 的情況下以低成本緩解 cross-user replay。為了在不破壞 conversation forking 或 turn compaction 等可攜性功能的前提下保護跨 session contexts，作者提出了 hash chain 搭配 Merkle tree 的方案。對於未包含 context 簽署的現有 blocks，key rotation 是主要的追溯修復手段，同時輔以 API gateway 的 model version 驗證和 refusal training。
takeaways: Reasoning block envelopes 驗證了內容，但並未驗證該 block 產生或被重放時的 context。
透過將帳戶識別碼嵌入已驗證的簽發資料中，無需 server-side storage 即可防止 cross-user replay 攻擊。
將 blocks 與完整的 transcripts 綁定，會破壞如 forking conversations、compacting history 和 model downgrades 等合法功能。
結合 hash chains 與 Merkle trees 可以在允許 pruned histories 的同時，實現 session binding 與順序完整性（ordering integrity）。
處理先前已發布的 blocks 需要進行 key rotation，這不可避免地會使舊 session 的合法延續失效。
補充的緩解措施包括 server-side storage、在 API gateways 進行 model version 驗證，以及訓練模型拒絕 transcription 請求。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: 這裡討論的安全問題並非源自密碼學技術的漏洞，而是因為 encrypted block 與生成它的 context 之間缺乏 binding。顯示的回答摘要與底層的 trace 是各自獨立的 artifact，兩者可能會產生分歧；同時，sanitization 無法在不完全移除不可檢視的 encrypted blocks 的情況下安全地清理資料。此外，整個 model family 的安全性取決於其防護最薄弱的模型，這意味著若較便宜的 sibling models 接受相同的 blocks，旗艦模型上的 anti-distillation 防護機制就會被削弱。
takeaways: Cryptographic envelopes 運作正常，但 blocks 與其生成 context 之間缺乏 authenticated binding。
顯示在回答旁邊的 summary 與它所描述的 trace 是彼此獨立的 artifact，因此兩者可能會產生分歧。
Session log 的 sanitization 僅對 plaintext 有效，由於 encrypted blocks 無法被檢視，因此必須將其完全剔除。
一個 model family 的安全性取決於其防護最薄弱的成員；若較便宜的 sibling models 接受相同的 blocks，旗艦模型的 anti-distillation 訓練成效便會大打折扣。

items.title: Build a Multi-Agent GTM Intelligence System

sections.title: Build a multi-agent GTM intelligence system
sections.summary: Brendan Short identifies that effective GTM re-engagement should be driven by specific company triggers rather than arbitrary calendar dates. The challenge lies in the fragmentation of data, where leadership changes and news announcements reside in separate records, requiring agents to scrape and parse multiple sources. Seltz solves this by providing structured people and news records in single API calls, enabling a three-agent pipeline to identify signals, enrich profiles, and generate personalized outreach efficiently.
takeaways: GTM timing should be based on company changes like new leadership or funding rounds rather than fixed nine-month intervals.
Standard search APIs return snippets that require agents to perform expensive fetch and parse steps to extract useful data.
Seltz provides structured records for people and news, allowing data joins to happen in a single pass without reassembling fragments.
The multi-agent pipeline consists of a Signal Hunter, a People Enricher, and an Outreach Strategist orchestrated via CrewAI.
The system utilizes the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to connect agents directly to the Seltz retrieval tool.
Seltz excels at director-level data and recent news, while open web search is recommended for initial high-level executive discovery.

sections.title: 5 context compaction strategies for LLM agents
sections.summary: Context compaction for LLM agents aims to manage finite context windows but can inadvertently increase costs by breaking prefix caching. While standard caching rewards stable prefixes, compaction edits the history, forcing expensive cache writes instead of cheap cache reads. Five main strategies exist: truncation, rolling summarization, prompt compression, RAG-based retrieval, and KV cache eviction. Tools like LMCache address these inefficiencies by enabling non-sequential cache reuse across different serving frameworks.
takeaways: Prefix caching significantly reduces costs by matching identical leading spans of text, with providers like Anthropic offering up to 90% discounts.
Compacting context by summarizing or editing history invalidates the cache, leading to higher cache write costs (1.25x base rate) compared to cache reads (0.1x base rate).
Truncation is the simplest compaction method but results in permanent information loss of early decisions.
Prompt compression tools like LLMLingua and LLMLingua-2 use smaller models or encoders to remove low-relevance tokens with minimal accuracy loss.
KV cache eviction manages GPU memory by dropping or offloading tensors rather than deleting text, allowing for recomputation or retrieval from slower storage.
LMCache is an open-source layer that enables cache reuse at any prompt position via CacheBlend, supporting vLLM, SGLang, and Dynamo.

sections.title: Scale models to billions of parameters
sections.summary: Lightning Fabric is a library designed to bridge the gap between the flexibility of raw PyTorch and the distributed training features of PyTorch Lightning. It allows developers to scale models to billions of parameters by making only four minor changes to existing PyTorch code, such as replacing manual device placement and loss backward calls. The tool supports advanced strategies like FSDP and DeepSpeed while maintaining control over manual training loops.
takeaways: Lightning Fabric combines PyTorch's flexibility with PyTorch Lightning's distributed training capabilities.
Scaling to billion-parameter models requires only four minor code modifications.
Fabric automates device placement, eliminating the need for manual .to() and .cuda() calls.
The library supports state-of-the-art distributed strategies including DDP, FSDP, and DeepSpeed.
Fabric is compatible with various hardware accelerators including Apple Silicon, CUDA GPUs, and TPUs.
Users can build custom training abstractions for checkpointing and logging using Fabric as a foundation.

sections.title: 建構 multi-agent GTM 情報系統
sections.summary: Brendan Short 指出，有效的 GTM 重新接觸應由特定的公司觸發事件驅動，而非隨意的行事曆日期。挑戰在於資料的破碎化，領導層異動與新聞公告分散在不同記錄中，需要 agents 爬取並解析多個來源。Seltz 透過在單次 API 呼叫中提供結構化的個人與新聞記錄來解決此問題，使三 agent pipeline 能高效識別訊號、豐富 profile 並生成個人化聯繫內容。
takeaways: GTM 的時機應基於公司變動（如新領導層上任或新一輪募資），而非固定的九個月間隔。
標準搜尋 API 回傳的 snippets 需要 agents 執行昂貴的 fetch 和 parse 步驟才能擷取有用資料。
Seltz 提供結構化的個人與新聞記錄，讓 data joins 可以在單次處理中完成，無需重新拼湊碎片化資訊。
這個 multi-agent pipeline 由 Signal Hunter、People Enricher 與 Outreach Strategist 組成，並透過 CrewAI 進行協同編排。
該系統利用 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 將 agents 直接連接到 Seltz 檢索工具。
Seltz 在 director 層級的資料和近期新聞方面表現出色，而 open web search 則建議用於初期的高階主管探索。

sections.title: LLM agents 的 5 種 context compaction 策略
sections.summary: LLM agents 的 context compaction 旨在管理有限的 context windows，但可能會因破壞 prefix caching 而無意中增加成本。標準 caching 偏好穩定的 prefix，而 compaction 卻修改了歷史紀錄，迫使系統進行昂貴的 cache writes 而非低廉的 cache reads。目前主要有五種策略：truncation、rolling summarization、prompt compression、RAG-based retrieval 與 KV cache eviction。像 LMCache 這類工具透過在不同的 serving frameworks 間實現非循序的 cache 重用，解決了這些低效問題。
takeaways: Prefix caching 透過比對開頭相同的一段文字大幅降低成本，如 Anthropic 等供應商提供了高達 90% 的折扣。
透過摘要或編輯歷史紀錄來進行 context compaction 會使快取失效，導致更高的 cache write 成本（基礎費率的 1.25 倍），相比之下 cache read 僅需基礎費率的 0.1 倍。
Truncation 是最簡單的 compaction 方法，但會導致早期決策資訊的永久遺失。
像 LLMLingua 和 LLMLingua-2 這類 prompt compression 工具使用較小的模型或 encoder，以極小的準確度損失移除關聯度較低的 tokens。
KV cache eviction 透過丟棄（dropping）或卸載（offloading）tensors 而非刪除文字來管理 GPU 記憶體，允許日後重新計算或從較慢的儲存空間中取回。
LMCache 是一個開源層，透過 CacheBlend 實現任何 prompt 位置的 cache 重用，並支援 vLLM、SGLang 和 Dynamo。

sections.title: 將模型規模擴展至數十億個參數
sections.summary: Lightning Fabric 是一個旨在彌合原生 PyTorch 的靈活性與 PyTorch Lightning 的分散式訓練功能之間差距的函式庫。它讓開發者只需對現有 PyTorch 程式碼進行四處微調（例如替換手動 device placement 與 loss backward 呼叫），就能將模型擴展到數十億個參數。該工具支援 FSDP 和 DeepSpeed 等進階策略，同時保留對手動 training loop 的控制權。
takeaways: Lightning Fabric 結合了 PyTorch 的靈活性與 PyTorch Lightning 的分散式訓練能力。
擴展到數十億參數的模型僅需四處微小的程式碼修改。
Fabric 自動化了 device placement，不再需要手動呼叫 .to() 和 .cuda()。
該函式庫支援最先進的分散式策略，包括 DDP、FSDP 和 DeepSpeed。
Fabric 相容於各種硬體加速器，包括 Apple Silicon、CUDA GPU 和 TPU。
使用者可以以 Fabric 為基礎，建構用於 checkpointing 和 logging 的客製化訓練抽象層。

items.title: Why Code Verification Matters More Than Ever in the Age of AI

sections.title: The Shift
sections.summary: Recent empirical studies reveal that while AI coding tools increase code production, they can negatively impact development efficiency and delivery stability. Research from Google's DORA shows that higher AI adoption correlates with lower delivery stability and lingering developer distrust. Furthermore, a controlled trial by METR found experienced developers took 19 percent longer to complete tasks using AI tools due to prompting, reviewing, and error correction. Consequently, the bottleneck in software development is increasingly shifting toward downstream code verification.
takeaways: Google's DORA research found that software delivery stability dropped as teams adopted more AI.
More than one-third of developers reported having little confidence in AI-generated code.
A controlled trial by research group METR showed AI-assisted tasks took 19 percent longer than unassisted tasks among experienced developers.
Developers in the METR trial initially anticipated a 25 percent speedup and mistakenly felt more productive despite taking longer.
Additional development time with AI was consumed by prompting, waiting, reading outputs, and fixing errors.
Increased AI-driven code generation creates a growing burden on downstream code verification.

sections.title: Earning Trust
sections.summary: Code verification is the comprehensive set of checks ensuring code is correct, safe, and maintainable before production deployment. Trust in software is established incrementally through progressive evaluations rather than granted in a single step. While high-risk domains like flight-control systems and kernels employ mathematically rigorous formal verification, most software relies on layered, lighter checks to balance cost and safety.
takeaways: Code verification serves as an umbrella term for checks validating code correctness, safety, and maintainability.
Trust in code is earned incrementally through layered evaluations rather than all at once.
Formal verification involves mathematically proving that code matches a precise specification.
Critical domains like flight-control systems and operating system kernels rely on formal verification to prevent defects that could risk lives.
Most standard software relies on lighter, layered checks because formal verification is often cost-prohibitive.

sections.title: The Filter Stack
sections.summary: Code verification can be structured as an ordered stack of filters where each layer addresses distinct failure modes and covers the blind spots of preceding checks. Fast, low-cost static verification tools like type checkers and linters run first to catch type mismatches and syntax or style issues. Below static analysis, unit tests execute code against known inputs to detect behavioral and computational errors that pass type checking. Further down, human code reviews evaluate system architecture, readability, and adherence to team guidelines, while production monitoring observes live traffic to flag any remaining issues before or during release.
takeaways: Type checkers verify data types before code execution to prevent a wide class of runtime errors.
Linters inspect code for suspicious patterns and violations of stylistic standards.
Unit tests detect behavioral flaws that type checkers and linters cannot catch, such as incorrect arithmetic operations.
Human code review identifies system-fit, readability, and policy violations that automated tooling overlooks.
Production monitoring acts as the final verification layer by tracking real-world traffic and detecting unhandled issues.
Filter layers are arranged in sequence so that each subsequent check covers the specific weaknesses of the layer above it.

sections.title: Static And Dynamic Analysis
sections.summary: Code verification filters are categorized into static analysis and dynamic analysis. Static analysis inspects source code without execution, enabling rapid, comprehensive scans across an entire codebase using tools such as type checkers and linters, though it risks false alarms due to unobserved runtime conditions. Dynamic analysis executes code using real inputs to observe actual behavior, exemplified by tests, but is strictly constrained by the specific execution paths exercised. Consequently, even a clean static scan paired with a passing test suite can leave defect gaps, necessitating multiple complementary verification filters.
takeaways: Static analysis inspects code without executing it, enabling fast, full-codebase scans in a single pass.
Linters and type checkers are examples of static analysis filters.
Static analysis can produce false alarms because runtime behavior remains partially invisible.
Dynamic analysis runs code with real inputs to observe actual execution behavior.
Dynamic analysis is limited to tested paths and can miss crashes if edge cases like empty inputs are omitted.
Combining static scans and test suites can still leave gaps, requiring layered verification filters.

sections.title: False Alarms
sections.summary: Code verification inherently involves a fundamental tradeoff between false positives and false negatives. Overly sensitive tools generate frequent false alarms, which erode developer trust and cause teams to ignore valid warnings or deactivate the tools entirely. Andrea from Sonar frames this challenge as a CAP theorem for code verification, where teams must balance competing priorities of speed, accuracy, and coverage. Consequently, effective verification pipelines prioritize actionable findings and signal quality over sheer coverage to keep developers engaged.
takeaways: Code verification requires balancing false positives (flagging benign code) against false negatives (missing actual bugs).
High rates of false alarms erode developer trust, often leading engineers to ignore warnings or disable static analysis tools altogether.
Andrea from Sonar likens code verification tradeoffs to the CAP theorem, with speed, accuracy, and coverage serving as competing priorities where no tool can maximize all three.
Sonar's team adheres to the principle that a finding is only worth raising if a developer can directly act upon it.
The positioning of a filter within a verification pipeline alters the practical cost of verification errors.

sections.title: The Pipeline
sections.summary: The lifecycle of a change request forms a pipeline starting in a developer's editor and progressing through commit checks, review, merge, deployment, and live monitoring. Verification checks become increasingly expensive the later they run because downstream work accumulates on top of flaws. The concept of 'shift left' describes moving these checks earlier in the pipeline so issues are resolved while they are still cheap to fix. Although precise marketing claims regarding cost multipliers warrant skepticism, the general direction of shifting checks earlier remains sound and cost-effective.
takeaways: A code change progresses through a pipeline spanning the editor, automated commit checks, review, merge, deployment, and live monitoring.
The cost of fixing a defect rises the later it is discovered in the pipeline.
Flaws caught in production can cause incidents, rollbacks, and adverse user impact compared to minor developer effort in the editor.
'Shift left' denotes moving automated and manual checks earlier in the delivery lifecycle to detect problems affordably.
Vendor claims of exact cost multipliers per stage should be viewed with skepticism, but the directional benefit of early testing holds true.

sections.title: AI Pressure
sections.summary: The traditional software review stack was designed under the assumption that humans author most code, but the rise of AI coding tools has undermined this premise. These tools introduce significant pressure through unprecedented code volume and larger batch sizes, often resulting in rubber-stamped reviews of massive pull requests. Furthermore, AI models frequently generate code containing known security flaws, observed in roughly 45 percent of tested cases, without matching improvements in security safeguards. Consequently, while functional correctness has advanced, the gap between working code and secure code continues to widen alongside rising duplication and falling reuse.
takeaways: AI coding tools dramatically increase review burdens by generating larger diffs and larger batch sizes at high speed.
Reviewers facing massive diffs, such as 5,000-line pull requests, are prone to superficial approvals under the assumption issues will surface in production.
A study across more than 100 models found AI-generated code introduced known security flaws in approximately 45 percent of cases.
While AI models have improved at generating functional code, their security capabilities have remained mostly flat, widening the safety gap.
An analysis of millions of code changes revealed rising code duplication and declining code reuse.

sections.title: Reviewing AI
sections.summary: AI-driven code review provides speed, coverage, and consistency when managing large volumes of generated code. The review process can run inside an agent's internal loop to self-correct drafts prior to human evaluation. However, when the reviewer and generator models share similar architectures and training, they share the same blind spots, validating superficial patterns rather than true intent. Consequently, combining AI reviewers with deterministic tools and human oversight remains necessary depending on the operational risk.
takeaways: AI code reviewers provide advantages in review speed, bug coverage, and rule consistency.
Because AI review is probabilistic, combining it with deterministic algorithmic tools helps maintain consistency.
Review processes can operate directly inside an agent's generation loop to filter routine issues before human inspection.
Models with similar training and patterns can share blind spots, acting as duplicate opinions rather than independent checks.
Pattern-matching code checks cannot determine if code correctly fulfills the original intent of a ticket.

sections.title: The Modern Stack
sections.summary: Engineering workflows involving AI coding agents must deal with brownfield codebases by providing shared context such as architecture and guidelines. A mature architecture relies on three distinct feedback cycles: an agentic loop for sandbox generation, a CI verification loop for automated quality gates and AI code review, and a background code maintenance loop for remediating legacy technical debt. Unchecked, tangled AI-generated code progressively increases token consumption costs over time as models struggle to parse dense logic. Additionally, protecting credentials requires 'starting left' by scanning for secrets directly at the terminal before code or configurations enter an AI session.
takeaways: Most engineering workflows occur in brownfield codebases, where unguided agents produce inconsistent, varying results across runs.
A mature AI-assisted development workflow relies on three loops: the agentic loop, the CI verification loop, and the background code maintenance loop.
Sonar's stack integrates static rule analysis via SonarQube and Sonar Vortex, AI code review acquired via Gitar, and a background remediation agent.
Sonar found that messy, AI-generated code increases token costs over time because models must spend more context effort understanding dense logic on every change.
Sonar advocates for 'starting left' to prevent secret leaks by running scanners directly at the terminal before developers paste credentials into AI prompts.

sections.title: Trust And Risk
sections.summary: The required depth of code verification depends primarily on the potential cost of failure for a specific change. Mature engineering teams modulate verification effort along a risk spectrum, applying light automated checks to low-risk updates while subjecting critical systems to thorough human scrutiny. Autonomous agents can advance changes within guardrails and auto-merge low-risk tasks, but routing work appropriately between automated pipelines and human developers remains a critical, team-driven judgment call.
takeaways: Verification depth should be calibrated based on the financial, operational, and reputational cost of a potential failure.
Mature teams treat verification as a dynamic dial rather than applying a uniform standard across all code changes.
Low-risk modifications can rely on light automated checks, whereas high-risk systems demand heavy scrutiny and human review.
Software agents can independently verify and merge low-risk changes while staying within defined guardrails.
Determining the risk tiers and routing rules between agents and human reviewers requires intentional team judgment.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: Software development is experiencing a shift where generating code is becoming faster and cheaper, while code verification demands increasing effort. Effective code verification relies on a layered stack of static and dynamic filters balancing cost, false alarms, and missed bugs. The rise of AI-generated code increases both the volume and risk of software defects, and using AI alone to review AI output presents significant blind spots. Consequently, developers must pivot from writing code to orchestrating agents, exercising judgment, and deciding what needs to be built.
takeaways: Code writing has become faster, but verifying code correctness and security requires increasingly more effort.
Code verification functions as a stack of static and dynamic filters trading cost for confidence, with earlier filters keeping mistake costs low.
Relying on AI to review AI-generated code creates risks where automated checks agree code looks fine while missing critical issues.
Cheaper code generation elevates the importance of developer judgment, agent orchestration, and problem definition.

sections.title: 重心轉移
sections.summary: 近期的實證研究顯示，雖然 AI coding tools 提高了程式碼產出量，但可能會對開發效率與 delivery stability 產生負面影響。來自 Google 的 DORA 研究指出，較高的 AI 導入率與較低的 delivery stability 以及開發者揮之不去的不信任感相關。此外，METR 的一項對照實驗發現，經驗豐富的開發者使用 AI tools 完成任務的時間反而多出 19 percent，原因在於 prompting、reviewing 與除錯修正。因此，軟體開發的瓶頸正逐漸轉向下游的 code verification。
takeaways: Google 的 DORA 研究發現，隨著團隊導入更多 AI，軟體 delivery stability 反而下降。
超過三分之一的開發者表示對 AI-generated code 缺乏信心。
研究團隊 METR 的一項對照實驗顯示，在經驗豐富的開發者中，有 AI 輔助的任務比無輔助的任務多花了 19 percent 的時間。
METR 實驗中的開發者最初預期會有 25 percent 的速度提升，而且儘管花了更多時間，卻誤以為自己生產力提高了。
使用 AI 所增加的額外開發時間，大多耗費在 prompting、等待、閱讀 output 以及修復錯誤上。
由 AI 驅動的程式碼生成量增加，對下游的 code verification 造成了日益沉重的負擔。

sections.title: 建立信任
sections.summary: Code verification 是在部署至 production 之前，確保程式碼正確、安全且具 maintainability 的全面檢查機制。對軟體的信任是透過漸進式的評估逐步建立的，而非一蹴而就。雖然像飛控系統與 kernel 等高風險領域採用數學上嚴格的 formal verification，但大多數軟體依賴分層且較輕量的檢查，以平衡成本與安全性。
takeaways: Code verification 是用來驗證程式碼正確性、安全性與 maintainability 的各項檢查之統稱。
對程式碼的信任是透過分層評估逐步贏得的，而非一蹴而就。
Formal verification 涉及透過數學方法證明 code 符合精確的 specification。
像 flight-control systems 和 operating system kernels 等關鍵領域，高度依賴 formal verification 來防範可能危害生命的 defects。
多數標準軟體依賴較輕量、分層的 checks，因為 formal verification 的成本通常高到令人卻步。

sections.title: The Filter Stack
sections.summary: Code verification 可以被構建為一個有序的 filter stack，其中每一層都針對不同的 failure modes，並補足前層 checks 的盲點。快速且低成本的 static verification 工具（例如 type checkers 和 linters）會先執行，以捕捉 type mismatches 以及 syntax 或 style 問題。在 static analysis 之後，unit tests 會針對已知 inputs 執行 code，以偵測通過 type checking 的 behavioral 與 computational errors。再往下，人工 code reviews 會評估 system architecture、readability 以及對團隊 guidelines 的遵循程度，而 production monitoring 則觀察 live traffic，以在 release 前或發布期間標記任何殘留的問題。
takeaways: Type checkers 在 code 執行前驗證 data types，以防止廣泛的 runtime errors。
Linters 會檢查 code 中可疑的 patterns 以及對 stylistic standards 的違反。
Unit tests 可以偵測到 type checkers 和 linters 無法捕捉到的 behavioral flaws，例如錯誤的 arithmetic operations。
人工 code review 能識別自動化 tooling 忽略的 system-fit、readability 以及 policy violations。
Production monitoring 作為最後一道 verification 層，透過追蹤 real-world traffic 來偵測未處理的 issues。
Filter layers 是按順序排列的，因此後續的每個 check 都能涵蓋其上一層的特定弱點。

sections.title: Static And Dynamic Analysis
sections.summary: Code verification filters 主要分為 static analysis 與 dynamic analysis。Static analysis 在不執行 code 的情況下檢查 source code，能使用 type checkers 和 linters 等工具對整個 codebase 進行快速且全面的 scans，但可能因未觀察到 runtime conditions 而產生 false alarms。Dynamic analysis 則使用真實 inputs 執行 code 以觀察實際行為（以 tests 為代表），但受到所執行的特定 execution paths 嚴格限制。因此，即使是乾淨的 static scan 搭配 passed 的 test suite，仍可能留下 defect 漏洞，這使得多個互補的 verification filters 變得不可或缺。
takeaways: Static analysis 在不執行 code 的情況下檢查 code，能一次性完成快速且全 codebase 的 scans。
Linters 和 type checkers 都是 static analysis filters 的範例。
Static analysis 可能會產生 false alarms，因為 runtime behavior 在此階段仍有部分無法被觀察到。
Dynamic analysis 透過真實 inputs 執行 code，以觀察實際的 execution behavior。
Dynamic analysis 僅限於測試過的 paths，如果遺漏了像 empty inputs 這類的 edge cases，就可能忽略掉 crashes。
結合 static scans 與 test suites 仍可能存在漏洞，因此需要分層的 verification filters。

sections.title: False Alarms
sections.summary: Code verification 本質上涉及 false positives 與 false negatives 之間的基本 tradeoff。過於敏感的工具會頻繁產生 false alarms，這會侵蝕開發者的信任，導致團隊忽略有效警告或完全停用工具。來自 Sonar 的 Andrea 將這項挑戰比喻為 code verification 的 CAP theorem，團隊必須在 speed、accuracy 與 coverage 這些相互競爭的優先事項之間取得平衡。因此，高效的 verification pipelines 會優先考慮具可操作性的 findings 與 signal quality，而非單純追求 coverage，以保持開發者的投入度。
takeaways: Code verification 需要在 false positives（標記正常 code）與 false negatives（遺漏實際 bugs）之間取得平衡。
高比率的 false alarms 會侵蝕開發者的信任，往往導致工程師忽略 warnings，甚至完全停用 static analysis 工具。
來自 Sonar 的 Andrea 將 code verification 的 tradeoffs 比喻為 CAP theorem，其中 speed、accuracy 與 coverage 是相互競爭的優先級，沒有任何工具能同時將這三者最大化。
Sonar 團隊堅持一項原則：唯有當開發者能直接針對其採取行動時，該 finding 才有回報的價值。
在 verification pipeline 中 filter 的放置位置，會改變 verification errors 的實際成本。

sections.title: The Pipeline
sections.summary: 一個 change request 的生命週期構成了一條 pipeline：始於開發者的 editor，接著經歷 commit checks、review、merge、deployment 以及 live monitoring。Verification checks 越晚執行，成本就越高，因為 downstream 的工作會累積在缺陷之上。「shift left」的概念是指將這些檢查移至 pipeline 的更早期階段，以便在修復成本仍低時解決問題。儘管行銷宣稱的精準成本倍數值得懷疑，但將檢查提前的大方向依然合理且具備成本效益。
takeaways: 一次 code change 會經歷橫跨 editor、自動化 commit checks、review、merge、deployment 到 live monitoring 的 pipeline。
Defect 在 pipeline 中越晚被發現，修復的成本就越高。
相較於在 editor 中只需開發者花費微小的精力，在 production 中發現的缺陷可能會引發 incidents、rollbacks 以及對使用者的負面影響。
「Shift left」代表在 delivery lifecycle 中將自動化與人工檢查提前，以低成本的方式及早發現問題。
廠商宣稱各階段確切的成本倍數應持保留態度，但早期 testing 的方向性效益依然成立。

sections.title: AI Pressure
sections.summary: 傳統的軟體 review stack 是建立在「大部分程式碼由人類編寫」的假設之上，但 AI coding tools 的興起打破了這個前提。這些工具帶來了前所未見的 code volume 與更大的 batch sizes，進而造成巨大的壓力，往往導致對龐大 pull requests 的形式化審查（rubber-stamped reviews）。此外，AI models 經常生成包含已知 security flaws 的程式碼（在測試案例中觀察到約 45% 的比例），卻未具備相應的 security safeguards 提升。因此，儘管 functional correctness 有所進步，但 working code 與 secure code 之間的差距持續擴大，伴隨著程式碼 duplication 增加以及 reuse 率下降。
takeaways: AI coding tools 透過高速生成更大的 diffs 與更大的 batch sizes，大幅增加了 review 的負擔。
面對龐大的 diffs（例如 5,000 行的 pull requests），reviewers 往往會抱著「問題會在 production 浮現」的心態而給予敷衍的核准。
一項涵蓋超過 100 個 models 的研究發現，AI 生成的程式碼在約 45% 的案例中引入了已知的 security flaws。
雖然 AI models 在生成 functional code 方面有所進步，但其 security 能力幾乎停滯不前，使得 safety gap 進一步擴大。
對數百萬次 code changes 的分析顯示，code duplication 正在上升，而 code reuse 則持續下降。

sections.title: Reviewing AI
sections.summary: 在處理大量生成的程式碼時，AI-driven code review 能提供速度、coverage 與 consistency。Review 流程可以在 agent 的內部 loop 中執行，以便在人類評估之前自我修正 drafts。然而，當 reviewer 與 generator models 共享相似的架構與 training 時，它們也會共享相同的盲點，僅驗證表面的 patterns 而非真實的 intent。因此，根據 operational risk 的不同，將 AI reviewers 與 deterministic tools 及人類監督相結合仍然是必要的。
takeaways: AI code reviewers 在 review 速度、bug coverage 以及 rule consistency 方面具備優勢。
由於 AI review 具有機率性（probabilistic），將其與 deterministic 的演算法工具結合有助於維持一致性。
Review 流程可以直接在 agent 的 generation loop 內運作，在進行人工檢查之前先過濾掉常規問題。
擁有相似 training 與 patterns 的 models 可能會有相同的盲點，只是產生重複的意見而非獨立的 checks。
Pattern-matching code checks 無法判斷程式碼是否正確滿足了 ticket 的原始 intent。

sections.title: The Modern Stack
sections.summary: 涉及 AI coding agents 的工程工作流程必須透過提供架構與 guidelines 等 shared context，來處理 brownfield codebases。成熟的架構依賴三種不同的 feedback cycles：用於 sandbox 生成的 agentic loop、用於自動化 quality gates 與 AI code review 的 CI verification loop，以及用於修復 legacy technical debt 的背景程式碼維護 loop。未經檢查且糾纏不清的 AI 生成程式碼，會隨著時間推移逐漸增加 token consumption 成本，因為 models 在解析高密度邏輯時會變得吃力。此外，保護憑證需要「start left」，在程式碼或配置進入 AI session 之前，直接在 terminal 掃描 secrets。
takeaways: 大多數工程工作流程都發生在 brownfield codebases 中，在缺乏引導的情況下，agents 在多次執行之間容易產生不一致且變動劇烈的結果。
一個成熟的 AI 輔助開發工作流程依賴於三個循環：agentic loop、CI verification loop 以及 background code maintenance loop。
Sonar 的技術棧整合了透過 SonarQube 和 Sonar Vortex 進行的靜態規則分析、透過 Gitar 獲得的 AI code review，以及一個 background remediation agent。
Sonar 發現，混亂的 AI 生成程式碼隨著時間推移會增加 token 成本，因為模型每次進行變更時，都必須花費更多 context 心力去理解稠密晦澀的邏輯。
Sonar 主張「左移起點」（starting left），在開發者將憑證貼入 AI prompt 之前，直接在終端機執行掃描工具以防止機密外洩。

sections.title: 信任與風險
sections.summary: 程式碼驗證所需的深度主要取決於特定變更潛在的失敗成本。成熟的工程團隊會依據風險光譜來調整驗證力度，對低風險的更新採用輕量級自動化檢查，同時對關鍵系統進行透徹的人工審查。Autonomous agent 可以在 guardrail 內推進變更並自動合併低風險任務，但在自動化 pipeline 與人類開發者之間妥善分流工作，仍然是仰賴團隊判斷的關鍵決策。
takeaways: 驗證深度應根據潛在失敗在財務、營運及商譽上的成本來進行校準。
成熟的團隊將驗證視為一個動態調整的度量表，而不是在所有程式碼變更中套用單一標準。
低風險的修改可以仰賴輕量級的自動化檢查，而高風險系統則需要嚴格的審查與人工 review。
Software agent 可以在既定的 guardrails 限制內，獨立驗證並合併低風險的變更。
釐定風險等級以及 agent 與人類審查者之間的分流規則，需要團隊審慎的判斷。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: 軟體開發正經歷一場轉變：生成程式碼變得愈來愈快且愈來愈便宜，而程式碼驗證卻需要投入更多精力。有效的程式碼驗證依賴於分層的靜態與動態過濾器技術棧，以在成本、誤報（false alarms）與漏檢（missed bugs）之間取得平衡。AI 生成程式碼的崛起同時增加了軟體缺陷的數量與風險，而僅使用 AI 來審查 AI 的產出存在顯著的盲點。因此，開發者必須從編寫程式碼轉向編排 agent、運用專業判斷力，並決定該構建什麼。
takeaways: 程式碼編寫已經變得更快，但驗證程式碼的正確性與安全性卻需要愈來愈多的精力。
程式碼驗證的運作方式是一組靜態與動態過濾器的技術棧，透過成本換取信心，而較早階段的過濾器能將出錯成本維持在較低水準。
依賴 AI 來審查 AI 生成的程式碼會帶來風險，即自動化檢查都認為程式碼看起來沒問題，卻忽略了關鍵問題。
更低成本的程式碼生成提升了開發者判斷力、agent 編排以及問題定義的重要性。

items.title: Preloading Knowledge Into a Model Instead of Retrieving It

sections.title: Preloading knowledge into a model instead of retrieving it
sections.summary: The RAG Systems course introduces preloading as a method to eliminate repetitive document processing by having the model read a knowledge base once and storing the resulting KV cache. This approach addresses the high cost of prefill, which scales quadratically with input length and often dominates inference expenses in production environments. While providers like Gemini and Claude offer significant discounts for cached tokens, technical challenges such as effective context limits and the need for query-agnostic compression must be addressed for successful implementation.
takeaways: Preloading allows a model to skip retrieval, chunking, and embedding by storing the KV cache of a corpus.
Prefill costs scale quadratically with input length, making it the dominant expense for high-volume RAG systems.
Provider-side caching for models like Gemini and Claude can reduce input token costs by up to 90 percent.
A model's effective context window is often significantly smaller than its advertised limit, with performance degrading as context grows.
Most KV cache compression methods are unsuitable for preloading because they require the query at the time of compression.
Modular preloading caches passages independently but can encounter cross-attention failures.
Trained preloading involves distilling a corpus into a compact cache through a specific training run.

sections.title: How to cut agent tokens by 2.7x (using an open harness)
sections.summary: The efficiency and cost of AI agents are primarily determined by the 'harness'—the runtime layer that manages context, tool execution, and memory—rather than the model itself. TrueFoundry's open-source harness, TrueForge, demonstrates how to reduce token usage by 2.7x through techniques like deferred tool loading, context offloading to sandboxes, and 'Code Mode' for data processing. Benchmarks on Enterprise-Bench show that these optimizations allow agents to achieve high success rates with significantly lower latency and cost compared to closed alternatives.
takeaways: Agent token costs are often a runtime problem caused by redundant context and inefficient tool definitions being sent in every model call.
TrueForge achieved a 2.7x reduction in token usage compared to Claude Managed Agents while maintaining the same task success rate.
Deferred tool loading prevents prompt bloat by only loading full schemas and documentation when a specific tool is identified as necessary.
Code Mode reduces context usage by executing Python scripts in a sandbox to join and process data, returning only the final result to the model.
Context offloading moves large tool responses into a sandbox file, providing the model with a short preview and file path instead of the full payload.
TrueForge is MIT-licensed, self-hostable, and integrates with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Daytona sandboxes.

大多數 KV cache 壓縮方法不適用於 preloading，因為它們在壓縮時需要 query。
Modular preloading 獨立快取各個段落，但可能會遇到 cross-attention 失效的問題。
Trained preloading 涉及透過特定 training run 將語料庫蒸餾為緊湊的 cache。

sections.title: 如何將 agent 的 token 減少 2.7 倍（使用開源 harness）

takeaways: Agent 的 token 成本通常是一個 runtime 問題，起因於每次模型呼叫時都傳送了冗餘的 context 與低效的 tool 定義。
與 Claude Managed Agents 相比，TrueForge 在維持相同任務成功率的同時，將 token 使用量減少了 2.7 倍。
Deferred tool loading 僅在確認需要特定 tool 時才載入完整 schema 與 documentation，進而避免 prompt bloat。
