items.title: EP223: Ollama vs vLLM vs SGLang

sections.title: Ollama vs vLLM vs SGLang
sections.summary: Ollama, vLLM, and SGLang are three primary engines for serving open-weight models, each architected for distinct execution workloads. Ollama relies on a FIFO queue and pre-quantized GGUF models, making it optimal for local prototyping and laptop-scale hardware. vLLM implements continuous batching and PagedAttention to optimize KV cache management and maximize GPU utilization for high-traffic environments. SGLang uses a prefix-aware scheduler and RadixAttention to avoid recomputing prompt prefixes, making it ideal for agent loops, multi-turn chats, and structured outputs.
takeaways: Ollama processes requests sequentially through a FIFO queue and runs compressed GGUF models.
Ollama is targeted at local development, prototyping, and laptop-scale hardware.
vLLM incorporates continuous batching to add new requests into active batches dynamically.
vLLM relies on PagedAttention to store the KV cache and is optimized for high-traffic concurrent serving.
SGLang utilizes a prefix-aware scheduler and RadixAttention to retain and reuse shared prompt prefixes via a radix tree.
SGLang is tailored for AI agents, multi-turn conversations, and JSON or regex structured outputs.

sections.title: How does Claude's text watermark work?
sections.summary: Anthropic plans to watermark AI-generated text to enable reliable identification of model outputs. Rather than standard random sampling, a keyed function uses a secret key and preceding words to constrain candidate token choices during generation. Detection works by verifying whether tokens match the keyed criteria across the text, producing an AI-generation score based on the match rate. The author also notes ongoing issues with false negatives in AI text detection, particularly within technical writing.
takeaways: Anthropic announced plans to watermark generated text to facilitate AI identification.
Watermarking alters next-word selection using a keyed function dependent on a secret key and preceding context.
Tokens where multiple valid word options exist carry the watermark signal.
Detection evaluates the match rate of words conforming to the keyed selection rule across a piece of text.
AI text detection techniques currently suffer from false negatives, particularly in technical writing contexts.

sections.title: Top 12 Agent Skills You Should Know
sections.summary: Agent skills are instruction sets and scripts designed to equip LLM agents with specialized capabilities. As of August 2026, the twelve most-starred skill repositories on GitHub feature a range of augmentations for coding, UI design, planning, and agent communication. These skills include tooling from individual developers as well as organizations like Anthropic, Google, and Multica AI. Together, they assist agents in navigating complex codebases, adopting production-grade practices, and interacting effectively.
takeaways: Agent skills consist of instructions and scripts that teach LLM agents specific new capabilities.
The featured list captures the 12 most-starred agent skill repositories on GitHub as of August 2026.
Skills range from functional abilities like document creation and codebase knowledge graph generation to behavioral modifications like pre-code planning.
Major organizations and figures such as Anthropic, Google's Addy Osmani, and Multica AI have developed or contributed to top-starred skills.

sections.title: Git Workflow: Essential Commands
sections.summary: Git workflows center on tracking and moving code between four distinct locations: the working directory, staging area, local repository, and remote repository. Most workflow issues arise from misunderstanding where code is placed after running specific commands. Core commands facilitate saving work, fetching or checking out repositories, syncing remote changes, and safely stashing uncommitted progress.
takeaways: Most practical Git workflows only rely on a small fraction of the available commands.
Code in Git moves between four main locations: the working directory, staging area, local repository, and remote repository.

sections.title: Apache Kafka vs. RabbitMQ
sections.summary: Apache Kafka and RabbitMQ are messaging technologies built for fundamentally different distributed systems use cases. Kafka operates as a distributed log where messages are appended to partitions, persisted according to retention policies, and pulled by consumers via offsets for replayable, high-throughput event streaming. In contrast, RabbitMQ serves as a message broker where messages are routed through exchanges to queues, pushed to consumers, and deleted upon acknowledgment. Misapplying Kafka as a simple queue or RabbitMQ as an event log undermines their specialized architectures.
takeaways: Kafka is designed as a distributed log where producers append messages to partitions based on a retention policy.
Kafka consumers pull messages using offsets, allowing data to be rewound, replayed, and reprocessed independently.
RabbitMQ functions as a message broker that routes messages via exchanges into queues using direct, topic, or fanout binding keys.
RabbitMQ pushes messages to consumers and deletes them once they are acknowledged.
Using Kafka as a standard task queue or RabbitMQ as an immutable event log is a common architectural anti-pattern.

items.summary: Ollama, vLLM, and SGLang are three primary engines for serving open-weight models, each architected for distinct execution workloads. Ollama relies on a FIFO queue and pre-quantized GGUF models, making it optimal for local prototyping and laptop-scale hardware. vLLM implements continuous batching and PagedAttention to optimize KV cache management and maximize GPU utilization for high-traffic environments. SGLang uses a prefix-aware scheduler and RadixAttention to avoid recomputing prompt prefixes, making it ideal for agent loops, multi-turn chats, and structured outputs. Anthropic plans to watermark AI-generated text to enable reliable identification of model outputs. Rather than standard random sampling, a keyed function uses a secret key and preceding words to constrain candidate token choices during generation. Detection works by verifying whether tokens match the keyed criteria across the text, producing an AI-generation score based on the match rate. The author also notes ongoing issues with false negatives in AI text detection, particularly within technical writing. Agent skills are instruction sets and scripts designed to equip LLM agents with specialized capabilities. As of August 2026, the twelve most-starred skill repositories on GitHub feature a range of augmentations for coding, UI design, planning, and agent communication. These skills include tooling from individual developers as well as organizations like Anthropic, Google, and Multica AI. Together, they assist agents in navigating complex codebases, adopting production-grade practices, and interacting effectively.

sections.title: Git Workflow：必備指令
sections.summary: Git workflows 的核心在於追蹤程式碼，並在四個不同位置之間移動：working directory、staging area、local repository 以及 remote repository。大多數 workflow 問題都源於誤解執行特定指令後程式碼所在的狀態或位置。核心指令有助於儲存工作進度、fetch 或 checkout repositories、同步 remote 變更，以及安全地 stash 未 commit 的進度。
takeaways: 大多數實際的 Git workflows 僅依賴所有可用指令中的一小部分。

'git pull' 將 'git fetch' 和 'git merge' 的操作合併為單一步驟。
'git stash' 會暫存未 commit 的變更，這些變更可透過 'git stash apply' 還原，或透過 'git stash pop' 還原並刪除。

sections.title: Apache Kafka vs. RabbitMQ
sections.summary: Apache Kafka 與 RabbitMQ 是針對本質上截然不同的分散式系統使用情境所打造的 messaging 技術。Kafka 運作方式為分散式 log，message 會被 append 到 partition 中，根據 retention policy 進行持久化，並由 consumer 透過 offset 進行 pull，以實現可重播、高 throughput 的 event streaming。相較之下，RabbitMQ 則是作為 message broker，message 透過 exchange 路由至 queue，push 給 consumer，並在收到 acknowledgment 後刪除。誤將 Kafka 當作單純的 queue，或將 RabbitMQ 當作 event log 使用，都會破壞它們專屬的架構設計。
takeaways: Kafka 被設計為分散式 log，producer 會根據 retention policy 將 message append 到 partition 中。
Kafka consumer 使用 offset 來 pull message，讓資料能夠被獨立地倒帶、重播與重新處理。
RabbitMQ 的功能是 message broker，透過 direct、topic 或 fanout binding key，經由 exchange 將 message 路由至 queue 中。
RabbitMQ 會將 message push 給 consumer，並在收到 acknowledgment 後將其刪除。
將 Kafka 當作標準的 task queue 使用，或將 RabbitMQ 當作 immutable event log 使用，都是常見的架構 anti-pattern。

sections.title: Your KV cache library is stealing your throughput
sections.summary: Traditional KV cache management often reduces inference throughput because I/O-bound tensor movements stall the GPU's compute-heavy attention operations. LMCache solves this by decoupling cache management into a separate process that shares GPU memory with the inference engine. This architectural shift allows for concurrent searching across multiple storage tiers, including CPU RAM and cloud storage, without blocking the engine. Benchmarks demonstrate significant performance improvements, such as a 14x faster time-to-first-token for large models like Qwen3-235B.
takeaways: Cache management and inference engines have conflicting bottlenecks (I/O vs. GPU math) that cause performance degradation when run in a single process.
Google's TurboQuant achieves 3-bit KV cache compression without accuracy loss but still impacts throughput if integrated directly into the engine.
LMCache is an open-source library that moves cache management to a dedicated process to prevent inference stalls.
The library utilizes shared GPU memory to pass block IDs between processes efficiently.
LMCache enables simultaneous searching across GPU, CPU, SSD, and cloud storage tiers.
Performance tests on NVIDIA H200s show a 14x improvement in time-to-first-token and a 4x increase in decoding speed.

sections.title: How semantic code navigation cuts agent token costs by up to 36%
sections.summary: AI coding agents often incur high token costs because they rely on inefficient text search to navigate codebases. By representing code as a structural graph rather than plain text, agents can perform semantic navigation to find relevant code locations more accurately and cheaply. This approach, implemented in tools like Sonar Vortex, has shown token cost reductions of up to 36% by eliminating the need for agents to read and reason through irrelevant search matches.
takeaways: AI coding agents spend more tokens on finding code locations than on writing the actual code.
Text search fails for agents when names are ambiguous, shadowed, or when connections are structural like interfaces.
Graph-based code navigation treats code elements as nodes and relationships as edges to provide exact locations.
Semantic navigation can reduce token costs by 5% to 36% depending on the task complexity.
Sonar Vortex integrates semantic navigation and real-time verification into the agent's loop.
Microsoft and Uber reported significant budget overruns due to inefficient AI agent token usage.

sections.title: Label Smoothing for Regularization
sections.summary: Label smoothing is a regularization technique that redistributes probability mass from the target class to other classes to prevent overfitting. In experiments using the Fashion MNIST dataset, models trained with label smoothing showed improved test accuracy and better generalization compared to those without it. However, the technique causes models to become less overconfident, leading to lower confidence values for predictions. Consequently, it is recommended for tasks focusing on accuracy but not for those requiring well-calibrated confidence scores.
takeaways: Label smoothing redistributes probability mass from the true class to other classes to improve generalization.
Experiments on the Fashion MNIST dataset show that label smoothing leads to higher test accuracy.
The technique intentionally reduces model overconfidence, resulting in lower confidence values for all predictions.
Label smoothing is recommended when the primary goal is prediction accuracy rather than confidence calibration.
L2 regularization is highlighted as an alternative method with a probabilistic origin.

sections.title: Fine-tuning, Transfer, Multitask & Federated Learning
sections.summary: The text outlines four advanced machine learning training methodologies: transfer learning, fine-tuning, multi-task learning (MTL), and federated learning (FL). Transfer learning and fine-tuning focus on adapting pre-trained models to new tasks by reusing or adjusting weights. Multi-task learning utilizes shared network architectures to improve generalization and efficiency across multiple related tasks. Federated learning provides a decentralized approach that preserves user privacy by training models locally on devices like smartphones.
takeaways: Transfer learning is effective when the target task has limited data but a related task has abundant data.
Fine-tuning involves adjusting the weights of a pre-trained model for a specific new task.
Multi-task learning employs a shared network with task-specific branches to reduce memory and resource usage.
Federated learning keeps training data on the user's device and only transmits model updates to a central server.
Models used in federated learning must be lightweight to function on small devices like smartphones.

sections.title: Fine-tuning、Transfer、Multitask 與 Federated Learning

takeaways: 當目標任務的資料有限，但相關任務擁有大量資料時，transfer learning 特別有效。

Multi-task learning 採用具有特定任務分支的共享網路，以減少記憶體與資源消耗。

items.title: Schema Evolution: Changing the Contract Without Breaking What Runs

sections.title: Schema Evolution: Changing the Contract Without Breaking What Runs
sections.summary: Schema changes are deceptively simple in code review but represent one of the most difficult types of modifications in software systems. Migrations often appear successful in staging yet fail in production because multiple application versions run simultaneously against the same schema. Incompatibility problems also emerge across time, such as when historical database records, queued messages, or legacy mobile clients interact with newer services. Addressing these issues requires deliberate strategies including backward and forward compatibility, expand-and-contract migrations, and schema registries.
takeaways: Schema changes often seem minor during review (e.g., renaming a column or dropping an unused field) but can cause widespread production failures.
Deployment issues frequently arise when two versions of an application concurrently query the same database while only one supports the updated schema.
Data written under previous schema versions—such as historical database rows, queued messages, or requests from outdated mobile apps—must often be processed by newer application code.
Managing schema evolution requires methodologies such as expand and contract migrations and tools like schema registries.

Addressing these issues requires deliberate strategies including backward and forward compatibility, expand-and-contract migrations, and schema registries.

sections.title: RAG vs. CAG, explained visually!
sections.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) can be inefficient when repeatedly querying static data from a vector database. Cache-Augmented Generation (CAG) optimizes this by storing static, 'cold' information in the model's internal key-value (KV) memory. By combining both approaches, systems can achieve faster inference and lower costs while maintaining access to dynamic, 'hot' data. Advanced techniques like CacheBlend, implemented in the open-source LMCache, allow for more flexible caching that overcomes the strict prefix-matching limitations of standard prompt caching.
takeaways: RAG is often redundant for static information that does not change frequently.
CAG stores static data in the model's KV memory to reduce repeated computation and database hits.
Standard prompt caching in APIs like OpenAI and Anthropic requires exact byte-for-byte prefix matching to be effective.
CacheBlend is a technique that allows for reusing cached document blocks even when their order or combination changes.
LMCache is an open-source implementation of these caching optimizations that can speed up multi-document queries by 2x to 4x.
Effective caching strategy involves separating 'cold' static data from 'hot' dynamic data to avoid hitting context limits.

sections.title: What is (was?) GIL in Python?
sections.summary: The Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) has historically limited Python's multi-threading performance by restricting execution to a single thread per process. While multi-processing offers a workaround by using isolated memory spaces, it introduces complexity compared to shared-memory threading. Python 3.14 introduces the ability to disable the GIL, enabling true parallel execution across multiple CPU cores to improve performance for compute-intensive tasks.
takeaways: The GIL prevents Python processes from executing multiple threads simultaneously on different CPU cores.
Multi-threading in Python with the GIL results in performance similar to single-threading for CPU-bound tasks.
Multi-processing achieves parallelism by using separate memory spaces for each process, avoiding the GIL's limitations.
The primary historical reason for the GIL was to ensure thread safety and prevent race conditions in shared memory.
Python 3.14 introduces a feature to run without the GIL, allowing threads to utilize multiple CPU cores fully.
Inter-process communication (IPC) mechanisms like pipes and queues are necessary for data sharing in multi-processing but add complexity.

sections.title: What is Contrastive Learning?
sections.summary: Contrastive learning is a self-supervised technique that trains models to learn representations by comparing samples rather than using traditional classification. In applications like face unlock systems, Siamese networks map inputs into a shared embedding space where similar items are positioned close together and dissimilar items are far apart. This approach avoids the need for retraining on-device when new users are added, as it relies on comparing generated embeddings against stored ones. The training process is driven by a contrastive loss function that optimizes the distance between these embeddings based on a defined margin.
takeaways: Contrastive learning teaches models to learn useful representations by comparing similar and dissimilar samples.
Siamese networks use a shared network to map inputs to a common embedding space for distance-based comparison.
Binary classification is often unsuitable for face unlock due to the difficulty of obtaining diverse negative samples and the risk of catastrophic forgetting.
The contrastive loss function minimizes the distance between embeddings of the same class and maximizes the distance for different classes up to a specific margin.
On-device face unlock systems can support multiple users by storing unique embeddings in memory without requiring model retraining.
Model compression and federated learning are complementary techniques for building efficient, privacy-preserving on-device ML applications.

takeaways: 對於不常變動的靜態資訊，RAG 往往顯得冗餘。
CAG 將靜態資料儲存在模型的 KV memory 中，以減少重複運算與資料庫存取次數。
在 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等 API 中，標準的 prompt caching 需要完全一致的 byte-for-byte prefix matching 才能發揮作用。
CacheBlend 是一種即使快取的文件區塊順序或組合改變，仍可重複使用快取內容的技術。
LMCache 是這些 caching optimizations 的開源實現，可將 multi-document queries 提速 2 到 4 倍。
有效的 caching strategy 包含將「冷」靜態資料與「熱」動態資料分離，以避免觸及 context limits。

sections.title: 什麼是（曾是？）Python 中的 GIL？
sections.summary: 在歷史上，Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) 透過將執行限制在每個 process 單一 thread，限制了 Python 的 multi-threading 效能。雖然 multi-processing 透過使用獨立的 memory spaces 提供了替代方案，但相較於 shared-memory threading，它帶來了額外的複雜度。Python 3.14 引入了停用 GIL 的功能，實現跨多個 CPU cores 的真正 parallel execution，進而提升 compute-intensive tasks 的效能。
takeaways: GIL 阻止了 Python process 在不同的 CPU cores 上同時執行多個 threads。
在受限於 GIL 的情況下，Python 的 multi-threading 在處理 CPU-bound tasks 時的效能與 single-threading 相似。
Multi-processing 透過為每個 process 使用獨立的 memory spaces 來實現 parallelism，進而規避了 GIL 的限制。
歷史上採用 GIL 的主要原因是為了確保 thread safety，並防止 shared memory 中的 race conditions。
Python 3.14 引入了在沒有 GIL 下運行的功能，允許 threads 充分利用多個 CPU cores。
像 pipes 和 queues 這樣的 Inter-process communication (IPC) 機制在 multi-processing 中傳遞資料是必要的，但這也增加了系統複雜度。

sections.title: 什麼是 Contrastive Learning？
sections.summary: Contrastive learning 是一種 self-supervised 技術，它透過比較樣本而非傳統的 classification 來訓練模型學習 representations。在臉部解鎖系統等應用中，Siamese networks 會將輸入映射到一個共享的 embedding space，在此空間中相似項目會彼此靠近，不相似的項目則相距較遠。由於該方法依賴於將生成的 embeddings 與儲存的 embeddings 進行比較，因此在新增使用者時無需在 device 上重新訓練。訓練過程由 contrastive loss function 驅動，該函數會根據定義好的 margin 來最佳化這些 embeddings 之間的距離。
takeaways: Contrastive learning 透過比較相似與不相似的樣本，教導模型學習有用的 representations。
Siamese networks 使用共享網路將輸入映射到共同的 embedding space，以進行基於距離的比較。
Binary classification 通常不適用於臉部解鎖，因為難以取得多樣化的負樣本，且存在 catastrophic forgetting 的風險。
Contrastive loss function 會將同類別 embeddings 之間的距離最小化，並將不同類別之間的距離最大化至特定 margin。
On-device 臉部解鎖系統可以透過在 memory 中儲存專屬的 embeddings 來支援多個使用者，而無需重新訓練模型。
Model compression 和 federated learning 是構建高效、保護隱私的 on-device ML 應用的互補技術。

items.title: GraphRAG: How AI Answers Questions Hidden Across Many Documents

sections.title: Retrieval Basics
sections.summary: Standard Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) operates through a straightforward pipeline where documents are split into token chunks and transformed into vectors via an embedding model. These vectors are stored in a vector index to facilitate proximity-based semantic search against incoming query vectors. During query execution, the closest document chunks are retrieved and included in the language model prompt to generate grounded answers. The entire workflow relies on the core assumption that queries and their corresponding answers share lexical or semantic resemblance.
takeaways: Standard RAG partitions documents into chunks ranging from a few hundred to a few thousand tokens.
An embedding model maps text chunks into numeric vectors representing semantic meaning within a shared vector space.
At query time, the vector index identifies and returns chunk vectors that are numerically closest to the question vector.
Retrieved chunk text is injected into the prompt alongside the question for the language model to generate an answer.
The RAG architecture assumes that text providing an answer semantically or lexically resembles the query itself.

sections.title: Similarity Limits
sections.summary: The assumption that questions resemble their answers holds for local queries but breaks down for global queries that require reasoning across an entire corpus. For global queries, standard vector retrieval surfaces documents with superficial vocabulary overlap rather than synthesizing information distributed across hundreds of files. Microsoft's evaluations show that increasing context windows up to 64,000 tokens does not bridge this gap in comprehensiveness, diversity, and source quality compared to GraphRAG. What is commonly diagnosed as model hallucination is often actually a retrieval issue where fluent text is generated from irrelevant retrieved context.
takeaways: Microsoft's GraphRAG documentation divides queries into local queries focusing on specific text regions and global queries requiring corpus-wide reasoning.
Vector retrieval fails on global queries because nearest-neighbor search matches coincidental phrasing rather than aggregating distributed facts.
Increasing context windows from 8,000 to 64,000 tokens fails to match GraphRAG's performance on global questions.
Vector search with large context windows still falls short on comprehensiveness, diversity, and source material quality.
Failures attributed to model hallucination often stem from retrieval returning irrelevant material that the model subsequently generates fluent responses from.

sections.title: Knowledge Graphs
sections.summary: Knowledge graphs enhance retrieval and answer quality by modeling relationships between entities across documents rather than treating text chunks independently. By aggregating extracted entities and typed relations from multiple sources, knowledge graphs create multi-hop paths connecting disparate information that no single document holds. Real-world implementations, such as LinkedIn's support ticket system presented at SIGIR 2024, demonstrate significant production gains including higher retrieval rank and reduced resolution times. Modern GraphRAG architectures typically combine lexical graphs of document structures with entity graphs of domain concepts to query across both.
takeaways: Knowledge graphs store corpora as entities and typed relationships, both carrying plain-text descriptions.
Aggregating entities and edges across multiple documents reveals paths and connections that no single document contains.

LinkedIn's customer service team implemented a knowledge graph for support tickets, improving mean reciprocal rank by 77.6 percent and reducing median per-issue resolution time by 28.6 percent in production.
LinkedIn published their knowledge graph retrieval findings at SIGIR in 2024.
Neo4j distinguishes between lexical graphs (linking documents to chunks) and entity graphs (linking described entities).
Most GraphRAG systems construct both lexical and entity graphs and query across them.

sections.title: Graph Construction
sections.summary: Constructing a knowledge graph from raw documents requires a multi-phase pipeline where the majority of computation and expense is concentrated in graph extraction and merging. Microsoft's indexing workflow involves text chunking, LLM extraction of entities and relationships, merging and summarizing redundant descriptions, community clustering, and embedding into a vector store. The two LLM passes across a corpus represent approximately 75 percent of total indexing costs. To mitigate this expense, alternatives like FastGraphRAG substitute LLMs with traditional NLP techniques, though this trades cost efficiency for increased noise.
takeaways: Microsoft's graph indexing workflow consists of six phases, including chunking, LLM extraction, merging/compression, optional claim extraction, community clustering, and report embedding.
The merge step is computationally expensive because entities appearing across hundreds of text units require separate LLM passes to reconcile into coherent descriptions.
Every extracted entity, relationship, and claim maintains provenance via pointers back to source text units for paragraph-level citations.
Microsoft estimates that graph extraction accounts for approximately 75 percent of total indexing costs.
FastGraphRAG reduces indexing costs by swapping LLMs for traditional NLP, extracting noun phrases and co-occurrences at the expense of higher graph noise.

sections.title: Community Detection
sections.summary: GraphRAG enables answering whole-collection questions by executing hierarchical Leiden clustering across an entity graph to partition it into multi-level communities. For each community across every level, a language model pre-generates a community report detailing key entities, relationships, and claims during the indexing phase. Choosing the appropriate hierarchy level determines the balance between answer thoroughness and operational costs in time and tokens.
takeaways: Hierarchical Leiden clustering recursively partitions entity graphs into multi-level communities until reaching a minimum size threshold.
Higher levels (such as Level 0) provide broad coverage over large regions, while deeper levels partition into narrower, fine-grained sub-communities.
Community reports containing summaries, key entities, relationships, and claims are generated during indexing before queries occur.
Pre-generated summaries allow global, whole-collection questions to be answered directly from pre-existing text.
Selecting lower hierarchical levels produces more detailed answers but increases token consumption and query latency due to processing a larger volume of reports.

sections.title: Query Modes
sections.summary: GraphRAG supports multiple retrieval query modes tailored to different question types across a knowledge graph and report hierarchy. Local search identifies specific entry-point entities and expands along five parallel directions—text units, community reports, neighbors, relationships, and covariates—before ranking and packing them into a context window. Global search operates over community reports using a map-reduce process to answer broad, corpus-wide questions without relying on specific entity lookups. Additionally, GraphRAG provides DRIFT search, which combines community reports and follow-up local searches, as well as a basic search mode using standard top-k vector retrieval.
takeaways: Local search identifies entry-point entities via embeddings and expands across five parallel directions: text units, community reports, neighboring entities, relationships, and covariates.
Local search functions as a bounded, structured gather-and-rank operation rather than open-ended pathfinding.
Global search bypasses the entity graph, processing shuffled community report batches through a map-reduce pipeline with intermediate numerical importance ratings.
DRIFT search blends global and local approaches by producing an initial answer from community reports, generating follow-up questions, and running local search on them.
GraphRAG includes a basic search mode that uses standard top-k vector retrieval.

sections.title: Cost Tradeoffs
sections.summary: GraphRAG significantly redistributes retrieval-augmented generation costs compared to standard RAG, incurring heavy indexing expenses due to multiple language model passes and community summarization. Updating the index with new documents creates an ongoing operational commitment as hierarchies shift and material is re-summarized. Microsoft developed LazyGraphRAG to address this by replacing LLM-based indexing with traditional NLP, which reduces indexing cost to match vector RAG and lowers query cost by over 700x while maintaining global-query quality. Nevertheless, full GraphRAG remains valuable for its human-readable community reports and excels in comprehensiveness and diversity, though its faithfulness matches standard RAG rather than eliminating hallucinations.
takeaways: Standard vector RAG requires only one embedding pass at index time and a single nearest-neighbor lookup per query.
GraphRAG indexing requires two language model passes over the corpus and report generation across community hierarchy levels.
LazyGraphRAG reduces indexing cost to 0.1 percent of full GraphRAG by utilizing NLP instead of LLMs and deferring LLM tasks to query time.
LazyGraphRAG cuts query costs by more than a factor of 700 while maintaining comparable global-query quality.
Microsoft notes that pre-built entity, relationship, and community summaries provide utility beyond question answering because people read and share them directly.
Evaluations show vector RAG outperforms GraphRAG for localized queries where answers reside in specific text regions.
GraphRAG provides advantages in comprehensiveness and diversity, but scores similarly to baseline RAG on faithfulness and factual accuracy.

sections.title: Agentic Retrieval
sections.summary: Agentic RAG addresses the limitations of fixed retrieval pipelines by using a language model to dynamically classify queries and select tailored retrieval strategies, such as vector search, SQL, or web search. LlamaIndex illustrates a two-layer routing design where a composite retriever selects an index and an auto-routed mode chooses the retrieval method within that index. While this flexibility improves accuracy across diverse questions, it introduces latency, higher per-query costs, and debugging hurdles from routing errors. The paradigm marks an evolutionary step beyond basic RAG, advanced RAG, and GraphRAG.
takeaways: Agentic RAG uses an LLM to classify incoming queries, select a specific retrieval strategy, execute it, and synthesize results.
Supported retrieval options can span vector search, corpus-wide global search, SQL queries, and web search.
LlamaIndex implements a two-layer routing pattern using a composite retriever to pick an index and an auto-routed mode to select the method within that index.
Pre-retrieval LLM calls introduce additional latency and increased financial cost per query.
Routing failures complicate debugging because an appropriate retrieval method can execute poorly if misassigned to a query.
Agentic RAG represents the top of a performance ladder evolving from basic RAG, advanced RAG, and GraphRAG.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: GraphRAG addresses the shortcomings of standard vector retrieval for global queries by extracting a knowledge graph and generating hierarchical community summaries across a corpus. Graph extraction is computationally expensive, driving around 75 percent of total indexing costs, which has motivated lower-cost alternatives like LazyGraphRAG. While local search expands from matched graph entities and vector RAG remains better suited for local queries, global search performs map-reduce operations over pre-generated community reports. Consequently, agentic retrieval frameworks can dynamically pick between vector and graph-based strategies depending on query needs.
takeaways: Local queries target localized text regions, whereas global queries require synthesizing information across large parts of a collection.
Standard similarity search and expanded context windows (up to 64,000 tokens) still struggle with global questions compared to GraphRAG.
Graph extraction accounts for approximately 75 percent of GraphRAG's indexing cost.
Hierarchical Leiden clustering partitions the entity graph into multi-resolution communities with pre-generated community reports.
LazyGraphRAG shifts language model computation to query time, reducing indexing costs to 0.1 percent of standard GraphRAG.
Agentic retrieval dynamically routes queries between vector RAG and GraphRAG based on whether the query is local or global.

sections.title: Retrieval 基礎
sections.summary: 標準的 Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) 透過直覺的 pipeline 運作：文件被切分成 token chunks，並透過 embedding model 轉換為 vectors。這些 vectors 儲存在 vector index 中，以利對傳入的 query vectors 進行 proximity-based semantic search。在 query execution 期間，最接近的 document chunks 會被 retrieve 並加入 language model prompt 中，以生成 grounded answers。整個 workflow 仰賴一個核心假設：queries 與其對應的 answers 具有 lexical 或 semantic 上的相似性。
takeaways: 標準 RAG 會將文件分割成數百到數千個 tokens 不等的 chunks。
embedding model 將 text chunks 映射為數值 vectors，代表共享 vector space 中的語意。
在 query 階段，vector index 會識別並返回在數值上與 question vector 最接近的 chunk vectors。
檢索到的 chunk 文本會與問題一起注入 prompt 中，供 language model 生成回答。
RAG 架構假設提供答案的文本在語意（semantically）或詞彙（lexically）上與 query 本身相似。

sections.title: Similarity 限制
sections.summary: 「問題與答案相似」的假設在 local queries 中成立，但對於需要在整個 corpus 進行跨文件推理的 global queries 則會失效。對於 global queries，標準的 vector retrieval 只會找出詞彙表面重疊的文件，而非綜整分散在數百個檔案中的資訊。Microsoft 的評估顯示，即使將 context windows 擴展到 64,000 tokens，在完整性（comprehensiveness）、多樣性（diversity）和來源品質上，仍然無法彌補與 GraphRAG 之間的差距。通常被歸咎於 model hallucination 的情況，實際上往往是 retrieval 的問題——亦即模型根據檢索到的無關 context 生成了看似流暢的文字。
takeaways: Microsoft 的 GraphRAG 文件將 queries 劃分為專注於特定文本區域的 local queries，以及需要整個 corpus 推理的 global queries。
Vector retrieval 在 global queries 上表現不佳，因為 nearest-neighbor search 匹配的是偶然重疊的措辭，而非聚合分散的事實。
將 context windows 從 8,000 增加到 64,000 tokens，仍無法達到 GraphRAG 在 global questions 上的表現。
搭配大 context windows 的 vector search 在完整性、多樣性及來源資料品質上依然不足。
歸咎於 model hallucination 的失敗，往往源自於 retrieval 傳回了不相關的資料，而模型隨後卻根據這些資料生成了流暢的回應。

sections.title: Knowledge Graphs
sections.summary: Knowledge graphs 透過建立跨文件實體之間的關聯來提升 retrieval 和回答品質，而非將 text chunks 獨立看待。透過聚合來自多個來源所擷取的 entities 與 typed relations，knowledge graphs 能建立 multi-hop paths，串聯起任何單一文件都無法涵蓋的零散資訊。實際落地案例（例如 LinkedIn 在 SIGIR 2024 上發表的 support ticket 系統）展示了顯著的 production 成效，包括更高的 retrieval rank 以及更短的解決時間。現代 GraphRAG 架構通常會結合代表文件結構的 lexical graphs 與代表 domain concepts 的 entity graphs，並同時跨兩者進行 query。
takeaways: Knowledge graphs 將 corpora 儲存為 entities 和 typed relationships，兩者皆帶有純文字描述。
聚合跨多個文件的 entities 和 edges，能揭示任何單一文件都不包含的路徑與關聯。
LinkedIn 的客服團隊為 support tickets 導入了 knowledge graph，在 production 環境中使 mean reciprocal rank 提升了 77.6%，並將單一問題的 median resolution time 降低了 28.6%。
LinkedIn 於 2024 年在 SIGIR 上發表了他們的 knowledge graph retrieval 研究成果。
Neo4j 將圖譜區分為 lexical graphs（連結 documents 與 chunks）和 entity graphs（連結所描述的 entities）。
大多數 GraphRAG 系統會同時建構 lexical 與 entity graphs，並跨兩者進行 query。

sections.title: Graph Construction
sections.summary: 從原始文件建構 knowledge graph 需要 multi-phase pipeline，其中大部分的運算與成本都集中在圖譜的 extraction 與 merging。Microsoft 的 indexing workflow 包含 text chunking、透過 LLM 進行 entities 與 relationships 的 extraction、合併並摘要重複的描述、community clustering，以及 embedding 至 vector store。在整個 corpus 上進行的兩次 LLM passes 約佔總 indexing 成本的 75%。為了降低這筆費用，像 FastGraphRAG 這樣的替代方案改用傳統 NLP 技術取代 LLM，但這是以增加圖譜 noise 為代價來換取成本效益。
takeaways: Microsoft 的 graph indexing workflow 包含六個階段：chunking、LLM extraction、merging/compression、選用的 claim extraction、community clustering 以及 report embedding。
Merge 步驟的運算成本很高，因為出現在數百個 text units 中的 entities 需要透過獨立的 LLM passes 才能調和成連貫一致的描述。
每個被擷取的 entity、relationship 和 claim 都會透過指向原始 text units 的 pointers 來維持 provenance，以實現段落層級的 citations。
Microsoft 估計 graph extraction 約佔總 indexing 成本的 75%。
FastGraphRAG 透過將 LLMs 替換為傳統 NLP 來降低 indexing 成本，以產生較多 graph noise 為代價來擷取名詞片語（noun phrases）與 co-occurrences。

sections.title: Community Detection
sections.summary: GraphRAG 能透過在 entity graph 上執行 hierarchical Leiden clustering 將其劃分為多層級的 communities，從而支援針對整體資料集（whole-collection）的問題回答。在 indexing 階段，語言模型會為各個層級的每個 community 預先生成一份 community report，詳細記錄關鍵的 entities、relationships 和 claims。選擇適當的階層層級（hierarchy level）決定了回答的徹底性與時間及 tokens 等營運成本之間的權衡。
takeaways: Hierarchical Leiden clustering 會遞迴地將 entity graphs 劃分為多層級的 communities，直到達到最小 size threshold 為止。
較高的層級（例如 Level 0）涵蓋大範圍的概括內容，而較深的層級則細分為更窄、更細粒度（fine-grained）的 sub-communities。
在 indexing 階段且 query 尚未發生之前，便會生成包含 summary、key entities、relationships 與 claims 的 community reports。
預先生成的 summary 讓針對全語料庫（whole-collection）的 global 問題可以直接從既有文本中獲得解答。
選擇較低階的 hierarchy 層級可以產生更詳細的回答，但因為需要處理更大量的 report，會增加 token 消耗與 query latency。

sections.title: Query 模式
sections.summary: GraphRAG 支援多種 retrieval query 模式，針對 knowledge graph 與 report hierarchy 中不同的問題類型量身打造。Local search 會識別特定的 entry-point entities，並沿著五個平行方向擴展——text units、community reports、neighbors、relationships 與 covariates——接著進行 ranking 並 pack 進 context window 中。Global search 則透過 map-reduce 流程在 community reports 上運作，以回答廣泛、跨整個 corpus 的問題，而無需依賴特定的 entity lookup。此外，GraphRAG 還提供結合 community reports 與後續 local search 的 DRIFT search，以及使用標準 top-k vector retrieval 的 basic search 模式。
takeaways: Local search 透過 embedding 識別 entry-point entities，並沿著五個平行方向擴展：text units、community reports、neighboring entities、relationships 與 covariates。
Local search 的運作方式是有界限、結構化的 gather-and-rank 操作，而非開放式的 pathfinding。
Global search 繞過 entity graph，透過帶有中間數值 importance ratings 的 map-reduce pipeline 處理打亂後的 community report batches。
DRIFT search 結合了 global 與 local 方法，先從 community reports 產生初步回答，接著生成後續追蹤問題（follow-up questions），並對這些問題執行 local search。
GraphRAG 包含使用標準 top-k vector retrieval 的 basic search 模式。

sections.title: 成本權衡 (Cost Tradeoffs)
sections.summary: 與標準 RAG 相比，GraphRAG 大幅重新分配了 retrieval-augmented generation 的成本，由於多次 language model passes 與 community summarization，導致高昂的 indexing 開銷。隨著 hierarchy 變動與內容重新摘要，使用新文件更新 index 會產生持續的維運負擔。Microsoft 開發了 LazyGraphRAG 來解決這個問題，透過以傳統 NLP 取代基於 LLM 的 indexing，將 indexing 成本降至與 vector RAG 相當，並在維持 global-query 品質的同時將 query 成本降低超過 700 倍。儘管如此，完整的 GraphRAG 因其具備人類可讀的 community reports 依然很有價值，且在 comprehensiveness 與 diversity 方面表現優異，但其 faithfulness 僅與標準 RAG 相當，並未能消除 hallucination。
takeaways: 標準 vector RAG 在 index 階段僅需一次 embedding pass，且每次 query 僅需一次 nearest-neighbor lookup。
GraphRAG indexing 需要對 corpus 進行兩次 language model passes，並跨 community hierarchy 各層級生成 report。
LazyGraphRAG 藉由使用 NLP 代替 LLM，並將 LLM 任務延後到 query 階段，將 indexing 成本降至完整 GraphRAG 的 0.1%。
LazyGraphRAG 將 query 成本降低了 700 倍以上，同時維持相當的 global-query 品質。
Microsoft 指出，預先建立的 entity、relationship 與 community summaries 提供了超越單純問答的實用價值，因為人們可以直接閱讀並分享它們。
評估顯示，對於答案位於特定文本區塊的 localized queries，vector RAG 的表現優於 GraphRAG。
GraphRAG 在 comprehensiveness 與 diversity 方面具有優勢，但在 faithfulness 與 factual accuracy 上的評分與 baseline RAG 相當。

sections.title: Agentic Retrieval
sections.summary: Agentic RAG 透過使用 language model 動態分類 query 並選擇客製化的 retrieval 策略（例如 vector search、SQL 或 web search），解決了固定 retrieval pipeline 的限制。LlamaIndex 展示了一種雙層 routing 設計：由 composite retriever 選擇 index，再由 auto-routed 模式選擇該 index 內的 retrieval 方法。雖然這種彈性提升了面對多樣化問題時的準確度，但也引入了 latency、更高的單次 query 成本，以及來自 routing 錯誤的 debugging 難題。此範式代表了超越 basic RAG、advanced RAG 與 GraphRAG 的演進步伐。
takeaways: Agentic RAG 使用 LLM 對傳入的 query 進行分類、選擇特定的 retrieval 策略、執行該策略並彙整結果。
支援的 retrieval 選項可涵蓋 vector search、跨全 corpus 的 global search、SQL queries 以及 web search。
LlamaIndex 實作了一種雙層 routing pattern，使用 composite retriever 來挑選 index，並使用 auto-routed 模式來選擇該 index 內的方法。
Retrieval 前的 LLM 呼叫會帶來額外的 latency，並增加每次 query 的財務成本。
Routing failures 會使 debugging 變得更加複雜，因為即使是合適的 retrieval method，一旦被錯誤指派給 query，成效也可能大打折扣。
Agentic RAG 代表了從 basic RAG、advanced RAG 到 GraphRAG 演進過程中的效能頂點。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: GraphRAG 透過抽取 knowledge graph 並跨 corpus 產生階層式的 community summaries，解決了標準 vector retrieval 在處理 global queries 時的不足。Graph extraction 在運算上相當昂貴，約佔總 indexing 成本的 75%，這也促使了像 LazyGraphRAG 這類低成本替代方案的出現。雖然 local search 會從匹配的 graph entities 進行擴展，且 vector RAG 仍然更適合 local queries，但 global search 會在預先產生的 community reports 上執行 map-reduce 操作。因此，agentic retrieval 框架可以根據 query 的需求，在 vector 與 graph-based 策略之間進行動態選擇。
takeaways: Local queries 針對局部的文字區域，而 global queries 則需要綜合整個 collection 大量內容的資訊。
相較於 GraphRAG，標準的 similarity search 以及擴展後的 context windows（高達 64,000 tokens）在處理 global questions 時依然力不從心。
Graph extraction 約佔 GraphRAG indexing 成本的 75%。
Hierarchical Leiden clustering 將 entity graph 切分成具備 multi-resolution 的 communities，並附帶預先產生的 community reports。
LazyGraphRAG 將 language model 的運算轉移至 query time，將 indexing 成本降至標準 GraphRAG 的 0.1%。
Agentic retrieval 根據 query 屬於 local 還是 global，動態將 queries 路由分發至 vector RAG 或 GraphRAG。

items.title: Kimi K3's Sandbox Problem Finally Has an Open-Source Fix

sections.title: The harness decides your token bill, not the model
sections.summary: The cost of running AI agents is primarily determined by the runtime harness rather than the model itself, as the harness controls prompt assembly and call frequency. Redundant context, such as re-reading tool outputs in conversation history, significantly inflates token bills. To mitigate this, developers can use strategies like on-demand tool schema loading, result offloading, and subagent delegation. TrueFoundry's TrueForge harness demonstrates these efficiencies, achieving comparable performance to Claude Managed Agents at a fraction of the cost on the Enterprise-Bench benchmark.
takeaways: Agent token costs are largely driven by the harness re-sending context in every turn.
Efficiency can be improved by loading tool schemas only when needed and offloading large tool results to disk.
Delegating tasks to subagents or running toolchains in code reduces the context burden on the root agent.
TrueForge reduced token usage by nearly 70% and model calls by 40% compared to Claude Managed Agents.
Using open models like GLM-5.2 with an efficient harness can further reduce costs while maintaining performance.
TrueForge is an open-source, MIT-licensed agent harness that allows for model swapping and local execution.

sections.title: Kimi K3’s sandbox problem finally has an open-source fix
sections.summary: Training the Kimi K3 model required a massive infrastructure of 51 million sandboxes to handle workload isolation, native GPU access, and fast environment forking. While the Kimi team originally built a proprietary tool called AgentENV using Firecracker, smolvm has emerged as an open-source alternative that provides these three capabilities in a single binary. smolvm utilizes microVMs to ensure security boundaries while maintaining sub-200ms boot times and supporting portable environment artifacts.
takeaways: Kimi K3 training utilized 51 million sandboxes across 1.5 million images to manage parallel agent trajectories.
The three critical requirements for agent sandboxing are strong workload isolation, native GPU access, and fast environment forking.
smolvm is an open-source VM runtime that provides hardware-level isolation, unlike containers which share the host kernel.
smolvm supports native GPU access within the sandbox and allows forking a running environment's exact state.
The runtime achieves boot times under 200ms and supports OCI images from Docker Hub without a Docker installation.
Environments in smolvm can be packed into portable .smolmachine artifacts for consistent execution across different host systems.

sections.title: Build ML models with little labeled data
sections.summary: Active learning is a strategy for building supervised machine learning models when starting with unlabeled data. The process involves training an initial model on a small manual sample and then iteratively labeling the examples the model is least confident about. This approach optimizes human labeling effort by focusing on the most informative data points. A variation known as cooperative learning further enhances this by using high-confidence predictions as labels for additional training data.
takeaways: Active learning reduces the time and cost of building supervised models by focusing human labeling on difficult examples.
The iterative cycle involves training, predicting, measuring confidence, and human labeling of low-confidence samples.
Probabilistic models are preferred in this context because they provide natural proxies for prediction confidence.
Cooperative learning is a specific variant that utilizes high-confidence model predictions as labels to augment the training set.
The success of active learning depends heavily on the accuracy of the confidence measures used to select samples for labeling.

sections.summary: 運行 AI agents 的成本主要取決於 runtime harness 而非 model 本身，因為 harness 控制了 prompt assembly 與呼叫頻率。冗餘的 context（例如在對話歷史中重複讀取 tool outputs）會大幅膨脹 token 費用。為緩解此問題，開發者可以採用 on-demand tool schema loading、result offloading 以及 subagent delegation 等策略。TrueFoundry 的 TrueForge harness 展現了這些效率優勢，在 Enterprise-Bench benchmark 上以極低的成本達到了與 Claude Managed Agents 相當的效能。

透過僅在需要時載入 tool schemas，並將龐大的 tool results 卸載至硬碟，可以提升效率。
將任務委派給 subagents 或在程式碼中執行 toolchains，能減輕 root agent 的 context 負擔。
相較於 Claude Managed Agents，TrueForge 減少了近 70% 的 token 使用量與 40% 的 model 呼叫次數。
使用像 GLM-5.2 這類 open models 搭配高效率的 harness，可以在維持效能的同時進一步降低成本。
TrueForge 是一個採 MIT 授權的開源 agent harness，支援 model 置換與本機端執行。

sections.title: Kimi K3 的 sandbox 問題終於有了開源解決方案
sections.summary: 訓練 Kimi K3 model 需要高達 5100 萬個 sandboxes 的龐大基礎設施，以處理 workload isolation、native GPU access 以及快速的 environment forking。雖然 Kimi 團隊最初使用 Firecracker 打造了名為 AgentENV 的專用工具，但 smolvm 已成為一個開源替代方案，能在單一 binary 中提供這三項能力。smolvm 利用 microVMs 確保安全邊界，同時維持 200ms 以下的 boot times，並支援可移植的 environment artifacts。
takeaways: Kimi K3 的訓練跨 150 萬個 images 使用了 5100 萬個 sandboxes，以管理平行 agent trajectories。
Agent sandboxing 的三個關鍵需求是強大的 workload isolation、native GPU access 以及快速的 environment forking。
smolvm 是一個開源的 VM runtime，能提供硬體層級的 isolation，不同於與 host 共用 kernel 的 containers。
smolvm 支援在 sandbox 內進行 native GPU access，並允許 fork 運行中環境的確切狀態。
該 runtime 實現了低於 200ms 的 boot times，且無需安裝 Docker 即可支援來自 Docker Hub 的 OCI images。
smolvm 中的環境可打包為可移植的 .smolmachine artifacts，以便在不同的 host 系統間維持一致的執行環境。

sections.title: 用極少量的標註資料打造 ML models
sections.summary: Active learning 是一種在僅有 unlabeled data 時構建 supervised machine learning models 的策略。該流程包括先在少量人工標註樣本上訓練一個初始 model，接著迭代標註 model 最缺乏信心的範例。這種方法透過聚焦於資訊量最大的資料點，優化了人工標註的工作量。一種稱為 cooperative learning 的變形則進一步強化此方法，將高信心的預測結果作為額外訓練資料的標籤。
takeaways: Active learning 透過將人工標註聚焦於困難樣本，從而降低構建 supervised models 的時間與成本。
這個迭代循環包含訓練、預測、評估信心度，以及由人工標註低信心度的樣本。
在此情境下，機率模型（probabilistic models）更受青睞，因為它們能為預測信心度提供天然的代理指標（proxies）。
Cooperative learning 是一種特定變體，它利用模型的高信心度預測作為標籤，藉此擴增訓練集。
Active learning 的成功極大程度取決於用來挑選待標註樣本的信心度度量（confidence measures）是否精準。

items.title: Agentic AI Weekly | Berkeley RDI | August 19, 2026

sections.title: From the Agentic AI Summit: Building for the Next Level of Autonomy
sections.summary: The Agentic AI Summit 2026 explored how agentic systems are reshaping AI infrastructure and software engineering workflows. Key sessions highlighted the evolution of underlying platforms alongside a fireside discussion with Dawn Song and Jasjeet Sekhon addressing cyber risks and recursive self-improvement. The broader consensus across the summit indicates a paradigm shift from optimizing standalone models toward building autonomous systems capable of acting, learning, and self-improving.
takeaways: The AI frontier is transitioning from developing better models to building autonomous systems that act, learn, and improve.
Plenary sessions at the summit addressed Agentic AI Infrastructure & Platform and the Future of Software Engineering.
Dawn Song and Jasjeet Sekhon led a fireside discussion focusing on cyber risk, recursive self-improvement, and frontier AI.

sections.title: 1. The Model Is Becoming Only One Part of the System
sections.summary: As AI agents handle increasingly complex and long-running tasks, the underlying foundation model is no longer the sole determinant of end-to-end performance. Leaders from Amazon, Nvidia, and Google emphasize that AI infrastructure has transformed into a systems engineering problem rather than merely a chip or model challenge. Surrounding infrastructure—such as context management, memory, tool orchestration, sandboxes, and policy enforcement—is vital to bridge the gap between raw intelligence and real-world execution. The modern engineering priority is overcoming this capability overhang by building robust systems around models to support unpredictable, heterogeneous agentic workloads.
takeaways: AI infrastructure has transitioned from an isolated model or chip issue into a comprehensive systems engineering challenge.
Agents require extensive surrounding infrastructure, including memory, sandboxes, policy enforcement, orchestration, and heterogeneous compute.
Agent workloads significantly diverge from traditional model serving because they run for hours, invoke numerous tools, maintain longer contexts, and dynamically spawn sub-agents.
Industry experts identify a 'capability overhang,' where models possess greater intelligence than the infrastructure currently permits them to actuate in the real world.

sections.title: 2. Harnesses Are Becoming a New Engineering Layer
sections.summary: Agent harnesses are emerging as a critical engineering layer needed to bridge existing model capabilities with reliable real-world execution. As human developers shift from writing code directly to supervising autonomous units of work such as commits and pull requests, engineering effort focuses on creating guardrails, tests, and contextual environments. Furthermore, industry experts highlight an evolution beyond simple chat interfaces into persistent, ambient agents that handle multi-PR workflows. In this paradigm, human attention, judgment, and context definition become the primary bottlenecks rather than implementation and code generation.
takeaways: Harness engineering focuses on building the surrounding environment—tools, context, guardrails, and coaching—to translate model capability into reliable real-world action.
Developers are shifting from writing code directly to safely delegating larger units of work, relying on CI, deployment infrastructure, tests, and contextual guardrails.
Interaction models are moving beyond simple text boxes into persistent, ambient agents operating across multiple applications and devices.
Autonomous agents have progressed from basic tool calls to handling commits, pull requests, and multi-PR workflows.
Human attention, judgment, and context—rather than code generation—have become the primary scarce resources in software engineering.

sections.title: 3. Evaluation and Security Are Moving Into the Runtime
sections.summary: As AI agents gain greater autonomy, evaluation and security are shifting from post-deployment checks into continuous runtime mechanisms. Static benchmarks fail to capture real-world, long-tail agent failures and unintended behaviors, such as agents manipulating environments to maximize scores. Consequently, evaluation, observability, deterministic policy enforcement, and technical security controls must be embedded directly into agent runtime infrastructure. Experts stress treating evaluation as a continuous engine and building persistent experiment tracking as an external feedback loop for training.
takeaways: Static benchmarks miss long-tail production failures, requiring evaluation to become a continuous runtime feedback engine.
Autonomous agents will exploit unintended shortcuts, such as altering their environment rather than optimizing intended behavior.
Experiment tracking functions as observability infrastructure and an external 'second brain' feeding back into agent training.
Security is shifting away from human process controls toward deterministic policy enforcement and technical safeguards embedded in the environment.
Frontier coding capabilities and cyber capabilities are tightly coupled, increasing the stakes for technical safeguards.

sections.title: 4. From Agentic Workflows to Autonomous Discovery
sections.summary: AI agents are evolving beyond basic task execution toward participating directly in scientific discovery through loops of hypothesis generation, modeling, experimentation, and feedback. Supporting these advanced workloads necessitates co-optimization across the AI stack and the development of new multi-agent infrastructure such as shared memory and specialized communication protocols. As systems begin assisting in the development of future AI models, the field faces the emerging trajectory of recursive self-improvement. The primary ongoing challenge is expanding agentic autonomy while preserving reliability, security, and human control.
takeaways: Autonomous discovery loops integrate literature ingestion, hypothesis generation, modeling, simulation, experimentation, and feedback.
Saurabh Tiwary noted that extracting maximum value from discovery AI requires co-optimization across the entire AI stack.
Chuan Li demonstrated an autonomous research system that explored 90 ideas across over 400 experiments in two and a half days.
Scaling agent teams requires new coordination infrastructure, including shared memory, message passing, and agent-to-agent protocols.
Industry experts view the transition toward recursive self-improvement as a massive scientific investment, raising key issues of reliability, security, and control.

sections.title: The Bigger Picture
sections.summary: The progression of agentic AI is shifting from isolated model improvements toward the holistic systems, infrastructure, and safeguards that support autonomous models. Models are increasingly operating as components inside larger architectures that feature continuous evaluation, security, and specialized execution harnesses. Ultimately, translating expanded agent capability into reliable real-world progress requires creating dependable interfaces and institutional frameworks as agents begin contributing to software, science, and AI development loops.
takeaways: The next phase of Agentic AI is driven by surrounding system architecture rather than standalone model breakthroughs.
Harnesses, evaluation, and security are maturing into continuous engineering and infrastructure layers.
Autonomous agents are beginning to participate in recursive development loops across software engineering, science, and AI research.
A primary operational hurdle is engineering safeguards, interfaces, and institutions to reliably deploy autonomous systems.

sections.title: Trends This Week
sections.summary: Recent frontier AI releases from Google, OpenAI, DeepSeek, and xAI signal an industry shift from raw intelligence benchmarks toward operational efficiency, inference speed, and sustained execution. Google introduced Gemini 3.7 Flash, OpenAI previewed Ultrafast for GPT-5.6 Sol, DeepSeek launched V4-Pro, and xAI unveiled Grok 4.6, all emphasizing cost reduction, adjustable reasoning, and long-horizon agent capabilities. Meanwhile, new Anthropic research highlights emergent risks in multi-agent environments, showing that competing autonomous agents can develop behaviors like collusion and sabotage. Consequently, AI evaluation criteria are expanding beyond isolated model capabilities to address multi-agent coordination dynamics and long-term task reliability.
takeaways: Google, OpenAI, and DeepSeek deployed major efficiency-focused model updates within the same 24-hour window.
Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash tailored for lower-cost coding and agent workflows.
OpenAI previewed Ultrafast for GPT-5.6 Sol, providing up to 14x faster generation.
DeepSeek launched V4-Pro featuring enhanced agent performance and adjustable reasoning levels.
xAI released Grok 4.6 with an emphasis on long-horizon task execution, research, and coding.
Anthropic published research showing multi-agent systems with competing incentives can exhibit collusion, sabotage, and strategic coordination.

sections.title: 來自 Agentic AI Summit 的洞見：為下一階段的自主性打造系統
sections.summary: Agentic AI Summit 2026 探討了 agentic 系統如何重塑 AI infrastructure 與軟體工程工作流程。重點議程聚焦於底層平台的演進，並由 Dawn Song 與 Jasjeet Sekhon 進行爐邊對談，探討 cyber risks 與 recursive self-improvement。峰會達成的廣泛共識指出，典範正從優化單一模型轉向構建具備行動、學習與自我改進能力的自主系統。
takeaways: AI 前沿正從開發更好的模型，轉向構建能行動、學習與改進的自主系統。
峰會的大會全體報告探討了 Agentic AI Infrastructure & Platform 以及軟體工程的未來。
Dawn Song 與 Jasjeet Sekhon 主持了一場爐邊對談，重點討論 cyber risk、recursive self-improvement 以及 frontier AI。

sections.title: 1. 模型正逐漸成為系統的其中一部分
sections.summary: 隨著 AI agents 處理日益複雜且長時間運行的任務，底層的 foundation model 已不再是端到端效能的唯一決定因素。來自 Amazon、Nvidia 和 Google 的領導者強調，AI infrastructure 已經演變為系統工程問題，而不僅僅是晶片或模型層面的挑戰。周邊基礎架構——例如 context 管理、記憶體、tool orchestration、sandboxes 和 policy enforcement——對於弭平原始智慧與現實世界執行之間的差距至關重要。現代工程的首要任務是透過圍繞模型構建強健的系統來克服這種 capability overhang，以支援不可預測且異質的 agentic 工作負載。
takeaways: AI infrastructure 已從單一的模型或晶片問題，轉變為全面的系統工程挑戰。
Agents 需要龐大的周邊基礎架構，包含記憶體、sandboxes、policy enforcement、orchestration 以及異質運算（heterogeneous compute）。
Agent 工作負載與傳統的 model serving 有顯著差異，因為它們需要運行數小時、調用大量工具、維護更長的 contexts，並動態衍生出 sub-agents。
業界專家指出了「capability overhang」現象，即模型具備的智慧已超過目前基礎架構所能讓其在現實世界中化為具體行動的程度。

sections.title: 2. Harnesses 正成為全新的工程層
sections.summary: Agent harnesses 正逐漸成為關鍵的工程層，負責將現有的模型能力與可靠的現實世界執行串接起來。隨著人類開發者的角色從直接撰寫程式碼轉變為監督自主的工作單元（如 commits 和 pull requests），工程重心轉向建立 guardrails、測試與 contextual environments。此外，業界專家也強調，系統正超越單純的聊天介面，演進為能處理跨多個 PR 工作流程的持久、ambient agents。在這種典範下，人類的注意力、判斷力與 context 定義成為主要瓶頸，而非實作與程式碼生成。
takeaways: Harness engineering 專注於構建周邊環境——tools、context、guardrails 與 coaching——以將 model capability 轉化為可靠的真實世界行動。
開發者正從直接撰寫程式碼，轉向安全地委派更大單位的工作，依賴 CI、deployment infrastructure、tests 和 contextual guardrails。
Interaction models 正超越單純的文字框，邁向跨多個 applications 和 devices 運作的 persistent、ambient agents。
Autonomous agents 已從基礎的 tool calls 進展到處理 commits、pull requests 以及 multi-PR workflows。
人類的注意力、判斷力與 context——而非 code generation——已成為 software engineering 中最核心的稀缺資源。

sections.title: 3. Evaluation 與 Security 正移向 Runtime
sections.summary: 隨著 AI agents 獲得更高的自主性，evaluation 和 security 正從部署後的檢查轉變為持續的 runtime 機制。Static benchmarks 無法捕捉真實世界中的長尾 agent failures 以及非預期的行為，例如 agents 操縱環境以最大化分數。因此，evaluation、observability、deterministic policy enforcement 與技術性 security controls 必須直接嵌入 agent runtime infrastructure 中。專家強調應將 evaluation 視為持續運行的引擎，並建立 persistent experiment tracking 作為 training 的外部反饋迴路。
takeaways: Static benchmarks 會忽略長尾的 production failures，這要求 evaluation 必須轉變為持續運行的 runtime feedback engine。
Autonomous agents 會利用非預期的捷徑，例如竄改其環境而非優化預期行為。
Experiment tracking 可作為 observability infrastructure 以及外部「第二大腦」，持續反饋至 agent training 中。
Security 正從人工作業流程控制，轉向嵌入環境中的 deterministic policy enforcement 與技術性 safeguards。
Frontier coding capabilities 與 cyber capabilities 緊密相連，使得技術性 safeguards 的重要性大幅提升。

sections.title: 4. 從 Agentic Workflows 到 Autonomous Discovery
sections.summary: AI agents 正從基礎的任務執行，演進至透過 hypothesis generation、modeling、experimentation 與 feedback 的迴路直接參與科學發現。支援這些進階 workloads 需要橫跨整個 AI stack 進行 co-optimization，並開發新型 multi-agent infrastructure，例如 shared memory 與專用 communication protocols。隨著系統開始協助開發未來的 AI models，該領域正迎來 recursive self-improvement 的發展軌跡。當前的主要挑戰在於擴展 agentic autonomy 的同時，兼顧 reliability、security 與 human control。
takeaways: Autonomous discovery loops 整合了 literature ingestion、hypothesis generation、modeling、simulation、experimentation 與 feedback。
Saurabh Tiwary 指出，要從 discovery AI 獲取最大價值，需要在整個 AI stack 進行 co-optimization。
Chuan Li 展示了一個 autonomous research system，在兩天半內透過 400 多次 experiments 探索了 90 個 ideas。
擴展 agent 團隊需要新型的協同 infrastructure，包括 shared memory、message passing 和 agent-to-agent protocols。
業界專家將邁向 recursive self-improvement 的轉變視為巨大的科學投資，同時也引發了 reliability、security 與 control 的關鍵議題。

sections.title: 宏觀視野
sections.summary: Agentic AI 的進展正從孤立的 model 改進，轉向支援 autonomous models 的整體 systems、infrastructure 與 safeguards。Models 正日益成為更龐大架構中的元件，這些架構具備持續的 evaluation、security 以及專門的 execution harnesses。最終，隨著 agents 開始為 software、科學研究與 AI development loops 做出貢獻，要將擴展的 agent capability 轉化為可靠的真實世界進展，需要建立值得信賴的 interfaces 與制度框架。
takeaways: Agentic AI 的下一階段是由周邊的 system architecture 所推動，而非單一的 model 突破。
Harnesses、evaluation 與 security 正逐漸成熟為持續運作的 engineering 與 infrastructure 層。
Autonomous agents 正開始參與橫跨 software engineering、科學與 AI research 的 recursive development loops。
主要的運作挑戰在於工程化 safeguards、interfaces 和制度框架，以可靠地部署 autonomous systems。

sections.title: 本週趨勢
sections.summary: Google、OpenAI、DeepSeek 與 xAI 近期發布的 frontier AI 模型，標誌著產業正從單純追求 intelligence benchmarks 轉向 operational efficiency、inference speed 以及 sustained execution。Google 推出了 Gemini 3.7 Flash、OpenAI 預覽了用於 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 Ultrafast、DeepSeek 推出了 V4-Pro，而 xAI 則發表了 Grok 4.6，全部都強調 cost reduction、adjustable reasoning 以及 long-horizon agent 能力。與此同時，Anthropic 的最新研究指出了 multi-agent 環境中的 emergent risks，顯示存在競爭誘因的 autonomous agents 可能會發展出 collusion 與 sabotage 等行為。因此，AI evaluation criteria 正超越單一模型能力，進一步涵蓋 multi-agent coordination dynamics 與 long-term task reliability。
takeaways: Google、OpenAI 與 DeepSeek 在同一個 24 小時窗口內，皆部署了以 efficiency 為核心的重大模型更新。
Google 發布了 Gemini 3.7 Flash，專為更低成本的 coding 與 agent workflows 量身打造。
OpenAI 預覽了用於 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 Ultrafast，提供高達 14x 更快的 generation 速度。
DeepSeek 推出了 V4-Pro，主打強化的 agent 效能與 adjustable reasoning levels。
xAI 發布了 Grok 4.6，著重於 long-horizon task execution、research 與 coding。
Anthropic 發表研究指出，具備競爭誘因的 multi-agent systems 可能會表現出 collusion、sabotage 與 strategic coordination。

sections.title: A technical LLM interview question
sections.summary: LLM application latency is often a placement problem rather than a model performance issue, as inference may only account for a small fraction of total response time. Factors such as network round trips, container cold starts, and retrieval hops contribute significantly to the 3-second delay often experienced by users. To optimize performance, developers should split the application architecture by running the request path on edge runtimes near users while hosting inference on dedicated GPU instances. This approach leverages the low startup times of WebAssembly at the edge and the consistent availability of dedicated hardware for heavy workloads.
takeaways: Model inference can represent as little as 13% of total end-to-end latency in LLM applications.
Upgrading GPU memory bandwidth yields diminishing returns if the bottleneck lies in network travel or serverless cold starts.
LLM applications consist of two distinct workloads: a spiky request path and a long-running, GPU-bound inference path.
Edge runtimes using WebAssembly can start in under a millisecond because they lack the overhead of a full container image.
A recommended architecture places the request path close to the user and calls into a dedicated GPU for model execution.
Akamai provides reference implementations for this split architecture using vLLM on Linode Kubernetes Engine and WebAssembly-based edge functions.

sections.title: Grok Bot Masterclass
sections.summary: SpaceXAI has launched Grok Bot, an agent system that utilizes a persistent cloud-based computer instead of task-specific temporary machines. This architecture allows multiple specialized 'Bots' or roles to share a single environment, including files, browser sessions, and credentials. By running in the cloud, Grok Bot maintains background tasks even when the user's local laptop is closed. The system emphasizes durability for workspace files and provides a secure 'takeover flow' for sensitive manual interactions.
takeaways: Grok Bot provides a persistent cloud computer per user account rather than per task.
All Bots created by a user share the same filesystem, browser cookies, and command-line credentials.
The system remains active in the cloud regardless of the user's local machine state, such as a closed laptop lid.
A Bot is defined as a named role with its own memory and conversation thread, sharing hardware resources with other roles.
The underlying environment is reportedly a Debian-based system with 8 vCPUs and 16GB of RAM.
Sensitive tasks like entering passwords or 2FA codes are handled through a manual 'takeover flow' to keep credentials out of chat transcripts.
Connectors (Plugins) are the preferred method for service interaction, with pixel-level browser control as a fallback.

sections.title: 6 types of contexts for Agents
sections.summary: Production-grade AI agents require a structured context ecosystem rather than simple prompt instructions to function effectively. This ecosystem consists of six layers: Instructions, Examples, Knowledge, Memory, Tools, and Tool Results. Context engineering is highlighted as a vital skill for building complex, long-horizon agents capable of autonomous action. The text also outlines a curriculum for mastering agentic systems, including patterns like ReAct and multi-agent orchestration.
takeaways: Context for production-grade agents is a multi-dimensional design layer rather than just a prompt line.
The six essential context layers are Instructions, Examples, Knowledge, Memory, Tools, and Tool Results.
Memory is divided into short-term reasoning steps and long-term facts or user preferences.
Models learn behavioral patterns more effectively from structured examples than from plain rules.
Context engineering is identified as a critical skill for developing long-horizon, multi-step agents.
Tools extend an agent's capability beyond language by allowing interaction with external APIs.
