sections.title: 一道 LLM 技術面試題
sections.summary: LLM 應用的 latency 往往是 placement 問題而非 model performance 問題，因為 inference 可能只佔整體 response time 的一小部分。像是 network round trips、container cold starts 以及 retrieval hops 等因素，都是造成使用者經常面臨 3 秒延遲的主要原因。為了最佳化效能，開發者應拆分 application 架構：在靠近使用者的 edge runtimes 上運行 request path，同時在 dedicated GPU instances 上託管 inference。這種做法結合了 WebAssembly 在 edge 端的超低啟動時間，以及專用硬體在處理高負載工作時的穩定可用性。
takeaways: 在 LLM 應用中，model inference 可能僅佔端到端（end-to-end）總 latency 的 13%。
若瓶頸在於 network travel 或 serverless cold starts，升級 GPU memory bandwidth 的邊際效益將會遞減。
LLM 應用包含兩種截然不同的 workloads：具備高突發性（spiky）的 request path，以及長時間運行且受限於 GPU（GPU-bound）的 inference path。
採用 WebAssembly 的 edge runtimes 可以在 1 毫秒內啟動，因為它們不需要承擔完整 container image 的 overhead。
建議的架構是將 request path 部署在靠近使用者的地方，並呼叫 dedicated GPU 進行 model execution。
Akamai 提供了這種拆分架構的參考實作，利用 Linode Kubernetes Engine 上的 vLLM 以及基於 WebAssembly 的 edge functions。

sections.title: Grok Bot 大師課
sections.summary: SpaceXAI 推出了 Grok Bot，這是一個採用 persistent cloud-based computer 而非針對特定任務建立臨時機器的 agent 系統。此架構允許多個專門的「Bots」或角色共享單一環境，包含檔案、browser sessions 和 credentials。透過在雲端運行，即使使用者的本地筆記型電腦關閉，Grok Bot 也能持續執行背景任務。該系統強調 workspace 檔案的 durability，並為敏感的手動操作提供安全的「takeover flow」。
takeaways: Grok Bot 為每個使用者帳號提供一台 persistent cloud computer，而非每個任務配置一台。
使用者建立的所有 Bots 皆共用相同的 filesystem、browser cookies 以及 command-line credentials。
無論使用者的本機端狀態為何（例如筆記型電腦螢幕闔上），系統都會在雲端保持 active。
一個 Bot 被定義為一個具名角色（named role），擁有自己的 memory 與 conversation thread，並與其他角色共用硬體資源。
據報導，底層環境是一個配備 8 個 vCPUs 和 16GB RAM 的 Debian-based 系統。
像輸入密碼或 2FA codes 這類敏感任務，會透過手動的「takeover flow」來處理，以避免 credentials 出現在 chat transcripts 中。
Connectors（Plugins）是服務互動的首選方式，並以 pixel-level 的瀏覽器控制作為 fallback。

sections.title: Agents 的 6 種 Context 類型
sections.summary: Production-grade 的 AI agents 需要結構化的 context 生態系統，而非單純的 prompt instructions 才能有效運作。此生態系統由六個層次組成：Instructions、Examples、Knowledge、Memory、Tools 以及 Tool Results。Context engineering 被強調為打造具備自主行動能力、可處理複雜且 long-horizon agents 的關鍵技能。內文亦概述了掌握 agentic systems 的課程規劃，包含像 ReAct 與 multi-agent orchestration 等 patterns。
takeaways: 對於 production-grade agents 而言，Context 是一個多維度的設計層（design layer），而非僅僅是一行 prompt。
六個核心的 context layers 分別是 Instructions、Examples、Knowledge、Memory、Tools 與 Tool Results。
Memory 被劃分為 short-term 的 reasoning steps，以及 long-term 的 facts 或 user preferences。
相較於純粹的 rules，Models 能更有效地從結構化的 examples 中學習 behavioral patterns。
Context engineering 被視為開發 long-horizon、multi-step agents 的關鍵技能。
Tools 透過允許與外部 APIs 互動，將 agent 的能力擴展到語言處理之外。

items.title: The New American AI Model Designed to be Customized

sections.title: Groundwork
sections.summary: This section explains four foundational concepts essential to understanding language model architecture: tokens, parameters, training, and layers. Tokens serve as the granular text chunks processed by models, while parameters are the internal numerical values iteratively refined during training. Training optimizes these parameters via next-token prediction, gradients, and backpropagation across vast quantities of text. Finally, inputs pass sequentially through stacked layers—such as the 66 layers in the Inkling model—where each layer executes an attention step followed by a feed-forward step.
takeaways: Tokens are text chunks typically smaller than sentences and often smaller than words, with uncommon words split into multiple tokens.
Parameters are individual learned numerical values that begin as random noise and are updated millions of times during training.
Training adjusts parameters based on next-token prediction errors using gradients computed simultaneously through backpropagation.
Layers are sequential processing stages where each layer contains both an attention step and a feed-forward step.
The Inkling model contains 66 stacked layers through which token representations pass sequentially.

sections.title: Sparsity
sections.summary: Inkling uses a Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture to decouple the cost of storing a model from the cost of running it. Instead of passing tokens through every feed-forward network, Inkling selects 6 out of 256 experts per token, following an approach published by DeepSeek. Across the full 975-billion-parameter model, only about 41 billion parameters (roughly 4 percent) are active during the processing of a single token. A full-precision checkpoint requires at least 2 TB of GPU memory across specialized hardware like NVIDIA B300 or H200 GPUs, while a quantized checkpoint reduces memory requirements to roughly 600 GB across four B300 cards.
takeaways: Inkling replaces the standard single feed-forward network per layer with 256 experts, running only six per token.
Inkling contains 975 billion total parameters, but only activates roughly 41 billion parameters (~4%) per token.
Thinking Machines implemented Inkling's Mixture of Experts design largely based on an approach published by DeepSeek.
Inkling's full-precision checkpoint requires at least 2 TB of combined GPU memory, runnable on 8 NVIDIA B300 cards or 16 NVIDIA H200 cards.
A quantized checkpoint version of Inkling requires around 600 GB of memory and fits onto four NVIDIA B300 cards.

sections.title: Routing
sections.summary: In Mixture of Experts architectures, routers score candidate experts to select a top subset for processing each token, but positive feedback loops during training can cause routing collapse where only a handful of experts are utilized. Traditional auxiliary balance loss penalties degrade output quality by generating gradients that conflict with the primary prediction task. Thinking Machines resolves this by adopting an approach originally introduced by Wang and colleagues and utilized by DeepSeek, which adjusts expert selection scores using non-backpropagated bias values updated by token counts. This keeps expert load balanced without compromising gradient updates, while two additional shared experts run unconditionally alongside the six routed experts.
takeaways: Inkling's router scores 256 experts using a sigmoid function and picks the top six to run for each token.
Unmitigated expert selection can lead to routing collapse, where a small fraction of experts dominate compute while the rest stay underdeveloped.
Traditional load-balancing penalties create competing gradients against the next-token prediction objective, often degrading text quality.
Thinking Machines and DeepSeek use a technique by Wang et al. that applies an external bias to expert selection scores without affecting output weighting or backpropagation.
Every token is processed by eight total experts: six routed experts and two shared experts, whose scores are normalized together.

sections.title: Attention
sections.summary: Standard attention computation scales quadratically with sequence length, making a one-million-token context window computationally prohibitive across 66 layers. To address this, Inkling alternates between sliding-window attention layers and full-attention layers in a 5:1 ratio, using 55 sliding-window and 11 full-attention layers. Long-range information flows through the full-attention layers, while sliding-window layers handle local context at lower computational cost. Inkling also utilizes eight key-value heads to reduce memory overhead during generation.
takeaways: Standard attention comparisons scale quadratically with sequence length, reaching roughly one trillion comparisons per layer for one million tokens.
Inkling supports a context window of one million tokens across 66 total layers.
Inkling alternates sliding-window layers and full-attention layers at a 5:1 ratio, comprising 55 sliding-window layers and 11 full-attention layers according to vLLM project notes.
Long-range dependencies are propagated through the 11 full-attention layers placed at regular intervals such as layers 6, 12, and 18.
Inkling employs 8 key-value heads to reduce memory consumption during text generation.

sections.title: Position
sections.summary: Attention mechanisms lack inherent sequence order information, necessitating positional representation methods like Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE). However, RoPE can struggle to extrapolate to context lengths far exceeding those seen during training because novel rotation angles fall outside the model's learned range. To address this for long sequences, Thinking Machines chose an older relative positional encoding scheme in the style of Shaw et al. for the Inkling model. This approach adds learned distance-based bias values directly to attention scores and clamps distances past a specific cutoff, avoiding the need to extrapolate unfamiliar values.
takeaways: Attention query and key comparisons contain no intrinsic order information, requiring explicit positional encoding.
Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) works by rotating queries and keys by angles proportional to sequence position, which can fail when extrapolating beyond training context windows.
The Inkling model utilizes a relative position scheme inspired by Shaw and colleagues instead of the modern standard RoPE.
The relative positioning method adds a learned value corresponding to token distance directly to attention scores, mapping all distances past a fixed cutoff to a single shared parameter.
Thinking Machines observed that this relative scheme both performed better and extrapolated to longer contexts more effectively than RoPE.

sections.title: Convolutions
sections.summary: Inkling incorporates a localized convolution operation with a sliding window of four tokens to handle local sequence mixing. Because standard attention mechanisms have no built-in bias toward adjacent tokens, convolutions supply this local context structurally using learned weights. Thinking Machines inserts these convolutions onto the keys and values within attention layers as well as onto attention and feed-forward outputs before they rejoin the main residual path. This enables attention to reserve its learning capacity for complex dependencies rather than basic local proximity.
takeaways: Inkling utilizes a convolution with a window of four positions to mix a token with its three preceding neighbors using learned weights.
Convolutions provide structural local mixing without requiring attention to learn that adjacent tokens are related.
Thinking Machines places convolutions on the keys and values inside each attention layer.
Convolutions are applied to the outputs of attention and feed-forward blocks before rejoining the main model stream.
Pre-mixing immediate context using convolutions frees attention capacity to focus on dependencies that genuinely require learning.

sections.title: Multimodality
sections.summary: Inkling processes images and audio directly without relying on separately pretrained encoder networks. Audio is represented as mel spectrograms and quantized via the dMel method, which requires no pretraining. Images are divided into 40x40 pixel patches and processed independently through a four-stage hMLP stem with minimal compute overhead. Both modalities pass through a lightweight conversion layer and merge into a single sequence alongside text tokens, with all multimodal components trained from scratch alongside the base model.
takeaways: Inkling eschews separately pretrained encoders for vision and audio in favor of an end-to-end architecture trained from scratch.
Audio processing uses the dMel method to round mel spectrogram loudness values into fixed levels without requiring prior training.
Images are segmented into 40x40 pixel patches and fed into an hMLP stem, adding less than one percent to compute overhead.
Multimodal inputs pass through a lightweight conversion layer to join text tokens across the model's 66 layers.
Thinking Machines first implemented this multimodal approach two months prior to Inkling in a real-time interaction system.

sections.title: Effort
sections.summary: Thinking Machines introduced an adjustable effort setting between 0 and 1 to control how long the Inkling model reasons before answering. Rather than enforcing a hard token budget, this behavior was trained into Inkling via reinforcement learning by varying token-cost penalties based on the effort prompt. Mechanically, the effort level is inserted as a system message before the conversation starts, independent of the maximum token limit. On the Terminal Bench 2.1 coding benchmark, Inkling achieves the same performance as NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Ultra using approximately one-third of the tokens.
takeaways: Effort is parameterized as a value from 0 to 1, with documented presets including 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.7, 0.9 (default), and 0.99.
The effort level is passed mechanically as an initial system message prior to the conversation.
The effort response was trained via reinforcement learning by varying per-token penalty costs corresponding to different effort labels.
Effort operates independently of the maximum token limit and encourages longer reasoning without offering hard guarantees on length or quality.
On Terminal Bench 2.1, Inkling matches the score of NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Ultra while generating roughly a third of the tokens.

sections.title: Tradeoffs
sections.summary: The architectural choices behind Inkling involve explicit trade-offs between computational efficiency, hardware requirements, and model behavior. Sparse routing and mostly-local attention lower per-token compute costs and enable large context windows, but they enforce high memory footprints and limited layer context. Furthermore, adopting relative position encoding broke compatibility with the prevailing RoPE-based serving infrastructure. While Thinking Machines acknowledges that other models surpass Inkling in baseline strength, Inkling is optimized for direct adaptation and fine-tuning via day-one quantized checkpoints.
takeaways: Sparse routing reduces per-token inference cost but keeps the minimum memory footprint high because the full model must be loaded.
Mostly-local attention facilitates a 1-million-token context window at the cost of providing most layers with a restricted sequence perspective.
Adopting relative position encoding solved extrapolation issues but required engineering new support in serving frameworks configured for RoPE.
Open weights are provided without training datasets, code, or exact training recipes, limiting auditing and full reproducibility.
Thinking Machines recommends employing external moderation tools for consumer deployments rather than relying on built-in model refusals.
Inkling is specifically targeted at customizable enterprise use cases through early fine-tuning support and quantized checkpoints.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: Inkling's architecture separates total parameter storage from per-token compute, storing 975 billion parameters while running approximately 41 billion active parameters. The model balances expert routing by applying a selection bias without including it in output weighting, avoiding conflicting training objectives. Its long-context design utilizes 55 sliding-window layers alongside 11 full-attention layers paired with relative position representations. Furthermore, reasoning effort is formulated as a trained setting, enabling benchmark evaluations to function across an adjustable performance curve.
takeaways: Inkling stores 975 billion total parameters while activating approximately 41 billion per token.
Expert load balancing applies bias during selection but omits it during output weighting to avoid auxiliary training conflicts.
The model handles long contexts using 55 sliding-window layers and 11 full-attention layers for long-range information propagation.
Relative position encoding allows tokens separated by large distances to rely on frequently observed distance values.
Reasoning effort can be configured as a trained setting, producing a variable benchmark curve rather than a fixed score.

sections.title: Groundwork
sections.summary: 本節說明理解 language model architecture 必備的四個基礎概念：tokens、parameters、training 與 layers。Tokens 是模型處理的細粒度文字塊（granular text chunks），而 parameters 則是訓練過程中迭代微調的內部數值。Training 透過大量文字上的 next-token prediction、gradients 與 backpropagation 來最佳化這些 parameters。最後，輸入會依序通過疊加的 layers——例如 Inkling 模型中的 66 個 layers——其中每個 layer 都會執行一個 attention 步驟，接著執行一個 feed-forward 步驟。
takeaways: Token 是文字區塊，通常小於句子，且往往小於單字，罕見字詞會被拆分成多個 token。
Parameter 是個別學習得來的數值，一開始為隨機雜訊，並在 training 期間更新數百萬次。
Training 會依據 next-token prediction 的誤差，利用透過 backpropagation 同時計算出的 gradient 來調整 parameter。
Layer 是循序處理的階段，其中每個 layer 都包含一個 attention 步驟與一個 feed-forward 步驟。
Inkling 模型包含 66 個 stacked layers，token representations 會循序通過這些 layer。

sections.title: Sparsity
sections.summary: Inkling 採用 Mixture of Experts (MoE) 架構，將儲存模型的成本與執行模型的成本解耦。Inkling 並非讓 token 通過每個 feed-forward network，而是依循 DeepSeek 發表的方法，針對每個 token 從 256 個 experts 中選出 6 個。在整個 975-billion-parameter 模型中，處理單一 token 時只有約 41 billion 個 parameter（約 4%）處於 active 狀態。Full-precision checkpoint 需要在 NVIDIA B300 或 H200 GPU 等專用硬體上具備至少 2 TB 的 GPU memory，而 quantized checkpoint 則可將 memory 需求降低至四張 B300 卡約 600 GB。
takeaways: Inkling 將每個 layer 的標準單一 feed-forward network 替換為 256 個 experts，每個 token 僅執行六個。
Inkling 總共包含 975 billion 個 parameter，但每個 token 僅活化約 41 billion 個 parameter（~4%）。
Thinking Machines 實作 Inkling 的 Mixture of Experts 設計時，主要基於 DeepSeek 發表的方法。
Inkling 的 full-precision checkpoint 需要至少 2 TB 的合併 GPU memory，可在 8 張 NVIDIA B300 卡或 16 張 NVIDIA H200 卡上執行。
Inkling 的 quantized checkpoint 版本需要約 600 GB 的 memory，可放入四張 NVIDIA B300 卡中。

sections.title: Routing
sections.summary: 在 Mixture of Experts 架構中，router 會對候選 experts 進行評分，以選出 top subset 來處理每個 token，但 training 期間的正回饋循環可能會導致 routing collapse，也就是只有少數幾個 experts 被使用。傳統的 auxiliary balance loss 懲罰會產生與主要 prediction 任務衝突的 gradient，進而降低輸出品質。Thinking Machines 透過採用 Wang 等人最初提出並由 DeepSeek 使用的方法解決了這個問題，該方法使用依 token 計數更新且不經過 backpropagation 的 bias 值來調整 expert selection 分數。這樣可以在不影響 gradient 更新的情況下維持 expert load balanced，同時還有兩個額外的 shared experts 與六個 routed experts 一起無條件執行。
takeaways: Inkling 的 router 使用 sigmoid 函數對 256 個 experts 進行評分，並為每個 token 挑選 top six 來執行。
未受約束的 expert selection 可能會導致 routing collapse，其中極少數 experts 主導了運算，而其餘 experts 則維持未充分訓練狀態。
傳統的 load-balancing 懲罰會產生與 next-token prediction 目標競爭的 gradient，通常會降低文字品質。
Thinking Machines 與 DeepSeek 採用了 Wang 等人提出的一項技術，將外部 bias 套用至 expert selection 分數，而不會影響 output weighting 或 backpropagation。
每個 token 都由總共八個 experts 處理：六個 routed experts 和兩個 shared experts，其分數會一起進行 normalization。

sections.title: Attention
sections.summary: 標準 attention 運算會隨 sequence length 呈平方級增長，這使得在 66 個 layers 上建立 one-million-token context window 的運算成本高到令人卻步。為了解決這個問題，Inkling 以 5:1 的比例交替使用 sliding-window attention layers 與 full-attention layers，包含 55 個 sliding-window layers 與 11 個 full-attention layers。Long-range 資訊會流經 full-attention layers，而 sliding-window layers 則以較低的運算成本處理 local context。Inkling 還利用八個 key-value heads 來降低 generation 期間的 memory overhead。
takeaways: 標準 attention 比較的複雜度會隨 sequence length 呈平方級增長，一百萬個 token 在每個 layer 的比較次數約達到一兆次。
Inkling 在總共 66 個 layers 中支援一百萬個 token 的 context window。
根據 vLLM 專案筆記，Inkling 以 5:1 的比例交替配置 sliding-window layers 與 full-attention layers，由 55 個 sliding-window layers 與 11 個 full-attention layers 組成。
Long-range dependencies 會透過等間距放置（例如第 6、12 和 18 層）的 11 個 full-attention layers 進行傳遞。
Inkling 採用 8 個 key-value heads，以減少文字生成期間的記憶體消耗。

sections.title: Position
sections.summary: Attention mechanisms 本身缺乏 sequence order 資訊，因此需要如 Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) 這類 positional representation 方法。然而，當 context lengths 遠遠超出訓練時所見的長度時，RoPE 在外推（extrapolate）上可能會遇到困難，因為新的旋轉角度落在了模型已學習的範圍之外。為了解決長序列的此問題，Thinking Machines 在 Inkling 模型中採用了 Shaw et al. 風格的早期 relative positional encoding 機制。此方法將基於距離學習到的 bias 值直接加到 attention scores 上，並對超過特定 cutoff 的距離進行 clamp，從而避免了外推未見過數值的需求。
takeaways: Attention 中 query 與 key 的比較不包含內建的順序資訊，因此需要顯式的 positional encoding。
Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) 的運作方式是依據 sequence position 等比例旋轉 query 與 key 的角度，但在外推至超出訓練 context windows 時可能會失效。
Inkling 模型採用了受 Shaw 等人啟發的 relative position 機制，而非現代標準的 RoPE。
此 relative positioning 方法會將對應於 token 距離的學習數值直接加至 attention scores 中，並將所有超過固定 cutoff 的距離映射至單一共享參數。
Thinking Machines 觀察到，此 relative 機制不僅表現更佳，且比 RoPE 能更有效地外推至更長的 contexts。

sections.title: Convolutions
sections.summary: Inkling 整合了滑動窗口為 4 個 token 的 localized convolution 操作，以處理局部 sequence mixing。由於標準的 attention mechanisms 對相鄰 token 沒有內建的 bias，convolution 能透過已學習的權重在結構上提供這種 local context。Thinking Machines 將這些 convolutions 插入到 attention layers 內部的 key 與 value 上，以及在 attention 與 feed-forward 輸出重新匯入主 residual path 之前。這讓 attention 能保留其學習容量給複雜的 dependencies，而非基礎的 local proximity。
takeaways: Inkling 使用窗口大小為 4 個位置的 convolution，透過已學習的權重將一個 token 與其前 3 個相鄰 token 進行 mixing。
Convolutions 提供了結構性的 local mixing，而無需依賴 attention 去學習相鄰 token 之間的關聯。
Thinking Machines 在每個 attention layer 內部的 key 與 value 上配置了 convolutions。
在重新匯入主模型流（main model stream）之前，convolutions 會被應用於 attention 與 feed-forward blocks 的輸出。
使用 convolutions 預先混合鄰近 context，能釋放 attention 的容量，讓其專注於真正需要學習的 dependencies。

sections.title: Multimodality
sections.summary: Inkling 直接處理影像與音訊，無需依賴個別預訓練的 encoder networks。音訊以 mel spectrograms 表示，並透過無需預訓練的 dMel 方法進行量化。影像被劃分為 40x40 像素的 patches，並透過四階段的 hMLP stem 獨立處理，compute overhead 極低。兩種模態都通過輕量級的 conversion layer，並與 text tokens 一起合併為單一序列，所有的 multimodal 組件均與 base model 一同從頭訓練（trained from scratch）。
takeaways: Inkling 捨棄了個別預訓練的 vision 與 audio encoders，轉而採用從頭訓練（trained from scratch）的 end-to-end 架構。
音訊處理採用 dMel 方法將 mel spectrogram 響度值四捨五入至固定層級，無需事先訓練。
影像被分割為 40x40 像素的 patches 並輸入至 hMLP stem，增加的 compute overhead 不到 1%。
Multimodal 輸入通過輕量級的 conversion layer，以加入貫穿該模型 66 個 layers 的 text tokens。
Thinking Machines 在推出 Inkling 的兩個月前，就已首次在即時互動系統中實作了這種 multimodal 方法。

sections.title: Effort
sections.summary: Thinking Machines 引入了介於 0 到 1 之間的可調式 effort 設定，以控制 Inkling 模型在回答前的推理（reasoning）時長。這項行為並非強制設定嚴格的 token budget，而是透過 reinforcement learning、根據 effort prompt 動態調整 token-cost penalties 來訓練 Inkling。在機制上，effort level 會在對話開始前作為 system message 插入，獨立於 maximum token limit。在 Terminal Bench 2.1 程式編碼 benchmark 上，Inkling 僅使用約三分之一的 token 就達到了與 NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 相同的效能。
takeaways: Effort 被參數化為介於 0 到 1 之間的值，文件中記錄的 presets 包括 0、0.1、0.2、0.7、0.9（預設）與 0.99。
effort level 是在對話開始前，以初始 system message 的方式制式傳入。
effort response 是透過 reinforcement learning 進行訓練，方法是針對不同的 effort labels 調整對應的 per-token penalty costs。
Effort 獨立於 maximum token limit 運作，並鼓勵進行更長的 reasoning，但不對長度或品質提供 hard guarantees。
在 Terminal Bench 2.1 上，Inkling 達到了與 NVIDIA 的 Nemotron 3 Ultra 相當的分數，同時生成的 token 數僅約為其三分之一。

sections.title: Tradeoffs
sections.summary: Inkling 背後的架構選擇涉及在運算效率、硬體需求與模型行為之間的明確 trade-offs。Sparse routing 與 mostly-local attention 降低了 per-token compute costs 並實現了大型 context windows，但它們也帶來了高 memory footprints 與受限的 layer context。此外，採用 relative position encoding 破壞了與主流基於 RoPE 的 serving infrastructure 的相容性。儘管 Thinking Machines 承認其他模型在 baseline strength 上超越了 Inkling，但 Inkling 透過首日提供的 quantized checkpoints，針對直接適應與 fine-tuning 進行了最佳化。
takeaways: Sparse routing 降低了 per-token 的 inference cost，但由於必須載入完整模型，因此最低 memory footprint 依然居高不下。
Mostly-local attention 實現了 100 萬 token 的 context window，代價是大多數層只能獲得受限的 sequence perspective。
採用 relative position encoding 解決了 extrapolation 問題，但需要在針對 RoPE 配置的 serving frameworks 中額外開發支援。
雖然提供了 open weights，但未附帶 training datasets、程式碼或確切的 training recipes，限制了審查與完全可重現性（reproducibility）。
Thinking Machines 建議在面向消費者的部署中採用外部 moderation tools，而非依賴模型內建的 refusals 機制。
Inkling 透過初期的 fine-tuning 支援與 quantized checkpoints，特別鎖定可客製化的企業級應用場景。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: Inkling 的架構將總參數儲存與 per-token compute 分離，儲存了 9750 億個參數，同時僅運行約 410 億個 active parameters。該模型透過在選擇時引入 selection bias、但在 output weighting 中將其排除來平衡 expert routing，避免了衝突的 training objectives。其 long-context 設計採用了 55 個 sliding-window layers 以及 11 個 full-attention layers，並搭配 relative position representations。此外，reasoning effort 被設計為一種可訓練的設定，使 benchmark evaluations 能夠在可調整的效能曲線上運作。
takeaways: Inkling 儲存了 9750 億個總參數，同時每個 token 僅活化約 410 億個參數。
Expert load balancing 在 selection 階段引入 bias，但在 output weighting 階段將其排除，以避免 auxiliary training 的衝突。
該模型使用 55 個 sliding-window layers 以及 11 個 full-attention layers 來處理 long contexts，以進行長距離的資訊傳遞（propagation）。
Relative position encoding 讓距離遙遠的 token 能夠依賴頻繁觀察到的距離數值。
Reasoning effort 可配置為一種經過訓練的設定，能產生可變的 benchmark 曲線而非固定分數。

items.title: How a GPU Actually Works

sections.title: Mock infrastructure for AI apps
sections.summary: AI application development often incurs high costs due to real API calls during continuous integration (CI) cycles. CopilotKit has introduced aimock, an open-source tool that provides a local mock server to replace these expensive calls. Unlike static mocks, aimock maintains schema accuracy by daily testing its responses against actual provider APIs and official client libraries. This approach allows developers to run offline tests while ensuring their integrations remain compatible with the latest provider updates across multiple platforms.
takeaways: CI runs for AI applications frequently incur significant costs by making real requests to LLM providers.
Traditional manual mocking often fails when providers update their API schemas without notice.
aimock is an open-source project by CopilotKit that serves as a local mock server for various AI APIs.
The tool ensures schema validity by running daily comparisons between its mock responses and real API outputs.
When schema changes are detected, aimock updates its built-in definitions and releases a patch via npm.
aimock supports a wide range of providers and tools, including OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, and vector databases like Pinecone.

sections.title: How a GPU actually works
sections.summary: GPU performance during LLM inference is primarily constrained by memory bandwidth rather than raw computational power. While arithmetic operations are inexpensive, fetching data from memory is costly, leading to a 'memory-bound' state where arithmetic units remain idle. Current hardware requires approximately 300 operations per byte to reach peak efficiency, yet token generation typically performs only two operations per weight. Consequently, common optimization techniques like batching and quantization are designed to either increase the work done per fetch or reduce the total data transferred.
takeaways: GPU utilization metrics can be misleading because a chip waiting for data appears identical to one performing active computation.
The break-even point for modern hardware efficiency is roughly 300 operations per byte at 16-bit precision.
Token generation for a 70B model is heavily memory-bound, achieving only about 24 tokens per second on hardware with 3.3 TB/s bandwidth.
The GPU memory hierarchy consists of the register file, shared memory, L2 cache, and HBM.
Optimization strategies like FlashAttention, fusion, and quantization all focus on improving the ratio of arithmetic operations to memory fetches.

sections.title: Prefix caching vs CacheBlend
sections.summary: Prefix caching is a powerful optimization for stable prompts, offering up to 90% cost reduction, but it fails when document order changes or multiple documents are combined due to its strict byte-for-byte prefix requirement. CacheBlend, a new method from the LMCache project, solves this by allowing modular reuse of cached document states and only recomputing boundary tokens. This approach enables 2-4x faster processing for multi-document queries without quality loss. LMCache serves as an open-source management layer that integrates this technology with major inference engines like vLLM and SGLang.
takeaways: Prefix caching requires an exact byte-for-byte match, making it fragile for RAG and dynamic conversation histories.
Alibaba Cloud data indicates that 10% of KV cache blocks account for 77% of all cache hits.
CacheBlend allows for the reuse of document caches regardless of their order or surrounding context by selectively recomputing boundary tokens.
CacheBlend provides a 2x to 4x speedup for multi-document queries compared to standard prefix caching.
LMCache is an open-source cache management layer that operates outside the inference engine to support vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM.
The CacheBlend research paper received the Best Paper Award at EuroSys 2025.

sections.title: AI 應用的 Mock infrastructure
sections.summary: AI 應用開發常因 continuous integration (CI) 週期中的真實 API 呼叫而產生高昂成本。CopilotKit 推出了 aimock，這是一款開源工具，提供本機 mock server 來取代這些昂貴的呼叫。與 static mocks 不同，aimock 每天針對實際的 provider API 與官方 client libraries 測試其回應，以維持 schema 的精確度。這種做法讓開發者能進行離線測試，同時確保跨多平台的整合與最新的 provider 更新保持相容。
takeaways: AI 應用的 CI runs 經常因為向 LLM providers 發出真實 request 而產生高昂成本。
當 providers 在未預先通知的情況下更新 API schemas 時，傳統的手動 mocking 往往會失效。
aimock 是 CopilotKit 的開源專案，可作為各類 AI APIs 的 local mock server。
該工具透過每天比對其 mock responses 與真實 API outputs，以確保 schema 的有效性。
當偵測到 schema 變更時，aimock 會更新其內建定義，並透過 npm 發布 patch。
aimock 支援廣泛的 providers 與工具，包括 OpenAI、Claude、Gemini 以及像 Pinecone 這類的 vector databases。

sections.title: GPU 實際上是如何運作的
sections.summary: 在 LLM inference 期間，GPU 效能主要受限於 memory bandwidth，而非原始運算能力。雖然 arithmetic operations 的成本低廉，但從 memory 抓取資料卻非常昂貴，導致運算單元處於閒置的「memory-bound」狀態。現有硬體大約需要每 byte 執行 300 次運算才能達到峰值效率，但 token generation 通常每個 weight 僅執行兩次運算。因此，像 batching 與 quantization 這類常見的 optimization 技術，目的都在於增加每次 fetch 的運算量，或是減少資料傳輸的總量。
takeaways: GPU utilization 指標可能會產生誤導，因為等待資料的晶片在狀態上看來與正在進行主動運算的晶片完全相同。
在 16-bit precision 下，現代硬體效率的損益平衡點大約是每 byte 300 次運算。
70B 模型的 token generation 嚴重受限於 memory-bound，在具備 3.3 TB/s bandwidth 的硬體上也僅能達到每秒約 24 個 tokens。
GPU 的 memory hierarchy 由 register file、shared memory、L2 cache 與 HBM 組成。
像 FlashAttention、fusion 和 quantization 等 optimization 策略，都聚焦於提高 arithmetic operations 與 memory fetches 的比例。

sections.title: Prefix caching vs CacheBlend
sections.summary: Prefix caching 是針對穩定 prompt 的強大 optimization，可降低高達 90% 的成本；但由於它嚴格要求 byte-for-byte 的 prefix 相符，當文件順序變動或組合多份文件時便會失效。LMCache 專案提出的全新方法 CacheBlend 解決了這個問題，它允許模組化重複使用已快取的 document states，並僅重新計算 boundary tokens。這種方法能在不損失品質的前提下，讓 multi-document queries 的處理速度提升 2 到 4 倍。LMCache 作為開源管理層，將此技術與 vLLM 和 SGLang 等主流 inference engines 整合。
takeaways: Prefix caching 需要完全一致的 byte-for-byte 匹配，這讓它在面對 RAG 和動態對話歷史時顯得相當脆弱。
Alibaba Cloud 的數據顯示，10% 的 KV cache blocks 佔了所有 cache hits 的 77%。
CacheBlend 透過選擇性重新計算 boundary tokens，讓 document caches 無論順序或周遭 context 為何都能被重複利用。
與標準 prefix caching 相比，CacheBlend 為 multi-document queries 帶來了 2 到 4 倍的加速。
LMCache 是一個開源 cache 管理層，運作於 inference engine 之外，可支援 vLLM、SGLang 和 TensorRT-LLM。
CacheBlend 的研究論文榮獲 EuroSys 2025 的 Best Paper Award。

items.title: Waymo vs Tesla: Two Ways to Build Self-Driving Cars

sections.title: Sensing
sections.summary: Autonomous vehicle perception fundamentally contrasts direct distance measurements from sensors like lidar against derived depth calculations from camera arrays. Waymo incorporates a redundant multi-sensor suite consisting of lidar, radar, and cameras to ensure reliability across adverse environmental conditions like rain and ice. In contrast, Tesla relies strictly on a pure vision strategy powered by exterior cameras and neural networks. Even as Waymo trims its camera count in sixth-generation vehicles through higher-resolution imagers, it retains sensor redundancy, highlighting the industry tradeoff between expensive direct physical measurements and cost-effective but error-prone derived estimates.
takeaways: Cameras require depth to be computed from pixel arrangements, creating potential ambiguity between object size and distance.
Lidar directly measures physical distance via laser pulse return times, producing a 3D point cloud.
Waymo's sixth-generation system includes 13 cameras, four lidar units, six radar units, and audio receivers, reaching up to 500 meters of overlapping coverage.
Waymo reduced its camera count from 29 on the fifth-generation Jaguar I-PACE to 13 on the sixth-generation system by using 17-megapixel imagers.
Tesla utilizes a 'pure vision' approach with Tesla Vision on Model 3 and Model Y, omitting radar in favor of camera input and neural network processing.

sections.title: Representation
sections.summary: Autonomous vehicle architectures hinge on how raw sensor inputs are converted into an operational representation. Waymo relies on the Waymo Foundation Model, combining a Sensor Fusion Encoder and a Gemini-trained Driving VLM to populate a World Decoder with compact, structured representations and pre-surveyed maps. In contrast, Tesla utilizes an extensive suite of per-camera neural networks to generate birds-eye-view representations on the fly without prior mapping surveys. This highlights an essential trade-off between inspectable, easily verifiable structured representations and expressive, nuance-capturing learned representations.
takeaways: Waymo's core architecture centers on the Waymo Foundation Model, composed of a Sensor Fusion Encoder and a Driving VLM.
Waymo's Driving VLM is trained using Gemini and fine-tuned on Waymo driving data to manage rare edge cases.
A World Decoder consumes outputs from both Waymo components to forecast behaviors, generate trajectories, and produce high-definition maps.
Waymo's compact structured representations facilitate inference-time safety verification, large-scale simulation, and measurable training feedback.

Tesla utilizes 48 networks requiring nearly 70,000 GPU hours of training to output 1,000 distinct tensors per time step across semantic segmentation, object detection, depth estimation, and birds-eye-view modeling.
Waymo relies on pre-surveyed prior mapping matched against live sensor feeds, whereas Tesla skips prior surveys and derives equivalent environmental context in real time.

sections.title: Prediction
sections.summary: Autonomous vehicle prediction systems must account for multiple possible future paths for each road user rather than committing to a single trajectory. In June 2025, Waymo published findings showing that motion forecasting quality scales predictably according to a power law with training compute, analogous to scaling laws in language models. This power-law relationship also held for closed-loop simulation performance, demonstrating that increasing data and compute directly enhances real-world driving safety. Meanwhile, Tesla introduced an updated reinforcement learning stage in version 14.3 to address long-tail edge cases.
takeaways: Predictive driving systems maintain several weighted future trajectories for road users to avoid fragility in critical scenarios.
Waymo's research showed that motion forecasting quality follows a power law relative to training compute, similar to language models.
Waymo evaluated motion forecasting using an internal dataset of 500,000 driving hours.
Increasing compute at inference time improved autonomous driving performance on more difficult driving scenarios.
The power-law scaling trend observed by Waymo translated to closed-loop simulation performance where agent actions affect the environment.
Tesla introduced an upgraded reinforcement learning stage in version 14.3 targeted at handling rare, long-tail edge cases.

sections.title: Planning
sections.summary: Autonomous vehicle planning systems select trajectories that require verification before execution. Waymo generates action sequences using large Teacher models distilled into onboard Student models, requiring trajectory confirmation from an independent validation layer before the vehicle acts. Conversely, Tesla relies on fleet-scale planning algorithms and human verification via Full Self-Driving (Supervised), using driver-monitoring strikeouts to enforce safety. While automated validation layers prevent defined failure modes, their protective scope is inherently limited by their explicit criteria.
takeaways: A trajectory is defined as a specific path paired with assigned speeds that must be verified before execution.
Waymo distills large Teacher models into onboard Student models to run action-sequence generation in real time.
Waymo requires agreement between two independent components—the generative student model and a validation layer—prior to vehicle movement.
Tesla relies on human drivers to verify trajectories in Full Self-Driving (Supervised), enforcing engagement via a strikeout suspension mechanism.
Validation layers evaluate trajectories strictly against pre-defined criteria, functioning similarly to assertions in production code.

sections.title: Validation
sections.summary: Waymo and Tesla take fundamentally different approaches to validating and reporting autonomous vehicle safety metrics. Waymo evaluates fully driverless operations without human intervention against adjusted local human baselines, reporting significant reductions in injury-causing crashes backed by peer-reviewed methodology and public data. Conversely, Tesla assesses its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) feature against manual Tesla driving using internal telemetry, measuring collision frequency where a human driver remains accountable. Because these reports measure distinct populations and operational paradigms, their safety figures cannot be compared directly side-by-side.
takeaways: Waymo recorded 220.6 million rider-only miles through March 2026, reporting a 94% reduction in serious injury crashes and an 82% reduction in injury-causing crashes relative to human benchmarks.
Waymo makes its validation methodology reproducible by publishing in peer-reviewed journals and releasing raw data.
Tesla evaluates Full Self-Driving (Supervised) by comparing it to manually driven Teslas using telemetry, reporting 7 times fewer major/minor collisions.
Tesla counts any crash where the system was active within five seconds before impact as an engaged collision, but omits fault attribution.
The metrics are not directly comparable because Waymo measures autonomous systems with no human backup, while Tesla measures a driver-assist system where the human remains responsible.
Waymo separates pre-deployment validation (governed by its Safety Framework and Safety Case) from post-deployment safety impact analysis.

sections.title: Training
sections.summary: Waymo and Tesla utilize fundamentally different training mechanisms to improve their autonomous driving systems between releases. Waymo operates a single foundation model powering three distilled components—the Driver, the Simulator, and the Critic—connected via simulation reinforcement learning and outer real-world safety loops. In contrast, Tesla relies on fleet telemetry and event packets collected from consumer vehicles to build automated test suites and simulation data. Tesla trains its models at scale on dedicated supercomputers, including Cortex 1 and Cortex 2, utilizing hundreds of thousands of H100-equivalent GPUs.
takeaways: Waymo powers three core components (Driver, Simulator, and Critic) off the same foundation model and distills them for production volume.
Waymo optimizes driving using an inner reinforcement learning loop in simulation and an outer validation loop driven by Critic evaluations of real driving.
Waymo reports that its fully autonomous mileage exceeds its manually driven data and encounters situations that simulation cannot fully reproduce.
Tesla collects consumer fleet data via two telemetry paths: trip-end anonymized mileage by road/control type and collision-triggered packets tied to specific vehicles.
Tesla reported receiving 2.5 billion telemetry packages in the third quarter of 2025.
Tesla conducts model training on Cortex 1 with over 100,000 H100-equivalent GPUs and Cortex 2 with over 130,000 in early ramp.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: Autonomous driving systems navigate a fundamental tradeoff across every operational stage: explicit, pre-determined knowledge versus real-time computation by internal model states. This dynamic shapes sensing, representation, prediction, planning, validation, and training. Waymo favors explicit, pre-written knowledge requiring city-specific preparation and bespoke hardware, whereas Tesla relies heavily on computed knowledge. It remains an open question whether one philosophy will dominate or if an intermediate hybrid approach will prevail.
takeaways: Autonomous driving continuously balances pre-determined, inspectable information against real-time model computation across all stages.
Waymo emphasizes written-down knowledge, which relies on per-city preparation and purpose-built hardware.
Tesla focuses more on computed knowledge derived on-the-fly during the drive.
Key architectural questions span distance sensing, inspectable world representations, multi-future prediction, trajectory verification, safety evidence, and training mileage selection.

Autonomous vehicle prediction systems must account for multiple possible future paths for each road user rather than committing to a single trajectory. In June 2025, Waymo published findings showing that motion forecasting quality scales predictably according to a power law with training compute, analogous to scaling laws in language models. This power-law relationship also held for closed-loop simulation performance, demonstrating that increasing data and compute directly enhances real-world driving safety. Meanwhile, Tesla introduced an updated reinforcement learning stage in version 14.3 to address long-tail edge cases.

zh.summary: 自動駕駛車輛的 perception 根本上是對比來自 lidar 等感測器的直接距離測量，以及來自 camera arrays 的推導深度計算。Waymo 整合了由 lidar、radar 與 cameras 組成的冗餘多感測器套件，以確保在雨、冰等惡劣環境條件下的可靠性。相較之下，Tesla 則完全依賴由外部 cameras 與神經網路驅動的 pure vision 策略。即便 Waymo 在第六代車輛中藉由更高解析度的感測元件精簡了 camera 數量，仍保留了感測器冗餘，凸顯出業界在昂貴的直接物理測量與具成本效益但容易出錯的推導估算之間的取捨。自動駕駛車輛架構取決於如何將原始感測器輸入轉換為可運作的 representation。Waymo 依賴 Waymo Foundation Model，結合 Sensor Fusion Encoder 與由 Gemini 訓練的 Driving VLM，以精簡的結構化 representations 和預先測繪的圖資來建構 World Decoder。相反地，Tesla 則利用一套龐大的 per-camera 神經網路，在無需事先測繪圖資的情況下即時生成 birds-eye-view representations。這突顯出可被檢視、易於驗證的結構化 representations，與具表現力、能捕捉細微差異的 learned representations 之間的核心權衡。自動駕駛車輛的 prediction 系統必須考量每位道路使用者的多種可能未來路徑，而非僅押注於單一軌跡。在 2025 年 6 月，Waymo 發表的研究顯示，motion forecasting 的品質會隨著 training compute 依循 power law 呈現可預測的擴展，類似於語言模型中的 scaling laws。這種 power-law 關係在 closed-loop simulation 表現上也同樣成立，證明了增加資料與運算量能直接提升真實世界的行車安全。同時，Tesla 在 14.3 版本中引入了更新的 reinforcement learning 階段，以因應長尾 edge cases。

sections.title: 感測
sections.summary: Autonomous vehicle perception 在根本上，是將來自 lidar 等 sensor 的直接距離測量，與來自 camera arrays 的衍生 depth 計算進行對比。Waymo 採用由 lidar、radar 和 camera 組成的冗餘 multi-sensor suite，以確保在雨天與結冰等惡劣環境條件下的可靠性。相較之下，Tesla 則完全依賴由外部 camera 與 neural networks 驅動的 pure vision 策略。即便 Waymo 在第六代車輛中透過更高解析度的 imagers 縮減了 camera 數量，仍保留了 sensor redundancy，這凸顯了業界在昂貴的直接物理測量，與具成本效益但容易產生誤差的衍生估算之間的 tradeoff。
takeaways: Camera 需要從 pixel 排列計算 depth，這會在 object size 與距離之間產生潛在的歧義性。
Lidar 透過雷射脈衝的回傳時間直接測量物理距離，產生 3D point cloud。
Waymo 的第六代系統包含 13 個 camera、4 個 lidar 單元、6 個 radar 單元以及音訊接收器，重疊覆蓋範圍可達 500 公尺。
Waymo 透過採用 17-megapixel 的 imagers，將 camera 數量從第五代 Jaguar I-PACE 上的 29 個減少到第六代系統的 13 個。
Tesla 在 Model 3 和 Model Y 上透過 Tesla Vision 採用「pure vision」方法，捨棄了 radar，改用 camera 輸入與 neural network 處理。

sections.title: 表徵
sections.summary: Autonomous vehicle 架構的關鍵在於如何將原始 sensor 輸入轉換為可運作的 representation。Waymo 依賴 Waymo Foundation Model，結合 Sensor Fusion Encoder 以及由 Gemini 訓練的 Driving VLM，將緊湊的 structured representations 與預先測繪的地圖填入 World Decoder。相較之下，Tesla 則利用一套龐大的 per-camera neural networks，在沒有預先測繪圖資的情況下即時（on the fly）生成 birds-eye-view representations。這突顯了在可檢視、易於驗證的 structured representations，與具備高度表達力、能捕捉細微特徵的 learned representations 之間的核心 tradeoff。
takeaways: Waymo 的核心架構以 Waymo Foundation Model 為中心，由 Sensor Fusion Encoder 和 Driving VLM 組成。
Waymo 的 Driving VLM 是使用 Gemini 進行訓練，並在 Waymo 的駕駛資料上進行 fine-tune，以處理罕見的 edge cases。
World Decoder 接收來自這兩個 Waymo 元件的輸出，以預測行為、生成 trajectories，並產出 high-definition maps。
Waymo 緊湊的 structured representations 有助於 inference-time 的安全驗證、大規模 simulation 以及可衡量的 training feedback。
Tesla 使用了 48 個 networks，需要近 70,000 個 GPU hours 的 training，在每個 time step 輸出 1,000 個不同的 tensors，涵蓋 semantic segmentation、object detection、depth estimation 以及 birds-eye-view 建模。
Waymo 依賴預先測繪的 prior mapping 與即時 sensor feeds 進行比對，而 Tesla 則跳過預先測繪，即時推導出等效的環境 context。

sections.title: 預測
sections.summary: Autonomous vehicle 的 prediction 系統必須考慮每個道路使用者多條可能的未來路徑，而不是只押注在單一 trajectory 上。2025 年 6 月，Waymo 發布的研究結果顯示，motion forecasting 的品質會隨著 training compute 依循 power law 呈現可預測的擴展，類似於 language models 中的 scaling laws。這種 power-law 關係在 closed-loop simulation 的表現中也同樣成立，證明了增加資料量與 compute 能直接提升真實世界的駕駛安全。與此同時，Tesla 在 14.3 版本中引入了更新的 reinforcement learning 階段，以解決 long-tail edge cases。
takeaways: Predictive driving 系統為道路使用者維護多條帶權重的未來 trajectories，以避免在 critical scenarios 下系統產生脆弱性。
Waymo 的研究顯示，motion forecasting 的品質與 training compute 呈 power law 關係，類似於 language models。
Waymo 使用包含 500,000 個駕駛小時的內部 dataset 來評估 motion forecasting。
在 inference time 增加 compute，能提升在更困難駕駛 scenarios 下的 autonomous driving 表現。
Waymo 觀察到的 power-law scaling 趨勢轉化為了 closed-loop simulation 效能，在此環境中 agent 的動作會影響環境。
Tesla 在 14.3 版本中引入了升級版的 reinforcement learning 階段，旨在處理罕見的 long-tail edge cases。

sections.title: Planning
sections.summary: Autonomous vehicle 的 planning 系統所選定的 trajectories 在執行前必須經過驗證。Waymo 使用大型 Teacher models 蒸餾為車載 Student models 來生成 action sequences，並在車輛採取行動前需要獨立 validation layer 的 trajectory 確認。相反地，Tesla 仰賴 fleet-scale planning 演算法以及透過 Full Self-Driving (Supervised) 進行的人工驗證，並藉由 driver-monitoring strikeouts 機制來強制確保安全。雖然自動化 validation layers 能防止預定義的 failure modes，但其保護範圍在本質上仍受限於其明確的 criteria。
takeaways: Trajectory 被定義為搭配指定速度的具體路徑，在執行前必須經過驗證。
Waymo 將大型 Teacher models 蒸餾為車載 Student models，以即時執行 action-sequence 生成。
Waymo 要求在車輛移動前，兩個獨立組件——生成式 student model 與 validation layer——必須達成一致。
Tesla 仰賴人類駕駛在 Full Self-Driving (Supervised) 中驗證 trajectories，並透過 strikeout 停權機制來強制駕駛保持專注。
Validation layers 嚴格根據預定義的 criteria 評估 trajectories，其運作方式類似於 production code 中的 assertions。

sections.title: Validation
sections.summary: Waymo 與 Tesla 在驗證和回報 autonomous vehicle 安全指標上採取了截然不同的方法。Waymo 將完全無需人為介入的 driverless 運作與調整後的當地人類 baselines 進行比對評估，並在同行評審方法論（peer-reviewed methodology）與公開數據的佐證下，報告了導致人員受傷的事故大幅減少。相反地，Tesla 使用內部 telemetry 將其 Full Self-Driving (Supervised) 功能與人類手動駕駛的 Tesla 進行比較，衡量人類駕駛仍需承擔責任下的 collision frequency。由於這些報告衡量的是不同的族群與 operational paradigms，因此其安全數據無法直接並列比較。
takeaways: 截至 2026 年 3 月，Waymo 累計記錄了 2.206 億英里的 rider-only 里程，相較於人類 benchmarks，嚴重傷害事故減少了 94%，致傷事故減少了 82%。
Waymo 透過在 peer-reviewed 期刊發表論文並釋出 raw data，使其 validation methodology 具備可重現性（reproducible）。
Tesla 透過 telemetry 將 Full Self-Driving (Supervised) 與手動駕駛的 Tesla 進行比較評估，報告指出 major/minor collisions 減少了 7 倍。
Tesla 將碰撞前五秒內系統處於 active 狀態的任何事故計算為 engaged collision，但並未計入事故責任歸屬（fault attribution）。
這些指標無法直接比較，因為 Waymo 衡量的是沒有人類作為 backup 的 autonomous systems，而 Tesla 衡量的則是由人類持續承擔責任的 driver-assist 系統。
Waymo 將部署前驗證（pre-deployment validation，由其 Safety Framework 與 Safety Case 規範）與部署後安全影響分析（post-deployment safety impact analysis）區隔開來。

sections.title: Training
sections.summary: Waymo 與 Tesla 在版本迭代之間，採用了根本不同的 training 機制來改進其 autonomous driving 系統。Waymo 運作單一 foundation model 來驅動三個 distilled components——Driver、Simulator 與 Critic——並透過 simulation reinforcement learning 與外部真實世界的 safety loops 相互連結。相較之下，Tesla 仰賴從消費級車隊收集的 fleet telemetry 與 event packets，以構建 automated test suites 與 simulation 數據。Tesla 在專屬的 supercomputers（包括 Cortex 1 和 Cortex 2）上大規模訓練模型，使用了數十萬顆 H100-equivalent GPUs。
takeaways: Waymo 由同一個 foundation model 驅動三個核心組件（Driver、Simulator 和 Critic），並針對量產規模進行蒸餾。
Waymo 透過 simulation 中的 inner reinforcement learning loop，以及由 Critic 對實際駕駛進行評估所驅動的 outer validation loop 來最佳化駕駛表現。
Waymo 指出其 fully autonomous 里程已超過手動駕駛數據，並會遇到 simulation 無法完全重現的狀況。
Tesla 透過兩種 telemetry 路徑收集消費級車隊數據：依據道路／控制類型記錄的 trip-end 匿名里程，以及與特定車輛綁定的 collision-triggered packets。
Tesla 報告在 2025 年第三季收到了 25 億個 telemetry packages。
Tesla 在擁有超過 100,000 顆 H100-equivalent GPUs 的 Cortex 1，以及在初期擴產階段（early ramp）擁有超過 130,000 顆的 Cortex 2 上進行模型訓練。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: 自動駕駛系統在每個運作階段都在應對一項根本的權衡取捨（tradeoff）：明確、預先決定的知識，對比由內部模型狀態進行的即時計算。這種動態關係形塑了 sensing、representation、prediction、planning、validation 與 training。Waymo 偏好明確、預先寫入的知識，這需要針對特定城市進行事前準備與客製化硬體；而 Tesla 則高度仰賴即時計算出的知識。究竟是其中一種哲學會成為主流，抑或折衷的混合方法（hybrid approach）會勝出，目前仍是個開放性問題。
takeaways: 自動駕駛在所有階段中，持續在預先決定且可檢查（inspectable）的資訊與即時的模型計算之間取得平衡。
Waymo 強調預先記錄的知識，這仰賴針對個別城市的事前準備以及專用硬體。
Tesla 則更專注於在行駛過程中即時（on-the-fly）推導出的計算知識。
關鍵的架構問題涵蓋距離感測（distance sensing）、可檢查的世界表徵（inspectable world representations）、多未來預測（multi-future prediction）、軌跡驗證（trajectory verification）、安全性佐證（safety evidence）以及訓練里程的選取。

The introductory article is offered for free, whereas future installments will be published on the E+ subscription service.

sections.title: Docker 與容器是什麼? 為什麼要用 Docker?
sections.summary: Docker is a platform and toolset designed to build and execute containerized applications. Software containers are analogous to physical shipping containers, encapsulating an application within an isolated execution environment containing virtual resources like hostnames, IP addresses, and file systems. Managed by Docker, multiple containers share the host's underlying hardware resources and operating system kernel while maintaining isolated processes, file systems, and network configurations.
takeaways: Docker functions as a platform and tool for building and running containerized software applications.
Containers encapsulate applications within isolated runtime environments that include virtualized hostnames, IP addresses, and disks.
Multiple containers on a single host share the same physical hardware resources such as CPU and memory.
Containers share the underlying operating system kernel while keeping their processes, file systems, and network stacks isolated from one another.

sections.title: Docker 解決了什麼問題?
sections.summary: Docker solves environment inconsistency issues in software development where code runs on one developer's machine but fails on another due to mismatched dependency versions such as Node.js or Postgres. By packaging an application's required runtime environment inside containers, Docker allows applications to execute reliably across diverse environments. With properly prepared Dockerfile and Compose configurations, new team members can get a project running locally with a single command. This portability also facilitates deploying and managing applications seamlessly across clouds, data centers, and serverless functions.
takeaways: Differences in host machines and dependency versions (e.g., Node.js 18 vs. 22 or Postgres variants) frequently lead to environment setup failures and inconsistent behavior.
Containers solve dependency drift by packaging the full execution environment required by an application.
With Docker, onboarding developers can launch an entire project locally with a single command rather than spending days debugging setup issues.
Streamlined Docker onboarding relies on teams preemptively preparing Dockerfile, Compose configurations, and initialization workflows.
Docker enables consistent builds, deployments, and management across local machines, cloud providers, data centers, and serverless architectures.

sections.title: 為什麼 Docker 出現前的解決方案會被 Docker 取代?
sections.summary: Before Docker, virtual machines were commonly used to isolate execution environments so applications with conflicting dependencies could run on the same machine. However, virtual machines bundle an entire operating system within each instance, consuming substantial CPU resources and gigabytes of memory. Docker containers solve the same isolation problem while sharing the host operating system, making them significantly more lightweight. As a result, the same hardware can run far more containerized applications concurrently than virtual machines.
takeaways: Docker containers allow applications with different dependency versions to execute concurrently without conflicts.
Prior to Docker, virtual machines (VMs) were the standard approach for isolating application environments.
Virtual machines do not share the host operating system, requiring gigabytes of memory and CPU cycles for each guest OS.
The heavy resource overhead of guest operating systems limits the number of applications that can run simultaneously on a VM-based host.
Docker containers share the underlying host operating system, enabling significantly higher application density on equivalent hardware.

sections.title: 本期推薦
sections.summary: This curated selection features technical articles covering software engineering best practices, AI-assisted development, programming languages, and web performance. takeaways: Coinbase rebuilt its engineering hiring process over the past year to adapt to the realities of AI-assisted engineering.

The 'Build Wide, Ship Narrow' development method emphasizes building and demoing full features with AI before splitting them into small, reviewable PRs.

Serializing JavaScript data into JSON introduces subtle data fidelity issues, such as precision loss in large integers, omission of undefined, conversion of Dates to strings, and mapping NaN to null.
Shopify store performance bottlenecks often stem from unoptimized homepage hero images, carousel sliders, and third-party app scripts.

sections.title: Docker 與容器是什麼? 為什麼要用 Docker?
sections.summary: Docker 是一個專為建構與執行 containerized 應用程式設計的平台與工具集。軟體 container 類似實體的貨櫃，將應用程式封裝在隔離的執行環境中，內含如 hostname、IP address 與檔案系統等虛擬化資源。在 Docker 的管理下，多個 container 共享 host 的底層硬體資源與作業系統核心，同時維持彼此隔離的 process、檔案系統與網路設定。
takeaways: Docker 扮演著建構與執行 containerized 軟體應用程式的平台與工具角色。
Container 將應用程式封裝在隔離的 runtime 環境中，其中包含虛擬化的 hostname、IP address 與磁碟。
單一 host 上的多個 container 共享相同的實體硬體資源，例如 CPU 與記憶體。
Container 共享底層的作業系統核心，同時讓各自的 process、檔案系統與 network stack 保持相互隔離。

sections.title: Docker 解決了什麼問題?
sections.summary: Docker 解決了軟體開發中的環境不一致問題——也就是程式碼在某位開發者的機器上可以運行，卻因為 Node.js 或 Postgres 等依賴版本不一致而在另一台機器上崩潰。透過將應用程式所需的 runtime 環境打包在 container 內，Docker 讓應用程式能在多元環境中可靠地執行。有了妥善準備的 Dockerfile 與 Compose 設定，新團隊成員只要一行指令就能在本地端啟動專案。這種便攜性也促進了在雲端、資料中心與 serverless functions 之間無縫部署與管理應用程式。
takeaways: Host 機器與依賴版本之間的差異（例如 Node.js 18 vs. 22 或不同的 Postgres 版本）經常導致環境建置失敗與行為不一致。
Container 透過打包應用程式所需的完整執行環境，解決了依賴漂移（dependency drift）的問題。
有了 Docker，新加入的開發者只需一行指令即可在本地端啟動整個專案，不必再花費數天 debug 環境設定問題。
順暢的 Docker 入門流程仰賴團隊預先準備好 Dockerfile、Compose 設定檔以及初始化工作流程。
Docker 實現了在本地端機器、雲端服務商、資料中心以及 serverless 架構之間一致的 build、部署與管理。

sections.title: 為什麼 Docker 出現前的解決方案會被 Docker 取代?
sections.summary: 在 Docker 出現之前，虛擬機器（virtual machine）常被用來隔離執行環境，讓依賴衝突的應用程式能在同一台機器上運作。然而，每個虛擬機器 instance 都打包了完整的作業系統，消耗大量的 CPU 資源與數 GB 的記憶體。Docker container 在解決相同隔離問題的同時共享 host 作業系統，因此輕量許多。其結果是，相同的硬體能夠比虛擬機器同時執行多得多的 containerized 應用程式。
takeaways: Docker container 讓具有不同依賴版本的應用程式能夠同時執行且互不衝突。
在 Docker 出現之前，virtual machines (VMs) 是用來隔離 application environments 的標準做法。
Virtual machines 不會共享 host operating system，每個 guest OS 都需要數 gigabytes 的 memory 與 CPU cycles。
Guest operating systems 龐大的 resource overhead 限制了在以 VM 為基礎的 host 上能同時運行的 applications 數量。
Docker containers 共享底層的 host operating system，讓同等硬體規格下能達到顯著更高的 application density。

sections.title: How to build your own AI company (100% local)
sections.summary: Alook is an open-source, self-hosted platform designed for multi-agent orchestration using a traditional organizational chart structure. Instead of manually wiring complex graphs, users define roles and reporting lines for agents who then communicate via email inboxes. This approach allows for intuitive local management of AI teams using existing agent runtimes like Claude Code and OpenCode.
takeaways: Alook replaces manual graph-based agent orchestration with a hierarchical organization chart structure.
Agents in the Alook system coordinate and exchange information through dedicated email inboxes.
The platform is designed to run 100% locally and is open-source, ensuring data privacy.
Alook supports multiple agent runtimes including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex.
The organizational structure allows for a single human point of contact with a 'CEO' agent who delegates tasks down the chain.

sections.title: A cheaper model does not imply a cheaper turn
sections.summary: Model routing is a strategy used to reduce costs by directing simple tasks to cheaper LLMs, but it can be counterproductive in long agent sessions. Because prompt caches are model-specific, switching models mid-conversation forces a full 'cold prefill' of the entire history, losing the 90% discount provided by warm caches. In scenarios with large conversation histories, the cost of re-processing the history on a cheaper model often exceeds the savings gained from its lower per-token rate.
takeaways: Prompt caching allows providers to bill tokens at 10% of the base input rate when the prefix matches a stored KV cache.
KV caches are model-specific and cannot be transferred between models like Opus 5 and Haiku 4.5 due to different weights.
Switching models mid-session invalidates the warm cache, requiring a full re-prefill of the entire conversation transcript.
For Anthropic's Opus 5 and Haiku 4.5, switching to the cheaper model only saves money if the history is less than 8 times the size of the new input.
Model routing is most effective for independent prompts or short sessions where the history penalty is minimal.
The most efficient time to switch models is during a context reset or compaction when the cache is already being invalidated.

sections.title: The anatomy of a Claude prompt
sections.summary: The quality of Claude's output is primarily determined by prompt structure, which can be broken down into eight essential building blocks. These blocks include defining a role, specifying objectives with success criteria, and using XML tags to clearly delineate context and examples. Research from Anthropic suggests that placing long documents at the start of a prompt can boost performance by 30%. Advanced techniques like pre-filling and reasoning tags further refine the model's accuracy and formatting.
takeaways: A well-structured Claude prompt uses eight building blocks: Role, Objective, Context, Examples, Thinking, Constraints, Output Format, and Pre-filling.
Defining a specific role in the system prompt significantly alters Claude's reasoning and communication style.
Including success criteria ('so that') provides Claude with a benchmark to evaluate its own performance.
Placing long documents at the top of the prompt and the query at the end can improve response quality by 30%.
XML tags like <context>, <examples>, and <thinking> are essential for organizing complex information and separating reasoning from final answers.
Pre-filling the start of a response via the API allows users to bypass preambles and enforce specific output formats.

sections.title: What do AI companies think about Agent Harness?
sections.summary: The agent harness represents the infrastructure surrounding an AI model that enables it to function as an agent, and companies currently disagree on how complex this layer should be. Anthropic advocates for a thin harness that relies on model intelligence, whereas LangGraph uses a thick harness with explicit graph-based logic. While this infrastructure often serves as temporary scaffolding that is removed as models improve, models can become dependent on specific harness structures during training. Evidence from TerminalBench 2.0 suggests that optimizing the harness alone can significantly improve agent performance without changing the underlying model.
takeaways: The agent harness is the infrastructure that wraps a model to manage turns, tools, and memory.
Anthropic's dumb loop approach assumes that as models get smarter, the need for complex infrastructure decreases.
OpenAI's Agents SDK prioritizes a code-first approach using native Python instead of domain-specific languages.
LangGraph uses a thick harness where every decision point and transition is explicitly defined as a node or edge in a graph.
The scaffolding metaphor describes harness logic that is removed once a model is capable of handling those tasks internally.
LangChain improved its ranking on TerminalBench 2.0 from outside the top 30 to rank 5 by only changing its infrastructure.
Models trained with a specific harness in the loop may see performance degradation if that harness is modified.

sections.title: 更便宜的 model 並不意味著更便宜的 turn
sections.summary: Model routing 是一種透過將簡單任務導向較便宜的 LLM 來降低成本的策略，但在長對話的 agent sessions 中可能適得其反。由於 prompt cache 是 model-specific 的，在對話中途切換 model 會強制對整個歷史記錄進行完整的「cold prefill」，因而失去 warm cache 提供的 90% 折扣。在對話歷史記錄龐大的情境下，在較便宜的 model 上重新處理歷史記錄的成本，往往會超過其較低 per-token rate 所節省的費用。
takeaways: 當 prefix 符合儲存的 KV cache 時，prompt caching 允許 provider 僅以基準 input rate 的 10% 來計算 token 費用。
KV cache 是 model-specific 的，由於 weights 不同，無法在像 Opus 5 與 Haiku 4.5 這類 model 之間轉移。
在 session 中途切換 model 會使 warm cache 失效，需要對整個對話 transcript 進行完整的 re-prefill。
對 Anthropic 的 Opus 5 與 Haiku 4.5 而言，只有在歷史記錄小於新 input 大小的 8 倍時，切換到較便宜的 model 才能省錢。
Model routing 對於獨立的 prompts 或歷史記錄 penalty 極小的短 sessions 最為有效。
切換 model 最具效率的時機是在 context reset 或 compaction 期間，因為此時 cache 本來就已經失效。

sections.title: Claude prompt 的結構剖析
sections.summary: Claude 的 output 品質主要由 prompt 結構決定，該結構可拆解為八個關鍵的 building blocks。這些 blocks 包括定義 role、指定帶有 success criteria 的 objectives，以及使用 XML tags 來清楚劃分 context 和 examples。Anthropic 的研究顯示，將長文件放在 prompt 的開頭可提升 30% 的效能。像 pre-filling 與 reasoning tags 等進階技巧可進一步優化 model 的準確度與格式。
takeaways: 一個結構良好的 Claude prompt 會使用八個 building blocks：Role、Objective、Context、Examples、Thinking、Constraints、Output Format 以及 Pre-filling。
在 system prompt 中定義特定的 role，會顯著改變 Claude 的 reasoning 與溝通風格。
納入 success criteria（「so that」）可為 Claude 提供評估自身表現的基準。
將長文件置於 prompt 頂端、並將 query 放在末端，可將 response 品質提升 30%。
像 <context>、<examples> 與 <thinking> 這類的 XML tags，對於組織複雜資訊以及將 reasoning 與最終答案分開至關重要。
透過 API pre-filling response 的開頭，能讓使用者跳過開場白（preambles）並強制套用特定的 output formats。

sections.title: AI 公司如何看待 Agent Harness？
sections.summary: Agent harness 代表圍繞著 AI model、使其能夠作為 agent 運作的 infrastructure，而各家公司目前對這一層應該具備多高的複雜度仍未達成共識。Anthropic 提倡依賴 model 智慧的 thin harness，而 LangGraph 則採用具有明確 graph-based logic 的 thick harness。雖然這種 infrastructure 通常是作為暫時性的 scaffolding，會隨著 model 進步而被移除，但 model 在訓練過程中也可能會對特定的 harness 結構產生依賴。來自 TerminalBench 2.0 的證據表明，在不改變底層 model 的情況下，單純優化 harness 就能顯著提升 agent 的效能。
takeaways: Agent harness 是包裝 model 以管理 turns、tools 與 memory 的 infrastructure。
Anthropic 的 dumb loop 方法假設隨著 model 變得更聰明，對複雜 infrastructure 的需求將會減少。
OpenAI 的 Agents SDK 優先採用 code-first 方法，使用 native Python 而非 domain-specific languages。
LangGraph 使用 thick harness，其中每個決策點和 transition 都被明確定義為 graph 中的 node 或 edge。
scaffolding（鷹架）隱喻描述了一種 harness 邏輯：一旦模型具備在內部處理這些任務的能力，該邏輯就會被移除。
LangChain 僅僅透過變更其 infrastructure，就將其在 TerminalBench 2.0 上的排名從 30 名以外提升至第 5 名。
在訓練迴圈中包含特定 harness 所訓練出的模型，若該 harness 被修改，可能會面臨效能下降的問題。

items.title: EP222: What is Google’s TPU?

sections.title: What is Google’s TPU?
sections.summary: A Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) is Google's custom AI chip designed specifically for deep learning matrix multiplications, unlike GPUs which were initially created for graphics. At Cloud Next '26, Google announced its 8th generation of TPUs, introducing two distinct hardware variants for the first time. The TPU 8t is built to maximize raw throughput for training workloads, whereas the TPU 8i focuses on low latency and chip-to-chip interconnect speed for inference. Both chips share identical Axion CPUs, liquid cooling systems, and software stacks to maintain software compatibility across both models.
takeaways: TPUs are custom Google chips engineered specifically for deep learning matrix operations rather than graphics workloads.
Google unveiled its 8th generation of TPUs at Cloud Next '26, splitting the hardware generation into two distinct variants.
TPU 8t is optimized for high raw throughput required in AI model training.
TPU 8i is tailored for AI inference, prioritizing latency and chip-to-chip communication speed.
Both TPU variants utilize the same Axion CPUs, liquid cooling infrastructure, and software stack to ensure code interoperability.

sections.title: 9 Types of API Testing
sections.summary: API testing encompasses multiple distinct methodologies designed to prevent various types of failures across the software lifecycle. Core operational checks like smoke, functional, and regression testing verify that endpoints perform correctly according to business rules without breaking existing features. System interactions and stability are validated using contract, integration, load, and stress testing across service boundaries and under heavy traffic. Finally, security and fuzz testing target vulnerability detection by validating access controls and exposing bugs via unexpected or invalid inputs.
takeaways: Smoke tests are executed immediately after a deployment to verify that critical endpoints like login, checkout, and health checks respond.
Functional testing verifies that endpoints meet business requirements rather than merely returning an empty or incorrect 200 HTTP status code.
Contract testing safeguards agreements between services, ensuring providers do not alter fields, types, or status codes without warning.
Integration testing validates complete workflows spanning multiple dependent systems like inventory, payment, and notification services.
Performance and resilience are assessed through load testing under expected traffic, stress testing until failure, and fuzz testing with unexpected or invalid inputs.
Security testing evaluates authentication, access control mechanisms, unsanitized input vulnerabilities, and data leaks in error messages.

sections.title: Common types of AI Agents guardrails on production
sections.summary: Production AI agents depend on multi-layered guardrails rather than better prompts to maintain reliability. These systems deploy input screening and context verification to block prompt injections, sensitive data, and off-scope queries before reaching the model. During execution, responses are constrained to verified context, and outputs are systematically evaluated for safety, formatting, and groundedness with retry mechanisms. Finally, operational controls enforce system limits, comprehensive logging, and human-in-the-loop escalation for low-confidence or high-risk actions.
takeaways: Reliable AI agents are built on wrapped guardrail systems rather than prompt engineering.
Input screening intercepts prompt injections, sensitive data, and off-scope queries before the model sees them.
Response generation is constrained so the model reasons only over verified context.
Output validation checks groundedness, formatting, and safety, permitting up to two retries before returning a safe fallback.
Operational controls provide logging, enforce system limits, and escalate high-risk or low-confidence actions to human review.

sections.title: Forward Proxy, Reverse Proxy, and API Gateway Explained
sections.summary: Forward proxies, reverse proxies, and API gateways differ primarily in which side of a network connection they represent and the problems they address. A forward proxy sits adjacent to the client, masking client IP addresses and enforcing outbound corporate policies. A reverse proxy sits in front of servers to handle TLS termination, routing, and backend isolation, with tools like NGINX and HAProxy commonly serving this role. An API gateway extends the reverse proxy pattern to centralize cross-cutting concerns like authentication, rate limiting, and request shaping across microservices.
takeaways: A forward proxy represents the client, hiding its real IP and managing outbound traffic rules such as site blocking and caching.
A reverse proxy represents the server side, terminating TLS, routing traffic, and shielding backend machines from the public internet.
NGINX and HAProxy are standard reverse proxies, frequently deployed alongside a load balancer.
An API gateway is a specialized reverse proxy that handles cross-cutting requirements such as authentication, rate limiting, API key validation, versioning, and request shaping across microservices.
Production systems typically run forward proxies, reverse proxies, and API gateways concurrently across different layers of their infrastructure.

Production AI agents depend on multi-layered guardrails rather than better prompts to maintain reliability. These systems deploy input screening and context verification to block prompt injections, sensitive data, and off-scope queries before reaching the model. During execution, responses are constrained to verified context, and outputs are systematically evaluated for safety, formatting, and groundedness with retry mechanisms. Finally, operational controls enforce system limits, comprehensive logging, and human-in-the-loop escalation for low-confidence or high-risk actions.

sections.title: 什麼是 Google 的 TPU？
sections.summary: Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) 是 Google 專門為 deep learning 矩陣乘法設計的客製化 AI 晶片，與最初為圖形處理而建立的 GPU 不同。在 Cloud Next '26 上，Google 發布了第 8 代 TPU，並首次推出兩種截然不同的硬體規格變體。TPU 8t 旨在最大化訓練 workload 的 raw throughput，而 TPU 8i 則專注於 inference 的 low latency 與 chip-to-chip 互連速度。這兩款晶片共用相同的 Axion CPU、水冷系統以及 software stack，以維持跨兩種型號的軟體相容性。
takeaways: TPU 是 Google 的客製化晶片，專門為 deep learning 矩陣運算而設計，而非圖形 workload。
Google 在 Cloud Next '26 上發表了第 8 代 TPU，將硬體世代拆分為兩種截然不同的變體。
TPU 8t 針對 AI 模型訓練所需的高 raw throughput 進行了最佳化。
TPU 8i 專為 AI inference 量身打造，優先考慮 latency 與 chip-to-chip 通訊速度。
兩種 TPU 變體均採用相同的 Axion CPU、水冷基礎架構和 software stack，以確保程式碼的互操作性。

sections.title: 9 種 API 測試類型
sections.summary: API 測試包含多種不同的方法論，旨在防止軟體生命週期中出現各種類型的 failure。像 smoke、functional 以及 regression 測試等核心運作檢查，可驗證 endpoint 是否依據 business rules 正確運作，且不破壞現有 feature。系統互動與穩定性則是透過跨 service 邊界及高流量下的 contract、integration、load 和 stress 測試來驗證。最後，security 與 fuzz 測試透過驗證存取控制以及利用非預期或無效 input 暴露 bug，來達成弱點偵測。
takeaways: Smoke 測試會在 deployment 完成後立即執行，以驗證登入、結帳和 health check 等關鍵 endpoint 是否有回應。
Functional 測試驗證 endpoint 是否符合 business requirements，而不僅僅是回傳空的回應或不正確的 200 HTTP status code。
Contract 測試保障 service 之間的協定，確保 provider 不會在沒有預警的情況下更改 field、type 或 status code。
Integration 測試驗證跨多個相依系統（如庫存、支付和通知 service）的完整 workflow。
效能與彈性是透過預期流量下的 load 測試、持續加壓直至故障的 stress 測試，以及使用非預期或無效 input 的 fuzz 測試來評估。
Security 測試評估 authentication、存取控制機制、未經過濾的 input 弱點，以及 error message 中的資料外洩風險。

sections.title: Production 環境中 AI Agent guardrails 的常見類型
sections.summary: Production 環境中的 AI agent 依賴多層 guardrails 而非更好的 prompt 來維持 reliability。這些系統部署了 input screening 與 context verification，以在請求到達模型之前阻擋 prompt injection、機敏資料以及超出範圍的 query。在執行期間，response 會被限制在經過驗證的 context 內，且 output 會針對安全性、格式以及 groundedness 進行系統性評估，並搭配 retry 機制。最後，運作控制措施強制執行系統限制、全面性 logging，並針對低信心度或高風險操作引入 human-in-the-loop escalation 機制。
takeaways: 可靠的 AI agent 是建立在封裝好的 guardrail 系統之上，而非 prompt engineering。
輸入篩選（Input screening）會在模型接收到資料前，攔截 prompt injection、敏感資料以及超出範圍（off-scope）的查詢。
回應生成（Response generation）受到約束，確保模型僅基於經過驗證的 context 進行推理。
輸出驗證（Output validation）會檢查 groundedness、格式與安全性，在返回安全 fallback 之前最多允許重試兩次。
維運控制（Operational controls）提供 logging、強制執行系統限制，並將高風險或低信心的操作上報（escalate）給人工審查。

sections.title: Forward Proxy、Reverse Proxy 與 API Gateway 解析
sections.summary: Forward proxy、reverse proxy 與 API gateway 的主要差異，在於它們代表網路連線的哪一端，以及各自要解決的問題。Forward proxy 緊鄰 client 端，負責隱藏 client IP 位址並強制執行企業的出站（outbound）政策。Reverse proxy 則位於伺服器前端，負責處理 TLS termination、routing 與 backend 隔離，常見的工具如 NGINX 和 HAProxy。API gateway 則延伸了 reverse proxy 模式，為跨 microservices 集中處理如 authentication、rate limiting 和 request shaping 等 cross-cutting concerns。
takeaways: Forward proxy 代表 client 端，負責隱藏其真實 IP 並管理網站封鎖、caching 等出站流量規則。
Reverse proxy 代表伺服器端，負責 terminating TLS、流量 routing，並保護 backend 機器免受公開網際網路的威脅。
NGINX 和 HAProxy 是標準的 reverse proxy，經常與 load balancer 一同部署。
API gateway 是一種專門的 reverse proxy，負責處理跨 microservices 的 cross-cutting 需求，例如 authentication、rate limiting、API key 驗證、versioning 和 request shaping。
生產環境系統通常會在基礎架構的不同層級中，同時運行 forward proxy、reverse proxy 和 API gateway。

sections.title: A smarter Claude model burns more tokens, not fewer
sections.summary: Benchmarks from MCPMark V2 indicate that advanced Claude models can consume 54% more tokens than expected when interacting with traditional backends. This inefficiency stems from the model's attempt to resolve missing or unstructured backend context through excessive discovery queries and retries. While platforms like Supabase provide verbose documentation and ambiguous errors, the agent-centric backend InsForge uses structured JSON topology to reduce token load. Testing shows InsForge completed a RAG application build with significantly fewer tokens and zero manual interventions compared to Supabase.
takeaways: Smarter models like Claude may increase token usage by 54% when forced to perform extensive discovery on unstructured backends.
Traditional backends often return 5-10x more tokens than necessary by providing full documentation instead of specific state data.
InsForge provides a full backend topology in approximately 500 tokens, significantly reducing the discovery phase.
Semantic exit codes and structured JSON in InsForge prevent the agent from entering infinite retry loops caused by ambiguous error codes.
In a comparative test, InsForge consumed 3.7M tokens versus Supabase's 10.4M tokens for the same RAG application build.
InsForge utilizes narrowly scoped skills to ensure the agent only loads context relevant to the current task.

sections.title: How production LLMs reason better at inference time
sections.summary: Inference-time compute scaling for LLMs involves parallel sampling or sequential trajectory extension to improve reasoning without altering model weights. While techniques like Majority Voting and Best-of-N leverage multiple outputs, sequential methods like Thinking Budgets and Self-Correction focus on internal processing. Advanced tree-based search methods like MCTS offer high performance but face challenges with reward model reliability and definition of step correctness.
takeaways: Inference-time scaling is categorized into parallel scaling (multiple samples) and sequential scaling (longer trajectories).
Test-time compute can enable a smaller model to outperform a model 14x its size on specific tasks.
Majority voting relies on answer agreement and does not require a separate reward model, but it cannot fix consistent errors.
Best-of-N sampling is limited by the quality of the reward model, which can be exploited if optimization pressure is too high.
Self-correction loops can sometimes decrease accuracy, as seen with GPT-3.5 on GSM8K where it changed more correct answers than wrong ones.
DeepSeek R1 moved away from MCTS and Process Reward Models (PRMs) in favor of rule-based reinforcement learning (GRPO).

sections.title: 7 decisions that define every Agent Harness
sections.summary: The focus of AI agent performance is shifting from the underlying LLM to the 'agent harness,' which manages orchestration, tools, and context. Benchmarks like SWE-bench Pro demonstrate that changes in the scaffold can have a 22x larger impact on performance than switching between frontier models. Building an effective harness involves seven key design decisions, including agent count, reasoning strategy, and verification methods. While models are becoming more capable and internalizing some planning logic, the harness remains a critical component for reliability and tool execution.
takeaways: Scaffold changes on SWE-bench Pro produce 22x larger performance swings than model swaps at the frontier.
Frontier models are saturating general benchmarks like MMLU, making infrastructure the primary differentiator.
Anthropic and OpenAI recommend a single-agent approach initially to avoid routing overhead and context loss.
Verification layers using computational checks like tests and linters provide deterministic ground truth for agents.
Tool scoping via lazy loading improves performance by only surfacing tools when they are relevant to the task.
Reasoning strategies like ReAct offer flexibility but are more costly than plan-then-execute approaches.
The industry trend shows harnesses getting thinner as models improve, though they remain necessary for context and tool management.

sections.title: Karpathy’s agentic engineering lifecycle, clearly explained
sections.summary: Google's Agents CLI streamlines the agentic engineering lifecycle by consolidating scaffolding, deployment, security, and evaluation into a natural-language interface. It allows developers to manage the transition from a local idea to a governed enterprise asset using simple prompts. The tool integrates with existing coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor to automate complex tasks such as identity provisioning and prompt injection screening. By leveraging Agent Runtime and Gemini Enterprise, it ensures agents are stateful, secure, and accessible across an organization.
takeaways: Google's Agents CLI automates the end-to-end lifecycle of AI agents using natural language prompts.
The CLI integrates with popular coding tools including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Antigravity.
Security features include Model Armor for prompt injection screening and the provisioning of least-privilege identities.
Deployment to Agent Runtime enables state persistence through Sessions and Memory Bank features.
The evaluation stage specifically targets grounding, hallucination prevention, and prompt optimization.
Finalized agents can be registered and published directly into Gemini Enterprise for organizational use.

sections.title: Continuous batching in LLMs
sections.summary: Continuous batching, also known as iteration-level scheduling, optimizes LLM inference by rebuilding the batch at every forward pass rather than waiting for all requests in a static batch to complete. This approach allows finished requests to exit and waiting requests to enter immediately, preventing GPU resources from being wasted on empty slots caused by varying output lengths. Serving engines like vLLM and TensorRT-LLM use this method to significantly increase throughput, often managing complex tasks like chunked prefill and KV cache allocation within a unified scheduling loop.
takeaways: Static batching is inefficient for LLMs because output lengths are unpredictable, causing the entire batch to run at the speed of the slowest request.
Continuous batching updates batch membership at every iteration, allowing for immediate replacement of completed sequences.
Selective batching flattens tokens into a single sequence for linear operations while splitting them for attention to handle unique KV caches.
The vLLM scheduler manages a token budget and sequence cap to balance throughput against inter-token latency.
Preemption occurs when KV cache memory is exhausted, forcing requests to be recomputed from scratch in default vLLM configurations.
Anyscale benchmarks demonstrated that vLLM can achieve 23x the throughput of naive Hugging Face serving on OPT-13B models.
Key metrics for monitoring scheduler health include the total_cumulative_preemption_cnt in Prometheus.
