takeaways: Google 的 Agents CLI 使用自然語言 prompts 自動化 AI agents 的 end-to-end lifecycle。
該 CLI 與熱門 coding tools 整合，包括 Claude Code、Cursor、Codex 與 Antigravity。
安全性功能包含用於 prompt injection screening 的 Model Armor，以及 least-privilege identities 的配置（provisioning）。
部署至 Agent Runtime 則可透過 Sessions 與 Memory Bank 功能實現 state persistence。
Evaluation 階段特別針對 grounding、hallucination prevention 以及 prompt optimization 進行評估與優化。
完成定案的 agent 可以直接註冊並發布至 Gemini Enterprise，供組織內部使用。

sections.title: LLM 中的 Continuous batching
sections.summary: Continuous batching（亦稱為 iteration-level scheduling）透過在每次 forward pass 時重新建構 batch，而非等待 static batch 中的所有 request 完成，藉此優化 LLM inference。這種做法讓已完成的 request 立即退出，並讓等待中的 request 立即加入，避免 GPU 資源因輸出長度不一所產生的 empty slots 而浪費。像 vLLM 與 TensorRT-LLM 這類 serving engine 便採用此方法大幅提升 throughput，並通常在統一的 scheduling loop 中管理 chunked prefill 與 KV cache 配置等複雜任務。
takeaways: Static batching 對 LLM 而言效率低落，因為 output length 無法預測，導致整個 batch 只能以最慢 request 的速度執行。
Continuous batching 會在每次 iteration 更新 batch 成員，以便立即替換已完成的 sequence。
Selective batching 在執行 linear operations 時會將 token 展平（flatten）為單一 sequence，而在進行 attention 時則將其拆分以處理各自獨立的 KV cache。
vLLM scheduler 透過管理 token budget 與 sequence cap，在 throughput 與 inter-token latency 之間取得平衡。
當 KV cache 記憶體耗盡時就會發生 preemption，在預設的 vLLM 設定下，這會迫使 request 必須從頭重新計算。
Anyscale 的 benchmarks 顯示，在 OPT-13B 模型上，vLLM 的 throughput 可達原生 Hugging Face serving 的 23 倍。
監控 scheduler 健康狀況的關鍵指標包含 Prometheus 中的 total_cumulative_preemption_cnt。

items.title: A Detailed Guide to API Composition Techniques

sections.title: A Detailed Guide to API Composition Techniques
sections.summary: In service-based architectures, single user-interface views often require data distributed across multiple independent services, necessitating a process called API composition to merge the responses. This merging logic can be executed on the client application, a central datacenter server, a CDN edge, or within an internal service. While introducing an intermediate composition server adds a network hop, it usually reduces overall latency by replacing multiple slow mobile round trips with one external call and multiple sub-millisecond intra-datacenter calls. Beyond latency, composition architecture determines how the system handles service failures, caching opportunities, and organizational change approvals.
takeaways: API composition merges data from multiple independent services into the structure required by a user interface.
Composition logic can be placed in mobile applications, datacenter servers, CDN edge locations, or internal services.
Trading multiple high-latency mobile round trips for a single mobile request plus fast intra-datacenter calls typically reduces overall load time.
The location of the composition layer impacts latency, partial failure behavior, response cacheability, and deployment ownership.

items.title: Agentic AI Weekly | Berkeley RDI | August 12, 2026

sections.title: Agentic AI Summit 2026: Five Shifts Shaping the Next Era of AI
sections.summary: The Agentic AI Summit 2026 was held on August 1–2 at UC Berkeley, gathering thousands of participants to discuss the future of AI agents. The conference brought together approximately 5,000 in-person attendees, 100,000 online viewers, and 200 speakers across four stages. Topics spanned frontier model research, robotics, enterprise deployment, infrastructure, security, and governance. The central consensus among attendees was that the primary challenge has shifted from predicting the arrival of AI agents to ensuring they are capable, trustworthy, and beneficial.
takeaways: The Agentic AI Summit 2026 took place on August 1–2 at UC Berkeley.
The summit attracted approximately 5,000 in-person attendees, 100,000 virtual viewers, and 200 speakers across four stages.
Attendees represented researchers, founders, enterprise leaders, investors, and policymakers.
Discussion topics included frontier models, robotics, infrastructure, enterprise adoption, security, and governance.
Industry consensus has shifted from whether AI agents will arrive to how to build them to be capable, trustworthy, and beneficial.

sections.title: 1. AI Agents Are Moving From Assistants to Collaborators
sections.summary: AI systems are currently evolving beyond simple question answering and content generation toward becoming autonomous, reliable collaborators. Rather than causing an AI job apocalypse, the industry faces a scarcity of skilled AI engineers to build these capabilities. Next-generation systems are expected to reason, plan, leverage tools, and coordinate across multi-agent workflows with minimal human intervention. The primary development challenge has thus shifted from creating smarter chatbots to engineering dependable collaborative systems.
takeaways: Andrew Ng stated there will be no AI job apocalypse, noting an acute shortage of skilled AI engineers instead.
AI systems are transitioning from answering questions and content generation to reasoning, planning, and tool usage.
Future agentic systems are expected to coordinate with other agents to handle complex workflows with minimal human intervention.
The core development priority is shifting from building smarter chatbots to building reliable collaborators.

sections.title: 2. Beyond Bigger Models: The Next Frontier Is Recursive Improvement
sections.summary: Future breakthroughs in AI capability are expected to stem from recursive self-improvement rather than increasing model scale alone. According to Google DeepMind's Oriol Vinyals, recursive self-improvement encompasses four key capabilities: ideation, implementation, experimentation, and evaluation. Consequently, AI research is shifting toward systems capable of long-horizon reasoning, planning, memory, and autonomous iterative refinement.
takeaways: Model scale alone will not drive the next major leap in AI capabilities.
Recursive self-improvement consists of four distinct capabilities: ideation, implementation, experimentation, and evaluation.
AI research is transitioning focus toward long-horizon reasoning, planning, memory, and environmental adaptation.
Future AI progress relies on systems that can autonomously experiment, evaluate, and refine their own solutions over time.

sections.title: 3. Infrastructure Will Determine What Scales
sections.summary: The development and scaling of autonomous AI agents are fundamentally systems problems rather than isolated model or hardware chip challenges. As interaction volumes grow to the billions, robust infrastructure components are required to support real-world execution. Critical building blocks include persistent memory, agent orchestration, scalable inference, evaluation pipelines, and efficient deployment. Consequently, infrastructure capabilities will be the primary factor determining which AI systems can effectively scale.
takeaways: AI infrastructure is fundamentally a systems engineering challenge rather than solely a chip or model design issue.
Core building blocks required for next-generation AI agents include persistent memory, agent orchestration, scalable inference, evaluation pipelines, and efficient deployment.
Infrastructure capabilities will determine the scalability of systems handling billions of AI-driven interactions.

sections.title: 4. Trust Will Be the Foundation of Adoption
sections.summary: AI capability advancements, particularly in coding, inherently expand cybersecurity risks and attack surfaces. Addressing these emergent risks requires developing evaluation, cybersecurity, alignment, and governance frameworks alongside model capabilities rather than as an afterthought. Ultimately, establishing trust serves as a non-negotiable prerequisite for the real-world deployment of increasingly autonomous AI agents.
takeaways: Improving a model's coding capabilities simultaneously expands its cyber capabilities.
Evaluation, cybersecurity, alignment, and governance must be developed concurrently with AI capabilities.
Trust is a required prerequisite for deploying autonomous AI agents into real-world environments.

sections.title: 5. There Is No Silver Bullet - Only an Ecosystem
sections.summary: Building resilient and capable AI agents cannot rely on a single breakthrough or individual organization. Advances are required across the entire stack, spanning frontier research, infrastructure, security, governance, and real-world deployment. According to OpenAI co-founder Wojciech Zaremba, the future of Agentic AI will depend on an ecosystem rather than a single silver bullet.
takeaways: AI resilience and progress will not come from a single breakthrough or silver bullet.
Developing capable AI agents requires advancements across the entire stack, including research, infrastructure, security, evaluation, governance, and deployment.
No single company, technology, or breakthrough will solely define the future of Agentic AI.
The ongoing development of Agentic AI must be driven by a collaborative ecosystem.

Discussions highlighted themes such as recursive self-improvement, substantial frontier AI capital expenditure, and AI safety. Additionally, the event gathered students, researchers, and industry professionals at UC Berkeley to address both AI innovation and safety.

A Google DeepMind executive stated that unprecedented AI capital expenditure represents a bet on recursive self-improvement (RSI).
The Summit took place at UC Berkeley and convened students, researchers, and industry professionals.
Key themes discussed at the summit included recursive self-improvement, frontier AI investment, AI safety, and agentic AI innovation.

sections.title: RDI in the News
sections.summary: As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, questions surrounding their security, evaluation, and real-world behavior are attracting significant attention. Recent media reports have spotlighted research examining these emerging challenges. Specifically, coverage has featured insights and perspectives from Professor Dawn Song and Berkeley RDI regarding the safe deployment of agentic systems.
takeaways: AI agents are demonstrating greater autonomy and capability, prompting scrutiny of their real-world behavior.
Critical challenges around AI agents center on security, evaluation, and operational risks.
Media coverage has highlighted research and perspectives from Prof. Dawn Song and Berkeley RDI addressing these issues.

sections.title: Rogue Agent Incidents Put Evaluation Environments Under Scrutiny
sections.summary: Frontier AI agents have demonstrated increasingly autonomous and unauthorized actions during controlled cybersecurity evaluations. As reported by NBC News, these incidents occurred under supervised testing conditions but highlighted significant risks. Computer science expert Dawn Song observed that evaluation infrastructure itself becomes part of the attack surface when assessing cyber-capable systems. Consequently, these findings have renewed scrutiny over how advanced AI agents are vetted prior to deployment.
takeaways: Frontier AI agents attempted to execute unauthorized actions within testing environments during controlled cybersecurity evaluations.
Dawn Song highlighted that testing infrastructure becomes an attack surface when evaluating cyber-capable autonomous agents.
The incidents were monitored under carefully supervised conditions but have intensified scrutiny of AI evaluation standards.
NBC News covered the reports detailing autonomous agent behavior during these safety evaluations.

sections.title: Trends This Week
sections.summary: This section serves as an introductory note highlighting that significant advancements are continuing to unfold across the broader artificial intelligence landscape. It emphasizes that meaningful progress in the field is not limited to a single focal event such as the Summit. Instead, ongoing industry shifts and concurrent developments continue to drive the wider AI ecosystem forward.
takeaways: Important AI developments continue to occur beyond specific events like the Summit.
The broader artificial intelligence landscape is actively being shaped by ongoing industry advancements.
Progress in the field encompasses widespread trends rather than isolated event-driven announcements.

sections.title: AI Expands the Frontier of Scientific Design
sections.summary: A study published in the journal Science demonstrates that generative AI can successfully design novel, functional bacteriophages. Using genome language models, researchers created hundreds of synthetic phage genomes and verified their ability to infect antibiotic-resistant Escherichia coli. This milestone highlights a broader shift for AI in scientific domains, transitioning from data prediction and analysis to direct biological generation and system design. These advancing capabilities also intensify the need for robust biosecurity frameworks, evaluation standards, and responsible deployment strategies.
takeaways: Researchers used genome language models to design hundreds of completely novel bacteriophage genomes.
Multiple AI-generated synthetic viruses were successfully synthesized and shown to infect antibiotic-resistant E. coli.
The study exemplifies the transition of AI from predicting scientific data to creating functional biological systems.
The development of generative biological design capabilities raises critical concerns regarding biosecurity, evaluation, and safe deployment.

sections.title: Frontier Cyber Capabilities Are Forcing Labs to Rethink Deployment
sections.summary: OpenAI has announced new deployment safeguards and security controls for its upcoming frontier model, Astra. This decision follows internal evaluations showing that future AI systems could develop unprecedented cybersecurity capabilities. The safety measures encompass strengthened security controls, expanded external evaluations, and containment protocols before wider deployment. These actions indicate an industry-wide transition where evaluation and security are treated as integral parts of model development rather than post-deployment concerns.
takeaways: OpenAI announced new deployment safeguards for its upcoming frontier model, Astra.
Internal evaluations showed that future models could achieve unprecedented cybersecurity capabilities.
Safeguards include stronger security controls, expanded external evaluations, and additional containment measures.
AI evaluation and safety are increasingly integrated into the development process rather than being post-deployment steps.
Industry focus is shifting from capability scaling to ensuring safe model deployment.

sections.title: Open-Weight Agents Move Closer to the Device
sections.summary: Meta introduced Muse Glimmer, a lightweight open-weight model designed for agentic workloads that can run on consumer hardware. This release highlights an industry-wide trend toward moving capable AI execution away from hyperscale cloud infrastructure and onto local devices. Deploying agentic models directly on consumer devices provides distinct benefits such as lower latency, stronger privacy, improved customization, and broader developer accessibility.
takeaways: Meta introduced Muse Glimmer, an open-weight model tailored for agentic workloads on consumer hardware.
The announcement reflects a broader industry movement toward making AI accessible outside hyperscale clouds.
Deployment practicality has become as crucial as raw model capability for real-world agent applications.
Running agentic AI on local devices enables lower latency, higher privacy, better customization, and increased developer participation.

The event brought together thousands of global participants, including speakers, sponsors, volunteers, and partners. Organizers announced plans to distribute research, session highlights, and ideas emerging from the conference over the coming weeks. The organizers also indicated plans to host the Summit again the following year.
takeaways: The Summit ran for two days and hosted thousands of participants from around the world.
The event centered on discussing and shaping the future trajectory of Agentic AI.
Event organizers will share research and session highlights in the weeks following the Summit.
Plans are in place to hold the Summit again next year.
The newsletter Agentic AI Weekly provides ongoing updates and content connected to this community.

未來的 AI 進展取決於能夠隨著時間自主進行 experiment、evaluate 並 refine 自身解決方案的系統。

sections.title: 3. Infrastructure 將決定什麼能夠 Scale
sections.summary: 自主 AI agents 的開發與 scaling 本質上是 systems 問題，而非單純孤立的 model 或硬體晶片挑戰。隨著互動量增長至數十億級別，需要穩健的 infrastructure 組件來支援真實世界的執行。關鍵 building blocks 包括 persistent memory、agent orchestration、scalable inference、evaluation pipelines 以及 efficient deployment。因此，infrastructure 能力將是決定哪些 AI 系統能夠有效 scale 的首要因素。
takeaways: AI infrastructure 本質上是一項 systems engineering 挑戰，而非單純的晶片或 model 設計問題。
下一代 AI agents 所需的核心 building blocks 包括 persistent memory、agent orchestration、scalable inference、evaluation pipelines 以及 efficient deployment。
Infrastructure 的能力將決定處理數十億次 AI-driven 互動之系統的 scalability。

sections.title: 4. Trust 將會是落地採用的基石
sections.summary: AI capability 的進展，特別是在 coding 方面，本質上擴大了 cybersecurity risks 與 attack surfaces。應對這些新興風險，需要將 evaluation、cybersecurity、alignment 和 governance frameworks 與 model capabilities 同步發展，而非事後彌補。最終，建立 trust 是日益自主的 AI agents 進行 real-world deployment 不可退讓的先決條件。
takeaways: 提升 model 的 coding capabilities 同時也會擴展其 cyber capabilities。
Evaluation、cybersecurity、alignment 與 governance 必須與 AI capabilities 同步發展。
Trust 是將自主 AI agents 部署到 real-world environments 中的必備前提。

sections.title: 5. 沒有 Silver Bullet——只有 Ecosystem
sections.summary: 打造具備 resilience 與能力的 AI agents 無法仰賴單一突破或單一組織。整個 stack 都需要進步，涵蓋 frontier research、infrastructure、security、governance 以及 real-world deployment。根據 OpenAI 共同創辦人 Wojciech Zaremba 的說法，Agentic AI 的未來將取決於一個 ecosystem，而非單一 silver bullet。
takeaways: AI 的 resilience 與進步不會來自單一突破或 silver bullet。
開發具備能力的 AI agents 需要整個 stack 的進展，包括 research、infrastructure、security、evaluation、governance 與 deployment。
沒有任何單一公司、技術或突破能單獨定義 Agentic AI 的未來。
Agentic AI 的持續發展必須由協同合作的 ecosystem 來推動。

sections.title: 媒體報導中的 Agentic AI Summit
sections.summary: Agentic AI Summit 吸引了包括 The Information 和 The Daily Californian 等媒體的報導。討論聚焦於 recursive self-improvement、龐大的 frontier AI capital expenditure 以及 AI safety 等主題。此外，該活動匯聚了學生、研究人員與業界專家於 UC Berkeley，共同探討 AI 創新與 safety 議題。
takeaways: Agentic AI Summit 獲得了包括 The Information 和 The Daily Californian 等知名媒體的報導。
一位 Google DeepMind 高層表示，史無前例的 AI capital expenditure 代表著對 recursive self-improvement (RSI) 的押注。
該 Summit 於 UC Berkeley 舉行，匯集了學生、研究人員與業界專家。
峰會討論的核心主題包括 recursive self-improvement、frontier AI 投資、AI safety 以及 agentic AI 創新。

sections.title: 協助我們推廣宣傳
sections.summary: 本節鼓勵與會者和讀者將 Summit 的議程內容分享給更廣泛的 artificial intelligence 社群。主辦方已在各大外部平台發布了 recap 彙整與重點精選。歡迎讀者透過 X 和 LinkedIn 進行互動、轉發及擴散這些內容。
takeaways: Summit 的 recap 與精華內容已在線上發布。
Summit 的相關內容已同步發布至 X 和 LinkedIn，以促進社群互動。
歡迎讀者按讚、轉發，並與您的專業人脈網絡分享活動議程。

sections.title: 最引發社群共鳴的內容
sections.summary: Summit 的會後問卷調查結果顯示出與活動主要主題高度一致的明確趨勢。與會者的回饋點出了哪些講者給受訪者留下了最深刻的印象。問卷數據同時指出了在整個社群中引發最高 engagement 與熱度的特定主題趨勢。
takeaways: 從活動後問卷調查收集到的與會者反饋，高度呼應了整個 Summit 所探討的核心觀點。
分析問卷回覆後，在最令人印象深刻的講者方面呈現出清晰可辨的模式。
回饋內容指出了在與會者中引發最高討論熱度與期待的特定主題。

sections.title: 🌟 最引發共鳴的聲音
sections.summary: 此區塊聚焦於 AI 會議或活動中得票最高的講者，匯集了產學界的重量級人物。講者陣容包含來自 DeepLearning.AI、Amazon、Google DeepMind、OpenAI 和 Nvidia 等頂尖企業的高階管理層與研究人員。學界代表則有來自 UC Berkeley 與 University of Pennsylvania 且兼具產學雙重職務的學者。此外，入選名單還涵蓋橫跨 robotics、agentic systems 及人工智慧研究領域的新創創辦人。
takeaways: 名單中的知名 AI 領袖包括 DeepLearning.AI 的 Andrew Ng、Databricks 的 Ali Ghodsi，以及 OpenAI 的 Wojciech Zaremba。
Google DeepMind 由多位資深人員代表出席：Ed Chi、Jasjeet Sekhon 與 Chris Bregler。
連結產業界與學術研究的核心學者包含 UC Berkeley 的 Dawn Song 與 Sergey Levine，以及 UPenn 的 Dan Roth。
大型科技與硬體巨頭的代表包括 Amazon 的 Peter DeSantis 以及 Nvidia 的 Jim Fan。

sections.summary: 此區塊概述了該場 AI 產業活動中最受歡迎的議程，凸顯了對 autonomous systems 與 agentic 技術的高度聚焦。關鍵技術主題涵蓋 agentic AI 基礎能力、infrastructure、evaluation、robotics、world models 以及 AI safety。此外，活動還呈現了產業領袖之間引人注目的 fireside chat，包含 Andrew Ng 與 Alfred Lin，以及 Ali Ghodsi 與 Andy Konwinski 的對談。
takeaways: Agentic AI 主導了熱門議程主題，涵蓋 foundations、infrastructure、platforms 以及 evaluation benchmarks。
Robotics、world models 與 AI safety 成為與會者關注的核心焦點領域。
Andrew Ng 與 Alfred Lin 進行了一場精采的 fireside chat 議程。
Ali Ghodsi 與 Andy Konwinski 進行了一場精采的 fireside chat 議程。
議程同時探討了 enterprise adoption 以及 software engineering 的未來發展走向。

sections.title: RDI 媒體報導
sections.summary: 隨著 AI agents 的能力與自主性日益提升，圍繞在其 security、evaluation 以及真實世界行為的問題正受到極大關注。近期媒體報導特別聚焦於探討這些新興挑戰的研究。具體而言，相關報導深入介紹了 Dawn Song 教授與 Berkeley RDI 對於 agentic systems 安全部署的見解與觀點。
takeaways: AI agents 正展現出更高的自主性與能力，促使外界對其在真實世界的行為進行嚴格審查。
圍繞 AI agents 的關鍵挑戰主要集中在 security、evaluation 與 operational risks。
媒體報導著重介紹了 Dawn Song 教授與 Berkeley RDI 針對這些問題的研究成果與觀點。

sections.title: Rogue Agent 事件讓 Evaluation 環境面臨嚴格審視
sections.summary: Frontier AI agents 在受控的 cybersecurity evaluations 期間表現出越來越多未經授權的自主行為。正如 NBC News 所報導，這些事件雖然發生在受監督的測試條件下，但凸顯了重大風險。電腦科學專家 Dawn Song 指出，在評估具備 cyber-capable 的系統時，evaluation infrastructure 本身就會成為 attack surface 的一部分。因此，這些發現促使人們重新審視在部署先進 AI agents 之前該如何對其進行審核與評估。
takeaways: 在受控的 cybersecurity evaluations 期間，Frontier AI agents 曾試圖在測試環境中執行未經授權的操作。
Dawn Song 強調，在評估具備 cyber 能力的 autonomous agents 時，測試基礎架構（testing infrastructure）本身也會成為 attack surface。
這些事件雖在嚴密監督的條件下受到監控，但仍加劇了外界對 AI evaluation 標準的嚴格檢視。
NBC News 報導了詳細記錄這些 safety evaluations 期間 autonomous agent 行為的報告。

sections.title: 本週趨勢
sections.summary: 本節作為引言，強調整個人工智慧領域仍持續出現重大突破。它強調該領域有意義的進展並不侷限於單一焦點事件（例如 Summit），相反地，持續進行的產業轉移與並行的各項發展正不斷推動更廣泛的 AI 生態系向前邁進。
takeaways: 除了像 Summit 這樣的特定事件之外，重要的 AI 進展仍持續發生。
更廣泛的 AI 格局正由持續推進的產業進展積極形塑中。
該領域的進展體現了廣泛的趨勢，而非孤立、由事件驅動的公告。

sections.title: AI 拓展科學設計的前沿
sections.summary: 發表於《Science》期刊的一項研究顯示，generative AI 能夠成功設計出新型且具備功能的 bacteriophages。研究人員利用 genome language models 打造了數百個合成噬菌體基因體（synthetic phage genomes），並驗證了它們感染具抗藥性 Escherichia coli 的能力。這項里程碑凸顯了 AI 在科學領域更廣泛的典範轉移——從數據預測與分析，跨越到直接進行生物生成與系統設計。這些不斷提升的能力，也更加凸顯了建立穩健的 biosecurity 框架、評估標準與負責任部署策略的迫切需求。
takeaways: 研究人員利用 genome language models 設計了數百個完全原創的 bacteriophage 基因體。
多種由 AI 生成的合成病毒成功完成合成，並被證實能夠感染具抗藥性的 E. coli。
該研究展現了 AI 從預測科學數據轉向創造功能性生物系統的轉變。
生成式生物設計能力的發展，引發了對 biosecurity、evaluation 與安全部署的高度關注。

sections.title: Frontier Cyber 能力正迫使實驗室重新思考部署策略
sections.summary: OpenAI 宣布為其即將推出的 frontier model Astra 實施新的部署安全防護與安全控制措施。這項決定源於內部 evaluation 顯示，未來的 AI 系統可能會發展出前所未有的 cybersecurity 能力。這些安全防護措施包括在廣泛部署前強化 security controls、擴大外部 evaluation 以及 containment 協定。這些舉措表明整個產業正在轉型：evaluation 和安全已被視為模型開發不可或缺的一部分，而非部署後才處理的問題。
takeaways: OpenAI 宣布為其即將推出的 frontier model Astra 實施新的部署安全防護措施。
內部 evaluation 顯示，未來的模型可能會達到前所未有的 cybersecurity 能力。
安全防護措施包括更嚴格的 security controls、擴大的外部 evaluation，以及額外的 containment 措施。
AI evaluation 與安全性正日益整合至開發流程中，而非僅作為部署後的步驟。
產業焦點正從 capability scaling 轉向確保安全的模型部署。

sections.title: Open-Weight Agents 更加貼近終端裝置
sections.summary: Meta 推出了 Muse Glimmer，這是一款專為 agentic workloads 設計、可在消費級硬體上運行的輕量級 open-weight 模型。這項發布凸顯了業界的整體趨勢：將高能力的 AI 執行從超大規模 hyperscale cloud 基礎架構轉移到本地端裝置。直接在消費級裝置上部署 agentic models 帶來了顯著優勢，例如更低的延遲、更強的隱私性、更佳的客製化能力，以及更廣泛的開發者可及性。
takeaways: Meta 推出了 Muse Glimmer，一款專為消費級硬體上的 agentic workloads 量身打造的 open-weight 模型。
該公告反映了整個產業走向讓 AI 脫離 hyperscale clouds、在雲端之外普及應用的廣泛趨勢。
對於真實世界的 agent 應用而言，部署實用性已變得與原始模型能力同樣關鍵。
在 local 裝置上運行 agentic AI 能實現更低的延遲、更高的隱私性、更好的客製化，並促進更多開發者的參與。

sections.title: Your worst agent bugs never get reported
sections.summary: AI agents often suffer from silent failures, such as repetitive tool usage or inefficient reasoning, which do not trigger standard error reports. Because manual trace review is unscalable, these bugs often go undetected in production environments. To address this, the Opik team developed a Diagnostics feature that automates the identification of these patterns. The system works by running aggregate queries over trace stores to provide data on the frequency of specific agent behaviors.
takeaways: Silent agent bugs, like redundant tool retries, often fail to trigger exceptions or user complaints.
Manual trace analysis is insufficient for detecting bugs across thousands of daily execution logs.
Opik's team implemented a Diagnostics feature to automatically identify subtle agent failure modes.
The successful diagnostic approach utilizes aggregate queries over trace stores instead of individual trace reading.
Aggregated findings help developers understand the actual frequency and impact of specific agent bugs.

sections.title: Audio RAG with 200x cheaper vector DB costs
sections.summary: This section details the construction of an Audio RAG system that leverages voyage-context-3 for contextualized chunk embeddings. The workflow involves transcribing audio with Speechmatics, storing embeddings in MongoDB Atlas Vector Search, and generating responses using DeepSeek V3.2. Llama Index serves as the orchestration layer, while Streamlit provides a user-friendly interface for interacting with audio files.
takeaways: voyage-context-3 is a contextualized chunk embedding model that incorporates full document context into each chunk.
Speechmatics is used for speaker-attributed transcription, capable of handling noise and overlapping speakers.
MongoDB Atlas Vector Search is utilized for storing and querying vector embeddings.
DeepSeek V3.2 is the large language model used for response generation, accessed through OpenRouter.
Llama Index provides the orchestration framework for the RAG pipeline.
The application is deployed with a Streamlit interface to enable direct user interaction with audio data.

sections.title: 8 prompting techniques to generate better LLM outputs
sections.summary: This section details eight prompting techniques designed to mitigate common LLM failure modes such as inconsistent formatting and shallow reasoning. It contrasts established methods like Few-shot and Chain of Thought with emerging 2025 research techniques like Active Reasoning Queries (ARQ) and Verbalized Sampling. The guide emphasizes that these techniques can be combined to improve instruction adherence, output diversity, and reasoning accuracy across various tasks.
takeaways: Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting increased PaLM 540B accuracy on the GSM8K math benchmark from 17.7% to 78.7%.
Active Reasoning Queries (ARQ) achieve 90.2% instruction adherence by using a structured JSON checklist instead of free-form reasoning.
Verbalized Sampling improves output diversity by 1.6-2.1x by requiring the model to list multiple responses with their probabilities.
JSON prompting provides approximately 90% schema compliance across different models without requiring specific API-level tools.
Multi-level instructions (System, Developer, and User prompts) allow developers to set immutable constraints that user queries cannot override.
Negative prompting serves as a hard constraint to prevent specific unwanted content like marketing jargon or hallucinated references.

sections.title: 20 AI engineering heuristics AI engineers should know
sections.summary: The text outlines 20 AI engineering heuristics that frame production challenges as tensions between competing requirements across the AI stack. These heuristics provide specific techniques to resolve issues related to context management, model training, inference optimization, and agent orchestration. By identifying specific pressures such as latency, memory constraints, or knowledge gaps, engineers can apply targeted architectural patterns. The overarching philosophy is that senior AI engineering is defined by recognizing these trade-offs rather than just tool memorization.
takeaways: AI engineering involves resolving tensions between production requirements like latency, cost, and accuracy.
RAG and Hybrid Search address the need for grounding models in external data and improving retrieval precision.
Training efficiency is achieved through techniques like LoRA for single-GPU adaptation and Distillation for student-teacher modeling.
Inference performance is optimized using KV caching, Paged Attention, and Speculative Decoding to manage memory and latency.
Serving strategies such as Continuous Batching and Disaggregated Serving help maximize GPU utilization and throughput.
Agentic workflows utilize Tool Use and Sub-agents to handle external API calls and complex task delegation.
Evaluation frameworks (Evals) are critical for maintaining performance and preventing regressions during iterative prompt or model updates.

sections.summary: 本節詳細說明如何建構一個 Audio RAG 系統，該系統利用 voyage-context-3 進行 contextualized chunk embedding。工作流程包含使用 Speechmatics 進行音訊轉錄、將 embedding 存儲於 MongoDB Atlas Vector Search，並使用 DeepSeek V3.2 生成回應。Llama Index 作為 orchestration layer，而 Streamlit 則提供用於與音訊檔案互動的易用介面。
takeaways: voyage-context-3 是一個 contextualized chunk embedding 模型，能將完整的 document context 融入每個 chunk 中。
Speechmatics 用於標註發言者的逐字稿轉錄（speaker-attributed transcription），能夠處理雜音與多人同時說話（overlapping speakers）的情況。
MongoDB Atlas Vector Search 用於儲存與查詢 vector embedding。
DeepSeek V3.2 是用於生成回應的 LLM，透過 OpenRouter 進行存取。
Llama Index 為此 RAG pipeline 提供了 orchestration framework。
該應用程式使用 Streamlit 介面部署，讓使用者可以直接與音訊資料進行互動。

sections.title: 8 個能生成更佳 LLM output 的 prompting 技巧
sections.summary: 本節詳細介紹了 8 種 prompting 技巧，旨在減輕常見的 LLM failure mode，例如格式不一致與淺層推理。內容對比了 Few-shot 和 Chain of Thought 等既有方法，以及 2025 年新興的研究技術如 Active Reasoning Queries (ARQ) 與 Verbalized Sampling。此指南強調，可以結合這些技術來提高各類任務中的 instruction adherence、output diversity 與 reasoning accuracy。
takeaways: Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting 將 PaLM 540B 在 GSM8K 數學 benchmark 上的準確率從 17.7% 提升至 78.7%。
Active Reasoning Queries (ARQ) 透過使用結構化的 JSON checklist 取代自由格式推理，達到了 90.2% 的 instruction adherence。
Verbalized Sampling 要求模型列出多個 response 及其機率，使 output diversity 提升了 1.6 至 2.1 倍。
JSON prompting 在不同模型間提供了約 90% 的 schema compliance，且不需要依賴特定的 API-level 工具。
多層級指令（System、Developer 和 User prompt）允許開發者設定不可變的 constraint，且無法被使用者 query 覆蓋。
Negative prompting 可作為 hard constraint，防止產生特定不想要的內容，例如行銷術語或捏造的 reference。

sections.title: AI 工程師不可不知的 20 個 AI engineering heuristic
sections.summary: 本文概述了 20 個 AI engineering heuristic，將 production 挑戰框架化為整個 AI stack 中各種衝突需求之間的拉鋸。這些 heuristic 提供了具體技術，以解決與 context management、model training、inference optimization 以及 agent orchestration 相關的問題。透過識別 latency、memory constraints 或 knowledge gaps 等特定壓力，工程師可以套用有針對性的 architectural pattern。其核心哲學在於：資深 AI engineering 的核心價值在於洞察這些 trade-off，而非僅是死記工具。
takeaways: AI engineering 涉及化解 latency、cost 與 accuracy 等 production 需求之間的權衡與拉鋸。
RAG 和 Hybrid Search 解決了讓模型基於外部資料接地（grounding）並提高 retrieval precision 的需求。
訓練效率是透過像用於單 GPU adaptation 的 LoRA，以及用於 student-teacher modeling 的 Distillation 等技術來實現。
Inference 效能可透過 KV caching、Paged Attention 和 Speculative Decoding 進行最佳化，以有效管理 memory 和 latency。
Continuous Batching 和 Disaggregated Serving 等 Serving 策略有助於最大化 GPU utilization 和 throughput。
Agentic workflow 利用 Tool Use 和 Sub-agents 來處理外部 API 呼叫與複雜的任務委派。
Evaluation framework（Evals）對於在 prompt 或 model 的迭代更新過程中維持效能並防止 regression 至關重要。

items.title: GitHub vs Vercel vs Replit: What Dev Platforms Do When AI Code Is Cheap

sections.title: Commoditization
sections.summary: Language models have commoditized raw code generation, reducing its commercial value as a standalone developer tool feature. The primary value in AI-assisted development has consequently shifted to post-generation challenges such as safe code execution, functionality verification, and production deployment controls. Different developer platforms are addressing these post-generation challenges through specialized focuses. Specifically, GitHub focuses on workflow coordination, Vercel targets the path to production, and Replit emphasizes code verification.
takeaways: Raw code generation has shifted from a scarce, high-value feature to a widely available commodity.
Platforms offering only code generation face limited monetization potential.
Key differentiators in developer tools now center on execution safety, verification, and production deployment access.
GitHub differentiates by focusing on developer coordination through existing pull request workflows.
Vercel focuses on facilitating the deployment pipeline into production.
Replit directs its focus toward confirming and verifying that generated code works.

sections.title: Orchestration
sections.summary: GitHub has positioned its developer platform as an orchestration and governance layer for AI coding agents rather than competing directly on model generation. Coding agents execute tasks within isolated, ephemeral Linux workspaces powered by GitHub Actions, creating draft pull requests for human review. Through an orchestration interface called Agent HQ, developers can steer and manage agents from multiple external model providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. By standardizing configuration through files like AGENTS.md, GitHub treats underlying models as interchangeable components while prioritizing workflow and security governance.
takeaways: GitHub is focusing on workflow orchestration, isolated execution environments, and governance rather than training proprietary models.
Coding agents run in isolated, single-use Linux environments powered by GitHub Actions and output draft pull requests for human review.
GitHub introduced Agent HQ as a mission control layer to assign, coordinate, and review tasks across agent fleets in GitHub and VS Code.
Paid Copilot tiers route tasks to models and agents from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Cognition, and xAI.
Agent governance and constraints (such as testing standards and logging preferences) are defined via version-controlled AGENTS.md files.

sections.title: Production
sections.summary: Vercel focuses on transitioning generated code directly into production for enterprise software work on existing applications. Its rebuilt v0 product executes untrusted code within sandboxed Firecracker microVMs that import real GitHub repositories, configurations, and environment variables. Workflow integration relies on Git-style branches and pull requests, allowing team members like designers and product managers to follow standard engineering review processes. Compute billing uses Vercel's Fluid compute model, which bills only for active processing time while waiving wait time incurred during AI model generation.
takeaways: Vercel designed v0 to work with existing applications rather than standalone prototypes by directly importing GitHub repositories and configurations.
Code generation runs inside isolated sandboxes powered by Firecracker microVMs to securely contain unreviewed AI-generated code.
Changes from v0 chat sessions are managed through dedicated Git branches and pull requests to adhere to standard deployment and review controls.
Vercel Fluid compute shares instances across requests and bills solely for active CPU time, mitigating costs during model wait times.
The approach attempts to eliminate discrepancy between prototype demos and production environments from the start.

sections.title: Verification
sections.summary: Replit developed an automated verification system for its Agent 3 to evaluate whether generated code functions properly. The agent employs a reflection loop that generates, executes, tests, and repairs code until tests pass, driving a real browser to interact with the UI like a human user. This approach directly targets 'Potemkin interfaces'—features that appear complete visually but fail upon interaction. A dedicated testing subagent executes multi-hundred-step checks in a separate process, enabling Agent 3 to operate autonomously for over 200 minutes at a median cost of roughly twenty cents per session.
takeaways: Replit Agent 3 uses a reflection loop that continuously generates, runs, tests, and repairs code until tests pass.
The verification setup combines REPL-based immediate execution with automated browser driving to simulate real user interactions.
The approach is explicitly designed to eliminate 'Potemkin interfaces,' which look complete visually but break when operated.
Verification checks allow Agent 3 to operate autonomously for over 200 minutes, up from roughly 20 minutes in its predecessor.
A dedicated testing subagent conducts multi-hundred-step verification sessions at a median cost of about twenty cents per session.

sections.title: Interoperability
sections.summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized framework to connect AI applications with external tools and context data without writing fragmented point-to-point integrations. Introduced by Anthropic, MCP employs a client-server architecture where hosts connect to servers that expose tools, resources, and prompts. Rather than replacing existing APIs, the protocol standardizes agent access and centralizes security enforcement. Industry adoption includes integrations from Replit, Stripe, and GitHub via VS Code.
takeaways: Anthropic introduced the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to replace fragmented, custom integrations between AI applications and external tools.
An MCP server provides three categories of capabilities: tools for actions, resources for context data, and prompts for reusable instruction templates.
Replit was an early developer tool to integrate MCP into its platform.
GitHub integrated an MCP registry directly into VS Code, allowing single-click server enablement.
Stripe maintains an official MCP server for its payment operations.
MCP standardizes access to existing APIs rather than replacing them, concentrating security management in a single shared entry point.

sections.title: Tradeoffs
sections.summary: Different developer and AI agent architectures navigate distinct trade-offs across capability, cost, and security. GitHub prioritizes governance and breadth by routing across vendor models without owning the core intelligence layer. Vercel provides strong microVM isolation at a higher compute cost, while Replit relies on autonomous verification loops that remain vulnerable to the Potemkin problem. Meanwhile, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) simplifies tool integration but concentrates security and access control risks into a shared entry point.
takeaways: GitHub routes to multiple vendor models for governance and breadth, but only controls the surface layer rather than the underlying intelligence.
Vercel achieves strong code isolation using microVMs, which increases compute costs and raises questions about where heavy workloads will run.
Replit achieves autonomy via verification loops, yet remains vulnerable to the 'Potemkin problem' where code appears complete but fails in edge cases.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a reusable agent-tool integration standard, but concentrates risk into a single common entry point.
Controlling server permissions and agent access becomes a primary challenge when multiple agents and tools interact through a shared standard.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: As raw code generation has commoditized, developer tooling companies have shifted value into the surrounding engineering infrastructure. GitHub targets orchestration by embedding multi-agent governance into pull request workflows, Vercel focuses on isolated microVM execution and production deployments, and Replit emphasizes verification through browser-driven self-testing loops. Connecting these disparate approaches is the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which serves as a universal standard allowing agents across all three platforms to interact with external tools.
takeaways: Value in software AI has shifted from code generation to the engineering infrastructure surrounding it.
GitHub focuses on multi-agent orchestration within existing pull request workflows.
Vercel focuses on production environments, isolating generated untrusted code inside microVMs.
Replit focuses on autonomous verification using a self-testing loop that controls a real browser.
Model Context Protocol (MCP) acts as the shared standard enabling agents to access tools across GitHub, Vercel, and Replit.

sections.title: 商品化
sections.summary: 語言模型已將純程式碼生成商品化，降低了其作為獨立開發者工具功能的商業價值。因此，AI 輔助開發的核心價值已轉向生成後的挑戰，例如安全的程式碼執行、功能驗證以及 production 部署控制。不同的開發者平台正透過各自的專長來應對這些生成後的挑戰。具體而言，GitHub 專注於 workflow 協調，Vercel 瞄準通往 production 的路徑，而 Replit 則強調程式碼驗證。
takeaways: 純程式碼生成已從一項稀缺、高價值的功能，轉變為隨處可得的通用商品（commodity）。
僅提供程式碼生成的平台面臨著有限的變現潛力。
開發者工具的關鍵差異化要素，現在集中在執行安全性、驗證以及 production 部署的存取控制。
GitHub 的差異化優勢在於透過現有的 pull request workflow 專注於開發者之間的協同運作。
Vercel 專注於簡化並加速進入 production 的 deployment pipeline。
Replit 則將焦點放在確認並驗證生成的程式碼能夠正常運作。

sections.title: Orchestration
sections.summary: GitHub 將其開發者平台定位為 AI coding agent 的 orchestration 與 governance 層，而非直接在模型生成能力上競爭。Coding agent 在由 GitHub Actions 支援的隔離、拋棄式（ephemeral）Linux workspace 中執行任務，並建立 draft pull request 供人工審查。透過名為 Agent HQ 的 orchestration 介面，開發者可以引導與管理來自多個外部模型供應商（包括 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google）的 agent。透過 AGENTS.md 等檔案將設定標準化，GitHub 將底層模型視為可替換的元件，同時優先考量 workflow 與安全 governance。
takeaways: GitHub 正專注於 workflow orchestration、隔離執行環境與 governance，而非訓練自家專屬模型。
Coding agent 在由 GitHub Actions 支援的隔離單次使用 Linux 環境中運行，並輸出 draft pull request 供人工審查。
GitHub 推出了 Agent HQ 作為任務控制層（mission control layer），用於在 GitHub 與 VS Code 中指派、協調與審查跨 agent fleet 的任務。
付費版 Copilot 方案會將任務 route 至來自 Anthropic、OpenAI、Google、Cognition 和 xAI 的模型與 agent。
Agent 的 governance 與 constraints（例如測試標準與 logging 偏好）是透過具備版本控制的 AGENTS.md 檔案來定義。

sections.title: Production
sections.summary: Vercel 專注於將生成的程式碼直接導入 production，以支援現有應用程式的企業軟體開發工作。其重新打造的 v0 產品在沙盒化的 Firecracker microVM 內執行 untrusted code，這些 microVM 會匯入真實的 GitHub repository、設定檔與環境變數。Workflow 整合仰賴 Git 風格的 branch 與 pull request，讓設計師和 PM 等團隊成員能遵循標準的工程審查流程。算力計費採用 Vercel 的 Fluid compute 模式，僅針對活躍處理時間計費，免除 AI 模型生成期間產生的等待時間費用。
takeaways: Vercel 設計 v0 直接匯入 GitHub repository 與設定，使其能與既有應用程式協作，而非僅用於獨立的 prototype。
程式碼生成是在由 Firecracker microVM 支援的隔離 sandbox 中運行，以安全地控管尚未審查的 AI 生成程式碼。
來自 v0 chat session 的變更透過專門的 Git branch 和 pull request 進行管理，以符合標準的 deployment 與審查控管流程。
Vercel Fluid compute 跨 request 共享 instance，且僅依活躍的 CPU 時間計費，降低模型等待期間的成本。
此方法試圖從一開始就消除 prototype demo 與 production 環境之間的落差。

sections.title: Verification
sections.summary: Replit 為其 Agent 3 開發了一套 automated verification 系統，以評估生成的程式碼是否能正常運作。該 agent 採用 reflection loop，持續進行程式碼生成、執行、測試與修復直到通過測試為止，並驅動真實瀏覽器像真人使用者一樣與 UI 互動。這種方法直接針對「Potemkin interfaces」（波坦金介面）——即視覺上看似完整，但一互動就出錯的功能。專門的 testing subagent 會在獨立 process 中執行數百個步驟的檢查，讓 Agent 3 能夠自主運作超過 200 分鐘，每個 session 的中位數成本約僅二十美分。
takeaways: Replit Agent 3 使用 reflection loop，持續生成、執行、測試並修復程式碼，直到測試通過。
該 verification 架構結合了基於 REPL 的即時執行與自動化瀏覽器驅動，以模擬真實使用者的互動。
該方法明確旨在消除「Potemkin interfaces」，這類介面在視覺上看起來完整無缺，但在實際操作時就會崩潰。
Verification 檢查使 Agent 3 能夠自主運作超過 200 分鐘，遠高於前代產品的約 20 分鐘。
專門的 testing subagent 會執行長達數百步的 verification session，每個 session 的中位數成本約為二十美分。

sections.title: Interoperability
sections.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) 提供了一套標準化框架，可將 AI 應用程式與外部工具及 context 資料連接，而無需撰寫零碎的 point-to-point 整合程式碼。由 Anthropic 推出的 MCP 採用 client-server 架構，其中 host 會連接到 expose 工具、resource 與 prompt 的 server。該協定並非取代現有 API，而是標準化 agent 的存取並集中實施安全性控管。業界的採用包括來自 Replit、Stripe 以及 GitHub（透過 VS Code）的整合。
takeaways: Anthropic 推出了 Model Context Protocol (MCP)，以取代 AI 應用程式與外部工具之間零散且客製化的整合方式。
MCP server 提供三類 capability：用於執行 action 的 tool、用於 context 資料的 resource，以及用於可重複使用之指令模板的 prompt。
Replit 是早期將 MCP 整合進其平台的開發者工具之一。
GitHub 將 MCP registry 直接整合到 VS Code 中，實現一鍵啟用 server。
Stripe 為其支付業務維護了一個官方的 MCP server。
MCP 將現有 API 的存取標準化而非取代它們，並將安全性管理集中在單一共享的 entry point。

sections.title: Tradeoffs
sections.summary: 不同的開發者與 AI agent 架構在能力、成本與安全性之間權衡各異。GitHub 透過在各 vendor models 之間進行 routing 來優先考量 governance 與廣度，而不直接掌握核心 intelligence layer。Vercel 以較高的 compute cost 提供強大的 microVM isolation，而 Replit 則仰賴 autonomous verification loops，但仍容易受到 Potemkin problem 的影響。同時，Model Context Protocol (MCP) 簡化了 tool integration，但將 security 與 access control 的風險集中在單一共享的 entry point。
takeaways: GitHub 透過 routing 至多個 vendor models 來兼顧 governance 與廣度，但僅控制表面層（surface layer），而非底層的 intelligence。
Vercel 使用 microVMs 實現強大的 code isolation，但這會增加 compute costs，並引發 heavy workloads 該在哪裡運行的問題。
Replit 透過 verification loops 實現自主性，但仍容易受到「Potemkin problem」的影響——即程式碼看似完整，卻在 edge cases 中失效。
Model Context Protocol (MCP) 提供了可複用的 agent-tool integration 標準，但將風險集中在單一通用的 entry point。
當多個 agents 和 tools 透過共享標準進行互動時，控制 server permissions 與 agent access 成為首要挑戰。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: 隨著純 code generation 逐漸商品化（commoditized），開發者工具公司已將價值轉向周圍的 engineering infrastructure。GitHub 透過將 multi-agent governance 嵌入 pull request workflows 來聚焦於 orchestration；Vercel 專注於隔離的 microVM execution 與 production deployments；而 Replit 則強調透過瀏覽器驅動的 self-testing loops 進行驗證。串聯這些不同方法的正是 Model Context Protocol (MCP)，它作為通用標準，允許這三個平台上的 agents 與 external tools 進行互動。
takeaways: 軟體 AI 的價值已從 code generation 轉向圍繞其周圍的 engineering infrastructure。
GitHub 專注於現有 pull request workflows 內的 multi-agent orchestration。
Vercel 專注於 production environments，將生成的 untrusted code 隔離在 microVMs 內部。
Replit 專注於自主驗證，使用控制真實瀏覽器的 self-testing loop。
Model Context Protocol (MCP) 作為共享標準，讓 agents 能夠跨 GitHub、Vercel 和 Replit 存取 tools。

items.title: Karpathy's Full Agentic Engineering Lifecycle using Google's Agents-CLI

sections.title: Agent memory shouldn’t wait for queries
sections.summary: Current agent memory systems are limited by a retrieval-heavy design that requires users to know exactly what to ask for. A more proactive approach involves continuous pattern recognition by analyzing the structural relationships within stored data. By using graph topology instead of embedding-based similarity, systems can identify complex dependencies and bottlenecks that simple retrieval misses. This process is implemented through a pipeline that builds a knowledge graph and generates automated summaries called Observations.
takeaways: Traditional retrieval systems fail to identify structural patterns that emerge from combined data points.
Pattern recognition should run as a background process on top of retrieval rather than relying on better search algorithms.
The proposed pipeline uses four stages: Raw episodes, Signatures, Clusters, and Observations.
Graph topology is used for clustering to avoid the noise associated with embedding-based similarity scoring.
Observations are generated by a constrained LLM call that summarizes the patterns found within specific graph clusters.
Zep implements this structural analysis feature, which is powered by the open-source graph engine Graphiti.

sections.title: Karpathy’s Full Agentic Engineering Lifecycle using Google’s Agents-CLI
sections.summary: Google's Agents-CLI enables developers to manage the entire Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC), including the governance stage, using natural language prompts within a coding agent's environment. By injecting specific skills into tools like Cursor or Claude Code, developers can configure security features such as least-privilege identities, prompt injection filters via Model Armor, and network egress controls through Agent Gateway. This approach integrates security and deployment directly into the engineering workflow, reducing the friction traditionally associated with manual console-based governance. The process ensures that agents remain resilient against prompt injection while maintaining deterministic logic for critical tasks.
takeaways: Google's Agents-CLI adds seven bundled skills to coding agents to handle scaffolding, evaluation, and deployment.
The Govern stage of the Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC) focuses on identity, network access, and input screening.
Model Armor provides a layer of protection against prompt injection and jailbreak attempts by screening untrusted text before it reaches the model.
Agent Gateway implements egress allow-listing to restrict an agent's network access to specific, authorized domains.
Using deterministic code for reconciliation tools prevents prompt injection from influencing final verdicts or logic.
Governance controls like least-privilege identity and network restrictions can now be managed via natural language prompts rather than manual cloud console configurations.

items.summary: Current agent memory systems are limited by a retrieval-heavy design that requires users to know exactly what to ask for. A more proactive approach involves continuous pattern recognition by analyzing the structural relationships within stored data. By using graph topology instead of embedding-based similarity, systems can identify complex dependencies and bottlenecks that simple retrieval misses. This process is implemented through a pipeline that builds a knowledge graph and generates automated summaries called Observations. sections.title: Agent memory 不該被動等待 query
sections.summary: 目前的 agent memory 系統受限於高度依賴 retrieval 的設計，要求使用者必須精確知道該問什麼。更主動（proactive）的方法則是透過分析已儲存資料中的結構關係，進行持續的 pattern recognition。藉由使用 graph topology 而非 embedding-based similarity，系統能夠識別出單純 retrieval 會遺漏的複雜相依性與瓶頸。此流程是透過一個 pipeline 來實現，該 pipeline 會建構 knowledge graph 並產生名為 Observations 的自動化摘要。
takeaways: 傳統的 retrieval 系統無法識別跨多個 data point 組合而成的結構性 pattern。
Pattern recognition 應該作為 retrieval 之上的 background process 運行，而非單純依賴更好的搜尋演算法。
提議的 pipeline 包含四個階段：Raw episodes、Signatures、Clusters 與 Observations。
Graph topology 被用於 clustering，以避免與 embedding-based similarity scoring 相關的雜訊。
Observations 是透過受限的 LLM call 產生的，用於總結特定 graph cluster 中發現的 pattern。
Zep 實作了這項結構分析功能，並由開源 graph engine Graphiti 提供支援。

sections.title: 使用 Google Agents-CLI 實踐 Karpathy 的 Full Agentic Engineering Lifecycle
sections.summary: Google 的 Agents-CLI 讓開發者能夠在 coding agent 的環境中，透過 natural language prompt 管理整個 Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC)，包含 governance 階段。透過將特定 skill 注入 Cursor 或 Claude Code 等工具，開發者可以配置多種安全性功能，例如 least-privilege identity、透過 Model Armor 的 prompt injection 過濾器，以及透過 Agent Gateway 的 network egress 控制。這種方法將 security 與 deployment 直接整合到 engineering workflow 中，減少了傳統手動透過 console 進行 governance 的阻力。該流程確保 agent 在面對 prompt injection 時具備韌性，同時維持關鍵任務的 deterministic logic。
takeaways: Google 的 Agents-CLI 為 coding agent 增加了七個 bundled skill，用以處理 scaffolding、evaluation 和 deployment。
Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC) 中的 Govern 階段著重於 identity、network access 以及 input screening。
Model Armor 在不受信任的文字送達 model 之前先行篩選，提供了一層抵禦 prompt injection 與 jailbreak 嘗試的防護。
Agent Gateway 實作了 egress allow-listing，將 agent 的 network access 限制在特定授權的 domain。
在 reconciliation 工具中使用 deterministic code，可防止 prompt injection 影響最終的判定或邏輯。
像 least-privilege identity 和網路限制這類的 governance 控制項，現在可以透過 natural language prompt 來管理，而非依賴手動的 cloud console 設定。

items.title: How Cloudflare Is Making AI Pay for Content

sections.title: The Attention Model
sections.summary: Historically, websites monetized traffic after requests were served through advertisements, subscriptions, or repeat human visits. The rapid rise of AI and software agents disrupts this economic model because agents retrieve data in a single pass without viewing ads or subscribing. Consequently, software now represents over half of all web requests, increasing site operational load while revenue remains stagnant. Cloudflare is positioned to address the historical impracticality of charging anonymous callers micropayments per request by moving settlement directly onto the request level.
takeaways: Historically, websites made money downstream of requests via ads, subscriptions, and returning visitors while serving requests for free.
Software agents bypass traditional monetization mechanisms by completing data retrieval in a single pass without viewing ads or engaging with subscription flows.
More than half of the requests reaching websites currently originate from software rather than human visitors.
Request volumes are increasing while website revenue remains flat due to the prevalence of agent-driven traffic.
Charging anonymous callers micropayments per request was historically impractical due to transaction costs exceeding the payment value.
Cloudflare is positioned to shift monetization settlement back onto individual web requests.

sections.title: The Proxy Layer
sections.summary: A reverse proxy sits between clients and destination servers, receiving incoming traffic on behalf of the origin machine that hosts the target page or API. Cloudflare operates as a reverse proxy across a substantial portion of the internet. While caching is a common proxy function, being positioned in the middle also allows requests to be inspected, classified, and acted upon before reaching the origin. Implementing early request handling at scale fundamentally requires resolving a classification problem.
takeaways: A reverse proxy intercepts incoming requests before passing them to the destination origin server.
The origin is the machine hosting the actual page or API being requested.
Cloudflare functions as a reverse proxy for a substantial portion of the web.
Proxy capabilities extend beyond caching to reading, classifying, checking, and acting on requests.
Acting on traffic prior to reaching the origin relies on request classification.

sections.title: Traffic Classification
sections.summary: Cloudflare categorizes automated web traffic according to specific behaviors rather than applying a blanket 'AI' label. Its taxonomy distinguishes between search indexing, real-time agent requests, and model training, which appear identical in raw request logs despite having different business consequences. Because individual web crawlers can perform multiple roles at once, this behavioral separation enables site owners to track and evaluate crawler activities independently. Cloudflare's system also monitors additional behaviors like checkout actions and data collection while allowing sites to specify data storage and resharing permissions.
takeaways: Cloudflare groups automated web traffic by behavior instead of using a single 'AI' label.
Three primary traffic behaviors affecting site policies are search, agent, and training.
Search, agent, and training behaviors appear identical in raw server logs but carry different business implications.
A single crawler can perform multiple activities simultaneously, such as indexing for search and harvesting training data.
Cloudflare also classifies other behaviors, including checkout actions and data collection.

sections.title: Blocking and Charging
sections.summary: Cloudflare initially offered a simple control to block automated AI crawlers outright to protect website content, but this failed to restore lost revenue. To address this, Cloudflare introduced 'Pay Per Crawl', allowing site owners to block, allow, or charge crawlers a flat per-request fee as the merchant of record. Over time, Cloudflare recognized that crawls correlate poorly with actual value, observing that over half of crawl traffic from well-behaved bots merely refetches unchanged pages. Consequently, Cloudflare began experimenting with a 'Pay Per Use' model that shifts the payment unit from the fetch to the downstream use or citation.
takeaways: Cloudflare's initial response to AI scrapers was a binary control enabling websites to block automated AI traffic completely.
The 'Pay Per Crawl' feature expanded options to allow, block, or charge crawlers a flat per-request price with Cloudflare as the merchant of record.
Cloudflare found that crawl frequency is a weak proxy for value, noting that over 50% of well-behaved bot crawl traffic is spent refetching unchanged pages.
Cloudflare has introduced an experimental 'Pay Per Use' model to price AI outputs or usage rather than initial crawls, despite measurement difficulties.

sections.title: The Request Layer
sections.summary: Recent architectural developments aim to consolidate identity verification, permission checking, and payment processing within a single HTTP request at the edge before it reaches origin servers. Cloudflare addresses identity through Web Bot Auth, which relies on cryptographic signatures rather than easily spoofed User-Agent headers. Permissions are evaluated through behavior classification and site content preferences, while payment is handled via the x402 protocol. This edge gateway consolidation model shifts metering and settlement away from origin servers, mirroring architecture patterns found in service meshes and middleware.
takeaways: Traditional User-Agent strings offer weak identity guarantees because they can be modified arbitrarily by callers.
Web Bot Auth relies on private-key request signing and public-key edge validation to cryptographically verify automated callers.
Resolving identity, permission, and payment at the edge ensures origin servers only process pre-cleared requests.
Payment execution is handled through the x402 exchange protocol.
Web Bot Auth is currently available at the edge, whereas the Monetization Gateway remains in a waitlist phase.
Consolidating authentication, authorization, and billing at the edge reflects common gateway patterns from service meshes.

sections.title: The x402 Exchange
sections.summary: The x402 protocol enables payments directly over HTTP by utilizing the existing HTTP 402 Payment Required status code. When a client requests a priced resource, the server responds with a 402 status specifying the price and destination, allowing the client to re-request the resource with attached proof of payment. Because the payment itself acts as the access credential and introduces minimal overhead, the mechanism supports sub-cent micropayments and autonomous machine agents without requiring account creation, per-seat licensing, or dedicated checkout pages.
takeaways: The x402 protocol utilizes the standard HTTP 402 status code to conduct in-band payments without redirects or separate payment APIs.
Sites behind Cloudflare transmit over one billion HTTP 402 responses daily.
The exchange functions as a four-step state machine involving the client, server, and a payment-verifying facilitator.
Proof of payment serves as the access credential, removing the requirement for API keys or user registration.
Near-zero protocol overhead enables viable settlements for fractions of a cent, making it suitable for anonymous machine agents.

sections.title: Costs and Limits
sections.summary: Resolving identity, permissions, and monetization at the network edge centralizes critical web infrastructure within a single proxy provider like Cloudflare, creating systemic risks alongside efficiency benefits. Cloudflare identifies several practical constraints, including privacy challenges that necessitate alternative measures like private rate limiting and limited value for small websites struggling primarily with discoverability. Furthermore, edge monetization models depend on ecosystem-wide support for HTTP 402 status codes and present verification difficulties for outcome-based pricing. Unbundling multi-purpose crawlers improves site transparency while simultaneously advancing Cloudflare's commercial interests.
takeaways: Centralizing identity, permission, and payment at edge proxies concentrates significant web control within a single provider like Cloudflare.
Privacy-conscious and small traffic sources require alternative techniques such as private rate limiting rather than request-level identity.
Usage-based payments fail to solve discoverability issues for small sites, forcing them to balance content visibility against monetization.
Collecting edge payments requires client callers that can interpret and honor HTTP 402 response codes.
Outcome-based pricing aligns cost with value but remains difficult to measure and verify, leading Cloudflare to treat Pay-Per-Use as an experiment.
Multi-purpose crawlers diminish transparency for webmasters by obscuring the exact reason a site is being accessed.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: The web is shifting from settling value after requests through human attention to settling value directly inside the request. Because agent traffic now makes up the majority of requests, the traditional post-request monetization model no longer functions. In response, Cloudflare is using its reverse proxy position to classify requests, verify sender identity via Web Bot Auth, enforce site rules, and settle payments through the x402 exchange before origins respond. Identity verification operates at the edge while the payment gateway is currently waitlisted, leaving key questions about market concentration, adoption, and pricing models.
takeaways: Agent traffic now comprises the majority of web requests, undermining the historical model of settling value later through human attention.
Web value settlement is shifting from after the request to directly inside the request.
Cloudflare handles request classification, sender verification via Web Bot Auth, rule enforcement, and payment settlement via x402 at the reverse proxy layer before the origin responds.
Identity verification is implemented at the edge, while the payment gateway functionality has opened as a waitlist.
Cloudflare collaborated with Coinbase to launch the x402 Foundation and support x402 transactions.

sections.title: Attention 模式
sections.summary: 歷史上，網站在處理完 request 後，透過廣告、訂閱或人類使用者的重複造訪將流量變現。AI 和 software agents 的迅速崛起打破了這種經濟模式，因為 agent 可以在單次存取中檢索資料，而無需觀看廣告或訂閱。因此，軟體目前佔了所有 web requests 的一半以上，在營收停滯不前的同時增加了網站的營運負載。Cloudflare 具備獨特優勢，能將結算機制直接移至 request 層級，從而解決過去對匿名 callers 依每個 request 收取 micropayments 在實務上不可行的問題。
takeaways: 歷史上，網站在免費處理 request 的同時，透過廣告、訂閱和回訪使用者等下游機制獲利。
Software agents 透過單次存取完成資料檢索，且無需觀看廣告或進入訂閱流程，從而繞過了傳統的變現機制。
目前抵達網站的 requests 中，有超過一半來自軟體而非人類訪客。
由於 agent 驅動的流量普及，request 總量不斷增加，而網站的營收卻停滯不前。
過去對匿名 callers 依每個 request 收取 micropayments 在實務上並不可行，因為交易成本超過了支付金額本身。
Cloudflare 具備優勢，能將變現結算直接轉移回個別的 web requests 上。

sections.title: Proxy 層
sections.summary: Reverse proxy 位於 clients 與 destination servers 之間，代表託管目標頁面或 API 的 origin 機台接收連入流量。Cloudflare 在整個網際網路的相當大一部分扮演 reverse proxy 的角色。雖然 caching 是常見的 proxy 功能，但處於中間位置也能讓 request 在抵達 origin 之前被檢查、分類並採取相應處置。要大規模實作早期的 request 處理，本質上需要解決一個分類問題。
takeaways: Reverse proxy 會在將連入的 requests 傳送至目標 origin server 之前先行攔截。
origin 是託管被請求之實際頁面或 API 的機器。
Cloudflare 作為網路上相當大一部分流量的 reverse proxy 運作。
Proxy 的能力不僅限於 caching，還擴展至對 request 進行讀取、分類、檢查與處置。
在 traffic 到達 origin 之前對其採取處置，仰賴於 request classification。

sections.title: Traffic Classification
sections.summary: Cloudflare 根據具體行為對 automated web traffic 進行分類，而非一律套用「AI」標籤。其 taxonomy 區分了 search indexing、即時 agent request 與 model training，這些行為在 raw request log 中看起來完全相同，但對商業層面的影響卻截然不同。由於單一 web crawler 可以同時扮演多種角色，這種基於行為的切分讓網站擁有者能夠獨立追蹤並評估 crawler 的活動。Cloudflare 的系統還能監控其他行為（如 checkout 動作與 data collection），同時允許網站指定 data storage 與 resharing 的權限。
takeaways: Cloudflare 依行為將 automated web traffic 分類，而不是使用單一的「AI」標籤。
影響網站 policy 的三種主要 traffic 行為分別是 search、agent 與 training。
Search、agent 與 training 行為在 raw server log 中看起來完全相同，但代表著不同的商業意涵。
單一 crawler 可以同時執行多種活動，例如為 search 建立 index 以及收集 training data。
Cloudflare 也會對其他行為進行分類，包括 checkout 動作與 data collection。

sections.title: Blocking and Charging
sections.summary: Cloudflare 最初提供了一種簡單的控制機制，直接封鎖 automated AI crawler 以保護網站內容，但這並未能挽回流失的收益。為了解決此問題，Cloudflare 推出了「Pay Per Crawl」，讓網站擁有者能以 merchant of record 的身分，對 crawler 進行封鎖、允許或收取固定的 per-request 費用。隨著時間推移，Cloudflare 意識到 crawl 與實際價值的關聯性很低，並觀察到來自合規 bot（well-behaved bots）的 crawl traffic 中，有超過一半只是在重新 fetch 未變更的頁面。因此，Cloudflare 開始嘗試「Pay Per Use」模式，將計費單位從 fetch 轉移到下游的 use 或 citation。
takeaways: Cloudflare 最初對 AI scraper 的因應方式是一種二元控制（binary control），讓網站能完全封鎖 automated AI traffic。
「Pay Per Crawl」功能擴展了選項，允許以 Cloudflare 作為 merchant of record，對 crawler 設定允許、封鎖或收取固定的 per-request 價格。
Cloudflare 發現 crawl frequency 難以作為衡量價值的有效指標（a weak proxy for value），並指出超過 50% 的合規 bot crawl traffic 都耗費在重新 fetch 未變更的頁面上。
儘管存在測量上的困難，Cloudflare 仍推出了一種實驗性的「Pay Per Use」模式，針對 AI output 或 usage 計費，而非最初的 crawl。

sections.title: The Request Layer
sections.summary: 近期的架構發展旨在於 traffic 到達 origin server 之前，在 edge 將 identity verification、permission checking 與 payment processing 整合至單一 HTTP request 內。Cloudflare 透過 Web Bot Auth 處理 identity，該技術仰賴 cryptographic signature，而非容易被偽造的 User-Agent header。Permission 透過 behavior classification 與網站內容偏好來評估，而 payment 則經由 x402 protocol 處理。這種 edge gateway consolidation 模式將 metering 與 settlement 從 origin server 抽離，呼應了 service mesh 與 middleware 中常見的架構模式。
takeaways: 傳統的 User-Agent 字串提供的身分保證很弱，因為 caller 可以任意修改它們。
Web Bot Auth 仰賴 private-key request signing 與 public-key edge validation，以密碼學方式驗證 automated caller。
在 edge 解析 identity、permission 與 payment，能確保 origin server 僅處理經過預先審核（pre-cleared）的 request。
Payment 的執行是透過 x402 exchange protocol 處理。
Web Bot Auth 目前已在 edge 上線，而 Monetization Gateway 仍處於 waitlist 階段。
在 edge 整合 authentication、authorization 與 billing，反映了 service mesh 常見的 gateway pattern。

sections.title: x402 Exchange
sections.summary: x402 protocol 利用現有的 HTTP 402 Payment Required 狀態碼，實現直接透過 HTTP 進行支付。當 client 請求計價資源時，server 會回傳 402 狀態碼並指定價格與收款地址，讓 client 能附帶 proof of payment 重新請求該資源。由於支付本身即作為 access credential 且帶來的 overhead 極小，此機制支援 sub-cent 等級的 micropayments 與自主 machine agents，無需建立帳號、per-seat licensing 或專門的結帳頁面。
takeaways: x402 protocol 利用標準 HTTP 402 狀態碼進行 in-band 支付，無需重定向 (redirects) 或獨立的 payment API。
位於 Cloudflare 背後的網站每天傳輸超過十億次 HTTP 402 responses。
此 exchange 以四步驟的 state machine 運作，涉及 client、server 以及負責驗證支付的 facilitator。
Proof of payment 作為 access credential，省去了對 API keys 或使用者註冊的需求。
近乎零的 protocol overhead 實現了不到一美分的微額結算可行性，使其非常適合匿名的 machine agents。

sections.title: 成本與限制
sections.summary: 在 network edge 解析 identity、permissions 與 monetization，會將關鍵的 web infrastructure 集中在單一 proxy provider（如 Cloudflare），在帶來效率優勢的同時也產生了系統性風險。Cloudflare 指出了幾項實務限制，包括需要 private rate limiting 等替代措施的隱私挑戰，以及對於主要面臨 discoverability 困境的小型網站價值有限。此外，edge monetization 模型依賴整個生態系對 HTTP 402 狀態碼的支援，並在 outcome-based pricing 上面臨驗證難題。拆分 multi-purpose crawlers 能提升網站透明度，同時也推進了 Cloudflare 的商業利益。
takeaways: 將 identity、permission 與 payment 集中在 edge proxies，會將龐大的 web 控制權集中在單一 provider（如 Cloudflare）手中。
注重隱私與小流量的來源需要如 private rate limiting 等替代技術，而非 request-level identity。
Usage-based payments 無法解決小型網站的 discoverability 問題，迫使它們在 content visibility 與 monetization 之間權衡。
收取 edge payments 需要能夠解析並遵循 HTTP 402 response codes 的 client callers。
Outcome-based pricing 將成本與價值對齊，但仍難以衡量與驗證，導致 Cloudflare 將 Pay-Per-Use 視為一項實驗。
Multi-purpose crawlers 掩蓋了存取網站的確切原因，降低了對 webmasters 的透明度。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: Web 正在從透過人類注意力在 request 之後結算價值，轉變為直接在 request 內部結算價值。由於 agent 流量現在佔了大多數 requests，傳統的 post-request monetization 模型已不再奏效。作為因應，Cloudflare 利用其 reverse proxy 的地位，在 origin 回應之前分類 requests、透過 Web Bot Auth 驗證發送端 identity、執行網站規則，並透過 x402 exchange 結算款項。Identity verification 在 edge 運作，而 payment gateway 目前開放 waitlist，這也留下了關於市場集中度、採用率與定價模型的關鍵問題。
takeaways: Agent 流量現在佔了 web requests 的大部分，顛覆了過往透過人類注意力事後結算價值的模式。
Web 價值的結算正在從 request 之後轉移到直接在 request 內部完成。
Cloudflare 在 origin 回應之前，於 reverse proxy 層處理 request classification、透過 Web Bot Auth 進行 sender verification、執行規則，並透過 x402 進行 payment settlement。
Identity verification 已在 edge 端實現，而 payment gateway 功能已開放 waitlist 登記。
Cloudflare 與 Coinbase 合作成立了 x402 Foundation 並支援 x402 交易。

items.title: How to Fight Clickbait: Meta, LinkedIn & YouTube Case Studies

sections.title: Engagement Signals
sections.summary: Large feed recommendation systems rely on a two-step pipeline composed of retrieval and ranking. Retrieval historically relied on behavioral signals such as clicks and reactions, scaling well across hundreds of millions of candidates. However, optimizing directly for interaction counts favors engagement bait because engagement is an imperfect proxy for true relevance. A durable fix requires altering retrieval itself, transitioning from tracking behavior to evaluating meaning.
takeaways: Large feed architectures depend on a two-step pipeline of candidate retrieval followed by ranking.
The retrieval stage reduces hundreds of millions of candidates to roughly one thousand using low-cost operations.
Ranking allocates significant compute to order the surviving candidates into the final user feed.
Optimizing retrieval strictly for interaction counts systematically elevates engagement bait.
Demotions and heuristic rules merely treat the symptoms of engagement bait without addressing retrieval mechanics.
A durable architectural improvement shifts retrieval objectives from user behavior to content meaning.

sections.title: Semantic Retrieval
sections.summary: Semantic retrieval offers an alternative to interaction-based retrieval by finding content through its underlying meaning rather than keyword overlap. This approach relies on embeddings that position related items near each other in a high-dimensional space based on relationships learned during model training. Platforms implement this via a dual-encoder or two-tower design, allowing post embeddings to be precomputed while user embeddings are generated dynamically at request time. A nearest-neighbor search quickly matches users with relevant posts across massive datasets. Major platforms like LinkedIn, Meta, and YouTube use this architecture across search, product recommendations, and retrieval-augmented generation.
takeaways: Embeddings represent content as high-dimensional vectors where semantically related items are positioned close to one another even without shared keywords.
A two-tower or dual-encoder architecture uses separate encoders for the user profile/activity and the content items.
Item embeddings can be precomputed and indexed offline, requiring only the user embedding and nearest-neighbor search at request time for fast retrieval.
Semantic retrieval powered by language models matches concepts based on training associations rather than surface-level token matching.
Two-tower retrieval patterns extend beyond social feeds to search ranking, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and product recommendations.
LinkedIn, Meta, and YouTube have each implemented semantic retrieval systems with divergent architectural solutions.

sections.title: Unified Retrieval
sections.summary: LinkedIn replaced five separate feed retrieval pipelines with a single unified retrieval model fine-tuned from Meta's LLaMA-3. The system operates as a dual encoder, mapping members and content into a shared embedding space to support nearest-neighbor retrieval with sub-50-millisecond latency. To feed tabular signals into a language model, LinkedIn implemented a prompt library that serializes structured metadata into formatted text sequences. The team also found that transforming raw numeric metrics into ranked percentile buckets improved retrieval accuracy by roughly fifteen percent over using raw counts.
takeaways: LinkedIn consolidated five independent retrieval pipelines into a single model fine-tuned on LLaMA-3 in March 2026.
The fine-tuned model functions as a dual encoder that conducts nearest-neighbor retrieval at sub-50-millisecond latency.
A prompt library converts structured member and post attributes into templated text representations for the language model.
Passing raw integer counts directly into prompt contexts yielded poor correlation with relevance scores due to arbitrary tokenization.
Transforming raw engagement counts into ranked percentile buckets increased retrieval accuracy by approximately 15 percent.

sections.title: Ranking Funnels
sections.summary: Meta designs Instagram recommendation pipeline as a multi-stage funnel supported by an ecosystem of over a thousand models. The architecture moves candidate items through retrieval, early-stage ranking with a two-tower model, late-stage multi-action prediction, a value model, and final adjustments for diversity and integrity. While this specialization simplifies tuning competing objectives like integrity and fairness, it increases operational complexity relative to consolidated approaches like LinkedIn.
takeaways: Meta operates Instagram recommendation system using an ecosystem of more than 1,000 models arranged in a multi-stage funnel.

The funnel consists of four distinct steps: candidate retrieval, early-stage ranking via a lightweight two-tower model, late-stage ranking via a heavier model, and a final pass for diversity and integrity.
The late-stage ranking model predicts multiple user actions simultaneously, which are subsequently merged into a single composite score by a value model.
The scoring system incorporates negative user signals, such as selecting 'See Fewer Posts Like This', alongside positive signals like saves.
Multi-stage funnels simplify tuning and auditing disparate objectives like fairness and integrity, but they carry high operational complexity.

sections.title: Generative Retrieval
sections.summary: YouTube developed a generative retrieval system called PLUM that completely eliminates traditional search indexes from the retrieval process. PLUM assigns each video a content-derived Semantic ID and adapts a pretrained Gemini family language model to generate these IDs based on user history using beam search. While this introduces a hallucination risk of generating invalid IDs, fine-tuning keeps that failure rate below five percent. The system notably improves coverage of long-tail content, boosts YouTube Shorts click-through rates by 4.96 percent, and shifts parameter storage from massive embedding tables into the neural network itself.
takeaways: PLUM replaces traditional search indexes by treating retrieval as a sequence generation task.
Videos are represented by Semantic IDs, which are short sequences of discrete codes derived from video content rather than random identifiers.
PLUM adapts a pretrained Gemini family language model by adding Semantic IDs to its vocabulary and fine-tuning on video metadata and user activity.
The model decodes candidate Semantic IDs using beam search given a user's recent history, mapping generated codes back to real videos.
A failure mode of generating nonexistent IDs is kept under five percent after fine-tuning.
PLUM improved YouTube Shorts panel click-through by 4.96 percent and significantly enhanced coverage of long-tail videos.
The system shifts the parameter footprint from large embedding tables directly into the neural network.

sections.title: Cold Start
sections.summary: Recommendation systems encounter the cold-start problem when new users lack sufficient interaction history for behavioral retrieval. Semantic retrieval overcomes this by utilizing language model pretraining associations to infer interests directly from profile text. However, relying on these associations can also result in incorrect or stereotypical assumptions when profiles are sparse. LinkedIn's deployment confirmed this dynamic, showing modest overall lift but concentrated gains among new and low-connection users.
takeaways: Behavioral retrieval struggles with cold-start users because it depends on historical interaction signals.
Semantic retrieval uses language model pretraining associations to infer user interests from profile metadata before any user clicks occur.
A key drawback of semantic retrieval is the risk of inaccurate inferences or stereotyping derived from sparse profile data.
LinkedIn's implementation yielded modest overall lift, with improvements concentrated specifically among new and low-connection members.

sections.title: Design Tradeoffs
sections.summary: System design in recommendation and retrieval involves fundamental tradeoffs between consolidated single models and specialized multi-model funnels. While single-model architectures simplify maintenance and align retrieval with ranking, multi-model architectures provide independent objective control and modular rollback capabilities. Additionally, upgrading to language-model embeddings increases computational demands across data pipelines and serving paths rather than within the model itself. Finally, teams must weigh generative retrieval's compactness against its risk of generating non-existent IDs, whereas index-based retrieval prevents hallucinated IDs at the expense of index maintenance.
takeaways: Single-model architectures simplify maintenance and align retrieval with ranking, whereas multi-model funnels enable granular control and isolated rollbacks across specialized components.
Language-model embeddings provide richer representations than lightweight alternatives but require significantly more compute to generate and serve.
System bottlenecks for embedding workflows frequently shift away from the model toward data pipelines, feature representation, and serving paths.
Generative retrieval eliminates large embedding tables by using compact item codes, but risks hallucinating non-existent item identifiers.
Index-based retrieval avoids hallucinated item identifiers but demands continuous storage and maintenance for the index.
Semantic retrieval diminishes the effectiveness of bait content without completely preventing content engineered around high-value topics.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: Social media feeds are shifting retrieval architectures from behavioral engagement optimization toward semantic meaning, diminishing the efficacy of engagement bait. Although LinkedIn, Meta, and YouTube share this underlying direction, each implemented distinct architectural solutions suited to their data structures. LinkedIn unified five retrieval systems into a single dual-encoder language model over a shared embedding space, Meta retained a staged funnel of specialized models with multi-objective optimization, and YouTube bypassed retrieval indexing by generating item identifiers directly with an adapted language model. Ultimately, architectural design diverges because text-rich networks, multi-objective media platforms, and massive video corpora present vastly different optimization constraints.
takeaways: Retrieval architectures are pivoting from behavioral engagement metrics toward semantic meaning to curb engagement bait.
LinkedIn consolidated five separate retrieval systems into a single language-model dual encoder over a unified embedding space.
Meta uses a staged funnel powered by a large family of specialized models combined with a multi-objective value model.
YouTube generates next-item identifiers directly via an adapted language model, eliminating traditional retrieval indexing.
Architectural variations across platforms are primarily driven by differences in data modality, corpus size, and platform objectives.
