sections.title: Engagement Signals
sections.summary: 大型 feed 推薦系統依賴由 retrieval 與 ranking 組成的兩階段 pipeline。Retrieval 歷來依賴點擊與 reaction 等行為訊號，能在數億個 candidate 中良好 scale。然而，直接針對互動次數進行最佳化會助長 engagement bait，因為 engagement 並不能完美代表真正的 relevance。持久的解法需要改變 retrieval 本身，從追蹤行為轉變為評估內容語意。
takeaways: 大型 feed 架構依賴 candidate retrieval 後接 ranking 的兩階段 pipeline。
Retrieval 階段使用低成本運算將數億個 candidate 縮減至約一千個。
Ranking 分配大量算力將留下來的 candidate 排序成最終的 user feed。
嚴格針對互動次數最佳化 retrieval 會系統性地推高 engagement bait。
Demotion 與 heuristic 規則僅能治標，並未解決 engagement bait 背後的 retrieval 機制問題。
持久的架構改進將 retrieval 目標從使用者行為轉移至內容語意。

sections.title: Semantic Retrieval
sections.summary: Semantic retrieval 提供了一種替代基於互動的 retrieval 方案，透過內容的潛在語意而非 keyword 重疊來尋找內容。這種方法依賴 embedding，根據模型訓練期間學到的關聯性，在高維空間中將相關 item 放置在彼此附近。平台透過 dual-encoder 或 two-tower 設計實現這點，讓 post embedding 可以離線預先計算，而 user embedding 則在 request time 動態生成。Nearest-neighbor search 可以在海量資料集中迅速將使用者與相關 post 進行匹配。LinkedIn、Meta 和 YouTube 等主流平台在 search、product recommendations 與 retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) 中廣泛使用此架構。
takeaways: Embedding 將內容表示為高維 vector，即使沒有共享的 keyword，語意相關的 item 也會被定位在彼此相近的位置。
Two-tower 或 dual-encoder 架構為 user profile/activity 與 content item 使用獨立的 encoder。
Item embedding 可以離線預先計算並建立 index，在 request time 僅需 user embedding 與 nearest-neighbor search 即可實現快速 retrieval。
由 language model 驅動的 semantic retrieval 會根據訓練獲得的關聯來匹配概念，而非僅依賴表層的 token matching。
Two-tower retrieval pattern 不僅限於社群 feed，還延伸應用至 search ranking、retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) 以及 product recommendations。
LinkedIn、Meta 和 YouTube 都各自實現了採用不同架構解法的 semantic retrieval 系統。

sections.title: Unified Retrieval
sections.summary: LinkedIn 以單一由 Meta 的 LLaMA-3 fine-tune 而來的 unified retrieval 模型，取代了五個獨立的 feed retrieval pipeline。該系統以 dual encoder 運作，將 member 與內容映射到共享的 embedding space 中，以支援延遲低於 50 毫秒的 nearest-neighbor retrieval。為了將 tabular 訊號輸入至 language model，LinkedIn 實作了一個 prompt library，將結構化 metadata 序列化為格式化的 text sequence。該團隊還發現，將原始數值指標轉換為 ranked percentile bucket，相比使用原始計數，能將 retrieval 準確度提高約 15%。
takeaways: LinkedIn 於 2026 年 3 月將五個獨立的 retrieval pipeline 整合為單一基於 LLaMA-3 fine-tune 的模型。
該 fine-tune 後的模型作為 dual encoder 運作，能以低於 50 毫秒的延遲進行 nearest-neighbor retrieval。
Prompt library 將結構化的 member 與 post 屬性轉換為提供給 language model 的模板化文字表示。
由於任意的 tokenization，直接將原始整數計數傳入 prompt context 會導致其與 relevance score 的相關性極差。
將原始 engagement 次數轉換為排序後的 percentile buckets，使 retrieval accuracy 提升了約 15 percent。

sections.title: Ranking Funnels
sections.summary: Meta 將 Instagram recommendation pipeline 設計為由超過一千個模型生態系統所支援的 multi-stage funnel。該架構引導 candidate items 依序通過 retrieval、使用 two-tower model 的 early-stage ranking、late-stage multi-action prediction、value model，以及針對 diversity 和 integrity 的最終調整。雖然這種專業化分工簡化了對 integrity 與 fairness 等相互競爭目標的調校，但相較於 LinkedIn 等整合式方法，它增加了 operational complexity。
takeaways: Meta 採用由 1,000 多個模型組成並以 multi-stage funnel 排列的生態系統，來運作 Instagram recommendation system。
該 funnel 包含四個明確步驟：candidate retrieval、透過輕量級 two-tower model 進行的 early-stage ranking、透過較重模型進行的 late-stage ranking，以及針對 diversity 和 integrity 的 final pass。
late-stage ranking model 會同時預測多個 user actions，隨後由 value model 將這些預測合併為單一 composite score。
該評分系統除了納入如 saves 等正面訊號外，也整合了負面 user signals，例如選取「See Fewer Posts Like This」。
Multi-stage funnels 簡化了對 fairness 和 integrity 等不同目標的調校與稽核，但同時也帶來了高昂的 operational complexity。

sections.title: Generative Retrieval
sections.summary: YouTube 開發了一套名為 PLUM 的 generative retrieval 系統，該系統在 retrieval 流程中徹底摒除了傳統的 search indexes。PLUM 為每支影片賦予一個從內容衍生的 Semantic ID，並微調 pretrained Gemini family language model，透過 beam search 根據 user history 生成這些 IDs。雖然這帶來了生成無效 ID 的 hallucination 風險，但 fine-tuning 將該 failure rate 壓低至 5 percent 以下。該系統顯著改善了 long-tail content 的 coverage，將 YouTube Shorts 的 click-through rates 提升了 4.96 percent，並將 parameter storage 從龐大的 embedding tables 轉移至 neural network 本身。
takeaways: PLUM 透過將 retrieval 視為 sequence generation 任務，取代了傳統的 search indexes。
影片以 Semantic IDs 表示，這些是由影片內容衍生出的離散代碼短序列（short sequences of discrete codes），而非隨機識別碼。
PLUM 透過將 Semantic IDs 加入其 vocabulary，並在 video metadata 與 user activity 上進行 fine-tuning，進而改編 pretrained Gemini family language model。
該模型在給定使用者近期歷史紀錄的情況下，使用 beam search 解碼候選 Semantic IDs，並將生成的代碼映射回真實影片。
生成不存在 ID 的 failure mode 在 fine-tuning 後被控制在 5 percent 以下。
PLUM 將 YouTube Shorts 面板的 click-through 提升了 4.96 percent，並大幅增強了 long-tail videos 的 coverage。
該系統將 parameter footprint 從大型 embedding tables 直接轉移到 neural network 中。

sections.title: Cold Start
sections.summary: 當新用戶缺乏足夠的互動歷史以進行 behavioral retrieval 時，推薦系統就會遇到 cold-start 問題。Semantic retrieval 透過利用 language model 的 pretraining associations 直接從 profile 文字推斷興趣，進而克服了這個問題。然而，當 profile 資訊稀疏時，依賴這些關聯也可能導致錯誤或刻板的假設。LinkedIn 的部署證實了這種動態，顯示整體 lift 有限，但成效高度集中在新用戶與 low-connection 用戶群中。
takeaways: Behavioral retrieval 在面對 cold-start 使用者時成效不彰，因為它依賴歷史 interaction signals。
Semantic retrieval 利用 language model pretraining associations，在使用者產生任何點擊之前，即可從 profile metadata 推斷使用者興趣。
Semantic retrieval 的主要缺點在於，源自稀疏 profile 資料可能帶來不準確推論或刻板印象的風險。
LinkedIn 的實作帶來了溫和的整體 lift，改善主要特別集中在新會員與 low-connection 會員之間。

sections.title: Design Tradeoffs
sections.summary: 推薦與檢索的系統設計涉及 consolidated single models 與專門化 multi-model funnels 之間的基本權衡。雖然單一模型架構簡化了維護並讓 retrieval 與 ranking 一致，但 multi-model 架構提供了獨立的目標控制與模組化 rollback 能力。此外，升級到 language-model embeddings 會增加整個 data pipelines 和 serving paths 的運算需求，而不僅僅是在模型內部。最後，團隊必須權衡 generative retrieval 的緊湊性與其生成不存在 ID 的風險，而 index-based retrieval 雖然防止了 hallucinated IDs，卻以維護 index 為代價。
takeaways: Single-model 架構簡化了維護工作，並讓 retrieval 與 ranking 的目標對齊；相對地，multi-model funnels 則允許針對特定組件進行更細緻的控制與獨立的 rollback。
相較於輕量替代方案，Language-model embeddings 能提供更豐富的表徵能力，但在生成與 serving 上需要顯著更多的運算資源。
Embedding 工作流程的系統瓶頸經常不是出在模型本身，而是轉移到 data pipeline、feature representation 以及 serving path 上。
Generative retrieval 透過使用精簡的 item code 來消除龐大的 embedding tables，但存在幻覺生成不存在的 item identifier 之風險。
Index-based retrieval 能避免幻覺生成 item identifier，但需要為 index 投入持續的儲存空間與維護成本。
Semantic retrieval 降低了誘餌內容的有效性，但無法完全防止針對高價值主題精心設計的內容。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: 社群媒體動態牆的 retrieval 架構正從以行為 engagement 最佳化轉向以 semantic meaning 為主，從而削弱了 engagement bait 的效果。儘管 LinkedIn、Meta 和 YouTube 都朝著這個基本方向前進，但各自實作了適合自身資料結構的獨特架構解決方案。LinkedIn 將五個 retrieval 系統整合為基於統一 embedding 空間的單一 dual-encoder language model；Meta 保留了結合多目標最佳化、由大量專屬模型所驅動的分階段 funnel；而 YouTube 則透過改編後的 language model 直接生成 item identifier，繞過了 retrieval indexing。歸根結底，架構設計的差異源於文字豐富的網路、多目標媒體平台以及龐大的影音語料庫所帶來的最佳化限制大相徑庭。
takeaways: Retrieval 架構正從行為 engagement 指標轉向 semantic meaning，以遏制 engagement bait。
LinkedIn 將五個獨立的 retrieval 系統整合為基於統一 embedding 空間的單一 language-model dual encoder。
Meta 採用了分階段的 funnel 架構，由龐大的專屬模型家族搭配 multi-objective value model 來驅動。
YouTube 透過改編後的 language model 直接生成下一個 item identifier，擺脫了傳統的 retrieval indexing。
不同平台之間的架構差異，主要受資料模態 (data modality)、語料庫規模 (corpus size) 和平台目標的不同所驅動。

sections.title: How to query billion+ rows on postgres without overhead
sections.summary: Cloudflare transitioned from manual Postgres partitioning and cron-based aggregates to TimescaleDB after facing performance bottlenecks with billion-row datasets. Tiger Cloud offers a managed version of TimescaleDB that automates time-based partitioning through hypertables and simplifies rollups with continuous aggregates. By using the Tiger CLI as an MCP server, developers can integrate these database capabilities directly into AI tools like Claude Code to automate infrastructure provisioning and querying.
takeaways: Standard Postgres requires manual partition management and custom cron jobs for aggregates when datasets scale to billions of rows.
TimescaleDB uses hypertables to automate time-based partitioning, ensuring queries only scan relevant data chunks.
Continuous aggregates in TimescaleDB replace manual rollup pipelines by incrementally refreshing data in the background.
Tiger Cloud is a managed TimescaleDB service that maintains compatibility with the standard Postgres wire protocol.
Tiger CLI functions as an MCP server, allowing AI agents like Claude Code to provision databases and run SQL directly.
Cloudflare reduced query times by up to 35x by moving to the technology underlying Tiger Cloud.
Tiger CLI is open source under the Apache 2.0 license and supports tools like Cursor, VS Code, and Gemini CLI.

sections.title: Cross-model KV cache transfer in LLM families
sections.summary: NVIDIA researchers have introduced a training-free method to transfer KV caches between different models within the same LLM family. This approach utilizes a closed-form linear mapping to convert one model's cache into the format required by another, effectively bypassing the prefill stage. The conversion process is significantly faster than re-processing context and maintains high accuracy levels for the target model. This technique addresses the inefficiency of model routing where switching models typically invalidates existing caches.
takeaways: NVIDIA's method enables KV cache transfer between models in the same family, such as Qwen to Qwen or Llama to Llama.
The conversion process runs 2.7x to 25x faster than re-processing the context through a full prefill.
The approach uses a closed-form linear map for each target layer and head, requiring no gradient descent or neural adapters.
Accuracy retention for the receiving model ranges from 73% to 98% across tested pairs like Llama 3.1 and Ministral 3.
The method involves stripping and reapplying RoPE (Rotary Positional Embeddings) to ensure position-free mapping.
Current limitations include a requirement for identical KV head counts and dimensions between the source and target models.

sections.title: A technique to understand TP, TN, FP and FN
sections.summary: The text describes a simplified two-step framework for identifying binary classification outcomes: True Positive (TP), True Negative (TN), False Positive (FP), and False Negative (FN). By asking whether the model's prediction was correct and what the predicted class was, users can easily derive the appropriate label. This method aims to reduce confusion when interpreting model performance metrics.
takeaways: Binary classification outcomes are categorized into four types: TP, TN, FP, and FN.
The first step in labeling is determining if the prediction matches the actual class, resulting in a True or False designation.
The second step identifies the predicted class as either Positive or Negative.
Combining the results of these two questions yields the final classification label.
This technique is presented as a way to simplify the understanding of confusion matrix components.

sections.summary: NVIDIA 研究人員提出了一種無需訓練（training-free）的方法，能在同一個 LLM 家族內的不同模型之間轉移 KV cache。此方法利用封閉形式線性映射（closed-form linear mapping）將一個模型的快取轉換為另一個模型所需的格式，從而有效跳過 prefill 階段。此轉換過程比重新處理 context 快上許多，並能維持目標模型的高準確度。這項技術解決了 model routing 中切換模型通常會導致現有快取失效的低效問題。

該轉換過程的執行速度比透過完整 prefill 重新處理 context 快 2.7 倍至 25 倍。
該方法針對每個目標 layer 和 head 使用封閉形式線性映射，無需梯度下降（gradient descent）或 neural adapters。
在 Llama 3.1 和 Ministral 3 等受測模型對中，接收端模型的準確度保留率介於 73% 至 98% 之間。
該方法包含剝除並重新套用 RoPE（Rotary Positional Embeddings），以確保進行 position-free 的映射。
目前的限制包括來源模型與目標模型的 KV head 數量及維度必須完全一致。

sections.title: 理解 TP、TN、FP 與 FN 的技巧
sections.summary: 本文介紹了一套簡化的兩步驟架構，用來判別二元分類（binary classification）結果：True Positive (TP)、True Negative (TN)、False Positive (FP) 和 False Negative (FN)。透過詢問模型的預測是否正確以及預測的類別為何，使用者可以輕鬆推導出對應的標籤。此方法旨在減少解讀模型效能指標時的困惑。
takeaways: 二元分類結果分為四種類型：TP、TN、FP 和 FN。
標記的第一步是判斷預測是否與實際類別相符，從而得出 True 或 False 的判定。
第二步則是將預測類別識別為 Positive 或 Negative。
結合這兩個問題的結果，即可得出最終的分類標籤。
此技巧旨在簡化對混淆矩陣（confusion matrix）各組成要素的理解。

sections.title: ReAct vs Plan-and-Act pattern in agents
sections.summary: The ReAct agent pattern suffers from context accumulation where failed steps persist in the prompt, potentially distracting the model from its objective. In contrast, the Plan-and-Act pattern separates the agent's logic into a planner and an executor, allowing for better context management by stripping unnecessary data like raw HTML. Research on web navigation tasks shows that while a poor planner can degrade performance, a well-trained planner with dynamic replanning significantly outperforms standard ReAct. This approach requires more API calls but prevents the accumulation of errors in the agent's reasoning trace.
takeaways: ReAct agents keep all previous thoughts, actions, and observations in the prompt, leading to context bloat and attention competition.
Plan-and-Act divides tasks between a high-level planner and a grounded executor to manage context more efficiently.
On the WebArena-Lite benchmark, a ReAct-style executor scored 36.97%, whereas a properly trained planner with replanning reached 53.94%.
A poorly trained planner can reduce performance significantly, scoring only 20.60% in the same tests.
Replanning after every action is essential for recovering from failed steps that a static plan cannot handle.
The Plan-and-Act pattern increases operational costs by requiring one planner call for every executor step.

sections.title: A 10-week roadmap to run LLMs in production
sections.summary: This section outlines a comprehensive 10-week curriculum designed to help AI engineers master the production deployment and optimization of Large Language Models (LLMs). The roadmap covers fundamental concepts like the roofline model and paged attention, alongside practical experience with serving frameworks like vLLM and SGLang. The curriculum emphasizes observability, performance benchmarking, and advanced techniques such as continuous batching and quantization to build robust inference services.
takeaways: AI engineers should use the roofline model to understand why LLM decoding is typically memory-bound.
Mastering production serving requires deep dives into the schedulers and paged attention mechanisms of vLLM and SGLang.
Observability stacks using Grafana and Prometheus are essential for tracking metrics like TTFT, inter-token latency, and queue depth.
Optimization strategies include continuous batching, chunked prefill, speculative decoding, and quantization methods like AWQ and GPTQ.
The roadmap involves building an inference service that is load-tested with over 1000 concurrent requests and publicly benchmarked.
The curriculum is available as an open-source project on GitHub under the repository patchy631/time-to-first-token.

sections.title: Phases of ML Modeling
sections.summary: Machine learning systems should evolve through a structured four-phase process rather than starting with complex deep learning architectures. The process begins with non-ML heuristics to establish a baseline, followed by simple interpretable models to validate the end-to-end pipeline. Subsequent phases focus on refining these simple models through feature engineering and hyperparameter tuning before finally moving to complex architectures like transformers only when evidence justifies the added cost. This incremental approach reduces risk, improves debuggability, and aligns with MLOps best practices.
takeaways: Unnecessary complexity in ML systems often leads to low utility and should be avoided until justified.
Phase 1 involves creating a non-ML baseline, such as a heuristic or rule, to set a minimum performance bar.
Phase 2 uses simple models like logistic regression or decision trees to validate data ingestion and serving pipelines.
Phase 3 focuses on maximizing the performance of existing simple models through feature engineering and hyperparameter tuning.
Phase 4 introduces complex models like deep neural networks only after simpler approaches are exhausted.
At every phase of development, the best model from the previous phase serves as the new baseline.
A well-tuned simple model or ensemble can often meet production requirements without the need for deep learning.

items.title: [Hands-on] Build Semantic Search Inside Your Database Without an Embedding Pipeline

sections.title: Build a semantic search inside your database without an embedding pipeline
sections.summary: MongoDB Atlas has introduced an auto-embedding feature powered by Voyage AI, allowing users to implement semantic search without building external embedding pipelines. This integration simplifies the AI stack by removing the need for separate embedding services and synchronization layers. The system automatically re-embeds documents when they are updated, ensuring that vector search results remain consistent and current. Users can configure this directly within the Atlas UI by setting up a vector search index with automated embedding enabled.
takeaways: MongoDB Atlas now supports auto-embedding directly within its vector search index configuration.
Voyage AI provides the models used for generating embeddings within the MongoDB Atlas platform.
Auto-embedding eliminates the need for manual synchronization between databases and external embedding services.
The system automatically updates vector embeddings whenever the source document changes to prevent search quality degradation.
Setting up semantic search involves selecting 'Automated Embedding' during the vector search index creation process in Atlas.
MongoDB University offers AI Skill Badges and Credly credentials for mastering vector search, RAG, and agentic memory.

sections.title: 8 LLM precision formats
sections.summary: LLM precision formats allow large models to run on hardware with limited memory by trading numeric detail for reduced storage requirements. Formats range from high-precision FP32 used in training to highly compressed 4-bit formats like NF4 and INT4 used for inference and fine-tuning. Each format balances exponent and mantissa bits differently to manage the trade-offs between overflow risks and rounding errors.
takeaways: FP32 is the standard high-precision format but requires 4 bytes per parameter, making it too large for consumer GPUs.
TF32 is an internal tensor core format on Ampere hardware that speeds up calculations without reducing memory usage.
BF16 has become the pre-training default because its exponent range matches FP32, preventing overflow during downcasting.
FP16 provides more precision than BF16 but has a limited range, requiring loss scaling to prevent gradients from becoming infinity.
INT4 and NF4 formats enable running large models on consumer hardware by using only 4 bits per weight, often with minimal quality loss.
GPTQ and AWQ are specific methods used to minimize the error introduced during 4-bit quantization using calibration data.
NF4 is a specialized 4-bit format designed for QLoRA that assumes weights follow a normal distribution.

sections.title: 6 memory optimization techniques for Agentic systems
sections.summary: The text outlines memory optimization techniques for agentic systems, emphasizing that memory is a system design challenge rather than a property of the underlying model. It introduces five specific types of memory—Short-Term, Long-Term, Entity, Contextual, and User—which allow agents to maintain state and context across interactions. The content is part of an AI Agents crash course that demonstrates practical implementations using LangGraph and CrewAI.
takeaways: Memory is a system design problem that requires explicit management of context, including retrieval and storage.
Agentic systems without memory are stateless and cannot recall information from previous iterations.
Five distinct types of memory are identified: Short-Term, Long-Term, Entity, Contextual, and User Memory.
LangGraph is used to implement production-grade memory optimization techniques in agentic workflows.
CrewAI is featured as a tool for implementing, customizing, and resetting agent memory settings.
Memory enables agents to be context-aware and practically applicable in production environments.

sections.title: 8 種 LLM precision formats
sections.summary: LLM precision formats 透過犧牲數值細節來降低記憶體需求，讓大型模型能夠在有限記憶體的硬體上運作。格式涵蓋從訓練時使用的高精度 FP32，到 inference 與 fine-tuning 使用的高度壓縮 4-bit 格式（如 NF4 和 INT4）。每種格式對 exponent 與 mantissa bits 的配置各有不同，以權衡 overflow 風險與 rounding errors。
takeaways: FP32 是標準的高精度格式，但每個 parameter 需要 4 bytes，這使得它對於消費級 GPUs 來說體積過大。
TF32 是 Ampere 硬體上的內部 tensor core 格式，可在不減少記憶體用量的情況下加速運算。
BF16 已成為 pre-training 的預設格式，因為其 exponent 範圍與 FP32 相符，能防止在 downcasting 過程中發生 overflow。
FP16 提供比 BF16 更高的精度，但數值範圍有限，需要使用 loss scaling 來避免 gradients 變成無窮大 (infinity)。
INT4 和 NF4 格式透過每個 weight 僅使用 4 bits，讓大型模型能夠在消費級硬體上運作，且通常品質損失極小。
GPTQ 與 AWQ 是使用 calibration data 來最小化 4-bit quantization 過程中引入誤差的特定方法。
NF4 是專為 QLoRA 設計的特化 4-bit 格式，其假設 weights 符合 normal distribution。

items.title: The Read Path versus the Write Path: Strategies and Techniques

sections.title: The Read Path versus the Write Path: Strategies and Techniques
sections.summary: Applications process two distinct types of operations: writes that record facts and reads that answer queries. As load grows, common optimizations like indexing, caching, and read replicas are progressively introduced to maintain read performance. However, these techniques duplicate and precompute data away from the primary source, leading to synchronization lags and staleness issues. Balancing read performance with write correctness inherently requires managing opposing data structures and distinct consistency models.
takeaways: Write operations record state facts, whereas read operations answer queries against stored data.
Scaling read operations under traffic involves layered fixes such as indexing, query caching, and read replicas.
Every read optimization fundamentally relies on data precomputation and duplication away from the source.
Asynchronous synchronization between authoritative sources and secondary read copies can introduce transient data staleness bugs.
Fast reads and correct writes require opposing data structures, necessitating tradeoffs in consistency and synchronization.

快速的 reads 與正確的 writes 需要相互對立的 data structures，這必然需要在 consistency 與 synchronization 之間做出權衡。

items.title: The Missing Piece of Agent Self-Improvement

sections.title: Postgres for time-series workloads at any scale
sections.summary: Tiger Cloud features Hypercore, a hybrid storage engine integrated into TimescaleDB that optimizes time-series workloads by combining row and columnar storage. Data is initially ingested into row storage for speed and automatically transitioned to compressed columnar storage as it ages. This unified approach eliminates the need for separate read/write systems and complex maintenance pipelines. The system further accelerates analytical queries by accessing batch metadata directly for common summary functions.
takeaways: Tiger Cloud utilizes the Hypercore hybrid storage engine to unify write and read workloads.
Data is initially stored in row format for performance and later converted to columnar format for efficiency.
Hypercore can compress aging data by up to 95% using its columnar storage engine.
Summary queries like COUNT and MAX are optimized to read directly from batch metadata.
The platform removes the need for maintaining complex pipelines between separate read and write systems.
New users are eligible for $1,000 in free credits on Tiger Cloud.

sections.title: The missing piece of agent self-improvement
sections.summary: AI agents often lack a continuous self-improvement loop, especially regarding production failures. The Hermes agent addresses this by saving successful strategies as reusable skills and using GEPA for offline prompt optimization. Opik complements this by providing observability and a diagnostic agent named Ollie that turns production traces into actionable code fixes and regression tests. Together, these tools create a closed loop where agents learn from both successes and failures without requiring manual retraining.
takeaways: Hermes captures successful strategies in SKILL.md files to enable runtime learning and reuse.
GEPA (Genetic-Pareto Prompt Evolution) performs offline evolutionary searches to improve prompts and tool descriptions without model retraining.
Opik is an open-source observability platform that records agent execution traces across over fifty agent frameworks.
The Ollie coding agent analyzes Opik traces to identify failure points and propose Git-style diff fixes for developer approval.
Opik's Agent Sandbox allows developers to verify fixes by rerunning agents against the exact scenarios that caused failures.
Production failures can be converted into regression tests using LLM-as-a-judge evaluations within the Opik workflow.

items.title: [Hands-on] How to Serve 5 Models On One GPU

sections.title: How to serve 5 models on one GPU
sections.summary: The shift from single large AI models to pipelines of specialized small models creates a hardware utilization challenge where dedicated GPUs often sit idle. Traditional serving tools like vLLM and TEI typically claim entire GPUs, preventing efficient resource sharing for sequential tasks. The Superlinked Inference Engine (SIE) addresses this by providing an open-source framework that allows multiple models to share a single GPU pool through dynamic memory management and a unified API. SIE optimizes performance by using a shared request queue and batching requests based on estimated compute costs rather than fixed counts.
takeaways: Production AI systems are evolving into agentic pipelines using multiple specialized models for parsing, extraction, reranking, and generation.
Assigning a dedicated GPU to each stage of a sequential pipeline results in high costs and low hardware utilization due to idle time.
Standard serving tools often lack the coordination to share GPU memory effectively, leading to manual configuration errors or system crashes.
The Superlinked Inference Engine (SIE) supports over 100 models through a unified API with three core primitives: extract, score, and generate.
SIE manages GPU memory dynamically by loading models on demand and using Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction when memory is constrained.
To minimize compute waste, SIE batches requests with similar estimated compute costs to avoid excessive padding of shorter inputs.
SIE includes a model catalog that pre-packages configurations for various architectures, simplifying the deployment of diverse model families.

items.title: How Big Models Teach Small Models to Be Smart

sections.title: Distillation
sections.summary: Distillation trains a new, separate student model to replicate the outputs and behavior of a larger teacher model. Unlike compression techniques such as quantization and pruning, which reduce the size of an existing model, distillation produces an entirely independent model with distinct parameters. The resulting smaller model provides practical benefits, including lower inference costs, decreased latency, and the ability to run on-device. This approach is exemplified by Google's Gemma models, which are distilled from the larger Gemini model family.
takeaways: Distillation trains a distinct student model to replicate a teacher model's behavior rather than modifying the original model directly.
Compression methods like quantization and pruning shrink an existing model by lowering precision or removing parts, whereas distillation trains a fresh model.
Distilled models offer lower latency, reduced cost per request, and the capability to operate on local hardware such as phones.
Google's Gemma models are created using distillation from the Gemini family of models.
Distillation and quantization can be chained sequentially to optimize a model for specific target devices.

sections.title: Soft Labels
sections.summary: Learning from a model's output provides richer information than standard hard labels because output distributions, termed soft labels, assign probabilities across all candidate options. These distributions capture relationships between classes, a concept often referred to as dark knowledge. During distillation, a student model learns to match the teacher's full confidence profile rather than just targeting single correct answers, which allows it to reach high performance using fewer training examples. A temperature control is employed to spread out probability values and further expose this fine structure for the student model.
takeaways: Soft labels provide a complete probability distribution over categories rather than a single discrete label.
Dark knowledge refers to the structural relationships and relative plausibility among classes captured within teacher model probabilities.
Student models in distillation are trained by minimizing the divergence between their output distribution and the teacher's soft labels.
Training on soft targets enables student models to achieve strong performance from significantly fewer examples.
Increasing the temperature parameter spreads out probability distributions, exposing finer category structures to the student model.

sections.title: Methods
sections.summary: Knowledge distillation generally takes three forms depending on what the student model replicates: output distillation, feature distillation, and synthetic data distillation. Output distillation matches the teacher's final output probabilities, while feature distillation aligns intermediate internal representations, as used by Google to train EmbeddingGemma from Gemini. Synthetic data distillation fine-tunes a student on teacher-generated data, an approach popularized by Stanford's Alpaca. Because modern closed-source models often restrict access to internal values and probabilities, synthetic data distillation has become the most widely adopted variant in practice.
takeaways: Distillation is split into three main variants: output distillation, feature distillation, and synthetic data distillation.
Output distillation dates to 2015 and requires access to the teacher's soft labels and probability distributions.
Feature distillation matches internal model representations; Google applied this method to train EmbeddingGemma using Gemini representations.
Synthetic data distillation fine-tunes a model on generated datasets, as demonstrated early on by Stanford's Alpaca.
Access constraints on closed models make synthetic data distillation the most common method in practice, as it requires only textual output.
Distillation strategies can be combined in a single training run, such as pairing synthetic data with soft labels.

sections.title: Results
sections.summary: In early 2025, DeepSeek demonstrated that fine-tuning smaller models on outputs from a large reasoning model yielded remarkable performance on specific benchmarks. Notably, a 7-billion-parameter distilled student outperformed a 32-billion-parameter model in competition mathematics while remaining small enough to run locally on a single GPU. However, an important qualifier is that these gains are largely confined to narrow, well-defined domains such as math and code. Across broader measures of general knowledge, smaller distilled models consistently trail their larger counterparts.
takeaways: DeepSeek fine-tuned smaller existing models on training examples generated by a large reasoning model in early 2025.
A 7-billion-parameter distilled model outperformed a 32-billion-parameter model on a competition mathematics benchmark.
The released distilled model family ranged from 1.5 billion to 70 billion parameters, enabling local execution on a single graphics card for smaller variants.
Distillation enables strong task-specific performance on narrow tasks like math and code cheaply and locally.
Smaller distilled models still lag behind larger models on broader measures of general knowledge.

sections.title: Limits
sections.summary: Knowledge distillation has notable constraints that influence its suitability for specific machine learning problems. Student models are bounded by a ceiling effect where their performance rarely exceeds the teacher, inheriting errors alongside accurate outputs. Furthermore, an excessively wide capacity gap between teacher and student can degrade transfer quality, sometimes necessitating intermediate models. Model architecture often outweighs raw parameter count in determining student success, and subtle behavioral traits can inadvertently transfer from teacher to student even through filtered, task-unrelated data.
takeaways: A student model's quality is typically capped at or below the teacher's level on seen data distributions, directly inheriting teacher errors.
A very wide capacity gap between a large teacher and a small student can degrade transfer performance.
Multi-step distillation using an intermediate-sized model can mitigate transfer degradation caused by wide capacity gaps.
Base model architecture can be more influential than parameter count, as demonstrated by a 32B student outperforming a 70B student.

Distillation can unintentionally transfer latent behavioral preferences and traits between models sharing the same base architecture, even when training data consists only of filtered number sequences.

sections.title: Automation
sections.summary: Recent advances in knowledge distillation focus on fully automating the process using a self-running loop driven by a large teacher model. In this setup, the teacher autonomously generates training data, fine-tunes the student, and evaluates performance iteratively until progress plateaus, reducing human involvement primarily to setup and final verification. Recent research in 2026 demonstrated that while this method cuts manual pipeline and dataset creation efforts, the initial selection of the teacher model plays a decisive role in the final student model's quality.
takeaways: Automated distillation loops allow a large teacher model to generate data, fine-tune the student, and evaluate progress autonomously.
Human responsibilities are restricted to defining the task and success criteria at the start and conducting a final evaluation on real data.
2026 research on a detection task showed that the choice of teacher model has a major impact on student model performance under identical loop settings.
The automated process removes the requirement to manually assemble large hand-labeled datasets prior to training small, task-specific models.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: Distillation is a training technique where a smaller student model learns to replicate the behavior of a larger teacher model rather than directly compressing it. It leverages soft labels that provide richer confidence distributions across outputs, often utilizing teacher-generated datasets. The effectiveness of distillation is subject to clear constraints, including the teacher's performance ceiling, negative effects from large size discrepancies, and the unintended transfer of behavioral traits. Consequently, the approach is best suited for well-defined, narrow tasks rather than broad, general-purpose capabilities.
takeaways: Distillation creates a separate, smaller model rather than compressing the original architecture directly.
Soft labels facilitate distillation by providing information about the teacher's confidence distribution across classes.
In practice, distillation is most commonly executed by having the teacher model generate training sets for the student.
A wider size disparity between teacher and student models can degrade performance rather than improve it.
Distillation can inadvertently transfer unintended behavioral traits from teacher to student models.
Distillation is better suited for narrow, well-defined tasks than for general, open-ended capabilities.

items.summary: Distillation trains a new, separate student model to replicate the outputs and behavior of a larger teacher model. Unlike compression techniques such as quantization and pruning, which reduce the size of an existing model, distillation produces an entirely independent model with distinct parameters. The resulting smaller model provides practical benefits, including lower inference costs, decreased latency, and the ability to run on-device. This approach is exemplified by Google's Gemma models, which are distilled from the larger Gemini model family. Learning from a model's output provides richer information than standard hard labels because output distributions, termed soft labels, assign probabilities across all candidate options. These distributions capture relationships between classes, a concept often referred to as dark knowledge. During distillation, a student model learns to match the teacher's full confidence profile rather than just targeting single correct answers, which allows it to reach high performance using fewer training examples. A temperature control is employed to spread out probability values and further expose this fine structure for the student model. Knowledge distillation generally takes three forms depending on what the student model replicates: output distillation, feature distillation, and synthetic data distillation. Output distillation matches the teacher's final output probabilities, while feature distillation aligns intermediate internal representations, as used by Google to train EmbeddingGemma from Gemini. Synthetic data distillation fine-tunes a student on teacher-generated data, an approach popularized by Stanford's Alpaca. Because modern closed-source models often restrict access to internal values and probabilities, synthetic data distillation has become the most widely adopted variant in practice.

sections.title: Distillation
sections.summary: Distillation 透過訓練一個全新且獨立的 student model，來重現較大 teacher model 的輸出與行為。不同於 quantization 和 pruning 等縮減現有模型大小的 compression 技術，distillation 會產出一個參數完全獨立的模型。這種產出的較小模型帶來了實質的效益，包括更低的 inference 成本、降低的 latency，以及在 on-device 上運行的能力。Google 的 Gemma 模型便是這種方法的代表範例，它們是從較大的 Gemini 模型家族 distillation 出來的。
takeaways: Distillation 透過訓練一個獨立的 student model 來重現 teacher model 的行為，而非直接修改原始模型。
像 quantization 和 pruning 這類的 compression 方法是透過降低 precision 或移除部分結構來縮減現有模型，而 distillation 則是訓練一個全新的模型。
Distilled 模型具有更低的 latency、降低的每次 request 成本，並具備在手機等本地硬體上運行的能力。
Google 的 Gemma 模型是透過從 Gemini 系列模型進行 distillation 所建立的。
Distillation 與 quantization 可以依序串接，以針對特定的 target devices 優化模型。

sections.title: Soft Labels
sections.summary: 從模型的輸出中學習比標準的 hard labels 能提供更豐富的資訊，因為被稱為 soft labels 的輸出分佈會為所有候選選項分配機率。這些分佈捕捉了類別之間的關聯性，這個概念通常被稱為 dark knowledge。在 distillation 過程中，student model 學習去匹配 teacher 的完整 confidence profile，而不只是針對單一正確答案，這使得它能使用較少的 training examples 達到高效能。系統採用 temperature 控制來平緩機率分佈，進一步為 student model 展現這種細緻的結構。
takeaways: Soft labels 為各類別提供完整的機率分佈，而非單一的離散 label。
Dark knowledge 是指 teacher model 機率中所捕捉到的類別間結構關聯與相對合理性。
Distillation 中的 student model 是透過最小化其輸出分佈與 teacher 的 soft labels 之間的 divergence 來進行訓練。
針對 soft targets 進行訓練，能讓 student model 以大幅減少的 examples 達成強大的效能。
提高 temperature parameter 會平緩機率分佈，向 student model 展現更細緻的類別結構。

sections.title: 方法
sections.summary: Knowledge distillation 根據 student model 複製的內容通常分為三種形式：output distillation、feature distillation 以及 synthetic data distillation。Output distillation 會匹配 teacher 的最終輸出機率；feature distillation 則對齊中間的內部 representations，如 Google 利用 Gemini 訓練 EmbeddingGemma 時所使用的方法。Synthetic data distillation 則是使用 teacher 生成的資料來 fine-tune student，這種方法由 Stanford 的 Alpaca 推廣普及。由於現代閉源模型通常限制存取內部數值與機率，synthetic data distillation 已成為實務上被最廣泛採用的變體。
takeaways: Distillation 主要分為三種變體：output distillation、feature distillation 以及 synthetic data distillation。
Output distillation 可追溯至 2015 年，需要存取 teacher 的 soft labels 與機率分佈。
Feature distillation 會匹配內部的模型 representations；Google 應用此方法，使用 Gemini 的 representations 來訓練 EmbeddingGemma。
Synthetic data distillation 會在生成的 datasets 上 fine-tune 模型，正如 Stanford 的 Alpaca 早期所展示的一樣。
由於 closed models 的存取限制，synthetic data distillation 成為實務上最常見的方法，因為它只需要文字輸出。
Distillation 策略可以在單次 training run 中結合使用，例如將 synthetic data 與 soft labels 搭配。

sections.title: 結果
sections.summary: 在 2025 年初，DeepSeek 展示了在大型 reasoning model 的輸出上 fine-tune 較小模型，能在特定 benchmarks 上取得顯著的 performance。值得注意的是，一個 7-billion-parameter 的 distilled student 在競賽數學上超越了 32-billion-parameter 的模型，同時體積依然夠小，足以在單張 GPU 上本地運行。然而，一個重要的前提是，這些提升大多局限於狹窄且定義明確的領域，例如數學與 code。在更廣泛的 general knowledge 評估中，較小的 distilled models 表現始終落後於較大的對應模型。
takeaways: DeepSeek 在 2025 年初利用大型 reasoning model 生成的 training examples，fine-tune 現有的較小模型。
一個 7-billion-parameter 的 distilled model 在競賽數學 benchmark 上的表現超越了 32-billion-parameter 的模型。
釋出的 distilled model family 參數規模涵蓋 1.5 billion 到 70 billion parameters，讓較小的 variants 能夠在單張顯卡上本地執行。
Distillation 能以低成本且本地化的方式，在數學和 code 等 narrow tasks 上實現強大的 task-specific performance。
在更廣泛的 general knowledge 衡量指標上，較小的 distilled models 仍落後於較大的模型。

sections.title: 限制
sections.summary: Knowledge distillation 存在顯著的限制，會影響其在特定 machine learning 問題上的適用性。Student models 會受到 ceiling effect 的限制，其 performance 很少能超越 teacher，並會在繼承正確輸出的同時也繼承錯誤。此外，teacher 和 student 之間過大的 capacity gap 可能會降低 transfer quality，有時需要透過 intermediate models 來過渡。在決定 student 的成效時，base model architecture 的影響往往超過單純的 parameter count，且即使透過過濾後、與任務無關的 data，teacher 的細微 behavioral traits 仍可能會無意間 transfer 給 student。
takeaways: 在看過的 data distributions 上，student model 的品質通常被限制在 teacher 的水準或其之下，並會直接繼承 teacher 的錯誤。
大型 teacher 與小型 student 之間過大的 capacity gap，可能會降低 transfer performance。
使用中等大小模型的 multi-step distillation 可以緩解因過大 capacity gaps 所導致的 transfer degradation。
Base model architecture 的影響力可能大於 parameter count，正如 32B 的 student 表現優於 70B 的 student 所證明的。
即使 training data 僅由過濾後的數字序列組成，distillation 仍可能在共享相同 base architecture 的模型之間，非預期地 transfer 潛在的 behavioral preferences 與 traits。

sections.title: 自動化
sections.summary: Knowledge distillation 的最新進展著重於透過由大型 teacher model 驅動的 self-running loop 來完全自動化該流程。在這種架構下，teacher 會自主生成 training data、fine-tune student，並反覆評估 performance 直到進展進入平原期，將人為介入大幅減少至僅剩初始設定與最終驗證。2026 年的最新研究顯示，雖然此方法減少了手動建立 pipeline 和 dataset 的工作量，但 teacher model 的初始選擇對最終 student model 的品質具有決定性影響。
takeaways: Automated distillation loops 讓大型 teacher model 能夠自主生成 data、fine-tune student 並評估進度。
人類的職責被限制在最初定義任務與成功標準，以及在 real data 上進行最終評估。
2026 年一項針對 detection task 的研究顯示，在相同的 loop settings 下，teacher model 的選擇對 student model 的 performance 有重大影響。
這套自動化流程免除了在訓練小型 task-specific models 之前手動收集大型 hand-labeled datasets 的需求。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: Distillation 是一種 training technique，讓較小的 student model 學習複製較大 teacher model 的行為，而非直接對其進行壓縮。它利用能為輸出提供更豐富 confidence distributions 的 soft labels，並通常使用 teacher 生成的 datasets。Distillation 的成效受限於明確的 constraints，包括 teacher 的 performance ceiling、龐大模型尺寸差異帶來的負面效應，以及非預期的 behavioral traits 轉移。因此，這種方法最適合定義明確的 narrow tasks，而非廣泛的 general-purpose capabilities。
takeaways: Distillation 會產生一個獨立且較小的模型，而不是直接壓縮原本的架構。
Soft labels 透過提供教師模型在各類別間的信心度分佈資訊，來促進 distillation。
在實務上，distillation 最常見的執行方式是讓教師模型為學生模型生成 training sets。
教師模型與學生模型之間的體積差距過大，可能會導致效能下降而非提升。
Distillation 可能會在無意間將非預期的行為特徵從教師模型轉移到學生模型上。
Distillation 更適合用於狹窄且定義明確的任務，而非通用且開放性的能力。

items.title: Why Your Agent Remembers Everything and Understands Nothing

sections.title: Code verification that runs inside the agent’s session
sections.summary: GitGuardian research indicates that AI-assisted commits via Claude Code leak credentials at a rate of 3.2%, significantly higher than the 1.5% human baseline. To mitigate this, Sonar has introduced a SonarQube CLI integration that embeds security verification directly into the Claude Code agent session. By using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, the tool provides real-time secrets detection and static analysis feedback. This allows the agent to identify and fix vulnerabilities within its active context before code is committed.
takeaways: Claude Code-assisted commits leak credentials at more than double the rate of human developers (3.2% vs 1.5%).
SonarQube CLI integrates secrets detection and static analysis directly into the Claude Code environment.
The integration utilizes an MCP server to pipe security findings back into the agent's context.
Verification occurs during the session on every file read or write, rather than later in the CI pipeline.
Sonar Vortex provides advanced features like context augmentation and deeper code analysis on paid plans.
The SonarQube free tier includes basic secrets detection and the MCP server functionality.

sections.title: Your Agent remembers everything and understands nothing
sections.summary: Current AI agent memory systems excel at storing and retrieving individual facts but often fail to recognize patterns across multiple interactions. Zep addresses this gap with a feature called Observations, which uses a knowledge graph to detect cross-conversation dependencies and structural insights. By employing a deterministic clustering algorithm followed by LLM-generated summaries, the system identifies root causes that individual facts might obscure, moving agents beyond simple recall toward a deeper understanding of complex data.
takeaways: Standard agent memory systems lack pattern recognition, treating related issues as isolated incidents.
Zep's Observations feature identifies cross-entity and cross-conversation patterns within a knowledge graph.
The system uses signatures (entity pairs and relationship types) to cluster related conversations deterministically.
Unlike embedding-based clustering, signature-based clustering groups data based on specific shared relationships rather than general topic similarity.
Observations are evidence-backed and read-only, automatically updating or retiring as new data is ingested.
The process involves a two-stage pipeline: a graph-topology algorithm for clustering and an LLM for summarizing the resulting structure.

sections.title: Automatic LLM routing in two lines of code!
sections.summary: Plano is an open-source tool designed to automate LLM routing by analyzing prompt intent instead of using hardcoded model calls. By redirecting the client's base URL to Plano's local endpoint, developers can dynamically assign tasks to specific models like claude-sonnet-4.5 or gpt-4o-mini. This system reduces operational costs and improves efficiency without requiring changes to the underlying agent code. Additionally, Plano provides observability tools to monitor routing decisions and request costs in real-time.
takeaways: Plano enables dynamic LLM routing based on the intent of the prompt.
Implementation requires only a configuration change to the client's base URL, leaving agent code untouched.
Routing tasks to appropriate models can reduce costs by up to 2x.
The planoai obs command provides real-time observability into routing decisions, model selection, and cost per request.
Plano is fully open-source and supports self-hosting natively or via Docker.

該流程包含一個兩階段的 pipeline：用於分群的 graph-topology 演算法，以及用於摘要所得結構的 LLM。

sections.title: 兩行程式碼實現自動化 LLM routing！
sections.summary: Plano 是一套開源工具，旨在透過分析 prompt intent 來實現自動化 LLM routing，而非使用寫死的 model calls。透過將 client 的 base URL 重新導向至 Plano 的 local endpoint，開發者可以動態將任務指派給特定模型，例如 claude-sonnet-4.5 或 gpt-4o-mini。該系統能降低營運成本並提高效率，且無需修改底層的 agent 程式碼。此外，Plano 還提供了 observability 工具，可即時監控 routing 決策與每次請求的成本。
takeaways: Plano 能夠根據 prompt 的 intent 實現動態 LLM routing。
實作僅需修改 client 的 base URL 設定，完全不需更動 agent 程式碼。
將任務 route 至合適的模型最多可降低 2 倍的成本。
planoai obs 指令提供了對 routing 決策、模型選擇及單次請求成本的即時 observability。
Plano 完全開源，並支援原生或透過 Docker 進行 self-hosting。

items.title: Why An LLM’s Memory Gets Expensive and How to Fix It

sections.title: Recomputation
sections.summary: To generate each token, a model executes an attention step comparing the newest token against earlier tokens using key and value vectors. Recomputing these vectors for every preceding token at each step is computationally wasteful because their values remain static. The KV cache resolves this inefficiency by storing computed key and value vectors so that only the new token requires computation. However, reading this cache on every step introduces a new cost bottleneck and can cause unexpected out-of-memory errors because the cache retains high-dimensional vectors rather than text.
takeaways: Generating a token requires an attention step where the newest token is compared against prior tokens using key and value vectors.
Recomputing prior keys and values at each step causes work per token to increase unnecessarily as context grows.
The KV cache eliminates redundant computation by storing key and value vectors after their initial calculation.
Reading the KV cache on every step constitutes an increasing operational cost.
Because the KV cache stores vector representations rather than raw text, it can cause out-of-memory errors even when the model weights fit comfortably in memory.

sections.title: Decoding
sections.summary: Token generation operates in two distinct phases with different hardware bottlenecks: prefill and decoding. During prefill, all input tokens are processed in parallel to construct the key-value cache, making this phase compute-bound and limited by arithmetic throughput. Decoding generates tokens autoregressively one by one, requiring a full read of the key-value cache from GPU memory for every step, which makes it memory-bound. As a result, the primary bottleneck in long-context generation stems from repeatedly streaming the entire cache across the memory bus rather than simply storing it.
takeaways: Token generation is split into two phases: prefill and decoding.
The prefill phase processes all input tokens in parallel and is compute-bound, limited by GPU arithmetic capacity.
The decoding phase produces one token at a time and is memory-bound, limited by memory bandwidth.
Each decoding step requires reading all stored key and value vectors out of GPU memory.
Long-context performance degradation is driven by the cost of sweeping through the cache on every generated token rather than memory capacity alone.

sections.title: Scaling
sections.summary: The key-value cache size of a large language model is determined by multiplying the number of layers, key-value heads, head dimension, bytes per number, context length, batch size, and a factor of two. Cache requirements scale linearly with both token count and batch size, making long contexts and concurrent users resource-intensive. For instance, a single 128,000-token request on Llama 3 70B demands approximately 40 gigabytes of memory, consuming half of an 80-gigabyte GPU card. Optimization techniques aim to mitigate memory demands by reducing individual factors in this multiplication.
takeaways: The KV cache size equals 2 times layers times key-value heads times head dimension times bytes per number times tokens times batch size.
Cache memory usage grows linearly with token count, meaning doubling context length doubles cache consumption.
Cache memory scales linearly with batch size, proportionally increasing with concurrent requests.
A single 128,000-token request on Llama 3 70B requires approximately 40 gigabytes of cache memory.
Llama 3 70B architecture parameters include 80 layers, 8 key-value heads, a head dimension of 128, and 2 bytes per number.

sections.title: Attention
sections.summary: Attention architecture modifications can substantially reduce the key-value cache memory footprint per token, though these designs must be committed to during training. Grouped-query attention saves memory by having multiple query heads share key-value heads, offering a stable middle ground compared to aggressive multi-query attention. Multi-head latent attention further compresses cache demands by projecting key and value representations into a smaller latent space before caching, as demonstrated by DeepSeek-V3. While these architectural techniques reduce memory traffic at large scale, they require trade-offs in serving overhead, quality, or implementation complexity.
takeaways: Grouped-query attention lets several query heads share one key-value head, reducing cache memory roughly eightfold in models like Llama 2 70B, Llama 3 70B, and Mistral 7B.
Multi-query attention achieves maximum memory savings by sharing a single key-value head across all query heads, but it often causes training instability and quality degradation.
Multi-head latent attention, introduced in DeepSeek models, compresses keys and values into a smaller latent representation before caching and decompresses them on read.
DeepSeek-V3 achieves a cache footprint of approximately 70 kilobytes per token via latent attention, compared to 192 to 328 kilobytes per token in comparable grouped-query attention models.
Head-sharing and latent attention techniques require architectural control during training rather than being applicable post-training.

sections.title: Quantization
sections.summary: Quantization reduces the memory footprint of the key-value cache by converting numbers from standard 16-bit precision down to 8-bit or 4-bit representations. This technique requires no model retraining, cutting cache size in half at 8 bits and in half again at 4 bits. While 8-bit quantization typically produces negligible accuracy drops under one percent, 4-bit storage shows measurable degradation on complex tasks like multi-needle retrieval. Although specialized algorithms outperform plain rounding by preserving precision for key values, simple rounding still captures the majority of compression gains.
takeaways: Quantization decreases memory usage by reducing key and value storage precision from 16 bits to 8 bits or 4 bits.
Transitioning from 16-bit to 8-bit precision halves the cache size, and moving to 4-bit halves it again.
Quantization can be applied directly to existing models without retraining.
Eight-bit storage typically loses well under one percent of accuracy for most standard workloads.
Four-bit storage introduces measurable performance degradation in demanding tasks such as multi-needle retrieval.
Specialized quantization methods outperform plain rounding by maintaining higher precision for outlier numbers in the cache.

sections.title: Eviction
sections.summary: Eviction reduces token counts in language models by discarding entries deemed unlikely to be needed. A typical implementation maintains both the most recent context window and a few opening tokens, which function as attention anchors to stabilize model generation. However, eviction faces a structural flaw because the model cannot predict whether a discarded token will be essential for subsequent queries. As a result, aggressive eviction techniques often fail on retrieval tasks where key information is buried mid-sequence.
takeaways: Eviction lowers memory usage by discarding tokens the model is predicted not to need.
A common eviction strategy retains recent tokens alongside a small set of opening sequence tokens.
Opening tokens absorb significant attention regardless of content, serving as stability anchors for generation.
The fundamental challenge of eviction is that token importance depends on future, unknown inputs.
Aggressive cache eviction disproportionately harms retrieval tasks by dropping details located in the middle of documents.
Importance-scoring schemes attempt to predict safe drops, but they do not eliminate the structural limitation.

sections.title: Serving
sections.summary: Serving systems historically suffered high memory fragmentation by reserving contiguous blocks sized for worst-case output lengths. Paged attention addresses this by splitting the cache into small fixed-size pages allocated on demand, reducing fragmentation from 60-80% to under 4% and boosting throughput by two to three times. Furthermore, storing cache in shareable blocks enables prefix caching, allowing requests with identical prefixes to point to the same physical memory. Providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic report 50 to 90 percent cost and latency reductions on cache hits, though cross-user cache sharing introduces timing side-channel security risks.
takeaways: Older serving architectures wasted 60 to 80 percent of cache memory on fragmentation by allocating contiguous blocks sized for maximum potential output length.
Paged attention adapts operating system memory paging to LLM caches, dropping fragmentation below 4 percent and doubling or tripling throughput.
Shareable cache blocks serve as the foundation for prefix caching (productized by major APIs as prompt caching).
Prefix caching yields 50 to 90 percent reductions in cost and latency for repetitive workloads like multi-thousand-token system prompts according to OpenAI and Anthropic.
Sharing cached memory blocks across users introduces potential timing side-channel vulnerabilities that can leak prompt data.

sections.title: Tradeoffs
sections.summary: Different memory-saving techniques for model caches offer varied tradeoffs between memory reduction, implementation complexity, and output quality. Methods like grouped-query attention, paged attention, and prefix caching provide memory benefits with virtually no quality loss. In contrast, techniques such as low-bit quantization, latent attention, and eviction introduce notable quality risks or require significant engineering effort. Ultimately, these optimizations become vital in long-context and high-concurrency settings where cache overhead dominates, requiring strategies to be matched to specific workload patterns.
takeaways: Grouped-query attention serves as a near-costless default that ships with almost every modern model.
Paged attention and prefix caching preserve output quality by altering how the cache is stored and shared rather than changing its content.
Quantization remains safe at 8 bits but increases the risk of quality degradation at 4 bits and below.
Latent attention yields substantial architectural savings but demands notable engineering effort to serve effectively.
Eviction frees large amounts of memory but risks discarding information required for subsequent token generation.
Cache reduction techniques are primarily necessary in long-context and high-concurrency workloads where cache memory becomes the dominant bottleneck.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: The cost of long-context inference is fundamentally determined by the size of the attention cache. Because decoding reads the entire cache for every generated token, the cache creates both storage and memory-bandwidth bottlenecks. Shrinking the cache improves generation speed, and optimization techniques target different aspects of cache size and management. Approaches include reducing per-token cost, quantizing values, evicting tokens, and improving memory layout and sharing.
takeaways: Long-context inference cost is dictated by cache size, which imposes both storage and memory bandwidth overheads.
During decoding, the full cache must be read on every token generation step.
Grouped query attention and latent attention decrease the memory cost associated with each token.
Quantization reduces memory requirements by encoding values in fewer bits.
Cache eviction reduces the total number of retained tokens.
Paged attention and prefix caching enhance cache management and enable sharing across requests.

zh.summary: 為了生成每個 token，模型會執行 attention 步驟，利用 key 和 value 向量將最新的 token 與先前的 token 進行比較。在每個步驟中為所有先前的 token 重新計算這些向量在計算上非常浪費，因為它們的數值是靜態不變的。KV cache 透過儲存計算過的 key 和 value 向量來解決這種低效問題，因此只需要計算新的 token。然而，在每個步驟讀取此快取會帶來新的成本瓶頸，並可能導致非預期的 out-of-memory 錯誤，因為快取保留的是高維度向量而非文字。Token 生成分為兩個具有不同硬體瓶頸的階段：prefill 和 decoding。在 prefill 期間，所有輸入 token 都會被平行處理以構建 key-value cache，這使得該階段受限於計算能力（compute-bound），並受限於算術吞吐量。Decoding 則是以 autoregressive 方式逐一生成 token，每一步都需要從 GPU 記憶體完整讀取一次 key-value cache，這使得它受限於記憶體頻寬（memory-bound）。因此，在 long-context 生成中的主要瓶頸在於反覆透過 memory bus 串流傳輸整個快取，而非單純儲存它。大型語言模型的 key-value cache 大小取決於以下項目的乘積：layer 數、key-value head 數、head dimension、每個數字的 bytes 數、context length、batch size，以及係數 2。快取需求隨 token 數量和 batch size 線性增長，這使得 long contexts 與並行使用者需要消耗龐大資源。舉例來說，在 Llama 3 70B 上處理單一 128,000 個 token 的請求大約需要 40 GB 的記憶體，吃掉一張 80 GB GPU 卡的一半容量。最佳化技術旨在透過減少該乘法公式中的個別因子來緩解記憶體需求。

sections.title: Recomputation
sections.summary: 為了生成每個 token，模型會執行一個 attention 步驟，利用 key 和 value 向量將最新的 token 與先前的 token 進行比較。在每個步驟為所有先前的 token 重新計算這些向量在計算上非常浪費，因為它們的值保持不變。KV cache 透過儲存已計算的 key 和 value 向量來解決這種低效問題，因此只有新的 token 需要計算。然而，在每個步驟讀取此快取會帶來新的成本瓶頸，並且可能導致非預期的 out-of-memory 錯誤，因為快取保留的是高維向量而非文字。
takeaways: 生成 token 需要一個 attention 步驟，其中使用 key 和 value 向量將最新的 token 與先前的 token 進行比較。
在每個步驟重新計算先前的 keys 和 values，會導致每個 token 的運算量隨著 context 增長而不必要地增加。
KV cache 透過在初次計算後儲存 key 和 value 向量，消除了多餘的計算。
在每個步驟讀取 KV cache 會構成不斷增加的運算成本。
由於 KV cache 儲存的是向量表示而非原始文字，即使模型權重可以輕鬆放進記憶體中，它仍可能導致 out-of-memory 錯誤。

sections.title: Decoding
sections.summary: Token 生成分為兩個具有不同硬體瓶頸的階段：prefill 與 decoding。在 prefill 期間，所有輸入的 token 都會被平行處理以構建 key-value cache，使得這個階段屬於 compute-bound，受限於算術吞吐量。Decoding 則是以 autoregressive 方式逐一生成 token，每一步都需要從 GPU 記憶體完整讀取 key-value cache，這使其成為 memory-bound。因此，長 context 生成的主要瓶頸，來自於在 memory bus 上反覆串流整個快取，而非單純儲存它。
takeaways: Token 生成分為兩個階段：prefill 與 decoding。
Prefill 階段會平行處理所有輸入的 token，屬於 compute-bound，受限於 GPU 的算術運算能力。
Decoding 階段一次生成一個 token，屬於 memory-bound，受限於記憶體頻寬。
每個 decoding 步驟都需要從 GPU 記憶體中讀取所有已儲存的 key 和 value 向量。
長 context 下的效能下降，主要是由每生成一個 token 就要掃描一次快取的成本所驅動，而非單純受限於記憶體容量。

sections.title: Scaling
sections.summary: 大型語言模型的 key-value cache 大小，是由 layers 數量、key-value heads 數量、head dimension、bytes per number、context 長度、batch size 以及 2 倍的係數相乘所決定。快取需求與 token 數量及 batch size 呈線性擴展，使得長 context 與高並行使用者變得非常消耗資源。例如，在 Llama 3 70B 上處理一個包含 128,000 個 token 的請求，大約需要 40 gigabytes 的記憶體，耗費了一張 80-gigabyte GPU 卡的一半容量。最佳化技術旨在透過減少這項乘法運算中的各個因子，來減輕記憶體需求。
takeaways: KV cache 大小等於 2 乘以 layers 乘以 key-value heads 乘以 head dimension 乘以 bytes per number 乘以 tokens 乘以 batch size。
快取記憶體用量隨 token 數量線性增長，這表示 context 長度翻倍時，快取消耗也會翻倍。
快取記憶體隨 batch size 線性擴展，與並行請求成比例增加。
在 Llama 3 70B 上，單一 128,000 個 token 的請求大約需要 40 gigabytes 的快取記憶體。
Llama 3 70B 架構參數包含 80 個 layers、8 個 key-value heads、128 的 head dimension，以及每個數字 2 個 bytes。

sections.title: Attention
sections.summary: Attention 架構修改可以大幅降低每個 token 的 key-value cache 記憶體佔用量（memory footprint），不過這些設計必須在 training 階段就確定下來。Grouped-query attention 透過讓多個 query heads 共用 key-value heads 來節省記憶體，相較於激進的 multi-query attention 提供了一個穩定的折衷方案。Multi-head latent attention 則進一步壓縮 cache 需求，在進行 caching 前先將 key 與 value 的表示投影到較小的 latent space 中，正如 DeepSeek-V3 所展示的。雖然這些架構技術能在大規模運行時減少記憶體頻寬負擔（memory traffic），但它們在 serving overhead、品質或實作複雜度上需要做出權衡（trade-offs）。
takeaways: Grouped-query attention 讓數個 query heads 共用一個 key-value head，在 Llama 2 70B、Llama 3 70B 和 Mistral 7B 等模型中將 cache 記憶體減少了大約八倍。
Multi-query attention 透過在所有 query heads 之間共用單一 key-value head 來達到最大程度的記憶體節省，但它通常會導致 training 不穩定和品質下降。
Multi-head latent attention 首次引入於 DeepSeek 模型中，它在 caching 之前將 keys 和 values 壓縮為較小的 latent representation，並在讀取時進行解壓縮。
DeepSeek-V3 透過 latent attention 實現了每個 token 約 70 KB 的 cache footprint，相比之下，同等規模的 grouped-query attention 模型每個 token 約為 192 到 328 KB。
Head-sharing 和 latent attention 技術需要在 training 期間進行架構控制，而無法直接在 post-training 階段套用。

sections.title: Quantization
sections.summary: Quantization 透過將數值從標準的 16-bit 精度轉換為 8-bit 或 4-bit representations，來降低 key-value cache 的 memory footprint。這項技術不需要重新 training 模型，在 8-bit 下可將 cache 大小減半，4-bit 下又再減半。雖然 8-bit quantization 通常只會產生低於百分之一、幾乎可忽略的 accuracy 降幅，但 4-bit storage 在 multi-needle retrieval 等複雜任務上會出現可測量到的效能退化。儘管專門的演算法透過為 key values 保留精度而優於單純的 rounding，但簡單的 rounding 仍能獲得大部分的壓縮效益。
takeaways: Quantization 透過將 key 和 value 的儲存精度從 16 bits 降低到 8 bits 或 4 bits 來減少記憶體使用量。
從 16-bit 轉移到 8-bit 精度可將 cache 大小減半，而轉移到 4-bit 則會再減半。
Quantization 可以直接套用到現有模型上，無需重新 training。
對於大多數標準 workloads，8-bit storage 通常損失遠低於百分之一的 accuracy。
4-bit storage 在 multi-needle retrieval 等嚴苛任務中會引入可測量到的效能退化。
專門的 quantization 方法透過為 cache 中的 outlier 數值保持較高精度，表現優於單純的 rounding。

sections.title: Eviction
sections.summary: Eviction 透過捨棄被認為不太可能需要的 entries 來減少語言模型中的 token 數量。典型的實作方式會同時保留最新的 context window 和少數開頭 tokens，後者充當 attention anchors 以穩定模型的 generation。然而，eviction 面臨結構性缺陷，因為模型無法預測被捨棄的 token 是否對後續的 queries 至關重要。因此，激進的 eviction 技術在關鍵資訊深埋於序列中間的 retrieval 任務上往往會失敗。
takeaways: Eviction 透過捨棄預測模型不需要的 tokens 來降低記憶體使用量。
常見的 eviction 策略是保留近期的 tokens 以及一小組序列開頭 tokens。
無論內容為何，開頭 tokens 都會吸收大量的 attention，作為 generation 的穩定性 anchors。
Eviction 的根本挑戰在於 token 的重要性取決於未來的未知輸入。
激進的 cache eviction 會因為丟棄位於文件中間的細節，對 retrieval 任務造成不成比例的損害。
Importance-scoring 機制試圖預測哪些可以安全捨棄，但它們無法消除這項結構性限制。

sections.title: Serving
sections.summary: Serving 系統在歷史上一直受到高度記憶體碎裂化（memory fragmentation）的困擾，因為其預先配置了針對最差情況 output lengths 大小的連續區塊。Paged attention 透過將 cache 分割為按需分配的固定大小 pages 來解決此問題，將 fragmentation 從 60-80% 降低至 4% 以下，並使 throughput 提升二到三倍。此外，將 cache 存放在可共享的 blocks 中實現了 prefix caching，讓具有相同 prefixes 的 requests 可以指向相同的實體記憶體。像 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等 providers 回報在 cache hit 時可降低 50 到 90% 的成本與 latency，不過跨使用者的 cache sharing 會引入 timing side-channel 的安全風險。
takeaways: 較舊的 serving 架構透過為最大潛在 output length 分配連續區塊，將 60 到 80% 的 cache 記憶體浪費在 fragmentation 上。
Paged attention 將作業系統的 memory paging 機制應用於 LLM cache，將 fragmentation 降至 4% 以下，並使 throughput 提升二至三倍。
可共享的 cache block 是 prefix caching 的基礎（主要 API 將其產品化為 prompt caching）。
根據 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 的數據，對於數千個 token 的 system prompt 等重複性 workload，prefix caching 可降低 50% 到 90% 的成本與 latency。
跨使用者共享 cached memory block 會引入潛在的 timing side-channel 漏洞，可能會洩漏 prompt 資料。

sections.title: Tradeoffs
sections.summary: 針對 model cache 的各種節省 memory 技術，在 memory 縮減、實作複雜度與輸出品質之間提供了不同的 tradeoff。像 grouped-query attention、paged attention 與 prefix caching 等方法能在幾乎不損失品質的情況下帶來 memory 優勢。相反地，low-bit quantization、latent attention 和 eviction 等技術則會帶來顯著的品質風險，或需要耗費大量的 engineering effort。最終，在 cache overhead 佔主導地位的 long-context 與 high-concurrency 情境中，這些最佳化至關重要，需要根據具體的 workload pattern 來匹配對應策略。
takeaways: Grouped-query attention 作為近乎零成本的預設配置，幾乎內建於所有現代 model 中。
Paged attention 與 prefix caching 透過改變 cache 的儲存與共享方式而非修改其內容，來保持輸出品質。
Quantization 在 8-bit 時仍算安全，但在 4-bit 及以下時，品質下降的風險會顯著增加。
Latent attention 在架構上能大幅節省資源，但需要投入相當多的 engineering effort 才能有效進行 serving。
Eviction 可以釋放大量 memory，但有遺失後續 token generation 所需資訊的風險。
Cache 縮減技術主要在 long-context 與 high-concurrency 的 workload 中不可或缺，因為在這些情境下，cache memory 會成為主要的瓶頸。

sections.title: 結論
sections.summary: Long-context inference 的成本根本上取決於 attention cache 的大小。由於 decoding 階段每生成一個 token 都必須讀取整個 cache，因此 cache 同時造成了 storage 與 memory bandwidth 的瓶頸。縮減 cache 能提升 generation 速度，而最佳化技術則針對 cache 大小與 management 的不同面向進行改善。常見方法包括降低 per-token cost、將數值 quantization、evict token，以及改善 memory layout 與共享機制。
takeaways: Long-context inference 的成本由 cache 大小決定，這會帶來 storage 與 memory bandwidth 的 overhead。
在 decoding 期間，每個 token generation 步驟都必須讀取完整的 cache。
Grouped-query attention 與 latent attention 降低了與每個 token 相關的 memory 成本。
Quantization 透過以較少的 bit 編碼數值來減少 memory 需求。
Cache eviction 減少了保留的 token 總數。
Paged attention 與 prefix caching 增強了 cache management，並實現了跨 request 的共享。

sections.title: The hands-on AI engineer playbook to build RAG apps for production
sections.summary: The RAG Systems course has released a deep dive into the prefill stage of RAG applications, which is identified as the primary source of latency and cost. While retrieval and vector search are fast, processing retrieved tokens scales quadratically and can take several seconds. The guide explores techniques like KV cache reuse and selective recomputation to reduce Time to First Token (TTFT) and GPU costs. Tools like LMCache and TurboRAG are highlighted for their ability to significantly improve performance without sacrificing answer quality.
takeaways: Prefill latency is the dominant performance bottleneck in RAG systems, often taking seconds compared to milliseconds for retrieval.
The prefill stage scales quadratically with input length because every token must attend to every other token.
Standard prefix caching typically results in a near-zero hit rate for RAG workloads.
CacheBlend reduces Time to First Token (TTFT) by 2-3x by recomputing only 10-15% of tokens.
TurboRAG can achieve up to a 9.4x reduction in TTFT by moving the prefill process offline.
LMCache is an open-source package that implements CacheBlend and integrates with the vLLM serving engine.

sections.title: ORM vs PRM: How LLMs verify their reasoning?
sections.summary: The text explores the differences between Outcome Reward Models (ORM) and Process Reward Models (PRM) in verifying LLM reasoning. While PRMs are more effective at ranking solutions by evaluating individual steps, they are susceptible to model-based errors when used as training objectives. Consequently, rule-based outcome scoring is often preferred for training loops to ensure robustness, a strategy notably employed by DeepSeek-R1.
takeaways: Process Reward Models (PRM) score every step of a solution, while Outcome Reward Models (ORM) only score the final answer.
In OpenAI's testing, a process scorer achieved 78.2% accuracy on a math test set, significantly higher than the outcome scorer's 72.4%.
PRMs are better for ranking and search because they can identify correct answers reached through faulty reasoning.
Rule-based outcome scoring is more reliable for training loops because it avoids the 'model gaps' and misjudgments inherent in model-based process scorers.
DeepSeek-R1 utilized rule-based outcome scoring to check final answers and output formats during its development.
Reinforcement learning techniques like PPO and GRPO are central to modern LLM post-training and reward modeling.

sections.title: 16 techniques to optimize neural network training
sections.summary: This section outlines 16 specific techniques to optimize neural network training, focusing on improving speed and reducing memory consumption. It covers a range of strategies, from basic hardware acceleration and optimizer selection to advanced methods like Bayesian optimization for hyperparameter tuning. The text also provides practical implementation advice for distributed training and efficient data loading using tools like DeepSpeed and PyTorch's DistributedDataParallel.
takeaways: Bayesian optimization is more efficient than standard hyperparameter searches, achieving better F1 scores in fewer iterations.
Mixed precision training utilizes float16 for specific operations to speed up training while maintaining float32 for precision.
Activation checkpointing can reduce memory usage by a factor of sqrt(M) by recomputing intermediate activations during the backward pass.
DistributedDataParallel is recommended over DataParallel for all training scenarios to improve performance.
Normalizing data on the GPU instead of the CPU reduces memory bandwidth requirements by transferring smaller 8-bit integer types.
Creating tensors directly on the GPU using the device argument is significantly faster than transferring them from the CPU.
Configuring max_workers and pin_memory in DataLoaders allows for overlapping CPU data preparation with GPU computation.
